title: Add document links for every tsconfig path
body: ### Description `TsconfigLinkProvider` links three fields today: `extends`, `files` and `references[].path`. Every other value in a project config that names a file or a directory is inert. `extends` also only works in its string form, so the array form [TypeScript 5.0 introduced](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/release-notes/typescript-5-0.html#supporting-multiple-configuration-files-in-extends) is silently dropped: the array node is handed to a check that requires a string node, and every entry disappears. This adds links for the rest. Eighteen contribution rows cover the existing three plus `include`, `exclude`, `compilerOptions.lib`, `types`, `typeRoots`, `rootDir`, `rootDirs`, `baseUrl`, `outDir`, `declarationDir`, `outFile`, `tsBuildInfoFile`, `mapRoot` and `sourceRoot`. ### Demo https://youtu.be/L0CBEplaOtc ### Approach The provider is table-driven rather than a method per field, because the previous shape meant every new field edited the same three methods. Adding a field is now one row, and adding a resolution strategy is a row plus a function. `languageFeatures/tsconfig/` holds four pieces: - **`links.ts`** maps JSON paths to link kinds and produces link candidates. It performs no file system access, which is what makes it directly testable. A path segment can be a symbol wildcard matching every array element, so `extends` is expressed as two rows and both its forms work with no branching. - **`resolvers.ts`** describes each kind in one record: how it resolves to a target URI, what it says when it cannot, and what to do when the target does not exist. The existing `extends` and `references` resolution moves here, with its path-versus-module test aligned with the compiler's, so `.\foo`, `..`, `\\server\share` and `C:\foo` count as paths on every platform instead of depending on the host's `path.isAbsolute`. Separators are normalized the way the compiler does before a value reaches a URI, since `Uri.file` and `Uri.joinPath` only read a backslash as a separator on Windows, so a path written on Windows resolves the same everywhere. - **`libMap.ts`**, with an `.electron.ts` and a `.browser.ts` implementation, reads a TypeScript install's `libMap`, which is what turns a `lib` entry into a file name. - **`index.ts`** registers the provider and the command, and carries out the outcome: open, reveal, or report. Behaviors worth calling out: - `include` and `exclude` entries are usually globs, so only the literal leading segments are underlined and followed. `src/**/*` links `src`. An entry that begins with a wildcard has no directory to point at and gets no link, and neither does `./*.ts`, whose only literal segment is the config's own directory. - Directory targets reveal in the explorer, since `vscode.open` cannot open a folder in an editor. This applies to `typeRoots`, `rootDir`, `baseUrl` and glob prefixes. A directory outside the workspace cannot be selected in the explorer, so it is revealed in the OS file manager in a local desktop window and reported with a message elsewhere, remote windows included, where that command has no local path to show. - `lib` entries resolve against the TypeScript the language service is actually using, honoring `typescript.tsdk` and the workspace version picker, then any other local install, then the bundled copy. The file comes from the install rather than from the entry's spelling: a name the install ships a `lib..d.ts` for resolves to that file, and every other name, which is to say the aliases, goes through the install's own `libMap`, so `ES7` and `ESNext.BigInt` open `lib.es2016.d.ts` and `lib.es2020.bigint.d.ts` exactly as the compiler would, and a name neither knows is reported. An install the service could not read is skipped, the same fallback the version manager makes. On desktop the map is read from the `typescript.js` beside the install's `tsserver.js`, which is why it is consulted only for the aliases: loading it is expensive, so the result is cached against that file's modification time and the module is dropped again once the map is taken from it. An install inside the workspace is only loaded once the workspace is trusted, the same rule tsserver follows. On web the bundle step writes `libMap.json` next to the `lib.*.d.ts` files it already copies, from the same TypeScript, and the lib opens as a readonly text document rather than being handed to the browser. - `types` entries that are paths rather than package names, such as `./typings/foo`, resolve as paths. - A missing target still opens, and so still offers to create the file, for the kinds that name files. The kinds that name directories report instead, so a missing `"rootDir": "./src"` no longer offers to create a file called `src`. - `mapRoot` and `sourceRoot` accept a URL as well as a path, so a value with a URI scheme gets no link. `TypeScriptVersionManager` decided which install is active inside its constructor. That rule moves into an exported function beside it, so the `lib` resolver can ask the same question instead of reading the manager's storage key and reimplementing the rule. The version provider is configured at activation from the two tsdk settings alone, and reconfigured when they change, so `lib` links work with the native preview enabled, where no service client ever configures it. The full configuration load is not used for this because it shells out synchronously when `tsserver.nodePath` is set to `node`, and that must not sit on the activation path. ### Deliberately left out Each is a row plus at most a resolver once this lands: - `compilerOptions.paths` values, which resolve against `baseUrl` and so need document context the resolver contract does not carry. They would also need an object wildcard, since `paths` keys are globs. - `plugins[].name` and `jsxImportSource`, which are package resolution rather than path resolution. - `watchOptions.excludeFiles` and `excludeDirectories`. - The deprecated `out`. Three known limitations are recorded in comments: `types` entries are not resolved against `typeRoots`, the `@typescript/lib-*` override introduced in TypeScript 5.0 is not honored, and a link followed from its hover rather than from the document has its command arguments decoded once more than a ctrl+click does, so a value carrying a literal `%` resolves differently between the two gestures. ### Supersedes This replaces two of my open pull requests, which I am closing in favor of it: - #318263, the array form of `extends`, which falls out of the contribution table rather than needing its own branch. - #318350, `lib` links, whose version lookup is done here through a shared helper rather than by exporting the version manager's storage key. It also touches the same seam as #318274, which makes the document selector configurable. That one is unaffected in substance: rebased onto this, it replaces only the selector-building step in `index.ts` and stops touching link logic. `tsconfig.ts` becomes `tsconfig/index.ts` here, so whichever lands second needs a rebase. ### How to test 1. Open a workspace with a `tsconfig.json` such as: ```jsonc { "extends": ["./tsconfig.base.json"], "files": ["src/main.ts"], "include": ["src/**/*"], "compilerOptions": { "lib": ["DOM", "ES2022"], "types": ["node"], "typeRoots": ["./typings"], "rootDir": "./src", "outDir": "./out" } } ``` with `tsconfig.base.json`, `src/`, `typings/` and `node_modules/@types/node` present, and no `out/`. 2. Ctrl+Click (Cmd+Click) each value. Files open, directories reveal in the explorer, `DOM` opens `lib.dom.d.ts`, and `node` opens the `@types/node` declaration. Add `"ES7"` and `"ESNext.BigInt"` to `lib` and confirm they open `lib.es2016.d.ts` and `lib.es2020.bigint.d.ts`; add `"NotALib"` and confirm it reports that the lib could not be resolved. 3. In `"include": ["src/**/*"]`, confirm only `src` is underlined and that following it reveals the folder. 4. Ctrl+Click `outDir` before building and confirm it reports that the path does not exist yet. 5. Switch between the bundled and workspace TypeScript with **TypeScript: Select TypeScript Version**, then follow a `lib` entry again and confirm the target follows the selection. 6. Confirm the single-string form of `extends` still works, and that `files` and `references` are unaffected. 7. Point `outDir` at an existing directory outside the workspace and confirm following it reveals the folder in the OS file manager. 8. On web (`./scripts/code-web.sh `, after `npm run bundle-web` in the extension), follow `DOM` and confirm it opens as a readonly editor rather than a browser tab. Unit tests cover the selection layer, the path classification, the lib map reading and the command handler's branches: `./scripts/test-integration.sh --suite typescript`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) https://claude.ai/code/session_014hRTv3iMuJ7GVzFybCs5j7 https://claude.ai/code/session_01WadC2xvsDdvGEyyV4ia2B8

title: Guard navigator.clipboard in the WebKit clipboard workaround
body:
`BrowserClipboardService.installWebKitWriteTextWorkaround()` calls
`getActiveWindow().navigator.clipboard.write(...)` without checking that the async clipboard API is
there. Outside a secure context — plain `http://` on anything but `localhost` — `navigator.clipboard`
is `undefined`, and since the handler is bound to `click` and `keydown` on every container, Safari
throws on every click and keystroke:

```
TypeError: undefined is not an object (evaluating 'getActiveWindow().navigator.clipboard.write')
```

Every other clipboard access in this very file is already guarded; five of them carry the comment
`// Guard access to navigator.clipboard with try/catch`. This one is the exception.

## Why it is more than noise

The handler assigns `this.webKitPendingClipboardWritePromise = currentWritePromise` *before* the
throwing line. `writeText()` then takes its early exit and never reaches the working fallback:

```ts
if (this.webKitPendingClipboardWritePromise) {
    return this.webKitPendingClipboardWritePromise.complete(text);   // stops here
}
…
this.fallbackWriteText(text);   // execCommand('copy') — never reached
```

So copying inside the editor silently does nothing on Safari over http, even though
`fallbackWriteText()` would handle it.

## The change

Read `navigator.clipboard` once and return early when it is absent. That leaves
`webKitPendingClipboardWritePromise` untouched, so `writeText()` proceeds to `fallbackWriteText()`
and copying keeps working. Where the API is present nothing changes; the local binding also removes
a repeated `getActiveWindow()` lookup.

## Reported downstream

https://github.com/microsoft/monaco-editor/issues/4496 describes this exactly, with the same reproduction: serve monaco over
`http://` on a LAN address, open it in Safari, type. Open since 2024-05-05 with three independent
confirmations and no maintainer response — reported against monaco-editor, while the code lives
here.

## Reproducing

1. Serve a monaco-based page over `http://` on a non-loopback address, so `window.isSecureContext`
   is `false` and `navigator.clipboard` is `undefined`
2. Open it in Safari and click into the editor
3. Every click and keystroke raises the TypeError above; copying does nothing

title: Fix primary side bar width reset when toggled with the side bar on the right
body:
Fixes #334167

## The bug

With Modern UI enabled and the primary side bar on the **right**, hiding and showing the side bar (<kbd>Ctrl/Cmd+B</kbd>) collapses it to its 170px minimum width instead of restoring the width the user set. The left-hand side bar is unaffected.

## Root cause

`ActivitybarPart.needsFloatingLeadingGap` makes the rail reserve an extra leading gap when the side bar is hidden and the bar is on the right, so the activity bar's fixed width changes with side bar visibility. It reports that change through `onDidChangePartVisibility`, which is fired **synchronously from inside `Part.setVisible()`** — i.e. re-entrantly, while `SplitView.setViewVisible()` has already restored the side bar to its cached size but has not yet reclaimed the space for it.

The resulting `SplitView.onViewChange` redistributed that difference in plain **index order**, unlike `resizeView`, which is layout priority aware. With the side bar on the right the view order is `[…, editor, sideBar, activityBar]`, so the side bar was the first candidate to be shrunk and gave up everything down to its minimum. On the left the order is `[activityBar, sideBar, editor, …]`, so the flexible editor happened to absorb it first — which is why the bug only appeared on the right.

## The fix

`SplitView.onViewChange` now redistributes using layout priorities — high priority first, low priority last — the same computation `resizeView` already uses. The flexible editor absorbs the change instead of the side bar.

## Verification

- **New regression test** in `splitview.test.ts` modelling the right-side arrangement. It fails without the fix (the side bar collapses to its minimum) and passes with it.
- **End to end in a real Code OSS window** (Modern UI, side bar on the right): `300px → 170px` after a single toggle without the fix; a steady `300px` across three toggle cycles with it, with no per-toggle drift. The left position was verified stable, the auxiliary bar is unaffected, and the standalone activity bar rail still renders its gap correctly while the side bar is hidden.
- **Full unit test suite**: 34468 passing, 0 failing.

title: agentHost: honor SSH ProxyJump when connecting
body:
Fixes #317445

## Problem

Agent Host resolves effective OpenSSH configuration with `ssh -G`, but did not carry `ProxyJump` into the `ssh2` connection. A host reachable only through its configured jump host was therefore dialed directly from the Agents window and failed with `ENOTFOUND` or `EHOSTUNREACH`, while native OpenSSH and Remote SSH succeeded against the same config.

## Change

Preserve the resolved `ProxyJump` value through initial and reconnect configuration. For a single jump host, start native OpenSSH with `BatchMode=yes` and `-W`, pass its standard streams to `ssh2` through `ConnectConfig.sock`, and stop the owned helper on connection teardown. The destination is passed after `--` so a config-derived value can never be read as an `ssh` option.

`ssh -G` reports `ProxyJump` with its percent tokens unexpanded, so `%%`, `%h`, `%n`, `%p` and `%r` are expanded here. Expansion happens per component *after* the value is split, because a token standing in for an IPv6 address would otherwise be mistaken for a port separator — `%h:24321` against an IPv6 `HostName` becomes `::1:24321`. The `ssh://` URI form is accepted directly as well, though `ssh -G` normalizes it away.
 A bracketed IPv6 jump host is passed to `ssh` bare while the `-W` target keeps its brackets, matching what `ssh -J` itself emits: glibc and Darwin `getaddrinfo` reject `[...]` for a numeric IPv6 destination, so forwarding the brackets fails name resolution everywhere except Windows.
The helper's stderr is the only place DNS, host-key and authentication failures for the jump host are reported; without it they all collapse into `ssh2`'s generic "Connection lost before handshake". A bounded tail is captured and attached to the surfaced error. It is attached by annotating the existing error rather than replacing it, so an `SSHHostKeyDeniedError` keeps the `name` the renderer dispatches on. That annotation is the single place it is added — the helper's own exit error carries the code and signal only — so a jump-host failure does not repeat the same OpenSSH diagnostic twice in the message the user sees.

The jump alias, not a pre-resolved hostname, is handed to OpenSSH, so the jump host's own `HostName`, `User`, `Port` and `IdentityFile` still apply. Final-host authentication, host-key verification, Agent Host bootstrap and WebSocket handling are untouched.

Single-hop only. Comma-separated chains, `ProxyCommand`, interactive jump-host authentication, askpass IPC and `HostKeyAlias` behavior are unchanged, and there are no dependency, build or pipeline changes.

## Validation

- `npm run compile-client`, `typecheck-client`, `valid-layers-check`, full `eslint`, and hygiene on the changed files — all clean
- `vs/platform/agentHost/test/{common,node}` — 6787 passing, 0 failing; `remoteAgentHost/test` — 280 passing. An earlier revision of this section reported three `CopilotAgent` state-file failures as pre-existing. They were not. `getCopilotHomePath()` prefers an ambient `COPILOT_HOME` over the injected `userHome`, so the value set in my shell escaped the test's sandbox — and failed on unpatched `main` for the same reason, which is what made it look pre-existing. Cleared, the suite is green.
- Each production change is mutation-proven: reverting the `ProxyJump` mapping in the configured-host action, the token expansion, the expand-after-split ordering, the `close`-instead-of-`exit` read, the annotate-in-place error handling, the `connected` gate on helper disposal, the bounded stderr wait, the single attachment of the helper diagnostic, or the IPv6 bracket strip each fails a specific regression test, and the suite returns to green when restored.
- Live built Code OSS A/B, captured on commit `dca870d` (base `7b763e653ee2`), using disposable profiles, real key-authenticated jump and target SSH servers, and the actual Agent Host WebSocket relay:
  - Native OpenSSH reached `proxyjump-target.invalid:2222` through the configured jump host.
  - Unpatched `main` used the same Agents UI action, dialed the target directly, failed with `getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND`, and never contacted the jump or target servers.
  - Patched Code OSS contacted the jump, forwarded to the target, authenticated, launched the real Agent Host, and completed the SSH-forwarded WebSocket connection.
  - A direct-host control completed the same Agent Host flow without starting a jump helper.
  - All owned helper and Agent Host processes exited after the UI closed.
- The `--` terminator was added after that run, so this revision is not byte-identical to the Electron-tested one and the Electron harness was not re-run. It is covered separately: against OpenSSH 9.5p2, `ssh -o BatchMode=yes -W target.invalid:22 -V` prints the version and exits 0, while the same command with `-- -V` treats it as a hostname and exits 255; ordinary `host` and `user@host` destinations are unaffected. A unit regression asserts `--` is always immediately before the destination, and it fails without the production change.
- Percent-token behavior was confirmed against OpenSSH 9.5p2 directly: `ssh -G` returns `proxyjump %n-bastion` and `proxyjump bastion-%h` literally, unexpanded.
- The bounded wait for stderr that is still in flight when `ssh2` rejects on the stdout EOF is covered directly against the proxy transport: one test asserts it does not settle before the helper's stdio closes and that the diagnostic is complete afterwards, another asserts it gives up rather than hanging when the helper never closes. Making `whenStderrSettled()` resolve immediately fails the first.
- Agent Host E2E, run locally in the CI configuration, twice per side on `d2da7c8d` (this branch before the stderr de-duplication): 176 passing / 1 failing, then 175 / 2; merge-base `7b7e49c8` 176 / 1 both times. title: Keep all repositories visible when a new one is discovered first
body: Fixes #334842 ## Problem `SCMViewService.onDidAddRepository` restores the visibility of repositories from `scm:view:visibleRepositories`. When a repository is **not** part of the previous state, the code takes the "select all" path, but it leaves `previousState` in effect and resets `didSelectRepository` to `false`. A repository that is discovered *after* that one, and that *was* visible in the previous session, then takes the `// First visible repository` branch: ```ts removed = [...this.visibleRepositories]; this._repositories.forEach(r => { r.focused = false; r.selectionIndex = -1; }); this.didSelectRepository = true; ``` which clears the selection of every repository added so far, leaving itself as the only visible repository. The bad selection is written back to storage by `onWillSaveState`, so it survives every subsequent restart. Because the outcome depends on the order in which repositories are discovered, the same workspace can end up with different subsets visible. Walking this logic through every discovery order for a workspace with repositories `A`, `B` (both visible last session) and a new `C`: | discovery order | visible today | |---|---| | A, B, C | A, B, C | | B, A, C | A, B, C | | C, A, B | A, B | | C, B, A | A, B | | B, C, A | A | | **A, C, B** | **B** | The `A, C, B` and `A, B, C` rows are the two I reproduced against a real build; the rest follow from the same code path. With this change all six orders produce `A, B, C`. ## Change Clear `previousState` once we have decided to select all repositories, so the rest of the load is no longer influenced by it. This makes the code do what its own comment says ("In this case, we should select all of the repositories") regardless of discovery order. ## Verification I could not build a full VS Code here (`native-keymap` needs `libxkbfile-dev`), so I verified the change by applying the equivalent one-statement patch to the `workbench.desktop.main.js` of a copy of the shipped 1.136.1 build and running the scenarios from #334842 against it. Each pair below uses the **same** profile and the **same** persisted state (restored byte-for-byte between runs); only the binary differs. `visible` is read from `scm:view:visibleRepositories` in workspace storage, and the Git extension log confirms every repository was opened in all runs. | previous state | workspace folder order | 1.136.1 | with this change | |---|---|---|---| | `all=[A,B] visible=[0,1]` | A, **C (new)**, B | `[B]` — A and C lost | `[A,C,B]` | | `all=[A,B] visible=[0]` (B hidden on purpose) | A, B (no new repository) | `[A]` | `[A]` — unchanged | | `all=[A,B] visible=[0]` (B hidden on purpose) | **C (new)**, A, B | `[A]` — the newly added C is not shown either | `[C,A,B]` | Row 2 is the regression case that matters: when no new repository is involved, an intentionally hidden repository stays hidden, exactly as before. Row 3 is a deliberate behaviour change worth calling out: when a brand-new repository appears, an intentionally hidden repository becomes visible again, because the "select all" path now applies consistently. Today's behaviour in that situation is order-dependent and hides the newly added repository, which seems worse. If you would rather preserve the previous selection and only add the new repository as visible, I am happy to change the patch to do that instead — that alternative would also address #301028, which reports a different failure of the same branch. ## Screenshot The first row of the table above, side by side. Two windows of the same 1.136.1 build, `--disable-extensions`, identical settings and repositories, both seeded with the same previous state (`A` and `B` visible), both opening a workspace with folder order `A, C, B`. The only difference is that the right-hand window runs a build with this change applied. Left: the Repositories view lists all three repositories but only `B` is selected, Changes has no repository headers and shows only B's files, and the status bar reads `B master*`. Right: all three repositories are selected, each with its own header and commit box. ## Tests There is currently no `scmViewService.test.ts`, and adding one needs a fair amount of service scaffolding (`ISCMService`, `SCMMenus`, storage, configuration, workspace). I did not want to submit a test I could not run in this environment. Happy to add one covering the discovery-order cases above if you want it in this PR.

title: automations: feat: add starter templates and clarify target selection
body:
## Summary

Add starter automation templates to the Agents Window, make new automation targets explicit, and distinguish an incomplete catalogue from an empty one.

This is the reviewed and updated version of #334368, based on the provider-owned session-template architecture already merged in #334521.

## Why

Automations are aggregated from legacy storage and local/remote providers. An empty array does not tell a consumer whether there are no automations, discovery is pending, or a provider is offline. Treating all of those situations alike either shows a misleading empty state or prevents a usable local target from being offered.

The new-automation dialog also restored a checked/recent workspace even though restoration from existing sessions was disabled. A remembered GitHub repository could therefore silently bind a template to Cloud. Cloud is legitimately the only agent for that workspace, but the disabled control did not explain how to choose a different target.

## Changes

### Templates and target selection

- Add editable starter cards for issue triage, pull request review, dependency audit, and release notes.
- Templates seed only name, prompt, and schedule; choosing one opens the existing dialog and does not create an automation.
- Require an explicit workspace or **No workspace** choice for a new target-less dialog. Honor the shared picker's existing `canRestoreWorkspace` callback during initial restoration, then opt out in the automation dialog without changing normal New Session defaults.
- Put workspace selection before the agent control, explain single-agent targets with a **Choose Workspace** action, and show the agent dropdown chevron when alternatives exist.
- Hide worktree and session-configuration controls until there is a relevant target. Preserve explicit edit/duplicate targets and unavailable saved provider/type choices.

| New automation before choosing a target | Explicitly selected Cloud-only workspace |
| --- | --- |
| ![New automation asks for an explicit workspace or No workspace choice](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ef4ed5d2-1d3b-4f04-a370-67e04e26dcdf) | ![Cloud-only target explains the workspace restriction and offers Choose Workspace](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e6157b47-67de-4d90-ad8d-f5cb88a654b0) |

### Honest catalogue state

Expose observable `catalogueState` on automation stores:

| State | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `loading` | Provider discovery or an authoritative snapshot is still in flight. |
| `ready` | All participating sources are readable and the catalogue is complete. |
| `unavailable` | A known provider is disconnected, disabled, or does not advertise automation support. |
| `error` | A participating source could not be read or loaded. |

- Compose states with `error > loading > unavailable > ready`.
- Settle initial discovery after AfterRestored contributions finish; provider-less windows then settle to their legacy-store state.
- Retain known cards beside partial-catalogue warnings. Offer templates whenever there are no known cards, even if a remote catalogue is unavailable. Only `ready` may claim that there are no automations.
- Keep operations routed to an independently usable local provider available regardless of aggregate completeness.
- Return `{ catalogueState, automations }` from `listAutomations`, preserving existing row fields and explaining incomplete results to the model.

### Storage, accessibility, and focus

- Publish legacy ledger readability and catalogue state with the corresponding definitions/runs. Include still-participating legacy sources in Agent Host projection state and recheck readability across asynchronous migration boundaries.
- Match accessible help/text to the visible templates and catalogue state, and provide full-text hovers for truncated template names and prompts.
- Preserve meaningful focus across view transitions; cancel delayed created-card focus after user navigation or blur instead of stealing focus later.
- Synchronize native keyboard-focus scrolling with the custom view's scrollbar.

## Compatibility

Provider-owned `IAutomationSessionTemplate` remains canonical, with opaque configuration preserved. Workspace trust, managed policy, and provider capabilities still govern drafts and runs. This does not introduce a scheduler, permission grant, AI setting, dependency, or persistence-schema change. Existing AI feature gating is preserved.

## Validation

- [x] 406 targeted Electron tests: automation storage, providers, tools, Agent Host stores, cards view, dialog, and workspace/agent pickers.
- [x] 29 targeted Chromium tests for target guidance and workspace/agent selection.
- [x] Additional native Chromium focus checks and catalogue/template fixture rendering during implementation.
- [x] Client type checking, targeted ESLint, CSS stylelint, and staged pre-commit hygiene. Stylelint reported only pre-existing token suggestions.
- [x] Isolated Code OSS verification: unbound new dialog, Cloud-only explanation, local Copilot/Claude/Codex choices, No workspace, keyboard focus restoration, preserved saved targets, and fresh dialogs remaining unbound.
- [x] All actual GitHub CI checks passed, including cross-platform tests, Compile & Hygiene, Screenshots & Tests, and CodeQL. macOS Remote passed after one retry for a runner DNS failure while cloning the smoke-test fixture, before any smoke tests ran.
- [x] Copilot review completed with no inline findings or unresolved threads.

title: [cherry-pick] Fix tab close button stuck showing "Close Others" after focus changes
body:
Cherry-pick of #334515 from `main`.

## Description

Alt+hover swaps a tab's **Close** action for **Close Others**. Both inputs to that swap could go stale across a focus change: `redrawTabAction()` read `modifierKeyEmitter.keyStatus.altKey` at paint time (the Alt `keyup` is delivered to whichever app you Alt+Tab'd into), and `hoveredTabIndex` was only cleared by a real `mouseleave`. Coming back to the window without moving the mouse could therefore leave the `x` armed as "Close Others", so a plain click silently closed every other editor in the group.

### Changes — `MultiEditorTabsControl`

- **Local Alt state.** A `isAltPressed` field, fed by the `ModifierKeyEmitter` event, replaces the two on-demand reads of `modifierKeyEmitter.keyStatus.altKey`. It is the single source of truth for the swap and redraws the hovered tab when it flips.
- **Give up the swap on focus loss.** `IHostService.onDidChangeFocus(false)` clears both the Alt state and the hovered tab, so a hover left over from before the focus change cannot be re-armed by Alt state re-established on return. Re-hovering a tab arms it again as usual.
- **Re-validate Alt from mouse events.** `mousemove`/`mousedown` on the tabs container carry the real modifier state even when a `keyup` was missed entirely — this covers macOS Mission Control, where the window may never see a `blur`.

The mouse listeners are registered in the **capture** phase because `BaseActionViewItem` calls `EventHelper.stop(e, true)` on `mousedown`; a bubble-phase listener never sees a press on the close button itself, which is precisely the reported "click without moving the mouse" case.

```ts
for (const eventType of [EventType.MOUSE_MOVE, EventType.MOUSE_DOWN]) {
	this._register(addDisposableListener(tabsContainer, eventType, (e: MouseEvent) => {
		this.setAltPressed(e.altKey);
	}, true));
}
```

In the stale-Alt case the capture handler swaps the action item mid-`mousedown`, so that first click is swallowed rather than executing "Close Others" — the icon is then correct and the next click closes the single tab.

`EditorTabsControl.hostService` becomes `protected` so the subclass can use it.

### Tests

`src/vs/workbench/test/browser/parts/editor/multiEditorTabsControl.test.ts` covers the baseline swap plus the focus-loss, mouse-move and action-mousedown paths; each regression test was checked to fail with its corresponding part of the change reverted.

### Notes for reviewers

- After returning from another application the swap requires a fresh hover (move to another tab, or leave and re-enter). This is the behaviour suggested in the issue and is what makes a stale hover unexploitable.
- `menuEntryActionViewItem.ts` has the same latent staleness pattern; left untouched to keep this scoped to tabs.

title: [cherry-pick] sessions: measure and unblock V3 onboarding GitHub personalization
body:
Cherry-pick of #334696 from `main`.

## Why

The V3 new-session onboarding personalizes its 3 prompt options with GitHub items (assigned issues, authored PRs with conflicts / failing CI / unresolved review comments), falling back to standard options.

Analysis of experiment `f716301b` over 3 weeks and ~780k users found that, restricted to users with a resolved GitHub repository who saw the options widget (222,470 impressions):

- **61.0%** timed out with zero GitHub options
- **~9.4%** saw at least one GitHub option (only **0.17%** saw a full 3/3 set)
- **29.6%** got all-standard options

And we could not measure *how* badly, because `fallbackReason` was only set to `'none'` when all 3 slots were GitHub — so a widget with 2 real GitHub issues logged identically to one with zero. That blind spot covered 81% of impressions.

The root cause of the timeouts is that per-stage budgets could exceed the total budget: the PR chain was summary(5s) → review(4s) = 9s, with repository resolution also inside the same 10s budget.

## Telemetry

Additive only — existing field names and values are emitted in the same situations, so live dashboards keep working.

`onboarding.promptStrategy` gains:

| Field | Question it answers |
|---|---|
| `gitHubOptionCount` | How many of the 3 slots were actually GitHub items — closes the main blind spot |
| `candidatesFound` | Pre-truncation count: "repo has nothing" vs "found items but were too slow" |
| `lookupDurationMs` | Total lookup time (plumbed from the value the code already computed for logging) |
| `repositoryMs`, `issueSummaryMs`, `issueLinkageMs`, `prSummaryMs`, `prReviewMs` | Which stage is actually slow |
| `issueSummaryOutcome`, `issueLinkageOutcome`, `prSummaryOutcome`, `prReviewOutcome` | Per-stage outcome, so "issues succeeded, PRs timed out" is distinguishable from total failure |
| `timedOutStage` | Which stage was in flight when the total budget expired |

`onboarding.promptOptionInteraction` gains `optionIndex` and `optionKindsShown`, making a true per-option CTR computable — today "implementFeature is most picked" is confounded with it being almost always present.

Both events gain a shared `impressionId`, so they can be joined per impression instead of on `DevDeviceId`, which is lossy for devices with multiple impressions.

Also splits the overloaded `noCandidate` — it meant both "no composer available" (an infra bug) and "lookup returned nothing" (a data outcome). The former is now `noComposer`.

**Privacy:** bounded categories and counts only. No issue/PR titles, URLs, numbers, repository names or prompt text. Every numeric has `isMeasurement: true`.

## Latency

`totalMs` stays at 10s.

1. **Publish issue candidates before linkage.** Linkage exists only to filter out issues that already have linked PRs, so a slow linkage call was discarding issues we already held.
2. **Review-thread enrichment off the critical path.** It fired N parallel lookups after a summary to produce `githubPRComments` — 30 selections, 0.37% of all picks — while `githubIssue` (the most-picked GitHub option) is the cheapest to fetch. The budget was being spent inversely to user value. It can now only refine, never delay first paint.
3. **Rebalanced sub-budgets** to `summaryMs: 4_000, linkageMs: 1_500, reviewMs: 3_000`. The issue and PR chains run concurrently under `Promise.all`, so the worst case for timed lookups is `max(4_000+1_500, 4_000+3_000) = 7_000ms`, leaving ~3s for repository resolution and rendering. Repository resolution has no budget of its own and a workspace change restarts the chain; both are bounded only by the `totalMs` race, and the comment on the constant says so rather than asserting a tighter bound than the code has.
4. **Streaming.** The 3 standard options are painted immediately and slots are replaced as GitHub items arrive, instead of blocking first paint on the whole lookup. Beyond timeouts, this also addresses V3's ~17pp tour-reach deficit versus V2.

## API change

`INewSessionPromptOptionsController.resolve` gains an optional progress callback:

```ts
export type NewSessionPromptOptionsProgress = (state: NewSessionPromptOptionsState) => boolean;

resolve(token: CancellationToken, progress?: NewSessionPromptOptionsProgress): Promise<NewSessionPromptOptionsState>;
```

Additive and optional, so existing callers are unaffected. It returns `boolean` rather than `void` deliberately: the composer refuses late updates while the user is already acting on the options, and the runner needs to know that so interaction telemetry describes what was actually rendered.

## Notes for reviewers

The streaming path has three subtle interactions that are each covered by a test that fails without its fix:

- `_renderedPromptOptions` is reset per `resolve`, not per `run`. `newChatWidget` calls `refreshPromptOptions()` on every workspace change against the same runner, and a per-run reset made the second refresh compare against the previous refresh's final set — suppressing first paint entirely in exactly the all-standard case this PR targets.
- `_promptOptionsSelected` is set at the *start* of `selectOption`, not in `onDidSelectOption`. The widget only reports a selection after the 2.5s prompt animation completes; a streamed update in that window would clear the selection and leave every option `aria-disabled`.
- The runner commits `_renderedPromptOptions` only when the composer accepted the update, so `optionIndex` / `optionKindsShown` can never describe options the user never saw.

`impressionId` is regenerated per `run`, not per `resolve`: strategy telemetry is emitted once per run, so a per-resolve id would orphan interaction events from any strategy event.

## Validation

- `scripts\test.bat --grep "NewSession"` → **93 passing**, 0 failing
- `npm run typecheck-client` → clean for `sessions/contrib`
- `eslint` → clean
- Code hygiene → clean on changed files (the repo-wide `npm run hygiene` task fails on an unrelated pre-existing Windows path bug in `checkPackageJSON`, reproducible on an untouched checkout; no `package.json` is touched here)

New test coverage: partial GitHub candidate counts, the early issue publish, streaming updates arriving after first paint, budget-stage attribution, re-resolve after a workspace change, and the composer refusing late updates.

## Kusto queries this makes answerable

- Distribution of `gitHubOptionCount` (0/1/2/3) — the true personalization rate, vs today's binary
- Per-stage p50/p95 latency and timeout rate, attributing the 61% bucket to `repository` vs `prSummary` vs `prReview`
- `candidatesFound == 0` vs `candidatesFound > gitHubOptionCount` — "nothing to show" vs "found more than we could show"
- Partial-success cohorts, e.g. `issueSummaryOutcome == 'success' and prSummaryOutcome == 'timeout'`
- True per-option CTR, joining `optionKindsShown` impressions with `option` selections
- Position bias: selections by `optionIndex`, controlling for slot content
- Impression-level funnel joined on `impressionId`

title: Skip extension host restart when adding the first folder to an empty window
body:
Fixes #319944

### Problem

When a window has no folder open and you **Add Folder to Workspace**, VS Code restarts the extension host. If Copilot Chat (or another session) is in progress, you get **Please confirm restart of extensions — A session is in progress.** Confirming kills the chat.

`N→N+1` folders in an existing multi-root workspace does not restart the host. `0→1` should behave the same.

Two restarts fire on that transition:

1. `NativeWorkspaceEditingService.enterWorkspace` — reason `Opening a multi-root workspace` (empty window always creates an untitled workspace and enters it).
2. `WorkspaceChangeExtHostRelauncher` — reason `Changing workspace folders` (first folder goes from none → one, for the deprecated `workspace.rootPath` API).

Skipping only (1) is not enough. Local logs still showed the veto from (2):

```
Extension host was not stopped because of veto (stop reason: Changing workspace folders, veto reason: A session is in progress.)
```

### Fix

Skip the extension host restart on the **0→1** path only. Storage switch, backup reinit, and `onDidEnterWorkspace` still run. Changing the first folder later (`A → B`) still restarts the host. Folder → multi-root and remote windows are unchanged.

`workspaceEditingService.ts` — do not stop/start the EH when coming from `WorkbenchState.EMPTY`:

```ts
const fromEmptyWorkspace = this.contextService.getWorkbenchState() === WorkbenchState.EMPTY;

if (!fromEmptyWorkspace) {
	const stopped = await this.extensionService.stopExtensionHosts(/* ... */);
	if (!stopped) {
		return;
	}
}
```

`relauncher.contribution.ts` — do not schedule a restart when there was no previous first folder:

```ts
const hadFirstFolder = !!this.firstFolderResource;
this.firstFolderResource = newFirstFolderResource;

// Skip 0→1 folders (#319944): same as adding a folder in an existing workspace
if (hadFirstFolder) {
	this.extensionHostRestarter.schedule();
}
```

Notes:

- Workspace folders still update live via `$acceptWorkspaceData` (`MainThreadWorkspace`), same as `N→N+1`.
- Chat session files still migrate through `ChatSessionStore` joining `onDidEnterWorkspace`.
- Caveat: extension-host workspace-scoped storage (`ExtensionStoragePaths`) stays bound to the empty-window workspace id until the next real EH restart. Workbench storage is switched with `preserveData`. Extensions that only read `rootPath` in `activate()` can stay stale until then (same class of issue as in-place folder add).

### Tests

- `nativeWorkspaceEditingService.test.ts`
  - empty window → `enterWorkspace` does not call `stopExtensionHosts` / `startExtensionHosts`
  - folder window → `enterWorkspace` still restarts the host

### How to test

1. `./scripts/code.sh` with **no folder** (empty window).
2. Start Copilot Chat and send a message.
3. Command Palette → **Add Folder to Workspace...** → pick a folder.
4. No restart confirmation dialog; chat stays.

Regression: open a **single folder**, add a second folder via Add Folder to Workspace — EH restart for `enterWorkspace` still applies. In an existing multi-root workspace, adding another folder (not replacing the first) still does not restart.

title: Fix backspace over a flag emoji leaving a dangling regional indicator
body:
Fixes #334807.

`getLeftDeleteOffset()` (via `getOffsetBeforeLastEmojiComponent()`) already treats an emoji modifier sequence — e.g. a skin-tone-modified emoji like 👶🏾 — as a single unit for Backspace, per the fix for #99629. Flag emoji weren't covered: a flag is two Regional Indicator Symbol code points (e.g. 🇺🇸 = U+1F1FA U+1F1F8), and backspacing over one deleted only the trailing code point, leaving a dangling, meaningless lone Regional Indicator behind — the exact class of bug #99629 was meant to prevent, just for a different emoji construct.

### What changed

Per Unicode UAX #29 rules GB12/GB13, Regional Indicators combine greedily in pairs from the start of a maximal run of consecutive indicators, so the run's length parity determines whether the last indicator in it is paired. Added `isRegionalIndicator()` / `isRegionalIndicatorPaired()` in `strings.ts` and used them in `getOffsetBeforeLastEmojiComponent()` so:

- A complete flag (paired Regional Indicators) is deleted as one unit.
- A trailing, genuinely unpaired Regional Indicator is still deleted alone (unchanged from before).
- Skin-tone modifier sequences and ZWJ-joined emoji (e.g. family emoji, which are intentionally peeled component-by-component to match Firefox's behavior per the discussion in #99629) are unaffected.

### Before / after

| Input, repeated Backspace | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| 🇺🇸 (single flag) | 🇺🇸 → 🇺 → *(empty)* | 🇺🇸 → *(empty)* |
| 🇺🇸🇬🇧 (two flags) | 🇺🇸🇬🇧 → 🇺🇸🇬 → 🇺🇸 → 🇺 → *(empty)* | 🇺🇸🇬🇧 → 🇺🇸 → *(empty)* |
| 🇺🇸🇬 (flag + lone indicator) | 🇺🇸🇬 → 🇺🇸 → 🇺 → *(empty)* | 🇺🇸🇬 → 🇺🇸 → *(empty)* |
| 👶🏾 (skin-tone modifier) | 👶🏾 → *(empty)* | unchanged |
| 👨‍👨‍👧‍👧 (ZWJ family) | peeled one ZWJ component per press | unchanged |

### Testing

I added `suite('getLeftDeleteOffset', ...)` to `src/vs/base/test/common/strings.test.ts`, covering all five rows above plus a plain-text sanity check.

**Verification method (please re-run before merge):** a full `npm install` + Electron test run (`./scripts/test.sh --run ...`) wasn't practical in the environment I used, so I verified two ways instead:
1. Imported the real, unmodified `strings.ts` directly with `tsx` (no hand-transpilation of the algorithm) and simulated repeated Backspace over the emoji constructs in the table above, before and after the fix, confirming the "before" column reproduces the bug and the "after" column matches the fix.
2. Ran the full, unmodified `src/vs/base/test/common/strings.test.ts` (54 tests, including the new ones) end-to-end via a minimal `suite`/`test`/`setup`/`teardown` shim under `tsx`, standing in for mocha — all 54 pass.

Both give me high confidence in the change, but since this bypassed the project's actual mocha/Electron test runner, I'd appreciate a maintainer (or CI) re-running it via `npm run test-node` / `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/base/test/common/strings.test.js` as the authoritative check before merge.

I used Claude Code to help locate this bug, derive the Unicode-spec-based fix, and draft this PR and description; I reviewed the diff and the reasoning by hand before submitting.

title: Fix terminal not focusing when clicking blank space below inline chat widget
body:
Fixes #333458

**What's happening**

The `.terminal-inline-chat` container is positioned absolutely with `bottom: 0`, while `terminalChatWidget.ts` also sets an inline `top` style to anchor it near the cursor. With `height: auto` and both `top` and `bottom` set, the container stretches to fill the whole gap instead of shrink-wrapping to the widget's actual content, leaving an invisible region below the visible widget that still captures clicks meant for the terminal.

![Blank space below the terminal inline chat widget](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Chethan616/vscode/pr-assets-terminal-chat-fix/terminal-chat-blank-space.png)

**Fix**

Make the outer container transparent to pointer events and only re-enable them on the visible `.inline-chat` box, so clicks in the empty space fall through to the terminal underneath.

**Testing**

- [x] Reproduced on Windows: opened terminal inline chat, maximized the panel, clicked below the widget — `document.activeElement` stayed on `<body>`, terminal never focused
- [x] Applied the fix and repeated the same click — `document.activeElement` became the terminal's `xterm-helper-textarea`
- [x] Confirmed the widget's own input is still focusable/clickable after the fix (no regression)

title: configuration: batch initial policy definitions
body:
## Summary

- submit regular and excluded policy definitions in one initialization batch
- avoid rebuilding the native policy watcher for a second changed batch
- add coverage that verifies included and excluded definitions reach one underlying policy update

## Root cause

While profiling Agents Window startup, the main process appeared to spend 40-50 ms reading state, loading settings, and creating required directories. Direct `fs/promises` measurements against the same signed-in profile showed that the actual operations are fast:

| Operation | Median | p95 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Concurrent startup I/O group | 1.02 ms | 1.41 ms |
| Read 3.6 KB `storage.json` | 1.02 ms | 1.30 ms |
| Read missing `settings.json` | 0.13 ms | 0.32 ms |
| Existing-directory `mkdir({ recursive: true })` | 0.62-0.76 ms | 0.83-1.18 ms |

The callbacks were delayed together because `PolicyConfiguration.initialize()` submitted definitions in two sequential groups:

1. regular/default configuration policies
2. excluded/internal configuration policies

`AbstractPolicyService` merges each changed group and invokes the native implementation. `NativePolicyService` therefore imported/updated the policy watcher for the first group, then disposed and recreated it for the second group before startup I/O callbacks could run.

This change combines both key sets before resolving and submitting policy definitions. The resulting policy model is unchanged, but native watcher initialization happens once.

## Instrumented startup impact

Three warmed packaged launches per variant, using the same Windows x64 Insiders runtime and signed-in isolated profile:

| Operation | Before median | After median | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Policy initialization | 45 ms | 33 ms | **-12 ms** |
| State read callback | 50 ms | 40 ms | **-10 ms** |
| Missing settings callback | 27 ms | 17 ms | **-10 ms** |
| Required-directory callbacks | 46 ms | 38 ms | **-8 ms** |

The callback improvements overlap; they are not additive. They show that removing the redundant watcher update frees the main event loop sooner.

The remaining combined policy segment spends approximately 27 ms importing `@vscode/policy-watcher` and 6 ms creating the watcher. #334769 independently targets the packaged ESM resolution work in that import.

## End-to-end A/B

The first 30 alternating paired launches measured spawn to renderer `code/didStartWorkbench`:

- baseline median: 1,330.31 ms
- change median: 1,326.40 ms
- median paired difference: **-6.01 ms**
- mean paired difference: **-4.03 ms**
- approximate 95% interval: -9.71 to +1.66 ms

A second 30-pair batch had a system disturbance around pairs 42-47. Across all 60 pairs, excluding five pairs where either launch exceeded 1,450 ms:

- included pairs: 55
- median paired difference: **-3.03 ms**
- mean paired difference: **-1.96 ms**
- approximate 95% interval: -5.76 to +1.83 ms

The end-to-end result is directional, not statistically significant. The deterministic result is one fewer native watcher build and an 8-12 ms reduction in the blocking initialization segment.

## Compatibility

The previous initialization called `update()` twice before registering policy-change listeners. The new initialization calls it once with the union of the same configuration keys. Existing behavior remains covered for:

- regular policy values
- excluded/internal policy values
- owning policies and references
- late owner registration
- owner deregistration fallback
- policy updates and removals

## Validation

- targeted ESLint
- `npm run transpile-client`
- focused `PolicyConfiguration` suite: 23 passing
- minified NLS desktop bundle
- instrumentation-free signed-in Agents Window product smoke
- `git diff --check`

title: editor: preserve restored font measurements on short sessions
body:
## Summary

Preserve the last trusted persisted font measurements until the current VS Code session produces its own measurement, including when restored readings are evicted before any editor revalidates them.

- retain restored provenance after the five-second untrusted-reading eviction so an editor-less window does not overwrite the trusted application-scoped snapshot with `[]`
- return `undefined` while the cache has only been populated from restored data, before or after those entries are evicted
- continue returning `[]` for a genuinely empty or explicitly cleared cache and for failed current-session measurements
- add focused regression coverage for restored, evicted, cleared, and current-session failure states

## Root cause

Profiling standalone file startup with VS Code Insiders `1.137.0-insider` (`de8cc55dae905582f191fdcfb6dff8c811a743c4`) exposed an alternating font-cache hit/miss pattern:

1. A launch measures fonts and persists trusted readings.
2. The next launch restores those readings as untrusted and correctly avoids DOM measurement.
3. If that session closes before the five-second revalidation timer, `serializeFontInfo` filters out the untrusted readings and returns `[]`.
4. The workbench writes `[]` over the last trusted persisted snapshot.
5. The following launch has no readings to restore and synchronously measures fonts again.

The same overwrite could occur after the five-second timer evicted restored readings in a window without an editor to remeasure them. The cache then appeared genuinely empty even though the current session had never produced a measurement.

Debugger breakpoints against the unchanged Insiders bundle confirmed the short-session lifecycle. Across seven launches after warm-up, cache behavior was:

`hit, miss, hit, miss, hit, miss, hit`

Each miss spent 25–27 renderer self samples in `_readFromDomElements`.

## Performance

An adjacent seven-run control reproduced the alternating behavior. A second seven-run series preserved the prior trusted JSON whenever a session attempted to replace it with `[]` without first producing a current-session measurement; all seven launches then hit the cache with zero font DOM-measurement samples.

| Series | Mean `didStartWorkbench` | Mean editor ready | Mean rendered edit |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Adjacent control hits | 1636.3 ms | 1689.8 ms | 2279.8 ms |
| Adjacent control misses | 1670.4 ms | 1718.5 ms | 2301.9 ms |
| Preserved cache | 1637.7 ms | 1689.0 ms | 2280.6 ms |

Within the adjacent control, a miss added:

- 34.1 ms to `code/didStartWorkbench`
- 28.7 ms to editor readiness
- 22.1 ms to rendered-edit responsiveness

The preserved series matched the control hit runs within 1.4 ms.

## Correctness

Restored measurements remain untrusted and the existing five-second eviction/revalidation behavior is unchanged. Provenance survives eviction only until the current session performs a measurement. Explicit cache invalidation and failed current-session measurements still serialize to `[]`, so stale persisted data is removed when the current environment indicates it should be.

The motivating main-process trace found 33 ASAR resolution attempts from `out/main.js` for seven unique specifier-parent pairs, including 15 resolutions of `@vscode/spdlog` and eight of `@vscode/policy-watcher`.

### Packaged resolver benchmark

40 alternating baseline/cached Electron runs, excluding five warmups, shaped as 33 import sites over seven unique contexts:

| Metric | Baseline | Cached | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Resolution workload median | 44.184 ms | 19.172 ms | **-25.012 ms / -56.61%** |
| Electron process median | 135.250 ms | 109.649 ms | **-25.601 ms / -18.93%** |
| Archive lookups | 33 | 7 | **-78.79%** |

### Main-process CPU profiles

Six packaged launches per variant, excluding one warmup:

| Metric | Baseline | Cached | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Active main CPU median | 378.879 ms | 360.334 ms | **-18.545 ms / -4.89%** |
| Attributed JavaScript median | 366.230 ms | 347.248 ms | **-18.982 ms / -5.18%** |
| `internalModuleStat` median | 12.605 ms | 4.880 ms | **-61.29%** |
| Profiled elapsed median | 1,926 ms | 1,892 ms | -1.77% |

The profiler adds roughly 33-35% overhead in this local Code OSS package, so the CPU deltas are more reliable than the profiled wall-time delta.

### Full packaged startup

Ten unprofiled launches per variant, excluding one warmup:

- warm median: 1,422 ms -> 1,418 ms (**-4 ms / -0.28%**)
- warm mean: 1,425.67 ms -> 1,408.67 ms (**-1.19%**)
- run CV: 1.89% baseline, 1.55% cached

The median wall-time change is below run variance, so this PR does **not** claim a statistically significant end-to-end startup improvement. The demonstrated benefit is reduced resolver and main-process CPU, including for later repeated imports.

For the full-package A/B, the baseline forced the generated cache lookup to miss while retaining the small key/map overhead; every other application byte was identical. The standalone resolver benchmark compares the exact pre-change and changed bootstrap revisions.

title: mcp: validate gallery server sources and package types
body:
## Summary

- restrict direct MCP server-document requests to the configured gallery origin and server path before performing network I/O
- disable redirect following for those requests and make the shared fetch request path honor `followRedirects: 0`
- validate package registry types at runtime in both supported gallery schema families and in the Copilot NuGet manifest mapper

## Why

MCP install links can open server documents by URL. Previously, the request was issued before confirming that the URL belonged to the configured gallery, and a non-gallery response could be processed by the compatibility serializer. In addition, older manifest shapes carried `registryType` values through without runtime validation, while the command mapper treated unknown values as executable names.

title: Keep every pending steering message instead of only the last
body:
`ChatState` models the two pending-message kinds inconsistently:

```ts
steeringMessage?: PendingMessage;     // a single slot
queuedMessages?: PendingMessage[];    // a list
```

The `chat/pendingMessageSet` reducer follows suit, overwriting any existing steering message with no id check, three lines above a queued branch that correctly finds by id and updates or appends:

```ts
if (action.kind === PendingMessageKind.Steering) {
    return { ...state, steeringMessage: entry };
}
const existing = state.queuedMessages ?? [];
const idx = existing.findIndex(m => m.id === action.id);
...
```

### What a user sees

Send one steering message, then a second before the first is consumed, and the first one's bubble disappears from the sidebar. It comes back later, when the model actually picks it up and it lands in the transcript.

Nothing is lost, because the agent was handed the first message before the second arrived. What is lost is the pending state, so the UI stops showing work the user has already queued. The reappearance is what makes it confusing: the message looks dropped, then returns from nowhere.

Nothing in the UI required this. The pending-request projection already builds a list carrying a kind per entry, and pushed at most one steering entry only because the state could hold at most one.

### What this changes

`steeringMessages` becomes a list, and the queued branch is mirrored in the three reducer sites, the state aggregation, the pending-request reconciliation and the projection. The provider hook becomes `setPendingMessages(chat, steeringMessages, queuedMessages)`, and Claude, Copilot and Codex each loop instead of handling a single optional message.

### Relationship to #333919

`setPendingMessages` is a state sync, so the provider is re-handed whatever is pending on every pending-message change. #333919 fixes that re-delivery for the Claude path, in `ClaudeSdkPipeline`, clearing on consumption and on abort.

This change makes that fix matter more rather than less: where re-delivery previously repeated one message, it now repeats each message in the list. It deliberately does not add a second guard of its own, since #333919 already places one better than this layer could. If these land in either order the result is the same, but #333919 is the one that should land first.

### Testing

New test in `agentSideEffects.test.ts` covering the reported case: two steering messages, both surviving in state and both reaching the agent.

`agentSideEffects`, `chatContributions`, `sessionServerTools` and `claudeAgent` run 624 passing. Two failures in `agentSideEffects` (shell confirmation rules and shell-language forwarding) reproduce identically on unmodified `main` in the same environment and are unrelated to this change.

title: Report chat activity from the Claude agent session
body:
AHP already has a progress channel, and the workbench already renders it well. `chat/activityChanged` carries a human-readable string, and the client turns it into a shimmering row with a stable id, so each update replaces the previous row rather than stacking another one, and the row hides itself as soon as real content follows.

Nothing produces it for Claude sessions. The only producer anywhere in the agent host is worktree creation (`AgentService._resolveWorktreeBeforeSend`), which is why "Creating isolated worktree" is the only activity a user ever sees. Every other turn reports no liveness at all, so a session waiting on MCP startup, on model latency, or inside a long-running tool is indistinguishable on screen from a hung one. That window can be minutes, and there is nothing in the chat to say otherwise.

### What this changes

`ClaudeAgentSession` now reports on the activity channel:

- **on `send`**, because nothing reaches the SDK stream until the CLI is up, and that pre-stream window is the worst of the dead time
- **on each `ChatToolCallStart`**, naming the tool being run
- **cleared on turn complete, cancel and error**, so a finished turn cannot strand a stale row

Labels are deduplicated, so an unchanged one is not re-sent.

### Why the session and not the stream mapper

`claudeMapSessionEvents` is deliberately a pure SDK-to-signal mapping, and says so where the MCP contributor enrichment was kept out of it. Activity is presentation state derived from the stream rather than a mapping of any single SDK event, so it sits with the other session-owned enrichment (`_enrichSignalWithCredits`, `_enrichSignalWithMcpContributor`). Doing it in the mapper would also have prepended a signal to arrays that its tests assert on with `deepStrictEqual`, for no behavioural gain.

### Notes

No protocol change: the action, the reducer and the rendering all already exist and are unchanged. The Copilot and Codex providers are untouched, and could adopt the same reporting separately.

title: agentHost: preserve archived state in surfaced session notifications
body:
## Summary

Fix archived sessions reappearing in the Agents Window after an agent-host catalog rescan. A full listing applied persisted archive/read metadata, but subsequent `root/sessionAdded` notifications for the **same sessions** did not. The client accepted those notifications and displayed previously archived sessions as active.

This was observed after an Insiders update/restart: the initial catalog correctly contained **470 sessions with only 9 unarchived**, then the host replayed **254 existing archived sessions without their archive bit**. All 254 session databases still contained `isArchived=true`; this was an incorrect notification, not a permanent unarchive or recreation of the sessions.

## Incident timeline and retained evidence

Investigated a Windows update to `1.137.0-insider` on **2026-09-05**:

- Before: [b6234bd71943c8a5caf5eef03bc4a8e49aef2698](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/b6234bd71943c8a5caf5eef03bc4a8e49aef2698).
- After: [de8cc55dae905582f191fdcfb6dff8c811a743c4](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/de8cc55dae905582f191fdcfb6dff8c811a743c4), built on September 4.

The table uses **UTC throughout**. Main-process logs establish the update/restart; retained AHP JSONL transport logs establish the session-list and notification sequence. The plain agent-host log no longer retained the beginning of startup.

| Time (UTC, September 5) | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| 09:39:57.086 | Last pre-update listing: 470 sessions, 9 unarchived. None of the unarchived sessions were last modified before August 15. |
| 09:40:53.341 | Update requested application quit/install. |
| 09:42:00.522 | Updated application started. |
| 09:42:08.851 | Another window subscribed to an unregistered `copilotcli:/untitled-...` session. |
| 09:42:31.584 | First post-update listing was still correct: 470 sessions, 9 unarchived; all 254 subsequently affected sessions were archived. |
| 09:42:32.389 to 09:42:36.383 | 254 `root/sessionAdded` notifications re-announced existing sessions with **status 33 instead of 97**. There were no new session IDs in this set. |
| 09:42:37.050 | The outstanding untitled-session subscription failed with `-32001`: `Session is not an adoptable legacy chat`. |
| 09:52:42.433 | A later full listing still reported all 254 affected sessions as archived. |

All 254 affected sessions were **created before August 15**; 249 were also **last modified before August 15**. Read-only inspection of their individual session databases found `isArchived='true'` and `isRead='true'` in **254/254**. There were no archive/unarchive commands in the three inspected startup client traces. The investigation did not modify user data.

### Relevant protocol excerpts

These are **redacted, pretty-printed field projections of actual JSONL records**, not complete payloads. Session URIs use stable placeholders; titles, prompts, project paths, working directories, connection IDs, and unrelated metadata are omitted. Full private log bundles are deliberately not attached.

**Another window -> host, 09:42:08.851Z** (that connection's line 30):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 4,
  "method": "subscribe",
  "params": { "channel": "copilotcli:/untitled-<draft>" },
  "_ahpLog": { "ts": "2026-09-05T09:42:08.851Z", "dir": "c2s" }
}
```

**Host -> Agents Window: initial list response, 09:42:31.584Z** (line 214; only one of the 470 items is shown):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 3,
  "result": {
    "items": [{
      "resource": "copilotcli:/<archived-session-A>",
      "status": 97,
      "createdAt": "2026-08-10T21:36:51.739Z",
      "modifiedAt": "2026-08-28T10:41:38.271Z"
    }]
  },
  "_ahpLog": { "ts": "2026-09-05T09:42:31.584Z", "dir": "s2c" }
}
```

**Host -> Agents Window: notification for that same session, 09:42:32.389Z** (line 216, the first of the 254 notifications on lines 216-469):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "method": "root/sessionAdded",
  "params": {
    "channel": "ahp-root://",
    "summary": {
      "resource": "copilotcli:/<archived-session-A>",
      "provider": "copilotcli",
      "status": 33,
      "createdAt": "2026-08-10T21:36:51.739Z",
      "modifiedAt": "2026-08-28T10:41:38.271Z"
    }
  },
  "_ahpLog": { "ts": "2026-09-05T09:42:32.389Z", "dir": "s2c" }
}
```

**Host -> the other window: completion of the untitled subscription, 09:42:37.050Z** (that connection's line 413):

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "id": 4,
  "error": {
    "code": -32001,
    "message": "Session is not an adoptable legacy chat: copilotcli:/untitled-<draft>"
  },
  "_ahpLog": { "ts": "2026-09-05T09:42:37.050Z", "dir": "s2c" }
}
```

The request/response correlation uses **connection + direction + request ID**, not request ID alone. This matters because the same connection can carry reverse-direction requests with reused numeric IDs.

The status difference is exactly the archive flag:

```text
97 = Idle (1) | IsRead (32) | IsArchived (64)
33 = Idle (1) | IsRead (32)
```

## Root cause

1. [The restore path](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b5e540e50a5fa6170cfa2f10e58a203683db1a94/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentService.ts#L5168) receives the unregistered, non-adoptable untitled-session probe. Before treating absence as authoritative, it calls `awaitCatalogReadable()`, which requests a readable provider catalog with `requireReadableCatalog=true`.
2. That can force [the legacy catalog migration/rescan](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b5e540e50a5fa6170cfa2f10e58a203683db1a94/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentService.ts#L1890), despite a persisted backfill marker. Registration is an UPSERT: success does **not** mean the session is new. Existing native sessions can therefore reach `_announceSurfacedSession`.
3. A session previously exposed by a full listing is not necessarily considered already *added*: [the state manager](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b5e540e50a5fa6170cfa2f10e58a203683db1a94/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostStateManager.ts#L880) separately tracks listed/published summaries and emitted add notifications. A correct initial listing consequently does not prevent this later announcement.
4. Before this fix, the announcement used provider metadata and forced the read bit, but **never overlaid persisted archive/read/title metadata**. Full listings did overlay it, explaining why the listings and database remained correct while the incremental notification was wrong.
5. [The Agents Window's notification handler](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b5e540e50a5fa6170cfa2f10e58a203683db1a94/src/vs/sessions/contrib/providers/agentHost/browser/baseAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts#L6055) updates an existing adapter from the incoming summary. Dropping `IsArchived` therefore resurfaces the old session. A request in another window can affect this window because they share the host.

The startup probe is present in the retained post-update trace and absent from the inspected first three minutes of the previous startup. The added regression reproduces the same **correct listing -> incorrect announcement -> correct listing/on-disk state** sequence using the public restore path.

## Fix

- Extract the full-listing metadata overlay into [a shared helper](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b5e540e50a5fa6170cfa2f10e58a203683db1a94/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentService.ts#L2119) and apply it [before incremental publication](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/b5e540e50a5fa6170cfa2f10e58a203683db1a94/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentService.ts#L2739). Most production diff lines move the existing overlay rather than introduce a second implementation.
- Preserve persisted archive/read flags, custom titles, host-owned metadata, and changes summaries. Keep the legacy `isDone` fallback, with an explicit `isArchived` value taking precedence.
- Apply the legacy default-read behavior **before** the overlay, so an explicitly stored unread state is not overridden.
- Recheck visibility, tombstones, and live state after the asynchronous read. Continue filtering internal chat backings and dispose database references.
- If a metadata read throws, do not publish a guessed summary; release the announcement reservation so retry remains possible. Existing full-list error handling is unchanged.

This fixes the publication boundary rather than adding an age filter, suppressing every duplicate notification, changing migration defaults, or rewriting archived sessions. **No user-data repair is required.**

## Recent PR review / attribution limits

The investigation also reviewed relevant PRs merged in the preceding two days:

| PR | Merged (UTC) | Finding |
| --- | --- | --- |
| #334250 - workspace-less session conversion | September 4, 10:06 | No evidence establishes it as the cause of this notification bug. |
| #334518 - migration setting consolidation/default true | September 4, 15:53 | This is the installed tip, but this user's effective migration setting was already true before updating. |
| #332824 - auth replay/provider shutdown | September 3, 19:04 | A startup timing effect is possible but not established by the retained evidence. |
| #334449 - experiment defaults on assignment refetch | September 4, 10:41 | The logs do not support a migration-setting flip for this user. |

Both startups forwarded:

```json
{
  "migrateLegacyCopilotCliEnabled": true,
  "showExternalSessions": "recent"
}
```

The actual before/after build comparison found `_migrateLegacyProviderChats`, `_announceSurfacedSession`, `_surfacedSessionSummary`, `_awaitInitialProviderMigrationForProvider`, `_setupChatDiscoveryForProvider`, and the state-manager listing/announcement methods unchanged.

**Conclusion:** this is an existing catalog-publication bug exposed during this restart, not evidence that the update intentionally unarchived old sessions. The missing-draft probe/rescan is observed and reproducible; the retained evidence does **not** identify which recent PR, if any, caused that probe to occur.

## Regression coverage and validation

title: chat: mount MCP App webview in the window it is rendered in
body:
Fixes #331140

The root cause was already correctly identified by @kboyce-cloud in the issue report. This PR confirms that analysis independently, adds the ordering detail that makes a minimal fix sufficient, and applies it.

## Problem

An MCP App card (`ui://` resource, `text/html;profile=mcp-app`) renders blank when the chat is in an auxiliary window (`workbench.action.newChatWindow`). No app JS executes. Scrolling the card out of view and back makes it appear.

## Root cause

`ChatMcpAppModel` mounts its webview from the constructor:

```ts
const targetWindow = dom.getWindow(this._container);
this._webview.mountTo(this._container, targetWindow);
```

At that moment the container is still detached — `ChatMcpAppSubPart` builds `div.mcp-app-part` with `dom.$` and constructs the model before that node is inserted into the tree. `dom.getWindow` falls back to the element's `ownerDocument`, which is the main document, so `targetWindow` is the main window even when the card is being rendered into an auxiliary one.

`WebviewElement.mountTo` uses that window for three things: `_windowId`, the `parentOriginHash` input, and `_registerMessageHandler`. With the handler on the main window, the iframe's handshake `postMessage` (which goes to *its* parent, the auxiliary window) is never observed, the MessagePort is never established, and the queued `content` message carrying the app HTML is never delivered. Hence a blank card and no app JS.

The scroll workaround works because re-rendering routes through `onDidRemount` → `ChatMcpAppModel.remount()` → `reinitializeAfterDismount()`, which re-runs `mountTo(this.element.parentElement, getWindow(this.element))` with the element attached — and so reads the correct window.

## Fix

Defer the mount by one microtask and resolve the window then.

The issue notes that `reinitializeAfterDismount` already does the right thing; what makes a microtask sufficient — rather than an attach observer or post-attach callback plumbing — is that every caller attaches the container synchronously, in the same task that constructs the model:

- `chatListRenderer.ts` constructs the content part (~L2286) and appends `newPart.domNode` to the content container (~L2312) in one pass.
- `chatToolInvocationPart.ts` creates the sub-part and calls `appDomNode.replaceWith(this.mcpAppPart.value.domNode)` in the same autorun.
- `ListView.insertItemInDOM` inserts the row's `domNode` into `rowsContainer` *before* invoking `renderer.renderElement`, so the ancestor chain is already in the correct document during render.

By the time the microtask runs, the container is attached and `getWindow` reports the window the webview actually lives in. Nothing is lost by mounting a microtask later: `WebviewElement` queues `_send` calls while in the `Initializing` state, which is precisely the mechanism the existing `reinitializeAfterDismount` path relies on. If some future caller were to attach across an `await`, the microtask would resolve the main window — no worse than today, and still corrected by the existing remount paths.

Note the main-window case has the same ordering bug; it just happens to guess right, since the fallback window and the intended window coincide.

## What I verified, and what I did not

**Verified:** the bug reproduces on VS Code 1.136.1 stable with a remote HTTP MCP server serving an MCP App resource — renders in the sidebar and in an editor tab, blank in a new chat window, with only the iframe sandbox warning in the auxiliary window's console. The code paths and orderings described above were read against this commit.

**Not verified:** I was not able to build and run this patch. **The change is untested at runtime** — it is reasoned from the source, not observed working in a dev build. Please treat it accordingly; I'm happy to iterate if a maintainer can exercise it.

## Related, not addressed here

Two other sites resolve a window from a possibly-detached node and are likely to have the same latent problem. I left them out to keep this scoped to the reported bug:

- `chatMcpAppSubPart.ts` — `dom.getWindow(this.domNode)` is used for `innerHeight` (max webview height) and to register the `resize` listener, on the same detached node. In an auxiliary window this yields the main window's height and a listener on the wrong window. It degrades quietly rather than blanking.
- `chatOutputItemRenderer.ts` — `webview.mountTo(parent, getWindow(parent))` at render time, for `ChatToolOutputSubPart`. I could not construct a repro for this one, so I have not touched it.
