title: sessions: measure and unblock V3 onboarding GitHub personalization
body:
## Why

The V3 new-session onboarding personalizes its 3 prompt options with GitHub items (assigned issues, authored PRs with conflicts / failing CI / unresolved review comments), falling back to standard options.

Analysis of experiment `f716301b` over 3 weeks and ~780k users found that, restricted to users with a resolved GitHub repository who saw the options widget (222,470 impressions):

- **61.0%** timed out with zero GitHub options
- **~9.4%** saw at least one GitHub option (only **0.17%** saw a full 3/3 set)
- **29.6%** got all-standard options

And we could not measure *how* badly, because `fallbackReason` was only set to `'none'` when all 3 slots were GitHub — so a widget with 2 real GitHub issues logged identically to one with zero. That blind spot covered 81% of impressions.

The root cause of the timeouts is that per-stage budgets could exceed the total budget: the PR chain was summary(5s) → review(4s) = 9s, with repository resolution also inside the same 10s budget.

## Telemetry

Additive only — existing field names and values are emitted in the same situations, so live dashboards keep working.

`onboarding.promptStrategy` gains:

| Field | Question it answers |
|---|---|
| `gitHubOptionCount` | How many of the 3 slots were actually GitHub items — closes the main blind spot |
| `candidatesFound` | Pre-truncation count: "repo has nothing" vs "found items but were too slow" |
| `lookupDurationMs` | Total lookup time (plumbed from the value the code already computed for logging) |
| `repositoryMs`, `issueSummaryMs`, `issueLinkageMs`, `prSummaryMs`, `prReviewMs` | Which stage is actually slow |
| `issueSummaryOutcome`, `issueLinkageOutcome`, `prSummaryOutcome`, `prReviewOutcome` | Per-stage outcome, so "issues succeeded, PRs timed out" is distinguishable from total failure |
| `timedOutStage` | Which stage was in flight when the total budget expired |

`onboarding.promptOptionInteraction` gains `optionIndex` and `optionKindsShown`, making a true per-option CTR computable — today "implementFeature is most picked" is confounded with it being almost always present.

Both events gain a shared `impressionId`, so they can be joined per impression instead of on `DevDeviceId`, which is lossy for devices with multiple impressions.

Also splits the overloaded `noCandidate` — it meant both "no composer available" (an infra bug) and "lookup returned nothing" (a data outcome). The former is now `noComposer`.

**Privacy:** bounded categories and counts only. No issue/PR titles, URLs, numbers, repository names or prompt text. Every numeric has `isMeasurement: true`.

## Latency

`totalMs` stays at 10s.

1. **Publish issue candidates before linkage.** Linkage exists only to filter out issues that already have linked PRs, so a slow linkage call was discarding issues we already held.
2. **Review-thread enrichment off the critical path.** It fired N parallel lookups after a summary to produce `githubPRComments` — 30 selections, 0.37% of all picks — while `githubIssue` (the most-picked GitHub option) is the cheapest to fetch. The budget was being spent inversely to user value. It can now only refine, never delay first paint.
3. **Rebalanced sub-budgets** to `summaryMs: 4_000, linkageMs: 1_500, reviewMs: 3_000`. The issue and PR chains run concurrently under `Promise.all`, so the worst case for timed lookups is `max(4_000+1_500, 4_000+3_000) = 7_000ms`, leaving ~3s for repository resolution and rendering. Repository resolution has no budget of its own and a workspace change restarts the chain; both are bounded only by the `totalMs` race, and the comment on the constant says so rather than asserting a tighter bound than the code has.
4. **Streaming.** The 3 standard options are painted immediately and slots are replaced as GitHub items arrive, instead of blocking first paint on the whole lookup. Beyond timeouts, this also addresses V3's ~17pp tour-reach deficit versus V2.

## API change

`INewSessionPromptOptionsController.resolve` gains an optional progress callback:

```ts
export type NewSessionPromptOptionsProgress = (state: NewSessionPromptOptionsState) => boolean;

resolve(token: CancellationToken, progress?: NewSessionPromptOptionsProgress): Promise<NewSessionPromptOptionsState>;
```

Additive and optional, so existing callers are unaffected. It returns `boolean` rather than `void` deliberately: the composer refuses late updates while the user is already acting on the options, and the runner needs to know that so interaction telemetry describes what was actually rendered.

## Notes for reviewers

The streaming path has three subtle interactions that are each covered by a test that fails without its fix:

- `_renderedPromptOptions` is reset per `resolve`, not per `run`. `newChatWidget` calls `refreshPromptOptions()` on every workspace change against the same runner, and a per-run reset made the second refresh compare against the previous refresh's final set — suppressing first paint entirely in exactly the all-standard case this PR targets.
- `_promptOptionsSelected` is set at the *start* of `selectOption`, not in `onDidSelectOption`. The widget only reports a selection after the 2.5s prompt animation completes; a streamed update in that window would clear the selection and leave every option `aria-disabled`.
- The runner commits `_renderedPromptOptions` only when the composer accepted the update, so `optionIndex` / `optionKindsShown` can never describe options the user never saw.

`impressionId` is regenerated per `run`, not per `resolve`: strategy telemetry is emitted once per run, so a per-resolve id would orphan interaction events from any strategy event.

## Validation

- `scripts\test.bat --grep "NewSession"` → **93 passing**, 0 failing
- `npm run typecheck-client` → clean for `sessions/contrib`
- `eslint` → clean
- Code hygiene → clean on changed files (the repo-wide `npm run hygiene` task fails on an unrelated pre-existing Windows path bug in `checkPackageJSON`, reproducible on an untouched checkout; no `package.json` is touched here)

New test coverage: partial GitHub candidate counts, the early issue publish, streaming updates arriving after first paint, budget-stage attribution, re-resolve after a workspace change, and the composer refusing late updates.

## Kusto queries this makes answerable

- Distribution of `gitHubOptionCount` (0/1/2/3) — the true personalization rate, vs today's binary
- Per-stage p50/p95 latency and timeout rate, attributing the 61% bucket to `repository` vs `prSummary` vs `prReview`
- `candidatesFound == 0` vs `candidatesFound > gitHubOptionCount` — "nothing to show" vs "found more than we could show"
- Partial-success cohorts, e.g. `issueSummaryOutcome == 'success' and prSummaryOutcome == 'timeout'`
- True per-option CTR, joining `optionKindsShown` impressions with `option` selections
- Position bias: selections by `optionIndex`, controlling for slot content
- Impression-level funnel joined on `impressionId`

title: Refresh markdown preview html before a hidden panel is rebuilt
body:
Fixes #271233
Part of #265277

Several reports in those issues describe the same sequence: the preview updates correctly while it is visible, the user switches to another tab and back, and the preview shows the content from before the update. This applies to the dynamic preview (`markdown.showPreview`) and to the `vscode.markdown.preview.editor` custom editor, with edits made in VS Code as well as with files overwritten on disk.

### Root cause

`MarkdownPreview` applies updates made while the panel is visible by posting an `updateContent` message to the webview, and leaves `webview.html` untouched. Neither preview uses `retainContextWhenHidden`, so VS Code discards the webview when the panel is hidden and rebuilds it from `webview.html` when the panel is revealed. That html is whatever the last full render produced, so every update applied through `updateContent` since then is lost on reveal. Nothing in the preview reacts to the panel being hidden, and the version check in `#updatePreview` keeps a later refresh from re-rendering unchanged content.

### Fix

- Track whether `webview.html` is behind what the webview shows (`#webviewHtmlOutOfDate`).
- When the panel is hidden while the html is behind, request a forced refresh, which goes through the existing full render path and brings `webview.html` up to date before the panel can be revealed. Panels that never received an in-place update, and panels updated while hidden (which already re-render fully), are unaffected.
- If the panel is hidden while an in-place update is still rendering, the update requests the forced refresh itself: the hide event found the html up to date and scheduled nothing, and the webview the message was meant for is already gone.
- `refresh(true)` now keeps its force flag when an update is already scheduled. Before, a forced refresh requested while the 300 ms throttle timer was pending was silently downgraded to a regular update.

### Verification

Measured by driving the extension from source in Insiders 1.137.0-insider (de8cc55dae) with `--extensionDevelopmentPath`, reading the rendered `.markdown-body` text of the preview iframe over the remote debugging port after each step. "hidden" reads as no preview iframe at all, which is the webview being discarded.

| Scenario | Step | main (42b37b7a) | with this change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Dynamic preview, file overwritten on disk while visible, tab switch | 1 preview opened | D1-A | D1-A |
| | 2 after external write | D1-B | D1-B |
| | 3 preview hidden behind another tab | hidden | hidden |
| | 4 preview tab shown again | **D1-A (stale)** | D1-B |
| Dynamic preview, edit + save in a text editor, tab switch | 1 preview opened | D1-A | D1-A |
| | 2 after edit and save | D1-C | D1-C |
| | 3 preview hidden behind another tab | hidden | hidden |
| | 4 preview tab shown again | **D1-A (stale)** | D1-C |
| Dynamic preview, file overwritten while hidden (control) | 1 preview opened | D1-A | D1-A |
| | 2 preview tab shown after the hidden write | D1-D | D1-D |
| `vscode.markdown.preview.editor`, file overwritten on disk while visible, tab switch | 1 editor opened | D1-A | D1-A |
| | 2 after external write | D1-E | D1-E |
| | 3 editor hidden behind another tab | hidden | hidden |
| | 4 editor tab shown again | **D1-A (stale)** | D1-E |

The new tests in `src/test/preview.test.ts` revive a `DynamicMarkdownPreview` on a real webview panel. The first applies an edit while the panel is visible, hides the panel behind a text editor and asserts that `webview.html` catches up; it fails on main at that last assertion and passes with this change. The second holds the in-place render of an edit, hides the panel while it is in flight, releases the render and asserts the same; it fails when the branch in `#updateWebviewContent` is removed. The third makes a further edit so a regular refresh is pending, hides and re-reveals the panel, and asserts the reveal still gets a full reload. The full markdown-language-features suite passes (99 tests, 1 skipped).

### Related issues

- #271233 is this sequence exactly (modify the file, hide the preview behind another editor in the same group, show it again). The later comment there about closing and reopening the preview is a different mechanism, see below.
- #165188 (closed as a duplicate of #147718) and #244328 (closed) describe the same tab-switch sequence.
- #331900, #194421 and #316067 are about a preview that is closed and reopened, or opened fresh, showing old content. The webview is created new in those flows, so this change does not apply; #332081 and #333712 target that path.

### Relation to the other open PRs

- #308427 (`refresh()` when the panel becomes visible, claims to fix #271233) calls the non-forced `refresh()` of the base class. The document version has not changed since the in-place update, so `#updatePreview` returns at the version check and `webview.html` stays stale. Measured with that diff applied on top of 1.128.0: step 4 of the first scenario above still shows D1-A.
- #166932 (`refresh()` when the dynamic preview becomes inactive, 2022) goes through `DynamicMarkdownPreview.refresh()`, which is forced, so it does fix the dynamic preview (steps 4 above render D1-B and D1-C with it). It reloads the whole page every time the preview loses focus, whether or not anything changed, which is the concern raised in its review, and it does not cover `vscode.markdown.preview.editor` (step 4 of the last scenario stays D1-A). This change reloads only when an in-place update has actually happened and covers both previews.
- #307245 defers refreshes while the panel is hidden and re-renders on reveal only if a change arrived while hidden. It does not change what happens to updates applied before the hide, so the two changes are independent.
- #333712 (identity-aware `PreviewDocumentVersion.equals`) and #332081 (token cache identity) address refreshes being skipped while the preview is visible; no overlap. #316756 removes the watcher guard for documents VS Code already tracks; it does not change what a hidden panel is rebuilt from, so the tab-switch case above stays stale with it.

title: Fix C/C++ auto-indent after brace-less if/for/while/else (#43244)
body:
## Fixes #43244

JS, TS, and PHP already indent the line following a brace-less `if`/`for`/`while`/`else` via `indentNextLinePattern` in their `language-configuration.json` (added in #209038 / #251465 and follow-ups). The `cpp` language configuration (shared by `c`, `cpp`, and `cuda-cpp`) already has the *matching* outdent-after-single-statement `onEnterRule`, but never got the `indentNextLinePattern` that triggers the initial indent, so today:

```c
if (condition)
<Enter> // does not indent, unlike JS/TS/PHP
```

This has been reported repeatedly in #43244 since 2018 (e.g. "This also applies to C/C++/D, as well" and a comment as recent as June 2025 asking specifically about C), but only JS/TS/PHP ever received the fix.

### Change

Adds the same `indentNextLinePattern` already shipped for JS/TS/PHP to `extensions/cpp/language-configuration.json`:

```json
"indentNextLinePattern": {
    "pattern": "^\\s*(((else ?)?if|for|while)\\s*\\(.*\\)\\s*|else\\s*)$"
}
```

This is the exact same pattern used as the `previousLineText` of the existing outdent `onEnterRule` in this same file, so the two rules are now consistent with each other and with the JS/TS/PHP configs.

### Testing

`shouldIncrease`/`shouldDecrease`/`shouldIndentNextLine` (src/vs/editor/common/languages/supports/indentRules.ts) are driven purely by these regexes with no language-specific code, so no engine changes are needed. I verified the new pattern against representative C/C++ lines (`if (x)`, `else if (x)`, `for (...)`, `while (...)`, `else`, brace/one-line/comment negatives) against the exact regex used by the engine — all matched as expected, mirroring the already-shipped JS/TS/PHP behavior.

I wasn't able to spin up a full Electron build in my environment to record a GIF, but happy to add one if a maintainer can confirm the expected behavior manually or point me at the fastest local-build path for a quick sanity check.

title: terminal: do not buffer local pty events that have no IPC client
body:
Fixes #328885

## Problem

The main process grows with terminal output until V8's ~4 GB heap limit and crashes, closing every window at once. `ProxyChannel.fromService` wraps every `on*` property of a service in an eager `Event.buffer` (`src/vs/base/parts/ipc/common/ipc.ts`) that keeps each emission until the first client listens. The `TerminalIpcChannels.LocalPty` channel registered in `app.ts` exposes `PtyHostService`, and a window never listens to the seven `IPtyService` events over it: it consumes them over the direct message port to the pty host (`TerminalIpcChannels.PtyHostWindow`, `localTerminalBackend.ts`). So the main process archived every `onProcessData` chunk for the lifetime of the session.

The pty host and the remote server do not leak by this path: the main process subscribes to the pty host's events as soon as it connects, and `RemoteTerminalChannel.listen` hands events out directly.

## Fix

- Register the channel with `unbufferedEvents` for the `IPtyService` events, the mechanism #328535 introduced for `onDidBlurMainWindow`. The five `IPtyHostController` events stay buffered, those do have a client on this channel.
- `ptyServiceEvents` lives next to `IPtyService` and is exhaustive by type (`satisfies Record<..., true>`): adding an event to the interface without listing it does not compile.
- The registration lives in `createLocalPtyChannel`, so a test can build the very channel production builds.

## Tests

`src/vs/platform/terminal/test/node/ptyHostService.test.ts`:
- every `on*` property of `PtyHostService` is either an `IPtyService` or an `IPtyHostController` event, reflected the way `fromService` does;
- the channel has no listener on any `IPtyService` event before a client asks for it, and a client who asks gets live events without a backlog.

Each guard was checked against its mutation: removing a name from the constant fails to compile, adding an `on*` to the class fails the first test, dropping `unbufferedEvents` from the factory fails the second.

## How to test manually

Open a few integrated terminals producing heavy output (for example `yes | head -c 500M`) and watch the private bytes of the main process. Before this change they grow with the output and never come back; after it they stay flat.

A general cap for `Event.buffer`, as defence in depth for any `fromService` channel with an unconsumed event, is a possible follow-up. This PR is deliberately limited to the channel that leaks.

title: Scope MCP tool availability to referenced servers only
body:
## Description

Fixes #334569 — MCP tool calls intermittently rejected with "disabled by the user" while the cache shows enabled and the server log shows execution.

**This is the conservative alternative to #334641.** Both PRs fix the same root cause; this one scopes the fix to the **referenced MCP server only**, preserving the authorization boundary. Maintainers can choose either approach (see the issue for the comparison).

### Root Cause

In **ask mode**, MCP tools can only enter `availableTools` via `request.toolReferences` (the `askAgentToolFilter` in `askAgentIntent.ts`). When the user references an MCP server (via the `@` picker), the toolset is expanded into a **static snapshot** at request-parse time (`chatRequestParser.ts`):

```ts
const value = Array.from(toolset.getTools()).map(t => ...);
```

MCP servers connect and discover their tools **asynchronously**. If the request is parsed while discovery is still in progress, the snapshot only contains the tools registered up to that point. Tools discovered later are registered in the tools service but never enter `availableTools` — the model's calls to them are rejected with `Tool ... is currently disabled by the user`.

### Fix (scoped to the referenced server)

In `askAgentIntent.ts`:

1. **Compute the set of referenced MCP servers** from `request.toolReferences` — for each referenced tool that is currently registered with an `LanguageModelToolMCPSource`, add that server's identity (label + name) to the set.
2. **In the filter**, a currently-registered MCP tool is enabled **only if it belongs to one of the referenced servers** (matching via `LanguageModelToolMCPSource`). Tools from other MCP servers the user never referenced stay unavailable — the authorization boundary is preserved.

```ts
const referencedMcpServerKeys = new Set<string>();
for (const ref of request.toolReferences) {
    const referencedTool = toolsService.getTool(ref.name);
    const source = referencedTool?.source;
    if (source instanceof LanguageModelToolMCPSource) {
        referencedMcpServerKeys.add(mcpServerKey(source.label, source.name));
    }
}
```

### Why not just enable all MCP tools (see #334641)

The request snapshot is both a timing mechanism *and* an **authorization boundary**: it limits the model to the servers the user explicitly referenced. Enabling every `mcp`-tagged tool whenever the user references *any* MCP server would expose the tools of all configured MCP servers (e.g. in a multi-server setup, referencing Firefox would also expose an unrelated IDA/GitKraken server's tools). This PR fixes the timing issue without widening that boundary.

### Validation

- `askAgentIntent.spec.ts` — 8 unit tests covering:
  - codesearch-tagged and directly referenced tools still included
  - MCP tools of a **referenced** server included (snapshot case)
  - MCP tools of a **non-referenced** server **excluded**
  - MCP tools without a resolvable source excluded (conservative fallback)
  - no references / non-MCP references → MCP tools excluded
- All 8 tests pass (`vitest run src/extension/intents/test/node/askAgentIntent.spec.ts`).

### Related

- Issue: #334569
- Alternative fix: #334641

title: terminal: avoid detached terminal listener leaks
body:
## Summary

- Prevents detached terminals from adding one theme listener and one configuration listener per instance.
- Eliminates listener leak warnings when agent and chat workflows create many detached terminals.
- Preserves live theme, configuration, and decoration updates through the existing centralized detached-terminal listeners.

<details>
<summary>Technical context for AI-assisted review</summary>

### Intent and previous behavior

Detached terminals skip `XtermTerminal` global service listeners because `TerminalService` forwards theme, configuration, and log-level changes to all detached instances. However, every detached terminal still creates a `DecorationAddon`, and that addon independently subscribed to the global theme and configuration services. Agent and chat workflows can keep enough detached terminal renderers alive to cross the listener leak threshold even though the main terminal listeners were already centralized.

### Implementation

`DecorationAddon` now accepts whether it should register global service listeners. Regular terminals retain the existing subscriptions. Detached terminals disable them, and the centralized `XtermTerminal.updateTheme()` and `updateConfig()` paths explicitly refresh decoration styles, layouts, capability listeners, and visibility.

A regression test constructs an addon with global listeners disabled and verifies that the theme service listener count does not increase.

### Behavior and constraints

- Regular terminal listener behavior remains unchanged.
- Detached terminals continue reacting to theme and relevant configuration changes through `TerminalService` existing centralized forwarding.
- Decoration refreshes remain owned by `DecorationAddon`; `XtermTerminal` only invokes the new public refresh entry points.
- Terminal disposal semantics and detached-terminal tracking are unchanged.

### Review context

The key review point is parity between the addon former direct subscriptions and the centralized detached-terminal refresh path. The centralized configuration handler already filters to terminal and decoration-related settings before calling `updateConfig()` or `updateTheme()`.

</details>

title: GitHub: cache and prioritize owned clone results
body:
Related to #141754.

This is a broader alternative to #310787. That PR fixes the immediate merge
ordering problem; this draft also explores making repository suggestions local-first
and persistent so repeated searches do not wait for GitHub again.

## Summary

- Add an optional Git Base remote-source change event so providers can return
  locally available results immediately and publish asynchronous updates later.
- Cache repository full names personally owned by the authenticated GitHub user in
  extension global storage. The cache is account-specific, written atomically, and
  contains no descriptions, star counts, or tokens.
- Rank personal repositories by exact name, prefix, then substring before matching
  public-search results.
- Debounce and cancel obsolete GitHub searches, cache completed searches briefly,
  and locally re-filter their results as the query changes.
- Validate the owned-repository cache hourly with an ETag and perform a full refresh
  daily. Clear account-specific state on account changes or sign-out.

## Motivation

The current clone picker waits for remote results and can rank a popular public
repository above a much more relevant personal repository. Repeating or narrowing a
query can also repeat the wait or temporarily remove still-valid suggestions.

This approach downloads the authenticated user's personally owned repository names
once, keeps them on disk, and filters/ranks them synchronously on every keystroke.
Public search remains available as a progressively loaded fallback.

## Scope question

This draft intentionally gives personally owned repositories priority over
organization and unrelated public repositories. It does not yet maintain an
organization-membership cache, so organization repositories discovered through
public search are ranked by match quality rather than membership. Before marking
this ready, I would like maintainer guidance on whether organization membership
should also be cached or exposed as a separate picker path, as discussed in
#141754.

## Testing

- GitHub remote-source provider tests: 16 passing.
- Git Base extension integration tests: 14 passing.
- TypeScript compilation for both changed extensions.
- ESLint on all changed TypeScript implementation/test files.
- Manual testing in an Extension Development Host with my GitHub account:
  - exact, prefix, and substring searches;
  - switching repeatedly between cached queries;
  - narrowing `transaction` to `transactio` without losing compatible results;
  - personal repositories ranking above organization/public results;
  - restart followed by an immediate result from the disk cache.

The full monorepo test suite has not been run.

## AI assistance disclosure

Most of this implementation was produced by OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol with high reasoning
effort in Codex, under my supervision. I directed the behavior and performed several
functional and UX testing passes with my own GitHub account, but I have not yet done
a thorough line-by-line human code review. The PR is therefore intentionally a draft
while the approach and implementation receive closer review.

title: agentHost: route MCP auth during session initialization
body:
Fixes #329223

## Root cause

The Copilot runtime intentionally keeps host-injected MCP bearer tokens session-scoped: the embedding host owns refresh, revocation, persistence, and per-server consent. Agent Host therefore has to deliver the workbench's persisted grant to every SDK session that challenges.

Two races could lose that delivery:

1. A `CopilotAgentSession` can issue `onMcpAuthRequest` while `initializeSession()` is still running. The session was added to `_chatEntriesBySdkId` only after initialization completed, while `handleAuthenticationToken()` searched only that live map.
2. Workbench silent MCP authentication coalesced by server identity across sessions. A session challenging after the shared operation's host-side fan-out had been snapshotted reused the promise but did not perform its own delivery.

## Before/after evidence

### Before — shipped Insiders, pre-fix

A real new Agent Host chat on the affected build immediately challenged again for an MCP whose VS Code authentication session and access grant already existed:

```text
[Copilot:<new-session>] MCP server 'vscode-slack' requires authentication for https://mcp.slack.com
[AgentHost] MCP authentication succeeded for vscode-slack
```

The same startup trace contained repeated `requires authentication` → renderer token-delivery pairs for other previously authorized MCPs. This shows that persistence was intact in the workbench, but the token still had to be recovered again for each new SDK session—and could be lost in the initialization/coalescing races above.

### After — this branch

#### Real signed-in Slack OAuth E2E

I loaded an isolated plugin containing only the `github-slack` MCP definition, authorized it once through the real Slack browser OAuth flow, and then started two brand-new Agent Host sessions. Isolating the definition prevents a second Slack client registration from changing the provider identity during the test.

Before the one-time authorization, VS Code correctly showed the server as requiring authentication. After authorization, both later sessions completed without an auth card, browser redirect, or other user interaction, and the server remained running:

| Before one-time authorization | After authorization and two new sessions |
|---|---|
| ![github-slack requires authentication](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/076dc626-0f39-47e6-8c7f-c2e27a49f62b) | ![github-slack remains running](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7a38b032-2c02-40bb-b136-40837ee4f832) |

The two later sessions are visible here as separate completed chats:

![Two new sessions completed without another MCP authentication prompt](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e19c300c-8267-4ca6-81ec-9c12b4909e85)

Each new SDK session still issued its expected session-scoped challenge. The workbench silently resolved that challenge from the persisted grant, and Slack reached `connected (ready)` in 326 ms and 350 ms respectively:

```text
Session 1
```

title: agentHost: rotate stale OTel session anchors
body:
## Problem

Agent Host emits one zero-duration `vscode.agent_host.session` span per session and parents every provider span under it for the session's whole lifetime. Some OTLP consumers keep the mapping needed to resolve that parent only for a limited time. Once it expires, they accept later child spans with HTTP 200 and never show them. I reproduced this with LangSmith: spans present in the local SQLite store were missing from the project.

## Behavior change

- Before each provider turn, the host re-exports the session's current anchor. Re-sending the identical span restores the consumer's parent mapping after an idle period.
- After 12 hours, the host issues a fresh anchor with a new span id and timestamp under the same trace id, keeping the anchor inside ingestion windows without rewriting history.
- Copilot and Codex pick up the current anchor at each turn. Claude gets it through its subprocess environment, so a rotated anchor triggers the existing resume-based rebuild before the next turn.
- Anchors are keyed by the chat's own resource. Peer and side chats keep one anchor each; a chat's rotation check and its rebuild always agree on that key.

## Trade-offs

- A consumer whose mapping has already expired may show a rotated anchor as the start of a new trace. Later spans stay visible instead of being dropped.
- Anchor re-export is queued, never awaited. In DB mode with an OTLP/HTTP JSON endpoint it shares the serialized forwarder with provider spans and arrives first. In pass-through mode the runtime exports on its own connection and ordering is best-effort.

Separate from github/copilot-cli#4726.

## Validation

- `tsc6 --noEmit` and `gulp compile-client` clean
- `agentHostOTelService.integrationTest.ts` and `claudeAgent.test.ts`: 308 passing, covering replay, rotation, Claude rebind, and peer-chat keying

body:
I'm the author of jschardet and this is a completely new version that follows chardet's 7.x rewrite from scratch. Its main benefits are much improved accuracy across a wider range of supported encodings, alongside substantial memory and performance improvements. It's now written in TypeScript and ships with ESM support. This release also closes all but one of jschardet's open issues, most of which originated from vscode reports.

The main goal of this PR is to gauge interest in the upgrade and see whether this is a direction you'd like to take. I haven't released a stable v4.0.0 yet but I've been publishing release candidates in the form of v4.0.0-rc.X.

Main improvements over 3.1.4:

    Metric                     jschardet 3.1.4   jschardet 4.0.0(-rc.3)
    Accuracy (3,138 files)     43.1%             99.4%
    Speed                      126 files/s       780 files/s
    Language detection         —                 93.4%
    Peak memory                831.8 MiB         85.5 MiB
    Supported encodings        ~30               86
    MIME type detection        no                yes
    License                    LGPL-2.1+         0BSD

The trade-offs: the minified bundle grows from ~334 to ~1,141 KiB
(691 KiB gzipped) and cold start from ~30 to ~109 ms.

Detection changes (encoding.ts):
- jschardet >= 4 accepts a Uint8Array directly, in Node and the browser
  alike, so the manual latin1 round-trip (encodeLatin1) is no longer
  needed and is removed.
- Map jschardet's cp932/cp949 outputs onto iconv-lite's shiftjis/euckr.
- Widen the local `guessed` type to `{ encoding: string | null }` to match
  v4's detect() return type (its `encoding` is `string | null`).

Test fixtures:
- Change some.shiftjis.1.txt's trailing text (こんにちは -> 日本語)
  because v4 now detects the old sample as Shift-JIS even without
  candidate encodings, making the test vacuous; the new sample is
  Windows-1252 on its own and Shift-JIS with candidates, restoring the
  contrast.
- Correct some.shiftjis.1.txt's in-memory copy in files.ts: the
  Shift-JIS lead byte 0x82 had been written as the decimal literal 82
  (0x52), so the bytes never matched the on-disk file. v4 declines to
  guess the garbage, which v3 happened to tolerate.

title: Spare a background subagent's in-flight tool call from the turn-end wipe
body:
`clearPending` drops all cross-message tool attribution on every `result` envelope. A background subagent outlives the turn that spawned it, so its inner tool call is still in flight and its result is still coming, but its entry is wiped along with the genuinely orphaned ones.

## Why it matters

The registry exists because a `tool_use` and its `tool_result` arrive in different SDK messages, so the tool name, parsed input and invocation message have to survive between them. Once the entry is gone, the late result renders with the generic past-tense message instead of the real one, and live output diverges from what replay produces from the same transcript.

## The precedent

`drainForegroundSpawns` is called from `mapResult` two lines after `clearPendingToolCalls`, and already makes exactly this distinction:

> Turn-end cleanup: remove and return foreground spawns whose completion never closed them. Background spawns survive across turns by design (their completion arrives later via `system.task_notification`).

The subagent registry keeps that state; the tool call registry simply never consulted it.

## The change

`clearPending` takes an optional lookup and skips entries whose parent spawn is background, leaving every other orphan drained and warned exactly as before. The lookup is declared as a narrow local interface rather than importing the subagent registry, to avoid a cycle between the two modules. `clearPendingToolCalls` already runs before `drainForegroundSpawns`, so the spawn and its inner edges are still present when the check happens.

## Tests

- `clearPending spares an inner tool of a background subagent and still drains the rest` fails without the change.
- `clearPending still drains an inner tool whose parent subagent is foreground` is the control and passes either way.

The suite goes from 12 passing with 1 failing to 13 passing, and both pre-existing `clearPending` tests are unaffected. No new type errors.

title: Do not mark a denied subagent tool call as a subagent
body:
A denied `Agent` or `Task` call still gets a subagent marker attached to its result, so on restore the host registers a subagent chat whose transcript can never exist.

## What happens

`toolKind` is derived from the tool **name**, with no regard for the outcome, and `_attachToolResult` pushes `ToolResultContentType.Subagent` unconditionally. On restore, `_registerRestoredSubagentSummaries` scans replayed turns for that marker and registers a chat with a lazy resolver, and the resolver throws `Subagent transcript is not available yet` forever, because nothing was ever spawned.

Since #334312 that is no longer fatal to the session, but the phantom chat is still registered, still fails to `subscribe`, and still shows in the session's chat list as a subagent that never produces anything.

## How it was hit

Auto mode could not classify an `Agent` call and denied it:

```
"...temporarily unavailable, so auto mode cannot determine the safety of Agent right now..."
"toolDenialKind": "automode-unavailable"
```

The SDK transcript for that session is 47 lines with zero `isSidechain` entries, confirming no subagent ran. Any denial reaches this the same way, so a permission rule or a user rejecting the call does too.

## The change

`is_error` alone is not the right test: it also covers a subagent that **started and then failed**, and those children have real transcripts that must still be linked on restore.

The SDK stamps `agentId: <hex>` on the tool_result of a call that actually spawned, which is what `scanTranscriptForAgentIds` already keys on through the exported `SUBAGENT_ID_SUFFIX_REGEX`. A pre-spawn denial is therefore the case with an error and no agentId:

```ts
const spawned = !isError || SUBAGENT_ID_SUFFIX_REGEX.test(resultText);
if (isSubagent && spawned) {
```

`resultText` is already computed immediately above for the past-tense message, so nothing new is derived.

## Tests

- `Fixture 5c: a denied Agent tool_use produces no subagent marker` asserts the call is still recognised as a subagent by name, that `success` is `false`, and that no marker is attached.
- `Fixture 5d: an Agent that spawned and then failed keeps its subagent marker` is the failed-after-spawn case, and fails against an `is_error`-only condition.

Fixtures 5 and 5b continue to pass, so successful spawns are unchanged. The suite is 30 passing. No new type errors.

title: Fix terminal prompt duplication when resizing the terminal panel
body:
Fixes #329946 (partial — see "Known limitations" below)

## Summary

When the terminal panel is resized, the shell prompt can be duplicated / new prompt lines created on every resize instead of the buffer reflowing cleanly. Two causes in the terminal resize path:

1. **Redundant PTY resizes on every layout event.** `TerminalResizeDebouncer.resize()` fired a resize even when the grid dimensions did not change (e.g. while dragging the panel), sending a PTY resize (SIGWINCH) on every layout event. Shells repaint the prompt on SIGWINCH, so this produced a storm of prompt redraws while dragging.

2. **Horizontal resizes debounced too briefly.** The debounced horizontal resize fired after 100ms, but shells such as zsh need longer than that to fully process a prompt redraw after a resize. When resizes arrived back-to-back, the shell computed its prompt redraw from a stale terminal width, which misplaces the erase/rewrite and leaves duplicated prompt fragments in the buffer.

## Changes

`src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalResizeDebouncer.ts`:
- Skip the resize entirely (and cancel any pending debounced resize) when the requested `cols`/`rows` equal the current grid — no more redundant PTY resizes / SIGWINCH storms while dragging.
- Only fire the immediate Y-resize when `rows` actually changed, and only schedule the debounced X-resize when `cols` actually changed.
- Increase `DebounceResizeXDelay` from 100ms to 300ms so the shell's prompt redraw is fully processed between consecutive resizes.

## Verification

- Reproduced the duplication headlessly with a real zsh 5.9 and bash shell in a pty driving the bundled xterm.js: with the 100ms debounce the buffer ended with 3 prompt copies after a shrink/grow/shrink cycle; with 300ms exactly 1 copy.
- Verified in a running Code OSS instance (launched with playwright over CDP): resizing the bottom-panel terminal (long prompt, shrink/grow cycles, continuous drags) reflows cleanly with no duplication.

## Known limitations (honest assessment)

This fixes the common cases (panel resizing at moderate widths, continuous drags). It does **not** fix every duplication scenario:

- **Extreme-narrow terminals with colored prompts** (e.g. terminal docked in the side panel and shrunk to its minimum width, ~15-20 columns, with a colored `PS1`/`PROMPT`): the prompt can still duplicate. Root cause: xterm.js deliberately does not reflow the cursor line on non-Windows (`reflowCursorLine=false`), so the prompt is a single buffer row rendered wrapped across several visual rows. The shell's redraw (readline/zsh) operates on visual rows, so its erase/rewrite misses rows and fragments accumulate. Enabling `reflowCursorLine` makes this worse due to https://github.com/xtermjs/xterm.js/issues/5295 (cursor mispositioned on reflow of cursor line), which the xterm.js maintainers have declined to fix. Upstream VS Code has no fix for this either; it would require a change in xterm.js or readline.

title: dictation: fix indefinite hangs by adding timeouts to Foundry Local native calls
body:
## What

On-device (`nemo`/Foundry Local) dictation could hang indefinitely with no error surfaced to the user — the toolbar spinner would just spin forever, or clicking Stop/Cancel would do nothing.

## Why

`LocalTranscriptionService` (the utility-process side of dictation) awaits several native `foundry-local-sdk` calls that have no `AbortSignal` and no timeout of their own:

- the model catalog lookup (`manager.catalog.getModel`)
- `model.load()` (explicitly called out in an existing code comment as having "no AbortSignal")
- `session.start()`
- each `session.append()` call — these are chained serially through `_appendChain` to preserve audio order, so one wedged append blocks every later chunk **and** `stop()`, which awaits the whole chain
- the result stream's `next()` (via `for await...of session.getStream()`) — `stop()` awaits the consumer promise, so a stream that silently stops yielding (without throwing) hangs Stop forever
- `session.stop()` / `session.dispose()`

If any of these stalls — a proxy/firewall silently dropping packets, a wedged native addon, a driver hiccup during model load, etc. — the corresponding promise never settles. Since `start()`/`pushAudio()`/`stop()`/`cancel()` all await these calls directly or transitively, the whole feature hangs with no recovery short of restarting VS Code.

The one existing exception was the native runtime tarball download, which already has a `DOWNLOAD_INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT_MS` guard (see `foundryLocalRuntime.ts`) — this PR extends the same pattern to the remaining unguarded native calls.

## Change

Adds a small `withTimeout()` helper and races each of the calls above against a bounded timeout (30s for catalog lookup, 120s for model load, 15s for session start/append/teardown, 60s inactivity for the result stream). A timeout now rejects with a descriptive error that flows through the existing error-handling path (`classifyModelError`, which gains a new `'timeout'` code) exactly like any other model/session failure, so the existing UI (progress ring, error notification, `_failModelSession`) picks it up instead of hanging silently.

This does not cancel the underlying native call (the SDK gives us no way to) — it only unblocks whichever caller is waiting on it so the failure is surfaced and the session can be reset/retried.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck-client` passes (the one remaining reported error, in `mcpSamplingLog.test.ts`, is pre-existing and unrelated to this change).
- This service wraps a native addon with no existing unit test harness (only `foundryLocalRuntime` and `foundryLocalModelImport` have tests), so validation here is via typecheck + code review; the change is a set of surgical `Promise.race` wraps around existing await points and does not alter behavior on the non-timeout success path.

title: Fix tab close button stuck showing "Close Others" after focus changes
body:
## Description

Alt+hover swaps a tab's **Close** action for **Close Others**. Both inputs to that swap could go stale across a focus change: `redrawTabAction()` read `modifierKeyEmitter.keyStatus.altKey` at paint time (the Alt `keyup` is delivered to whichever app you Alt+Tab'd into), and `hoveredTabIndex` was only cleared by a real `mouseleave`. Coming back to the window without moving the mouse could therefore leave the `x` armed as "Close Others", so a plain click silently closed every other editor in the group.

### Changes — `MultiEditorTabsControl`

- **Local Alt state.** A `isAltPressed` field, fed by the `ModifierKeyEmitter` event, replaces the two on-demand reads of `modifierKeyEmitter.keyStatus.altKey`. It is the single source of truth for the swap and redraws the hovered tab when it flips.
- **Give up the swap on focus loss.** `IHostService.onDidChangeFocus(false)` clears both the Alt state and the hovered tab, so a hover left over from before the focus change cannot be re-armed by Alt state re-established on return. Re-hovering a tab arms it again as usual.
- **Re-validate Alt from mouse events.** `mousemove`/`mousedown` on the tabs container carry the real modifier state even when a `keyup` was missed entirely — this covers macOS Mission Control, where the window may never see a `blur`.

The mouse listeners are registered in the **capture** phase because `BaseActionViewItem` calls `EventHelper.stop(e, true)` on `mousedown`; a bubble-phase listener never sees a press on the close button itself, which is precisely the reported "click without moving the mouse" case.

```ts
for (const eventType of [EventType.MOUSE_MOVE, EventType.MOUSE_DOWN]) {
	this._register(addDisposableListener(tabsContainer, eventType, (e: MouseEvent) => {
		this.setAltPressed(e.altKey);
	}, true));
}
```

In the stale-Alt case the capture handler swaps the action item mid-`mousedown`, so that first click is swallowed rather than executing "Close Others" — the icon is then correct and the next click closes the single tab.

`EditorTabsControl.hostService` becomes `protected` so the subclass can use it.

### Tests

`src/vs/workbench/test/browser/parts/editor/multiEditorTabsControl.test.ts` covers the baseline swap plus the focus-loss, mouse-move and action-mousedown paths; each regression test was checked to fail with its corresponding part of the change reverted.

### Notes for reviewers

- After returning from another application the swap requires a fresh hover (move to another tab, or leave and re-enter). This is the behaviour suggested in the issue and is what makes a stale hover unexploitable.
- `menuEntryActionViewItem.ts` has the same latent staleness pattern; left untouched to keep this scoped to tabs.

title: feat: implementing word wrap indicators
body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/47855 https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4a7be874-cb00-41a9-8d38-616456c31323 Adds an opt-in indicator at the wrapping column of every soft wrapped line, so a wrap can be told apart from a real line break. Addresses #47855. Off by default. Set `editor.wordWrapIndicator` to `true` to turn it on; it only has an effect while `editor.wordWrap` is enabled. ## How it works ### Rendering Rendering is done by `WordWrapIndicatorOverlay`, a `DynamicViewOverlay` registered on the content overlay layer in `view.ts` alongside the selection and whitespace overlays. `prepareRender` walks the view lines of the viewport and produces one HTML string per line. A line gets a glyph only when `continuesWithWrappedLine` is set — that is, when it is followed by a soft wrap rather than by a real line break, and is not the last line of the model. The glyph itself is a single `
` holding U+21A9 LEFTWARDS ARROW WITH HOOK. Its content-relative `left` is the effective wrapping column multiplied by the font's typical half-width character width, so every glyph stays aligned with the boundary that produced the wrap. Horizontal scrolling moves the glyph with the document content instead of pinning it to the viewport edge. Its height comes from `getLineHeightForLineNumber`, so lines carrying a custom line height keep the indicator vertically aligned. ### Color `editorWordWrapIndicator.foreground` is a new theme colour that defaults to `editorWhitespace.foreground`, so out of the box the indicator is as muted as rendered whitespace, while themes can still override it on its own. ## Known Limitations The indicator marks the wrapping boundary rather than the exact end of the rendered text, so a segment that wraps at whitespace can leave a gap before the glyph. When a fixed `wordWrapColumn` lies beyond the viewport, the indicator remains offscreen until horizontal scrolling reveals that column. The indicator is a visual-only overlay; it has no equivalent representation for screen readers or the minimap. ## Other Editors - Visual Studio - Notepad++ - IntelliJ IDEA Word wrap indicator is shown at the beginning of the wrapped line Does not have word wrap indicator: - XCode - Sublime Text --- ## Manual checklist before marking ready for review - [x] Toggle `editor.wordWrapIndicator` live with a wrapped file open: the glyph appears and disappears without needing a reload. - [x] Glyph stays aligned with the effective wrapping column at several `editor.fontSize` values and with a proportional font (`editor.fontFamily` set to a non-monospace family). - [x] Correct with variable line heights. - [x] Interacts sanely with `editor.renderWhitespace: 'all'` — the glyph should not collide with a trailing whitespace dot. - [x] Not selectable and not copied when selecting across a wrapped line (`pointer-events: none` covers hit testing; verify the clipboard). - [x] Inline suggestions / inlay hints / injected text on a wrapped line do not push the glyph to the wrong position. - [x] `editorWordWrapIndicator.foreground` shows up in `workbench.colorCustomizations` IntelliSense and overriding it takes effect. - [x] Legible in Dark+, Light+, and both high contrast themes — the inherited `editorWhitespace.foreground` is deliberately faint, so confirm it is visible enough in HC without being noisy in the default themes. - [x] Accessibility: confirm the glyph is not announced by the screen reader as line content. ## Feedback from standup Team members mentioned in the standup that they would prefer having the word wrap indicator on the left-hand side in the gutter instead of at the wrapping column on the right. The issue with this idea is that it requires the gutter to be present, so people with no gutter would not see this, and sometimes people only show every 5 lines so the word wrap indicator would look weird.

title: Copy the image when using Copy in a webview context menu
body: Fixes #292567 ### Problem Right clicking an image in a webview and choosing **Copy** puts nothing on the clipboard. Selecting the image first and then copying works, which is the clue to what is going on. The webview context menu's `Copy` is the standard `CopyAction`, routed to `webview.copy()` in `webview.contribution.ts`, which sends an `execCommand` message that the webview shell runs as `contentDocument.execCommand('copy')`. That only ever copies the *text selection*. Right clicking an image does not create a selection, so there is nothing to copy — and no error, which is why the issue reports silence rather than a failure. ### Fix Track the element the context menu was opened on in `pre/index.html`. When `copy` arrives with a collapsed selection and that element is an ``, encode it as a png and write it with `navigator.clipboard.write` instead of running `execCommand`. Details worth noting: - **Selection still wins.** If the user actually has something selected we fall straight through to `execCommand`, so selecting an image and copying behaves exactly as before. Cut, paste, undo and redo are untouched. - **Cross origin images.** Most webview images are served by the webview service worker, which synthesises the response, so drawing them into a canvas works directly. An image fetched from a genuinely opaque cross origin response taints the canvas and `toBlob` throws, so we fall back to re-requesting it in cors mode and going through `createImageBitmap`. - **Focus.** `navigator.clipboard.write` rejects unless the document is focused, and copy is dispatched as the context menu is closing. We give focus a moment to come back, but still attempt the write if it does not, so we never silently do nothing. - **Staleness.** The tracked image is cleared on the next click or keypress, so a later keyboard copy with nothing selected does not resurrect an image the user right clicked earlier. ### Testing The two encode paths were measured in a webview on VS Code 1.108 with a probe extension: drawing a `vscode-resource` image into a canvas succeeds (`ok: true`), and the cors re-fetch fallback also succeeds (`fetchStatus: 200`, `ok: true`). The end to end context menu flow has not been exercised against a build of this branch — I would appreciate a check on Windows and Linux in particular, where the context menu is rendered differently and the focus timing may not match macOS. ### Related The same missing cors fallback exists in three other copy-image implementations that each grew independently — `markdown-language-features`, `media-preview`, and the notebook webview. A remote image in a markdown preview fails there today with `SecurityError: Tainted canvases may not be exported`. Not touched here; happy to follow up if it is worth consolidating.

title: agentHost: Keep passive session opens from changing recency
body:
## Summary

- suppress the SDK `session.resume` event when Agent Host cold-opens an existing Copilot session
- keep observational session opens from advancing the persisted session modification time
- cover the resume configuration passed by the Copilot session launcher

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/334501

## Problem

The Sessions view can show an old session as modified recently even though its last message was sent days ago.

For Copilot sessions, the displayed `updatedAt` ultimately comes from the SDK/runtime `modifiedTime`, which is based on the `events.jsonl` modification time. Cold-opening a session calls `resumeSession`; publishing a `session.resume` event can modify that journal, making a passive open look like recent user activity.

## Resolution

Agent Host now passes `suppressResumeEvent: true` when it resumes an existing session for display. This lets the runtime restore the live session without recording an observational resume event that changes recency.

## Dependency

**Blocked by https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/pull/18323. Do not merge until VS Code consumes a runtime release containing that change.**

The current runtime couples resume-event suppression with resume-state processing. Runtime PR #18323 separates those concerns so suppressed resumes still restore model/context and preserve orphan and pending-work semantics while avoiding journal writes, subscriber publication, and modified-time updates.

## Validation

- `npm run hygiene`
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- ESLint on both changed files

title: Agent Host: Use VS Code certificates for Dev Container CLI
body:
## Summary

Configure the bundled Dev Container CLI to use the certificates loaded by VS Code, including enterprise system certificates and user-provided `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`.

<details>
<summary>Session Context</summary>

Key decisions from the development session:

- **Do not force Node `--use-system-ca`**: That runtime switch would bypass VS Code certificate settings. The CLI instead receives a `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` bundle, matching the approach used by the Remote Containers extension.
- **Reuse VS Code certificate policy**: Certificate loading goes through `IRequestService.loadCertificates()`, while `http.systemCertificates` gates whether system certificates are added. The request service also honors `http.systemCertificatesNode`.
- **Preserve explicit environment configuration**: A valid existing `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` value wins and is passed through unchanged.
- **Use a VS Code-owned temporary namespace**: Generated content-addressed PEM files are cached under `<tmpDir>/vscode-dev-container`, rather than the Remote Containers extension-specific `vsch` directory.
- **Handle concurrent writers safely**: Each process writes a unique temporary file and atomically renames it to the certificate-content hash. A rename failure is accepted only when another process has already published the expected target.

</details>

## Changes

- Inject the shared-process request service into the Dev Container Agent Host launcher.
- Resolve the Dev Container CLI environment once per process.
- Preserve valid `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` or generate a hashed PEM file from VS Code-loaded certificates.

title: Keep auto experiment defaults applied when assignments are refetched
body:
This stops experiment-driven setting defaults from being dropped and re-applied whenever assignments are refetched, which made the workbench visibly blink between the classic and Modern UI layouts shortly after startup.

### Changes

- `ConfigurationDefaultOverridesContribution` now keeps an experiment default that is already registered with the same resolved value, instead of re-evaluating it and deregistering it.
- This fixes an oscillation: the configuration registry mutates `property.default` to reflect registered default overrides, so once an `auto` experiment was applied, the next resolution compared the treatment against itself, concluded it matched the default, and removed the override. `WorkbenchAssignmentService` fires `onDidRefetchAssignments` shortly after the initial assignment fetch, so this happened during startup — `workbench.experimental.modernUI` flipped back to `false`, `updateFloatingPanels()` stripped the `modern-ui` classes, and a later refetch flipped it back.
- `shouldOverride` is deliberately left unchanged. Comparing against the schema-authored default instead would silently drop a control-arm assignment whenever another non-experiment `configurationDefaults` override exists for the same key, and would make `preventExperimentOverride` redundant.
- Startup-mode latching, the `preventExperimentOverride` guard, the Agents window `agentsWindow.default` comparison, and removal when a treatment resolves to `undefined` are all unaffected.
- Added regression coverage for an auto experiment surviving a refetch, and for a control-arm value still winning over an unrelated default override.

### Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --grep "Configuration|Sessions ConfigurationService|WorkspaceService"` — 770 passing, 7 pending.
- Both new tests were confirmed to fail against the unmodified source and pass with the fix. The guard test's initial-resolution assertion is identical before and after, confirming the existing override semantics are preserved.

title: Agent Host: provide inline editor context before send
body:
## Summary

- Actualize a bounded source window for editor inline chat inside the Agent Host immediately before provider dispatch.
- Keep the protocol selection attachment and browser/UI state unchanged.
- Mark `<editor_inline_context>` as current, authoritative source and tell the model to edit directly without a redundant read when it has sufficient context.
- Scope the behavior to the existing Agent Host chat-surface contribution.

The injected context is bounded to 16 lines, 220 characters per line, 4,096 rendered characters, and a 1 MiB source read. The target attachment is matched against the editor-inline surface URI so another selected attachment cannot be used accidentally.

## Performance investigation

We profiled repeated `comment out this line` requests in editor inline chat using Agent Host debug logs and CPU profiles.

| Stage | Original | Context only | Context + authoritative instruction | Final delta vs. original |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Session ready | 1.662s | 1.201s | 0.960s | -0.702s |
| Provider begins | 8.771s | 7.197s | 7.615s | -1.156s |
| First model call | 5.709s | 5.488s | 6.111s | +0.402s |
| `view` tool | 1.274s | 1.154s | eliminated | -1.274s |
| Tool-planning model call after `view` | 3.585s | 10.593s | eliminated | -3.585s |
| `edit` tool | 0.784s | 0.763s | 1.379s | +0.595s |
| Final model call | 3.056s | 2.936s | 2.707s | -0.349s |
| **Total** | **23.289s** | **28.241s** | **17.907s** | **-5.382s (-23.1%)** |

With context alone, the model still requested `view` for almost exactly the lines already present in `<editor_inline_context>`. After strengthening the instruction, the first model response was the `edit` call and the redundant `view` plus follow-up planning round trip disappeared.

The CPU captures were approximately 91-93% idle/program/GC, so the latency is dominated by SDK/runtime and model waits rather than Agent Host CPU work.

## MCP investigation and follow-up

The traces also showed roughly seven seconds before the first provider turn while 13 MCP servers started, authenticated, or failed/retried. This happened even though the session was definitively marked `vscode.chat.ephemeralSession: true`.

We tested all of the following for ephemeral sessions:

1. `enableConfigDiscovery: false`
2. omitting `mcpServers` instead of sending `{}`
3. additionally omitting `pluginDirectories`

None changed MCP startup: the same 13 servers still launched, including Azure, GitHub, Slack/WorkIQ, `vscode-tools`, `context7`, and the failing/retrying Docker-backed `awesome-copilot` server. The first request also remained around 45.8k uncached input tokens.

Those VS Code-side MCP experiments have been rolled back from this PR. We should instead add a Copilot SDK session option that acts as a master MCP switch: when disabled, the runtime must not discover, start, authenticate, or expose any MCP server regardless of config-directory discovery, plugin directories, explicit server maps, or runtime defaults. VS Code can then set that option for ephemeral inline-chat sessions.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- Focused Agent Host suites previously passed 388 tests during implementation.
- After the final instruction update, 372 tests passed and one stale expected-instruction assertion failed; that assertion was updated before commit and was not rerun at the requester's direction.
- Pre-commit hygiene passed for all changed files.

## Problem

Agent Host start/stop handling reverse-resolved customization IDs only through the controller's runtime `_live` inventory. During a same-name collision, the runtime can first associate a server name with a published plugin child and then receive a distinct same-name workspace top-level customization.

Agent Customizations presents the workspace entry and sends its exact ID, but the live lookup no longer recognizes that ID. The provider logs `Cannot start unknown MCP server customization ...`, no server process starts, and the optimistic client reducer leaves the row at `Starting`.

## Change

Keep the runtime lookup as the first choice, then fall back to an exact-ID lookup across the session's currently published customizations.

The fallback accepts only an ID that is present in current session state. It does not add a broad same-name alias and does not change collision precedence. The SDK lifecycle API remains name-keyed, so it starts the effective server winner already selected for that name.

## Validation

- `npm run gulp compile-client`
- `npx mocha test/unit/node/index.js --delay --ui=tdd --timeout=20000 --exit --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/shared/mcpCustomizationController.test.ts` — 20 passing
- Targeted ESLint and `git diff --check`
- Regression coverage verifies published IDs resolve before the SDK has populated the live inventory and unknown IDs remain rejected.
- Deterministic live Code OSS A/B with a real Copilot Agent Host session and real local stdio MCP processes:
  - A host-only plugin published and started `dupe`; the real UI then stopped it through its plugin-child customization ID.
  - A workspace-root `.mcp.json` with another `dupe` was published afterward, producing two distinct current customization IDs with no synthetic `mcp-top-level:*` ID and no intervening SDK state event that could repair the mapping.
  - Unpatched main: the UI dispatched `SessionMcpServerStartRequested` with the exact workspace ID, Agent Host logged the matching unknown-customization warning, no process spawned, and the clicked row remained stuck at `Starting`.
  - Patched: the UI dispatched the same workspace ID, no unknown-customization warning was logged, a new real MCP process spawned, the workspace entry transitioned `stopped -> starting -> ready`, and the clicked row reached `Running`.
  - A separate `solo` server completed stop/start successfully as a control.
- The patched live arm was repeated through the repository's normal `scripts/code.bat` launch path with the same result.

Current source combines user and `.vscode/mcp.json` inputs before Agent Host receives them, so the live harness used a host-configured plugin child plus workspace-root `.mcp.json` to deterministically reproduce the same published child/top-level identity collision described by the issue.

title: Fix per-turn chat diff reloads
body:
## Summary

Fix completed per-turn change summaries changing or disappearing when switching Agent sessions.

Completed response rows were mixing three lifecycle-dependent views of a turn: provisional tool-edit totals, the authoritative per-turn checkpoint diff, and the active Sessions Changes view's mutable last-turn changeset. Session activation caused the UI to switch between these sources, so counts could change (for example `+77/-33` to `+76/-32`) or resolve to zero and hide the summary.

This change makes the per-request checkpoint diff the single source of truth for a completed response's header, file list, visibility, and open action. Default Agent Host chats now wait for the authoritative checkpoint rather than flashing provisional raw-edit totals. Peer-chat and failed-checkpoint fallbacks remain supported.

## Root cause

#332297 added raw response edits as a temporary fallback while the server-computed turn changeset was loading. Raw edit totals count intermediate operations and can differ from the final net checkpoint diff.

#332759 then routed the latest response header through the active Sessions Changes view while leaving its file list on the per-request provider. Because Changes subscriptions are gated by the active session, switching sessions caused an immutable completed response to follow a mutable active-session changeset.

#332982 correctly made authoritative empty results clear cached summaries, which exposed the existing race as a disappearing row.

The existing tests covered each mechanism independently, but did not model the combined lifecycle: a restored response row rendering provisional response edits, activating its session, and then receiving a different or empty checkpoint changeset.

## Fix

- Remove the active Changes-view stats override.
- Derive completed-turn counts from the same per-request diffs used by the file list.
- Wait for authoritative checkpoint diffs for default chats while changesets are loading.
- Preserve response-edit fallback for peer chats and checkpoint failures.
- Add regression coverage for provisional `+77/-33` response totals resolving directly to authoritative `+76/-32` totals without rendering the provisional state.

## Result

- Opening or switching sessions no longer changes a completed turn's counts.
- A restored row stays hidden until its authoritative checkpoint arrives instead of flashing provisional totals.
- Once an authoritative diff has rendered, temporary recompute/reconnect states retain it.
- An authoritative no-op turn can still correctly clear/hide the summary.

## Validation

- `npm run compile-client`
- `npm run hygiene`
- 26 focused tests across `SessionTurnChanges`, `ChatTurnPillsContentPart`, and `AgentHostResponseFileChangesProvider`
- Pre-commit hygiene hook
- `git diff --check`

## Summary

## Summary

Fixes #332423 by allowing new parent-chat turns to proceed when a restored historical subagent has no transcript.

title: [typescript] Add setting to include closing braces in folding ranges
body:
Solves #3352 for TypeScript/JavaScript. Adds `js/ts.folding.includeClosingBraces` (false) to `typescript-language-features`, allowing users to control whether closing braces and tags are included in folding regions. Historically, and due to the workaround for #47240, the TypeScript extension excludes closing braces from folding regions. As a result, collapsed code blocks leave the closing-brace lines visible as a separate line. This change allows users who prefer code blocks to collapse to a single line, as requested in #3352, to opt into that behavior. For example, many users prefer the collapsed code to look like the right side of the provided screenshot, rather than the current behavior shown on the left:
The change only extends code folding ranges that were affected by the #47240 workaround, leaving comment, region, and import folding ranges intact. It also accounts for adjacent folding regions, avoiding changes that would corrupt folding of constructs such as `if () { ... } else { ... }`, which produce multiple adjacent regions, by checking that extending a region does not overlap another existing region. This is implemented in the `typescript-language-features` extension rather than in VS Code's core folding implementation. The current direction is not to modify folding ranges on the VS Code side or introduce a common, language-agnostic folding-preferences carrier API for folding range providers, as proposed in #298676. Consequently, extensions need to expose their own settings for such folding preferences. There are several folding extensions available in the Marketplace, but some are broken and have been unmaintained for a long time. The ones that still partially work are generally based on regular expressions rather than syntax-aware folding, and are not aware of language-specific exclusions. For example, the best configuration I found for TypeScript is the [ExplicitFolding](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=zokugun.explicit-folding) extension: https://gist.github.com/n-gist/7a7fed4f9ef90a5e7e31c1879f88efc4. The regular expression is already complex and difficult to maintain, yet it still fails in some cases. When a case it cannot handle is encountered in a file, all subsequent folding regions are broken. Since the folding provider currently has no test coverage, I did not introduce a new test area as part of this change. I am attaching a file with the test cases I used to manually verify the changes with the setting enabled and disabled. [folding_cases.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31810980/folding_cases.txt)

title: Add MCP customization migration
body:
## Summary

- Add an MCP server migration category to the Agent Customizations editor, behind `chat.customizations.mcpServerMigration.enabled`.
- Move eligible workspace server entries from `.vscode/mcp.json` to workspace-root `.mcp.json` so the active Agent Host harness can discover them directly.
- Show source and destination before confirmation, preserve selection and keyboard focus across refreshes, and leave unsupported or unselected servers in place.

<details>
<summary>Technical context for AI-assisted review</summary>

### Eligibility and editor integration

The migration service extends its existing support reporting with executable MCP candidates. Candidates must be enabled, applicable to the session, client-forwarded, fully supported, and exactly representable in the destination format. The source configuration must match the current Agent Host delivery projection without losing properties or relying on unresolved configuration variables.

MCP entries reuse the editor's existing virtualized migration lists, grouping, selection, confirmation, and notification flow. They are server entries rather than customization files, so rows show a name and source-to-destination path without file-specific actions. Existing prompt, user-data, and configured-location migration behavior is preserved.

### Session context and URI routing

The service recomputes eligibility after confirmation and checks the active session and ordered working-directory roots before and between writes. The support scope remains live during execution. Guards compare coverage and the pending candidates' delivery eligibility and projected configuration, rather than support-snapshot object identity, so equivalent snapshot refreshes do not abort migration merely because a new object was published.

`IAgentHostCustomizationService.getWorkingDirectoryUris` derives client-resolvable roots in the shared abstract service. Existing root getters retain host-side URI strings for workspace classification and protocol enablement decisions. The Agents Window uses the provider's stable resource mapper instead of depending on a feedback channel or falling back to identity mapping, preventing remote roots from being mistaken for matching local paths.

Workbench root resolution uses provisional roots until session state is available and falls back to the subscription's verified state on errors. MCP computation honors caller cancellation while waiting for initial support resolution, checks cancellation around planning, and disposes the acquired support scope.

### Write safety and failure handling

Each source/destination pair is handled as a guarded two-file update:

1. Re-read the source and destination, reject changed source entries and conflicting destination entries.
2. Write missing destination entries first, or accept equivalent entries already present.
3. Recheck execution context before removing the selected source entries.
4. Re-read both files to verify the result; restore original content only when doing so is safe.

Existing wrapped (`mcpServers`) and flat JSONC `.mcp.json` files are accepted. Edits preserve surrounding comments and formatting. Existing-file writes compare exact expected content and use file-service etag/mtime guards; new-file creation does not overwrite an existing destination.

These are best-effort optimistic-concurrency checks, not an atomic cross-file transaction. If rollback cannot be performed safely, the operation reports a structured failure and asks the user to review the affected files. A newly created destination is retained rather than deleted during rollback. Planning exclusions and execution phases are trace-logged for diagnosis.

</details>

Fixes #333895

## Summary

This updates every page in the AI Customizations management editor to use independent virtualized `WorkbenchList` controls while preserving each page's existing structure and actions.

The change expanded beyond the original Plugins page because the same list, sizing, scrolling, and disclosure behavior needed to remain consistent across Plugins, MCP Servers, Agents, Skills, Instructions, Hooks, Prompts, Tools, and the migration flows.

- Adds reusable section-list layout helpers in `customizationCardList.ts`.
- Distributes the available viewport height across all expanded sections instead of relying on an outer scrolling region.
- Reserves at least one complete row for each populated section, then water-fills the remaining height based on content.
- Redistributes freed space immediately when a section is collapsed or expanded.
- Uses stable loading placeholders so asynchronous item discovery does not initially collapse sections to tiny slivers.
- Preserves each list's scroll position during layout, refreshes, filtering-related rerenders, and collapse/expand cycles.

### 2. Page coverage

- **Agents, Skills, Instructions, Hooks, and Prompts:** each storage/source group is its own virtualized list.

- **MCP Servers:** Featured, Installed, and Available sections remain separate and virtualized; existing server status badges are preserved.
- **Tools:** each tool provider section uses its own virtualized list with dynamic row heights.
