title: Add `editor.textDirection` to lay out editor contents right-to-left
body:
Part of #4994 and #11770. See also #270580, which specifies this design.

VS Code can be localized into right-to-left languages, but the editor has no way to lay out its
**contents** right-to-left. The direction of a line is inferred per line, so a file written in
Arabic, Hebrew, Persian or Urdu renders as a stack of independently-resolved paragraphs: the caret
starts on the wrong side, a line beginning with an identifier or a symbol flips to left-to-right,
and line numbers and glyph margin stay on the left of text that reads from the right.

### The option

`editor.textDirection: 'auto' | 'ltr' | 'rtl' | 'uiLanguage'`

| value | behaviour |
|---|---|
| `auto` (default) | **exactly today's behaviour**: lines are laid out left-to-right |
| `ltr` | the same as `auto` today; the explicit counterpart of `rtl`, and the value to reach for to opt one language out of a broader `rtl` |
| `rtl` | lines are laid out right-to-left and the editor mirrors its layout (table below) |
| `uiLanguage` | `rtl` when the user interface is itself displayed in a right-to-left language |

A line whose direction a decoration declares keeps that direction under **every** value, exactly as
it does today. That is also why `auto` and `ltr` coincide: nothing here infers direction from
content, so both resolve to a left-to-right layout.

The setting is language-overridable, which is usually the scope it wants — direction is a property
of what a file contains, not of the window.

What `rtl` moves, and what it does not:

| element | `ltr` | `rtl` | |
|---|---|---|---|
| line numbers, glyph margin, folding | left edge | right edge, **and mirrored inside the strip**: reading outwards from the text come decorations, then line numbers, then the glyph margin | mirrored |
| minimap | side set by `minimap.side` | left edge, with its canvases flipped so the shape it paints matches the text. `minimap.side` is not honoured, and its description now says so | mirrored |
| text of each line | left-to-right | right-to-left, via a per-line `dir` attribute set by `ViewLine` | mirrored |
| vertical scrollbar | right of the content | right of the content | **unchanged** |
| overview ruler | with the scrollbar | with the scrollbar | **unchanged** |

The scrollbar staying put is deliberate: right-to-left lines already reserve `verticalScrollbarWidth`
with `padding-right` in `ViewLine#renderLine`, which predates this PR, so moving the bar would
reserve one side and paint on the other. The overview ruler annotates the scrollbar, so it stays
with it.

### Changing the direction of one file

`View: Change Editor Text Direction`, also in the View menu next to Word Wrap. It cycles the active
editor between the direction its settings give it, right-to-left, and left-to-right.

It is built like `toggleWordWrap`, and for the same reason: direction is not really a property of a
language. A repository holds an English README and an Arabic guide, both Markdown, and a
per-language setting cannot tell them apart. So the command writes **transient per-model state**
rather than settings — it never edits a `.vscode/settings.json` that is checked into git — and a new
editor option `textDirectionOverride: 'inherit' | 'auto' | 'ltr' | 'rtl'` carries that state into
`EffectiveTextDirection`. The setting remains the place to express a lasting preference.

### Why `uiLanguage` is not the default

Most people who localize the interface into Arabic, Hebrew or Persian still write Latin identifiers
all day; flipping their editor on an update, with no setting they ever touched, is not a change to
make silently. It is there for the people who do want it, as a value they choose.

### How it is built

- **The internal coordinate system is unchanged.** The editor still measures from a physical left
  origin. The mirrored layout is applied by the view parts and by CSS guarded on a
  `text-direction-rtl` class that `EditorClassName` contributes.
- **One physical origin.** In a mirrored layout the minimap occupies the leading strip, the content
  box starts where it ends, and the margin is flush with the right edge. Hit testing, content
  widgets, block decorations and the drag-select boundaries all derive that origin the same way.
- **Decorations still win, per line.** `ViewModel._getTextDirection` returns a decoration-declared
  direction when there is one — resolved exactly as before, ties included — and falls back to the
  option only for lines that declare none. Indent guides, sticky lines and the GPU renderer's
  fallback check the line's direction, not the layout's.
- **`EffectiveTextDirection`** is a computed option, so the setting is resolved once rather than at
  each read site.
- Exposed on `IEditorOptions`, so the Monaco standalone editor gets the setting too.

### Size, and what this does not change

21 files in the editor plus one new workbench contribution. 85 of the added lines are generated
(`standaloneEnums.ts` renumbering and `monaco.d.ts`); the rest is hand-written, most of it in the
view parts.

Two generated lines look unrelated and are not. Registering a new option shifts the order in which
TypeScript prints an unrelated union in `monaco.d.ts`, and `compile-src` fails the build when the
checked-in file does not match the generator. I verified this with the generator's own `execute()`:
on `main` untouched it reports `isTheSame: true`, with this branch applied and those lines reverted
it reports `false`, and with them as committed it reports `true` again.

**No change to default rendering.** With the setting at `auto` the resolved direction is always
`ltr`, whatever the display language. `editorLayoutProvider.test.ts` asserts that the mirrored
layout differs from the left-to-right one *only* in the order of the margin strip's children.

### Known limits

These are real, and I would rather name them than have them found:

- **Widgets that sit over the editor are not mirrored**: peek, inline chat, the inside of the find
  widget. They read as left-to-right panels above a mirrored editor rather than as broken layout.
- **Word-wise cursor movement is not direction-aware.** `wordOperations` has no notion of direction
  today, so `Ctrl+Left` moves against `Left` on a right-to-left line. This is pre-existing — it
  already applies to decoration-declared right-to-left lines — but this PR makes it reachable for
  whole files. It needs its own change, with the delete-word and select-word commands alongside.
- **IME and screen-reader anchoring** compute their position from `contentLeft`, which is the width
  of the margin strip rather than the content origin once the layout is mirrored. Five call sites
  across the edit contexts; also better as its own change.
- **Performance**: a right-to-left line takes neither the GPU renderer nor `ViewLine`'s fast path,
  as a line containing right-to-left characters already does not.

### Relationship to #318214

An earlier version of this description said the two PRs touch disjoint files. That was wrong:
#318214 also registers `editor.textDirection` and edits `editorOptions.ts`, `viewModelImpl.ts` and
`monaco.d.ts`, so they overlap on the option contract and need to be sequenced.

The contracts differ. #318214 registers `'ltr' | 'rtl' | 'auto'` defaulting to `'ltr'`, with `auto`
meaning first-strong-character detection per line. This PR registers
`'auto' | 'ltr' | 'rtl' | 'uiLanguage'` defaulting to `'auto'`, where `auto` is today's behaviour
unchanged. Beyond the option, this PR has what #318214 does not: the mirrored layout, view parts,
hit testing and CSS. I can rebase on #318214 and drop this registration, or fold the two —
whichever you prefer.

### Test

Set `"editor.textDirection": "rtl"` and open a file with Arabic or Hebrew text. Verify: line numbers
on the right with the glyph margin outside them, minimap on the left showing the same shape as the
text, caret on the right of an empty line, ruler columns measured from the right, a click on a line
number selecting the line rather than toggling a breakpoint, and the vertical scrollbar still on the
right of the content. Then run `View: Change Editor Text Direction` twice and confirm that nothing
is left behind and that no settings file changed.

title: Agent Host: stop the reconnecting banner nagging on a flapping transport
body:
A coworker reported a reconnecting banner appearing constantly on a session that otherwise worked fine. Their tunnel relay was dropping and restoring the transport on a ~6s cycle — each outage healed in ~2s with session state preserved, so the chat kept working the whole time.

Two separate causes, both from #334111.

## Stale outage start time

The outage start lives in a `derivedObservableWithCache`. While the host is connected nothing reads the reconnecting state, so that derived lost its observers — and a derived that is not observed keeps its last value without ever recomputing it. The next outage read `last?.session === session`, matched, and reused the *previous* outage's timestamp. The delay had therefore already elapsed, so the banner appeared immediately.

That is why it looked constant rather than merely frequent: only the first outage was ever debounced.

Fixed with `recomputeInitiallyAndOnChange`, which keeps the derived observed for the lifetime of the view so it recomputes on reconnect. The derived and its session keying are otherwise unchanged.

## Threshold shorter than a routine reconnect

`RECONNECTING_BANNER_DELAY` was 1s, but a self-healed reconnect here took ~2.05s. The delay exists to suppress blips the user would not otherwise notice — a reconnect that preserves session state is exactly that — so 1s was mistuned. Raised to 5s, comfortably past an observed reconnect.

Both changes are needed: with only the longer delay, a 2s outage still shows the banner on every cycle after the first, because the stale timestamp makes the delay a no-op.

## Test

`stays quiet while a flapping transport keeps healing itself` replays the reported cadence (2.1s outage, 3.7s healthy, five cycles) and asserts the banner never appears. It fails with either fix reverted — the stale-cache bug reproduces as the banner appearing from the second cycle onward.

The underlying relay instability (`[TunnelAgentHost] onDidRelayClose`) is pre-existing and out of scope here; this only stops the UI nagging about a connection that is working.

title: Fix RemotePty.resize dropping the last resize of an A-B-A sequence
body: Refs #325743, #239310 ### Problem https://disk.yandex.ru/i/Z-KpZ2owm_4hEg Showing a hidden **maximized** panel leaves a **remote** terminal (Remote-SSH / Dev Containers) with a pty at the *restored* height while xterm.js is at the maximized height, so TUIs such as tmux paint only the top part of the panel. The next hide/show repairs it, and it strictly alternates. Local terminals are not affected. ### Root cause `setPanelHidden(false)` lays the terminal out at the restored size and immediately re-maximizes it within the same task, so `RemotePty.resize` is called with F, R, F from consecutive microtasks (`setVisible(true) -> _resize()` with the stale size, `composite.layout(contentAreaSize)`, then `toggleMaximizedPanel()`). `RemotePty.resize` compared the requested size against `_lastDimensions` synchronously but only assigned `_lastDimensions` inside `_startBarrier.wait().then(...)`, one microtask later. So the first F was dropped as identical, R passed, and the final F was compared against the not-yet-updated `_lastDimensions` and dropped as well. Only R reached the pty host. `LocalPty.resize` assigns `_lastDimensions` synchronously before calling the proxy, which is why the symptom is remote-only. ### Fix Assign `_lastDimensions` synchronously in `RemotePty.resize`, mirroring `LocalPty`, and add a regression test for the A-B-A case (and for deduping identical consecutive sizes, which was also broken within one turn). ### Notes The test was not run locally (no build environment on the machine where this was authored); it targets the same shape as `agentHostPty.test.ts`. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Add opt-in auto-archive/delete inactive sessions with merged pull requests
body:
## Summary

This PR adds two application-scoped Preview settings for inactive agent sessions that have at least one merged pull request and no open related pull requests:

- `chat.agentSessions.autoArchiveMergedSessionsAfterDays`
  - disabled by default (`0`)
  - accepts any positive whole number of inactive days; 15 is the recommended value
  - archives eligible sessions through the normal archive lifecycle, including safe worktree cleanup and provider notification
- `chat.agentSessions.autoDeleteArchivedMergedSessionsAfterDays`
  - disabled by default (`0`)
  - accepts any positive whole number for the separate post-archive deletion grace period; 15 is the recommended value
  - permanently deletes only sessions that carry durable automatic-archive provenance

Worktree cleanup is part of archiving rather than a separate setting. If a retained worktree is still present when permanent deletion becomes eligible, deletion applies the same safe cleanup first.

## Lifecycle behavior

- lifecycle candidates are prefiltered from durable session metadata before restoring sessions
- active and external sessions are excluded
- every related pull request is refreshed before restoration and again immediately before lifecycle side effects, so reopening a closed PR blocks the action
- no related pull request may be open, and at least one must be merged; closed-unmerged PRs do not block cleanup once another related PR has merged
- archive/delete settings, session state, retention periods, and pull request identity are revalidated after session restoration
- automatic deletion applies only to sessions carrying durable automatic-archive provenance
- manually archived sessions are never made deletion-eligible by this lifecycle
- unarchiving clears automatic-archive provenance
- automatic archive uses the normal archive action and side-effect path
- deletion cleans a retained worktree inside the disposal critical section, where concurrent unarchive is rejected
- deletion uses the persisted primary repository root when removing checkpoint/review refs, including after worktree cleanup and Agent Host restart
- startup/hourly evaluation remains active when either lifecycle setting is enabled

## Worktree cleanup safety

Archiving or deleting an eligible session removes its worktree only when Git reports all of the following:

- the worktree has a branch
- the branch tracks an upstream
- outgoing and uncommitted change counts are both known
- there are zero outgoing commits
- there are zero uncommitted changes

Incoming commits do not block cleanup. Missing or unknown Git state fails closed. Cleanup uses ordinary, non-force `git worktree remove`, so Git performs a final dirty-worktree check as well. The lifecycle does not commit local changes or force-remove the worktree.

Removing a worktree is reversible for an archived session: the checkout can be recreated when the session is unarchived.

## User experience

Both settings default to disabled, so sessions remain visible, are not automatically archived, and are not permanently deleted.

The existing one-time **Turn On Session Cleanup** notification appears for an eligible merged-PR session after 15 days of inactivity while both settings are disabled. Its actions are:

- **Turn On Session Cleanup**: sets archive and delete thresholds to 15 days
- **Open Settings**: opens the `chat.agentSessions.auto*` settings

## Validation

- client transpilation
- focused Agent Host lifecycle tests
- AgentService unit tests
- targeted ESLint for changed TypeScript files
- `git diff --check`

Fixes #334334

title: agent host: stop chat queues from wedging on a non-settling SDK RPC
body:
agent host: stop chat queues from wedging on a non-settling SDK RPC

All chat operations for one chat serialize on a single per-chat sequencer. A control-plane RPC in that
queue had no timeout, so an RPC that never settled kept the queue head forever. Every later send,
model change, and abort stayed queued and never ran. The client showed a turn that stayed active with
no response and no error. Abort shared the same queue, so Cancel could not recover the chat.

- Bounds the short SDK control-plane RPCs at 30 seconds through a new `_awaitControlPlaneRpc` helper.
  This covers `session.setModel`, `rpc.agent.select`, `rpc.agent.deselect`, and `rpc.history.truncate`.
  A timeout now rejects the operation and lets the queue continue. Turn delivery through `session.send`
  stays unbounded, because a turn can correctly run for a long time.
- Removes abort from the per-chat queue. Abort must interrupt a blocked queue, so it cannot wait behind
  the task it must cancel.
- Adds an operation name to each `_queueChat` call and logs a warning if a queue task runs for more than
  60 seconds. The warning names the operation that holds the queue.
- Adds regression tests for the timeout, for a queued send that continues after a timeout, and for an
  abort that completes while a queue task is blocked.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/334159

title: agentHost: scale E2E protocol timeouts for CI contention
body:
Fixes the Agent Host E2E failures in [build 470786](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=470786&view=logs&j=193e9987-1fae-53fa-a82e-3ae14c27c30d&t=947af107-991d-500d-0eee-76fd05e265dc).

## What failed

The Linux Electron integration step lost four E2E tests across three parallel suites. None was a wrong result; every one was a wait expiring:

- **Codex**, after-each hook for `archiving a never-restored session survives a host restart`: cleanup called `subscribe` on a session never re-subscribed after two host restarts, so the host had to restore it from disk first, and the 5s default expired.
- **Claude**, `session changeset aggregates provider edits from default and peer chats`: `createChat` hit the 5s default. Every other suite already passes 30s for that call.
- **Claude**, `a GitHub remote with changes advertises pull request creation`: create-pr was not advertised within the ~10s poll.
- **Conformance**, `a client can clear review state from a changed file`: the review-changed notification did not arrive within 5s.

The run was starved. All four suites start at the same second on one agent, and this run took roughly twice as long as neighbouring runs (Copilot suite 312s vs. 165–214s).

## Cause

Not a single commit. The exact `Failed to release ... Timeout waiting for response to subscribe` signature already appeared on main on 2026-08-27 (Copilot) and 2026-09-02 (Claude, Windows), predating the recent Copilot, Codex and Claude SDK bumps. What changed is load: E2E coverage grew substantially on 2026-09-02, running four-wide against a default protocol timeout that scaled for Windows and coverage mode but never for CI.

## Fix

Waits are made environment-aware; no assertion changes.

- `serverIntegrationTestHelpers.ts`: default protocol operation timeout is 20s on CI. Local stays 5s (8s on Windows) so a wedged host still fails fast. Nothing relies on the default firing for a negative assertion. `fetchSessionWithChat` gains an optional timeout.
- `agentHostE2ETestHarness.ts`: `release()` uses the extended cleanup bound for its subscribe calls, matching the dispose calls, so a slow cleanup no longer fails a passing test and forces a server restart.
- `changesetSuite.ts`: operation polling allows 300 retries on CI, and the peer-chat `createChat` passes 30s like its siblings.

## Verification

ESLint and TypeScript are clean on the changed files. The E2E suites were not run locally (no product build in the worktree); CI on this PR is the real check.

## Separate observation

Two Windows-only failures of the Claude `archiving a never-restored session survives a host restart` test on 2026-09-02/03 were real assertions (`listSessions` missing the session after restart), landing within a few builds of the Claude Agent SDK 0.3.258 bump. Different failure, not addressed here.

title: Bind MCP protected-resource metadata to the server that advertised it
body:
A pending MCP authentication request is matched to an arriving token by its `resource` value, so `resource` is what decides where that token goes. `CopilotAgentSession._protectedResourceFromMcpAuthRequest` took that value from the metadata the MCP server supplied, checked only that the JSON had the right shape, and used it as given. A server could therefore advertise a resource belonging to somewhere else and be handed the token approved for that resource.

`fetchPrm` in `base/common/oauth.ts` already refuses metadata whose `resource` does not identify the URL it was fetched for, citing RFC 9728. This path had no equivalent check, so the two disagree about whether an advertised resource has to be bound to anything. This adds the missing one.

The rule is origin plus URL prefix, not equality. Equality would be wrong here, and the existing tests show why: a server at `https://mcp.slack.com/mcp` legitimately advertises `https://mcp.slack.com` as its resource. The prefix is compared by path segment, so `https://example.com/mcp` does not cover `https://example.com/mcpx`.

Metadata that fails the check is dropped rather than the request being rejected outright, and the request falls back to the identity derived from the server's own URL, so a server can still authenticate as itself.

## Testing

`src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/mcpProtectedResourceBinding.test.ts` adds 24 cases for the binding itself: the prefix and equality shapes that should pass, host case and default port normalisation, and on the other side a different host, a host that merely shares a prefix, differing scheme or port, a path prefix that is not a segment boundary, a server above the advertised resource rather than under it, values that are not URLs, and opaque origins.

`copilotAgentSession.test.ts` adds one end-to-end test through the existing session harness: a server advertising another server's resource has the claim dropped, is not settled by a token approved for that other resource, and can still authenticate as itself. That test fails without the change.

The existing 413-test session suite still passes, including the cases that rely on a server advertising a resource that is a prefix of its URL, which is what ruled out the equality reading.

`tsc -p src` and `eslint` are clean.

## Note on reporting

This was reported through MSRC (case 128144) and closed as not meeting the definition of a vulnerability, on the basis that discovery-time validation binds the advertised resource to the server's own origin. That validation does hold in `fetchPrm`; the point of this change is that this particular path does not go through it. I am sending the change here rather than opening a public issue describing it, since SECURITY.md asks that issues not be used for this. Happy to open one if you would prefer the PR to reference it.

title: Keep MACHINE target storage keys out of applied profile content
body:
`GlobalStateResource.getGlobalState` only writes out `StorageTarget.USER` values, so a key held at `StorageTarget.MACHINE` is never something a profile produced. Applying profile content did not hold to the same rule. `GlobalStateResourceInitializer.initialize` took every key it was given, and `writeGlobalState` excluded application scope and workspace scope machine keys but not profile scope ones. Both wrote what they took at `StorageTarget.USER`.

`chat.transferedWorkspaces` is a profile scope, MACHINE target key. It is the machine's own record that a chat session was moved to a folder, and `ChatTransferService.checkAndSetTransferredWorkspaceTrust` grants that folder workspace trust on open. The read did not look at the target, so a value carried in profile content satisfied it.

Two changes, either of which closes it, both worth having:

Applying profile content now uses one shared rule for the keys it will not take, and that rule includes profile scope MACHINE keys. The initializer uses the same rule instead of taking everything. Rejecting one key no longer costs the rest of the content, which the initializer would previously not have been able to express at all.

`ChatTransferService` requires the list to be at MACHINE target before honouring it. This is the half that holds when the key is not already present on the machine, which a rule based on the keys currently known cannot see.

Not addressed here: trust is still granted from an emptiness check made before the folder is opened, so a folder that gains content in between is still trusted. That is a change to how the transfer flow decides trust rather than to which values it believes, so it seemed better kept separate.

## Testing

`src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/chatTransferService.test.ts` adds 5 tests: a workspace the machine recorded is trusted on open; a list arriving at USER target does not grant trust; a USER target write over an existing machine record does not either; an unrelated workspace and no record at all do not.

`src/vs/workbench/services/userDataProfile/test/browser/globalStateResource.test.ts` adds 5 more: a key held at MACHINE target in profile scope is not taken and its value is left alone, the same for application scope, ordinary profile keys are still taken, and content carrying both keeps the ordinary one.

Two of them fail without the change while the rest keep passing.

328 passing across the chat common suites. `tsc -p src` and `eslint` are clean. Two failures in `StorageMainService` under the storage glob reproduce on an unmodified checkout and are unrelated.

## Note on reporting

This was reported through MSRC (case 127429) and closed as defence in depth. I am sending the change here rather than opening a public issue describing it, since SECURITY.md asks that issues not be used for this. Happy to open one if you would prefer the PR to reference it.

title: Withhold the GnuPG sandbox grant from Git commands that can run a supplied program
body:
The agent terminal sandbox grants a Git command `allowAllUnixSockets` together with read and write access to `~/.gnupg`, so that a signing operation can reach gpg-agent and the keyring. The rule matched on the `git` keyword alone.

Git reaches gpg through a child process, and the grant is applied to the whole sandboxed process tree, so whatever Git spawns inherits it. Several ordinary parts of a Git command line choose that child: an alias whose value begins with `!` is a shell command, `core.pager`, `core.editor`, `credential.helper` and `core.hooksPath` all name programs, `--exec` and `--upload-pack` take one directly, and `git bisect run` exists to run one. A command line of the shape `git -c alias.<name>='!...' <name>` reads as an ordinary Git command to the rule and as an arbitrary shell command to Git, which then holds the keyring and every Unix socket on the machine.

The grant is now refused for those invocations. None of them is a signing operation, so nothing a signing flow needs is lost, and a command that does need signing and is refused fails visibly rather than silently running with the keyring exposed.

Points worth a reviewer's attention:

- Configuration overrides are checked against an allow list of keys that cannot name a program, rather than a deny list. Git keeps adding keys that can name one, and a deny list would sit one release behind.
- `-c` is only read as a configuration override before the subcommand. After it, `-c` belongs to the subcommand — `git commit -c <commit>` reuses a commit message — and reading that as a configuration key would refuse the grant to an ordinary signing command. `--exec`, `--upload-pack` and `--receive-pack` are the other way round: they belong to the subcommand, so the whole argument list is scanned for them.
- The subcommand is resolved with the existing `getCommandSubcommand` helper, so a subcommand's own argument cannot be mistaken for one; `git commit -m submodule` keeps the grant.
- The check runs over the whole invocation next to the existing Docker check, since the grant covers the process tree and one such command anywhere in a chain is enough to pass the keyring on.

The environment can redirect what Git runs just as effectively as the arguments can, through `GIT_CONFIG_*`, `GIT_SSH_COMMAND`, `PATH` and others, so `TreeSitterCommandParser` now reports the assignments that prefix a command instead of discarding them, and `ITerminalSandboxCommand` carries them. The field is left off entirely when there are none, so the common shape is unchanged.

One consequence worth calling out explicitly, since it is a behaviour change rather than a pure tightening: an invocation carrying one of those assignments no longer receives the grant, and that includes `GIT_EDITOR=true git commit -S`. The command still runs sandboxed; it just does not get the keyring. I took the fail-closed reading here, but that is a judgement call and I am happy to narrow the list if you would rather keep those working.

## Testing

`src/vs/platform/sandbox/test/common/terminalSandboxRuntimeConfigurationPerOperation.test.ts` adds 49 tests. The refusal side covers alias, pager, editor, hooks path, credential helper, ssh command, external diff, gpg program, filter and pack-objects-hook overrides, mixed case, `--exec` in both spellings, `--upload-pack`, `--receive-pack`, `bisect`, `submodule`, `filter-branch`, a chained invocation, and the environment assignments. The retained side covers signing commits and tags, rebase, merge, cherry-pick, revert, push, status, log, `-C` and `--git-dir`, benign `-c` overrides, and a commit message that happens to name a guarded subcommand.

26 of the 49 fail without the change while the 23 retained-behaviour cases keep passing.

The existing suites are unaffected: 1365 passing across all `sandbox` and `chatAgentTools` tests, including the 70 in `terminalSandboxService.test.ts` that assert the grant survives for `git commit -S`, `git rebase main`, `git push` and `git status`. `treeSitterCommandParser.test.ts` has two expectations updated for the reported assignments and is at 212 passing.

`tsc -p src` and `eslint` are clean.

## Note on reporting

This was reported through MSRC (case 127366), acknowledged, and closed with a fix planned; it has not landed on `main` as of this branch point. I am sending the change here rather than opening a public issue describing it, since SECURITY.md asks that issues not be used for this. Happy to open one if you would prefer the PR to reference it, and equally happy to close this if it collides with work already in progress.

title: Authorize the extension id passed to SecretStorage RPC
body:
`MainThreadSecretState` takes `extensionId` off the wire and uses it directly as the storage namespace for `$getPassword`, `$setPassword`, `$deletePassword` and `$getKeys`. Nothing checks that the extension host on the other end of the connection has anything to do with that extension.

`ExtensionSecrets` does bind the id to the calling extension's own identifier, but it does so on the extension host side — the far side of the connection — so it cannot be what the workbench relies on. A remote extension host runs code from the remote machine, while the store it reaches here is the local secret store, holding the tokens of UI extensions such as the authentication providers. A remote host could therefore name a local extension and read, overwrite or delete its secrets.

The change resolves the extension's running location on the workbench side, which is the trusted answer to where an extension actually runs, and refuses the call when its kind differs from the connection's kind. This follows the same shape as the `extHostContext.extensionHostKind` check already used in `mainThreadAuthentication.ts` and `mainThreadMcp.ts`.

Two details worth a reviewer's attention:

- An extension this window does not run is refused as well, because secrets belonging to a disabled or uninstalled extension can still be sitting in the store, and nothing legitimate asks for a namespace with no running extension behind it.
- Identifiers are compared through `ExtensionIdentifier.toKey`, so case cannot be used to slip past the check.

This separates hosts, not extensions within a host. Extensions sharing a host share a process and can already reach each other's state, so a check at that granularity would not be a boundary; I have left it alone deliberately rather than by oversight.

## Testing

`src/vs/workbench/api/test/browser/mainThreadSecretState.test.ts` adds 11 tests: a remote host naming a local extension is refused for get, set, delete and keys, with the stored secret asserted unchanged in each case; a differently-cased identifier does not get through; the local host naming a remote extension is refused the same way; an extension this window does not run is refused; and each host reaches its own extension normally, including through a differently-cased identifier.

Seven of the eleven fail without the change and all four positive-path tests keep passing, so they are pinning the behaviour rather than restating it.

`tsc -p src` and `eslint` are clean.

title: Fix unresponsive compact menu bar in the Modern UI activity bar
body:
## Description

With `workbench.experimental.modernUI` enabled, the compact (hamburger) menu bar in the activity bar appears unresponsive — clicking it either does nothing visible or renders a sliver of a menu clipped into the icon rail. Disabling the setting was the known workaround.

**Root cause:** `floatingPanels.css` centered the rail's icon column with `transform: translateX(...)` on `.part.activitybar > .content`. A transformed element becomes the containing block for its `position: fixed` descendants, so the compact menu bar's menu (`.menubar-menu-items-holder`, placed by `Menubar.showCustomMenu` in viewport coordinates) was offset by the rail's position and then clipped away by the part's `overflow: hidden`.

### Changes

- **`floatingPanels.css`** — centering is now a `padding-left` with the same computed offset, which no longer establishes a containing block or stacking context. The comment records why this must stay a plain layout offset.

  ```css
  .monaco-workbench.floating-panels .part.activitybar > .content {
  -	transform: translateX(calc((var(--modern-ui-activitybar-lane) - 2px) / 2));
  +	padding-left: calc((var(--modern-ui-activitybar-lane) - 2px) / 2);
  }
  ```

- **`modernUI.contribution.test.ts`** — new test `keeps floating rail overlays anchored to the viewport` builds the compact menu bar DOM inside a floating rail and asserts the fixed menu keeps its viewport coordinates and full width. It fails against the previous CSS (`left: 256, top: 142` instead of `240/120`).

### Notes for review

Rendering is unaffected: `PartLayout.layout` gives `.content` an inline `width`, and `.content` is `content-box`, so the padding grows its border box exactly as the translate shifted it. Comparing both variants in Chromium, `.action-item`, `.action-label`, `.active-item-indicator`, `.badge`, `.menubar` and the hamburger glyph land at identical rects at both densities; only the fixed menu moves. Nothing measures the content area's DOM width — the composite bar's overflow computation uses the `Dimension` passed from `ActivitybarPart.layout`.

title: Report a browser tool failure with an empty message as a failure
body:
Follow-up to #330707. That PR merged with two review points from @dmitrivMS unaddressed. I replied at the time saying both were fixed in it, on the mistaken belief that it had not merged yet. It had, and neither change landed. Nothing has touched `errorResult` since.

## An empty error message reports success to the model

`errorResult` set `toolResultError` to the raw message, unlike the conversion sixteen lines above it, which already falls back:

```ts
...(result.error !== undefined ? { toolResultError: result.error || failedMessage, toolResultMessage: failedMessage } : {}),
```

So `errorResult('')` left `toolResultError` falsy, and that is the sole error signal downstream:

```ts
// agentHostSessionHandler.ts
const isError = !!result.toolResultError;
...
success: !isError,
```

The call was serialized as a success with `error: undefined`, while `toolResultMessage` still set the completed row to "Browser action failed". The user saw a failure, the model was told it succeeded.

Three call sites can produce an empty message, all of the form `e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e)`, which is `''` for both `new Error()` and `throw ''`: `playwrightInvoke` in `browserToolHelpers.ts` (used by the click, type, hover, drag, navigate and screenshot tools), the deferred-result wait in `runPlaywrightCodeTool.ts`, and `handleDialogBrowserTool.ts`. The fourth site prefixes its message and was never affected.

The fix falls back to the same label the conversion uses, for the content part as well as the error, so the model is given a reason rather than an empty string.

## The comment on `failedMessage` was wrong

It asserted these tools "declare only an `invocationMessage`". They do not: the screenshot tool prepares "Captured browser screenshot", and `didExecuteTool` keeps a prepared past-tense label unless the result carries a `toolResultMessage`. That is the mechanism @dmitrivMS described, and the comment still stated the version I had wrong. Rewritten to say what the constant is actually for.

## Tests

`errorResult with an empty message still reports a failure` covers both the error signal and the content part. It mirrors the existing empty-message test for `invokeFunctionResultToToolResult`, which had no `errorResult` counterpart. Without the source change it fails on the first assertion; with it the file is 6 passing. No new type errors, 349 before and after.

*AI disclosure: this comment and the related code were written with the assistance of AI.*

title: fix: wait for settled empty branch changeset in Agent Host E2E tests (build fix for vscode-engineering#3777)
body:
## Build failure

The Agent Host E2E Conformance test `an edit restored in the same turn leaves no branch change` (in `src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/e2e/suites/changesetSuite.ts`) failed with:

```
expected [] to deeply equal [ { diff: { added: 0, removed: 1 }, id: seed.txt, reviewed: false } ]
```

The assertion expected an empty branch changeset but observed a single edit reporting `seed.txt` as `{ added: 0, removed: 1 }` — i.e. git saw `seed.txt` as a zero-byte file (its one committed line removed, nothing added).

## Root cause

The test drives a bang (`!node`) turn that rewrites `seed.txt` twice: first to `changed`, then back to its committed content `seed\n` (via `writeFileTwiceBase64Command`). `fs.writeFileSync` opens with `O_TRUNC`, so the file passes through a transient **zero-byte window** during the double write. The final on-disk content equals HEAD, so a `git diff` taken after the turn completes deterministically yields `[]`.

The test, however, asserted on the **first** `changeset/contentChanged` notification (`await changed`) and then read state. A file-monitor–driven recompute can sample the working tree during the truncate window and publish a **torn** intermediate changeset (`{ added: 0, removed: 1 }` for the momentarily zero-byte file). The turn-completion recompute then supersedes it with the settled empty diff, but the test had already resolved on the torn event and read the intermediate state.

This is a test-synchronization defect: the producer (branch changeset) is correct — it converges to `[]` once the turn's writes settle — but the test observed a transient intermediate rather than the final state. Two sibling tests in the same suite (`ignored files do not appear in a branch changeset`, `a file created and deleted in one turn leaves no branch change`) use the identical first-`contentChanged` pattern and are exposed to the same race.

## How the fix works

Adds a `waitForEmptyBranchChangeset` helper that polls `changesetState` until the changeset reports status `ready` with zero files, reusing the suite's existing `retry` utility (the same settle-then-assert pattern already used by `waitForChangesetFiles`). The three affected tests now wait for the settled empty state after the bang turn instead of racing on the first `changeset/contentChanged`. No production code changes are required because the branch changeset already converges correctly at turn completion.

## Rollback evaluation

Recommendation: **Do not roll back**. Public culprit: #333922 (`2583f029c67`) introduced this test and the `writeFileTwiceBase64Command` double-write helper. The commit adds valuable E2E coverage; the defect is a narrow observation race in the test synchronization, and a bounded fix-forward is clearly safer than reverting the coverage expansion. Owners to consult: `@roblourens`.

## Validation

`git`, `node`, and `tsc` are blocked in the execution sandbox, so the TypeScript compile and the E2E suite could not be run here. The change reuses existing suite helpers (`retry`, `changesetState`) and types with no new imports, and mirrors the established settled-state polling pattern already present in `waitForChangesetFiles`.

## Risk

Low. The change is confined to test synchronization in a single E2E suite file; no production code is touched. The new helper only relaxes the observation timing to the settled state, so it cannot mask a genuine non-empty changeset regression — a persistently non-empty `ready` state would still fail via the `retry` timeout.

## Recommended reviewer

Recommended owner: `@roblourens`

title: agentHost: ignore host notice turns when resolving the last turn
body:
Fixes the Agents Window intermittently showing an empty changeset for the last turn.

## Cause

Agent Merge posts status notices ("Agent Merge is enabled for `x`", "…was disabled because its pull request is closed") as **complete, hidden turns** via `_writeAgentMergeNotice`. They never reach the provider and never capture a checkpoint, but both last-turn resolvers took `turns.at(-1)`:

```ts
return chatState.activeTurn?.id ?? chatState.turns?.at(-1)?.id;
```

So the notice became "the last turn" and its permanently-empty changeset replaced the real one. Because the notice's *request row* is hidden from the transcript, the chat still ended on the user's turn — so the UI looked correct while the changeset was silently wrong.

Traced in an agent host log bundle (session `a4a41e80`):

| time | event |
|---|---|
| 09:38:15.159 | `chat/turnStarted` `7a5d8bd1…` — `systemNotification`, request-hidden |
| 09:38:15.210 | `chat/turnComplete` `7a5d8bd1…`, duration 0 |
| 09:38:15.388 | client re-points its subscription to `…/changeset/turn/7a5d8bd1…` |
| 09:38:15.639 | snapshot → `{"status":"ready","files":[]}` |
| 09:38:16.518 | the real last turn `10b7d721…` reports its files — nothing subscribed any more |

Regression introduced by #332598.

The same notice also displaced the **session** changeset's git fast path: `_latestTurnIdAcrossChats` found no checkpoint for it, so `_tryComputeGitDiffs` fell back to the edit tracker, which cannot see terminal-tool edits.

## Fix

`isHostNoticeTurn` / `lastAttributableTurnId` in `sessionState.ts`, used by both `AgentHostLastTurnChangeset` (client) and `_latestTurnIdAcrossChats` (host).

A *visible* system notification — a background-agent completion, an Agent Merge repair prompt — is a real turn that runs the agent and owns real edits, and is deliberately **not** matched.

## Diagnostics

An empty per-turn changeset was indistinguishable from a turn that changed nothing, so the remaining paths stayed invisible in logs:

- Every branch of `_computeSingleFolderTurnDiffs` that can return `[]` now logs why (no checkpoint pair → edit-tracker fallback, git returning nothing, no working directory, the `parent === current` no-op).
- `showBlob` discarded git's error entirely, so a timeout or pruned ref reached the user only as `git blob not found`. It now logs the real reason. Its budget goes 5s → 15s: logs show git blowing 5s under startup contention, and a timeout there drops a diff's original side.

## Reviewer notes

- This fixes the trigger I could prove. Other paths can also produce an empty last-turn changeset — failed checkpoint capture, overlapping turns, and multi-root sessions where `filterChangesToPrimaryWorkingDirectory` hides changes outside `root[0]`. The new logging is what makes those identifiable from a log bundle. I left the multi-root filter alone as it looks deliberate (the Changes tree is single-root).
- Both new tests were verified to fail without the fix; the host one reproduces the exact symptom (`diffCalls: []`, `files: []`).

## Validation

`tsc --project src/tsconfig.json` 0 errors · eslint clean · `agentHostChangesetService` 29 · `agentHostGitService` 53 · `agentService` 407 · `localAgentHostSessionsProvider` 216 (×3 browsers) · `sessionTurnChanges`/`sessionChangesService`/`changesViewService` 8/4/9

title: test: stabilize empty Agent Host changesets
body:
## Summary

- subscribe to empty branch changesets only after the local turn completes
- queue a fresh branch recompute behind stale setup work
- apply the synchronization to all three empty-final-state scenarios

## Root cause

The conformance test created a session, subscribed to its branch changeset, and then ran a local `!node` command that briefly changed a tracked file before restoring its original contents. Session materialization, Git-state refresh, the implicit session subscription, and the explicit branch subscription can each schedule branch recomputation. The changeset state can report `ready` while another queued recompute is still pending.

Local instrumentation observed three pre-turn empty `changeset/contentChanged` publications for one setup. In build [470746](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/a6d41577-0fa3-498e-af22-257312ff0545/_build/results?buildId=470746&view=logs&j=193e9987-1fae-53fa-a82e-3ae14c27c30d&t=947af107-991d-500d-0eee-76fd05e265dc), one stale setup recompute overlapped the command and sampled the tracked file while `writeFileSync` had truncated it, publishing a transient one-line deletion. The test accepted that publication before the post-turn empty branch state.

The revised test starts the local turn before directly subscribing to the branch. Its explicit post-turn subscription schedules a fresh recompute after stale setup work; every recompute from that point sees the restored filesystem.

## Why it surfaced now

The test had a latent synchronization bug since it was added, but recent changes altered its timing surface:

- [#333110](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/333110) changed session materialization to always recompute current changeset subscriptions instead of only draining a deferred refresh, increasing duplicate setup work.
- [#333922](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/333922) added eleven conformance scenarios before the changeset suite and moved this test from the 37th use of a shared host to the 9th use of the next host. Its expansion-only product build `470377` passed, so this is a timing change rather than a deterministic regression.
- The Copilot SDK/runtime bump is not on the tested path: `LocalCommandContribution` handles the `!node` turn before `agent.chats.sendMessage`, and the scenario is registered as no-model-traffic conformance coverage. The immediately preceding successful build, failed build, and two immediately following successful builds all used the same Copilot versions.
- The failed source revision changed notebook attachment handling only; the immediately preceding and following product revisions passed this test.

I searched prior failed Linux Electron task logs containing this test and found no earlier occurrence of the exact assertion.

## Validation

- `npm run compile`
- hygiene on `changesetSuite.ts`
- focused revised scenario: 20 consecutive passes
- grouped empty-final-state scenarios: 3 passing
- prior PR revision passed Linux, macOS, and Windows Electron CI before the stronger synchronization follow-up

(Written by Copilot)

title: clipboard: fix OSC 52 writes in web by typing the target
body: Fixes #318254, and the shape of the API that allowed it. Same bug as #318255, which fixes it minimally in four lines. That one should land first if you prefer the smaller change; this removes the class of defect behind it. ## Problem `IClipboardService` declares `writeText(text: string, type?: string)`. Only two values are ever legal, and `NativeClipboardService` already says so by narrowing its own signature to `'selection' | 'clipboard'`, but the contract does not. So `undefined` and `'clipboard'` are two spellings of the same target, and every implementation has to know they are synonyms. `NativeClipboardService` gets this for free because Electron collapses them. `BrowserClipboardService` does not, and files `'clipboard'` into an in-memory `Map` instead of writing it out. Because the parameter is `string`, `if (type)` looks exhaustive while actually being a catch-all over an infinite set. It was written in [45552c0a2d4](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/45552c0a2d406917e153734bdb0c7b423f5c4a55#diff-853e597d65208ed60f14e8d5c6f3c35eb36943262243c3983a70706fe9863c5f) (2020) as one of three "unsupported in web" stubs and was correct for every caller that existed then. It became wrong years later when the terminal started passing `'clipboard'`, with nothing to force a revisit. ## Change Replace the untyped parameter with a closed union: ```ts export type ClipboardTarget = 'system' | 'primary'; ``` - One spelling per target. `'clipboard'` is gone as a value, so there is no synonym rule left to remember. - Implementations `switch` over both cases with `assertNever`, so a third target becomes a compile error rather than a silent no-op. - `mapTextToType: Map` becomes `primarySelectionText: string | undefined`. The open-ended map only existed to model a domain that was never open-ended. - Electron's naming is confined to the Electron boundary via `toElectronClipboardType`, instead of leaking into the platform contract. - The workbench browser service no longer smuggles `type = 'vscode-tests'` through the same parameter to force in-memory behaviour under extension tests; that is now an explicit flag. - The OSC 52 narrowing at the terminal call site is named and documented, including that `q`, `s` and `0`-`7` deliberately collapse onto the system clipboard, as xterm.js's own provider does. - The target is named `primary` rather than `selection`, to match X11's own wording: ICCCM [§2.6.1](https://tronche.com/gui/x/icccm/sec-2.html#s-2.6.1) is explicit that PRIMARY, SECONDARY and CLIPBOARD are all *selections*, so `'selection'` names the category rather than the member. VS Code's own description of `editor.selectionClipboard` already says "the Linux primary clipboard". Happy to keep `'selection'` if you would rather avoid the churn; the substance here is removing the synonym, which works under either spelling. Deliberately unchanged: the set of supported targets, the clipboard-read permission prompt, and desktop behaviour. Electron already defaults to `'clipboard'` when `type` is omitted, so passing it explicitly is equivalent. ## Validation - `tsc --project ./src/tsconfig.json --noEmit`: 100 pre-existing errors on `main`, 99 on this branch, set-diff shows zero introduced. The rest are missing optional native modules and SDK drift in my environment, all reproducible on unmodified `main`. - `npm run test-node`: 15771 passing, 195 pending, 0 failing. - `npm run test-browser -- --browser chromium`: 25855 passing, 139 pending, 0 failing. - The closed union located all five call sites at compile time, two of which I had missed by grep (`selectionClipboard.ts:129` and `terminal.clipboard.contribution.ts:101`). Under `type?: string` both would have compiled silently. `./scripts/code-server.sh` -> open a terminal -> seed the clipboard with something recognisable -> run ```sh printf '\033]52;c;%s\a' "$(printf 'Hello, OSC 52!' | base64)" ``` -> paste at the next prompt. The clipboard was seeded with `nothing-copied-yet` first, so a dropped write shows up instead of failing silently. Before, the write is dropped and the paste returns the stale clipboard: After, the paste returns the OSC 52 payload: Also cross-checked with `navigator.clipboard.writeText` wrapped in the page, so the result is attributable to the OSC 52 path and not to some other clipboard write: never called before the change, called with the payload after. A UTF-8 payload (`héllo 日本語 🎉`) round-trips intact.

title: Declare defaults for the accessibility signal delay settings
body:
Fixes #286430

## Problem

The three `accessibility.signalOptions.experimental.delays.*` settings (`general`, `warningAtPosition`, `errorAtPosition`) are `object` settings that declare `default` values on their properties only, without a `default` for the setting itself. The configuration registry therefore registers an empty object as the default:

- The settings editor renders an empty table with an "Add Item" button instead of the default rows, and "Preferences: Open Default Settings (JSON)" shows `{}` for the three settings.
- `AccessibilitySignalService.getDelayMs` reads `value.sound` and `value.announcement` from that empty object when the settings are not configured, so the documented delays are not applied.

These are the only object settings in the core that rely on property level defaults alone.

## Fix

Declare the object defaults explicitly, using the values already documented on the properties (`announcement: 3000`, `sound: 400` for general, `sound: 1000` for the two position signals). The settings editor now shows the default rows, and the runtime default matches the documentation. Users who configured the settings themselves are not affected.

## How to test

1. Open the settings editor and search for `accessibility.signalOptions.experimental.delays`.
2. Before this change: each of the three settings shows an empty table with an "Add Item" button.
3. After this change: each setting lists its `announcement` and `sound` rows with the default values, and "Preferences: Open Default Settings (JSON)" shows the objects instead of `{}`.

"Reveal in Explorer View" from the search results context menu has its own implementation in `RevealInSideBarForSearchResultsAction`. It always opens the Explorer view container in the primary side bar and then looks the Explorer view up in that container. When the Explorer view has been moved somewhere else (the panel, the secondary side bar, or its own container), the primary side bar switches to the Files container without the view, the lookup returns `undefined`, and the action fails with:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'setExpanded')
    at .../contrib/search/browser/searchActionsFind.js
```

Nothing is revealed or selected. The same command from an editor tab or from the Open Editors view works, because `revealInExplorer` resolves the view through the views service wherever it currently lives.

## Fix

The search action now delegates to the generic `revealInExplorer` command with the file match resource, and the side bar specific code is removed. One consequence to be aware of: for a resource outside the workspace, the generic command falls back to revealing the Open Editors view, which matches the behavior of the editor tab context menu. Previously the search action did nothing in that case.

Two unit tests cover the delegation and the no-argument path.

## How to test

1. Open a folder and run "View: Move View", pick "Folders", and move it into the panel (for example next to Problems) or into the secondary side bar.
2. Search for any text, right click a file result, and choose "Reveal in Explorer View".
3. Before this change: the primary side bar shows an empty Explorer container, the file is not selected, and the error above is logged in the developer tools console.
4. After this change: the file is selected and focused in the Explorer view wherever it lives. With the default layout the behavior is unchanged.

The shared compact-button renderer now exposes a small configuration hook. - inherits the button label's UI font, line height, and foreground, while using the quieter `label2` type role;

- keeps platform-native chord notation from `KeybindingLabel`.

The background treatment adds a subtle surface around the complete shortcut using existing keybinding-label colors and design tokens.

Because hidden settings are excluded from automatic experimental-default processing, the contribution explicitly resolves the treatment. title: fix: path, URI, JSON edit utility bugs
body:
fix: path, URI, JSON edit, and shell quoting bugs in utility modules

Five distinct correctness bugs across four files:

## 1. extpath.ts -- isRootOrDriveLetter checks wrong length variable

`isRootOrDriveLetter` normalizes the path then guards on `path.length` instead
of `pathNormalized.length`. A path like `C:\\` (4 chars) normalizes to `C:\`
(3 chars), but `path.length > 3` incorrectly rejects it. Same issue on the
drive-letter-only `=== 2` check.

## 2. jsonEdit.ts -- last-array-element removal corrupts the array

The deletion span was computed as `parentEndOffset - 2 - offset`.
`parentEndOffset` is one past the closing `]`, so the correct span is
`parentEndOffset - 1 - offset`. The extra `-1` left a stale character before
`]`, producing invalid JSON after removing the last array element.

## 3. terminalEnvironment.ts -- escapeNonWindowsPath uses invalid POSIX quoting

The `singleQuotes` branch produced `'path with '\'' embedded quote'`.
Single-quoted strings in POSIX sh/bash/zsh are literal -- `\'` inside them is
not an escape sequence, it ends the string and emits a literal backslash-quote.
Fixed to `$'...'` (ANSI-C quoting), which correctly handles embedded single
quotes and matches the existing `bothQuotes` branch.

## 4. terminalEnvironment.ts -- collapseTildePath matches home path anywhere

`normalizedPath.includes(normalizedUserHome)` matches the home directory
anywhere in the path, e.g. `/tmp/backup/home/viraj/file` would incorrectly
collapse. Also susceptible to prefix collisions like `/home/virajfoo`.
Fixed to `normalizedPath.startsWith(normalizedUserHome + '/')` with an
additional equality check for the exact-home case.

## 5. uri.ts -- password in userinfo not fully percent-encoded

The password segment was encoded with `encoder(..., false, true)`
(`isAuthority=true`), which leaves `:` unencoded (safe in hostnames).
Per RFC 3986 ss. 3.2.1, `:` inside a password MUST be percent-encoded.
Fixed to `encoder(..., false, false)`.

## Summary

Make **Open in Agents** from an editor connected to an Agent Host Dev Container open the new-session page for the corresponding local folder and preselect Dev Container execution when the feature is enabled.

<details>
<summary>Session Context</summary>

Key decisions from the development session:

</details>

title: fix: memory leak in shared process logger
body: ### Details Opening and closing a window registers per-window log resources in every `LoggerChannelClient`, including the long-lived shared process. The IPC event contains serialized URIs. Added resources were revived, but removed resources were passed directly to `AbstractLoggerService`. `ResourceMap` therefore derived `[object Object]` instead of the original URI key and could not delete the entries. The shared-process measurement opened and gracefully closed 37 windows. It found 211 additional `ResourceMapEntry` objects. Heap paths point to `LoggerChannelClient._loggers`; the keys include each closed window's `renderer.log`, `network.log`, `views.log`, notebook rendering log, and output logs. ### Change Revive removed logger resource URIs before deregistering them. Add a regression test that sends serialized added and removed events through the client and verifies that the logger entry is deleted. ### Before After 37 window open/close cycles, the shared process had 211 additional `ResourceMapEntry` objects. ### After After the same 37 window open/close cycles, the shared-process measurement found no named-function leak rows. ### Test Video Three window open/close cycles on the candidate build: [window-open-close.webm](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/3dc73ed3-8e0a-44b3-b56a-0b2d7c5a85cb)

title: Agent Host: accept claude.ai keychain logins in the Claude native account check
body:
Fixes #333738

### Problem

With the Claude agent host in native mode (`claudeUseCopilotProxy: false`, or the signed-out fallback from #331739), a claude.ai subscription signed in with `claude login` (credential in the macOS keychain) is reported as "not set up". The native model catalog comes back empty and the Agents window pushes the user to GitHub sign-in, or to `claude setup-token` plus a plaintext `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` in `settings.json`:

```
[Claude] Native account check: setUp=false, provider=firstParty, tokenSource=absent, apiKeySource=absent
[Claude] Models refreshed (merged). Count: 0
```

### Root cause

`isClaudeAccountSetUp` (`src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/claude/claudeTransportMode.ts`) infers "set up" from `tokenSource` / `apiKeySource` only. Those fields name the environment variable a credential came from, so a keychain login sets neither. For that login the SDK's `accountInfo()` answers with the account itself — `subscriptionType`, `email`, `organization` — plus `apiProvider: 'firstParty'`, which the check deliberately does not treat as a presence signal. Every branch is false, by construction. Full analysis in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/333738#issuecomment-5524769330.

Measured on macOS with the credential in the login keychain and no `ANTHROPIC_*` / `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` in the environment (SDK 0.3.258 typings, CLI 2.1.259), `accountInfo()` returns exactly:

```
{ email, organization, subscriptionType: "Claude Max", apiProvider: "firstParty" }
```

### Fix

- `isClaudeAccountSetUp`: after the unchanged third-party and token / API key branches, also accept a first-party account that reports `subscriptionType` or `email` — the fields the SDK's `AccountInfo` type exposes for a claude.ai login (`loggedIn` / `authMethod` from `claude auth status` are not part of `AccountInfo`, so they are not used). title: Clarify Agent Merge notice scope and use On/Off for the session merge choice
body:
## Description

Two wording changes to Agent Merge:

1. The transcript notice posted when Agent Merge behavior changes read `Agent Merge settings changed.` regardless of whether the change was made for that one session or to the defaults every session follows.
2. The session-scoped Merge Pull Request menu labeled its options `Always`/`Never`, absolutes that only hold for the setting, which applies across all sessions.

### Notices name the scope

`agentMergeConfigurationChangedNotice` now takes a required scope and heads the notice accordingly:

```
Agent Merge settings changed for this session.
Agent Merge default settings changed for all sessions.
```

`AgentMergeController` derives the scope by comparing the session overrides that produced the last announcement with the current ones — a per-session change is exactly what writes overrides, so anything else that moved the effective configuration came from the defaults. Deriving it in one place rather than passing it from each call site also attributes changes that land while a session's runtime is stopped, which the existing `announces effective session and global configuration changes while monitoring` test exercises.

To support that, `_announcedConfigurations` records the overrides alongside the configuration it resolved from.

### Session merge choice says On/Off

- Menu labels are now `On` / `Off`; `Only if Agent Merge Made No Changes` is unchanged, and its description now says it "switches itself off".
- Stored setting values remain `always` / `ifUnchanged` / `never`, unchanged in the settings editor.

### Tests and fixtures

- Updated the notice assertions in `agentMerge.test.ts` and `agentMergeController.test.ts`; the controller test now distinguishes the session heading from the global one.
- Added a `DefaultsChanged` component fixture beside the existing `ConfigurationChanged` one so both headings render.

body:
## Summary

Fix local MCP gateway disposal so gateway routes and listeners are released when their owner disposes them.

## Problem

Recent Insiders logs show a gateway being created and then reported as unknown when the workbench disposes it:

```text
15:04:37.427 [info] [McpGatewayService] Created gateway 01cd3fb5-... with 5 server(s) for client window:2
15:05:10.087 [info] [McpGateway][Workbench] Disposing local gateway: 01cd3fb5-...
15:05:10.089 [info] [McpGateway][Channel] Disposing gateway: 01cd3fb5-... for client window:2
15:05:10.090 [warning] [McpGatewayService] Attempted to dispose unknown gateway: 01cd3fb5-...
15:07:38.541 [info] [McpGatewayService] Gateway 01cd3fb5-... servers changed: 2 server(s)
```

The final line confirms the gateway remained active after disposal was requested. The same sequence occurred for another gateway in the same session.

`ProxyChannel.toService` wraps method arguments in an array, while `McpGatewayChannel` expects the raw gateway ID. Template interpolation made that array look like the correct UUID in the logs, but the array did not match the string key in the gateway map, so cleanup was skipped.

Call the channel directly with the expected argument shape, matching the existing remote disposal path, and report disposal failures.

title: agentHost: report where a subagent's task model came from
body:
## Summary

Adds `subagentTaskModelSource` to the `agentHost.turnCompleted` telemetry event for subagent turns, so we can tell where a subagent's model input came from. The value is read from the Copilot SDK's `subagent.started` event (github/copilot-agent-runtime#18727, github/copilot-sdk#2572), stored with the subagent chat reference, and emitted on the initial, nested, and resumed turns of that subagent. Root turns leave it `undefined`; unknown or absent wire values become `undefined`.

| Value | What it tracks |
| --- | --- |
| `task_argument` | The parent agent passed `task.model` |
| `subagent_configuration` | No `task.model`; the per-subagent settings entry supplied a concrete model |
| `custom_agent_definition` | No `task.model`; a user-defined custom agent's definition supplied its model |
| `unset` | Neither the task call nor structured configuration supplied a model |

This describes the source of the model input, not which model actually ran; the existing `model` column on the same row reports that. The existing `modelSelectionKind` is unchanged: it describes VS Code's top-level client selection, not subagent provenance.

## SDK compatibility

The runtime change is merged and present in the published CLI `1.0.84-2` schema. VS Code currently pins `@github/copilot-sdk` to `1.0.13`, whose generated event declarations do not yet include `taskModelSource`.

This PR intentionally uses a temporary compatibility cast in `readSubagentTaskModelSource` to read the field when present. The validation switch only forwards the four known values above. Events from runtimes that do not supply the field continue to produce `undefined`; the cast does not synthesize a value or change model selection. No SDK dependency bump is included in this PR.

Typed SDK adoption is a follow-up rather than a merge prerequisite for this compatibility implementation. Once github/copilot-sdk#2572 lands and a containing release is published and adopted:

- Remove the compatibility cast and use the generated event type directly.
- Retain the validation switch as the unknown-value guard.
- Rerun the targeted tests and verify real SDK-to-telemetry delivery with a subagent run.

## Validation - September 8, 2026

Validated head `d481e6cdf30`, including the merge of upstream main at `3c81a516ca6`.

- All **34 targeted telemetry and source-validation tests passed**.
- Editor diagnostics reported no errors in the seven changed files.
- PR-relative `git diff --check` passed.
- CI **Compile & Hygiene** and **telemetry metadata validation** passed. See the Checks tab for the remaining CI status.

The targeted tests verify event handling and telemetry propagation using injected events; they do not establish delivery of the new field from a released SDK in a real subagent run.

## How to test

```sh
./scripts/test.sh --grep "turn tracker telemetry|forwards only known subagent task model sources"
```

The `AgentSideEffects` suite asserts the field on root (`undefined`), initial, nested, and resumed subagent turns. The `CopilotAgentSession` test asserts that each known value passes through and unknown or absent values become `undefined`.

body:
Follow-up to #332799 and #333253.

## State indicator feedback

- Uses a solid yellow/amber one-stroke outer frame while a request is running; the existing chat input progress border remains unchanged. The outer frame has no looping animation or halo.
- Uses a green dotted one-stroke frame for an idle completion that has not been visited.
- Keeps the red dashed needs-input frame.
- Requires owning-window focus when determining whether a completion is visited; window activation alone does not clear an unvisited marker.
- Preserves a synchronous request-start edge when an accumulated add/complete batch is delivered after the model is already idle.
- Uses the same pending-aware idle rule as window notifications, including canceled/error-stranded queues.
- Relies on the effective `.monaco-reduce-motion` state instead of overriding it with a local OS media query.
- Clarifies the experimental setting description to match the states it now indicates.

## Chat Editor topology telemetry

Adds the count-only `chat.editorTopology` event after main-editor restoration and on coalesced topology changes involving Chat Editors:

- `openChatEditorCount`
- `visibleChatEditorCount`
- `chatEditorGroupCount`
- `visibleEditorCount`
- `editorGroupCount`

The event excludes dedicated Agents windows, is scoped to the main editor part, suppresses identical snapshots, and collects no session IDs, resources, titles, prompts, or content.

## Theme customization

Registers three independent theme colors so themes and `workbench.colorCustomizations` can style state frames without changing other UI:

- `chat.sessionStateIndicator.inProgressBorder`: defaults to `charts.yellow` in light/dark themes.
- `chat.sessionStateIndicator.unvisitedBorder`: defaults to `charts.green` in light/dark themes.
- `chat.sessionStateIndicator.needsInputBorder`: defaults to `errorForeground` in light/dark themes; the halo is derived from this color.

All three default to `contrastActiveBorder` in high-contrast themes. High-contrast mode honors explicit color overrides, suppresses the halo, and preserves solid/dotted/dashed state cues. Visited-idle sessions remain unframed.

Example (the feature still defaults to disabled):

```json
{
  "chat.experimental.sessionStateIndicator.enabled": true,
  "workbench.colorCustomizations": {
    "chat.sessionStateIndicator.inProgressBorder": "#D7BA7D",
    "chat.sessionStateIndicator.unvisitedBorder": "#44CC88",
    "chat.sessionStateIndicator.needsInputBorder": "#FF6677"

}
```

title: Admit a client tool call once, instead of racing two triggers
body:
Gives a client tool call a single event that says a client now owns it, so execution is no longer driven by two independent triggers racing.

Supersedes #330933.

## The problem

Two things independently decide that a client tool should run: the stream mapper's ready action, which drives the session-input-needed contribution to publish an execution request, and the in-process MCP handler registering the parked request. Nothing connects "a client owns this" to "the SDK is parked waiting for it", so a replayed call has no owner, an unclaimed call waits forever, and there is no bound on either.

## What this adds

A `client_tool_invoked` signal carrying the root chat, the SDK tool use id, the tool name, the input and the parent tool call id for a subagent. The Claude session fires it from the registry's fire-on-register path at the moment the MCP handler parks, so a result buffered before the SDK asked for it short-circuits and never fires. Providers opt in, and only Claude does, so Copilot and Codex take the unchanged path.

Admission is recorded in the side effects, next to the tool-call tracking already there, and stamped into the tool call's protocol meta rather than living only in a process-local map, so it survives a client reconnect. The stamp rides a re-dispatched ready that also repairs the input from the runtime's arguments. Two details that took reading rather than assuming: the reducer replaces the meta bag wholesale rather than merging, so the streamed bag is carried forward explicitly, following the existing precedent for the auto-approve stamp; and a call sitting in pending confirmation is re-readied without the confirmed flag, which the reducer treats as a refresh, so admission can never bypass a user confirmation.

The contribution then publishes a client execution request only for an admitted call, and only for an opted-in provider.

An admitted call that nobody claims within the existing client disconnect window is failed with the same error shape the ownerless path uses. The constant was moved rather than duplicated, into the dependency-light connection service both users already import. The timer no-ops if the call settled or its owning client is still active, so it cannot fire while a client is running the tool. The failure is dispatched as a server action and forwarded to the provider exactly once by the existing envelope listener, which is why the proposal's explicit forward is not carried over: on current main it would forward twice.

Rebind now keeps buffered results, because the fire-on-register path consults that buffer and a destroyed buffer would turn an answered call into a second admission. Admission is also idempotent host-side, so a re-fired invocation for a known call returns early.

## Why the proposal could not simply be rebased

#330933's base was closed, and the publish point it patches has since moved out of the side effects into a chat contribution, so its central hunk no longer exists. What was worth keeping is kept: the signal shape, the opt-in flag and its placement on the agent rather than the wire-visible capability bag, repairing the input from the runtime arguments, synthesising start and ready with the resolved owner for a replayed call, the registration ordering, and its replay and subagent test intents.

## Scope

No protocol change; admission rides the existing open meta bag and nothing under the synced protocol directory is touched. The mapper is unchanged, the workbench is unchanged, and the bound does not re-arm after no-opping for a connected owner, since a client that claims and then vanishes is the disconnect sweep's job.

## Tests

Eleven new, including that a streamed ready alone does not publish for an opted-in provider, that an invocation admits and repairs the input and publishes exactly one request, that a non-opting provider still publishes on ready, that an ownerless call fails once and forwards once, that the bound does not fire while the owner is connected and does once it is gone, that a replayed call synthesises start and ready with the owner, and that a subagent call is admitted on the subagent chat and completes back on the root chat.

Reverting only the gate fails the streamed-ready test. Across the agent host suites: 5227 passing in node, 731 in common, Copilot 1059, Codex 402, all with zero failures. No new type errors.

## Merge note

This conflicts with #334127 in one place worth deciding rather than resolving mechanically: that PR tags the owning client inside the MCP server builder, while this replaces that parameter with a callback. The tagging belongs in the session's await path, which already holds both the tool diff and the registry, whichever branch carries it.

Part of #333174.
