title: fix: treat terminal disposal during run_in_terminal as cancellation (fixes #333549)
body:
### Summary

`run_in_terminal` (the terminal chat agent tool) throws a plain `Error('The terminal was closed')` when the terminal instance is disposed while a command is in progress (or was already disposed at strategy entry). Terminal disposal mid-command is an **expected** lifecycle event (the user closed the terminal, or the process exited), but a plain `Error` propagates up through `RunInTerminalTool.invoke` and is re-thrown as an `unexpectedException`, which reaches the global unhandled-error telemetry pipeline (`onUnexpectedError`). This produces the `unhandlederror-The terminal was closed` bucket.

The fix makes the producer throw `CancellationError` — the codebase idiom for an expected abort — which `onUnexpectedError` filters out via `isCancellationError`, and which the caller already maps to `error='canceled'`.

Fixes microsoft/vscode#333549
Recommended reviewer: `@Tyriar`

### Culprit Commit

`b537b64aa360` — "Handle terminal exit while terminal tool is in progress, Fixes \#264565" by `@Tyriar` (Daniel Imms), 2025-10-24.

This commit introduced the `onDisposed` race handling in both `richExecuteStrategy.ts` and `basicExecuteStrategy.ts`, and in doing so added the `throw new Error('The terminal was closed')` statements at both the strategy-entry disposal check and the post-race disposal branch.

### Code Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[RichExecuteStrategy.execute] -->|instance disposed at entry / disposal race wins| B[throw Error 'The terminal was closed']
    B --> C[RunInTerminalTool.start]
    C --> D[RunInTerminalTool.invoke catch e]
    D -->|e not instanceof CancellationError| E[error = 'unexpectedException'; rethrow]
    E --> F[LanguageModelToolsService.invokeTool]
    F --> G[onUnexpectedError]
    G -->|not isCancellationError| H[Unhandled error telemetry bucket]
```

After the fix, the producer throws `CancellationError`, so at step D `e instanceof CancellationError` is true → `error='canceled'`, and `onUnexpectedError` filters it via `isCancellationError` before it can reach telemetry.

### Affected Files

- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/browser/executeStrategy/richExecuteStrategy.ts` — 2 throw sites (strategy-entry disposal check, post-race disposal branch).
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/browser/executeStrategy/basicExecuteStrategy.ts` — 2 throw sites (same two positions).
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/test/browser/richExecuteStrategy.test.ts` — test updated to assert `isCancellationError`.
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/test/browser/basicExecuteStrategy.test.ts` — test updated to assert `isCancellationError`.

### Repro Steps

1. Ask Copilot to run a shell command via the `run_in_terminal` tool.
2. While the command is executing, close the terminal (or have the shell process exit) so the terminal instance is disposed mid-command.
3. The disposal race resolves and the strategy throws `Error('The terminal was closed')`.
4. `RunInTerminalTool.invoke` re-throws it as `unexpectedException`, and it surfaces in unhandled-error telemetry as `unhandlederror-The terminal was closed`.

### How the Fix Works

**Chosen approach** (both strategy files): replace `throw new Error('The terminal was closed')` with `throw new CancellationError()` at each disposal site. This fixes the error at the data producer, not the crash site: terminal disposal mid-command is an expected cancellation, not an exceptional condition. `CancellationError` (message/name `'Canceled'`) is the codebase idiom for expected aborts. The immediate caller `RunInTerminalTool.invoke` already contains `e instanceof CancellationError ? 'canceled' : 'unexpectedException'`, so the cancellation flows through cleanly as `error='canceled'`, and the global `onUnexpectedError` handler already filters `CancellationError` via `isCancellationError`, so it never reaches telemetry. Both strategy files already import `CancellationError` and use it directly below these sites for token-cancellation, so this aligns the disposal path with the existing cancellation path. The two test files were updated to assert `isCancellationError` on the rejection instead of matching the removed message string.

After this change, `richExecuteStrategy.ts` and `basicExecuteStrategy.ts` cannot produce an `unexpectedException` on terminal disposal because the thrown value is now a `CancellationError`, which both the caller and `onUnexpectedError` recognize and route as an expected cancellation rather than an unhandled error.

**Alternatives considered**:
- Wrapping the throw in a try/catch at the caller — rejected because it hides the error from telemetry instead of correctly classifying the expected event at the producer.
- Suppressing the message in `onUnexpectedError` — rejected because it special-cases a string in a global handler rather than fixing the producer's error type.

### Recommended Owner

`@Tyriar` (Daniel Imms) — author of the culprit commit `b537b64aa360` and owner of the terminal chat agent tools area.

title: Use setting for dictation cleanup model experiment
body:
## Problem

The dictation cleanup experiment and the Settings UI used two separate paths:

- ExP returned the legacy `dictationLlmCleanupModel` treatment.
- Settings exposed `dictation.experimental.llmCleanupModel`, which continued to display `auto`.
- `ChatSpeechToTextService` separately read and cached the ExP treatment.

The experiment could change runtime behavior, but the visible setting did not reflect the effective model, making the experiment difficult to understand and verify.

## Fix

This PR makes `dictation.experimental.llmCleanupModel` the single application-facing source of truth and removes the separate assignment-service lookup from `ChatSpeechToTextService`:

- ExP controls the setting default through the conventional `config.dictation.experimental.llmCleanupModel` treatment name.
- `auto` follows the model supplied by that experimental default.
- An explicit user selection still overrides the experiment.
- The effective experimental model is available through the configuration system.

The ExP experiment must target `config.dictation.experimental.llmCleanupModel`; the legacy `dictationLlmCleanupModel` treatment is no longer used.

This also updates automatic experiment refreshes to replace or remove their previous default. If ExP changes from Nano or Luna back to the control model, the old model no longer remains stuck. Experiment defaults are tracked per setting so refreshing one experiment does not disturb another.

title: fix: cancel pending single-pane docked-tab reconciles on dispose (fixes #333537)
body:
### Summary The single-pane docked-tabs reconcile pipeline runs asynchronously on a `Sequencer`. When `SinglePaneDockedTabsCoordinator` is disposed (session switch / Existing-session strategy teardown / window close) while a reconcile is still queued or in-flight, that reconcile keeps running and eventually calls `IEditorGroup.replaceEditors`, which instantiates an editor pane through the coordinator's `IInstantiationService`. By then the DI tree has been disposed, so `createInstance` throws `InstantiationService has been disposed`. Impact: an unhandled error on the Agent Sessions window during teardown/session switching (Mac + Windows, 1.136 insiders). Fixes microsoft/vscode#333537 Recommended reviewer: `@sandy081` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | [`f45fb5350b9`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/f45fb5350b9) | | Author | `@sandy081` | | PR | #330573 | | Message | sessions: stabilize single pane lifecycle behavior | | Why | This commit introduced the `Sequencer`-based asynchronous reconcile pipeline (`queueReconcile` to `_reconcile` to `_reconcileCore`) with generation checkpoints, but `dispose()` was never overridden to cancel work already queued on the sequencer. A reconcile queued before disposal therefore survives teardown and reaches `replaceEditors`, which instantiates an editor pane through the disposed instantiation service. | > The reconcile pipeline has since been extended (e.g. #332365, "Show Changes view for new sessions", which added the `_reconcileForeignChangesEditors` to `replaceEditors` path seen in the stack), but the missing disposal cancellation is the underlying defect. ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Trigger as Ambient trigger participant Queue as queueReconcile / Sequencer participant Reconcile as _reconcileCore participant Group as replaceEditors participant DI as InstantiationService Trigger->>Queue: queueReconcile(target, trigger) Note over Queue: reconcile queued on Sequencer Note over DI: Root cause: coordinator disposed,
DI tree torn down,
queued reconcile not cancelled Queue->>Reconcile: _reconcile(generation) runs after dispose Reconcile->>Group: _reconcileForeignChangesEditors then replaceEditors Group->>DI: createInstance(editor pane) Note over DI: Error thrown:
InstantiationService has been disposed ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/sessions/contrib/layout/browser/singlePane/singlePaneDockedTabsCoordinator.ts` | root cause / fix | L288-L297: `queueReconcile` queues `_reconcile(generation)` on `this._sequencer`; class had no `dispose()` override to cancel queued work | | `src/vs/sessions/contrib/layout/browser/singlePane/singlePaneDockedTabsCoordinator.ts` | crash path | L458-L478: `_reconcileForeignChangesEditors` calls `group.replaceEditors([{ replacement: this._instantiationService.createInstance(...) }])` | | `src/vs/workbench/browser/editor.ts` | crash site | L78 (from stack): `instantiate` to `createInstance` | | `src/vs/platform/instantiation/common/instantiationService.ts` | throw site | L69 (from stack): `_throwIfDisposed` throws `InstantiationService has been disposed` | ### Repro Steps This is a teardown/dispose race, so it is timing-dependent: 1. Open the Agent Sessions window with a workspace-backed session that shows managed docked tabs (Changes + Files). 2. Trigger a reconcile (switch sessions, reveal the side pane, or open/close an editor) so a reconcile is queued on the sequencer. 3. Immediately dispose the coordinator before the queued reconcile resolves — e.g. switch away to a different session (Existing to New/QuickChat) or close the window while the async `replaceEditors`/`openEditor` step is pending. 4. The surviving reconcile reaches `replaceEditors` to `createInstance` on the disposed instantiation service and throws. To increase likelihood: rapidly switch sessions or close the window right after a session switch, which maximizes the window between "reconcile queued" and "reconcile reaches an editor-open call." ### How the Fix Works **Lifecycle pattern**: use-after-dispose. **Producer site**: `SinglePaneDockedTabsCoordinator.dispose()` (previously absent) — the disposable owner did not cancel callbacks already queued on `this._sequencer`. **Fix location**: `singlePaneDockedTabsCoordinator.ts` — new `dispose()` override plus entry guards in `_reconcile` / `_reconcileCore`. **Chosen approach** (producer-side; fix where the lifecycle is owned rather than guarding the crash site): - Added an `override dispose()` that bumps `this._generation` and clears `this._pending` before `super.dispose()`. title: Preserve pre-encoded characters in MCP HTTP request URLs
body:
Fixes #289129

## Problem

When an HTTP MCP server is configured with a URL that contains percent-encoded reserved characters in its path (for example AWS Bedrock AgentCore runtime ARNs, which encode `:` as `%3A` and `/` as `%2F`), the connection fails because requests are sent to the wrong path.

Root cause: the configured URL string is turned into a `URI` via `URI.parse(configuration.url)` in `McpServerLaunch.fromServerConfiguration`. `URI.parse` percent-decodes the path and query, so `runtime%2Fmy-runtime-id` becomes `runtime/my-runtime-id`, and the encoded slash is now indistinguishable from a real path separator. The network layer then serializes with `uri.toString(true)`, which cannot restore information that was already discarded at parse time.

Note the query-string half of the original report (`=` becoming `%3D`) was already fixed by #247241 (`fc5d4141f9b`) switching `.toString()` to `.toString(true)`. That change does not help the path case, because no `toString` variant can recover pre-decoded reserved characters.

## Fix

Carry the exact configured URL string on the HTTP launch alongside the parsed `URI`, and use it verbatim for the actual network requests. The parsed `uri` is still used for origin, auth discovery, and display, none of which are affected by path/query decoding.

- `McpServerTransportHTTP` (and its serialized form) gains an optional `url?: string`, carried through `toSerialized` / `fromSerialized`. Optional with a fallback so the many existing construction sites keep working unchanged.
- `fromServerConfiguration` and the native discovery adapter set `url` from the raw configured string.
- `McpHTTPHandle` sends requests to `this._launch.url ?? this._launch.uri.toString(true)` at the five network call sites (DELETE close, POST message, streamable backchannel GET, SSE GET, and the SSE endpoint `new URL(...)` base), and its request logs report the same value.
- The MCP allow/deny policy identity (`McpServer._identityFromLaunch`) and the agent-host configuration projection use the raw URL with the same fallback, so security decisions and forwarded config describe the exact request target rather than the decoded one.
- `McpServerLaunch.hash` excludes `url` from the trust nonce when it equals the legacy request URL (`uri.toString(true)`), so preserving the raw string does not invalidate existing `TrustedOnNonce` approvals. Only URLs whose pre-encoding actually changes the request target get a new nonce.

The OAuth client-secret storage key and consent bookkeeping in `mainThreadMcp.ts` are left keyed on `uri.toString(true)`: switching them changes stored-credential and consent key derivation (invalidating existing entries on upgrade) for no practical gain, since OAuth discovery is origin-based and unaffected by path encoding.

## Before / after

For a configured URL like `https://…/runtimes/arn%3Aaws%3A…%3Aruntime%2Fmy-runtime-id/invocations?qualifier=DEFAULT`:

- Before: request goes to `…/runtimes/arn:aws:…:runtime/my-runtime-id/invocations?qualifier=DEFAULT` (decoded, wrong path segments) and 404s.
- After: request goes to the exact configured URL, byte for byte.

## Tests

- `mcpTypes.test.ts`: asserts `fromServerConfiguration` preserves the raw `url` (including `%2F` / `%3A`), that the parsed `uri` drops the pre-encoding, and that the raw `url` survives the serialize / revive round trip. Adds two `McpServerLaunch.hash` cases: the nonce is unchanged when `url` matches the legacy request URL, and changes when the pre-encoding differs.
- `extHostMcp.test.ts`: a handle-level test stubs the network boundary (overriding the protected `_fetchInternal`) and asserts the initial POST is sent to the raw configured URL, plus a companion test that the handle falls back to `uri.toString(true)` when no raw `url` is present.

Ran the MCP suites locally (`mcpTypes`, `mcpRegistry`, `nativeMcpDiscoveryAdapters`, `extHostMcp`, `agentHostMcpServerSupport`), all passing, including the `mcpRegistry` trust-flow nonce tests that guard the approval behavior above.

title: Fix SelectionMatchFindAction to respect seedSearchStringFromSelection setting
body:
Fixes #300085

## Description

`editor.action.nextSelectionMatchFindAction` / `editor.action.previousSelectionMatchFindAction` (Find Next/Previous Selection, `Cmd+F3`/`Ctrl+F3` and their Shift variants) ignore the `editor.find.seedSearchStringFromSelection` setting.

`SelectionMatchFindAction.run()` in `src/vs/editor/contrib/find/browser/findController.ts` hardcodes:

```ts
const selectionSearchString = getSelectionSearchString(editor, 'single', false);
```

Passing `false` for `seedSearchStringFromNonEmptySelection` unconditionally enables the word-at-cursor fallback inside `getSelectionSearchString`, regardless of the setting. So with `editor.find.seedSearchStringFromSelection: "selection"`, pressing `Ctrl+F3` with the cursor sitting on/near a word but no active selection still overwrites the current search term with that word — the same behavior as `"always"`, even though `"selection"` is documented to only seed from an actual selection.

`StartFindAction` in the same file already derives both parameters correctly from the setting:

```ts
seedSearchStringFromSelection: editor.getOption(EditorOption.find).seedSearchStringFromSelection !== 'never' ? 'single' : 'none',
seedSearchStringFromNonEmptySelection: editor.getOption(EditorOption.find).seedSearchStringFromSelection === 'selection',
```

This PR makes `SelectionMatchFindAction.run()` follow the same logic: skip seeding entirely when the setting is `"never"`, and pass `seedSearchStringFromNonEmptySelection = true` when it's `"selection"` so an empty selection no longer falls back to the word at the cursor.

## Testing

Added `issue #300085: Find Next Selection respects seedSearchStringFromSelection: selection` to `src/vs/editor/contrib/find/test/browser/findController.test.ts`: selects a word, runs `NextSelectionMatchFindAction`, then moves the cursor onto a different word with no selection and runs the action again, asserting the search string is unchanged rather than replaced by the word at the new cursor position.

## Verification

I don't have Visual Studio's C++ build tools set up in this environment, so `npm ci` can't build the native modules needed for the full Electron test run, and I didn't want to burn a lot of time compiling the whole project just to execute one test through Playwright, per the guidance in `.github/copilot-instructions.md` to prefer the smallest targeted verification over a full build/test run when confident in a change.

What I did verify:
- `npx tsc --project ./src/tsconfig.json --noEmit --skipLibCheck` — no errors in either changed file (the only errors reported are pre-existing `Cannot find module 'electron'` ones caused by `--ignore-scripts`, unrelated to this change).
- Manual review confirming the fix mirrors `StartFindAction`'s already-shipped, already-tested derivation of `seedSearchStringFromSelection`/`seedSearchStringFromNonEmptySelection` from the same setting, in the same file.

I'm flagging this explicitly rather than claiming a full test run I didn't do.

title: Center full-width characters in two monospace cells
body:
Adds an opt-in rendering and wrapping mode that forces full-width graphemes (CJK, Hangul, full-width Latin/digits, emoji, …) to occupy **exactly two monospace cells**, with the glyph centered inside that fixed-width box, instead of relying on the font's natural advance width.

New setting: `editor.forceFullwidthCharacterWidth` (boolean, **default `false`**). It is additionally gated on `fontInfo.isMonospace`, and is skipped for any line containing RTL characters.

The approach and its trade-offs (fixed-width spans vs. letter-spacing, grapheme clustering, bidi handling) are documented in `src/vs/editor/test/common/viewLayout/fullwidth-character-centering.md`.

Touched surfaces: view line renderer, `viewLine` pixel-offset reading, `RangeUtil`, both line-breaks computers (monospace + DOM), view model wrapping settings, GPU renderer eligibility, sticky scroll, ghost text, diff editor view zones, accessible diff viewer, and rich screen reader content.

---

## Manual UI verification checklist

Boxes are ticked as each behavior is verified.

**Setup** — monospace font, `"editor.forceFullwidthCharacterWidth": true`, and a scratch file containing:

```
AＡA 1１1 | ｶタカナ漢字 | ，。、；：？！ | 👩‍💻Ａ | 擦́ | ك漢字 | 𠀋𠀍 | 한글 | →∑
```

### Core rendering & alignment

- [x] Full-width Latin (`ＡＢＣ`), full-width digits (`１２３`) and CJK (`漢字`/`かな`/`カナ`) are centered in a 2-cell grid; adjacent ASCII columns stay aligned
- [ ] Stacking a CJK line directly above an ASCII line, the columns line up on the character grid
- [ ] Halfwidth katakana (`ｶ`) and ambiguous-width characters (`→`, `∑`) are **not** widened
- [ ] Full-width punctuation (`，。、；：？！`) gets two cells like other full-width characters
- [ ] Emoji and ZWJ emoji sequences (`👩‍💻`) render as one two-cell box, not one box per code point
- [ ] Combining marks and variation selectors (`擦́`) stay attached to their base glyph — no orphaned accents
- [ ] Surrogate pairs (`𠀋`) render as a single box, never split
- [ ] Syntax colors, semantic tokens and bracket pair colorization are unchanged on CJK lines
- [ ] Long line past `editor.stopRenderingLineAfter` (10k chars) containing CJK still renders and truncates correctly

### Caret & cursor

- [ ] Arrowing left/right through full-width text moves the caret exactly two cells at a time, no half-cell drift
- [ ] Caret sits flush against the box edges, not the glyph edges — the centering space belongs to the character
- [ ] `Home`/`End`, word-wise motion and `Ctrl/Alt+Left/Right` land on grapheme boundaries
- [ ] Status bar column indicator matches the caret position
- [ ] Multi-cursor (`Alt+Click`, `Ctrl/Cmd+Alt+Down`) aligns across mixed CJK and ASCII lines
- [ ] Column selection (`Shift+Alt+drag`) produces a straight rectangle across mixed CJK/ASCII lines
- [ ] IME composition (Japanese/Chinese/Korean input) anchors the candidate window correctly and commits in place
- [ ] No caret jitter while typing full-width characters

### Selection & mouse

- [ ] Drag-selecting full-width text highlights whole two-cell boxes, with no gaps or overlaps between adjacent characters
- [ ] Clicking the blank left half of a centered glyph places the caret **before** it; the right half places it **after**
- [ ] Double-click word selection and triple-click line selection cover whole graphemes
- [ ] Hover widget anchors at the correct character

### Decorations

- [ ] Squiggles and underlines align with the centered glyph spans
- [ ] Find-match, selection and word-occurrence highlights box the full two cells
- [ ] Bracket-match highlights and inline background decorations align correctly
- [ ] A decoration that starts or ends mid-grapheme falls back to normal rendering without splitting the grapheme

### Word wrap

- [ ] `"editor.wordWrap": "on"` with `"editor.wrappingStrategy": "simple"` — wraps at two-cell boundaries, never mid-grapheme
- [ ] Same with `"editor.wrappingStrategy": "advanced"` (DOM-based computer)
- [ ] Both strategies produce the **same** wrap points for the same content
- [ ] `editor.wordWrapColumn` and `editor.wordBreak: "keepAll"` behave correctly for full-width text
- [ ] `wrappingIndent` (`same` / `indent` / `deepIndent`) — wrapped continuation lines align correctly
- [ ] Narrow editor width where only the indent fits: no degenerate or infinite wrapping

title: Preserve pre-encoded characters in MCP HTTP request URLs
body:
## Problem

When an HTTP MCP server is configured with a URL that contains percent-encoded reserved characters in its path (for example AWS Bedrock AgentCore runtime ARNs, which encode `:` as `%3A` and `/` as `%2F`), the connection fails because requests are sent to the wrong path.

Root cause: the configured URL string is turned into a `URI` via `URI.parse(configuration.url)` in `McpServerLaunch.fromServerConfiguration`. `URI.parse` percent-decodes the path and query, so `runtime%2Fmy-runtime-id` becomes `runtime/my-runtime-id`, and the encoded slash is now indistinguishable from a real path separator. The network layer then serializes with `uri.toString(true)`, which cannot restore information that was already discarded at parse time.

Note the query-string half of the original report (`=` becoming `%3D`) was already fixed by `247241` (`fc5d4141f9b`) switching `.toString()` to `.toString(true)`. That change does not help the path case, because no `toString` variant can recover pre-decoded reserved characters.

## Fix

Carry the exact configured URL string on the HTTP launch alongside the parsed `URI`, and use it verbatim for the actual network requests. The parsed `uri` is still used for origin, auth discovery, and display, none of which are affected by path/query decoding.

- `McpServerTransportHTTP` (and its serialized form) gains an optional `url?: string`, carried through `toSerialized` / `fromSerialized`. Optional with a fallback so the many existing construction sites keep working unchanged.
- `fromServerConfiguration` and the native discovery adapter set `url` from the raw configured string.
- `McpHTTPHandle` sends requests to `this._launch.url ?? this._launch.uri.toString(true)` at the five network call sites (DELETE close, POST message, streamable backchannel GET, SSE GET, and the SSE endpoint `new URL(...)` base).

## Before / after

For a configured URL like `https://…/runtimes/arn%3Aaws%3A…%3Aruntime%2Fmy-runtime-id/invocations?qualifier=DEFAULT`:

- Before: request goes to `…/runtimes/arn:aws:…:runtime/my-runtime-id/invocations?qualifier=DEFAULT` (decoded, wrong path segments) and 404s.
- After: request goes to the exact configured URL, byte for byte.

## Tests

Added a unit test in `mcpTypes.test.ts` asserting that `fromServerConfiguration` preserves the raw `url` (including `%2F` / `%3A`) and that it survives the serialize / revive round trip. Ran the MCP suites locally (`mcpTypes`, `mcpRegistry`, `nativeMcpDiscoveryAdapters`, `mainThreadMcp`, `extHostMcp`), all passing.

title: mcp: Avoid stopping servers for equivalent URI definitions
body:
Fixes #327970

## Problem

`McpServerDefinition.equals` uses generic structural equality for URI-bearing fields. A `URI` stores enumerable lazy caches such as `_formatted` and `_fsPath`, so equivalent definitions can compare unequal when only one URI instance has populated a cache. `McpService.updateCollectedServers()` then treats the equivalent definition as changed and stops the live server.

## Change

Compare nested `URI` values by normalized resource identity while preserving the existing structural comparison behavior for arrays, objects, primitives, inherited enumerable properties, and missing versus explicit `undefined` values.

The change is scoped to the `launch`, `presentation`, and `variableReplacement` comparisons in `McpServerDefinition.equals`. Serialization, revival, hashing, and server lifecycle behavior are unchanged.

This shares the URI-cache diagnosis from #329857, but is intentionally narrower. #329857 also changes serialization, revival, hashing, and malformed or cyclic value handling; this PR changes only the in-memory equality used by the reproduced stop path and adds service-level coverage for that path.

## Validation

- Node tests: `mcpTypes` (20 passing), `mcpService` (3 passing)
- Chromium tests: `mcpTypes` (19 passing), `mcpService` (2 passing)
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- Targeted ESLint and hygiene checks
- Live desktop A/B/C validation with a stateful Streamable HTTP MCP server:
  - VS Code 1.135 and the same Code OSS build with the comparator reverted both sent a session-termination request after an equivalent warm/cold URI republish and logged `stopped because the definition changed`.
  - The patched Code OSS build kept the original session connected for 60 seconds after the equivalent republish.
  - A genuinely changed URI still stopped the original session; starting the updated definition created a new session.

title: nes: fix: normalize Windows workspace path casing
body:
Fixes #325491

## Root cause

NES creates its document ID from `doc.uri.toString()`. On Windows, URI serialization lowercases the drive letter, producing `/c:/workspace/...`, while the workspace-folder URI can retain `/C:/workspace`. `toUniquePath` compared these paths case-sensitively, failed to strip the workspace root, and leaked an absolute drive path into the Lysithea prompt and speculative prediction.

The first native Windows CI run reproduced this exactly:

```text
Expected: "space folder/test.py:"
Received: "/c:/workspace/space folder/test.py:"
```

## Fix

- Normalize only the Windows drive-letter segment before workspace-root comparison.
- Preserve case-sensitive semantics for every other path segment, including virtual notebook providers.
- Cover file-backed notebook cells with fragment retention and case-sensitive virtual notebook cells.
- Make response coverage assert progressive reveal, which requires correct active-document matching.

## Validation

- Initial native Windows CI reproduced the absolute-path leak.
- Refined fix passed `Copilot - Test (Windows)`.
- All actual PR CI checks passed.
- Targeted Xtab tests: 267 passed, 4 Windows-only tests skipped on macOS.

title: Show action icons on title bar buttons, replace auto-merge with Agent Merge
body:
The action buttons in the agents window title bar (Create Pull Request, Commit, Merge, …) stopped showing their icons — they only rendered the pixel spinner while their work was in flight. This shows the icon again, with the spinner taking its place rather than adding to it. It also replaces the auto-merge buttons with Agent Merge.

| | |
|---|---|
| ![Icon to spinner](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0c5cd0b6-0a38-4618-bb06-e97d969634a4) | ![Icon only to spinner](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/754ab899-352d-4d15-9c2a-91e4c7753baf) |

### Leading slot

Every button now gets a leading slot that holds **either** the icon its action carries **or** the pixel spinner, never both. Both are sized identically (`16 × 16` plus a `4px` gap to the label), so a button keeps its width when its work starts.

This replaces the previous approach of inlining `$(icon)` into the label text — a hack the code itself described as "REALLY hacky", and which the button then had to strip back out again via `stripIcons`.

### The icon comes from the action

`IButtonConfig` gained no icon option. The icon is always the action's, read off `action.class` — which is exactly how `MenuItemAction` carries one (`this.class = ThemeIcon.asClassName(icon)`), including the toggled icon while it is checked. The changes view actions therefore pass their icon along instead of prefixing it onto their label. This has no effect on the dropdown entries: `Menu.doGetActionViewItem` leaves `options.icon` unset, so `updateClass` never applies the class there.

Two icon-only bugs surfaced while building the fixtures and are fixed here: a busy icon-only button rendered *both* the spinner and its icon glyph (the glyph is a class on the button element itself), and its spinner kept a trailing gap meant to separate it from a label that isn't there — making the button 4px wider while busy.

### Agent Merge replaces the auto-merge buttons

"Enable Auto Merge" and "Disable Auto Merge" no longer appear on the changes title bar button or in its dropdown. Agent Merge covers the same intent — let the pull request merge on its own once it is ready — and takes the primary button in those states instead, opening its own options so it can be enabled or disabled from there. title: nes: let settings and experiments override baked strategy values
body:
Follow-up to #332018 / #332316, addressing two problems with the `patchBased02Optimized` strategy.

Originally this was structured as a revert of e845953 plus a re-land. That is no longer possible: #332802 and its follow-ups have since merged on top of e845953, so reverting would take a colleague's merged work with it and leaves four commits that do not compile. The change is now expressed directly on top of current `main`, with the same end state.

## 1. Model configuration outranked settings and experiments

Every baked knob was read as `modelConfig.x ?? getExperimentBasedConfig(x)`. Since `getExperimentBasedConfig` already resolves **user setting → experiment treatment → default**, putting the model configuration first placed it above *both*. Once a strategy baked a knob in, neither the user nor a flight could move it, and an A/B arm assigning one of these settings measured nothing.

Reads now go through `resolveModelConfigValue`:

> user setting → experiment treatment → **model configuration** → setting default

This needed a new configuration primitive, `getExperimentBasedConfigIfSet`, which reports only an explicitly provided value instead of falling back to the default — that is what makes "is this setting actually driven?" answerable. Registration-time reads use the observable form, since an imperative read inside an `autorun` would not subscribe and would miss a treatment arriving after the graph was built.

## 2. Two definitions of "unified" that could disagree

`supportsUnifiedCompletions` was resolved in `InlineEditProviderFeature` (for the provider `excludes`) and again per request in `InlineCompletionProviderImpl`. Nothing kept them in agreement, and disagreement is user-visible: if registration excludes the separate provider while a request declines to stand in for it, there is **no inline suggestion at all**. Both paths, plus the joint provider, now resolve through one `observeUnifiedCompletions`, which keeps the existing OR with the core `modelUnification` toggle.

## Also

- `defaultModelConfiguration()` applies `applyStrategyConfig`, so the `forceUseDefaultModel` (404) fallback stops silently dropping every baked knob.
- Renamed `patchBased02Optimized` → `patchBased02Unified`. "Optimized" did not say what the variant does; "unified" names its defining property and matches the existing `xtabUnifiedModel`. The wire value is renamed with the identifier — see the reviewer thread on this.
- Fixed a pre-existing bug where `updateExperimentBasedConfiguration` only matched `config.<fullyQualifiedId>`, so a treatment arriving under `copilotchat.config.<id>` never invalidated the setting's observers. This affects every existing `getExperimentBasedConfigObservable` consumer, not just this change, so it is a separate commit.

## Commits

Each compiles independently.

1. `configuration: refactor:` — hoist the duplicated treatment lookup into the base class (no behavior change)
2. `configuration: fix:` — invalidate observables for every treatment name a setting is published under
3. `configuration: feat:` — add `getExperimentBasedConfigIfSet`
4. `nes: fix:` — the precedence inversion, the single unified-completions definition, and the rename

## Known limitations

- **Flights win over baked values.** Experiments currently assigning these settings will override the strategy, so it only becomes self-contained for those users once those flights are retired. Values coincide today, so there is no behavior change.
- **Startup window (#332837) unchanged.** `supportsUnifiedCompletions` is the only baked value read at provider-registration time rather than per request, so on the fetched `/models` path there is a brief window before the model list resolves. Measured at ~600 ms against a real account.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck --prefix extensions/copilot`, and each commit typechecks independently
- 2494 vitest tests pass across `platform/inlineEdits`, `platform/configuration`, `platform/proxyModels`, `extension/inlineEdits`, `extension/xtab`
- Ran a Code OSS build from these sources: the extension activates cleanly, and a local model configuration is accepted with `patchBased02Unified` and rejected with `patchBased02Optimized` (`Expected undefined, but got string`), confirming the rename end to end

title: Fix Copilot memory tool infinite loop with empty old_str in str_replace
body:
This PR fixes #333395

## Description

The Copilot memory tool's `str_replace` command enters an infinite loop when the model sends an empty `old_str`: `String.prototype.indexOf('', pos)` never returns `-1` (an empty pattern matches at every position, clamped to the string length), so the occurrence scan in `_localStrReplace` never terminates. The loop pins a CPU core at 100% and grows the `occurrences` array without bound until V8 throws `RangeError: Invalid array length` — observed in a real session where a chat turn froze for ~21 minutes before the tool failed (see the linked issue for the full timeline and logs).

## Changes

- Guard against an empty `old_str` at the start of `_localStrReplace` and return a descriptive error result pointing at the `create`/`insert` commands for appending content instead.
- Add a regression test that invokes `str_replace` with an empty `old_str`, asserts the error message, and verifies the target file is left untouched.

## How to test

```
cd extensions/copilot
npx vitest --run --pool=forks src/extension/tools/node/test/memoryTool.spec.tsx
```

All 35 tests pass (34 existing + 1 new regression test).

title: Add ignore setting
body:
This PR fixes #210145.

## Description

Ignore file names used by VS Code search were previously hardcoded. This PR introduces a declarative `contributes.ignoreFiles` extension point that allows enabled extensions to register additional ignore file names without requiring extension activation.

For example:

```json
{
  "contributes": {
    "ignoreFiles": [
      ".hgignore"
    ]
  }
}
```

Contributed files must use gitignore-compatible syntax and must be declared by file name rather than by path.

The following defaults are provided:

- .ignore remains a built-in VS Code default.
- .gitignore is contributed by the built-in Git extension.

Consequently, .gitignore is only considered when the Git extension is enabled. Other extensions can contribute their own ignore files without VS Code hardcoding knowledge of individual tools or ecosystems.

The contribution point is intentionally named ignoreFiles rather than searchIgnoreFiles so it can be reused by other VS Code features in the future. Search is currently the first consumer.

The contributed file names are propagated through file and text search providers and supported by both native ripgrep search and the web file-system search worker.

Testing

Automated tests cover:

- Combining contributions from multiple extensions.
- Removing duplicate file names.
- Rejecting invalid names containing path separators.
- Passing contributed file names to file and text search providers.
- Generating the appropriate ripgrep arguments.
- Excluding files from file and text search using a contributed .customignore file.

Manual verification:

1. Create an extension that contributes .customignore.
2. Add a .customignore file to a workspace containing ignored.txt.
3. Verify that ignored.txt is excluded from file and text search when search.useIgnoreFiles is enabled.
4. Disable the contributing extension and reload the window.
5. Verify that ignored.txt is included in search results again.
6. Repeat the test with the built-in Git extension and .gitignore.

title: Fix macOS Pinyin English candidate insertion
body:
Fixes #333366

## Summary

- keep the native EditContext input state synchronized before model content listeners run
- ignore composition-only selection updates that move beyond unchanged replacement text
- add focused browser coverage for normal updates, English candidate commits, and non-composition selection changes

## Reproduction

1. Enter `1234` and place the caret before `1`.
2. Switch to the macOS system Pinyin input method.
3. Type `revie`, then type `w` so the English candidate appears.
4. Press Enter to commit the candidate.

Before this change, the caret moved after `1` and the result was `revieww234`. After this change, the editor caret remains before `1` while the candidate is pending and the committed result is `review1234`.

## Root cause

Chromium updates the native EditContext before dispatching `textupdate`. The editor then synchronously changes the model, whose content listener wrote the same update back using stale cached EditContext text. This duplicated trailing content inside EditContext. The English candidate also sends a temporary selection beyond its unchanged replacement text; treating that temporary selection as a model caret move caused the final commit to consume and reinsert the adjacent `w`.

title: fix: filter invalid env keys before forking utility processes
body:
**Problem**

The utility process extension host inherits the entire environment block via the default generic env processing. On Windows it is possible for the current process environment to contain keys that Node.js considers illegal (for example a variable whose name starts with a digit, often left behind by installers or tampered environments). Because the inherited block is passed on to the forked utility process, the utility process fails to launch with Node \TypeError: Invalid value for env\, and the whole extension-host stack silently dies while the front-end UI stays up (built-in commands \command not found\, GitHub auth provider never registers, Copilot \
o bundle location\, logs never initialize).

This makes a trivially-poisoned environment take down all utility processes with no crash surface and no diagnostic trail.

**Changes**

- Add \isValidEnvVariableKey()\ in \src/vs/platform/utilityProcess/common/envKey.ts\ - a pure predicate that validates an environment variable key according to Node's name rules (non-empty, starts with a letter or \_\, remaining chars alphanumeric or \_\).
- In \utilityProcess.ts\ \createEnv()\, filter the inherited environment with \isValidEnvVariableKey\ before handing it to the child utility process, so an illegal key is dropped instead of crashing the child.
- Add unit tests in \src/vs/platform/utilityProcess/test/common/envKey.test.ts\.

The patch is minimal and purely defensive; legal keys are preserved unchanged.

**Why not reuse \emoveDangerousEnvVariables\?**

\emoveDangerousEnvVariables\ targets *specific* high-risk keys/values inside an already-valid key namespace (e.g. \NODE_OPTIONS\). This fix addresses a different layer: the *key itself is not a valid identifier*, which Node hard-fails on and which no value-stripping can repair. They are complementary, so a separate pure predicate keeps the boundary check explicit.

**Testing**

- \isValidEnvVariableKey\ covered for accepted forms, leading-digit rejection, and special-character rejection (digit/symbol/case variants).

**Related**

Closes nothing; complements the research issue https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/333316

Fixes #333062. `Reindent Lines` on Rust files misindents code that uses `[`/`]` (e.g. `vec![...]`), with the error compounding on every following line.

title: Fix remote agent-host workspace URI translation
body:
## Summary

**Root cause:** In WSL and Remote SSH, working-directory URIs are sent through the Agent Host Protocol as strings inside JSON, so normal remote IPC URI conversion does not apply. The host receives vscode-remote://wsl+Ubuntu/home/user/project instead of file:///home/user/project. Comparing this workspace root against file: tool targets can incorrectly trigger “outside workspace” permission prompts. This PR adds the missing translation in both directions.

Fixes #331566 — Agent file tools incorrectly prompt "Allow reading file outside of workspace?" for the current workspace in WSL. The same URI mismatch also affects Remote SSH.

The editor supplies workspace directories as `vscode-remote:` URIs, but the agent host runs on the remote machine and needs host-local `file:` URIs. AHP carries these values as strings inside JSON frames, so the regular remote IPC URI-object transformation does not apply. This breaks workspace containment checks and can cause customization watchers to fail with `ENOPRO`.

## Changes

- Add `EditorRemoteAgentHostTransport`, an editor-remote connection adapter that reuses the existing `createURITransformer` rather than introducing new conversion rules.
- Convert outgoing working directories for session/chat creation, configuration requests, terminal creation, and directory-change actions. Only remote URIs matching the connected authority are converted.
- Restore workbench directory identities in incoming session listings, snapshots, notifications, folder-picker metadata, and reconnect snapshots/replayed actions. Correlate JSON-RPC response IDs with their request methods.
- Wire the adapter into `EditorRemoteAgentHostServiceClient` and unwrap the shared protocol client's session-list directory wrappers.
- Add regression coverage for multi-root directories, authority casing, query/fragment preservation, response correlation, lifecycle cleanup, immutability, and preserving opaque message/configuration content.

Permission checks and sandbox policy are unchanged. Existing persisted sessions with incorrect host-side directory URIs are not migrated; use a new session when verifying.

title: Enforce the enterprise MCP allow/deny policy on the agent-host path
body:
Fixes #328241

## The bug

`ChatAllowedMcpServers` / `ChatDeniedMcpServers` are enforced in `McpServer` (`_policyBlock` / `_evaluatePolicy`), which governs MCP servers **VS Code launches itself**. A delegated agent-host session never goes through that code.

Instead, `resolveCustomizationRefs` -> `collectNonPluginMcpServers` projects eligible servers into a synthetic synced plugin's `.mcp.json` and hands it to the agent host, which is a **separate process that launches the server on its own**. Nothing on that path consulted the allow/deny policy, so a server blocked for the local agent connected normally in a delegated session.

This matches the customer report exactly: with an allowlist of `["npx","--yes","--registry","..."]`, `deepwiki` (`type: http`) was blocked for the local agent but connected and answered `read_wiki_structure` in a delegated session. `Developer: Policy Diagnostics` reported the policy as applied because it *was* applied - just not on this path.

## The fix

Evaluate the policy in `resolveMcpServerForAgentHostDelivery`, ahead of every delivery branch, so client forwarding, plugin-contributed servers and provider built-ins are all gated. A blocked server becomes `NotDelivered` with a new `BlockedByPolicy` reason, so it is both withheld from the bundle and reported honestly in the UI rather than being shown as forwarded.

Details worth reviewing:

- The check runs against the **resolved** configuration that would actually be forwarded, so it covers `http` and `stdio` identically and matches the same fields the local path matches.
- It **fails closed** on unverifiable input: when an allow verdict relied on a URL or command still carrying `${...}`, the server is re-checked with that field dropped and blocked unless it is still allowed on its name alone. So a `serverUrl` wildcard that merely matched the literal `${...}` text does not grant access, while an allowlist entry matching by `serverName` is honoured (the URL never affected that verdict). `McpServer` can defer this until launch resolves; here, forwarding *is* the last decision point.
- Both `AgentCustomizationScope` and `AgentHostMcpServerSupportScope` now recompute on `onDidChangeAllowedMcpServers`, so a newly blocked server is withdrawn instead of lingering for the life of the session.
- The identity derivation moves into a shared `mcpServerIdentityFromConfiguration`, used by `AllowedMcpServersService` and by this path, so the two enforcement points cannot drift.

## Explicitly out of scope

Servers the agent host **discovers itself** — workspace-root `.mcp.json` (`AgentHostMcpServerDelivery.RuntimeDiscovered`) — are unaffected. The client never forwards those, and the agent host has no access to `chat.mcp.allowedServers` (the setting declares no `agentHostSync`, and `allowedMcpServers` is not part of `IAgentHostManagedSettingsPermissions`). Closing that remaining gap means plumbing the matchers to the host and gating per provider, which is a separate change and partly runtime-side.

One further limit worth calling out: for `ProviderBuiltIn` (a provider's own bundled GitHub MCP server) the client can now correctly *report* the block, but it cannot stop the provider from starting its own built-in server — that also needs host-side support.

## Tests

New `resolveCustomizationRefs - enterprise MCP policy` suite, driving the **real** `AllowedMcpServersService` off configuration rather than a stub, covering the reported allowlist:

- `http` server blocked by the allowlist is not forwarded (the `deepwiki` repro)
- `stdio` server blocked by the allowlist is not forwarded
- a server matching the allowlist is still forwarded
- `http` and `stdio` servers blocked by the denylist are not forwarded
- with no allow/deny list configured, every server is still forwarded

All three blocking tests were confirmed to fail against the unpatched code.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` - clean for all touched files
- `npm run valid-layers-check` - no violations
- `./scripts/test.sh --grep "resolveCustomizationRefs"` - 33 passing
- `./scripts/test.sh --grep "MCP|Mcp|mcp"` - 722 passing
- `./scripts/test.sh --grep "agentHost"` - 199 passing

title: agentHost: graduate the legacy-settings managed-permissions bridge
body:
Graduates the legacy-settings → `managedSettings.permissions` bridge from its experimental opt-in to the default enforcement path.

Refs microsoft/vscode#332011. Bridge shipped in #331415; runtime blocker github/copilot-sdk-internal#243, fixed by github/copilot-agent-runtime#16249.

## Why this was gated

The runtime treated **any** managed rule from **any** source as activating the global managed policy, so one narrow restriction (a single denied domain, one terminal `false` rule) turned into session-wide prompting for unmatched shell/read/write/URL/factory requests.

github/copilot-agent-runtime#16249 makes **client/session-injected** managed permissions **non-activating**: `deny`/`ask`/`disableBypassPermissionsMode` still bind, but they no longer flip unmatched families to "default ask". Server/MDM layers keep today's activating lockdown. Behavior-only and source-based, so VS Code sends nothing new on the wire.

It also fully covers #243 rather than partially: the runtime split the conflated flag into `rules_active` (client rules still authoritative) and `default_ask_active` (external layers only). That satisfies #243's first three acceptance criteria; the fourth is this PR.

## Verifying the bundled runtime contains #16249

This needed care, because the bump was reverted and re-landed: #332803 bumped it, #332951 reverted it in full after an unrelated session-restore hang (#332885), and #333198 has since re-landed it. `main` now pins `@github/copilot` **1.0.82-0** and `@github/copilot-sdk` **1.0.13-preview.2**.

Verified by **tag containment** on the runtime merge commit — the only reliable check here:

```
gh api repos/github/copilot-agent-runtime/compare/<tag>...9caaa2f --jq .status
```

| tag | status vs. #16249 merge (`9caaa2f`) | contains fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `cli-1.0.80` | `diverged` | no |
| `cli-1.0.81-0` | `diverged` | no |
| `cli-1.0.81-10` | `behind` | yes (first release with it) |
| **`cli-1.0.82-0`** (current pin) | `behind` | **yes** |

Worth flagging for anyone re-checking this: **binary symbol presence is not a valid test.** Grepping the 1.0.81-0 runtime for `_defaultAskActive` — the internal key #16249 introduces — returns a match, but that release does **not** contain the fix. The string ships ahead of the logic. Version-number ordering is also unsafe, since the `-N` suffixes are not ordered by merge date. Only tag containment answered this correctly.

The re-bump also retires a second hazard. Under the older pins there were two runtimes on disk, including a `1.0.80` nested under `@github/copilot-sdk` without the fix, and only the explicit `resolveCopilotCliPath()` override in `copilotAgent.ts` guaranteed the fixed one enforced. Now that `copilot-sdk@1.0.13-preview.2` depends on `@github/copilot@^1.0.82-0`, that copy dedupes to the same version, so both the explicit path and ordinary module resolution land on a fixed runtime.

## Behaviour for users who set the experimental setting

`chat.agentHost.copilot.mapLegacySettingsToManagedSettings` has been **removed from the settings registry**. It no longer appears in Settings, and its value is ignored wherever it still exists on disk.

- `true` → no change; now the default.
- unset → the bridge applies; only administrator-configured restrictions are mapped, and per #16249 they bind without broadening unrelated families.
- `false` → ignored, the bridge applies. A leftover entry in `settings.json` will read as an unknown setting and can be deleted.

Ignoring an explicit `false` is deliberate. Every mapping contributes **only restrictions**, sourced from policy/global enterprise settings, so honoring `false` as a permanent opt-out would let an ordinary user switch off an administrator-configured `deny`. The escape hatch remains the underlying legacy settings.

## Changes

- `agentHostManagedSettings.ts` — drop the gate check; replace the stale "contributing any rule makes the managed policy active" JSDoc with the non-activating semantics; drop the setting from `managedPermissionsConfigurationIds`; document the constant as a deprecated no-op.
- `chat.shared.contribution.ts` — remove the setting registration entirely, so Settings no longer advertises a checkbox whose description claims mapping happens "when enabled" while the value does nothing.
- Tests — remove the inert gate fixture everywhere (including those added by #333264 and the protocol-boundary forwarding tests); replace the "bridge disabled" test with default-on coverage; keep a guard, using the raw setting id, that a stale `settings.json` entry cannot switch off a mapped restriction.
- `.github/skills/policy-and-managed-settings/` — the guidance listed the false-by-default gate as a bridge invariant in three places, which would have instructed future work to restore it. Updated.

`chat.tools.eligibleForAutoApproval` (#333264) landed after this branch and is now default-on too. It's registered `policyOnly`, so only an enterprise policy value can trigger it — no user preference can lock bypass mode by default.

Not changed, per the issue: no `allow` list is contributed, host-side `SessionPermissionManager` stays (still used by Claude/Codex and remote hosts), and expressiveness-gap mappings remain SDK-side work.
author: joshspicer

title: chat: fix per-marketplace plugin auto-update never running
body:
Fixes #330090

## Root cause — a real product bug, not tester environment

The per-marketplace `autoUpdate` plumbing from microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#8462 is **correct end to end** (managed settings → `copilotManagedSettings` normalization → `chat.plugins.extraMarketplaces` → `marketplaceReference` parsing → `isMarketplaceAutoUpdateEnabled`). Six of the seven new tests pass on `main` unchanged, which is the evidence that the policy layer itself was never broken.

The defect is one layer down, in the *periodic update check* that the policy gates:

1. Installed plugin metadata hydrates asynchronously (`_hydratePluginMetadata` re-reads each marketplace to rebuild descriptors from `installed.json`).
2. `_scheduleUpdateCheck()` is armed from `runWhenGlobalIdle`, which fires long before that completes.
3. `_doRunUpdateCheck()` therefore sees `installedPlugins.get().length === 0` and returns early.
4. Its `finally` block unconditionally re-armed with `_scheduleUpdateCheck(PLUGIN_UPDATE_CHECK_INTERVAL_MS)` — a hard 24 h delay — and nothing observed `installedPlugins` to re-arm sooner.

So in every real session the one scheduled check lost the race against hydration, then went quiet for a day. No marketplace was fetched, `marketplacesWithUpdates` stayed empty, `PluginAutoUpdate` was never signalled, and no plugin ever auto-updated — which is why @eleanorjboyd saw no update with `extensions.autoUpdate` **disabled** *and* **enabled**. The early return also never wrote `PLUGIN_UPDATE_LAST_CHECK_STORAGE_KEY`, so restarting just repeated the lost race.

This is independent of the `autoUpdate` override, which is why the feature looked correct in review but shipped non-functional. **microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#8462 should be reopened.**

## Fix

Track whether the last check bailed out purely because metadata had not hydrated, and re-arm as soon as installed entries appear:

- `_lastCheckFoundNoInstalledPlugins` records that state, set only by an actual empty check.
- An `autorun` on `installedPlugins` re-schedules with delay `0` the first time entries appear, guarded on `_updateCheckRunning` so it cannot overlap an in-flight check.
- The check's own backoff picks `0` instead of a full interval when it previously found nothing and entries have since appeared — covering hydration landing *while* a check runs.

The flag returns to `false` as soon as a check observes installed plugins, so this cannot loop; normal 24 h backoff resumes. With no plugins installed, both paths short-circuit to exactly the previous behaviour.

Enforcement stays strictly per-marketplace: `_doRunUpdateCheck` still filters every marketplace through `isMarketplaceAutoUpdateEnabled(ref)` and `_isMarketplaceAllowedByStrictPolicy(ref)` before fetching, and reports only canonical IDs with real upstream commits, so `PluginAutoUpdate` keeps calling `updateAllPlugins({ marketplaceIds })` with a targeted set rather than acting on a global "something has updates" signal. `strictKnownMarketplaces` gating is unchanged on every refresh and update path.

## Tests

New suite `PluginMarketplaceService - per-marketplace auto-update enforcement`, covering the matrix from #8462:

| case | expectation |
| --- | --- |
| `autoUpdate: true`, global `off` | marketplace is refreshed anyway |
| `autoUpdate: false`, global `on` | marketplace is not refreshed |
| `undefined`, global `on` | follows global (refreshed) |
| `undefined`, global `off` | follows global (not refreshed) |
| mixed marketplaces in one config | only the permitted subset is fetched |
| `strictKnownMarketplaces` + `autoUpdate: true` | still blocked when not allow-listed |
| regression | plugins hydrated *after* startup idle are still checked |
| regression | a recent successful check is **not** re-run when metadata is already hydrated at startup |

Both regression tests were verified to fail without their corresponding fix and pass with it.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`, `npm run typecheck-client` — no errors in touched files
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — clean
- `./scripts/test.sh --grep "PluginMarketplaceService|PluginAutoUpdate|PluginInstallService"` — 124 passing

Scope is deliberately minimal: 2 files, 21 production lines changed.

title: Fix custom/BYOK model selection when spawning subagents
body:
### Problem

You can't pin a subagent (the built-in `task` / `runSubagent` tool) to a custom or BYOK model. It's broken on both subagent surfaces, for two unrelated reasons.

**Classic workbench.** The `model` parameter only accepted a display-style qualified name, `"Model Name (Vendor)"`. Every model configured under a single custom endpoint shares one vendor, so those qualified names collide. A request could quietly resolve to a sibling model, or not resolve at all.

**Agents window (agent-host BYOK bridge).** Spawning a subagent on a custom model fails with an error that contradicts itself, listing the requested model as available:

```
Model 'customendpoint/Acme/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6-high' is not available.
Available models: …, customendpoint/Acme/anthropic/claude-sonnet-4.6-high, …
```

### Root cause

In the classic workbench, resolution went only through `lookupLanguageModelByQualifiedName`, which is ambiguous for BYOK models by construction.

The Agents window case is more interesting. The model id advertised to the runtime keeps the configured provider group verbatim (`Acme` above), so the selection id carries an uppercase character. The runtime's subagent-model validator lowercases the *candidate* ids but not the *requested* id, so a model like that can never match itself. Hence "not available" for something the same message lists as available.

### Fix

**`runSubagentTool`** now accepts either the qualified name or the model identifier (`<vendor>/<group>/<id>`), and advertises the unambiguous identifier for any model whose qualified name isn't safe to use. A name is only advertised when it's unique within the agent-mode list *and* `lookupLanguageModelByQualifiedName` resolves it back to that same identifier, since that lookup scans the whole model cache and a same-named model outside the list could otherwise win. Both the explicit-`model` site and the agent-pinned resolution loop go through this.

**The agent-host BYOK bridge** advertises the selection id case-folded so both sides of the runtime's comparison agree, and resolves ids case-insensitively on the way back so the bridge still routes to the source model. The whole `vendor/[group/]id` is folded, not just the suffix, because the vendor is part of the string the runtime compares. Model-visibility state keyed on the pre-folding id is honoured for both forms, so existing sessions aren't disturbed.

Folding isn't injective, so two models differing only in case now collapse to one selection id. Rather than let one silently vanish, `resolveByokSessionConfig` detects that collision and logs a warning naming both ids while keeping the first. I preferred this over a lowercase-safe encoding because an encoding changes the ids people type into the `model` parameter, which is the usability problem this PR set out to fix. Happy to switch if reviewers would rather have the hard uniqueness guarantee.

### Testing

Unit tests added and updated for both surfaces, including collision handling and identifier-before-name precedence. The `agentHost` node suite is at 5056 passing / 53 pending, the BYOK handler suite at 14, and the `runSubagentTool` suite at 39. `typecheck-client` is clean.

Also verified end to end in the Agents window against a real custom endpoint: a fresh session spawns a subagent pinned to the previously-failing model and runs to completion, with the AHP protocol log showing real inference (`usage.model` is the pinned model) and no rejections.

### Note

The Agents-window half is a workaround. The actual bug is the case-sensitivity asymmetry in the closed-source Copilot CLI runtime's subagent-model validator, which lowercases the candidate list but not the requested id. This PR makes the id VS Code advertises match what that validator can resolve, but it'd be better to fix the comparison in the runtime, at which point the folding here can be removed.

title: policy: make Policy Diagnostics fail loudly instead of silently
body:
Ref microsoft/vscode#329973. microsoft/vscode#330027 is a **duplicate** of #329973 (reported independently by a second tester) — both left open for a human to dedupe.

### Problem

`Developer: Policy Diagnostics` could end as a complete no-op: no editor, no notification, nothing to look at. As diagnosed in #329973, querying the SDK/account stack can stall, and the report generator awaited those calls with no bound:

- `IDefaultAccountService.getDefaultAccount()` waits on an init barrier that never settles when account resolution stalls.
- `IAuthenticationService.getSessions()` per provider was likewise unbounded.
- Only the agent-runtime probe had a timeout, so any other stall swallowed the whole export.

This matters beyond the annoyance: the command is what enterprise admins use to confirm policy is applied (see #328241), and three efforts are actively extending it (#332388, #321991, vscode-internalbacklog#7941). A diagnostic that silently aborts hides real enforcement bugs.

### Fix

Every hang-prone probe is now bounded and rendered as data — the report never aborts:

- New `policyDiagnosticsProbe.ts` with `probePolicyDiagnostics()`, which converts a hang, a rejection, or a synchronous throw into an `ok` / `timeout` / `error` result, plus the agent-runtime section renderer (moved out of `developerActions.ts`).
- Failed sections render an explicit *"… is unavailable: <reason>. The rest of this report was generated without it."* note, and the summary table shows the same reason.
- Account and authentication probes are bounded (6s each).
- Report generation as a whole is bounded (30s), and the editor is **always** opened — even a catastrophic failure yields a report stating why it could not be generated.
- If the editor itself cannot be opened, the user now gets a visible error notification instead of silence.

### Tests

`src/vs/workbench/test/browser/actions/policyDiagnosticsProbe.test.ts` covers SDK success, SDK timeout, and SDK error, asserting output is produced in all three cases (plus empty-diagnostics, resolved-`undefined`, and synchronous-throw cases).

### Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` — no new errors (pre-existing agent-host SDK typing errors unchanged).
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — no layering violations.
- `./scripts/test.sh --grep "Policy diagnostics"` — 7 passing.

title: chat: migrate supported workspace MCP servers
body:
## Summary

- Adds a dedicated customization migration for supported MCP servers defined in workspace-folder `.vscode/mcp.json` files.
- Lets users select individual servers and move them into the workspace-root `.mcp.json` consumed directly by Agent Host harnesses.
- Preserves unsupported, disabled, out-of-scope, and unselected servers in their original configuration.
- Refuses migrations that would drop behavior, expose resolved variables, overwrite conflicts, or race concurrent file changes.

<details>
<summary>Technical context for AI-assisted review</summary>

### Intent and previous behavior

Agent Host support reporting can distinguish MCP configurations it can consume from configurations whose source or shape is unsupported. Supported workspace-folder servers were forwarded through the client because Agent Host discovers root `.mcp.json` files but not `.vscode/mcp.json`. The customizations experience reported compatibility but offered no way to move those servers into the runtime-native location.

### Implementation

The customization migration service now projects eligible workspace-folder servers as individual migration candidates. Candidate discovery uses the active session's working-directory scope, current MCP enablement, support assessment, and the original source entry. Only configurations whose source and projected destination forms are equivalent are offered, excluding unresolved variables and destination-incompatible behavior.

MCP is registered as a separate migration category alongside prompt-file and user-data migrations. The shared migration page provides per-server selection, source and target paths, confirmation, completion feedback, and live refresh when the MCP inventory or active session roots change.

The file transaction merges selected entries into strict `{ "mcpServers": { ... } }` JSON at each workspace root and removes only those entries from `.vscode/mcp.json`. Existing equivalent entries are deduplicated; conflicting entries are left untouched. Reads and writes retain file metadata for optimistic concurrency checks, and the destination is verified after the source update so a concurrent destination change restores the source entry.

### Behavior and constraints

- Migration is limited to enabled, applicable, fully supported `.vscode/mcp.json` servers.
- Servers using unresolved variables, SSE transport, explicit working directories, environment files, sandbox or development behavior, OAuth configuration, or marketplace metadata are not offered when root discovery cannot preserve that behavior.
- Existing root `.mcp.json` files must use strict JSON and the supported `mcpServers` wrapper.
- Multi-root sessions resolve one destination per workspace folder.
- Unselected and unsupported entries remain in the source file.
- Prompt-file and user-data migrations remain independent categories with their existing behavior.

### Review context

The main review boundary is data safety across two independently editable configuration files. Candidate eligibility is recomputed after confirmation, source contents are revalidated before deletion, writes use optimistic concurrency metadata, and post-write verification avoids reporting success when the destination changed concurrently.

</details>

## Problem
Experiments served by the new TAS assignments endpoint (`POST /api/v1/assignments`) were not being applied for some users, even though their `abexp.assignmentcontext` telemetry showed the experiment as assigned.

**Root cause:** the new endpoint namespaces the feature-variable keys it returns with a `/vscode/` scope (e.g. `/vscode/config.chat.copilot.subagentModelGuidance.enabled`), while VS Code core and the Copilot extension query treatments by the **bare** name (`config.chat...`). `tas-client` / `vscode-tas-client` store those keys verbatim under the `vscode` config, so `getTreatmentVariable('vscode', '<bare name>')` misses and returns `undefined`.

## Fix (interim, VS Code side)
Until the scope is stripped upstream `AssignmentsApiFeatureProvider.toFeatureData`, resolve treatments **scoped-first**: read the `/vscode/`-scoped key first, then fall back to the bare key.

- **Core** (`assignmentService.ts`): added a small pure helper `resolveScopedTreatment(read, name)` (scoped key first, bare fallback) and use it in `doGetTreatment`. Also simplified the pre-fetch handling into a single "await the initial fetch when not yet initialized" barrier and removed a redundant re-read.
- **Copilot extension** (`baseExperimentationService.ts`): centralized reads into `_readTreatmentVariable` (scoped-first, bare fallback), used by both `getTreatmentVariable` and the treatment-change detection so they stay consistent.

## Why scoped-first (new endpoint wins on collision)
This matches the behavior once the upstream strip lands: with the prefix removed, both endpoints produce the same bare key and the library merges them last-writer-wins in provider order (legacy registered first, assignments second → **new wins**). Making the interim shim scoped-first keeps the winner **consistent before and after** the upstream fix, so there's no behavior flip at cutover.


## Tests
- **Copilot** (`experimentation.spec.ts`): added cases for new-endpoint-only (scoped) resolution and collision (new wins); updated the suite mock so scoped lookups model "not assigned by the new endpoint," exercising the bare fallback.
- **Core** (`assignmentService.test.ts`): new unit tests for `resolveScopedTreatment` covering collision (new wins), legacy-only, new-only, neither, and a defined-falsy scoped value.

title: agentHost: give every remote connection one owner and one reconnect path
body:
Remote agent host connections were established in six different places, and reconnection was
implemented five times over. Only WebSocket connections could use the protocol client's soft
reconnect, so SSH, WSL, tunnel and Dev Container connections were torn down and rebuilt on every
transport drop: a new clientId, no action replay, and pending tool calls cancelled by the host.
This moves connection ownership into RemoteAgentHostService and gives every kind the same
reconnect behaviour.

- Adds ReconnectingTransport, which re-establishes an inner transport through an owner-supplied
  callback. Relay-backed kinds now supply a transport factory, so they get the protocol client's
  backoff, clientId preservation, server-side action replay and outbox draining.
- Adds a reconnect policy per connection kind, replacing five hand-written backoff loops. The
  protocol client now honours a maximum attempt count instead of retrying forever, and reports
  terminal failure upward rather than running its own recovery.
- Adds a `reconnecting` connection status, distinct from `connecting`. Recovery loops no longer
  replace a protocol client that is already restoring itself, and a send during a drop waits for
  the connection instead of failing.
- Adds IRemoteAgentHostConnectionFactory. A factory builds an unconnected client and exposes the
  entries of its kind; the service performs the handshake, classifies the result, sets the status
  and owns retries. WebSocket and SSH use this path.
- Moves entry persistence to the owning producer. The service reads entries and never writes them,
  so an address that moves between stores cannot be resurrected.
- Moves malformed-frame protection into RelayTransport, where it now closes the transport instead
  of the connection, so a corrupted stream recovers through soft reconnect. SSH and WSL did not
  have this protection before.
- Opens the SSH configuration file, instead of a setting that cannot contain the host, for an SSH
  host defined by an ~/.ssh/config alias.

WSL, tunnel, cloud sandbox and Dev Container connections still register through
addManagedConnection. Later changes move them to connection factories, after which
addManagedConnection and the dialableByService flag can both be removed.

title: agentHost: map legacy `chat.tools.eligibleForAutoApproval` to managed settings
body:
## What

Adds a **temporary compatibility mapping** for the legacy VS Code setting `chat.tools.eligibleForAutoApproval` (enterprise policy `ChatToolsEligibleForAutoApproval`) to the Copilot SDK managed-settings bridge in [`agentHostManagedSettings.ts`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/agentHostManagedSettings.ts). Like the other four legacy mappings, it is gated behind the existing false-by-default `chat.agentHost.copilot.mapLegacySettingsToManagedSettings`.

## Why it maps to the bypass lock rather than per-tool `ask` rules

The setting is **per-tool** (`{ "fetch": false, "runTask": false }` → those tools may never be auto-approved). The SDK managed rule grammar has **no tool-name family** — `ManagedRuleFamily` is only `Shell | Read | Write | Domain`, and an unknown family rejects the *entire* managed document. So a faithful per-tool `ask` rule cannot be built and would silently miss `runTask`, `runTests`, and every MCP/extension tool.

Any policy-configured, non-empty value therefore maps onto the **family-agnostic** bypass lock `{ disableBypassPermissionsMode: 'disable' }`. The runtime's `bypass_blocked()` refuses blanket escalation "regardless of how it was requested", and `'disable'` additionally sets `auto_approval_blocked()` — matching this setting's core intent that a tool "will never offer the option to auto-approve."

This is deliberately **coarser** than the setting and errs **more restrictive** (fail-closed), which is the safe direction for an interim shim: it can never silently grant more than the administrator intended.

- `policyOnly` sourcing: only an enterprise `policyValue` drives it — never user/application/workspace — because it removes a capability the user would otherwise have.
- Empty `{}` (the registered default), absent, and malformed (non-object/array) values contribute nothing.
- A non-empty object whose members are malformed (e.g. `{ "fetch": "no" }`) fails **closed** toward the lock rather than being silently dropped.

## Known trade-offs (documented in the module header)

- A permissive value such as `{ "fetch": true }` still disables escalation session-wide (no way to scope to one tool).
- It does not force per-request confirmation — only an `ask` rule sets `managedApprovalRequired`, so a user may still grant a standing approval for an individual tool.
- **Removal criterion:** replace with a faithful per-tool translation once the runtime managed grammar gains a tool-name rule family.

## Scope

- Declares `ELIGIBLE_FOR_AUTO_APPROVAL_SETTING_ID` in [`agentHostSchema.ts`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/agentHostSchema.ts) so the platform-layer bridge avoids importing `ChatConfiguration` from workbench (passes `valid-layers-check`).
- Leaves the workbench consumers (`languageModelToolsService.ts`, `terminalToolAutoApprove.ts`) **untouched** so in-workbench chat keeps its per-tool behavior.

## Testing

- `./scripts/test.sh --grep AgentHostManagedSettings` — 26 passing (7 new: configured value, empty `{}`, non-policy layers contribute nothing, removal clears, malformed array ignored, fail-closed non-boolean member, un-duplicated co-existence with a policy-disabled `chat.tools.global.autoApprove`).
- `./scripts/test.sh --grep AgentHostProtocolClient` — 97 passing (no regression).
- `npm run typecheck-client`, `npm run valid-layers-check`, and `npm run eslint` all clean.

## Review

Cross-checked by a three-model review council (GPT-5.5, Claude Opus 4.7, GPT-5.3-Codex): no blocking issues. The one raised point — a non-boolean object member still locks bypass — is the intended fail-closed behavior; a documenting test and a doc-comment clarification were added in response.
