title: chat: show one OS notification when a session has no more work
body:
chat: show one OS notification when a session has no more work

Agent host sessions can be open in the editor window and the agents window at the
same time. This caused two problems with the OS notifications. A "finished" toast
came when a response ended, even if more requests were in the queue. A session that
was open in two windows made one toast from each window.

- Adds an idle observable in the chat window notifier. It combines the request
  state, the input state, and the count of queued requests. The notifier shows the
  toast only when the session has no more work. A 500ms delay prevents a toast in
  the short gap between two queued turns.
- Makes the chat window notifier the only source of toasts in a window. It now
  shows the toast for needed input and for the idle state. The toast in the chat
  accessibility service is removed. That service keeps the accessibility signal and
  the ARIA announcement.
- Limits the sessions window notifier to sessions that have no chat model in this
  window. Sessions with a model are the responsibility of the chat window notifier,
  which knows about the queue.
- Adds a dedupe key to the toast options. The main process does not show a second
  toast while a toast with the same key is on the screen. This prevents duplicate
  toasts from two windows for one session.
- Delays the toast 250ms in a window that does not show the session. The window
  that shows the session makes its toast first, so a click opens the window that
  the user worked in.
- Delays the completed toast 1500ms in the sessions window notifier. A session with
  no chat model here gives no queue information, so the delay prevents a toast in
  the gap between two queued turns. See
  https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/issues/426 for the permanent fix.

title: Fix stale Open Recent entries after failed open on macOS
body:
Fixes #332665

## Problem

On macOS, opening a deleted folder from **File > Open Recent** shows the "Path does not exist" dialog, but the entry stays in the menu when all editor windows are closed.

The MRU store is updated correctly (`removeRecentlyOpened` runs on failure), but the main-process `Menubar` keeps serving stale cached menu data because it never listens to `onDidChangeRecentlyOpened`. With zero windows open, no renderer is alive to push fresh menu data.

## Fix

- Add `pruneRecentMenuItems()` to walk cached menu trees and drop recent items no longer in the MRU list.
- In `Menubar`, listen to `workspacesHistoryMainService.onDidChangeRecentlyOpened`, prune stale entries from `menubarMenus`, persist the updated cache, and rebuild the native menu.

This is self-healing: even if the cached menu was stale at startup, clicking the dead entry removes it from history, triggers pruning, and rebuilds the menu.

## Tests

- `src/vs/platform/menubar/test/common/menubar.test.ts` — prunes absent folder/workspace/file items, recurses into submenus, leaves actions/separators untouched, returns `false` when nothing changed.

## Manual repro

1. Open a local folder so it appears under File > Open Recent.
2. Close the VS Code window, delete the folder in Finder.
3. From the macOS menu bar, File > Open Recent > choose the deleted folder.
4. Dismiss the "Path does not exist" dialog.
5. Open File > Open Recent again — entry should be gone.

title: fix: make ahead-of-time terminal executable resolution best-effort (fixes #333012)
body:
### Summary On a remote (SSH) terminal, `TerminalInstance` eagerly resolves the shell executable ahead of process creation as an optimization. This path calls `TerminalProcessManager.getBackendOS()`, which throws `Failed to get remote environment for remote authority "..."` when the remote agent environment cannot be fetched yet (connection still establishing or dropped). Because the call runs inside the non-disposed `_xtermReadyPromise.then()` chain, the rejection escapes as unhandled-error telemetry even though the OS/executable is re-resolved later through the normal process-creation path. Affects ~117 users across two sibling buckets on Windows and Mac. Fixes microsoft/vscode#333012 Recommended reviewer: `@meganrogge` ### Culprit Commit No single culprit commit could be pinned. The throw at `terminalProcessManager.ts:594` and the eager-resolution consumer at `terminalInstance.ts` both predate the regression window: `git blame` attributes the `getBackendOS` throw to `f7b171120126` (Megan Rogge, 2022-01-25). The regression-scan comment notes the bucket ID drifts across insider builds throughout the 1.134→1.135 window with no clean first-bad commit, indicating a **pre-existing** latent bug surfacing more frequently (likely a re-bucketing / environmental shift in remote-connection timing) rather than a code regression. Per the pre-existing classification, no culprit is named. ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Xterm as _xtermReadyPromise.then participant Instance as TerminalInstance participant PM as TerminalProcessManager participant Remote as RemoteAgentService Xterm->>Instance: eager executable resolution (optimization) Instance->>PM: getBackendOS() PM->>Remote: getEnvironment() Note over Remote: ⚠️ Root cause:
returns null when SSH
remote env unavailable Remote-->>PM: null Note over PM: 💥 throw Error:
Failed to get remote environment PM-->>Instance: rejected promise Note over Instance: instance not disposed →
escapes as unhandled telemetry ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalProcessManager.ts` | crash site | L594 (from stack): `throw new Error("Failed to get remote environment for remote authority ...")` | | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalInstance.ts` | root cause (consumer) | L557-L558: eager optimization awaits `getBackendOS()`, which throws when the remote env is not yet available, inside the non-disposed `.then()` chain | ### Repro Steps 1. Open a workspace connected to an SSH remote (`ssh-remote+`). 2. Enable terminal shell integration (default) and ensure the shell launch config has no explicit executable. 3. Create a terminal while the remote connection is unavailable or still being established (e.g. the SSH host is briefly unreachable). 4. `getBackendOS()` rejects because `getEnvironment()` returns null; the rejection escapes the eager-resolution path and is reported to error telemetry. Because it depends on remote-connection timing it is non-deterministic; interrupting/degrading the SSH connection during terminal creation increases the likelihood. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/terminalInstance.ts`: the ahead-of-time executable resolution is purely an optimization; the same OS/executable resolution happens again through the normal path in `_createProcess()` → `createProcess()`. The eager block is now wrapped so that if `getBackendOS()` (or the profile resolution) rejects, `os` is reset to `undefined` and a `logService.trace` note is recorded, letting terminal creation continue normally instead of surfacing an unhandled error. This is a consumer-side fix at the optimization site — the producer's deliberate throw (which still feeds telemetry for genuinely required remote-env fetches) is left intact, and no `logService.error` call is removed. The fix targets the code that invokes a throwing call opportunistically, not the crash site itself. **Why this fix works**: after this change, the eager-resolution branch at `terminalInstance.ts:557` can no longer let a `getBackendOS()` rejection escape into the non-disposed `.then()` chain, because the awaited calls are contained and a failure downgrades the optimization to a no-op that the later `_createProcess()` path recovers from. **Alternatives considered**: adding a guard at `getBackendOS()` to return `OS` instead of throwing was rejected — it would silence a legitimate error for callers that genuinely require the remote OS and remove diagnostic signal from the telemetry pipeline. Removing the eager-resolution optimization entirely was rejected as a broader behavior change than the regression warrants. ### Recommended Owner `@meganrogge` — terminal-area team member with write access, highly active (commits landed the same day), and the original author of the `getBackendOS` crash-site code (`f7b171120126`). > Generated by [errors-fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/33105062922) · opus48 · 349.5 AIC · ⌖ 11.9 AIC · ⊞ 18.6K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-id%3A+errors-fix%22&type=pullrequests)

title: Open Dev Container agent sessions in the editor
body:
## Summary

Fixes **Open in Editor** for Agent Host sessions running in a Dev Container. The action now translates the Agent Host workspace URI into the `vscode-remote://dev-container+...` URI expected by the Dev Containers extension.

Follow-up to #331934.

Tracking issue: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/317380

<details>
<summary>Session Context</summary>

Key decisions from the development session:

- **Use `dev-container+`, not `attached-container+`**: These sessions originate from a local source folder with a Dev Container configuration. Encoding that source folder lets the Dev Containers extension rediscover the configuration and reconnect using its normal resolver path.
- **Carry the source host folder explicitly**: The runtime Dev Container connection now retains `hostPath`; the container ID alone is not sufficient to construct a `dev-container+` authority.
- **Preserve the container workspace path**: Only the URI scheme and authority are translated. The Agent Host's remote path (for example `/workspaces/project`) remains the folder opened inside the container.
- **Match the extension's authority encoding**: The host path is UTF-8 hex encoded, matching `getDevContainerUri`. This safely preserves POSIX paths, Windows drive-letter paths, spaces, and explicitly supported WSL UNC paths.
- **Do not claim generic UNC-share support**: Dev Containers explicitly routes `\\wsl.localhost` / `\\wsl$` paths through WSL, while ordinary network-share UNC support is not reliable end to end.
- **Code OSS testing limitation**: The marketplace Dev Containers extension intentionally does not register its resolver without the Microsoft-only `vsda` dependency. The exact generated URI was therefore validated separately in official VS Code Insiders rather than bypassing that product check.

</details>

## Changes

- Retain the original local source folder on managed Dev Container Agent Host connections.
- Resolve Dev Container session workspaces to `vscode-remote://dev-container+<hex-host-path>/<container-path>`.
- Share Agent Host folder URI translation between remote provider types and the Open in Editor action.
- Add regression coverage for POSIX, Windows drive-letter, and WSL UNC source paths.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- Focused `resolveRemoteAuthority` tests: 3 passing
- ESLint on all changed files
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- Live validation in VS Code Insiders 1.136.0 with Dev Containers 0.467.0: the resolver reused the running container and opened `/workspaces/test`

title: agentHost: keep a model reference for chats that are created
body:
agentHost: keep a model reference for chats that are created

A side chat that was started with `/btw` during an active turn opened an empty widget that
never answered. `createSideChat` acquired a chat model, applied the carried-over model and
agent, then released the reference immediately. The reference count fell to zero, which
disposed the provided session and released its agent host chat subscription. The open and
send steps that followed raced that asynchronous teardown. Both steps resolved the session
content at the same time and each built an `AgentHostChatSession`. The second session
replaced the first in `_activeSessions`, but the chat model kept the first. Turn progress
went to a session that no widget observed.

- Deduplicates concurrent session resolution in `ChatSessionsService`. Callers share one
  in-flight promise. The shared work is cancelled only after every caller cancels, so one
  caller that gives up cannot abort the work of the others.
- Disposes a session that the service does not adopt. This covers the session that loses the
  cache race and a session that a provider returns after cancellation. The agent host
  provider does not honour cancellation, so it can still return a fully wired session.
- Replaces the immediate release in `createSideChat`, `forkChat`, and `_createAdditionalChat`
  with a model reference that expires after 10 seconds. The reference keeps the model alive
  across the open and send steps and cannot become permanent.
- Removes the redundant `getOrCreateChatSession` call from those three paths. The standard
  `acquireOrLoadSession` path resolves the session and owns it with a reference count.
- Logs an error when a new agent host session replaces an active session for one resource.
  This invariant was assumed in many places but was enforced in none.

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/332862

title: sessions: pull request operations in the changes title bar
body:
The changes button bar in the Agents window title bar only offered "Create PR" variants, and those disappeared as soon as a pull request existed. It now keeps offering the next step for that pull request, and gives Agent Merge a home next to it.

| PR state | Primary button |
| --- | --- |
| Draft | **Mark Ready** |
| Open, mergeable | **Merge** |
| Open, not mergeable | **Enable Auto Merge** / **Disable Auto Merge** |
| Open, not mergeable, Agent Merge on | **Agent Merge** |
| Merged or closed | *(nothing)* |

The dropdown lists the other applicable pull request actions first, then a separator, then the Agent Merge entries: its session toggle, the repair-action toggles, the merge-choice submenu, and **Agent Merge Defaults** (which opens the settings editor filtered to `@tag:agentMerge`).

## Agent host

- **`AgentHostPullRequestStatusService`** (new) watches the `core` and `mergeability` fragments of the session's pull request. It subscribes only while a client is subscribed to the session's changeset, so the GitHub API cost is bounded to the session the user is actually looking at.
- **`AgentHostPullRequestOperationContribution`** advertises `pr-mark-ready`, `pr-merge` and `pr-enable-auto-merge` / `pr-disable-auto-merge` instead of bailing out once a pull request exists. Auto-merge is driven off GitHub's own capability flags (`viewerCanEnableAutoMerge` is already false for a PR that can simply be merged) rather than re-deriving its rules here. Nothing is advertised while the state is unresolved — the bar stays hidden rather than flashing the wrong action — or once the PR is merged or closed.
- **`AgentHostPullRequestLifecycleOperationHandler`** (new) executes them. Merging goes through `prepareMerge`, so a pull request that stopped being mergeable between the button being rendered and clicked is rejected rather than force-merged, and enqueues when the repository requires a merge queue.
- Adds the `markReadyForReview` and `disableAutoMerge` GitHub mutations, which the mutation service was missing.

## Agents window

- New `MenuId.AgentsChangesOperationsDropdown`, whose entries are merged into the primary button's dropdown. A submenu contributed to its `primary` group *names* a group of related actions rather than being one, so clicking the button opens exactly those as a context menu — the arrow dropdown also carries unrelated pull request operations, so it would be wrong to run its first entry.
- Agent Merge registers its entries there, gated on the existing `chat.agentMerge.enabled` precondition plus the session having an open pull request.

## `chat.agentMerge.mergePullRequest` becomes a three-way enum

`always` | `ifUnchanged` | `never`, defaulting to `never`. Existing boolean values migrate (`true` → `always`, `false` → `never`) in the settings migration, the legacy-key migration, and when reading session overrides from disk.

`ifUnchanged` merges only while Agent Merge has not changed the pull request. It is self-demoting rather than evaluated at merge time: the head SHA is recorded when a repair turn starts, and if a later head differs that turn landed a commit, so the session's value rewrites itself to `never` and posts a notice in the transcript. That way the chosen value always reflects what will actually happen, and the submenu title shows it — `Merge Pull Request (Never)` — without having to open it. Re-selecting `ifUnchanged` clears the baseline and starts fresh.

A repair turn that pushed nothing (for example one that only replied to a review comment) leaves auto-merge on.

## Logging

Because "why is *this* button showing" spans four layers, each one logs its transitions (deduped against a signature, so steady state is silent):

- `AgentHostPullRequestStatusService` logs every flag the button choice branches on, and names the reason when a session is *not* being watched (archived, no subscriber, no PR for the branch, account/host mismatch).
- The operation provider logs the advertised set, calling out the primary separately.
- The lifecycle handler logs invocation, the merge-queue decision, and failures.
- The widget logs the rendered button with a `source` of `running-operation`, `contributed-menu` or `advertised-operation`.

## Validation

Clean `typecheck-client` and `valid-layers-check`. 50 node tests and 31 browser tests pass across the touched areas, including new coverage for the operation state machine, the two new mutations, the boolean→enum migration, and the six demotion cases.

## Note for reviewers

**Merge has no confirmation dialog** — one click merges, by design. The `prepareMerge` gate is what makes that safe.

The demotion notice reuses `AgentSystemNotificationKind.AgentMergeDisabled`, so it renders like the existing auto-disable notice. If it should be visually distinct from "Agent Merge turned itself off entirely", that needs a new notification kind.

title: agentHost: Prefer stored Copilot restore metadata
body:
Fixes #332885

## What changed

- Pass stable registry timestamps to provider metadata reads during explicit session restore.
- Restore registered Copilot sessions from VS Code-persisted working-directory and project metadata when available.

A Copilot SDK `session.getMetadata` request can remain pending for an affected persisted session, preventing Agent Host state hydration. title: Chat: unify Agent Host status pills across chat surfaces
body:
## Summary

This pull request brings Agent Host session status pills to editor and panel chat inputs and, more importantly, consolidates the Agents Window and editor/panel implementations onto the same reusable pill architecture.

The result is one shared composition and lifecycle path for Changes, Pull Requests, Issues, Artifacts, References, Browsers, Customizations, and Subagents. Each surface now supplies observable data and an allowed set of pill kinds; it no longer independently decides ordering, rendering, compact behavior, visibility, keyboard behavior, or dropdown mechanics.

## User experience

- Shows session status pills above the chat input for Agent Host-backed editor and panel chats.
- Keeps Local chat inputs pill-free. The editor/panel integration is intentionally Agent Host-specific.
- Offers these editor/panel pill kinds:
  - Changes
  - Pull Requests
  - Issues
  - Artifacts
  - References
  - Browsers
- Keeps Agents Window-only data such as Customizations and Subagents available in the Agents Window without exposing inappropriate worktree-specific UI in editor/panel chat.
- Uses the existing `chat.turnStatusPills` setting, which remains enabled by default.
- Preserves chat pet interaction by publishing the same rendered pill elements as horizontal pet platforms.
- Uses responsive compact behavior in smaller chat surfaces: pills remain expanded while they fit and collapse to icon-only presentation only when the row would overflow.

## Shared architecture

### One controller for both surfaces

`ChatInputPills` now owns the common row and widget lifecycle:

- setting enablement;
- per-kind user visibility;
- the visibility context menu and hidden-pill recovery state;
- row and widget creation;
- keyboard and focus restoration;
- chat pet element publication;
- visible/hidden lifecycle notifications.

Both the Agents Window and Agent Host editor/panel adapter instantiate this controller instead of maintaining separate toolbar implementations.

### One canonical pill composition

`StandardChatInputPillSources` is the canonical builder for the standard session pill set. It owns:

- pill ordering;
- component selection;
- Changes rendering and activation;
- Pull Request, Issue, Artifact, Reference, Browser, Customization, and Subagent section pills;
- shared per-kind labels, icons, summaries, and single-entry behavior.

The two surfaces only provide observable sections, callbacks, and the kinds they support. This prevents presentation drift such as the previously different Pull Request pill between the Agents Window and editor chat.

### Shared presentation helpers

- Common Pull Request state-to-icon and aggregate-priority logic moved into shared workbench code.
- Common session pill options moved into a shared options module.
- Live Pull Request presentation is resolved once through a reusable Sessions model, while polling remains centrally owned by the existing GitHub polling contribution.
- Provider-specific session and changeset resolution remains in Agent Host connection/provider policy rather than being reconstructed by the UI.

### Removed duplicate pill path

The old `SessionHeaderMeta` metadata-pill path is no longer needed after the input toolbar migration. This change removes:

- `SessionMetadataPills`;
- specialized Changes, Pull Request, and Issue header action view items;
- their action-view-item registrations;
- legacy component fixtures and tests that exercised the now-unreachable header implementation.

The commands themselves remain available for the shared pills and session context menus. This leaves a single active rendering architecture instead of two independently evolving implementations.

## Flicker and lifecycle improvements

The shared pill primitives were updated to avoid rebuilding UI for routine observable changes:

- Pill membership updates are incremental and preserve existing DOM nodes.
- Existing pill buttons and keyboard focus survive unrelated pill additions and removals.
- An open dropdown remains open when an unrelated pill changes.
- If the open pill itself disappears, focus moves to the nearest remaining pill, the empty configuration row, or the owning chat input.
- Open dropdown contents update in place when their observable sections change and close when the pill is no longer summarized.
- Stable section-pill descriptors prevent toolbar recreation while visible presentation is unchanged.
- Dropdown buttons update only the label, tooltip, icon, and accessibility state that actually changed.
- Responsive compact measurement caches intrinsic pill width instead of repeatedly measuring the viewport-sized row.
- The intrinsic-width cache is invalidated only when pill sizing changes.
- Agent Host change summaries retain the last authoritative files during transient changeset recomputation and clear only when a ready changeset is authoritatively empty.
- Change caches are isolated by connection authority and changeset URI.

These changes address the visible flashing during session startup, new pill discovery, changeset recomputation, and session completion.

## Agent Host and GitHub correctness

- Editor/panel pills resolve the backend session URI, scheme aliases, relative changeset templates, and configured default changeset kind through shared Agent Host connection policy.
- Cloud Sandbox aliases therefore resolve to the correct backend session and changeset channel.
- Browser pills include browsers owned by direct tool-origin subagent chats.
- Hiding the Browser pill allows matching website artifacts or references to appear in their corresponding pills instead of disappearing entirely.
- Pull Request state is applied only to the URL it describes; unrelated Pull Requests keep their own open/default state.
- Pull Request summary icons are derived from the per-entry icons using shared priority rules.
- Agents Window Pull Request pills retain live CI/review state and Agent Merge-aware blocker presentation.
- Combined failing-check and unresolved-review states are announced together.
- Cached draft, merged, and closed Pull Request icons retain matching accessible state before live details arrive.
- Pull Request polling is not duplicated by the presentation layer.
- Issue refresh/polling only runs while the Issue pill feature is enabled and visible.

## Accessibility

- The row and pills keep consistent toolbar, button, listbox, and popup semantics.
- The empty hidden-pill recovery row is keyboard accessible and exposes `aria-haspopup="menu"`.
- Inline single-entry and single-resource pills expose both their actionable label and their status/location description.
- Focus is preserved across incremental updates and safely restored when a focused or expanded pill disappears.
- Auxiliary-window rendering uses the correct DOM realm and target-window observers.
- Sessions accessibility help now describes status pills above the chat input rather than the removed session-header controls.

## Validation

Validated after rebasing onto the latest `main`:

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- ESLint across all TypeScript files changed by the PR
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- 197 focused workbench, Sessions, Agent Host changeset, GitHub, accessibility, and pill unit tests
- forced `npm run build-fast -- --force`
- Component Explorer checks for:
  - the shared `3 Pull Requests` summary/dropdown presentation;
  - the `1 File +12 -5` Changes presentation;
  - responsive expanded/compact behavior.

title: agentHost: avoid SDK metadata lookup during session restore
body:
Prevents registered Agent Host Copilot sessions from blocking before SDK resume when `getSessionMetadata` does not settle. Once the Copilot SDK/runtime bump is reintroduced, existing sessions with complete host-owned persistence can hydrate and proceed directly to `resumeSession`.

Provider-native sessions and incomplete legacy sessions still use the SDK metadata lookup because VS Code does not have sufficient local state for them.

Fixes #332885

## How

- Pass stable registry timestamps into activating provider metadata reads.
- Build registered Copilot restore metadata from the persisted title, project, and working directories.
- Avoid the second SDK metadata lookup before resume when a persisted working directory is available.
- Cover fallback propagation, metadata hydration without an SDK request, and cold resume without an SDK metadata request.

## Current status

The SDK/runtime bump was reverted from `main` in #332951, so the failure is no longer reproducible on current `main`; this draft preserves the proposed hardening for the next adoption attempt.

A clean OSS build at the exact first-bad commit `a29f231dfa3` (`@github/copilot-sdk` `1.0.13-preview.0`, runtime `1.0.81-12`) did not reproduce the issue. The persisted `Sanity test Copilot SDK` session reached SDK resume and restored 25 turns in about 2.6 seconds. Per the requested validation rule, no with-fix OSS comparison was run, so this proposal remains unvalidated against a reproducing baseline.

The exact-bad product and all built-in extensions compiled with zero errors before the attempt. The source diff passes `git diff --check`.

## Measurement question

Which MCP access, native discovery, allow/deny, managed-only, gallery, strict-plugin-only, and stored enablement controls are explicitly configured?

This completes the local MCP configuration denominator for #332083 while keeping values and identities outside telemetry.

The reporter emits initial explicit state, recomputes on configuration changes and profile/workspace enablement-storage changes, suppresses unchanged keyed rows, emits changed dimensions only, emits zero tombstones for removals, and caps a fully absent snapshot at one `all` marker.

Legal layers follow each registered setting: user/workspace/policy for MCP access and native discovery; application/policy for allow/deny and managed-only controls; application/policy for strict-plugin-only; user/workspace/policy for gallery enablement; profile/workspace storage for persisted server enablement. | access | all / registry / none explicit state |

| policy controls | allowed, denied, managed-only, strict-plugin-only |

None. These listeners observe existing configuration/storage. They do not alter discovery, activate providers, resolve collections, or start servers.

title: mcp: report server discovery outcomes
body:
## Measurement question

Which local or remote MCP discovery sources produce usable, blocked, disabled, unresolved, invalid, or otherwise rejected server candidates?

This adds the server-discovery denominator for #332083 on top of the typed diagnostic contract and VS Code configuration-presence signal.

## Events and row grain

- `mcp/serversFound`: one row per `(source, format, scope, host, installProvenance)`.
- `mcp/configurationFound`: extends the platform-owned contract with non-VS-Code file/provider configuration rows at `(source, format, scope, host)` grain.

Allowed dimensions are the fixed platform MCP enums plus `all`. Rows contain candidate/outcome or configuration counts only; no server identities, extension IDs, plugin IDs, paths, URIs, commands, URLs, headers, environment, or inputs are reported.

## Emission, deduplication, and tombstones

Aggregation waits for every active discovery implementation's domain snapshot, but functional collections remain independent. `chat.mcp.access = none` emits a bounded zero denominator. Strict-plugin-only mode reconciles non-plugin usable/disabled/unresolved candidates to `blocked` while retaining parse/unreadable diagnostics. Keyed rows suppress identical snapshots, emit only changed dimensions, and emit zero tombstones plus bounded `all` markers for removals/empty completion.

This layer emits no explicit setting-presence rows. It consumes effective access and strict-plugin-only state only to classify the active discovery population. Configuration rows come only from observed files/providers.

title: Add "Continue with Microsoft" sign in for GitHub
body:
Lets someone already signed in to Microsoft reach Copilot without a second trip through the browser. The `microsoft` provider already holds an Entra token; this trades it for a GitHub one.

## How the flow works

Two exchanges, on purpose.

The first buys a `read:user` discovery token, just enough to call `GET /user` and find out which GitHub account the Entra identity maps to. That account is shown to the user, and nothing is published until they confirm it. The second exchange then mints the scopes the caller actually asked for.

The discovery token is never persisted and never published as a session. Neither token is ever logged.

## What survives a reload

Entra-brokered sessions live in memory for the life of the window and never touch the Keychain. What persists is the user's consent: a row in global state holding the GitHub account label, the Microsoft account label, and the GitHub user id. A fresh window mints the session again from that row without prompting, re-running discovery to confirm the row still points at the same account.

Rows are keyed by GitHub account label, because that is what VS Code itself keys an account by. `getAccounts` collapses sessions by label and the account preference is stored by label. A session read back from the Keychain can carry a placeholder id, an old numeric one, or one from a lookup that failed, so the id is no way to tell two accounts apart. The id has exactly one job here: checking that the token GitHub just returned belongs to the account the row names, which a label cannot do because logins get renamed and freed logins get taken.

## Signing out

Signing out of GitHub drops the row. Signing out of Microsoft drops the sessions, since nothing can renew them, but deliberately leaves the rows alone.

That asymmetry matters. The Microsoft account list is a per-window cache that legitimately reads empty for a moment while it repopulates, and the rows are global state shared by every window. Acting on a blink of that list would sign the user out everywhere with no way back. Dropping only the in-memory sessions self-heals: the next read mints them again from the row that is still there. Getting it wrong costs one round trip instead of the account.

## Testing

37 unit tests pass across `accountLinks.test.ts`, `entraTokenExchange.test.ts`, `flows.test.ts`, plus the workbench tests in `chatSetup.test.ts` and `defaultAccount.test.ts`. End to end this was exercised through sign in, window reload, cross-window sign in from the Agents window, and both sign-out paths.

## Note for reviewers

`extensions/github-authentication/src/config.ts` is intentionally untouched here. The client secret this endpoint requires lives in vscode-distro, not in this repo.

Draft while the endpoint registration is finalized.

title: Keep the full URI reachable in the prompt URL confirmation dialog
body:
The confirmation dialog shown when installing a prompt / instructions / agent file from a URL truncates the URI in the middle: ```ts uriLabel = `${uriLabel.substring(0, 35)}...${uriLabel.substring(uriLabel.length - 15)}`; ``` Because the middle is what gets removed, the host can end up entirely inside the hidden part. For example ``` https://raw.githubusercontent.com.cdn.example.com/copilot-instructions.md ``` renders in the dialog as ``` https://raw.githubusercontent.com.c...instructions.md ``` which reads as a `raw.githubusercontent.com` URL, while the request actually goes elsewhere. `extensionUrlHandler` truncates the same way, but keeps the full URI reachable. That was added in #239527 ("Provide a way to reveal the entire URI in an 'Allow extension to open URI' dialog", fixes #239272): ```ts new MarkdownString(`
${uriLabel}
`, { supportHtml: true }) ``` The prompt dialog renders its label as a markdown link, so it does get `title` automatically from the renderer (`markdownRenderer.ts`: `effectiveTitle = title || href`), but it has no `aria-label`. The accessible name of the link is therefore the truncated text, and a screen reader user has no way to reach the real host. This change emits the link as HTML and sets both `title` and `aria-label` to the full URI, matching what `extensionUrlHandler` already does. Two things I checked before proposing this: - `URI.toString()` percent-encodes `"`, `'`, `<` and `>`, so interpolating it into the attributes cannot break out of them. - Anchors coming from raw HTML are handled exactly like markdown links: `markdownRenderer.ts` walks every `a[href]` in the rendered root and moves the href to `data-href`, and the click/keydown listeners are attached to the container. Click behaviour is unchanged.

title: sessions: fix broken "Sent from another chat" request-origin link
body:
## What

Fixes two independent bugs that broke the "Sent from another chat" / "Sent by another session" request-origin link (the small pill shown above a delegated chat request, linking back to the chat/session that sent it).

## Why

1. **Agents window** — `OpenSessionLinkOpenerContribution` fell back to a bare `openSession()` when the link carried no chat id. Per `buildOpenSessionLinkUri`'s documented invariant, an absent chat id means "the session's default chat," but `openSession()` only activates the session without switching the active chat. So clicking the pill was a no-op whenever a *different* chat of the same session (e.g. a peer/subagent chat) was already showing — exactly the case when a delegated request originates from the session's default chat.
2. **Regular editor window** — `AgentHostOpenSessionLinkOpenerContribution` only registered an opener with `IOpenerService` (for markdown-authored links), never with `IChatRequestOriginService` (which is what the pill's click handler actually calls). So clicking the pill found no opener and fell back to treating the opaque `agent-host-session://` link as a session resource directly, which never resolves.

## Fix

- `OpenSessionLinkOpenerContribution._open()` now always resolves a concrete target chat — the peer chat when a chat id is present, otherwise the session's `mainChat` — and opens it uniformly via `ISessionsService.openChat()`.
- `AgentHostOpenSessionLinkOpenerContribution` now also registers a request-origin opener that reuses its existing link-opening logic.

## Testing

- Added a regression test for each fix, reproducing the exact metadata shape captured from a live repro (delegation link with no chat id, and a request-origin link opened from the editor window).
- Updated an existing test that encoded the old (buggy) "no chat id → openSession" expectation.
- `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run valid-layers-check`, and `npm run hygiene` all pass clean.

title: agentHost: don't tell the agent to reply-and-stop after create_session
body:
Fixes #330138

### Problem
After a request like "spawn a session for X and then do Y", creating the child session caused the parent to stop early instead of continuing with Y.

The `create_session` / `send_message` server tools instructed the model to **"Reply with one short sentence confirming the … was created"** — in both the tool *result* and the tool *description*. The model read that as a turn terminator, so it created the session and stopped.

### Change
- **Results** are now neutral statements of fact, carrying the open link with no reply-and-stop imperative:
  - `New session created (agent-host-session://…).`
  - `Chat created in the current session (…).`
  - `Chat created (…).`
  - `Message sent (…).`
- **Descriptions** are now purely functional: dropped the UI-presentation policy ("the UI renders…", "don't print the URL", "don't tell the user to click a button") and the "reply with a single short sentence" instruction. Presentation is the client's concern; the result already carries the link.
- Added a focused regression test locking both the neutral results and the functional descriptions.
- Regenerated the 19 Copilot prompt snapshots for the updated descriptions (tokenless replay update).

This preserves the #332225 rollback intent — no child-session orchestration/fan-in code is touched.

### Validation
- Targeted node unit suite (`sessionServerTools.test.ts`) — 56 passing incl. the new regression test.
- Prompt-snapshot suite regenerated and green (22 passing); e2e replay captures unaffected (tool_result payloads are elided from the request projection).
- `typecheck-client` clean; eslint clean on changed files.

### Reviewer note / known limitation
Removing the explicit stop signal is a real improvement, but it is a **mitigation, not a guarantee**. The agent host runs a model-driven loop, so after *any* tool result the model itself decides whether to continue or end the turn — a debug-log capture on a patched build still showed the parent occasionally ending with an empty terminal message after `create_session`. A fully reliable fix would be structural (e.g. an `onTurnEnd` continuation nudge for the side-effect-tool class, with a loop guard). Discussion and a question for @roblourens are on #330138.

---

🤖

## Summary

Prevents an asynchronous Agent Host customization refresh from publishing into a session that was removed while customization discovery was still pending.

## Symptom

Recent Code - Insiders Agent Host logs contained warnings such as:

```text
2026-08-25 16:02:20.956 [info] [Copilot] Chat created; its backing stays deferred until the first send: copilotcli:/9d927329-1762-430f-a91b-a10ca927afcf
2026-08-25 16:02:23.072 [warning] [AgentHostStateManager] Action for unknown session: copilotcli:/9d927329-1762-430f-a91b-a10ca927afcf, type=session/customizationsChanged
```

The warning means a provider-side customization refresh produced a state action after the target session had already left the state manager.

## Root cause

`AgentSideEffects._publishSessionCustomizations` reads the session's current customizations, awaits `agent.getChatCustomizations(...)`, and then compares the newly resolved set against the current session state before dispatching `session/customizationsChanged`.

Previously, both reads used optional chaining directly on `getSessionState(...)`. This collapsed two distinct states to the same value:

- an existing session whose customizations have not been published yet; and
- a session that was removed while discovery was pending.

Both yielded `undefined`. Consequently, if the session disappeared during the `await`, the existing deduplication/supersession logic could still reach `dispatchServerAction` and emit an action for an unknown session.

## Fix

- Require the session to exist before starting customization discovery.
- Recheck that it still exists after the asynchronous discovery completes.
- Preserve the existing structural deduplication and superseded-refresh retry behavior for live sessions.

The guard is intentionally at the asynchronous producer rather than in `AgentHostStateManager`: unknown-session warnings remain useful for finding other stale producers, while this refresh simply has no valid target after removal.

## Test coverage

Adds a regression test that:

1. starts customization discovery;
2. waits until discovery is pending;
3. removes the session from the state manager;
4. completes discovery; and
5. verifies that no `SessionCustomizationsChanged` envelope is emitted.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/agentSideEffects.test.ts --grep "customizations"` - 9 passing
- pre-commit hygiene - passed for both changed files
- `git diff --check`

## Reviewer note

The main point to verify is that the explicit existence checks preserve the intended idle-eviction/restore behavior: a later refresh for a restored session with the same URI still publishes normally, while an in-flight refresh belonging to the removed incarnation is dropped.

title: fix: clear terminal drag-and-drop observer on detach (fixes #311164)
body:
## Summary

Fixes #311164.
Supersedes #318756 with requested unit tests and race condition guards.

`TerminalInstance._dndObserver` (a `MutableDisposable<IDisposable>` holding the per-container `DragAndDropObserver`) was set by `_initDragAndDrop` but never cleared by `detachFromElement`. When a `TerminalEditor` pane reuses its container across tab switches (`setInput` calls `detachFromElement` on the old instance and `attachToElement` on the new one), newly-attached terminals stacked additional `DragAndDropObserver`s on top of leaked ones.

When shift-dropping a file onto the active editor-area terminal, each previous instance's observer fired on the shared container and inserted the path.

### Changes
1. Dispose `this._dndObserver.clear()` in `detachFromElement()` so drops on the old container no longer route to the detached terminal instance.
2. Guard the deferred `setTimeout` in `attachToElement` with `if (this._store.isDisposed || this._container !== container) return;` so a synchronous detach in the same tick does not re-attach a stale observer.
3. Added unit tests in `terminalInstance.test.ts` verifying that `detachFromElement` properly clears the observer.

Co-authored-by: Vlad Gerasimov <vlad@vlad.studio>

title: Launch Skill: Quick Pick should expose item IDs for automation
body:
## Motivation

This is part of the Launch Skill automation improvements. The skill needs to invoke VS Code commands through the real Command Palette consistently, without silently accepting a different fuzzy result when the requested command is unavailable in the current UI context.

For example, automation requested `workbench.action.chat.newChat`. That command was not available in the Command Palette because its context condition did not match after the palette opened. The palette still produced a fuzzy result, **Create New Terminal (With Profile)**, and the previous automation accepted it because it only checked that some result was focused. This then opened the terminal-profile Quick Pick instead of creating a new chat.

## Changes

- Expose the existing Quick Pick item `id` on rendered flat Quick Pick rows as `data-quick-input-id`.
- Set Command Palette item IDs to their command IDs.
- Update smoke test automation scripts to check these ids before running commands, to avoid running the wrong command. These automation script may be used by the Launch Skill in the future, and they're currently used by the `validate-ui-scenario` agent skill. Command matching modes:
  - `exactCommandId` — require the focused item's ID to match; this is the default.
  - `exactLabel` — require the focused item's primary label to match.
  - `fuzzy` — intentionally accept the Command Palette's focused fuzzy result.
- Clear `data-quick-input-id` when a recycled Quick Pick row renders an item without an ID.

**Still pending:** Updating Launch Skill itself to make use of these new IDs, either by adding an explicit script for doing that, or by making it leverage the smoke test automation library. Note, however, that the `validate-ui-scenario` agent skill will benefit immediately, since it already uses the smoke test automation library.

## Validation

- Targeted ESLint for changed Quick Input, automation, MCP, and smoke-test files.
- `test/automation` and `test/smoke` TypeScript compilation.

title: sessions: Reconcile offscreen chat approval row heights
body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #332795 (merged), which surfaced pending chat approvals on their own nested-chat rows. That PR was reviewed after merge; this addresses the two remaining review points.

## What changed

- **Fix stale row height for approvals that change while a chat row is virtualized offscreen.** The per-row approval autorun is tied to the row template, which is disposed when the row scrolls offscreen. If an approval then appears, clears, or changes line count, the ListView kept the row's stale cached height, and on re-entry the renderer re-seeded its height baseline from the new state — so the first autorun emitted no height update and the blocking "Allow" control could be clipped by `overflow: hidden`.

  `SessionsList` now owns an autorun (`reconcileChatApprovalHeights`) that watches each chat's live approval and reconciles its cached height via the tree delegate, **independent of whether the row is currently rendered**. Height updates applied to offscreen elements correct the ListView's cached size, so the row shows the right height (and never clips the Allow control) when scrolled into view. The autorun is re-established after every `update()` because chat items are rebuilt each render.

- **Accessibility: keep the one-time permission scope in the Allow button's accessible name** — `Allow: {0}` → `Allow once: {0}`. Simultaneously visible Allow buttons still get a distinct accessible name (the command they approve), and now retain the "once" semantics.

## Why not reconcile during render instead

A render-time reconcile was considered and rejected: firing the height change synchronously during `renderElement` re-enters the tree's render/transaction (`Error: Already in transaction`), and a deferred fire cannot be distinguished from the tree's own ambient re-render in tests. Tracking heights outside the rendered-template lifetime (a list-owned autorun) corrects the cache synchronously on the model change and is deterministically testable.

## Testing

- Added a regression test that mutates an approval while its chat row is virtualized offscreen, then brings the row onscreen and asserts it reserves the reconciled height and shows the Allow control. Verified it fails without the fix (stale 28px) and passes with it.
- All 207 sessions contrib browser tests pass; `typecheck-client` clean.

title: Reduce timeout polling overhead in dynamic programming diff
body:
Related to #253704

## Summary

The dynamic programming diff algorithm called `timeout.isValid()` for every matrix cell. `DateTimeout.isValid()` calls `Date.now()`, so on hosts with expensive clock reads the timeout bookkeeping itself can consume the computation budget and produce a timed-out whole-file diff.

This moves timeout polling to the outer row boundary. For an M x N matrix, timeout/clock probes fall from M x N to M while diff output remains unchanged. Deadline detection can be delayed by at most one row; current production call sites select this algorithm only below 1,700 combined lines or 500 combined character offsets.

This addresses the polling overhead identified in #253704. It intentionally does not change how a genuine timed-out result is consumed; #303517 covers that complementary behavior.

## Tests

- Added a deterministic regression test proving timeout checks scale with rows rather than cells.
- Added coverage proving expiration still returns `hitTimeout: true` before the next row is processed.
- Focused new and existing diffing suites: 7 passing.
- Strict TypeScript 6 no-emit diagnostics pass for the production dependency path.

To run the new regression: `scripts/test.sh --grep "DynamicProgrammingDiffing"`.

title: Improve sandbox chat session discovery and handling of rate limits
body:
Sandbox chat sessions sometimes don't appear in the sessions list until you create a new sandbox session — at which point all of them show up at once.

### Root cause

Discovery is the only thing that surfaces sandbox sessions, and it was its own worst enemy. Each pass resolved **every** sandbox task with a single `Promise.all`, so a user with a few dozen tasks issued a few dozen simultaneous requests and tripped GitHub's rate limit.

From a user's log (~350 tasks, 38 of them sandbox tasks), 68 HTTP 429s in tight bursts:

```
8 at 17:22:58    2 at 17:22:59
8 at 17:24:54    2 at 17:24:56
9 at 18:12:36    1 at 18:12:38
```

Two failure modes follow:

1. **Sessions silently missing.** 8-9 `getTask` calls were rejected on every pass, so each "successful" pass was really `partial` and dropped roughly a quarter of the user's sessions. Nothing retried them.
2. **Nothing at all.** The burst starved whichever pass ran next. A window reloaded ~30s later had its `listTasks` page 1 fail, and page 1 failing returns `failed` — which seeds nothing and registers no providers. That window showed zero sandbox sessions.

Creating a new session appears to fix it because a failed pass leaves **zero** providers registered, and the new-chat composer calls `rediscover()` precisely when the host list is empty. By then the rate limit has recovered, so every session lands at once. Nothing else recovers: there is no timer, no backoff, and no refresh on focus.

### Changes

- **Bounded the fan-out.** Task-detail fetches now run through a `Limiter` capped at 5 concurrent instead of all at once. This is the root cause fix.
- **Retry rate-limited discovery reads.** A new `_retryWhileRateLimited` wraps `listTasks`, `getTask` and the repository-name lookup. It honors a server-supplied `Retry-After` **verbatim** and applies exponential backoff (1s → 2s → 4s, capped at 8s) only when the response names none.
- **Bounded the pass with a wait budget rather than a per-wait cap.** Shortening a server `Retry-After` would re-issue the request inside the window the server just asked us to stay out of — with `Retry-After: 60` that meant retries at 8s/16s/24s, three more 429s, and the session dropped anyway. A delay that doesn't fit the remaining budget now ends the retries instead, so the read reports its 429 and leaves the scan `partial` for a later pass.

Scoped to discovery only. Credential mints, task creation and history replay are untouched.

### Validation

- 5 new tests: peak concurrency stays at 5 across 30 tasks; a task that 429s twice still resolves; a rate-limited `listTasks` page 1 no longer fails the pass; a long `Retry-After` is not re-issued early; a persistently limited task gives up and leaves the scan `partial`.
- 112 passing across the sandbox and remote-agent-host provider suites.
- `typecheck-client` and eslint clean.

### Not covered

If discovery still fails for an unrelated reason (genuine network loss), the list stays empty until something triggers `rediscover()`. Retrying a failed pass in `CloudSandboxAgentHostContribution` would close that gap and is worth a follow-up.

title: Let a host declare which changeset the Changes view defaults to
body:
## The problem

On a cloud sandbox session the Changes panel says **No Changed Files** while the chat reports `1 file changed +2 −0`. Both are telling the truth — they answer different questions.

The panel defaulted to **Branch Changes** (`changeKind: 'branch'`), which means *the commits `HEAD` introduces relative to its merge-base with the base branch*. A sandbox agent edits files in the working tree without committing, so `branch` is legitimately empty.

The default was hardcoded:

```ts
const defaultChangeset = changesets.find(c => c.changeKind === ChangesetKind.Branch) ?? changesets[0];
```

That is a sensible default for a host whose agent commits as it goes. It is the wrong one for a sandbox.

## The change

Rather than teach the generic changeset code about sandboxes, let a host declare what it wants. `IAgentHostAdapterOptions` gains an optional `defaultChangesetKind`, threaded through the existing provider-config path already used for per-host traits like `sessionSchemeAlias` and `workspaceTypeIcon`:

```ts
// cloudSandboxAgentHostContribution.ts
sessionSchemeAlias: SANDBOX_SESSION_SCHEME_ALIAS,
// The sandbox agent edits without committing, so `branch` is always empty.
defaultChangesetKind: ChangesetKind.Session,
```

The selection keeps its original shape — only the kind being looked up becomes configurable:

```ts
const defaultKind = options.defaultChangesetKind ?? ChangesetKind.Branch;
const defaultChangeset = changesets.find(c => c.changeKind === defaultKind) ?? changesets[0];
```

A host that declares nothing — every local session, and every remote host that is not a sandbox — resolves `defaultKind` to `branch` and behaves exactly as before.

## Why `session` for a sandbox

`session` is the changeset whose entry reads *"Cumulative file edits the agent has made in this session."* It is derived from the agent's own tool calls rather than from git, so it shows the agent's work whether or not anything was committed — which is what someone opening the Changes panel on a sandbox session is asking to see.

The other candidate was `all` (working tree vs. the base-branch merge-base, the union of `branch` and `uncommitted`). It would also have fixed the empty panel, but it is a git query rather than a record of the agent's work, and it is labelled "All Changes" — colliding with the label this host already uses for its own `session` changeset. Preferring `session` avoids introducing that ambiguity.

## Alternatives considered

- **Fall back when the selected changeset is empty.** "Empty" and "still loading" are indistinguishable at selection time, so the panel would flicker between views as diffs arrive.
- **Detect the sandbox inside `createChangesets`** by comparing the session URI scheme against `CLOUD_SANDBOX_SESSION_SCHEME`. Works, but puts knowledge of one specific host inside generic code. Declaring the preference at the host keeps the dependency pointing the right way.
- **Use whichever entry the host lists first.** Both hosts happen to lead their catalogue with the view they consider primary, so this would produce the right answer today with no new option — but nothing in the protocol promises that ordering, and the rule would silently change behaviour for every host if a catalogue were ever reordered.

## Tests

Six cases in `agentHostSessionChangesets.test.ts` covering the declared preference, the untouched fallback, and a preference the catalogue does not advertise.

Each was control-tested — the production change was reverted piecewise and the failure reason checked, not just the failure:

| Reverted | Fails | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| The declared preference is ignored (`defaultKind` pinned to `branch`) | the declared-preference test, and the not-advertised test | `branch*` instead of `session*` |
| The fallback kind is wrong (`?? ChangesetKind.Session`) | both no-preference tests | `session*` where `branch*` was expected |

The two no-preference tests pass with and without the fix by design: they are regression guards pinning that hosts which declare nothing are unaffected, and they are what catches an over-broad implementation.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` — clean
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — clean
- `npx eslint` on the five changed files — clean
- `./scripts/test.sh --glob "**/vs/{sessions,workbench/contrib/chat,platform/agentHost}/**/*.test.js"` — 14781 passing, 0 failing

Not verified end to end against a live sandbox session; that needs a human.

title: agentHost: gate turns through an onIncomingRequest chat contribution hook
body:
agentHost: gate turns through an onIncomingRequest chat contribution hook

Adds an admission hook to the chat contribution model and moves the read-only guard and
local command interception onto it. Turn admission was duplicated: `handleAction` and
`QueueDrainContribution` each ran the same preamble, and the read-only guard sat further
down in the send path. Admission now has one route and one copy.

- Adds `onIncomingRequest`, which decides whether a turn may proceed to its provider. A
  contribution returns `accept`, `handled`, or `reject`, and the first non-accept
  disposition wins.
- Makes the hook fail closed. Every other hook skips a contribution that throws; a throwing
  admission contribution rejects the request instead. The gate stops a client from running
  work in a session that can have no worktree on disk, so a failure must not open it.
- Makes the hook synchronous. A gate must decide before the send path awaits, so the state
  it reads cannot change before the decision takes effect. An asynchronous version deferred
  the read-only guard by one microtask and broke three existing tests.
- Adds `TurnAdmissionContribution` (order 100), which rejects turns on read-only chats and
  archived sessions.
- Adds `LocalCommandContribution` (order 50), which handles `/rename` and `!command`. The
  order is load-bearing: local commands were always intercepted before the read-only guard,
  so they stay available in read-only and archived chats.
- Adds the `startTurn` function, which runs the shared preamble: the gate, title seeding,
  provider lookup, the `noAgent` error, and turn telemetry. Both admission paths invoke it
  with `IInstantiationService.invokeFunction`. It is a function and not a service because it
  holds no state, so a service registration would only add one line to every hand-built test
  service graph.
- Moves `AgentHostTurnFailureStage` to `common` so the disposition can name a failure stage.
  The node telemetry reporter re-exports it, so no importer changes.
- Removes the admission block from `_sendTurnMessage`, which is now only the send tail.
- Accepts that a rejected turn no longer reports `userMessageSent` or `turnCompleted`. The
  gate runs before `turnStarted`, so there is no turn to complete. `chatContributions/TODO.md`
  records this.
- Rewrites `chatContributions/TODO.md`. It listed `githubReferences` as an outgoing-turn
  contribution although it only implements `onTurnEnd`, and described an admission flow that
  no longer exists. Adds a table of all six hooks and their contributions in order.

title: chat: choose compatibility when creating Agent Plugins
body:
## Summary

- generate a canonical Agent Plugins 1.0 package from **Chat: Create Plugin**
- after resource selection, offer either the standard package or the standard package with additive legacy compatibility files
- keep portable and Copilot-specific components in their sanctioned Agent Plugins locations
- validate MCP definitions before writing files and preserve SSE/Streamable HTTP semantics without exporting configured headers

Fixes #332811

## Format choices

- **Agent Plugin** — Standard plugin format
- **Open Plugin (Legacy Compatibility)** — Also supports older clients

Both choices generate the same valid Agent Plugins 1.0 package. Compatibility mode additionally projects the selected resources into `.plugin/plugin.json`, legacy `commands/`, `agents/`, `rules/`, `hooks/hooks.json`, and `.mcp.json` paths. The canonical root manifest and component paths remain authoritative and cause modern clients to detect the package as an Agent Plugin.

## Decision log

- **Agent Plugins 1.0 is always canonical.** Generated content should be as future-proof and portable as possible.
- **Compatibility is additive, not an alternate legacy-only package.** Older clients get redundant legacy paths without weakening or omitting the standard representation.
- **The choice follows resource selection.** Users first choose what to package, then decide whether older-client compatibility files are needed.
- **Use established compatibility terminology.** The picker labels the additive compatibility choice `Open Plugin (Legacy Compatibility)` while the canonical package remains Agent Plugins 1.0.
- **Canonical validity gates both modes.** If an MCP server cannot be represented safely by Agent Plugins 1.0, creation fails before writing files rather than producing a legacy-only partial package.
- **Credential safety applies to both modes.** Configured HTTP headers are never copied into distributable output.
- **Internal parser naming is unchanged.** Existing `PluginFormat.OpenPlugin` terminology remains an implementation detail outside this PR’s scope.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- `node test/unit/browser/index.js --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/actions/createPluginAction.test.ts --browser firefox` (45 passing)
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/actions/createPluginAction.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/actions/createPluginAction.test.ts`

title: nes: apply supportsUnifiedCompletions on the default provider path
body:
## Summary

Follow-up hotfix to #332018. The `supportsUnifiedCompletions` capability (baked into the `patchBased02Optimized` prompting strategy) was only wired into the **joint** completions provider (`JointCompletionsProviderContribution`), which is gated behind `chat.advanced.inlineEdits.jointCompletionsProvider.enabled` (default **`false`**).

On the **default** provider path, `InlineEditProviderFeature.registerProvider()` registers NES and suppresses the separate completions/ghost-text provider via a `modelUnification`-derived `excludes` list. Because that block only consulted the core `unificationStateValue?.modelUnification`, a model that sets `supportsUnifiedCompletions` purely through its prompting strategy (e.g. a `copilot-proxy` `/models` deployment with no ExP/local unification toggles) still emitted ghost-text completions.

## Fix

Derive the effective unification in `InlineEditProviderFeature` from the baked `supportsUnifiedCompletions` flag, OR-ed with the core `modelUnification` state, and use it to gate the `excludes`:

```ts
const modelUnification = this._supportsUnifiedCompletions.read(reader) || (unificationStateValue?.modelUnification ?? false);
```

When set, both `'completions'` and `'github.copilot'` are excluded -- matching the `excludedProviders: "completions,github.copilot"` behavior the strategy is meant to replace. The flag is observed reactively via `IInlineEditsModelService.onModelListUpdated`, mirroring the wiring already added to the joint provider in #332018. The core experiment/deployment path is unchanged for models that do not set the flag.

## Known limitations

- **Startup flicker (fetched `/models` path only).** `supportsUnifiedCompletions` is the only strategy-baked value read at provider-registration time rather than per-request, so it depends on the async `/models` resolution. During the cold-start window before the fetch resolves, `selectedModelConfiguration()` has no strategy yet, the flag reads `false`, and the separate completions provider is not yet excluded -- so ghost text can briefly appear. It self-corrects the instant `onModelListUpdated` fires (the observable has no debounce and re-registers immediately). This does **not** affect local/ExP model configuration, which resolves synchronously at startup. Fully eliminating the window would require holding the separate `github.copilot` completions provider until the NES model list first resolves; that is a larger change tracked in #332837 and intentionally left out of this hotfix.
- **`forceUseDefaultModel` fallback drops baked knobs (pre-existing, all strategies).** If the deployed model returns `NotFound` (404), the provider falls back to `defaultModelConfiguration()`, which does not apply `applyStrategyConfig`. All strategy-baked values are bypassed under this fallback -- this is shared graceful-degradation behavior affecting every strategy (including `patchBased02WithRecentLineNumbers`), not specific to `patchBased02Optimized`.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck --prefix extensions/copilot` (changed file clean)
- focused Vitest for `applyStrategyConfig` / `MODEL_CONFIGURATION_VALIDATOR` and `UserInteractionMonitor`
- `npm run precommit`

title: sessions: Show pending approvals on their own chat rows
body:
## Overview

Follow-up to #332739 (nested chats shown as child rows under each session). Now that a session's nested chats render as their own rows, this surfaces each chat's pending tool approval **on that chat's row** instead of aggregating every chat's approval onto the parent session row.

## What changed

- **Per-chat approval rows**: `SessionChatItemRenderer` now renders a chat's pending approval (command label + **Allow** button) on the chat's own row, keyed on that chat's resource. The row layout became a flex column: a fixed-height title row with the approval stacked beneath it.
- **Session row shows only its main chat's approval**: the parent session row uses `getMainChatApproval` (main chat only) instead of aggregating across all chats. Nested/side chats surface their approvals on their own rows.
- **Flat, chat-less lists unchanged**: the blocked-sessions dropdown and automations view render no nested chat rows, so their session rows still aggregate an approval from *any* of a session's chats. This is gated by a new `aggregateChatApprovals` flag on the shared renderer/delegate.
- **Shared rendering**: the approval-row markup + "Allow" behavior are extracted into a shared `renderApprovalRowContent` helper, and the CSS is hoisted to a top-level `.session-approval-row` rule so the session row and chat rows render identically.
- **Virtualization**: the tree delegate reserves the extra row height for a chat with a pending approval (plus a small bottom slack for code-block line-height rounding) and updates it reactively via `onDidChangeItemHeight` as approvals appear and clear.

## Why

With multiple chats per session, aggregating all approvals onto the parent row made it ambiguous which chat needed input and only surfaced one approval at a time. Rendering each approval on its owning chat row makes the pending action unambiguous and lets multiple sibling chats show their approvals simultaneously.

## Notes for reviewers

- `mainChat.resource` is guarded so a session with an unresolved main chat simply shows no approval.

title: Do not resolve content references as filesystem entries
body:
Opening a file diff from a remote agent session fails:

```
Unable to read file 'vscode-agent-host://.../changeset/turncontent/2011679d…'
  → -32602 invalid params: unsupported scheme `ahp-session`; expected `file`
```

The changes list populates; only opening a diff fails. Local sessions are fine.

## What the protocol says

A `ContentRef` is "a reference to large content stored outside the state tree". It carries its own `sizeHint` and `contentType`, and `resourceRead`'s `uri` is documented as "Content URI from a `ContentRef`".

`resourceResolve` is "the combination of POSIX `stat` and `realpath`" — its result `type` is `file` \| `directory` \| `symlink`.

So a content ref is **read**, never **resolved**. It is not a filesystem entry, so `resourceResolve` has no answer to give, and needs none: the metadata travels with the ref.

## What we do instead

`AHPFileSystemProvider` serves remote content, so the editor's file layer `stat`s before reading. `stat()` and `realpath()` short-circuited content refs with a hardcoded scheme allowlist:

```ts
if (decoded.scheme === 'session-db' || decoded.scheme === 'git-blob') {
```

Those are two of the shapes VS Code's own host emits, which is why local sessions always hit the shortcut and this went unnoticed. But the shape is the host's choice, and there are already more of them in tree — `agenthost-content:` and `pending-edit-content:` are content refs too, and neither is in the list.

A remote host publishes `ahp-session:/<id>/changeset/turncontent/<sha>`. Not in the list, so the `stat` went to the host, reached its filesystem resolver, and was rejected as a malformed file path. The read that follows would have succeeded — the host routes `/changeset/turncontent/` correctly — but it is never reached.

## Content URI shapes, for comparison

VS Code's own host — path is the real file path, lookup keys in the query:

```
session-db:/Users/me/.copilot/session-state/e580756b/files/capture_addon.py
           ?{"sessionUri":"copilotcli:/9b08d9c3…","toolCallId":"toolu_019SSYR2…"}

git-blob:/Users/me/…/baseAgentHostSessionsProvider.ts
         ?{"sessionUri":"copilotcli:/9b08d9c3…","sha":"3d079185299158cc…"}
```

A remote host — an opaque reference, the path is not a file path:

```
ahp-session:/ab456a26-9bfd-4e69-8538-787d4e664c52/changeset/turncontent/2011679d9182…
```

The protocol's own `resourceRead` example is the same shape as the latter: `ahp-session:/<uuid>/content/img-1`.

## The fix

Stop inferring from the scheme. Callers read these URIs straight out of a `ContentRef` field, so they know what they are holding — that fact was simply dropped when the URI was wrapped for transport, leaving the provider to reconstruct it by sniffing.

`toAgentHostContentUri()` records it in the metadata the transport URI already carries (`?_ah=…`), and `stat` / `realpath` short-circuit on that marker. Because the marker lives in the URI, it survives persistence.

Every site that wraps a `ContentRef` now uses it: the changes view (`agentHostDiffs`, `agentHostSessionFiles`), the chat response file changes, the snapshot controller, and the pending-edit confirmations. The `_diffUriMapper` hook gained an options argument so the two mapper-based sites can signal it.

The scheme allowlist stays, narrowed to its real job: content refs minted before the marker existed, e.g. ones persisted in restored editor state.

## Risk

A wrapped URI without the marker behaves exactly as before. `file:` content refs on the local connection stay unwrapped and resolve normally, as they do today. The only behaviour change is for URIs that previously failed to `stat`.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`, `npm run valid-layers-check`, `eslint` on all changed files
- `./scripts/test.sh --glob "**/vs/{sessions,workbench/contrib/chat,platform/agentHost}/**/*.test.js"` — 14,620 passing
- New tests: marker round-trip, `stat` and `realpath` not calling the host for a content ref, and `readFile` still reaching it
- One existing snapshot updated — `pending-edit-content:` is a content ref, so its expectation now uses the content wrapper

Control-tested by reverting the marker check: `stat` then reports `resolved: 1` instead of `resolved: 0`, reproducing the production failure rather than merely failing.

title: Flag Agent Merge initiated turns in agent host turn telemetry
body:
## Description

Agent Merge starts turns by sending a host-generated prompt, which was indistinguishable in telemetry from any other host notification. This extends the existing message-origin field with a third value so automated merge work is separable from turns a person or an agent asked for.

**Telemetry**
- `messageOriginKind` on `agentHost.userMessageSent` gains `agentMerge`, alongside the protocol's `user` / `agent` / `tool` / `automation` / `systemNotification`.
- `agentHost.turnCompleted` now reports `messageOriginKind`, so a finished turn is attributable to whoever started it. `turnFailed` / `turnHung` are untouched — `turnCompleted` is emitted for failures too.
- `MessageKind` lives in the auto-generated protocol (`DO NOT EDIT`), so this is a telemetry-only widening: `MessageKind | 'agentMerge'`.

**Identifying merge turns**
- Agent Merge prompts carry `MessageKind.SystemNotification`, but so do the merge notice and Copilot session notifications, so origin kind alone is insufficient. `common/meta/agentMergeMessageMeta.ts` stamps a `vscode.chat.agentMerge` marker into `_meta`, following the `agentMessageDelegationMeta.ts` convention.
- `agentService._startAgentMergePrompt` — the only path that turns a merge decision into a turn — stamps it.
- `getMessageOriginTelemetryKind` honours the marker only on the host-stamped `systemNotification` origin, so a client-supplied `_meta` can't dress a user message up as merge work:

```ts
export function getMessageOriginTelemetryKind(message: Message): AgentHostMessageOriginTelemetryKind {
	if (message.origin.kind === MessageKind.SystemNotification && isAgentMergeMessage(message)) {
		return 'agentMerge';
	}
	return message.origin.kind;
}
```

**Plumbing**
- Threaded through `AgentHostTurnTracker.turnStarted` → `ITurnTiming` → the `turnCompleted` report.
- Queue-drained turns derive it from their message like direct turns.
- Subagent turn starts synthesize a seed message claiming `user` origin; those two call sites now report `tool` explicitly (the protocol's meaning for a tool spawning a worker chat) without altering the stored message.

**Tests**
- Reporter: `agent` / `agentMerge` / `user` on both standard and GitHub events, plus a spoofed-marker user message still reporting `user`.
- End-to-end through `AgentSideEffects`: `turnCompleted.messageOriginKind` is `user` for a user turn and `agentMerge` for a merge turn.

title: agentHost: run Codex workspace hooks
body:
Fixes #331285

## Problem

A `.codex/hooks.json` hook in the workspace never ran. It showed up correctly in the Customizations view (**Hooks: 1**), but nothing executed.

Codex refuses to *dispatch* a hook until its exact command hash has been recorded as trusted in `config.toml`. That ledger is only written by the codex TUI's startup hook-review screen — a surface agent host users never reach — so workspace hooks were discovered and then silently dropped.

Confirmed by driving `codex app-server` directly, outside VS Code:

| run | `hooks/list` | hook ran |
|---|---|---|
| baseline | `sessionStart` / `untrusted` | ❌ |
| `bypass_hook_trust: true` | `sessionStart` / `untrusted` | ✅ |

Project trust was a red herring: `thread/start` already auto-persists `projects.<cwd>.trust_level = "trusted"` on its own, and the hook still did not run.

## Change

Pass `bypass_hook_trust` on every codex thread via a shared `codexThreadBaseConfig` fragment, applied to all four thread-creation paths — `thread/start` (materialize + side chat), `thread/fork`, and `thread/resume`.

This is the documented purpose of the flag ("automation that already vets hook sources"). The agent host vets them up front: `_ensureFoldersTrusted` refuses to start a session until **every** working directory passes VS Code Workspace Trust. That makes codex's per-hook ledger redundant here, and brings Codex in line with the Claude and Copilot harnesses, which already run workspace hooks.

Enterprise policy is unaffected: `HookDiscoveryPolicy::allows` is independent of `bypass_hook_trust`, so `allow_managed_hooks_only` still wins. Verified both by reading the codex source and empirically. Per the `policy-and-managed-settings` guidance this control stays runtime-owned, so no VS Code policy is added.

**Coupled fix:** `ALWAYS_CHECKED_EDIT_PATTERNS` covered `.github/hooks/**` and `.claude/settings*.json` but not `.codex`. Since these hooks now actually execute, `.codex/hooks.json`, `.codex/config.toml` and `.codex/agents/**` are added so the agent cannot silently install one without user confirmation.

## Validation

Built Code OSS and ran a real A/B in the Agents window, same build / workspace / prompt, using the issue's exact `hooks.json`:

- **With the fix** — `.codex-dummy-hook.log` created; agent host logged `hook/started` + `hook/completed`
- **Fix reverted** — no log, no `hook/*` notifications (bug reproduced)

`npm run compile` and `npm run hygiene` are clean. `CodexLaunchConfig` 4/4 and the lifecycle-hook / casing permission tests pass.
