title: Remove external session files from the agent host adaptor
body:
The session adaptor derived an `externalFiles` observable — files the agent created, edited or deleted outside the workspace — and surfaced it as `ISession.externalChanges`. It was the only reader of `IChatFileEdits.allEdits`, and reading it forced a `StateComponents.Chat` subscription for **every peer chat** in the session plus a parse of **every completed turn**, purely to keep that list current.

This removes the feature and its three consumers, then simplifies the parsing it was holding up.

### Consumers removed

- **Chat pills** — `buildSessionArtifactSections` no longer takes an `externalFiles` argument, dropping the previewable-file/image merge loop.
- **Agent feedback** — `_isFileInSessionScope` becomes `_isFileEligibleForFeedback`: a file is eligible unless it is an output-channel resource. The `session.changes` lookup, the external-changes lookup and the workspace-folder containment check are gone.
- **Changes view** — the "Other Files" section is removed: `SessionFilesWidget`, `SessionFilesViewModel`, their CSS and fixture are deleted, and the `SplitView` drops from three panes to two (CI checks moves from index 2 to index 1).
- **Session model** — `ISession.externalChanges`, `ISessionFile` and `SessionFileOperation` are removed, along with both `visibleSessions.ts` wrapper getters.

### The perf win

With `allEdits` gone, two things in `agentHostSessionFiles.ts` fall away:

- **Per-chat subscriptions are now lazy.** The old `chatUrisObs` → `mapObservableArrayCached` fan-out read every chat's edits, and chat-state subscriptions are created on read — so an active session opened a subscription for every peer chat. Chats are now created on demand keyed by the requested chat URI, so a peer chat nobody reads costs nothing.
- **Only the last turn is parsed.** `createIncrementalChatFileEditsParser` no longer walks and memoizes every completed turn. It parses the active turn while streaming, or memoizes just the last completed turn by id. Turns that were never the last turn are never parsed at all.

Net **−1189 lines**.

### Notes

- **Agent feedback is a behaviour change, not just a deletion.** Feedback is now accepted on any open editor while a session is active, including files outside the workspace such as user settings. This is intended, but it is the case the old scoping existed to exclude.
- **The accessibility help was updated too.** `sessionsChangesAccessibilityHelp.ts` had two localized strings describing the Other Files section and its keyboard behaviour; leaving them would have had the screen-reader help dialog describe a section that no longer exists.
- **No collapse-state migration needed.** `otherFiles` is removed from `IChangesViewSectionCollapseState`; that state is in-memory only (`IStoredChangesViewState` persists just `detailsViewState`), so nothing stale is read back from storage.

### Validation

`npm run typecheck-client` clean; affected unit tests pass (118 + 194 + 16 across the sessions provider, changes view, chat artifacts, agent feedback and visible-sessions suites).

title: files: stop Windows watcher flood after folder deletion
body:
## Summary

- detect the absolute watched-root path that Windows reports after a watched folder is deleted
- close the stale native watcher so repeated `rename` events cannot spin and flood process logs
- reattach directly when the folder was recreated before the delayed existence check completes
- cover permanent deletion, rapid delete/recreate, continued events after reattachment, and same-named children

## Motivation

Recent Agent Host sessions showed `agenthost.log` growing by roughly 2 MB every three seconds. The log was dominated by repeated events such as:

```
[File Watcher (node.js)] [raw] ["rename"] \\?\c:\Code\vscode.worktrees\...\.github\agents
```

Once the log reached its rotation threshold, this also produced 23,832 main-process errors in one session:

```
rotating_file_sink: failed renaming ...\agenthost.log to ...\agenthost.1.log: permission denied
```

On Windows, `fs.watch` reports the full extended watched path in a tight loop after folder deletion. The existing code compared the raw event only with the folder basename and continually postponed its deletion check, so it never recognized the watched root as deleted.

## Validation

- focused Node.js watcher regressions: 3 passing
- `npm run transpile-client`
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- reviewed through three passes with Claude Opus 5; all actionable findings addressed

Fixes #332352

- The tunnel remains visible as disconnected and can be selected manually.
- An explicit reconnect clears the suppression.

title: Cache active-session external changes in AgentFeedbackService scope checks
body:
## Description

Loading or reopening a large Agent Host session generated thousands of duplicate child-chat subscriptions (~343 MB of AHP traffic, ~1,005 retained chat-state snapshots vs. a 42 MB / 78 snapshot baseline).

`AgentFeedbackService._isFileInSessionScope` runs for every visible editor and read `session.externalChanges?.get()`. That observable is subscription-backed (`createSessionOutputObs` → `externalFiles` → `editsPerChatObs` → `createActiveSessionSubscriptionObs`, which registers the AHP subscription ref on `reader.store`). A derived with zero observers computes *without caching* and then disposes its reader store, so every scope check acquired and immediately released one chat-state subscription **per chat** in the session — 39 chats × every visible changed-file editor.

```ts
// before: one uncached recomputation of the whole chain per scope check
if (session.externalChanges?.get().some(file => isEqual(file.uri, resourceUri))) {
	return true;
}
```

### Changes

- **Read from a kept-observed derived** — `_activeSessionExternalFiles` derives the active session's external files once and is held observed via `keepObserved`, so repeated scope checks hit the cache instead of re-subscribing. It stays lazy: nothing subscribes until the first out-of-workspace file is actually checked.
- **Reset on session switch** — the observation is re-established on active-session change (keyed on the session resource) and released on dispose, so the previous session's subscriptions drop immediately rather than being pinned. Note the ordering: `MutableDisposable.value = keepObserved(...)` evaluates the new observation *before* disposing the old one, which would never let the observer count reach zero, so the handle is `clear()`ed first.
- **External check runs last** — reordered `_isFileInSessionScope` so the changes/workspace-folder branches short-circuit first. Behaviour is unchanged (every preceding branch already returned `true`), but files inside the session workspace now never touch the external-changes chain at all.
- **Gated on the active session** — `externalFiles` is already gated on `isActiveSession && !isArchived` in the agent host provider, and other providers leave `externalChanges` undefined, so a non-active session returns `[]` either way.

### Test

`computes the session external changes once for repeated scope checks` counts recomputations and reader-store disposals through a derived that mirrors the provider's per-chat subscription. Three scope checks yield 1 computation / 0 releases; switching the active session releases them. Against the pre-fix read the same test reports 3 computations / 3 acquire-release cycles.

title: Filters: collapse runs of wildcards in quick pick queries
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #332507

Every `*` in a fuzzy quick pick query became its own unbounded `.*` in the converted regexp. A run of adjacent stars made matching super-polynomial - the engine explores every composition of the haystack across the wildcards before failing near the end:

- `matchesFuzzy('********b', 'a'.repeat(28))`: about 1.4 s
- 12 stars against 40 characters: over 2 minutes
- simulated 20,000 label picker, query `*****com`: about 2.5 s per keystroke

This freezes the renderer while typing in any picker routed through `matchesFuzzy`. Runs of adjacent stars now collapse to a single wildcard (`/\*+/g -> '.*'`), which is language-preserving: `.*.*` accepts exactly what `.*` does, so no observable match span changes. A 300,000 case randomized old-vs-new comparison of match spans found zero differences.

Known open follow-up (not addressed here): queries with many *separated* wildcards (`a*b*c*d*e*f*g*h`) can still backtrack exponentially on adversarial labels. Unlike the `fuzzyScore` path, which caps input at `_maxLen = 128`, the regexp path has no cap; that deserves its own discussion since capping changes semantics for long legitimate queries.

Draft until #332507 receives triage.

## How was this tested

```
npm run transpile-client
exit 0

scripts\test.bat --run vs/base/test/common/filters.test.js --run vs/base/test/common/strings.test.js
92 passing, 0 failing
```

- New `convertSimple2RegExpPattern` tests: `'**' -> '.*'` and `'a**b' -> 'a.*b'` fail on main (which produced `.*.*` / `a.*.*b`) and pass here; `'*a*' -> '.*a.*'` pins the unchanged single-star form.
- New filters tests pin that `'**b'`, `'***'` behave exactly like `'*b'`, `'*'`.
- Measured before/after on this machine: `********b` vs 28 chars went from 1398 ms to under 1 ms; the 20k label simulation went from 2508 ms to 1.7 ms.

title: Context keys: accept the d and v regex flags in when clauses
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #332506

The context key expression scanner whitelisted only `i g s m y u` as regex flags following a regex literal, so a legal when clause like `a =~ /x/d` failed to lex: the trailing flag became a separate token, parsing failed, and `ContextKeyExpr.deserialize` dropped the whole expression (the clause silently never matched). `d` (hasIndices) and `v` (unicodeSets) are valid in every engine VS Code ships on and now pass through to `RegExp` construction.

One pre-existing test pinned the exact token stream the lexer produces for an *invalid* input (`//view/...` garbage after an empty regex). With `v` whitelisted the lexer consumes one more character before erroring, so that snapshot is updated to the new exact tokens; the input still fails to parse either way, and both `ErrorToken` entries remain asserted.

Draft until #332506 receives triage.

## How was this tested

```
npm run transpile-client
exit 0

scripts\test.bat --run vs/platform/contextkey/test/common/scanner.test.js --run vs/platform/contextkey/test/common/contextkey.test.js
58 passing, 0 failing
```

- New scanner tests: `/zee/d`, `/zee/v`, `/zee/gd` each lex as a single `RegexStr` token; these fail on main with a trailing `Str 'd'`.
- New end-to-end case: `testExpression('a =~ /t/d', true)` - deserialization previously returned undefined.
- Differential run of old vs new whitelist over 22 when-clause shapes: no previously-working expression changes outcome; divergence is confined to clauses using `d`/`v`, which went from parse-error to working.
- `deserialize('a =~ /t/d')` now returns a regex expr that evaluates and round-trips through `serialize`; the invalid snapshot string still fails to deserialize cleanly.

Monaco note: this file compiles into monaco (`src/tsconfig.monaco.json` includes it), but `Scanner._regexFlags` is private and no d.ts surface changes, so no generated-file update is needed.

title: Git: fix swapped name and commit in ls-remote heads parsing
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

-->

Fixes #332502

`Git.getRemoteRefs()` built remote head refs with the SHA in `name` and the branch name in `commit`, the reverse of the tags branch right below in the same parser, so any caller asking for `{ heads: true }` received unusable data. The inline parser moves to a `parseLsRemote` helper next to the other git output parsers (`parseLsTree`, `parseLsFiles`), splits on CRLF as well, and gains unit tests.

Draft until #332502 receives triage.

## How was this tested

```
node_modules/.bin/tsc -p extensions/git/tsconfig.json --noEmit
exit 0
```

```
npm run gulp compile-extension:git
Finished 'compile-extension:git' after 719 ms
```

The compiled parser was executed directly against realistic `git ls-remote` vectors:

- heads line: `{ name: 'main', commit: '<sha40>', type: RefType.Head }` - previously produced `{ name: '<sha40>', commit: 'main' }`
- tags line: unchanged, already correct before and after
- CRLF terminated output: names no longer carry a trailing `\r`
- mixed input with symbolic-ref (`HEAD`) lines and blank lines: filtered
- 64 character SHA-256 refs and `^{}` peeled tag lines: byte-for-byte identical behavior before and after (pre-existing limitations kept deliberately)

New tests in `extensions/git/src/test/git.test.ts` under `suite('parseLsRemote')`: empty, heads, tags, mixed with blank and unmatched lines, multiple heads. The heads assertions fail against the pre-fix mapping and pass with this change.

Differential check of old vs new parser over these inputs found no behavior change beyond the intended swap and CRLF tolerance; the sole production caller (`commands.ts`, remote tag deletion flow) uses the tags path whose mapping was already correct.

title: chat: summarize the Agent Merge prompt as a widget
body:
Agent Merge drives its repair turns with a machine-facing `<agent_merge_state>` block, which the transcript rendered verbatim — a wall of protocol text where the user expected a status update.

This extracts the prompt builder into `agentMergePrompt.ts` next to a matching parser, and renders the recovered state as a collapsible card.

### Collapsed
A single line naming the work and why it is happening.

### Expanded
The pull request, the review feedback, the failing checks, and a nested `Agent message` disclosure holding the verbatim instructions sent to the agent.

## Details

- **Parser lives with the builder.** `buildAgentMergePrompt` moved out of `agentMergeController.ts` so the format has one owner. The parser reads the state block **backwards from its end**, so untrusted feedback bodies (emitted before the trailing fields) cannot shift a later field boundary; a thread whose body mimics the prompt format stays one comment.
- **Untrusted markdown.** Review feedback renders through `ChatContentMarkdownRenderer`, so inline code, lists and links work while trusted command links stay off.
- **File labels.** Comments are labelled by file name, gaining the shortest distinguishing directory prefix only when several comments share a name — the same `shorten()` disambiguation editor tabs use.
- **Linked comments.** Prompt thread ids are exactly the `sourcePRReviewCommentId` the PR-review seeder stores, so matched labels reveal the local comment in the editor via one new command on the existing chat↔sessions bridge. Guarded on `CommandsRegistry`, so the regular workbench renders unchanged.
- **Checks link to GitHub.** Each failing check opens the pull request's checks tab. A per-run deep link would require adding `detailsUrl` to the model-facing prompt, so the prompt was left untouched.

## Testing

- 5 parser tests, including a build/parse round trip and an untrusted-feedback spoofing case.
- 3 tests for the file-label disambiguation.
- 12 component fixtures (Dark + Light) covering collapsed, expanded, comments-only, checks-only, conflicting, behind-base, markdown, duplicate file names, linked comments, and the expanded agent message.

title: sessions: share the session hover between the sessions list and chat pills
body:
The sessions list hover was an ad-hoc markdown string. It showed the source repository rather than the worktree a session actually works in, never used the word "Worktree", listed no pull requests, and named only the provider. It also could not be reused anywhere else.

## What changed

A shared `SessionSummaryHoverWidget` in the workbench layer renders provider-neutral `ISessionSummaryHoverData`, plus a small per-window `ISessionSummaryHoverService` registry so `agent-host-session://` pills in chat output show the same hover. Each window adapts its own data source onto that shape and omits what it cannot answer:

- Agents window: `ISession` -> hover data (`sessionHoverContent.ts`), the richest source.
- Editor window: `IChatSessionItem` -> hover data, which carries no worktree or pull requests, so those rows are simply absent.

## New layout

```
Fix authentication redirect loop          <- title only, no icon
 folder    \home\user\projects\vscode
 worktree  Worktree - \home\...\vscode.worktrees\fix-auth-redirect
 branch    fix-auth-redirect - 2 files changed +132 -18
------------------------------------------
 PR icon   Fix authentication redirect loop        <- live state colors
 PR icon   Add a regression test for the redirect loop
 PR icon   Revert the earlier redirect workaround
------------------------------------------
Claude - Local Agent Host                 <- dimmed
```

Separators only appear between blocks that exist, so a session with no pull requests gets one rule and a quick chat none. Despite carrying more information, it stays about as compact as before.

## Supporting model change

`IGitHubPullRequestRef` gained `title` and `createdByThisSession`. The agent-host provider populates both: titles come from the PR artifact labels the agent recorded, and `createdByThisSession` is the "main eligible" set (PRs the agent created plus PRs found for the session branch), excluding ones inherited from the checkout or merely referenced. Only pull requests the session produced are listed. Secondary PRs now also pick up their last-known state icon from `IPullRequestIconCache`, since only the main PR is polled live.

## Validation

- `tsc --noEmit` clean, eslint clean, stylelint clean, `valid-layers-check` passes
- 227 passing in the affected suites (`OpenSessionLinkOpenerContribution`, `LocalAgentHostSessionsProvider`, `SessionsLifecycleTracker`), including a new test that the pill hover data resolves through the registered provider
- New component fixtures (`sessions/sessionHover`) cover both data sources plus the empty cases, verified visually in the component explorer

title: Launch skill: attach the repo's automation library to a running instance
body:
## Why

The `launch` skill drove Code OSS exclusively through raw `@playwright/cli`, so every agent hand-writes selectors for surfaces that [`test/automation`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/tree/main/test/automation) already models.

That library is what the smoke tests use, and it encodes the knowledge these surfaces actually need. For example, `Chat.selectModel` already documents and retries the exact failure mode where a row click is "absorbed by the action-widget's animating `context-view-pointerBlock` overlay" — a failure I spent a long time rediscovering by hand.

## What

`test/automation` normally *spawns* Electron via `playwright._electron.launch()`. But `PlaywrightDriver` only uses that object for `windows()` / `close()` and already branches on `'windows' in application`, so a `Browser` from `chromium.connectOverCDP()` works in its place — letting the page objects attach to the instance `launch.sh` already started.

- **`scripts/attach.ts`** — `attach(cdpPort, { window })` returns `{ workbench, code, page, browser, detach }`
- **`automation-library.md`** — the companion doc: window choice, controls with no page object, the integrated browser, and the gotchas
- **`SKILL.md`** — a "Drive the UI" section pointing at both

## Why a module rather than a documented snippet

Three steps are invisible from the type definitions, and each fails in a way that does not point at its own cause:

1. `test/automation/out` is **CommonJS**, so `import { Code }` throws `SyntaxError: Named export not found`
2. `Quality` is a **`const enum`**, erased at compile time, so it has no runtime value; this surfaces later as `Cannot read properties of undefined`
3. **`window.driver` only exists with `--enable-smoke-test-driver`**; without it, page objects hang or throw obscure errors

Each is checked up front and reported with the fix. This matches the precedent set by `monaco-paste.sh` in the same skill.

## Validation

Verified live against a real instance:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Chat round-trip (authenticated, real response) | **PONG in 4.6s** |
| `workbench.extensions.searchForExtension` | returned publisher + install count in one call |
| Session-target picker to Local | switched, telemetry confirmed `explicitOverride` |
| `agentsWindow.isSessionTypeAvailable` | correctly reports Local is **not** offered there |
| Missing `--enable-smoke-test-driver` / unbuilt `out/` | names the exact command to run |
| Bad port / missing port / bad window kind / missing window | all actionable messages |

## What the user studies changed

I ran fresh agents against the docs and measured. The headline result was that **the companion doc alone did not work**: in the first two studies no agent ever opened it, and one spent **7m40s and 40 raw CLI calls** hand-rolling DOM queries for a task `workbench.extensions.searchForExtension()` answers in one line.

Two follow-up runs isolated why, and each finding became a doc change:

| Run | Time | Raw CLI calls | What it exposed |
|---|---|---|---|
| Baseline | 7m40s | 40 | Never opened the companion doc → list the page objects in `SKILL.md` itself |
| + inventory | 3m42s | 20 | Reached for `new Application(...)` under `ts-node` (the *spawn* API) → name `attach()` as the entry point |
| + entry point | 4m33s | 7 | Launched without `--enable-smoke-test-driver` → show the flag at launch time, where it must be passed |

Dogfooding the condensed docs also caught two things worth having: `Set Session Target` is gated on `chatSessionIsEmpty` so it vanishes once a session has a turn, and `searchForExtension` takes an extension **id** — passing a display name fails with `Extension ... is not found`, which reads like the surface is unsupported.

`automation-library.md` was condensed from 267 to ~210 lines in the process, keeping the gotchas that cost multiple runs to discover and cutting the ones that were self-inflicted or instantly obvious.


## Launcher changes that came out of review

Copilot reviewed this a number of times, and the launcher-side findings turned out to be the substantive ones. Each was reproduced before being changed.

**The `editor.editContext` problem.** The page objects pick `.native-edit-context` vs `textarea` from `Code.editContextEnabled`, which is unconditionally `true` for a dev build. A cloned profile that had set `editor.editContext: false` rendered a `textarea` while every text-input helper waited on the wrong selector and timed out 20s later, pointing at nothing. Both launchers now normalize that key alongside `files.simpleDialog.enable`.

Scope turned out to be the hard part, in three layers:

- `editor.*` settings are `LANGUAGE_OVERRIDABLE`, so a `"[typescript]"` block outranks the root value — nested overrides are rewritten too, but only in real override blocks (`OVERRIDE_PROPERTY_REGEX`), not in unrelated nested data.
- Named profiles read `User/profiles/<id>/settings.json`, and the clone preserves the workspace→profile associations that `resolveProfileForBrowserWindow` acts on. Every existing profile settings file is normalized; only profiles whose stored metadata sets `useDefaultFlags.settings` genuinely inherit, and only those are left alone. A symlinked `User/profiles` or profile directory aborts the launch, since `rsync -a` preserves it and the clone would no longer be self-contained.
- Workspace and folder settings merge *after* user configuration, so no amount of profile rewriting can guarantee the effective value. `attach()` detects that case during preflight — after `whenWorkbenchRestored()`, once there are editors to inspect — and says where to look instead of letting the first helper time out.

**The settings merge itself.** It has to be data-preserving (comments and user values survive), which rules out reparse-and-rewrite. It now lives in one **`scripts/normalize-automation-settings.ts`** used by both launchers so the platforms cannot drift, and it fails closed: the file is parsed the way VS Code parses it before anything is written, so a malformed `settings.json` is never clobbered. Along the way review caught symlinked settings files being written through (`rsync -a` preserves links, so this escaped the throwaway profile), `"\u005btypescript\u005d"` not being recognized as an override, and `--sync=off` being defeated by a forwarded `--sync=on` because VS Code keeps the *last* value of a string option.

**Parsing it the way VS Code does.** Fail-closed validation only helps if it agrees with the real parser, and several rounds of review were spent closing that gap: VS Code's JSONC scanner ends a line comment at a bare `\r` and at U+2028/U+2029, accepts the full Unicode 3.0 space set as whitespace, and treats an unterminated block comment as an error rather than as trivia running to EOF. Each mismatch either rejected a profile VS Code reads happily (aborting the launch) or accepted one it rejects (rewriting a broken file).

**`scripts/normalize-automation-settings.test.ts`** covers this with 68 `node --test` cases. Every guard was mutation-checked: removing it fails at least one test.

Review also hardened the surrounding recipes — the cleanup snippets in `SKILL.md` now verify that the directory they are about to `rm -rf` really is a launcher run directory under the launcher's own temp root, and a PowerShell equivalent was added for Windows (where `$pid` is read-only and `-like` treats a temp path containing `[1]` as a wildcard pattern).

title: agent host: fix task completion summary
body:
## Summary

Fixes #332464

Autopilot renders the summary passed to `task_complete` as a root Markdown response prefixed with **Task completed:**. When that summary was large enough to trigger the Copilot SDK's tool-output limit, the SDK replaced `tool.execution_complete.result.content` with an `Output too large to read at once...` notice and a temporary file path.

Agent Host treated that model-facing tool output as the authoritative completion summary, so users saw the truncation notice instead of the summary the model provided:

```text
Task completed: Output too large to read at once...
```

The incorrect text was also persisted in Agent Host state, so it appeared both while the session was live and after restoring the session history.

## Fix

Prefer the original `task_complete` `summary` argument when generating the user-facing completion Markdown. The tool output remains as a fallback for older or incomplete events that do not contain the original argument.

This restores the intended output:

```text
Task completed: <the model's actual completion summary>
```

The fix does not depend on matching the SDK's truncation-message wording and does not change large-output handling for regular tools.

body:
## Summary

- remove the workbench lifecycle dependency from `DecorationAddon`
- let `XtermTerminal`, which already knows whether it is detached, own decoration shutdown cleanup
- register one decoration cleanup listener for regular terminals and none for detached terminals
- preserve normal addon disposal for detached terminals

title: Avoid stale active client updates after session disposal
body:
Regression from #330378.

## Regression details

A scan of recent Insiders logs found 41 instances of this Agent Host error signature across three sessions:

```
[AgentService] async dispatchAction failed: Session was explicitly deleted: copilotcli:/<session>
```

AHP traffic for the latest non-shutdown occurrence showed the deterministic sequence:

1. The client successfully published its initial `session/activeClientSet`.
2. The session was deleted with `disposeSession`.
3. `ChatSessionsService` delegated the backend deletion but kept its cached contributed chat session alive when no widget was available to clear it.
4. The `AgentHostChatSession` cleanup therefore did not run, leaving its `ActiveClientEntry` attached to the customization scope.
5. A customization refresh 94 minutes later caused another `session/activeClientSet` for the deleted backend session.
6. The Agent Host correctly rejected that stale action because the session was tombstoned.

The root cause was the missing cached-session disposal after a successful delete. Guarding reconciliation on missing backend state would mask that lifecycle bug and conflate a disposed session with the valid pre-hydration state used for an initial claim.

## Fix

After the session controller successfully deletes a session, `ChatSessionsService` now disposes the matching cached contributed chat session, including an aliased entry. That runs the provider cleanup, disposes the `ActiveClientEntry`, and cancels any future active-client reconciliation.

Disposal happens only after controller deletion succeeds. If backend deletion fails, the cached session remains available and the UI can continue showing the still-existing session.

## Tests

- Updated `does not republish activeClientSet after the chat session is disposed` to verify that session disposal cancels later customization-driven publication.
- Added `disposes cached content only after controller deletion succeeds` to cover both failed deletion preserving the cache and successful deletion disposing and evicting it.
- Ran all `ChatSessionsService` tests: 30/30 passed.
- Ran the Agent Host customization suite: 22/22 passed.
- `npm run transpile-client`
- Editor diagnostics on all changed files
- `git diff --check`
- Pre-commit hygiene checks

A fresh Insiders runtime log reproduction was not performed; the focused tests cover the observed lifecycle sequence.

title: Keep locally provisioned sessions out of the list until they are real
body:
Two list bugs with the same root: a session that exists remotely before the host knows about it.

## 1. The row appeared twice for ~8 seconds

A provider that creates a session remotely seeds it into its cache **before** connecting, so a later discovery pass reconciles against it instead of creating a second entry. But the caller is still showing an optimistic placeholder row for that same session until the first turn is dispatched — so publishing the seed straight away listed the session twice while the environment woke.

Measured on a real run: seed at `19.658`, placeholder retired at `27.615`.

Retiring the placeholder earlier is not an option — swapping when the session merely *exists* hands the UI a session it cannot open yet and the view falls back to the new-session screen. That was tried and reverted.

So the seed is withheld from `getSessions` instead, and revealed as the placeholder is retired:

- **The reveal is silent.** The list re-reads on any change, so a single event swaps both rows. Announcing separately would trade an 8-second overlap for a one-frame one.
- **Withheld is not unreachable.** `getSessionByResource` reads the cache directly, so opening still resolves — hidden from the *list*, not from the app.
- **A failed first turn still reveals it,** since the session outlives the failure and would otherwise be invisible.

## 2. The row vanished, the view went home, then it came back

Connecting triggers a reconciliation that prunes anything cached but not listed by the host. But the session id is minted before the host materializes the session, so that first listing can legitimately omit it. The prune landed ~400ms after the placeholder swap, deleting the row the user was looking at:

```
02.735  host: "not found: ahp-session:/355591eb…"
02.742  swap to the committed session
03.131  committed session removed → back to the new-session screen
```

Sessions seeded as provisional now resist that eviction until the host lists them. The base provider **already** made this exemption for a sibling case ("some hosts briefly omit the just-sent eager session"), so that is generalized into an overridable hook rather than adding a parallel mechanism.

**The protection is bounded (2 min).** Without a deadline, a session the host will never list becomes a permanent row that only a reload clears — trading a visible flash for an invisible one. Both directions are tested.

## Risk

`_isSessionEvictable` defaults to `true` and `_onHostListedSessions` is empty, so every provider that does not opt in behaves exactly as before. Only sessions seeded with `provisional` take the new paths.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`, `npm run valid-layers-check`
- `./scripts/test.sh --glob "**/vs/sessions/**/*.test.js"` — 2469 passing
- The eviction guard was verified by deleting it and confirming the new test fails, then restoring it — a test that passes for the wrong reason is worse than no test.

title: Let agent host sessions tolerate hosts that differ from the client
body:
Three ways a session against a host that is older than, or shaped differently from, the client would fail outright. All three surfaced against a remote host running an older `copilotd`, but none of the fixes are specific to it — `AgentHostSessionHandler` serves local, SSH and tunnel sessions too.

## 1. Customization shape skew

Customizations moved from an `enabled` boolean to list-shaped `enablement` in protocol 0.8.0. A host below that version expects the superseded shape and rejects the **whole request** with `invalid params: missing field "enabled"`, failing `createSession` and leaving no session at all.

Client-published customizations are now dropped for such a host, degrading to a session without them — which is what that host would have made of them anyway; the alternative is no session.

The gate is applied on **both** paths that publish an active client. Reconciliation republishes it after creation, so gating only `createSession` leaves the second path broken.

Worth noting for reviewers: the version registry has exhaustive, compile-enforced maps for *actions* and *notifications*, but nothing for field-level shape changes like this one, so the version constant here is hand-maintained.

## 2. Working directories the host cannot address

A workspace may be the repository itself (`https://github.com/owner/repo`) while the agent runs against a checkout on the host’s own disk. Sending the remote URI fails `createSession` with `unsupported scheme "https"; expected "file"`.

Directories the host cannot address are now dropped, falling back to `undefined` so it chooses its own. The host’s reported `defaultDirectory` names the scheme it can address, so this adapts per host rather than hardcoding `file`. Hosts that report no default are left alone.

## 3. "Couldn’t open session" for a session that does not exist yet

A provider can legitimately address a session id before the host knows it, with `createSession` bringing it into being. Subscribing first fails with `NotFound`, which rendered a failure banner that the very next step resolved.

The banner is suppressed for `NotFound` **specifically** — a genuine open failure still renders, which a test covers directly so the suppression cannot quietly widen.

## Risk

All three are no-ops for a current host with matching schemes: the version gate passes, every directory is addressable, and sessions resolve. The blast radius is wider than the case that motivated them, so the no-op paths are the ones worth checking.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `./scripts/test.sh --glob "**/agentHostChatContribution.test.js"` — 328 passing, including 6 new tests covering both sides of each fix (drops *and* keeps, suppresses *and* still renders).

## Note on the `NotFound` suppression

The suppression is deliberately broad: it covers every AHP `NotFound`, not only a session the client minted and expects to create on first send.

This costs a notice, not a capability. A session the host does not know is unreadable either way and is recreated on the next send in both cases, so the only difference is that "Couldn't open session" no longer appears. Cloud sandbox sessions are unaffected entirely, since Mission Control mirrors their history at `/events` and a dormant environment opens read-only from that rather than reaching this path.

The remaining case — a persisted local/SSH/tunnel session the host has lost — is also short-lived, because `_refreshSessions` evicts any cached session the host does not list. Narrowing the suppression would need a positive provider-level signal that the client minted the id; not worth the API surface for a missing notice in that window.

title: Wait for complete sandbox credentials before connecting
body:
Connecting to a freshly provisioned sandbox could leave the session unable to make authenticated requests. Nothing about it looked like a failure — the relay opened, the handshake completed, the connection registered — but every session request against it then failed.

The credentials a new environment returns can be incomplete for a short window after it comes up.

## What this does

Re-mints credentials until they are complete.

**The bound is derived, not guessed.** It is sized to cover the backend's own registration retry cycle, so a warm environment succeeds on the first mint and never enters the loop.

**It degrades rather than failing.** An environment may legitimately never return the missing piece, and a session with reduced capability beats refusing to connect at all. The last credentials are used either way, and the degraded case is logged so the cause is visible rather than leaving only downstream symptoms to puzzle over.

If the environment drops back to "waking" mid-wait, the loop stops rather than re-entering the wake path; the handshake watchdog already covers a host that has gone away. A transient failure while re-minting is also non-fatal — the credentials already in hand are used instead of discarding them.

## Risk

Only reachable when the initial credentials are incomplete, which is the broken case today. A warm environment takes the same path it always did.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`, `eslint` on both changed files
- `./scripts/test.sh --glob "**/cloudSandboxAgentHostService.test.js"` — 7 passing, covering: re-mint until complete, give up and connect anyway, no re-mint when the first mint is already complete, a value that is present but unusable, a failed re-mint, and the environment returning to waking mid-wait.

Each behavioural change was checked against the case it is meant to handle by reverting it and confirming the matching test fails.
author: osortega

title: Give sandbox task creation a realistic timeout and diagnosable failures
body:
Creating a cloud sandbox task ran on the generic 10s request budget, but the call waits on a sandbox environment being provisioned rather than on a record being written. Successful creates routinely take considerably longer than that, so **every** create was aborted client-side before any response arrived. It surfaced as a network failure, when really we were hanging up while the request was still in flight.

## What this does

**Task creation gets its own 60s budget.** Other calls keep the 10s one.

**Failures are now diagnosable.** A failed create can come back with a generic message that does not identify the underlying cause, so nothing client-side can explain it on its own. Failed creates now log the response verbatim — status, body, and `x-github-request-id`, which is what a support escalation is keyed on. A small set of retry-related response headers is captured for the same reason.

**Orphaned tasks are cleaned up.** A task record can already exist by the time a create fails, so a failure can leave one behind — not just the authorization rejection that was previously handled. When the response names the task, it is deleted; when it does not, the log says so explicitly rather than staying silent about something that can then only be removed server-side.

**A rejected cleanup is no longer reported as a successful one.** `_request` resolves non-2xx responses rather than throwing, so a failed DELETE was logged as "Cleaned up" while the orphan was still there. The status now decides, and a rejected delete takes the same warning path as a thrown one.

## Two subtleties worth a reviewer's eye

- `asText(context)` consumes the stream. Reading it twice silently yields an empty string, which was dropping the message explaining the failure — so the body is read once and threaded through to `_throwForStatus`.
- **No blind retry on 5xx.** It is tempting, but a generic 500 here does not by itself indicate a retryable condition, and the backend signals genuinely retryable failures explicitly — ours carried no such signal. Retrying blind would also multiply the orphaned tasks.

Also fixes a hardcoded `GET` in the request failure log, and sends `Content-Type: application/json` for bodied requests, which `fetch` would otherwise label `text/plain`.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`, `eslint` on both changed files
- `./scripts/test.sh --glob "**/cloudSandboxApiService.test.js"` — 17 passing

Each new assertion was checked against the bug it is meant to catch, by reverting the production change and confirming the test fails:

| Reverted | Test that fails |
| --- | --- |
| 60s create budget | `posts the on-demand sentinel and returns the bound environment` |
| `Content-Type: application/json` | same |
| `isSuccess` check on cleanup | `reports a rejected cleanup rather than claiming the orphan was removed` |

The request stub previously discarded `timeout` and `headers`, so an earlier revision of this PR would have stayed green with the budget and content type reverted. It no longer does.
author: osortega

title: Log AHP frames for the Web PubSub relay transport
body:
The Web PubSub relay was the only agent host transport with no AHP JSONL logging. Cloud sandbox hosts also do not implement `vscode/collectAgentHostDebugLogs`, so the debug-log export cannot gather frames for them either. Between the two, a sandbox session had no way to show what it actually put on the wire.

## What this does

Records every AHP frame to a JSONL transcript, gated on `chat.agentHost.ahpJsonlLoggingEnabled`, which defaults to `product.quality !== 'stable'` — on in Insiders and dev builds, off in stable. `AhpJsonlLogger` truncates oversized values rather than retaining everything.

Outbound frames are logged **before** chunking, so the transcript holds whole AHP messages rather than the relay frames they were split into. Inbound frames are logged after reassembly, for the same reason.

The logger is optional and owned by the transport, so it is disposed with it. Each soft-reconnect builds a fresh transport and gets its own logger keyed on the connection id.

## Risk

No behaviour change when the setting is off, which is the default. The only non-logging change is that the transport registers the logger for disposal.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- Verified against a live session: the transcript captured the full handshake and per-request frames.

title: [cherry-pick] github-authentication: prevent session hydration write loop
body:
Cherry-pick of #332447 from `main`.

## Summary

Accountless GitHub authentication sessions are hydrated through the `/user` endpoint when they are read. The hydrated account and avatar were then written to secret storage. Browser secret storage emits a change event for every write, while a web embedder can continue exposing the original accountless session. This re-enters session loading and repeats the `/user` request followed by the secret write.

Keep account and avatar hydration on the in-memory authentication session, but do not make hydration alone trigger persistence. Existing persistence for numeric account-ID migration and invalid-session removal remains unchanged.

Adds regression coverage that models browser secret storage firing a change after a write while the embedder continues returning accountless session data.

## Validation

### Automated

- `npm run gulp compile-extension:github-authentication`
- `npm run eslint -- extensions/github-authentication/src/github.ts extensions/github-authentication/src/test/github.test.ts`
- `.\scripts\test-integration.bat --suite github-authentication` — 27 passing
- Red/green check for the new test:
  - Without the fix: 0 passing, 1 failing; 2 `/user` requests and 2 secret writes.
  - With the fix: 1 passing; 1 `/user` request and 0 secret writes.

### vscode.dev with a Codespace and browser debugger

1. Sign in to GitHub, open a Codespace through `vscode.dev`, and open browser Developer Tools.
2. In **Network**, enable **Preserve log** and filter for `api.github.com/user` or `/user`.
3. In **Sources**, select the extension-host worker/frame that contains `github-authentication`. Open the source-mapped `extensions/github-authentication/src/github.ts`; if source maps are unavailable, search the browser extension bundle for `Reading sessions from keychain`.
4. Set breakpoints on the `getUserInfo(session.accessToken)` call in `readSessions` and on the `storeSessions(verifiedSessions)` call below it.
5. Reload the Codespace window and let the seeded accountless GitHub session load.
6. Without this change, the debugger repeatedly reaches `getUserInfo`, then `storeSessions`, then re-enters `readSessions`; the filtered `/user` request count continues increasing.
7. With this change, `getUserInfo` is reached once for the accountless session, `storeSessions` is not reached solely because account data was hydrated, and the `/user` request count stops increasing.
8. At the end of `readSessions`, inspect `verifiedSessions[0].account.icon`, then open the Accounts menu. The URI is populated and the avatar remains visible for the active session.

### VS Code Insiders avatar smoke test

1. Compile the extension with `npm run gulp compile-extension:github-authentication`.
2. Launch Insiders with the checkout's extension, for example: `code-insiders --user-data-dir <temporary-profile> --extensionDevelopmentPath=<checkout>\extensions\github-authentication --enable-proposed-api vscode.github-authentication`.
3. Sign in to GitHub from the Accounts menu.
4. Verify the GitHub avatar appears in the Accounts menu.
5. Run **Developer: Reload Window** and verify the avatar still appears. Newly created sessions continue to persist their account icon; this change only prevents read-time hydration of an accountless session from causing a write.

title: github-authentication: prevent session hydration write loop
body:
## Summary

Accountless GitHub authentication sessions are hydrated through the `/user` endpoint when they are read. The hydrated account and avatar were then written to secret storage. Browser secret storage emits a change event for every write, while a web embedder can continue exposing the original accountless session. This re-enters session loading and repeats the `/user` request followed by the secret write.

Keep account and avatar hydration on the in-memory authentication session, but do not make hydration alone trigger persistence. Existing persistence for numeric account-ID migration and invalid-session removal remains unchanged.

Adds regression coverage that models browser secret storage firing a change after a write while the embedder continues returning accountless session data.

## Validation

### Automated

- `npm run gulp compile-extension:github-authentication`
- `npm run eslint -- extensions/github-authentication/src/github.ts extensions/github-authentication/src/test/github.test.ts`
- `.\scripts\test-integration.bat --suite github-authentication` — 27 passing
- Red/green check for the new test:
  - Without the fix: 0 passing, 1 failing; 2 `/user` requests and 2 secret writes.
  - With the fix: 1 passing; 1 `/user` request and 0 secret writes.

### vscode.dev with a Codespace and browser debugger

1. Sign in to GitHub, open a Codespace through `vscode.dev`, and open browser Developer Tools.
2. In **Network**, enable **Preserve log** and filter for `api.github.com/user` or `/user`.
3. In **Sources**, select the extension-host worker/frame that contains `github-authentication`. Open the source-mapped `extensions/github-authentication/src/github.ts`; if source maps are unavailable, search the browser extension bundle for `Reading sessions from keychain`.
4. Set breakpoints on the `getUserInfo(session.accessToken)` call in `readSessions` and on the `storeSessions(verifiedSessions)` call below it.
5. Reload the Codespace window and let the seeded accountless GitHub session load.
6. Without this change, the debugger repeatedly reaches `getUserInfo`, then `storeSessions`, then re-enters `readSessions`; the filtered `/user` request count continues increasing.
7. With this change, `getUserInfo` is reached once for the accountless session, `storeSessions` is not reached solely because account data was hydrated, and the `/user` request count stops increasing.
8. At the end of `readSessions`, inspect `verifiedSessions[0].account.icon`, then open the Accounts menu. The URI is populated and the avatar remains visible for the active session.

### VS Code Insiders avatar smoke test

1. Compile the extension with `npm run gulp compile-extension:github-authentication`.
2. Launch Insiders with the checkout's extension, for example: `code-insiders --user-data-dir <temporary-profile> --extensionDevelopmentPath=<checkout>\extensions\github-authentication --enable-proposed-api vscode.github-authentication`.
3. Sign in to GitHub from the Accounts menu.
4. Verify the GitHub avatar appears in the Accounts menu.
5. Run **Developer: Reload Window** and verify the avatar still appears. Newly created sessions continue to persist their account icon; this change only prevents read-time hydration of an accountless session from causing a write.

title: inline chat: scope Agent Host permissions and fix its file context
body:
inline chat: scope Agent Host permissions and fix its file context

Four fixes for editor inline chat backed by the Agent Host, found while testing the feature end to
end. Each is a separate commit.

**Scope write approvals to the target file.** Inline chat auto-approved every tool confirmation on
the client, so an Agent Host session could edit any file without asking. The decision now happens in
the agent host, where it applies to all providers that use the shared permission layer.

- Adds a surface edit scope to `SessionPermissionManager`. It reads the target file from the chat
  surface metadata, so no launch-plan plumbing is necessary and other file-bound surfaces can use
  the same mechanism later.
- Auto-approves a write to the target file, also when that file is outside the working directory.
  All other writes and all shell commands require confirmation.
- Fails closed when the surface records no usable target. No write auto-approves in that case.
- Stops the Copilot sandboxed-shell shortcut for a file-scoped surface. The sandbox contains a
  command to the workspace, not to the one target file.
- Limits the client-side blanket auto-approval to the legacy extension-host path.

Codex does not use the shared permission layer and its approval requests carry no file path, so it
keeps the prompt instruction and the read-only document as its defenses.

**Send the cursor line.** A request attached the target file as a whole document when the user had
no text selected, so the model could not tell which line a request such as "comment this line out"
referred to. The full range of the cursor line is now attached instead. A non-empty selection is
still sent unchanged, and no range is attached when the editor reports no selection.

**Save an untitled document before a request.** An Agent Host request needs a file on disk, because
the agent writes files directly and the review session compares snapshots of that file, so an
untitled document could not be edited at all. Submitting now prompts to save and replays the request
against the saved file. Cancelling the save sends no request and keeps the prompt in the input. The
save goes through the editor service so the saved file replaces the untitled editor and keeps its
view state; the text file service writes the file but leaves no editor behind. The legacy path is
unchanged when Agent Host inline chat is disabled.

**Do not prompt to read the target file.** The agent must read the target file before it can edit
it. A target outside the working directory failed the normal read rules, so the user got a
confirmation prompt for the very file they opened inline chat on. Reads of every other file stay on
the normal rules.

title: Fix terminal sticky scroll showing output instead of the executed command
body:
## Description

Sticky scroll could pin rows of unrelated output (e.g. the tail of a previous `npm install`) instead of the command line that produced the output currently in view.

The overlay built its render window starting at the prompt start and capped it at `maxLineCount` rows **from the top**:

```ts
const stickyScrollLineStart = startMarker.line - (promptRowCount - 1);
const stickyScrollLineCount = Math.min(promptRowCount + commandRowCount - 1, maxLineCount) - rowOffset;
```

When `promptRowCount > maxLineCount`, that window ends *above* the command line, so only rows preceding the command are rendered. `promptRowCount` inflates easily: `handlePromptStart` clones the previous command's end marker as the prompt start, so anything printed between a command finishing and the next prompt being drawn (background/late process output, job control notices, shell chatter) counts as prompt rows. `maxLineCount` is `min(terminal.integrated.stickyScroll.maxLineCount, floor(rows * 0.4))`, so a short panel (≈11 rows → 4) makes this easy to hit.

### Changes

- **`terminalStickyScrollOverlay.ts`** — row math extracted into an exported pure `getStickyScrollLayout()` that prioritizes the command line: prompt rows are included only when prompt + command fit within `maxLineCount`, otherwise the window starts at the command start row (which still carries the prompt terminator, e.g. `$ `). Unchanged in the common case where the prompt fits.
- **`isTruncated`** — the trailing ` …` is now appended only when content is genuinely cut off at the bottom, rather than whenever the prompt didn't fit.
- **Empty overlay** — hide when `rowOffset` clips every row, instead of resizing to a zero/negative row count and serializing a stray output row.
- **Tests** — new `stickyScroll/test/browser/terminalStickyScrollOverlay.test.ts` covering the layout function, plus a case driven by the real `CommandDetectionCapability` that reproduces the reported scenario (output printed after the previous command finished ⇒ `promptRowCount: 6` vs `maxLineCount: 5`).

```ts
const { lineStart: stickyScrollLineStart, lineCount: stickyScrollLineCount, isTruncated } =
    getStickyScrollLayout(startMarker.line, promptRowCount, commandRowCount, maxLineCount, rowOffset);
```

Note the hide check `buffer.viewportY <= stickyScrollLineStart` now compares against the command start row when the prompt is dropped, so the overlay disappears exactly when the command line itself scrolls into view.

An alternative to dropping the prompt entirely would be trimming prompt rows from the top to fill the available space — that keeps the overlay full height but still shows the unrelated output the issue complains about, so this takes the simpler route. Happy to switch if preferred.

title: agentHost: move side chat behavior into a contribution
body:
Moves the side chat ("btw") feature out of the individual agent harnesses and into one chat contribution, using the contribution model added in #332150.

The agents no longer know what a side chat is. Each one now receives a plain fork, and the host owns the context injection and the history filtering.

## Codex is not enabled yet

The original intent was that Codex would gain side chat support for free, because a side chat now reaches an agent as an ordinary fork and Codex already handled forks. Review showed that is not sufficient. A side chat usually branches from a turn that is still running, and Codex maps a host turn id to its own turn id only when that turn completes (`codexAgent.ts:2485`), so it cannot resolve an active turn fork. Codex therefore continues to advertise `multipleChats: { fork: true }` only, which is what the shared end to end suite already expects.

The structural work still holds: the agents no longer contain side chat logic, and enabling Codex later is a matter of resolving an active turn fork rather than reimplementing context injection and history filtering.

## What the contribution owns

`SideChatContribution` reads the chat origin and the source chat state through `IAgentHostStateManager`, so it needs no protocol change and no provider private data.

- `onOutgoingTurn` prepends the source context to the first message of a side chat.
- `onHydrateTurns` removes the inherited turns and the injected context from the restored history.

The context stays in the **user message** rather than moving to host instructions, because a change to instructions invalidates the provider prompt cache and increases cost for the user.

## Supporting changes

- `ISendContribution` gains an optional `message`. The dispatcher threads it through the contributions in order, in the same way it threads restored turns. This extends an existing payload rather than adding a fifth hook.
- The side chat creation option collapses into the fork option. The host resolves the anchor turn.
- The inherited turn id returns from the create result instead of living in each agent's private data. The host persists it and the contribution uses it to find the boundary. A chat persisted before this change still uses the seed marker scan, and an unlocatable boundary returns the turns unchanged rather than removing them.
- An independent queue flag on the fork options keeps the Copilot behavior where a side chat does not block the queue of its source chat.
- The side chat helpers move next to the contribution. `agentPeerChats.ts` now holds only provider data concerns.

## Validation

The full agent host suite passes: 6114 passing, 0 failing.

A driven window confirms the behavior end to end on all three agents. A side chat answers a question that can only be answered from the source conversation, and its transcript shows neither the inherited turns nor the raw injected context. A normal fork still inherits its history, a queued message still drains after a turn completes, and a cancelled turn still does not send the message queued behind it.

## Follow-up

`IAgentCreateChatSideChatSource` and `IAgentCreateChatSideChatSelection` still sit in the provider model even though no agent reads them now. Whether they belong in the provider seam, and whether part of `_resolveSideChatOrigin` is contribution shaped, is left for a separate change.

title: Perf: Implement LRU node eviction in AsyncDataTree to prevent OOM
body:
## Fixes

Fixes #332420 

## Description

**What this PR does:**
This PR addresses OOM (Out Of Memory) crashes in the Renderer when dealing with massive workspaces by capping the memory footprint of the `AsyncDataTree`.

When opening massive workspaces (e.g., mono-repos with 500k+ files) or returning massive search results, expanding the Explorer tree causes the `AsyncDataTree` to materialize hundreds of thousands of nodes in memory. Even though the DOM is virtualized via `listWidget.ts`, the in-memory metadata for these nodes scales linearly until the browser engine exhausts its memory limit.

**Architectural Changes:**
- Introduces a strict LRU (Least Recently Used) cache mechanism directly into `src/vs/base/browser/ui/tree/asyncDataTree.ts`.
- Hooks into `_onDidChangeCollapseState` to track node access history.
- Runs an asynchronous background Garbage Collector interval (`performGarbageCollection`).
- When the internal node count exceeds `MAX_RETAINED_NODES` (default 50k), the tree automatically collapses and evicts the least recently rendered nodes outside of the current viewport.

## Verification Steps
1. Open a workspace with >500,000 files.
2. Recursively expand the root node in the Explorer to aggressively materialize tree nodes.
3. Monitor the Renderer memory footprint in the Task Manager or Activity Monitor. 
4. Verify that the memory footprint plateaus instead of growing unboundedly until an OOM crash.

title: Perf: Implement chunked streaming for oversized IPC payloads
body:
## Fixes
Fixes #332418
## Description
**What this PR does:**
This PR introduces automatic payload chunking at the core IPC layer to prevent Extension Host messages from freezing the Renderer UI thread. 
Currently, when the Extension Host sends massive payloads to the Renderer (e.g., thousands of diagnostic markers, massive search results, or huge string buffers), it serializes and transmits the entire object synchronously over the RPC protocol bridge. If this payload exceeds a few megabytes, the deserialization and processing block the UI event loop, causing the renderer to freeze, drop frames, or display the "Window is not responding" dialog.
**Architectural Changes:**
- Modifies `src/vs/base/parts/ipc/common/ipc.ts` to detect oversized `VSBuffer` packets during serialization.
- Introduces a `ChunkingProtocolAdapter` wrapper around `IMessagePassingProtocol`.
- Messages exceeding `1MB` are automatically split into chunked packets.
- `ChannelServer` and `ChannelClient` automatically buffer and reassemble incoming chunks asynchronously without blocking the main event loop, yielding via `setTimeout(..., 0)`.
## Verification Steps
1. Run `npm run test -- ipc` to verify unit tests pass.
2. Launch the Extension Host and trigger an extension that sends >10MB of diagnostics or search results.
3. Observe via the Developer Tools Performance profiler that the UI remains responsive (60fps) during transmission, as the massive payload is chunked and streamed.

title: [cherry-pick] Agent Host: apply multi-root capability change to open drafts without a reload
body:
Cherry-pick of #332403 from `release/1.135`.

Fixes #332335

## Problem

The hidden setting `chat.agentHost.copilotAgent.multiRootEnabled` (and the `claudeAgent` / `codexAgent` variants) only took effect after running **Developer: Reload Window**. In a multi-root workspace, an already-open chat kept its single-root scope — e.g. the **Agent** dropdown listed only the primary folder's custom agents — until the window was reloaded.

## Root cause

The live path up to the point of consumption already works:

1. The renderer mirrors the setting to the agent host: the `onDidChangeConfiguration` listener in `agentHostProtocolClient.ts` forwards `agentHost`-schema settings as a `RootConfigChanged` action.
2. The host re-advertises the capability: on `RootConfigChanged`, `agentSideEffects.ts` re-reads `getDescriptor()` and republishes agent infos, so `rootState.agents[].capabilities.multipleWorkingDirectories` updates in the renderer.

The gap is on the **consumption** side: a session's working-directory set is derived from that capability via `computeWorkingDirectories()` **only at session creation**. Nothing recomputed the set for an already-open, not-yet-started (untitled) provisional session when the capability flipped, so it stayed single-root until a reload rebuilt every session.

## Fix

In `AgentHostUntitledProvisionalSessionService`, re-run the existing working-directory reconciliation for each open **untitled** draft whenever the advertised capability can change, so a runtime toggle re-scopes the draft (and its active-client customization scope, which drives the Agent dropdown) immediately — no reload.

- **Gated to untitled drafts** via `isUntitledChatSession`, because a started (rebound) session's working directories are the agent's fixed process root once the session has started; recreating its backend would tear down the live conversation.
- The reconcile body previously inlined in the `onDidChangeWorkspaceFolders` handler is extracted into a shared `_reconcileWorkspaceRootSet(...)` helper (behavior-preserving) and reused by both reactions.
- **Robust to lazy host start / restart.** The desktop `rootState` is a noop whose event never fires until `startAgentHost()` creates the protocol client, and the host can restart behind a fresh root state. The listener therefore re-binds on every `onAgentHostStart` and reconciles once per (re)bind, mirroring the existing pattern in `agentHostSdkSetupNotification` — so a service constructed before the host starts (e.g. AI enabled mid-session) still picks up the change.
- `OFF → ON` and `ON → OFF` transitions both behave: `usesWorkspaceRootSet` only escalates one-way, but `_computeEntryWorkingDirectories` re-gates on the live capability, so disabling the setting collapses the draft back to `[primary]`.

## Testing

- `npm run compile-client` — 0 errors.
- Full unit-test file run headless (Chromium) — **50 passing, 0 failing**, including four runtime tests:
  - *recreates an untitled draft with the workspace root set when multi-root is enabled at runtime*
  - *does not recreate a started session when multi-root is enabled at runtime*
  - *recreates an untitled draft with the workspace root set when the agent host starts after the draft*
  - *recreates an untitled draft with a single root when multi-root is disabled at runtime*

## Note for reviewers (pre-existing, out of scope)

The sibling `onDidChangeWorkspaceFolders` handler is not gated to untitled drafts, so **adding** a workspace folder to a *started* multi-root session can recreate its backend via the same shared helper. This predates and is unrelated to this change (the body was extracted verbatim), so it is intentionally left as-is here; happy to file a follow-up if desired.

title: agentHost: centralize session and chat catalog metadata
body:
## 1. What this PR changes

Today, `listSessions` often enumerates providers and opens many individual `session.db` files to obtain titles, workspace information, read state, changes, and chats.

This PR makes `agent-host.db` the central index for session-list data:

- **`sessions_v2`:** authoritative session identity, provider, timestamps, registration source, external state, and chat-backing identity.
- **Central chat membership:** authoritative chat list, ordering, routing, and origin information.
- **Rebuildable list payload:** title, read/archive state, project presentation, Git/GitHub summaries, aggregate changes, artifacts, and lightweight chat summaries.

Full conversation data—including turns, drafts, attachments, annotations, and detailed edits—remains isolated in individual session and chat databases.

## 2. Listing and synchronization

Normal `listSessions` calls now read verified payloads directly from `agent-host.db` instead of opening every conversation database.

If one payload is missing, stale, or invalid:

- Only that session uses the fallback path.
- Other valid central rows remain fast.
- The invalid row is scheduled for background repair.
- Provider unavailability does not discard the last valid cached representation.

Changes to titles, read state, workspace information, changes, or chats mark the payload dirty. Background reconciliation uses revisions and compare-and-set operations so delayed work cannot overwrite newer state.

## 3. Migration and compatibility

Existing sessions are imported from the legacy registry and provider discovery. Migration is resumable, tracked per provider, and normally runs in the background so the first list does not wait for the full migration.

The PR also protects upgrade and downgrade scenarios:

- Central chat membership is temporarily mirrored into legacy `peerChats`.
- Changes made by an older build are imported when a newer build starts again.
- Tombstones prevent deleted sessions from being rediscovered.
- Invalid provider entries are isolated and retried.
- Title precedence remains consistent before and after opening a session.
- Oversized summaries are bounded without changing provider-native data.

All product schema changes are introduced in one new **v5 migration**, after upstream’s existing v4 migration. A separate normalizer handles databases produced by earlier versions of this draft PR.

## 4. Rollback setting

`chat.agentHost.sessionCatalog.enabled` (default `true`, tagged advanced) is the rollback lever for the catalog read path. When disabled, the host performs no catalog import and no background repair, and `listSessions` uses provider metadata and the per-session fallback instead of the cached payload.

The value is frozen at its first read, so the store backing the list cannot change while the host runs and a change requires a full restart. Registry identity and every compatibility write run in both modes, so the two stores stay current and interchangeable and switching either way is safe and reversible. The verification marker is cleared while disabled, so the next enabled start re-verifies every row.

It is a safety switch rather than a tuning option: section 6 measures what it costs.

## 5. Testing

Coverage includes:

- Fresh databases and existing profiles
- Partial and interrupted migration
- Restarts and crash recovery
- Concurrent Agent Host processes
- Session and chat deletion
- Provider failures and retries
- Corrupt or stale payload fallback
- Title and background-update races
- Old → new → old → new build cycles
- Oversized metadata and Unicode truncation
- Pre-release schema normalization

The affected unit suites pass, and the real-process compatibility matrix passed **20/20 scenarios**.

## 6. Performance

Measured on one build (`0a96803ad20`, content-identical to current `08aae258ce2`) with the catalog enabled versus disabled, so both arms share the same code, profile, and session set: ~645 registered sessions, `mode='recent'`. Every sample self-identifies its mode in the `listSessions computed` log line, so no arm is inferred from settings.

| Metric | Enabled | Disabled | Ratio |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Cold start (first listing after launch) | 108 ms | 1,329 ms | **12.3x** |
| Steady state (median listing) | 146 ms | 610 ms | **3.8-4.2x** |
| Database opens per listing (steady) | 17.1 | 1,837 | 107x |
| Database opens per minute (steady) | 104 | 17,855 | 172x |
| Resolve phase | 0 ms | 475-665 ms | |

Steady state n=34 enabled / n=22 disabled; cold start three matched quit-and-relaunch cycles per arm.

Every disabled listing performs 645 provider fallbacks and zero catalog reads; every enabled listing is the exact inverse, at roughly 2.85 database opens per session per listing. The win is replacing 645 per-session provider round-trips with a single batch read. It does not make reads free and it does not eliminate startup database I/O -- enabled mode still performs about 1,180 opens cold, which is why cold start is only 2.5x on database opens while steady state is 172x. The `resolve 0 ms` figure means the resolve loop had nothing left to do, not that the catalog read is free: that read happens in an earlier batch phase, outside the measured window.

Caveats: single profile and machine, so this is directional evidence rather than a benchmark. The cost is per-session and will not generalize to a much smaller session count, and only `mode='recent'` was measured. The enabled steady-state window contained more chat-turn activity than the disabled one, and turn-triggered listings are faster (95 ms versus 161 ms median), so excluding them gives 3.8x rather than 4.2x. Cold start rests on three runs per arm: enough for a ratio, not a tight interval.

These steady-state numbers were not collectable before the listing-cache fix below.

### Listing-cache fix

A settled listing computation could be pinned in `_inFlightListSessions`, after which every later listing was served from that stale entry and the host never recomputed until restart, so the session list silently stopped updating.

This was a regression introduced by this PR in e1bc2e30576 ("agentHost: harden catalog reconciliation"), not a pre-existing `main` issue. `main` attaches its trailing refresh as `inFlight.promise.then(startTrailing, startTrailing)`, where both handlers start a fresh computation that replaces the map entry, so the map self-heals. e1bc2e30576 made the success handler conditional (`result => inFlight.epoch === epoch ? result : startTrailing()`), so on the matching-epoch path it returns the settled result without starting a replacement, and the stale entry is never evicted.

Fixed in b7bc7972446 by releasing the entry once the trailing hand-off settles, with a regression test that fails before the fix and passes after.

## 7. PR size

The PR adds **18,315 lines**, but approximately **11,547 lines—63%—are tests**.

The remaining approximately 6.8K lines implement the database schema, catalog projection, migration, synchronization, reconciliation, chat membership, compatibility handling, and Agent Service integration. The size reflects the reliability work required for a persistence migration rather than the amount of data being moved.

title: Fix extension host OOM when listing Copilot CLI sessions
body:
## Summary

Listing Copilot CLI sessions could exhaust the extension host's memory and abort the process with a V8 OOM. `_getAllSessions()` fanned out over **every** persisted session with an unbounded `Promise.all`, and each session without a cached title fell through to a path that opened a real SDK session and deserialized its entire event log.

This is not a leak — `closeSession` is correctly balanced, and the thread count does recover. The problem is that all of the work happens *at once*.

## Evidence

Captured from three extension host crashes on a machine with 328 persisted sessions:

| Measurement | Value |
|---|---|
| Session event logs on disk | 328 files |
| `tokio-rt-worker` threads at crash | 327 / 329 / 329 |
| Raw JSONL parsed concurrently | 0.74 GB |
| `VM_ALLOCATE` at OOM | 8.0 GB (~10× JSON→V8 expansion) |
| Thread stacks | 833.9 MB across 356 threads |

The crash backtrace terminates in `node::OOMErrorHandler(...)` → `abort()`, and the main process log records `exited with code: 6 ... crashed`.

The number of concurrently-open SDK sessions tracks the number of session logs almost exactly, which is what identifies the fan-out as the source.

## Changes

All in `copilotcliSessionService.ts`:

- **Bound the fan-out.** `_getAllSessions()` now queues item construction through a `Limiter` with a max parallelism of 10. `Limiter` is already exported from the `async` module this file imports, and matches existing usage elsewhere in the repo.

- **Stop opening a full SDK session just to derive a title.** `readSessionEventsFile(sessionId, 'user.message')` only breaks early when it *finds* a user message, so when it finds none it has already scanned the whole file. Retrying through `getChatHistoryImpl` re-read that same log the expensive way. The SDK fallback now runs only when the event log was genuinely unreadable.

- **Don't cache a title derived from a cancelled read.** Previously a cancellation stored an empty first-user-message, which permanently poisoned the lookup for that session.

## Validation

- `tsc --noEmit` clean
- 47/47 in `copilotCliSessionService.spec.ts`
- 804 passing across `src/extension/chatSessions/copilotcli/`

One pre-existing, unrelated failure in `copilotCLISDKUpgrade.spec.ts` (unexpected `pty.node` / `spawn-helper` in SDK prebuilds) — confirmed to fail identically with this change stashed. It's fallout from `ensureShims()` copying native binaries in during local runs.

## Notes for reviewers

The parallelism value of 10 is a conservative starting point rather than a tuned number; happy to adjust.

Two related issues found while investigating, deliberately **not** addressed here to keep this change contained:

1. `createSession` / `getSession` both have a window between acquiring an SDK session and wiring up its disposal where a rejection would orphan the session. That's a genuine leak, but a separate one.
2. When the extension host OOMs, js-debug dies with it and severs the inspector connection mid-write, which trips a null-`this` use-after-free in Node's `inspector::TcpHolder::WriteRaw` and takes down the process being debugged. That's an upstream Electron/Node bug worth reporting separately.
