title: Agent Host: apply multi-root capability change to open drafts without a reload
body:
Fixes #332335

## Problem

The hidden setting `chat.agentHost.copilotAgent.multiRootEnabled` (and the `claudeAgent` / `codexAgent` variants) only took effect after running **Developer: Reload Window**. In a multi-root workspace, an already-open chat kept its single-root scope — e.g. the **Agent** dropdown listed only the primary folder's custom agents — until the window was reloaded.

## Root cause

The live path up to the point of consumption already works:

1. The renderer mirrors the setting to the agent host: the `onDidChangeConfiguration` listener in `agentHostProtocolClient.ts` forwards `agentHost`-schema settings as a `RootConfigChanged` action.
2. The host re-advertises the capability: on `RootConfigChanged`, `agentSideEffects.ts` re-reads `getDescriptor()` and republishes agent infos, so `rootState.agents[].capabilities.multipleWorkingDirectories` updates in the renderer.

The gap is on the **consumption** side: a session's working-directory set is derived from that capability via `computeWorkingDirectories()` **only at session creation**. Nothing recomputed the set for an already-open, not-yet-started (untitled) provisional session when the capability flipped, so it stayed single-root until a reload rebuilt every session.

## Fix

In `AgentHostUntitledProvisionalSessionService`, re-run the existing working-directory reconciliation for each open **untitled** draft whenever the advertised capability can change, so a runtime toggle re-scopes the draft (and its active-client customization scope, which drives the Agent dropdown) immediately — no reload.

- **Gated to untitled drafts** via `isUntitledChatSession`, because a started (rebound) session's working directories are the agent's fixed process root once the session has started; recreating its backend would tear down the live conversation.
- The reconcile body previously inlined in the `onDidChangeWorkspaceFolders` handler is extracted into a shared `_reconcileWorkspaceRootSet(...)` helper (behavior-preserving) and reused by both reactions.
- **Robust to lazy host start / restart.** The desktop `rootState` is a noop whose event never fires until `startAgentHost()` creates the protocol client, and the host can restart behind a fresh root state. The listener therefore re-binds on every `onAgentHostStart` and reconciles once per (re)bind, mirroring the existing pattern in `agentHostSdkSetupNotification` — so a service constructed before the host starts (e.g. AI enabled mid-session) still picks up the change.
- `OFF → ON` and `ON → OFF` transitions both behave: `usesWorkspaceRootSet` only escalates one-way, but `_computeEntryWorkingDirectories` re-gates on the live capability, so disabling the setting collapses the draft back to `[primary]`.

## Testing

- `npm run compile-client` — 0 errors.
- Full unit-test file run headless (Chromium) — **50 passing, 0 failing**, including four runtime tests:
  - *recreates an untitled draft with the workspace root set when multi-root is enabled at runtime*
  - *does not recreate a started session when multi-root is enabled at runtime*
  - *recreates an untitled draft with the workspace root set when the agent host starts after the draft*
  - *recreates an untitled draft with a single root when multi-root is disabled at runtime*

## Note for reviewers (pre-existing, out of scope)

The sibling `onDidChangeWorkspaceFolders` handler is not gated to untitled drafts, so **adding** a workspace folder to a *started* multi-root session can recreate its backend via the same shared helper. This predates and is unrelated to this change (the body was extracted verbatim), so it is intentionally left as-is here; happy to file a follow-up if desired.

title: fix: guard against null diagnostic code in Copilot CLI diagnosticsChanged (fixes #332348)
body:
### Summary The Copilot CLI diagnostics-changed notification crashes with `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'value')` when serializing a diagnostic whose `code` is `null`. `getDiagnosticsForUri` uses `typeof d.code === 'object' ? d.code.value : d.code`, but `typeof null === 'object'` is `true`, so a `null` code falls into the object branch and dereferences `null.value`. Language servers and extensions are free to set `Diagnostic.code` to `null`, so this fires whenever such a diagnostic changes while a Copilot CLI session is active (50 users / 251 hits, new in extension 0.62.0). Fixes microsoft/vscode#332348 Recommended reviewer: `@alexweininger` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | [`ab48d553b302`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/ab48d553b302777d41cb06fa304e6673730db5f2) | | Author | `@alexweininger` | | PR | #3529 | | Message | Migrate Copilot CLI integration (#3529) | | Why | This commit introduced `getDiagnosticsForUri` with the `typeof d.code === 'object' ? d.code.value : d.code` mapping at line 52. Because `typeof null === 'object'`, a `null` code is routed into the object branch and `.value` is read off `null`. The code shipped in extension 0.62.0, which is when the bucket first appeared. | ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant LS as Language Server / Extension participant API as vscode.languages.getDiagnostics participant Producer as getDiagnosticsForUri (map) participant CrashSite as d.code.value LS->>API: publishes Diagnostic with code = null API->>Producer: returns Diagnostic[] (code: null) Note over Producer: ⚠️ Root cause:
typeof null === 'object' is true,
so null enters the object branch Producer->>CrashSite: read d.code.value on null Note over CrashSite: TypeError: Cannot read
properties of null (reading 'value') ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | |------|------| | `extensions/copilot/src/extension/chatSessions/copilotcli/vscode-node/tools/push/diagnosticsChanged.ts` | Crash site and root cause — the `code` mapping on line 52 | ### Repro Steps 1. Open a Copilot CLI chat session so the diagnostics-changed notification is registered. 2. Trigger a diagnostic from a language server/extension whose `Diagnostic.code` is `null` (rather than a string, number, or `{ value, target }` object). 3. When the diagnostics change fires, `getDiagnosticsForUri` maps the diagnostic and throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'value')`. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `extensions/copilot/src/extension/chatSessions/copilotcli/vscode-node/tools/push/diagnosticsChanged.ts:52`: tighten the type test to `typeof d.code === 'object' && d.code !== null` so that a `null` code falls through to the `: d.code` branch and is emitted as `null`, instead of being dereferenced. This is the correct location because the `code` value crosses an external/untrusted boundary — `vscode.languages.getDiagnostics` returns data authored by arbitrary language servers and extensions, which the consumer cannot constrain — so the guard belongs at the point where the value is first narrowed and consumed. The fix is the standard `typeof x === 'object' && x !== null` idiom, preserves the existing behavior for real `{ value, target }` code objects and for string/number codes, and does not swallow or hide any error. **Alternatives considered**: wrapping the `.map` body in try/catch was rejected because it would silence a legitimate serialization failure and hide it from telemetry rather than correctly serializing a valid (`null`) code. ### Recommended Owner `@alexweininger` — authored the migration commit that introduced `getDiagnosticsForUri`, is a VS Code team member with write access, and has landed commits to `microsoft/vscode` within the last 90 days. > Generated by [errors-fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/32745004652) · opus48 · 325.6 AIC · ⌖ 11.2 AIC · ⊞ 18.6K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-id%3A+errors-fix%22&type=pullrequests)

title: Adding widthInEm field to injected text options
body:
🤖 

## What this does

Adds an internal `widthInEm` field to `InjectedTextOptions`. Some injected text is not sized by its own characters — it is sized by CSS (colour decorators, inlay hint spacing, the inline progress spinner, the breakpoint placeholder). Until now the soft-wrap code had no way to know that, so it measured those decorations as if they were one ordinary character wide, and the line wrapped in the wrong place.

`widthInEm` tells the wrapping code the real width. It also makes it possible to reserve space with no character at all: `{ content: '', widthInEm: 1 }`.

## Design choices

### 1. The unit is `em`, the field is internal, and it is validated once

`em` is used rather than pixels because the CSS these features write is already in `em`, and an `em` value stays correct when the editor font size changes. A stored pixel value would go stale. The field is marked `@internal` — it is not part of the extension API, only built-in editor features use it.

### 2. Empty content is kept when `widthInEm` is set

`LineInjectedText.fromDecorations` used to throw away injected text with empty content. It now keeps it when `widthInEm` is present:

```ts
function occupiesHorizontalSpace(options: InjectedTextOptions): boolean {
	return options.content.length > 0 || (options.widthInEm !== undefined && options.widthInEm > 0);
}
```

This is what lets callers stop using a placeholder character. A placeholder was misleading: it took up a real column in the model, so it affected cursor movement and selection, and its own width had nothing to do with the width the CSS actually reserved.

### 3. Wrapping decides in pixels; tab stops stay in columns

This is the main change to `MonospaceLineBreaksComputer`. There are two variables doing two jobs:

- **`currentLinePixelWidth`** — decides *where the line wraps*. Only this is compared against the wrap width. A fixed-width injection contributes `widthInEm * fontInfo.fontSize`; its own characters contribute nothing.
- **`visibleColumn`** — decides *how wide the next tab is*. This is a character grid and never sees `widthInEm`.

They have to be separate. `breakOffsetsVisibleColumn` is handed to the renderer, which uses it as the starting column for tab expansion. The renderer has no idea `widthInEm` exists. If `widthInEm` moved tab stops, the wrapping code and the renderer would disagree about how wide a tab is, and lines would render differently from how they were measured.

### 4. Width-only injections get their own decoration type

`InlineDecorationType.WidthOnly = 4` is new. The existing code drops zero-length decorations (`start !== end`), so a spacer needed a type that is allowed to be empty and is rendered as an element of its own rather than as a pseudo element of a neighbour.

Two knock-on changes:

- `lineDecorations.ts` sorting: `ORDER = [3, 1, 2, 4, 0]`. `WidthOnly` sorts first, because injected text renders before any other decoration.
- `viewLineRenderer.ts` counts `WidthOnly` as a `Before` foreign element, so the empty-line path still emits its span.

### 5. The DOM computer gives each spacer its own empty span

A spacer cannot share a span with the character next to it. The span is `display:inline-block` with a fixed width, and everything inside such a span is laid out inside that box — the neighbouring character would become fixed-width too, and a spacer that covers zero characters would swallow the rest of the line.

So each spacer is emitted as a childless span, and the character after it opens a fresh span. `spanStartOffsets` keeps one entry per span, in document order. `findSpanIndex` returns the *last* span starting at a given offset, so the childless spacer span is always shadowed by the real span opened right after it — `readClientRect` (which does `.firstChild!`) never tries to measure it.

A spacer at the very end of a line is skipped by both computers on purpose: nothing follows it, so it cannot move a break point.

### 6. Ordering is guaranteed, not assumed

`getFixedWidthInjectedTextRanges` relies on the same sort by (line, column, order) that `applyInjectedText` already relies on to compute offsets at all. Given that order, the ranges come out sorted by start offset and never overlap: two injections at the same column produce *adjacent* ranges, so two ranges share a start offset only when the earlier one is empty. That is why the code needs one drain loop for empty ranges plus a single check for a range that covers characters, rather than general overlap handling.

title: [cherry-pick] nes: add optimized PatchBased02 prompt strategy
body:
Cherry-pick of #332018 from `release/1.135`.

## Summary

Adds `patchBased02Optimized`, an implementation-neutral prompting strategy for the optimized inline-suggestion treatment. It inherits everything from `patchBased02WithRecentLineNumbers` (current/recent-file line numbers, cross-file edits/imports, disabled next-cursor prediction) and additionally bakes in the client, latency, and completions-unification knobs this unified model was tuned for, so a single `promptingStrategy` value carries the whole treatment rather than relying on many separate client settings or experiment/deployment toggles.

This makes the treatment self-contained enough to ship purely as the prompt template of a `copilot-proxy` `/models` deployment: the proxy only specifies `promptStrategy: "patchBased02Optimized"` and the client derives everything else.

Analogous to the change for 2-in-1 models made in this PR: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/321755

### Baked-in configuration

`patchBased02Optimized` spreads the shared `patchBased02WithRecentLineNumbers` config and adds:

| Setting | Baked value |
| --- | --- |
| `patchModelPredictionKind` | `currentLineCompleted` |
| `splitPatchOnDiff` | `true` |
| `patchFastYieldLineWithCursor` | `true` |
| `extraDebounceEndOfLine` | `0` |
| `nesMimicGhostTextBehavior` | `true` |
| `cacheDelay` | `200` |
| `rebasedCacheDelay` | `0` |
| `debounce` | `0` |
| `supportsUnifiedCompletions` | `true` |

### How it works

- These are exposed as optional `ModelConfiguration` fields (each with a `MODEL_CONFIGURATION_VALIDATOR` entry), following the same pattern used to bake in `allowImportChanges` and `supportsNextCursorLinePrediction`.
- Every read site resolves via `modelConfig.<field> ?? experimentDefault`, so behavior is unchanged for any strategy that does not set a value.
- `selectedModelConfiguration()` returns the strategy-resolved config, so consumers outside `xtabProvider` observe the baked values:
  - **xtabProvider** (`patchModelPredictionKind`, `splitPatchOnDiff`, `patchFastYieldLineWithCursor`, `extraDebounceEndOfLine`) via the already-resolved model config.
  - **NextEditProvider** (`cacheDelay`, `rebasedCacheDelay`) and **UserInteractionMonitor** (`debounce`) inject `IInlineEditsModelService`.
  - **inline completion provider** (`nesMimicGhostTextBehavior`) via its existing model service.
- Adds a reusable `NullInlineEditsModelService` test double for the newly-injected dependency.

### Completions unification

`supportsUnifiedCompletions` bakes completions unification into the strategy, following the exact `supportsNextCursorLinePrediction` precedent where a baked capability overrides the deployment toggle at each read site. When the selected NES model's strategy sets it, the client runs as the single unified provider — one baked boolean replaces all three unification settings:

- **`inlineCompletionProvider.ts`**: `unification` resolves via `selectedModelConfiguration().supportsUnifiedCompletions ?? InlineEditsUnification` (replaces `github.copilot.chat.advanced.inlineEdits.unification`).
- **`jointInlineCompletionProvider.ts`**: the baked flag is observed reactively (via `onModelListUpdated`) and OR-ed into the effective `modelUnification`, which both suppresses the separate GitHub Copilot completions provider and pushes `github.copilot` into the provider `excludes` (replaces `inlineCompletionsUnificationModel` (ExP) and `excludedProviders: "completions,github.copilot"` (local)).

The baked value never replaces the existing experiment path for other models — it only short-circuits it when set, so unrelated deployments are unaffected.

### Intended deployment

```jsonc
{
  "modelConfiguration": {
    "modelName": "copilot-suggestions-lysithea-0024",
    "promptingStrategy": "patchBased02Optimized",
    "includeTagsInCurrentFile": false
  }
}
```

No `inlineCompletionsUnificationModel` / `unification` / `excludedProviders` toggles are required — the strategy carries them.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck --prefix extensions/copilot`
- focused Vitest coverage for `applyStrategyConfig`, `MODEL_CONFIGURATION_VALIDATOR`, `pickSystemPrompt`, `NextEditProvider` caching/speculative, and `UserInteractionMonitor`
- `npm run precommit`

title: [cherry-pick] chat: don't prompt for workspace trust on internal agent-session folders
body:
Cherry-pick of #332280 from `release/1.135`.

Fixes #332249

## Problem

The send-time workspace-trust gate added for agent-host chat treated two **internal** folders as user workspaces and prompted _"Do you trust the authors of the files in this folder?"_:

1. **Workspace-less quick chats** — the agent host runs them in an internal scratch dir `~/.copilot/chats/<id>`, which is persisted as the session's working directory. The gate read `workingDirectories` but ignored the `workspaceless` marker, so it prompted for the scratch dir.
2. **Worktree sessions** — VS Code creates isolated worktrees in a **sibling** `<repo>.worktrees/<name>` dir. Workspace-trust inheritance is equal-or-descendant only, so trusting `/repo` does not cover `/repo.worktrees/x`; opening such a session from the list (and a follow-up send) prompted even though the base repo is trusted.

Regression from #331895 / #331981.

## Fix

- **Quick chats:** `AgentHostSessionHandler._resolveSessionTrustFolders` now reads the session state once and, when `readSessionWorkspaceless(state._meta)` is set, returns a sentinel so `_invokeAgent` **skips the folder-trust gate** entirely — the scratch dir is an implementation detail, not a user workspace.
- **Worktrees:** trust is **inherited from the already-trusted base repository** before the gates run:
  - `SessionsService.canOpenSession` calls a shared `ensureSessionWorktreesTrusted` helper (open gate).
  - The handler's send gate applies the equivalent inheritance (covers follow-up turns, which bypass the sessions open gate — the handler is the only universal chokepoint).
  - Both are guarded **structurally** to `getWorktreesRoot(<repo>)`: bare `workTreeUri` does not prove VS Code created the worktree, so a working directory outside `<repo>.worktrees` can never inherit trust just because its reported base repo is trusted (addresses the [#331981 review note](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/331981#discussion_r3831310974)).
- Extracts `getWorktreesRoot` into `platform/agentHost/common/worktreePaths.ts` so the node agent host and the browser trust gates share one implementation.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` — clean; `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed.
- Browser unit tests: `workspaceFolderManagement` (8) and agent-host `workspace trust` suite (10, incl. 5 new: quick-chat skip, worktree grant + follow-up turn, untrusted-repo prompt, structural-guard rejection, worktree-pending window).
- Full node unit suite: 15198 passing, 0 failing.

title: agent host: normalize empty Kerberos proxy SPN to avoid spurious restart
body:
Fixes #332305
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/8895
For https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/331648

## Problem

Restarting VS Code with an Agents Window session sometimes leaves the **Chat Panel empty** ("Couldn't open session"), even though the session data is intact. This is a spurious Copilot SDK client restart that tears down a healthy client **mid session-restore**.

The trigger is the Kerberos proxy SPN (`http.proxyKerberosServicePrincipal`), which reaches the agent host as two different representations of the same "not configured" state:

- When the Copilot client first spawns (on the reconnect-after-restart path), the host reads the setting as **absent** → `undefined` and records that as the applied baseline (`_applyProxyEnv`).
- A moment later the workbench mirrors its config down. The mirror transform coerces an **unset** setting to an **empty string** (`request.ts`: `value => typeof value === 'string' ? value : ''`). The `''` is load-bearing — it is how *clearing* a previously-set SPN propagates under the host's **merge** reducer, so it cannot simply be dropped.

`_refreshProxy` then compared the two values raw:

```
'' === undefined  →  false  →  "proxy config changed"  →  restart the Copilot client
```

Because the restart is not deferred during a restore, it calls `_stopClient()`, the in-flight resume's `_throwIfClientReplaced` throws a `CancellationError` ("Canceled"), that error is not classified as recoverable and the resume is not retried — so the panel is left empty. It is a race (spawn must win over the config push), which is why it only reproduces intermittently and only after a restart. The misleading `CAPI proxy configuration changed ((none) -> (none))` log hid that the SPN — not the proxy URL — drove the restart.

Only the SPN is affected: the proxy URL and no-proxy list are normalized before the restart comparison, and the sibling `enterpriseHost` already collapses empty≡absent (`enterpriseUri || undefined`). The SPN was the one proxy key compared raw.

## Fix

Read the SPN through a single helper, `_readKerberosSpn`, that normalizes `''` to `undefined`, and use it at **both** read sites — the applied baseline (`_applyProxyEnv`) and the effective value (`_refreshProxy`). Now an absent-vs-empty transition compares `undefined === undefined` and no restart is requested. This mirrors the existing `enterpriseHost` normalization and matches how the SPN is already treated everywhere it is *used* (the Kerberos lookup falls back to a hostname default for any falsy SPN), so it is a semantic reconciliation rather than a workaround.

Also replaced the misleading restart log with one that names the actual trigger(s) (`proxy … -> …` and/or `Kerberos SPN changed`).

### Why the fix lives on the host, not the workbench transform
Making the transform emit `undefined` would regress clearing a set SPN: the patch builder omits `undefined` keys and the host reducer *merges* patches, so the old value would survive. The reconciliation belongs on the host.

## Tests

Added two regression tests to the `restart on startup config change` suite in `copilotAgent.test.ts`:

- **`does not restart the Copilot runtime when an unset Kerberos proxy SPN is mirrored as empty`** — the core regression. Verified **red before / green after**: without the fix it fails with `stopCallCount: 1` (spurious restart); with the fix `startCallCount: 1, stopCallCount: 0` and the proxy refresh still runs.
- **`restarts the Copilot runtime without a Kerberos proxy SPN when a configured SPN is cleared`** — a guard proving the normalization does **not** suppress a legitimate clear (`A → ""` still restarts and respawns without the SPN).

All 5 Kerberos SPN tests pass. `tsc --noEmit` and ESLint are clean.

title: chat: Refresh customization source after harness registration
body:
I generated this by scanning my logs, pls take if it's good/useful

---
🤖 

## Summary

- cache an empty AI customization item source while its harness descriptor is unavailable
- invalidate that cache when the matching descriptor is registered or replaced
- refresh already-observed customization sections after late harness registration

## Problem

Recent Insiders renderer logs repeatedly emitted warnings during startup while customization harnesses were still registering:

```text
2026-08-17 15:21:43.525 [warning] No harness descriptor found for session type file
2026-08-17 15:21:43.783 [warning] No harness descriptor found for session type agent-host-copilotcli
```

The model also did not observe harness registration as an input to its source cache. As a result, an already-observed section could remain bound to the placeholder source until another unrelated change caused the source to be rebuilt.

Keep the existing `MutableDisposable` source cache and make its cache identity include both:

- the active session resource
- the resolved harness descriptor identity

The existing autorun now resolves the descriptor from the observed `availableHarnesses` value and passes it to the cache. This means:

- repeated reads while the descriptor is missing reuse one empty source
- registering the descriptor changes cache identity, replaces the placeholder source, and refetches observed sections
- re-registering a descriptor under the same ID still creates a fresh source

The change intentionally preserves the existing cache and lifecycle structure rather than introducing a broader observable refactor.

## Tests

Added a regression test that verifies the placeholder source is reused, then replaced and fetched exactly once when its harness registers.

title: fix(markdown): preserve table delimiter rows when injecting diff markers (closes #332119)
body: ## Summary Prevents Markdown diff inner change markers (`` / ``) from being injected into structural delimiter lines (such as table delimiter rows, code block fences, and horizontal rules), ensuring Markdown tables and code blocks parse correctly in visual diff previews. ## Problem When reviewing changes to a Markdown file containing a table in the Source Control rendered Markdown diff preview: 1. If a cell edit causes a column width change (or if a formatter re-aligns table pipes), the git diff detects changes across table delimiter rows (e.g. `| --- | --- |`). 2. The inner change diff injector places `` / `` marker tags into the table delimiter row. 3. Because the delimiter row no longer consists strictly of pipes, dashes, colons, and whitespace, markdown-it's GFM table parser fails to recognize the table syntax. 4. The entire table collapses into a block of raw unformatted text with literal pipes and dashes, making the diff unreadable. ## Root Cause `injectInnerChangeMarkers` in `documentRenderer.ts` injected diff marker `` tags into all modified lines without checking whether a line represents a Markdown structural block delimiter. When tags were inserted into table delimiter rows (e.g. `| --- |`), the delimiter row ceased to satisfy GFM table grammar rules. ## Solution 1. Added `isStructuralDelimiterLine` helper to `documentRenderer.ts` to identify structural Markdown lines: - Table delimiter rows (e.g. `| --- | :---: | ---: |` or `|---|---|`). - Code block fences (```` ``` ```` or `~~~`). - Thematic breaks / horizontal rules / frontmatter delimiters (`---`, `===`, `***`, `___`). 2. Skipped inner change marker tag injection for structural delimiter lines in `injectInnerChangeMarkers`. 3. Table headers and table body cells continue to receive inner change markers for rich in-cell word diff highlights, while the delimiter row remains clean so markdown-it renders an HTML ``. 4. Added test coverage in `engine.test.ts`. ## Behavioral Changes - Before: Editing table columns or reformatting table delimiter rows turned the rendered Markdown diff into raw unformatted pipes and dashes. - After: The table delimiter row remains valid GFM syntax, allowing the table to render as an HTML table with highlighted cell edits. ## Testing - Ran `node --experimental-strip-types build/hygiene.ts` (passed with 0 errors). - Ran `node --experimental-strip-types build/checker/layersChecker.ts` (passed with 0 errors). - Added regression test in `engine.test.ts`. ## Edge Cases Considered - Multi-column tables with varying alignment colons (`:---`, `:---:`, `---:`). - Compact tables without leading/trailing pipes (e.g. `Col A | Col B\n---|---`). - Tables inside blockquotes or indented contexts. - Genuine content lines containing single hyphens (e.g. `| - | text |`): only lines where every cell is a delimiter are recognized as structural. ## Compatibility - Backwards-compatible; preserves all existing diff highlighting for non-delimiter lines and cell content. ## Related Issue Closes #332119

title: chat: keep an agent turn's changes summary from flickering
body:
## What

The per-turn **"N files changed +A -B"** summary under a completed agent turn in the Agents window appeared, disappeared, reappeared, and sometimes stayed hidden for good.

## Why it happened

Every source behind the summary has windows where it legitimately reports no files, and `AgentHostResponseFileChangesProvider` treated each of them as *"this turn changed nothing"* — which makes each consumer hide itself:

- The part renders before session state resolves, so there is no turn changeset URI yet.
- Subscribing triggers `computeTurnChangeset`, whose `registerChangeset` seeds `{ status: Computing, files: [] }`.
- `onTurnComplete` schedules a **second** recompute for the same turn, flipping the status back to `Computing`. The old code required `status === Ready`, so it threw away files it already had (the reducer deliberately preserves `files` across a status change) and fell back to the response stream — which is empty while the turn moves from `activeTurn` to `turns`. That is the second flicker.
- A failed compute (`ChangesetStatus.Error`), an evicted changeset state, or a genuinely empty git turn diff left the summary hidden permanently.

The subscription is also released whenever the derived loses all observers (list recycling, the part being recreated when `isLastTurn` flips), so every re-read restarts from an empty snapshot.

## What changed

**`agentHostResponseFileChanges.ts`** — per-request diffs are now monotonic:

- Non-empty changeset files win regardless of status, so a recompute or an error keeps the last published list instead of falling back.
- An empty `Ready` changeset is still authoritative ("this turn changed nothing"), but only before anything has been shown — so no-op turns stay hidden and never appear-then-vanish.
- Otherwise the response stream, otherwise the previously emitted value.

**`chatTurnPillsPart.ts`** — the part latches its diffs as well, covering what the provider latch cannot: the observable being rebuilt on reconnect, LRU eviction, or the part being recreated.

**Logging** — each turn traces its diff source on change:

```
[AgentHostResponseFileChanges] <session> turn <id>: diffs from 'changeset|response|retained|authoritativeEmpty|unsupported' (files=N, changesetStatus=…)
```

## Reviewer notes

- **Trade-off:** a turn that shows streamed file-edit counts and whose authoritative changeset then computes to zero files now keeps the streamed counts instead of hiding. A trace line with `source='response'`/`'retained'` **and** `changesetStatus=ready` identifies exactly that case.
- `AgentHostResponseFileChangesProvider` gained a required `ILogService` parameter; `_resolveBackendChat` is now explicitly `| undefined` since it precedes it.
- `ChatCheckpointFileChangesSummaryContentPart` is untouched — it consumes the same provider, so agent-host sessions get the fix there too, while local chat sessions keep their existing behavior.

## Validation

- New provider test walks `Ready → Computing → Error → session-state loss → Ready-empty` and asserts the counts never change.
- New `ChatTurnPillsContentPart` test asserts the summary stays visible after its diffs go empty.
- `scripts\test.bat` over the provider, turn pills and checkpoint summary suites: 15 passing. `npm run typecheck-client` clean, eslint clean on changed files.

title: editor: hide mouse cursor while typing
body:
Adds an opt-in `editor.hideMouseCursorOnTyping` setting (default `false`) that hides the mouse
pointer after keyboard text input in the editor and reveals it again on the next pointer or focus
activity.

**Hiding** is driven from the semantic text input path (`_type`), not from raw key events, so
navigation keys, modifiers, paste, and programmatic edits leave the pointer alone.

**Revealing** happens on pointer move (guarded so that a re-render under a resting pointer does not
count as movement), pointer leave of the editor container, pointer down, wheel, context menu, editor
blur, and owner-window blur. The state is also cleared when the setting is turned off, when the model
is replaced, and when the editor is disposed.

**IME composition deliberately keeps the pointer visible.** Composition candidate windows are
positioned relative to the pointer on several platforms, and hiding it mid-composition makes the
candidate window hard to track, so `_startComposition` reveals the pointer and `_compositionType`
keeps it revealed for the duration of the composition.

Scope is the editor only. The integrated terminal and the rest of the workbench are unaffected — see
the follow-ups below.

The Monaco editor API declarations (`monaco.d.ts`, `standaloneEnums.ts`) are regenerated, and the
diff editor gets a targeted CSS override because its pre-existing `!important` resize cursors would
otherwise beat the `cursor: none` rule.

Fixes #29351

## Follow-ups

Deliberately out of scope for this PR:

- **Integrated terminal.** The terminal draws its own cursor and does not go through
  `CodeEditorWidget`, so it needs a separate hook; the setting description says so explicitly.
- **Shared overflow widget containers.** Suggest/hover widgets rendered into a workbench-level
  overflow container live outside the editor's DOM subtree, so the `cursor: none` class does not
  reach them. Handling that means either hiding at a shared ancestor or propagating the state, both
  of which affect non-editor UI.
- **Chromium `kHideCursorWhileTyping`.** Chromium can do this natively at the compositor level.
  Once Electron ships a version exposing it, this implementation could delegate instead of managing
  the class in JS.

## Testing

title: chat: don't prompt for workspace trust on internal agent-session folders
body:
Fixes #332249

## Problem

The send-time workspace-trust gate added for agent-host chat treated two **internal** folders as user workspaces and prompted _"Do you trust the authors of the files in this folder?"_:

1. **Workspace-less quick chats** — the agent host runs them in an internal scratch dir `~/.copilot/chats/<id>`, which is persisted as the session's working directory. The gate read `workingDirectories` but ignored the `workspaceless` marker, so it prompted for the scratch dir.
2. **Worktree sessions** — VS Code creates isolated worktrees in a **sibling** `<repo>.worktrees/<name>` dir. Workspace-trust inheritance is equal-or-descendant only, so trusting `/repo` does not cover `/repo.worktrees/x`; opening such a session from the list (and a follow-up send) prompted even though the base repo is trusted.

Regression from #331895 / #331981.

## Fix

- **Quick chats:** `AgentHostSessionHandler._resolveSessionTrustFolders` now reads the session state once and, when `readSessionWorkspaceless(state._meta)` is set, returns a sentinel so `_invokeAgent` **skips the folder-trust gate** entirely — the scratch dir is an implementation detail, not a user workspace.
- **Worktrees:** trust is **inherited from the already-trusted base repository** before the gates run:
  - `SessionsService.canOpenSession` calls a shared `ensureSessionWorktreesTrusted` helper (open gate).
  - The handler's send gate applies the equivalent inheritance (covers follow-up turns, which bypass the sessions open gate — the handler is the only universal chokepoint).
  - Both are guarded **structurally** to `getWorktreesRoot(<repo>)`: bare `workTreeUri` does not prove VS Code created the worktree, so a working directory outside `<repo>.worktrees` can never inherit trust just because its reported base repo is trusted (addresses the [#331981 review note](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/331981#discussion_r3831310974)).
- Extracts `getWorktreesRoot` into `platform/agentHost/common/worktreePaths.ts` so the node agent host and the browser trust gates share one implementation.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` — clean; `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed.
- Browser unit tests: `workspaceFolderManagement` (8) and agent-host `workspace trust` suite (10, incl. 5 new: quick-chat skip, worktree grant + follow-up turn, untrusted-repo prompt, structural-guard rejection, worktree-pending window).
- Full node unit suite: 15198 passing, 0 failing.

## Manual testing

- **Quick chat:** clear trust → Agents Window → "New Quick Chat" → send → no trust dialog (previously prompted for `~/.copilot/chats/<id>`). Control: "New Session" on an untrusted folder still prompts.
- **Worktree:** trust only a base repo → "New Session" on it with Worktree isolation → send (creates `<repo>.worktrees/<name>`) → reload → open from list and send a follow-up → no prompt. Control: with the base repo untrusted, it still prompts.

## Notes

- Branch is based on `release/1.135` (the regression ships in 1.135), so this PR targets `release/1.135`.
- Deferred follow-ups: validating creation provenance via `WORKTREE_META_REPOSITORY_ROOT` (stronger than the structural guard), and worktree-trust lifecycle/revocation (pre-existing; `setUrisTrust` is never revoked on worktree deletion).

title: Add table of contents with persistent visibility & code block language labels
body:
#332300 

This PR introduces two new features to the Markdown preview:

Table of Contents (TOC) — A navigable sidebar showing document headings with auto-scroll sync
Code Block Language Labels — Language badges (e.g., php, javascript, python) displayed on fenced code blocks
Both features are brand new and did not exist previously.

---

#### Features
1. Table of Contents

UI/UX:
- Collapsible sidebar on the left of the preview
- Shows all headings (h1–h6) with indentation by level
- Active heading highlighted based on scroll position
- Resizable width (drag handle), persisted in localStorage
- Toolbar toggle button with checkbox (synced to context key markdown.tocVisible)
- Persistence:
  - Visibility preference stored in extension globalState (markdown.preview.tocVisible)
  - Survives: tab close, VS Code restart, preview reopen
  - Default: visible (true)
Auto-scroll behavior:
- During document scroll: TOC panel scrolls minimally to keep active entry visible (with 4px edge gap)
- Manual click on TOC entry: Does not trigger TOC panel scroll — user stays at clicked position
- First/last headings can now reach true top/bottom of panel (no visual gap)

2. Code Block Language Labels
- Language identifier from fenced code blocks (php, js, python, etc.) displayed as a badge in the top-right corner of the code block
- Uses the existing tokenization from the markdown renderer
- Styled with theme-aware colors (uses `--vscode-editorCodeBlockLabel-background/foreground`)

#### Technical Implementation

TOC Architecture

```
MarkdownPreviewManager (owns globalState)
    ├── #tocVisible: boolean (persisted)
    ├── createPreview() / revivePreview() → passes tocVisible
    └── #setActivePreview() → sets context key 'markdown.tocVisible'

StaticMarkdownPreview / DynamicMarkdownPreview
    └── getAdditionalState() → includes tocVisible

Webview (preview-src/index.ts)
    ├── Reads State.TocVisible from vscode.getState() / data-state
    ├── Calls buildTableOfContents()
    └── If TocVisible === false → toggleTableOfContents()

tableOfContents.ts (webview module)
    ├── Module-level tocVisible (synced from State)
    ├── skipScrollActiveEntry flag (prevents auto-scroll on manual click)
    ├── scrollActiveEntryIntoView() (minimal scroll with edge gap)
    └── Resize handle → persists width to localStorage
```

Language Labels
- Injected during markdown rendering via markdown-it plugin
- Added as <span class="code-block-language-label"> inside code block wrapper
- CSS uses design tokens for theming consistency

##### Test Workspace
Open the test workspace file:

```
extensions/markdown-language-features/test-workspace/e.md
```

This file contains:
- Multiple heading levels (h1–h6) for TOC testing
- Fenced code blocks with various languages (php, javascript, python, typescript, etc.)
- Enough content to trigger scrolling

Table of Contents:

1. Open e.md in VS Code
2. Open Markdown Preview (Ctrl+Shift+V / Cmd+Shift+V)
3. Verify TOC appears on the left with all headings
4. Scroll in the preview → verify active heading highlights in TOC
5. Click a heading in TOC → verify navigation works without scrolling the TOC panel
6. Scroll to first/last heading → verify TOC scrollbar reaches true top/bottom
7. Click toolbar toggle button → verify TOC hides/shows, checkbox matches
8. Close preview tab, reopen → verify TOC visibility persists
9. Restart VS Code → verify TOC visibility persists

Code Block Language Labels:

2. Verify each block shows a language badge (e.g., php, js, py, ts)
3. Switch themes (light/dark/high contrast) → verify badge colors adapt

title: chat: clear progress when session provider is disposed
body:
I generated this by scanning my logs, pls take if it's good/useful

---
🤖 

## Summary

- clear a chat session provider's in-progress entry synchronously when its item controller is disposed
- prevent an in-flight progress refresh from publishing after its controller has been removed or replaced
- add regression coverage for adding and removing provider progress across controller disposal

## Problem

Recent Code Insiders renderer logs repeatedly showed warnings while Agent Host-backed chat session providers were shutting down:

```text
2026-08-22 15:34:26.089 [warning] Attempted to report in-progress status for unknown chat session type 'copilotcli'
2026-08-22 15:34:26.282 [warning] Attempted to report in-progress status for unknown chat session type 'copilot-cloud-agent'
```

The warning was produced by the controller disposal path itself. `registerChatSessionItemController` removed the controller from `_itemControllers` and then called `updateInProgressStatus`. That asynchronous recomputation eventually called `reportInProgress`, which correctly noticed that the controller no longer existed and logged the warning. It also retained a zero-count entry for a provider that was no longer registered.

There was a related race for progress updates already in flight: a refresh could start while a controller was registered, await item resolution, and publish after that controller had been disposed or replaced.

## Fix

Controller disposal now deletes the corresponding progress entry directly and emits `onDidChangeInProgress` only when an entry was actually removed. This keeps controller registration and its derived progress state within the same lifecycle instead of querying a provider after teardown.

`updateInProgressStatus` also captures the current controller identity before awaiting item resolution and verifies that the same controller is still registered before publishing. This prevents stale work from restoring progress for a disposed or replaced provider.

Active providers retain the existing progress computation behavior.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chatSessions/chatSessions.contribution.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatSessions/chatSessionsService.test.ts`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/chatSessions/chatSessionsService.test.ts --grep "removes in-progress state when its controller is disposed"`
- pre-commit hygiene checks

The focused regression test passes and verifies that an in-progress entry is published while the controller is registered and removed when its registration is disposed.

title: Prevent stale Claude queries from consuming prompts after rebind
body:
## Summary

- retire the previous Claude prompt iterator when a `Query` is rebound, so it cannot consume the fresh query's first prompt
- stop messages from a stale `Query` before they reach the router or settle the shared prompt queue
- cover both races with deterministic queue and pipeline regressions

## Problem

The Claude pipeline keeps one prompt queue across SDK `Query` rebinds. The previous query can remain alive briefly after the swap:

1. Its input loop can still be parked on the shared iterable. The SDK checks its abort signal only after pulling a prompt, so it can remove the new query's first prompt and then drop it.
2. Its output loop can still yield a buffered `result`. Without an ownership check, that result settles the new query's queue head and completes the turn without an assistant response.

In both cases the affected prompt appears to do nothing, while a subsequent prompt works normally.

title: Add worker-src to MCP app webview CSP (fixes #331633)
body:
Fixes #331633.

`_injectPreamble` in `chatMcpAppModel.ts` builds the MCP app webview CSP with `default-src`, `script-src`, `style-src`, `connect-src`, `img-src`, `font-src`, `media-src`, `frame-src`, `object-src` and `base-uri` — but no `worker-src`. Per CSP spec the browser then falls back to `script-src`, which carries no `blob:` scheme, so any MCP app that spawns a Web Worker from a `blob:` URL is blocked:

```
Creating a worker from 'blob:vscode-webview://…' violates the following Content
Security Policy directive: "script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline' <domains>".
Note that 'worker-src' was not explicitly set, so 'script-src' is used as a
fallback. The action has been blocked.
```

This breaks a class of MCP apps rather than a single case — anything using MapLibre/Mapbox GL JS (tile parsing), PDF.js, Monaco, or other blob-worker libraries. The failure is silent: the data layer renders, the basemap never paints, and nothing surfaces in the chat UI.

Not fixable from the MCP resource side, and no MCP Apps spec change needed — the reference host (`examples/basic-host/serve.ts` in `modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps`) already sets `worker-src 'self' blob:` unconditionally. `modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps#566` (resource-level `workerDomains`) is an independent optional enhancement, not a prerequisite.

Verified against `main`: the directive is still absent.

title: agent host: self-heal Copilot client cold-start config-changed abort
body:
## What

When a startup-config value (session sync, SDK log level, enterprise host, system proxy, built-in GitHub MCP, …) changes **while the Copilot SDK client is starting**, `_ensureClient` aborts the now-stale start and throws `CopilotClientStartupConfigChangedError`. Because the *next* start uses the current config, that abort is transient — yet it was surfaced to session restore, producing sticky, user-visible failures such as **"Provider copilotcli could not describe … yet"** / **"Couldn't open session"**, even though the backend recovered moments later.

## Change

`_ensureClient` now transparently re-acquires the client **once** with the current config instead of propagating the transient abort:

- The existing acquisition body is extracted into `_ensureClientOnce()` — per-attempt coalescing via `_clientStarting` is unchanged.
- `_ensureClient()` wraps it in a bounded retry loop that retries **only** on `CopilotClientStartupConfigChangedError`, bounded by `MAX_STARTUP_CONFIG_RETRIES` (1).
- The acquire-and-retry sequence is shared across all concurrent callers via `_ensureClientHealing`, so the retry budget is **global** (a late caller cannot reset it and drive unbounded starts).
- Shutdown still short-circuits; every other startup failure propagates unchanged.

No caller observes the transient abort; a genuinely persistent config problem still gives up after the bound.

## Tests

`src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts`:
- self-heals a clean config-changed cold-start abort and returns the catalog
- self-heals a clean config-changed cold-start abort on the restore describe path
- gives up after the bounded number of re-acquires when the startup config keeps changing
- shares one global re-acquire budget across concurrent client acquisitions
- coalesces concurrent client acquisitions across a single re-acquire
- (updated) self-heals a config-changed cold-start abort when stopping the started client fails

Full suite green (318 passing, 0 failing).

## Notes for reviewers

- This is the **provider-side** half only. The **host-side** readiness gap (`AgentService._restoreSessionState` throwing `-32603 "could not describe … yet"` without waiting for provider readiness) and the **client-side** sticky error-model reconciliation are tracked separately and intentionally **not** addressed here.
- Deliberately narrow and defensive.

Related to https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/8895

title: [Reference only] Launch skill: batched automation prototype
body:
## Reference / inspiration only

This draft collects the full launch-skill prototype developed during the performance investigation. It is **unlikely to land as-is**: the change is intentionally broad and should instead be mined for smaller, focused follow-ups. The main purpose is to preserve working examples and measurements for inspiration.

## Ideas demonstrated

- A one-process direct-CDP driver with JSON scenarios (`prepare`, checked `chat`, and `fork` actions).
- Aggressive but validated modal handling: known Workspace Trust dialogs are handled immediately, awaited until hidden, and unknown dialogs fail instead of allowing clicks behind them.
- Exact Monaco prompt insertion/read-back before Send is enabled and clicked.
- Adaptive response waiting that observes loading and completion instead of sleeping a fixed 30 seconds.
- Fast fork completion detection based on actual transcript/session state changes.
- Automatic workspace selection/reselection for transient Agents-window state.
- Privacy-aware action recording hints with redacted text and compact DOM mutation summaries.
- An isolated benchmark runner, scenario JSON format, raw result JSON, and an in-skill dashboard covering both Agents and Editor windows.

## Why it is useful as inspiration

The prototype is especially effective at the expensive inner loop: dismissing modals, sending chat messages, waiting for model replies, and validating fork completion without additional model turns or separate Playwright processes for every action. Those techniques can be extracted into a general Playwright CLI batching approach or smaller reusable helpers.

Historical three-run results in the included dashboard reduced the two-turn/fork scenario from roughly 45–62 seconds and 21–43 Playwright invocations to 14.87–15.37 seconds median with one automation process, with 3/3 passes on both surfaces and ~0.22–0.24 second median fork detection.

Fresh validation after rebasing onto current `main`:

| Surface | Result | Launch | Full scenario | Fork | Visible modals after |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Agents | Pass | 1.17 s | 20.04 s | 0.27 s | 0 |
| Editor | Pass | 0.72 s | 15.30 s | 0.23 s | 0 |

Both fresh runs used unique non-git fixture folders, handled Workspace Trust where needed, verified both model replies, left the repository worktree list unchanged, and cleaned the launched profiles.

## Scope warning

This includes the benchmark runner, dashboard, raw JSON results, scenario format, driver, modal gate, chat/fork recipes, and recorder in one reference PR. Reviewers should treat it as a design/prototyping artifact and source of smaller optimizations, not as a request to approve the entire architecture unchanged.

## Summary

Fixes Agent Host debug exports for completed Copilot sessions so the archive includes the provider's `events.jsonl` journal and reports `providerLogsIncluded` accurately.

## Description

Fixes #331433.

### Problem
When hovering a color swatch (e.g. `color: white` in CSS), the hover color picker is easily dismissed by a tiny mouse movement while the pointer is still over the color decorator (the injected swatch).

The keep-open logic in `ContentHoverController._shouldKeepCurrentHover` only keeps the hover alive when the mouse is **inside** the hover/picker widget's DOM node (or while the mouse button is held). When the pointer remains on the swatch itself but moves a few pixels, the `showsOrWillShow` path can recompute a different anchor and hide the picker.

### Fix
Extend `isMouseOnColorPickerOrChoosingColor` so that, while the color picker is visible, the hover is also kept open when the mouse is over the color decorator (`isOnColorDecorator`). This mirrors the existing mouse-down behaviour in `_shouldKeepHoverWidgetVisible`, which already uses `isOnColorDecorator` to keep the hover visible while interacting with the swatch.

```ts
const isMouseOnColorDecorator = isColorPickerVisible && isOnColorDecorator(mouseEvent);
return isMouseOnHoverWithColorPicker || isMaybeChoosingColor || isMouseOnColorDecorator;
```

1. Open a `.css` file and write `color: white;` (color decorators on hover).
2. Hover the white swatch so the color picker appears.
3. Move the mouse slightly while remaining over the swatch — the picker should stay open.
4. Move the mouse onto the picker — it should remain open.
5. Move the mouse off the swatch/picker — the hover should dismiss as before.

title: Persist session archiving without restoring the session
body:
## The bug

Archiving a session in the Agents window could appear to succeed — the session vanished from the list — while recording nothing, so it reappeared after a refresh or restart. This hit hardest on old sessions whose working directories or worktrees no longer exist.

## Root cause

When a client dispatched `session/isArchivedChanged` for a session with no live host state, `AgentService.dispatchAction` first `await`ed `restoreSession(...)`. Restore reopens the session's working directory, and for a missing one **only an *already* archived session resumes read-only** — otherwise it tries to recreate the worktree and throws.

That is circular: archiving is precisely what would have made it archived. The operation was impossible for exactly the sessions that needed it most. The failed restore rejected the action, nothing was persisted, and the client never rolled back.

## The fix

Archived/read toggles are now applied **without materializing the session**: the flag is written to the session database and the catalogue delta is published via `root/sessionSummaryChanged`. The envelope and its side effects — worktree cleanup on archive, `onArchivedChanged`, Agent Merge sync — still run, since none of them need live state.

### Further bugs found and fixed along the way

- **`SessionSummaryNotifier` could not publish for an un-loaded session.** It re-derives summaries from live state and bails when there is none, so AHP-specified catalogue mutations were silently dropped. It now supports pushing changes into an announced summary, keeping a single notification path.
- **`removeSession` cleared the announced summary** — but it is also the idle-eviction hook, and eviction emits no `sessionRemoved`, so clients keep listing the session. A session that was opened and later evicted therefore looked *unknown*, and archiving it was dropped entirely. This is likely the most common archive flow (open a session, navigate away, archive later). The baseline now outlives eviction; `deleteSession` clears it explicitly.
- **The passive route was chosen from a stale snapshot.** `requiresSessionRestore` is computed at dispatch entry, but the callback runs behind earlier queued dispatches — so a toggle was dropped outright if an earlier action restored the session meanwhile. Residency is now re-checked at execution time, joining any in-flight restore.
- **The Agents window applied rejected envelopes.** It ignored `rejectionReason`, contradicting AHP reconciliation (a rejected action's optimistic effect must be reverted). It also flipped the archived observable with no connection to persist through.

## Protocol conformance

Dispatching a session action while *not subscribed* to that session is explicitly supported by AHP:

> "A client therefore answers by dispatching the ordinary `chat/*` action **to that chat's channel** — it does **not** need to have subscribed to the chat first." — `docs/specification/session-channel.md`

`dispatchAction` is a fire-and-forget notification, so the client is not owed an acknowledgement, and convergence for such clients is specified to ride `root/sessionSummaryChanged`, which is broadcast to every client regardless of subscription. Since that channel documents `read/done state` as part of its payload, the previous behaviour was a **conformance gap** — we dropped a mutation the protocol says we must publish. No protocol change was needed.

Creating `agentSessionData/<id>` is how Agent Host claims a session away from the extension host's Copilot CLI list, so the passive path refuses to do it for a session the host has never surfaced, matching AHP's "silently ignore actions for non-existent sessions".

## Out of scope

Un-adopted legacy Copilot CLI sessions (`ehcliAdoptable`) continue to be dropped rather than persisted, since persisting them would claim ownership away from the extension host. Filed separately.

## Testing

Nine regression tests added, **each verified to fail without the fix and pass with it**:

- persists + publishes without restoring (archive and read)
- succeeds when the working directory is gone (the motivating case)
- succeeds for a session that was opened and then idle-evicted
- lands when an earlier queued action restored the session
- creates no session database for an unknown session
- `deleteSession` still clears the announced baseline
- a rejected envelope leaves the session unarchived

Full suites green: 5,584 agentHost + 2,464 sessions + 1,222 workbench agentSessions. `typecheck-client`, `eslint`, and `valid-layers-check` all clean.

title: Process listing fails when a process exits during scanning
body:
Fixes #186500

## Problem

On Linux, opening the process explorer (or anything that calls `listProcesses`) can fail with **"Listing processes failed"** whenever a short-lived process happens to exit while the list is being built. The reported error is `cat: /proc/<pid>/stat: No such file or directory`.

## Root cause

When GNU `ps` is unavailable, we fall back to `vs/base/node/ps.sh`, which enumerates numeric entries under `/proc` and then reads each process's `stat`, `cmdline`, etc. A process can exit at any point between enumeration and those reads:

- the `ls -d [0-9]*` enumeration itself races with process exit (`ls: cannot access '<pid>': No such file or directory`),
- the per-pid reads race too (`cat: /proc/<pid>/stat: No such file or directory` from `awk` reading `stat`, or errors from the `cmdline` redirection).

Any of these writes to stderr. `listProcesses()` in `ps.ts` treats **any** stderr output as total failure and rejects, so one vanished process out of hundreds kills the entire listing for the user.

## Fix

Every access to a process's files in `ps.sh` can race against that process exiting, so this change suppresses errors from those accesses and handles the vanished process gracefully:

- `2>/dev/null` on the `/proc` enumeration and on each per-pid read,
- an emptiness guard on the resident-set-size value so a failed `stat` read reports `0.0` memory instead of injecting an empty operand into the shell arithmetic (which would itself print an error),
- a comment explaining why the suppression is correct here.

The rest of the pipeline is unchanged: processes that still exist produce exactly the same output as before.

## Testing

- New regression suite in `src/vs/base/test/node/ps.test.ts`: spawns short-lived background processes while repeatedly executing the real `ps.sh`, asserts stderr stays empty across multiple rounds, with a quiet-system baseline control first. It is gated to run only where `/proc` exists (skipped elsewhere).
- Reproduced the bug deterministically before the fix on a real Linux environment (WSL2): under churn, **10/10** measurement rounds produced race stderr (`ls: cannot access '<pid>'` / `cat: /proc/<pid>/stat` shapes), while the quiet-system baseline was clean - proving the failures are churn-induced.
- After the fix: repeated measurement rounds under sustained identical churn produced **zero stderr**, and a quiet-system output-equivalence check (original vs fixed script, excluding the checker's own transient processes) showed identical listings.
- `npm run transpile-client` passes; targeted ESLint on the changed test file is clean; unit run of `Process Utils` shows the existing regex tests passing and the new Linux-gated suite correctly *pending* on Windows.

## Potential risks

- Low: behavior changes are confined to the fallback shell script used on Linux when `ps` is missing, plus the new test. Output shape for live processes is unchanged (verified by the equivalence check), so parsing in `parsePsOutput` is unaffected.
- A process that exits mid-scan now appears with placeholder values (or is omitted by the enumeration filter) instead of failing the whole listing - that degraded-but-useful row is strictly better than the current total failure, and matches what `ps` itself does under the same conditions.
- Not verified on macOS (unchanged code path) or inside a packaged VS Code client; the Linux verification was done against the real script in a real `/proc` environment rather than through the full app UI.

title: Cancelling cells of a closed notebook throws instead of being ignored
body:
Fixes #187448

## Problem

Cell cancellation is sent from the renderer to the extension host, but by the time it arrives the notebook document can already be gone - the notebook was closed, or the extension host restarted while cancellation was in flight. The lookup then throws `NO notebook document for 'file:///...'` straight out of the RPC dispatcher (`$cancelCells` -> `getNotebookDocument`), which is a long-running top error-telemetry bucket and interrupts whatever else the extension host was doing.

## Root cause

`$cancelCells` uses the strict overload of `getNotebookDocument` and has no guard for a missing document, unlike the kernel-lookup right above it in the same method which already handles a disposed kernel gracefully.

## Fix

`$cancelCells` now looks the document up in relaxed mode and returns silently when it is gone - there is nothing left to cancel. The existing behavior for live notebooks is unchanged.

## Testing

New test in `extHostNotebookKernel.test.ts`: cancelling cells of an unknown notebook URI is ignored (no throw, no interrupt call), and cancelling cells of a live notebook still reaches the interrupt handler.

Before the fix, the new test fails with exactly the production error: `Error: NO notebook document for 'file:///path/to/gone.ipynb'`. After: passing. Full `NotebookKernel` suite: 19 passing. `npm run typecheck-client` clean, ESLint clean on both changed files.

## Potential risks

None known - the only behavior change is for documents that no longer exist, where the previous behavior was an unhandled throw.

title: Notebooks of a view type break when their serializer registers twice
body:
Fixes #174051

## Problem

After a crash or restart of the extension host, an extension that provides a notebook serializer (for example the `sql-book` provider from the issue) registers again, but the stale registration from the previous extension host is sometimes still present. Registration then throws `notebook provider for viewtype 'X' already exists` out of the RPC dispatcher, the serializer never becomes active, and every notebook of that view type fails to open until the window is reloaded. This has been one of the top error-telemetry buckets for years.

## Root cause

`NotebookService._registerProviderData` treats an existing entry for the same view type as a hard error. That is correct for two different extensions fighting over one view type, but wrong when the *same* registration arrives again after an extension host restart and the old disposable was not run in time.

## Fix

Registering now replaces the existing entry instead of throwing:

- the fresh serializer takes effect immediately, so notebooks of the view type keep working across extension host restarts
- when the replacement switches extensions, that is logged as a warning (`ILogService`), since it indicates two extensions claiming the same type
- disposing a stale registration no longer removes the fresh entry — a registration only removes itself while it is still the current one
- the replace logic lives in a small exported helper (`registerProviderData`) so it can be unit tested without instantiating the service (its constructor claims process-global extension points)

## Testing

New test in `notebookServiceImpl.test.ts`: re-registering replaces the entry, reports the replaced extension id, stale disposal does not remove the fresh registration, and disposing the current one cleans up.

Before the fix, the equivalent call sequence fails with exactly the production error: `Error: notebook provider for viewtype 'sql-book' already exists`. After: passing. Also ran the neighboring `NotebookProviderInfoStore` suite (passing), `npm run typecheck-client` (clean) and ESLint on the changed files (clean).

## Potential risks

- Extensions that relied on the throw to detect duplicate view types will no longer see an error; the last registration wins, which matches what users expect (the newly activated extension works).

title: Fix unfolding folded regions on Android vscode.dev
body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/292361

## Problem
On **vscode.dev in Android Chrome**, folding a region works, but tapping the same region to unfold does not. The reporter’s video shows the inline fold placeholder (`...`), not only the gutter chevron.

This is a high-impact editor-folding bug: once a region is collapsed on a phone, there is no reliable way to get that code back without a reload or a desktop client. I prioritized it because the folding *model* is fine — the failure is in touch input — so a small, targeted fix restores a basic editing action on the web.

## Root cause
Two cooperating input bugs on Android phones (`PointerEventHandler` is used when `isIOS || isAndroid` and pointer events exist):

1. **Inline `...` placeholder (primary, matches the issue video)**  
   Gesture is registered only on `linesContentDomNode`. A tap on `...` is handled as a Gesture `Tap`, which calls `preventDefault()` and originally dispatched with `leftButton: false`. `FoldingController.onEditorMouseDown` returned immediately unless the event had a left or middle button, so the unfold path never ran.

2. **Duplicate `mouseup` on the gutter**  
   `PointerEventHandler` skipped touch `pointerdown` but still handled touch `pointerup`. Android Chrome also fires a compatibility `mouseup`. After unfold, the same icon is still under the finger, so the second `mouseup` immediately re-folded the region.

Android tablets were also left on `TouchHandler`, which never forwarded taps to folding contributions at all.

## What changed
- **`pointerHandler.ts`**: emit mouse down/up from Gesture taps (`PointerEventHandler` and `TouchHandler`) so folding sees the tap; ignore touch `pointerup` as well as `pointerdown`; use the pointer+gesture path on all Android devices, not only phones (`isMobile`).
- **`folding.ts`**: accept Gesture-shaped taps (`leftButton: false`) on `CONTENT_TEXT` (the `...` placeholder) and `CONTENT_EMPTY` (when `unfoldOnClickAfterEndOfLine` is on); clear `mouseDownInfo` after a successful toggle so a duplicate `mouseup` cannot toggle again.
- **`folding.test.ts`**: regression tests for duplicate gutter `mouseup`, placeholder tap unfold, and empty-content tap unfold.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run eslint` on the three changed files
- [x] `npm run typecheck-client`
- [x] `npm run compile-client` and `npm run compile-web` (0 errors)
- [x] Chromium folding unit tests, including the new `#292361` cases (3 passing in `folding.test.ts`; existing folding suites still green)
- [x] Manual: vscode.dev / Android Chrome — open a file, fold via gutter, tap `...` to unfold; fold/unfold again and confirm it does not snap back
- [x] Manual: gutter fold/unfold still works on desktop mouse

title: Restore persisted platform root config on agent host startup
body:
## Problem

The Agents window UI showed `chat.agentSessions.showExternal` as **Last 30 Days** while the agent host logged `showExternalSessions: 'none'` and hid external sessions.

`persistRootConfig` writes the whole root value bag to `agent-host-config.json`, but `_loadPersistedRootConfig` only restored five schema groups — customization, sandbox, copilotCli, agentMerge and proxy. Every `platformRootSchema` key was dropped on load, and [`AgentHostStateManager`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostStateManager.ts) seeds only `permissions` and `telemetryLevel`, so those keys were genuinely absent from root config until a window connected and re-pushed them.

The host reads several of them before that happens, so they silently fell back to schema defaults.

## Evidence

From an `ah-logs` bundle, the `initialize` response carrying the host's cold-start root snapshot:

| Path in root-state snapshot | Present? |
| --- | --- |
| `config.schema.properties.showExternalSessions` | yes |
| `config.values.showExternalSessions` | **no** |

…even though `agent-host-config.json` on disk did contain `"showExternalSessions"`. A second window's `initialize` 48s later *does* carry the value — only because the first window had already re-pushed it.

The resulting sequence:

```
11:44:01  root/configChanged … "showExternalSessions":"none"
11:45:03  listSessions hid 48 of 394 session(s) (showExternalSessions: 'none')
11:46:32  showExternalSessions changed 'none' -> 'recent'; queueing session list reconciliation
```

`_getExternalSessionsMode()` fell through to `?? AgentHostExternalSessionsMode.None`, so the first catalog pass and the initial external-session reconciliation both ran under `none`.

## Impact beyond the reported symptom

The same gap affected every other `platformRootSchema` key read before a client connects:

- `codexAgentEnabled` — read during provider registration in `agentHostMain.ts` / `agentHostServerMain.ts`, so Codex could fail to register on a cold start
- `migrateLegacyCopilotCliEnabled` — read early in `listSessions`
- `editTelemetryEnabled`
- hand-edited values in a remote `agent-host-config.json`, which operators expect to be authoritative

## Fix

Restore the platform-owned keys alongside the other schema groups, via `platformRootSchema.validateOrDefault` so malformed entries still fall back to defaults rather than being loaded verbatim.

Root `permissions` stays excluded: it mirrors the connected client's managed settings, so reviving a previous run's value could re-grant an allow rule that has since been revoked. It is left for the client to republish.

## Testing

Added a round-trip test in `agentConfigurationService.test.ts` that persists `last30Days` plus a permissions rule, constructs a fresh service against the same file, and asserts the mode survives the restart while permissions do not.

- `tsc --noEmit` clean
- New test passes
- Full node unit suite: same pre-existing Windows failures (`SessionPermissionManager` path tests, `AgentHostDebugLogsCollector`) before and after the change

title: sessions: hide external Recent sessions superseded by newer local ones
body:
Adjusts the `Recent` external-sessions mode so it stops surfacing external sessions the user has clearly moved on from.

## What changed

`Recent` still shows the 2 most recently updated external sessions from the last 7 days, but now hides any of them that **2 locally created sessions have started after its last update**.

Implemented in `_getRecentSessionKeys` via a single cutoff — the start time of the 2nd-newest local session. An external session is dropped when its `modifiedTime` predates that cutoff:

| Local sessions | 10am external | 4pm external |
| --- | --- | --- |
| none after 10am | shown | shown |
| one at 11am | shown | shown |
| 11am + 5pm | **hidden** | shown |
| 5pm + 5pm | **hidden** | **hidden** |

## Why the cutoff is snapshotted

Sending a first message is what materializes a local session, so a cutoff derived on every listing would rotate an external row out of the list while the user is looking at it. `_getRecentSupersedingCutoff` therefore snapshots the value on the first `Recent` listing and refreshes it only when the external-sessions mode changes.

The existing external-session reconciliation listener is untouched, so the top-2 selection still rotates when external sessions are discovered or updated.

## Notes for reviewers

- Three setting/banner strings now read "up to the 2 most recently updated…" instead of promising exactly 2.
- Two new tests in `agentService.test.ts`: the four scenarios above, and one asserting the visible set stays put after two local sessions appear but updates once the mode changes.
- Validation: `npm run typecheck-client` clean, eslint clean on changed files, full `agentService.test.js` suite passes (357 passing), sessions banner test passes. `npm run hygiene` fails in this worktree on a pre-existing doubled-drive-letter path bug (`C:\C:\...\remote\package.json`), unrelated to these changes.

title: File watcher silently stops working when watched folder is renamed
body:
Fixes #309241

## Problem

When you rename or move a folder that is being watched recursively from outside the workspace, the file watcher never tells anyone. On Windows and macOS the underlying watcher handle survives the rename, so no events arrive at all: no `onDidDelete` for the base folder, and every later change inside the renamed folder goes unnoticed. The same rename inside the workspace behaves correctly, which is exactly the inconsistency reported in #309241.

I reproduced this on current main against the real `ParcelWatcher` backend: after renaming the watched root, the watcher delivered zero events, fired no fail signal, and stayed silent even for new files created inside the renamed folder.

## Root cause

`ParcelWatcher` only reacts to a lost watch path when an explicit `DELETED` event for the root arrives (`filterEvents` → `rootDeleted`). A rename produces no such event, so the existing recovery machinery in `BaseWatcher` (suspend/resume) never kicks in, and clients are left watching a ghost.

## Fix

This change adds a small periodic existence check on the watched root to `startWatching()`. If the root disappears without any event having been received, we synthesize the root `DELETED` event and run it through the exact same pipeline as a real deletion (`handleParcelEvents` → fail → suspend/resume). That means:

- clients now get `onDidDelete` for the renamed base folder
- the watcher enters suspend and automatically resumes when the path comes back
- polling watchers are untouched; Linux is unaffected because inotify already reports the rename as real events (and the new check backs off once the watcher has failed)

The check itself is one `fs.access` per watcher every 5 seconds (~0.05 ms per call measured), in line with the existing suspended-request monitoring cadence.

## Testing

- Added a regression test to the existing parcel watcher suite: `renaming watched path emits watcher fail and delete event if correlated`
- Verified it **fails before** the fix (timeout waiting for events) and **passes after** it
- Full parcel suite: 29 passing before and after, only pre-existing flaky failures unchanged
- Broader unit suite: 52 failures before the change on this machine, 52 identical failures after (all unrelated `agentHost`/environment issues)
- `npm run typecheck-client` passes; ESLint clean on both changed files

## Potential risks

- macOS behavior is expected to mirror Windows (FSEvents also keeps handles alive across renames), but I could only verify Windows locally
- The synthetic delete can arrive up to ~5 s after the actual rename

title: agentHost: add a chat contribution model for cross-cutting behavior
body:
Introduces a registry-driven contribution model for the agent host so cross-cutting behavior lives in self-contained modules instead of branches inlined in `AgentSideEffects` and `AgentService`.

The goal is that a feature which touches several points in the turn lifecycle (contribute a command, add context on the way out, strip it from rendered history) can be written once, in one folder, rather than as separate branchy code in each place.

## Hooks

| Hook | Fires |
|---|---|
| `onTurnEnd` | every terminal outcome, discriminated by a `TurnEndReason` union |
| `contributeSend` | before a turn is sent; results concatenated in `order` |
| `onHydrateTurns` | whole restored turn list, as a pipeline |
| `onAction` | client dispatched actions |
| `onUserMessage` | a user message admitted on the direct path |

## Contributions

`queueDrain`, `persistedTurnUsage`, `sessionTitle`, `checkpointAndChangeset`, `markdownPlanRichLinks`, `markUnread`, `githubReferences`, `chatSurface`, `worktreeAnnouncement`, `artifactTools`.

Each lives in its own subfolder and is registered explicitly in `createAgentService` from one shared list, mirroring `IAgentHostChangesetOperationService`. Sequencing comes from an explicit `order`; registration order is only a tiebreak.

## Supporting work

- A per-contribution context with chat and session scoped mementos, evicted centrally when a chat or session is disposed. This replaces the pattern of each collaborator keeping its own URI keyed map with its own cleanup path, and let `clearQueuedMessageSenders` and both of its call sites be deleted.
- Several collaborators that `AgentSideEffects` constructed privately are now services owned by the composition root: the session title controller, telemetry reporter, turn tracker, and local command dispatcher.
- The bespoke host bridge that existed because these were not injectable is down from seven members to two: `hostLaunchKind` and `sendTurnMessage`.

## Behavior

Behavior preserving throughout. The existing `agentSideEffects` suite is unchanged and still passes, which is the proof for each extraction. Full agent host suite after merging `main`: 6069 passing, 70 pending, 0 failing (`main` alone is 6037 passing).

## Known gaps, recorded in `chatContributions/TODO.md`

- The queued admission path does not attach GitHub references from a user message, while the direct path does. This predates the PR; it closes when turn admission is unified.
- Direct and queued admission now duplicate local command interception, title seeding, agent lookup, and telemetry setup. That duplication was previously hidden behind a bridge method; making it visible is deliberate, and `onIncomingRequest` removes it.

## Not done yet

- `onIncomingRequest` to unify turn admission, retire `sendTurnMessage`, and fold in the local command registry.
- Migrating the side chat (`/btw`) feature onto `contributeSend` plus `onHydrateTurns`, which should delete its per harness wiring in the Copilot and Claude agents and give Codex support by deletion.

## Merge status

`origin/main` is merged in. Upstream had changed `AgentHostTurnTracker.turnStarted` to take the agent object plus a trailing client id, and moved the tracker to `createInstance`; both call sites this PR created were updated, and the queued path passes its own sender client id.
