title: agentHost: fix legacy Copilot CLI migration issues (opening, worktrees, archived state)
body:
Follow-up to #331606, which migrates a legacy extension-host Copilot CLI session into the agent host when the user opens it. Migration succeeded on disk, but the session could then disappear from every list, silently reopen as legacy, or come
back unarchived.

Behind `chat.agentSessions.migrateLegacyCopilotCli` (experimental, default off). Sessions are untouched when it is disabled.

**Opening a migrated session no longer opens the legacy one.** Migration finishes just before the session is opened, so the migrated session had not always reached the sessions list yet. Opening then fell back to the legacy session it had just replaced — migration looked like it had done nothing, and the next open migrated it again.

**Worktree sessions now migrate correctly.** A worktree-isolated session was filtered out of the window opened on its own repository, so migrating it appeared to do nothing. A deleted worktree is also recreated on resume instead of failing, matching how native worktree sessions already behave.

**Sessions are no longer lost.** Migration claims the chat on disk, which is what makes the extension host stop listing it. If any later step failed, the session existed in no list at all. Sessions that cannot be migrated now stay on the legacy provider, and one that fails to restore reports an error like any other session.

**Archived state is preserved,** so migrating no longer resurfaces sessions the user had filed away.

**Diagnosability.** Adoption records why it did or did not migrate a session, in both logs and telemetry, so a migration that did nothing can be diagnosed from an agent host log instead of reproduced.

## Summary

Follow-up to #331794, which landed the chat pill path/URI hovers and centred the dropdown chevron with a `transform: translateY(1px)` nudge on `chevron-down`.

title: Add end-to-end trace logging for opening a session
body:
Opening a session runs through a long chain — the sessions list, the chat model load, an AHP round trip, the agent host''s session restore and its SQLite reads, the turn→history conversion, and finally the chat widget render. Most of that chain had no logging, so it was not possible to tell from a log file how long opening a session took or where the time went.

This adds `trace` markers along that whole path. Log lines are already timestamped, so no stopwatch code was added; each marker carries the session resource so one open can be followed end to end.

### Covered path

Both list entry points are covered:

- **Agents window** (`src/vs/sessions`): `SessionsService.openSession` → `ChatView.setChat`
- **Workbench chat sessions list**: `openSession` in `agentSessionsOpener.ts`

They funnel into the shared path:

`ChatService.loadRemoteSession` → `ChatSessionsService.getOrCreateChatSession` → `AgentHostSessionHandler.provideChatSessionContent` → AHP `subscribe` → `AgentService.subscribe` / `restoreSession` / `_restoreSessionState` / `_getChatMessages` → provider event read → back to the client's history→model conversion → `ChatWidget` first render.

### Notes

- Markers were added **only where none existed**. `ChatWidgetService.openSession` and `ChatViewPane.loadSession` were already instrumented and are untouched.
- `AgentService.subscribe` now reports whether the snapshot was served from memory or required a restore, which is the single biggest branch in the backend cost.
- `ChatWidget` logs the first render for a newly bound model once, tracked by session resource so a render triggered while the outgoing model unbinds cannot be misattributed and rapid switching cannot log the wrong session.
- The one non-log change is in `AgentService._getChatMessages`, where a nested `await` was split into two statements so the provider read can be bracketed; evaluation order is unchanged.

### Validation

- `tsc --project ./src/tsconfig.json --noEmit`
- `build/hygiene.ts` over the changed files
- `eslint` over the changed files

title: Fix chat math ResizeObserver loop warnings
body:
## Summary

Fixes the concentrated `ChatMarkdownContentPart.mathLayout` ResizeObserver warning by removing redundant nested observation and folding math scrollbar convergence into the existing chat row observer.

## Root cause

Late KaTeX font metric changes resize both the markdown content and its containing virtualized row. The nested math observer participates in the same delivery cycle as `ChatListItemRenderer.itemHeight`, producing skipped notifications:

```text
ResizeObserverLoopContext(
  ChatListItemRenderer.itemHeight,
  ChatMarkdownContentPart.mathLayout
)
```

Making the math observer callback a no-op still reproduced the warning, proving that `scanDomNode()` writes were not the cause. Removing the redundant nested observer eliminated it.

## Fix

- Math markdown parts register their scrollbar layout callbacks with the owning row.
- The existing row observer runs those callbacks synchronously before publishing the final row height.
- Registrations follow each markdown part's render lifecycle, including nested markdown in tool and confirmation parts.
- No animation-frame deferral or production timing change is introduced.

## Validation

- Real KaTeX/CSS Chromium fixture: 7 native warnings before, 0 after.
- Math overflow remains horizontally scrollable after asynchronous font metric changes.
- Existing chat ResizeObserver scenarios remain warning-free.
- Native warning positive control still emits and preserves observer context.
- `compile-client`
- 26 `ChatMarkdownContentPart` unit tests
- 6 targeted Playwright tests

Fixes #316501

title: Replay the user's prompt without the host's added context
body:
## Problem

Returning to an agent-host session shows context inside the user's own messages that they never typed, for example:

```
what's that smoke test for
No browser pages are currently shared with you.

1 page is open but not shared.
Use the 'open_browser_page' tool to open a new page or to help the user share an existing page.

Repository name: printstream-cloud
Owner: PrintStreamApp
Current branch: dev
```

The user typed only the first line. It appears only on returning to a session, never while the turn is live.

The same text also leaks into session titles, which are seeded from the first turn. That produces sessions permanently named things like "No browser pages are currently shared with you.  1 page is open but not shar…".

## Root cause

`resolvePromptToContentBlocks` deliberately sends a turn as several sibling text blocks: the prompt first, then the rendered attachment representations, then the `<system-reminder>` reference block.

```ts
const blocks: Anthropic.ContentBlockParam[] = [{ type: 'text', text: prompt }];
// ... feedbackBlocks, simpleBlocks, refLines appended as further text blocks
```

The live path is clean: the client dispatches `ChatTurnStarted` with the prompt as `message.text` and the context as separate attachments, and the reducer stores that verbatim. The flattening happens only on the way back, in the replay mapper:

```ts
return { kind: 'user-text', uuid: msg.uuid, text: textBlocks.map(b => b.text).join('\n'), timestamp };
```

Every text block is joined, so the host's own additions are returned as the user's words. Because `turnsToHistory` renders the restored request as `prompt: turn.message.text`, and the title controller seeds from the same text, both symptoms follow from that one line. This affects anything reconstructed from the transcript: session restore, `getMessages`, fork inheritance, and subagent transcripts.

## Fix

Take the first block, which is the prompt. The rest is host-composed and regenerated on every turn, so replaying it is wrong regardless of how it renders.

## Testing

Added a replay-mapper test that feeds a user envelope containing a prompt block plus an attachment-representation block plus a `<system-reminder>` reference block, and asserts the reconstructed turn's message is the prompt alone. Existing tests are unaffected: the helpers build single-block user messages, and the string-content path above this is untouched.

Verified against a real dev container session, where a turn whose typed prompt was one line came back with the browser-context block appended, and no longer does.

## Note on a sibling path

`codexPromptResolver.ts:106-117` merges the prompt and `modelRepresentation` into a single input item with `join('\n\n')` at send time rather than at replay, so the codex provider appears to have the same symptom with a different separator and an earlier origin. I have not touched it here since I cannot test that provider.

*AI disclosure: this comment and the related code were written with the assistance of AI.*

title: Default to an installed build, and report missing video tooling
body:
Three problems found running the `validate-ui-scenario` skill from a fresh checkout against [#244597](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/244597).

## Nothing ran without a target flag

With no flags the runner used the build from the checkout, which only exists after compiling the product. Verified on unmodified `main`: the documented starting point fails to launch.

```
Failed to launch Electron within 60000ms.
Original error: electronApplication.waitForEvent: Target page, context or browser has been closed
```

Reproducing a reported issue means running the shipped product anyway, so with no target flag the runner now finds an installed VS Code Insiders — falling back to Stable — and logs the choice:

```
No target given, using the installed build at C:\...\Microsoft VS Code Insiders. Pass --dev to run this checkout instead.
```

`--dev` selects the checkout build, and `--build <app-root>` still pins an exact install. Existing callers that pass `--build` are unaffected.

## A missing ffmpeg was only discovered after the run

Captions are rendered once the scenario finishes, so a missing ffmpeg surfaced as a raw `spawnSync ffprobe ENOENT` **after** VS Code had been driven and the report written — and it threw out of `runScenario`, so the run never printed its outcome.

The runner now checks before launching anything and names the fix for the platform:

```
Warning: ffmpeg and ffprobe not found on PATH, so the recording will not be captioned with step titles.
         The run still produces the raw video, screenshots, trace and report.
         To caption it, install ffmpeg (winget install Gyan.FFmpeg), make sure it is on PATH, and re-run,
         or annotate the finished run with: node test/scenario/out/renderEvidenceChapters.js <run-dir>
```

Caption rendering can no longer fail a run that has already produced its evidence, and the post-run message is actionable rather than an ENOENT stack.

## The window did not fill the recording

The recording canvas is 1920x1080, but VS Code sizes its own window — `DEFAULT_WORKSPACE_WINDOW_SIZE` is 1440x900 and `DEFAULT_EMPTY_WINDOW_SIZE` is 1200x800 — so the capture showed the window in the top-left corner of a larger frame, wasting about 30% of every pixel recorded.

Measured on the reporting machine:

| | |
|---|---|
| Window viewport | 1440 x 900 |
| Video canvas | 1920 x 1080 |
| Display work area | 1512 x 901 |

The window is now sized to the canvas once recording is enabled. The display being smaller than the canvas is fine — confirmed by probing before implementing: after `setBounds`, `innerWidth`/`innerHeight` report 1920x1080 and both the screenshot and the video come back full frame on a 1512x901 display. Sizing only happens when video recording is on, so non-recording smoke runs are untouched.

## Verification

Against installed Insiders on Windows, with the skill's own documented example:

- no flags, ffmpeg absent: warns up front, runs both steps, writes the report, warns again with the install command, exits `1` for the reproduced failure
- no flags, ffmpeg present: same run, plus `videos/annotated.mp4` at 1920x1300 (1080 of workbench + the caption band) with no dead space
- screenshots and raw recording are both 1920x1080, where they were 1440x900 inside a 1920x1080 frame before
- `--dev` still resolves the checkout build; it fails to launch here only because this checkout is not built, identically to unmodified `main`


## ffmpeg was installed, and still not found

A PATH edit only reaches processes started afterwards, so an editor that was already running never sees it. On the reporting machine ffmpeg was installed *and* present in the persisted user PATH, yet invisible to the shell the skill ran in — so the run produced no annotated video.

The runner now probes the usual install locations (winget `Links` and `Packages`, chocolatey, Program Files, Homebrew, `/usr/local/bin`) in addition to PATH. Verified with ffmpeg deliberately off PATH:

```
$ node test/scenario/out/runScenario.js .build/vscode-playwright-mcp/issue-250159.cjs
Captioned 2 steps into videos/annotated.mp4
```

No warning, no manual setup.

## Steps flowed past too quickly to read

A caption is only legible for as long as its step is on screen, and an asserting step can finish in a few hundred milliseconds. Each finished step is now held briefly — `stepPauseMs`, default `1000`, set `0` for timing-sensitive scenarios.

## Blocked steps are classified and reported

`skip` previously recorded only that a step did not run. It now takes `needs`:

| `needs` | Meaning | Consequence |
|---------|---------|-------------|
| `human` | A person is required — hardware, a judgement call, a sign-in that cannot be scripted | Reported so someone can check it by hand |
| `infrastructure` | Automatable, but the harness cannot do it yet | Reported as an enhancement request against the skill |

The distinction is recorded in `manifest.json`, highlighted in a **Needs attention** section of `report.html`, shown on the caption band, and printed at the end of the run:

```
  SKIP B-02 Verify the printed page matches [needs human]: Comparing physical print output requires a person with a printer.
Needs a person: B-02 Verify the printed page matches - Comparing physical print output requires a person with a printer.
Outcome: aborted
```

Both variants were exercised end to end; the caption band renders `SKIPPED - NEEDS HUMAN` in amber, later steps do not run, and the outcome is `aborted` rather than passed. `test/mcp` still compiles against the widened `EvidenceService.step` signature.

title: Defer breadcrumb reveal layout measurement
body:
## Summary

This change avoids a synchronous layout flush when the editor breadcrumbs are populated during startup.

- Defer non-focus breadcrumb reveals to the next animation-frame measurement phase.
- Cancel an obsolete pending reveal when another reveal or a focus change occurs.
- Keep focus-driven reveals synchronous so keyboard navigation behavior is unchanged.
- Reuse the measured `offsetLeft` value.
- Add a focused unit test for scheduling and cancellation behavior.

## Background

An overall profile-driven audit of the latest Insiders startup identified `BreadcrumbsWidget._reveal` as a stable renderer critical-path hotspot. Opening the restored editor populates the breadcrumb items and immediately reveals the last item. Reading `offsetLeft` directly after appending the breadcrumb DOM forces layout before startup can complete.

Across three warmed profiles, `_reveal` accounted for a median **11.8 ms** of CPU self-time between `code/didStartRenderer` and `code/didStartWorkbench`.

The reveal is visual bookkeeping rather than a prerequisite for constructing the workbench. Scheduling the measurement through the existing `dom.measure` read phase avoids blocking the synchronous editor-restore path while still updating the scroll position on the next frame.

## Measurements

Both variants were independently minified from the same source commit and overlaid onto the same Insiders runtime. The startup scenario restored one text editor in a deterministic folder with extensions and GPU acceleration disabled.

### Uninstrumented warm startup

30 per-start alternating pairs:

| Metric | Baseline | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Median total startup | 1401.0 ms | 1396.5 ms |
| Median paired difference |  | **-5.5 ms** |
| Bootstrap 95% interval |  | -13.5 ms to +6.5 ms |

The total-startup interval crosses zero, so this result alone is directional rather than statistically conclusive.

### Profiled renderer startup

Three measured warmed traces:

| Metric | Baseline | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `didStartRenderer` to `didStartWorkbench` | 1507.1 ms | 1498.0 ms (**-9.1 ms**) |
| `BreadcrumbsWidget._reveal` self-time | 11.8 ms | **0 ms** |

Trace instrumentation increases absolute startup time, but the targeted critical-path leaf was consistently present in every baseline trace and absent from every fix trace.

## Compatibility

- Keyboard and DOM-focus reveals remain immediate.
- Only non-focus programmatic reveals are deferred to the next measurement phase.
- Repeated reveals dispose the previous pending callback.
- The callback verifies that the target DOM node is still current before applying the scroll position.
- Disposal cancels any pending reveal.

## Validation

- `npm run compile-client`
- Targeted ESLint for the changed implementation and test
- Targeted Electron unit test for deferred reveal scheduling and focus cancellation

title: policy: gate Copilot on a fresh managed-settings fetch
body:
Makes `forceRemoteSettingsRefresh` a genuine fail-closed startup gate: when an enterprise sets it, VS Code fetches managed settings **fresh** before enabling Copilot agent functionality, and blocks rather than falling back to cached policy when that fetch fails.

Tracking: microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#8825

> [!NOTE]
> This replaces the two previous commits on this branch (a contract-only `managedSettingsFreshness.ts` state machine). That approach designed a general contract before it had a consumer; this is the behaviour itself, built on the pattern already in the codebase.

## Approach

VS Code already has a working fail-closed gate of exactly this shape — the HTTP 466 "client update required" path. This copies it rather than inventing a parallel mechanism:

| 466 gate | This gate |
| --- | --- |
| `managedSettingsCompatibilityError` on `IDefaultAccountService` | `managedSettingsRefreshBlocked` |
| `onDidChangeManagedSettingsCompatibilityError` | `onDidChangeManagedSettingsRefreshBlocked` |
| consumed in `AccountPolicyGateContribution.updatePolicyGateState()` | same method, same context key, same `setForceHidden` |

Sign-in stays reachable throughout, so a user can always recover.

`shouldForceRemoteSettingsRefresh()` (dead code since 661f18fdeb7 — it had no production caller) becomes `resolveForceRemoteSettingsRefresh()`, which additionally consults the **file** channel and reports the **winning channel**. It returns `undefined` when no channel sets the key, so an explicit managed `false` is distinguishable from an absent value.

## Behaviour worth reviewing

**A fresh 404 satisfies the requirement.** It means "no policy file configured". Blocking on it would permanently lock out every org that has no policy file.

**The requirement outlives the policy cache.** The cache is honoured for one hour and a failed fetch returns `managedSettings: undefined` — dropping the restrictions *and the flag itself*. A naive sticky gate would silently reopen after an hour offline, so the requirement is persisted separately under `defaultAccount.managedSettingsRefreshRequired`.

**Scope follows the delivery channel.** The server delivers the control per organization, so it is recorded **per account** — one account's response must never speak for another's. Native MDM and the on-disk file are machine-wide and read **live** on every evaluation, so precedence is applied when the requirement is *read* (which is what lets a native MDM `false` override a server `true`). A machine-wide `local` hint covers only the startup window in which those channels are still loading.

Because the local channels are read live rather than behind an authenticated fetch, **a signed-out machine carrying an MDM- or file-delivered flag is gated on first launch** — one of the gaps called out during planning.

**Migration.** The flag already lives in users' cached server bags today, so a requirement recorded by a previous build is recovered from there on first run; without it, every flagged org would get one ungated offline launch on upgrade.

**Retries are throttled** (60s), because a refresh fires on every window focus and an offline client would otherwise issue a request per alt-tab. Skipping a retry inside the window never reopens the gate.

## Behaviour change to confirm ⚠️

The managed-settings fetch is now **restricted to the evaluated account's sessions**. `request()` otherwise falls through to the next session on 401/404, which is a cross-*account* fallback: another organization could answer for your account, and its settings were merged and cached under your account.

This fixes a permanent-lockout path (MDM sets the flag → server 404s for account A → account B always answers first → A's satisfying 404 is discarded and A is gated forever). But it is **not bit-identical for unflagged users**: in a multi-account setup with an expired primary token, VS Code today fetches managed settings with a different account's token and applies that org's policy to you. I judged "more correct" beats "bit-identical" here, but it deserves an explicit ack.

## Inertness

The feature is inert when the flag isn't set — that's essentially all users — and this is asserted, not assumed:

- `no fetch is blocked when the refresh flag is not set anywhere` — an unflagged org is never gated, even with the endpoint down
- `a failed fetch never escalates from another account cached settings` — the policy cache is never consulted for gate decisions, so an unflagged user cannot be blocked by a polluted cache

## Scope

Not included, deliberately:

- **No HTTP header work.** The request already sends `cache-control: no-cache`; the transport is `fetch` and `disableCache: true` is already passed.
- **No schema validation.** The Copilot runtime owns the managed-settings schema; duplicating it here is forbidden by `.github/skills/policy-and-managed-settings`.
- **No telemetry or diagnostics** until the behaviour itself is settled.
- **Renderer-side gating only.** Remote/SSH/tunnel Agent Hosts are not gated: the managed-settings channel to them intentionally does not exist (`remoteAgentHostProtocolClient.ts` sends `{}` to non-local hosts).

## Validation

- 28 tests in `defaultAccount.test.ts` and 2 in `accountPolicyGateContribution.test.ts`, covering first launch, cached flag, MDM/file-delivered flag, explicit managed `false`, successful refresh, each failure class, account switching, migration and retry throttling
- 178 passing across the affected policy/accounts/agentHost suites
- `npm run typecheck-client`, `npm run valid-layers-check`, eslint — all clean

Tests were run directly under mocha: this environment can't build the native modules the Electron harness needs (`npm install` fails on an authenticated NuGet feed with a 401, unrelated to this change), so please let CI confirm.

This change went through seven rounds of adversarial review, which surfaced eleven fail-*open* paths in a gate whose only job is to fail closed — several only becoming visible once an earlier fix was in place. The tests named above encode each of them.

inline chat: add experimental Agent Host backend

Adds an Agent Host backend for editor inline chat. The setting
`chat.inlineChat.agentHost.enabled` controls it and is off by default. When the setting is
off, inline chat operates as before.

The Agent Host writes files to disk. It does not stream edits into the editor. Inline chat
therefore builds its review UI from before/after snapshots.

- Adds `InlineChatSessionResolver`. It selects the Agent Host session or the legacy local
  session. It falls back to the legacy session on failure. It does not fall back when the
  user cancels.
- Extracts `IChatEditReviewSession` as a supertype of `IChatEditingSession`. A surface can
  supply reviewable entries without checkpoints, storage, streaming edits, or multi-diff.
  Editor review UI, such as decorations and keep/undo, continues to operate.
- Adds `InlineChatEditReviewSession`. It saves and snapshots the target file, makes the file
  read-only for the turn, and reuses `ChatEditingModifiedDocumentEntry`. Diff decorations and
  hunk review operate without new diff code.
- Shows diff decorations in real time. Each turn starts and stops external-edit mode, so disk
  reloads count as agent edits. The diff stays cumulative across turns.
- Tracks the files that the agent edits outside the target file. The Agent Host announces each
  edit when a tool call completes. The baseline content comes from that edit.
- Lets `IFilesConfigurationService.updateReadonly` accept an `IMarkdownString`. A programmatic
  lock can then show its own reason.
- Shows the current agent operation in the inline input placeholder.
- Keeps notebooks and untitled documents on the legacy path.

Makes throwaway (ephemeral) sessions start and run more quickly:

- Disables MCP servers, subagents, and custom agents for these sessions.
- Skips the turn-start checkpoint. This work is on the critical path of each turn.
- Skips title generation and the rename instruction. The title is never shown.
- Adds `enabledForEphemeralSessions` to server tool definitions. A tool must opt in before an
  ephemeral session receives it.

Also keeps throwaway sessions out of the session lists. The host no longer sends
`root/sessionAdded` for an ephemeral session. The chat history index no longer stores an
external session from a transient surface.

title: Complete a background subagent that settles after its turn
body:
## Problem

A subagent spawned in the background keeps its row spinning for the rest of the session even though it finished, and its entry is never evicted from the subagent registry.

## Root cause

`ClaudeSdkPipeline` derives the turn id for every SDK message from the prompt queue head:

```ts
const parent = this._queue.peekParent();
const turnId = parent?.turnId;
```

and `ClaudeSdkMessageRouter.handle` returns early when there is none, so once the queue drains every message is dropped before reaching the mapper. A background subagent settles after the turn that spawned it has ended, which is precisely when the queue is empty, so its `system.task_notification` never becomes a `subagent_completed` signal.

This contradicts the contract `SubagentRegistry` documents for itself, that background spawns survive across turns by design because their completion arrives later via `system.task_notification`. The foreground path is unaffected, since its `tool_result` arrives inside the turn.

## Fix

Route the subagent system messages when there is no turn. They carry their own chat and tool call id, so they never needed one, and `completeSubagentSession` resolves the turn on the subagent's own chat rather than the parent's, so it works while the parent is idle. Turn-scoped messages are still dropped exactly as before. The mapping is pulled into a small helper so both paths share the existing swallow-and-log behaviour.

## Testing

Added a router test that records a background spawn, delivers a terminal `task_notification` with no turn id, and asserts a `subagent_completed` signal is produced and the spawn is evicted. The existing turn-less assertion is kept, narrowed to the turn-scoped message it actually covers. I could not find existing coverage for a background subagent completing while the parent is idle, and the e2e subagent suite has no background case at all.

title: Resolve agent host file paths against the window's remote
body:
## Problem

In a remote window (a dev container, for example) every file link, image, attachment and diff the agent host produces resolves against the client's own disk instead of the workspace. Clicking a `Read [file]` row opens nothing and images never load. Because the URI is treated as client-local, a POSIX host path even renders with client separators, so `/workspace/a.ts` shows as `\workspace\a.ts` on Windows.

## Root cause

`toAgentHostUri` hands `file:` URIs through untouched for the in-process host:

```ts
if (connectionAuthority === 'local' && originalUri.scheme === Schemas.file) {
	return originalUri;
}
```

That is correct only while the invariant stated on `LOCAL_AGENT_HOST_AUTHORITY` holds, that the host "always runs on the same machine ... as the client". `AgentHostContribution` registers the in-process host with that authority unconditionally, but in a remote window the host runs on the remote machine. One fast path feeds roughly thirty `toAgentHostUri` call sites, which is why the entire surface fails together rather than a single content type.

## Fix

Let the authority name whose filesystem the paths are on. A local window keeps `local` and its existing pass-through. A remote window uses `local+<remoteAuthority>`, which `toAgentHostUri` rebases onto `vscode-remote:`.

Rebasing rather than wrapping is what makes images work. `FileAccess.uriToBrowserUri` rewrites `vscode-remote` through `RemoteAuthorities` into a URL the browser can load and turns `file:` into `vscode-file:`, but leaves `vscode-agent-host:` alone. Wrapping would fix the links and leave the images broken. Rebasing also opens the same editor the explorer already uses instead of a second one backed by the agent host filesystem provider.

Host URIs that are not files still wrap as before, and a remote agent host is unaffected.

## Testing

Added coverage in `agentHostFileSystemProvider.test.ts` for the local pass-through, the remote-window rebase, non-file URIs still wrapping in a remote window, and a remote agent host being unaffected by the encoding. Verified against a dev container, where the invocation message the host sends is `Read [MarketingHomePage.tsx](file:///workspace/...)` and the client now resolves it to `vscode-remote://dev-container%2B.../workspace/...`.

title: Move the scenario runner out of the MCP server
body:
Follow-up to #331674, and a prerequisite for deleting the VS Code automation MCP server.

## Why

The `validate-ui-scenario` skill runs `runScenario`, which drives VS Code through `test/automation` and writes an evidence bundle (video, per-step screenshots, trace, `manifest.json`, `report.html`).

**None of that is MCP.** Verified by hooking `Module.require` and loading the runner:

```
MCP SDK modules loaded by runScenario: NONE
```

The `McpServer` import it inherited is used only in type positions, so TypeScript already elides it — compiled `evidence.js` requires just `fs`, `path`, `zod` and `./application`. The runner lived under `test/mcp` only because that is where the evidence pipeline was first written.

That matters now that deleting the MCP server is on the table: today `rm -rf test/mcp` would silently take the skill with it.

## What

Six files with no MCP dependency move to a new `test/scenario` package:

| | |
|---|---|
| `runScenario.ts` | scenario entry point |
| `application.ts` | launch + isolated profile |
| `evidence.ts` | manifest, report, screenshots, video |
| `renderEvidenceChapters.ts` | caption band |
| `utils.ts`, `options.ts` | helpers |

`test/mcp` becomes a consumer of that package, alongside the skill. The MCP evidence tools move to `test/mcp/src/evidenceTools.ts`, where the server-specific zod schemas belong. **Deleting `test/mcp` now removes only MCP code.**

The new package emits declarations, matching `test/automation` — without that the MCP server would have compiled against an untyped module and silently degraded to `any`.

## The step banner goes too

`showOverlay` appended a banner to the DOM of the product under test, which can shift layout and influence focus or selectors, so the runner always opted out with `VSCODE_EVIDENCE_CLEAN_CAPTURE=1`. With the runner as the only remaining caller that opinion is unanimous, so the overlay and its opt-out both go and the capture is unconditionally faithful. Step titles are still rendered onto the finished recording by `renderEvidenceChapters`.

## Verification

- `test/scenario` and `test/mcp` both compile from clean, with types flowing across the boundary
- the skill's documented example runs end to end against installed Insiders from the new path, and still reproduces [#250159](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/250159) with a captioned video and a full evidence bundle
- the MCP server still starts over stdio and lists its tools (4 at rest — the rest stay disabled until an app is running, unchanged)
- eslint passes, and the new `test/scenario/**` import boundary was confirmed active by probing it with a deliberately forbidden import rather than trusting a clean run

## Not included

`.build/vscode-playwright-mcp/` keeps its name. It is generated output shared with the MCP server today, and renaming it would invalidate paths documented in a skill that shipped this week — better as a follow-up once the server is actually gone.

title: Persist state between profiled startup runs
body:
## Problem

Desktop startup profiling writes its timing output and then calls `nativeHostService.exit(0)`. This intentionally avoids waiting for a complete application shutdown, but it also bypasses the normal shutdown storage flush.

That makes repeated profiler runs less representative of a normal clean warm start. State normally persisted during shutdown is absent from the next run.

One confirmed example is the editor font measurement cache:

- Current profiler behavior: no `editorFontInfo` entry after the run
- With this change: `editorFontInfo` is persisted after the warmup

Without the persisted entry, the next profiler run repeats synchronous DOM character-width measurement instead of restoring the cached font metrics. CPU traces confirmed that `DomCharWidthReader._readFromDomElements` is present in every current profiler run and absent after a persisted warmup.

This is a performance-infrastructure accuracy issue. Normal VS Code shutdown already flushes the same state; this does not change normal user startup or shutdown behavior.

## Change

After startup timers, duration markers, heap statistics, and output files have been completed:

1. Flush the workbench storage service with `WillSaveStateReason.SHUTDOWN`.
2. Wait up to five seconds for persistence.
3. Preserve the existing hard process exit in a nested `finally`.
4. Exit nonzero if the flush rejects or times out.

The flush happens after all measured values are collected and written, so storage persistence is not included in the reported startup interval. It only extends the unmeasured process lifetime after results are available.

## Measurement accuracy

This makes repeated profiler runs use the same persisted state that follows a normal clean VS Code shutdown.

Verified behavior:

| State/behavior | Current profiler | With change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `editorFontInfo` after warmup | Missing | Persisted |
| Next-run DOM font measurement | Repeated | Restored from cache |
| Flush failure/timeout | Not applicable | Logged and reported through nonzero exit |

The nonzero exit is important: if persistence fails, the performance harness must reject the run rather than silently accepting a following run with unexpectedly cold state.

The flush also emits the standard shutdown save event, so other components participating in normal shutdown persistence can provide representative warm state to subsequent measurements.

## Scope / lack of product behavior changes

- The new code only runs when startup profiling output or duration markers were requested.
- Regular VS Code windows return before entering this profiling path.
- Normal product startup remains unchanged.
- Normal product shutdown remains unchanged.
- Reported timer and marker values are captured before the flush.
- Existing hard-exit behavior remains, including on flush failure.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run transpile-client`
- Repeated source profiler runs completed successfully.
- Repeated fully bundled profiler runs completed successfully.
- SQLite inspection verified `editorFontInfo` is persisted only with the fix.
- Warmed CPU inspection verified the unwanted font DOM measurement is absent after persistence.
- Flush timeout is bounded to five seconds.
- Flush rejection/timeout exits nonzero so the harness cannot accept inaccurate warm-state measurements.
- Independent implementation and final diff reviews found no significant correctness issue.

title: Read chat responses aloud
body:
This PR makes it possible to read chat messages aloud.


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dec3ff3b-5d1e-4b61-9a33-c319d2f9b53c



## How it works

```
click Read Aloud
      │
      ▼
take the response text     ── the answer, not the step narration
      │
      ▼
clean it up                ── strip emoji, strip markdown,
      │                       punctuate so it pauses between blocks
      ▼
split into pieces          ── first piece short, so sound starts fast
      │
      ▼
POST SSML to the speech service
      │
      ▼
play (24 kHz) while the next piece is already being fetched
```

## ⚠️ Authentication is the one open piece

**There is no product endpoint for verbatim synthesis yet, so this cannot ship as-is.** Opening as a draft for that reason.

The voice backend VS Code already talks to (`voiceWsUrl`) does not expose plain synthesis — `request_narration` runs the text through an LLM narrator first, so the text is rewritten rather than read.

**So this PR calls the Azure Speech endpoint directly** — currently `https://eastus2.tts.speech.microsoft.com` with `en-US-Harper:MAI-Voice-2` — supplied by the user as a setting, with the key in `ISecretStorageService`.

@accnops has confirmed a verbatim HTTP endpoint looks feasible. When it lands, only `maiSpeechCredentials.ts` changes: the endpoint moves to `product.json`, auth becomes the identity the user already signed in with, and the setup step disappears. The engine never sees a key — it asks the credentials service for `{ endpoint, credential }` and does not care where they came from.

## Trying it today

1. Run **`Speech: Set Up Read Aloud`** → endpoint (URL-validated) → key (masked input)
2. Click **Read Aloud** on any chat response

The engine becomes available immediately — no reload. With nothing configured, reading falls back to the speech synthesizer of the platform.

## Testing

`198` targeted tests, `5,475` across the broader chat / markdown / speech / accessibility sweep. Typecheck, eslint and layer checks pass. No dependencies added — `package.json` and `package-lock.json` are unchanged.

Verified end to end in Code OSS: the engine switches the moment the key is set without a reload, an unconfigured install falls back to the platform voice, markdown and emoji are stripped, and code blocks are separated from the text that follows.

title: Bound concurrency of prompt file discovery reads
body:
Fixes #331853

Agent, slash command and hook discovery each fan out over every discovered prompt file with an unbounded `Promise.all`, and each iteration reads the file through `parseNew` → `fileService.readFile`. Every file is therefore opened at once.

Because a discovery pass can be re-triggered before the previous one settles (`CachedPromise` clears its cached promise on invalidation without cancelling the in-flight computation), several full passes can be in flight simultaneously. On profiles with large agent-plugin/skill collections this exhausts the process file handle limit: the main process reached ~150k pending libuv filesystem requests and ~9.5k handles, after which unrelated reads failed with `EMFILE` — including `settings.json`, `mcp.json` and chat session writes — and the pty host and extension hosts stopped responding. This reproduces with no folder open, since the files involved are global.

This change routes the three unbounded sites through a `Limiter`:

- `computeSlashCommandDiscoveryInfo`
- `computeAgentDiscoveryInfo`
- `computeHooks`

`computeSkillDiscoveryInfo` and `getInstructionsDiscoveryInfo` in the same file already iterate sequentially and are unchanged.

Bounding discovery concurrency with `Limiter` is already the established pattern in this codebase — it is used 35+ times under `src/vs/platform`, including for comparable discovery work in `agentService.ts` (`new Limiter<boolean>(4)`). The limit is set high enough that typical installations (a handful of files) behave exactly as before, while keeping the worst case bounded.

This PR intentionally addresses only the unbounded fan-out. The non-cancelling invalidation in `CachedPromise` changes cancellation semantics and is better reviewed separately.

### Test

Adds a unit test asserting that agent discovery never exceeds the configured concurrency while still reading files in parallel.

title: Add experiment driven inline model feedback survey
body:
Adds an inline feedback survey that can be attached to chat responses through an experiment treatment, so a survey can be authored, changed, or retired without shipping code.

When a survey applies to a response, a combined thumbs up and down control replaces the usual helpful and unhelpful actions in the footer. Pressing it opens a short multi step survey underneath, and pressing it again closes it.

### How a survey is configured

Everything comes from a versioned JSON payload delivered as the `chatModelFeedbackSurvey` treatment:

```jsonc
{
  "version": 1,
  "id": "auto-routing-2026-08",
  "match": { "selectedModels": ["auto"] },
  "prompt": {
    "cooldownDays": 7,
    "maxPerSession": 1,
    "chance": { "initial": 0.05, "increment": 0.05, "max": 0.5 },
    "triggers": { "modelSwitchedAway": { "enabled": true, "bypassCooldown": true } }
  },
  "steps": [
    { "kind": "choice", "id": "routing", "title": "Did Auto choose the right model for the job?",
      "options": [ { "id": "yes", "label": "Yes" }, { "id": "too-heavy", "label": "No - too heavy" } ] },
    { "kind": "text", "id": "comments", "title": "Anything else you'd like to share? (optional)",
      "placeholder": "Optional feedback", "maxLength": 1000 }
  ]
}
```

A malformed payload is rejected whole rather than in part, since dropping one bad step would quietly change what the experiment measures. An omitted `prompt` block gives a manual only survey, so a config that forgets to describe its pacing under prompts rather than nags.

Model identifiers are not qualified the same way across harnesses. The language model service uses `<vendor>/<group>/<id>` while agent host sessions use `<sessionType>:<id>`, so a selector is matched against each segment as well as the whole id. That lets `auto` match both `copilot/auto` and `agent-host-copilotcli:auto`.

### Manual and automatic surfacing are separate

Manual activation is never rate limited, because the pacing rules exist only to pace surveys the user did not ask for. Those rules cover a weekly cooldown, a per session cap, a probability that ramps with each response that passes without prompting, and a trigger for switching off the surveyed model.

Only the newest response offers a survey, and only one is open at a time, so history never fills with stale controls. A survey the user is part way through is never pulled away by a newer response or an automatic prompt.

### Telemetry

Answers are reported as each step is taken, so surveys the user abandons still produce data. Events reach GitHub restricted telemetry through a command the Copilot extension registers; a command is used rather than a data channel because invoking it activates the extension, so results produced before activation are not dropped. Free text only ever reaches the restricted sink, and nothing is sent when `telemetry.feedback.enabled` is off or telemetry is disabled.

Core already has a sender for the same table in `agentHostRestrictedTelemetry.ts` using the same ingestion key, but it is node layer inside the agent host process with no channel to the renderer. Exposing it would let this forwarder and the existing `GithubTelemetryForwardingContrib` both go away; that is worth a follow up.

### Accessibility

The panel is a card with a listbox of options, matching the ask question tool. Arrow keys, Home, End, Enter, and Space move and pick, and the widget stops those keys from also reaching the chat list. Escape dismisses. Focus moves into the survey only when the user asked for it, and returns to the feedback control when the panel closes. The active option carries `aria-selected` so screen readers announce what will be submitted.

### Notes for review

- `isLast` was added to `IChatResponseViewModel`. The getter already existed on the single implementer.
- `ToolBar.focus` now forwards an optional index, which `ActionBar.focus` already accepted.

### Testing

46 tests covering config validation and matching, prompt pacing, the manual and automatic paths, state lifecycle across the virtualized list, keyboard and ARIA behaviour, and the telemetry contract. The full chat suite passes at 3242.

title: Let the setup banner reload an agent's configuration
body:
Follow-up to #331739. Four changes to the **no account** state of the Agent SDK setup banner.

### Before / after

> **Choose how you want to use Claude.**
> ~~Sign in to GitHub to use GitHub Copilot models, or read the setup instructions for other ways to set up Claude.~~
> **Sign in to GitHub to use GitHub Copilot models or [reload the configuration]() if you have set up Claude elsewhere. For other ways to set up Claude, [learn more]() on their docs.**

And the richest variant, an agent that declares an in-app sign-in as well:

> **Choose how you want to use Codex.**
> **Sign in to GitHub to use GitHub Copilot models, sign in to ChatGPT to use your ChatGPT subscription, or [reload the configuration]() if you have set up Codex elsewhere. For other ways to set up Codex, [learn more]() on their docs.**

1. **"read the setup instructions" → "learn more"**, and it is a link rather than a run of plain text.
2. **The docs button goes away.** Docs were the one route with both a button and a mention in the copy; now they are only the link inside the sentence that already explains them.
3. **A "reload the configuration" link.**
4. **Claude's docs URL** moves from the generic setup page to [third-party integrations](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/third-party-integrations), which is what "other ways to set up Claude" means in this banner: Console, Bedrock, Claude Platform on AWS, Vertex, Foundry, Teams and Enterprise.

### Why reload exists

Setup finished outside the app — `claude login` in a terminal, an exported key — produces no signal the app can observe. Until something else happened to re-trigger discovery, the banner went on asking a user to sign in to something they had already signed in to. This restores the recheck behaviour an earlier iteration had and dropped.

The re-look is the tail of a download promoted to its own gesture: restart chat discovery (it defers itself while there is no SDK to read the catalog from), *then* refresh models — in that order, because the refresh is what asks the SDK about the account, and announcing `ready` ahead of it would show "no account found" to a user who has one for as long as enumeration takes.

### Shape

`AgentSdkSetupChannel` grows a **second request key**, not per-agent code, so agent #3 still needs no edit here. One consumed nonce *per key* (`Map<string, string>`), cleared as it is claimed, so pressing the same link twice is two requests. Reload deliberately does not join `_pendingRequests` — that set gates the download offer, and a reload happens in a state where there is nothing to offer.

The `noAccount` copy stays at four whole sentences-per-combination rather than doubling to eight: reload is unconditional, so it adds no branches, and no localized string is assembled from fragments (a translator reorders clauses freely). Within each variant the sign-in routes and reload share one "or" list, ordered by how prominently the same routes are offered as buttons: GitHub leads the sentence and is the primary button, the provider sign-in is second in both, and reload closes the list as a link. Docs then trail in their own sentence, as the one route that leaves the app — and as their own sentence rather than a trailing clause, which would have put them under the "if you have set up Claude elsewhere" conditional.

Both links are `command:` hrefs rather than raw `https:` ones, built through `createCommandUri`, so each takes the same route a button would — funnel step recorded, and for docs the agent-declared URL validated through `openerService`. The markdown is trusted for exactly those two commands, and the two proper nouns the host supplies (`displayName`, `signInProviderName`) are escaped before interpolation, so neither can synthesize a third link into either of them.

### Verification

Banner suite (30), channel suites (18), and a broad agent-host sweep (5348 passing / 71 pending / 0 failing) are green, as is `test-agent-host-e2e` in replay mode (157 passing / 15 pending, all four suites PASS). The Claude, Codex and setup suites were re-run together after the copy rewrite and the URL change: 440 passing, 0 failing.

Checked live in a signed-out window: both the Claude and the Codex variant render with the copy above, both links as real anchors. Clicking reload logs `[AgentSdkSetup] claude: reloading the agent's configuration at the user's request` and records `step: "reloadClicked"`, only the addressed agent claims it, and a second press lands as a second request. That live reload check predates the copy rewrite, which did not touch the route it exercises.

title: Add proposed TreeView.clearSelection API
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please: -->
This adds a `TreeView.clearSelection()` method behind a new `treeViewClearSelection` API proposal.

Refs #48754

### Why

`TreeView.reveal(element, { select: true })` selects an element, but there is no way to undo it: `TreeView.selection` is read-only, and the selection survives refreshes because the tree tracks it by tree item handle.

This matters for any view that mirrors state owned by something else (an active editor, a running process, a cursor position). When that state stops corresponding to an element in the tree, the view keeps advertising a selection that is no longer true. VS Code's own explorer does not have this problem — open a file outside the workspace folders and it simply shows nothing selected.

The workaround extensions use today is to change `TreeItem.id` for the affected rows so the old handles stop resolving and the tree drops the selection along with the focus trait. It works, but it has real costs:

- it needs a full `onDidChangeTreeData` refresh for what is purely a UI change, so the view visibly re-renders;
- `TreeItem.id` becomes unstable, so anything else keyed off it needs to be kept on a separate identity;
- providers end up carrying a generation counter per row plus the bookkeeping to expire those counters.

Given #48754 has been open for a while and the id-rewriting trick keeps being rediscovered, a small explicit API seemed worth proposing.

### What

```ts
export interface TreeView<T> extends Disposable {
	clearSelection(): void;
}
```

- Forwards to the existing internal `ITreeView.setSelection([])`, which is already used by `$reveal`.
- Leaves the focused element alone — only the selection is cleared.
- Unlike `reveal`, it does **not** open the view. Clearing a selection is not a request for the user's attention, and a view that was never created has no selection to clear.
- Deliberately kept separate from the `treeViewReveal` proposal: `reveal(undefined)` there means "show an empty tree view" (#90005), which is a different operation and still under discussion. Overloading it further did not seem helpful.

### Tests

- `mainThreadTreeViews.test.ts`: the empty selection reaches the tree view, the view is not opened, and an unknown view id is a no-op.
- `vscode-api-tests`: exercises the API surface and the round trip to the main thread.

I could not run the integration test suite in my environment (no display), so the `vscode-api-tests` addition is only verified as far as compiling and the API being reachable — worth a CI run.

Happy to adjust the name, the shape, or drop the "does not open the view" behaviour if you'd rather it match `reveal`.

title: Avoid forced layout when measuring the Chat view title
body:
## Background

This change comes from a Windows startup performance investigation across published Insiders builds and subsequent packaged CPU profiling.

A warmed renderer profile showed repeated synchronous calls to `ChatViewTitleControl.getHeight()` consuming about 20-30 ms during startup. `getHeight()` read `titleContainer.offsetHeight`, which could force Blink style/layout after the title or its toolbars changed.

Observed startup caller paths included:

```text
ChatViewTitleControl.getHeight
<- ChatViewTitleControl.updateTitle
<- ChatViewTitleControl.doUpdate
<- ChatViewTitleControl.update
<- ChatViewPane.showModel
```

and:

```text
ChatViewTitleControl.getHeight
<- ChatViewPane.layoutChatAndSessions
<- ChatViewPane.doLayoutBody
<- ViewPane layout
```

The title height is dynamic, but the browser already exposes that state asynchronously and before paint through `ResizeObserver`.

## Change

- Observe the Chat title container's border-box height.
- Cache the most recently reported height.
- Fire the existing `onDidChangeHeight` event only when the observed height changes.
- Return the cached value from `getHeight()` instead of reading `offsetHeight`.
- Keep the existing `ChatViewPane` relayout path, which applies the final observed size before paint.
- Make the observer factory injectable so unit tests use a real-interface fake instead of replacing the global `ResizeObserver`.

There is no intended visual or accessibility change.

## Startup improvement

Focused warmed CPU traces:

| Metric | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `ChatViewTitleControl.getHeight` self-time | 29.5 ms | **0 ms** |

End-to-end validation used fully bundled current-source Windows desktop applications with identical Electron, resources, extensions, minification, and NLS processing. The applications differed only by this change.

Two independent campaigns ran 30 interleaved measured pairs each, alternating A/B and B/A order after three warmups.

| Campaign | Median startup change | Bootstrap 95% interval |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| First 30 pairs | -9.5 ms | -27.5 ms to +4.0 ms |
| Repeat 30 pairs | -11.5 ms | -19.5 ms to -1.0 ms |
| Combined 60 pairs | **-11.5 ms** | **-19.0 ms to -1.0 ms** |

The conservative end-to-end startup gain is **11.5 ms** on this Windows host.

Repeated phase improvements across both campaigns:

| Startup phase | Combined paired change | Bootstrap 95% interval |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Restore primary viewlet | **-13.0 ms** | -14.0 ms to -11.0 ms |
| Restore auxiliary bar | **-13.0 ms** | -14.0 ms to -11.0 ms |
| Workbench create/restore | **-5.0 ms** | -8.0 ms to -3.0 ms |
| Restore editors | **-4.0 ms** | -8.0 ms to -1.0 ms |
| Renderer start to workbench ready | -7.0 ms | -11.0 ms to 0.0 ms |

The phase measurements overlap and should not be summed.

## Improvements to other scenarios

The removed forced layout was not startup-specific. The same code runs when:

- A Chat model is shown or switched.
- A session title/custom title changes.
- A request updates a title.
- Chat view actions or navigation controls change size.
- Chat is restored in the primary sidebar.
- Chat is restored in the auxiliary bar.
- The containing pane is resized or moved between view locations.

These paths now consume the cached browser-reported height instead of synchronously flushing style/layout. `ResizeObserver` continues to trigger the existing relayout event whenever the real border-box height changes.

The measured 13 ms improvements in both primary viewlet and auxiliary-bar restoration demonstrate that the gain applies across multiple Chat view locations.

## Compatibility and behavior

- The title remains dynamically sized.
- Visibility changes are reflected by the observer, including a height of zero.
- Duplicate height notifications do not trigger redundant relayouts.
- Final layout is applied before paint through the existing `onDidChangeHeight` listener.
- The observer is disconnected with the control's disposables.
- The observed element belongs to the same window as the Chat view, so auxiliary-window behavior is unchanged.
- Keyboard navigation, ARIA state, labels, and focus behavior are unchanged.

The focused test verifies:

1. An observed height updates `getHeight()`.
2. The existing height-change event fires.
3. Repeating the same height does not fire another event.
4. Observing zero updates the cache and fires the second real change.

## Validation

```text
npm run typecheck-client
npm run transpile-client
scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\widgetHosts\viewPane\chatViewTitleControl.test.ts --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\widget\chatWidget.test.ts
```

- Client typecheck passed.
- Client transpilation passed.
- 16 focused Chat tests passed.
- Production desktop baseline/fix bundles succeeded.
- Packaged startup succeeded.
- Two independent correctness/diff reviews found no significant issue.

## Rejected alternatives

- Coalescing title-bar overflow checks did not reduce the targeted CPU or forced-layout cost.
- Replacing toolbar `getBoundingClientRect()` reads with cached observer width removed that leaf but did not improve packaged startup over 30 interleaved pairs.

title: agentHost: stop the agent editing host-created attachment snapshots (#331154)
body:
## What

When a user-message attachment is **not** a plain, already-existing `file://` file — pasted content, an unsaved editor, or a read-only `git:` diff — the Agent Host snapshots the bytes to `…/agentSessionData/<session>/attachments/…` and handed the copy to the model as an ordinary **editable** file. The model then edited the throwaway copy instead of returning the transformed content / editing the real file. This is the uncovered sibling of #319314 (the #319452 fix only exempted existing `file://` attachments).

This PR keeps each snapshot **visible** (path preserved so the model can read it) but signals it **read-only** so the agent doesn't edit it.

## How

- **Tag** every host-created snapshot with a `_meta` marker (new `agentSnapshotAttachmentMeta`) — at the snapshot-write point and when a snapshot copy is re-attached from the attachments folder. `isHostSnapshotAttachment` is the shared discriminator.
- **Copilot** → send the snapshot as `{ type: 'file', path }` with a **plain** display name; deliver a read-only note via the existing `additionalContext` channel (rendered by the runtime as a `<system_reminder>`) on the main turn. Steering doesn't fire the `user-prompt-submitted` hook, so its note is appended to the steering prompt as a `<reminder>` block (stripped from the bubble, forwarded to the model).
- **Codex** → annotate the existing `@path` mention with `(read-only snapshot — do not edit this file)`.
- **Claude** → annotate the existing `<system-reminder>` path line likewise.
- **Write-deny backstop** → when a provider raises an interactive confirmation for a write under the session attachments dir, the host hard-denies it before auto-approval (`isForbiddenSnapshotWrite` + `_handleToolReady`).

## Why the Copilot approach differs

The runtime **drops a file attachment's `displayName` for text snapshots** (a text file is rendered only as a path line in `<tagged_files>`), so the read-only marker can't ride the attachment for Copilot — it has to travel in the prompt/context. The `additionalContext` channel is the existing host→model context mechanism and is not shown in the user's chat bubble.

## Reviewer notes / known limitation

The write-deny only fires on an **interactive** permission prompt. In autopilot/bypass modes the provider auto-approves upstream without a host callback (Copilot "Allow All" → SDK mode `on`; Claude `acceptEdits`/`bypassPermissions`/`auto` + subagents; Codex never routes tool calls through the host permission layer), so there the read-only signal is **advisory only**. A mode- and provider-independent guarantee — marking snapshots **read-only on disk** (`chmod 0444`) at write time — is left as a follow-up (needs cross-platform validation and session-cleanup handling).

Deferred non-goal ("Problem B"): mapping a `git:` diff back to the real workspace file so "edit this" edits the real file.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck-client` + `npm run transpile-client`: green.
- agentHost unit suites (agentService, copilotAgentSession, sessionPermissions, codex/codexPromptResolver, claude/claudePromptResolver): **693 passing, 0 failing**.
- eslint on all changed files: clean.

Fixes #331154

title: Dismiss a submenu only when the parent menu actually scrolled
body:
Fixes #331838

On a touch screen, dragging a finger inside a menu with an open submenu dismissed the submenu instead of scrolling. Three pieces interact: a gesture is dispatched to every registered target containing the touch point, so a drag inside the submenu also reaches the parent menu's `Gesture.Change` handler and its `setScrollPosition`; `ScrollState`'s change detection compares the raw, unclamped position, so a menu that cannot scroll still emits `onScroll`; and the submenu entry dismissed itself unconditionally on the parent's `onScroll`. Since a drag is the only way a touch user can scroll, submenu items below the fold were unreachable by touch. Details and event-by-event measurements are in the issue.

The change gates the dismissal on the `ScrollEvent`'s clamped change flags (`scrollTopChanged` / `scrollLeftChanged`), which are false for these phantom events and true whenever the menu genuinely moved. A parent that really scrolls still dismisses its submenu, which is what the handler exists for: the submenu is anchored to an item that has moved away. Mouse behaviour is unchanged.

The defect was measured event by event on Android WebView 109 and 150 (portrait, hamburger menu, File submenu): one `touchmove` produced ten synthetic gesture change events with identical `translationY`, no real scroll, then the dismissal. A device run of this change in a downstream build is in progress; I will post the result here.

title: agentHost: measure time to first edit
body:
## Overview

### What

Report an optional `timeToFirstEdit` measurement on `agentHost.turnCompleted`. It measures wall-clock milliseconds from Agent Host turn start until the first provider tool request that is known to modify files.

The measurement is recorded at most once per turn and omitted when the turn never requests a classified file edit. It ends at request observation rather than confirmation, tool completion, or proof that a file changed.

Provider adapters classify native lifecycle events before the shared turn tracker records the latency:

- Copilot reuses its command-aware edit-tool classification, so `str_replace_editor` edit operations qualify while `view` does not.
- Claude reuses its built-in file-edit tool table.
- Codex marks its native `fileChange` item when mapping it to the provider-neutral tool lifecycle.

Shell commands and otherwise unclassified client or MCP tools are deliberately omitted rather than inferred from command or argument content.

### Why

[microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#8891](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/8891) identifies a gap in measuring how quickly Agent Host turns express edit intent. Existing `timeToFirstProgress` can stop on text, reasoning, reads, searches, or any tool start, while forwarded Copilot SDK telemetry is Copilot-specific and measures model-call time rather than end-to-end host latency.

This adds a provider-neutral Agent Host UX measure without parsing forwarded SDK telemetry or adding another event.

## Property-by-property parity

No properties are added or renamed. Existing turn identifiers, provider/model dimensions, result, permissions, interaction mode, and workspace context remain on the same `agentHost.turnCompleted` row.

## Measurement-by-measurement parity

| Metric | Previous/local source | Agent Host source | Parity |
|---|---|---|---|
| Time to first edit intent | Historical scorecard sums model-call durations through the first edit-producing response | Local Agent Host stopwatch from turn start through the first classified file-modifying tool request | ? New wall-clock UX semantic; not a continuation of the historical series |
| Time to first visible progress | `agentHost.turnCompleted.timeToFirstProgress` | Unchanged | ? Unchanged existing signal |
| Total turn time | `agentHost.turnCompleted.totalTime` | Unchanged | ? Unchanged existing signal |

## Row-count and dashboard implications

- The event remains one row per completed, cancelled, or errored Agent Host turn; no additional event rows are emitted.
- `timeToFirstEdit` is optional, so its presence defines turns with observed classified edit intent.
- The event remains in VS Code core telemetry as `monacoworkbench/agenthost.turncompleted`.
- Existing provider, model, session, chat, and turn dimensions remain available on the same row; no downstream join is required.
- Units are milliseconds.
- Copilot, Claude, and Codex built-in edit lifecycles are covered. Shell, unclassified client, and unclassified MCP edit behavior is unavailable and omitted.
- Historical dashboards must use a named semantic break rather than splice this field into the scorecard's cumulative model-time series.

## Semantic-shift ledger

| Field | Shift | Impact |
|---|---|---|
| `timeToFirstEdit` | Uses host wall clock rather than summed model-call duration | Includes intervening tool execution, approval waits, scheduling, and provider overhead |
| `timeToFirstEdit` | Stops when an edit request is observable rather than when an edit-producing response succeeds | Failed, denied, or later-cancelled edit intent can still be measured |
| `timeToFirstEdit` | Covers Agent Host Copilot, Claude, and Codex rather than the historical local Copilot edit-agent population | Enables provider comparison but starts a new metric series |
## Manual validation

Launched an isolated authenticated Code OSS Agents window against a throwaway workspace and completed a Copilot turn that read and edited `hello.ts`. The Agent Host inspector captured the report at the `agentHost.turnCompleted` emission boundary:

```json
{"provider":"copilotcli","timeToFirstProgress":3074,"timeToFirstEdit":7602,"totalTime":37806,"result":"success"}
```

This verifies that the measurement is populated before the confirmed edit completes and is forwarded on the successful turn-completion report.

title: fix: guard against parallel-refresh node removal in AsyncDataTree (fixes #331811)
body:
### Summary

The SCM History tree intermittently crashes with `TreeError [SCM History Tree] Unknown compressed tree node`, thrown from `CompressibleObjectTreeModel.setChildren` when it looks up a node that is no longer present in the inner compressed tree's node map. This is a lifecycle/race bug in the base `AsyncDataTree`: between the awaited `refreshNode(node)` and the synchronous `render(node)` in `refreshAndRenderNode`, a concurrent (parallel/re-entrant) refresh of an ancestor can splice `node` out of the inner tree, so the subsequent `render` dispatches `setChildren` for an element the inner model has already dropped. The bucket has hits across nearly all Insider versions (approximately 1.110 through 1.135), so it is a **pre-existing** race, not a 1.134 regression. The fix adds an early-return guard at the same orchestration point that already guards for disposal, skipping the stale render when the inner tree no longer contains the node.

Fixes microsoft/vscode#331811
Recommended reviewer: `@benibenj`

### Culprit Commit

Not a single-commit regression. `get_bucket_history` for bucket `936d3c96-3e33-8eb3-8c5a-8ca47ff47cd1` shows hits in effectively every tracked Insider version going back to ~1.110 (April 2026), so the `recent-regression`/`stable-anomaly` labels reflect re-bucketing rather than a new defect. Culprit: **not identified — pre-existing race** in the base async tree refresh/render orchestration (`src/vs/base/browser/ui/tree/asyncDataTree.ts`). The same class of inner-vs-outer node-map desync was previously addressed for a sibling code path in `c81880276af` ("fix: make AsyncDataTree.hasNode check inner tree consistency (fixes \#316443)").

### Code Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[updateChildren / parallel refresh scheduled] --> B[refreshAndRenderNode node]
    B --> C[await refreshNode node]
    C -. concurrent ancestor refresh .-> D[inner compressed tree splices node out]
    C --> E[render node]
    E --> F[tree.setChildren node, children]
    F --> G[CompressibleObjectTreeModel.setChildren]
    G --> H{nodes.get element}
    H -- undefined --> I[throw TreeError: Unknown compressed tree node]
    D --> H
```

### Affected Files

- `src/vs/base/browser/ui/tree/asyncDataTree.ts` — `refreshAndRenderNode` orchestration point (the fix).
- `src/vs/base/browser/ui/tree/compressedObjectTreeModel.ts` — `setChildren` crash site (throws when `nodes.get(element)` is undefined); unchanged.
- `src/vs/base/browser/ui/tree/objectTree.ts` — `hasElement` consistency check used by the guard; unchanged.
- `src/vs/workbench/contrib/scm/browser/scmHistoryViewPane.ts` — consumer creating the "SCM History Tree" and driving throttled `updateChildren`; unchanged.

### Repro Steps

Non-deterministic (timing-dependent). It surfaces when the SCM History view issues overlapping/throttled refreshes (e.g. rapid repository/ref changes or graph reloads) such that an ancestor refresh removes a node from the inner compressed tree while a child's `refreshAndRenderNode` is between its awaited refresh and its synchronous render. Telemetry shows ~82 users / ~88 hits across many versions.

### How the Fix Works

**Chosen approach** — `src/vs/base/browser/ui/tree/asyncDataTree.ts`, `refreshAndRenderNode`: after the `await this.refreshNode(...)` resolves and after the existing disposal guard, add:

```typescript
if (node !== this.root && !this.tree.hasElement(node)) {
    return; // node removed from the inner tree by a parallel refresh (#331811)
}
```

This fixes the bug at the data producer / orchestration point — the exact place that decides whether to dispatch a render — rather than at the crash site inside the throwing utility. `this.tree.hasElement(node)` queries the inner compressed tree model's node map, which is the same map `setChildren` reads and throws on; if a concurrent refresh has already removed the node, we skip the now-stale render instead of asking the inner model to operate on an element it no longer knows about. It mirrors the two disposal guards already present in this method (`#228211`, `#199264`) and is consistent with the framework's own acknowledgement of this scenario in `_updateChildren`, which wraps a parallel-refresh `rerender` in try/catch noting "missing nodes are fine, this could've resulted from parallel refresh calls". The precedent commit `c81880276af` applied the identical inner-tree consistency check to `hasNode` for the sibling `isCollapsed` path.

After this change, `refreshAndRenderNode` cannot dispatch `render(node)` to `setChildren(node, ...)` for a node a concurrent refresh removed, because the render is now skipped whenever the inner tree no longer contains `node`.

**Alternatives considered**

- Wrapping `setChildren`/`render` in try/catch: rejected — hides the symptom at the crash site, swallows a real error, and would break telemetry, rather than preventing the stale render at its source.
- Guarding inside `CompressibleObjectTreeModel.setChildren`: rejected — that is the crash site in a shared low-level utility; absorbing a missing-node there masks other legitimate callers' contract violations instead of fixing the async-tree orchestration that produced the stale call.

### Recommended Owner

`@benibenj` — most active recent author of `src/vs/base/browser/ui/tree/asyncDataTree.ts` and the surrounding compressed-tree code (core VS Code team member, active within the last day). The precedent fix for the same inner/outer node-map desync class also lives in this area.

title: fix: handle snippy post-insertion rejection to avoid unhandled error (fixes #331807)
body:
### Summary The Copilot code-referencing ("snippy") post-insertion check is fired as an unawaited, uncaught floating promise from `NextEditProvider.runSnippy`. When the snippy service returns a non-200 response, `SnippyFetchService.fetch` throws, `handlePostInsertion` re-throws, and — because the promise is neither awaited nor given a rejection handler — the error surfaces as an unhandled rejection that is reported to error telemetry. The specific 400 seen here (`source too short (must be at least 110 tokens, but is 105)`) is an expected server-side rejection: the client's local pre-check uses a 65-lexeme minimum while the service enforces its own, higher token minimum, so short accepted suggestions routinely trip it. Impact is noisy telemetry only — no user-facing functionality breaks. Fixes microsoft/vscode#331807 Recommended reviewer: `@ulugbekna` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | `333d9a4053e` (vendored-import boundary) | | Author | `@not-determined` | | PR | n/a | | Message | Initial import of the Copilot Chat extension ("Hello Copilot") | | Why | The fire-and-forget `handlePostInsertion(...)` call in `runSnippy` has existed without a rejection handler since the extension was vendored into `microsoft/vscode`. `git blame` shows the throwing call site predates all recent changes, so this is a **pre-existing** bug re-bucketed by telemetry (the specific 400 message text changed the bucket), not a new regression. | > Pre-existing / re-bucketing: the underlying floating-promise pattern is not introduced by any recent commit in the regression window; the new bucket is driven by the server's error-message text, not by a change in triggering logic. ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant User as User accepts NES participant NEP as NextEditProvider.runSnippy participant Svc as SnippyService.handlePostInsertion participant Fetch as SnippyFetchService.fetch participant Server as Snippy service User->>NEP: handleAcceptance() Note over NEP: ⚠️ Root cause:
handlePostInsertion() called
without await / .catch NEP->>Svc: handlePostInsertion(uri, doc, edit) Svc->>Fetch: fetchMatch(source) Fetch->>Server: POST snippy/match Server-->>Fetch: 400 "source too short (110 > 105)" Note over Fetch: 💥 throw new Error(`Failed with status 400 ...`) Fetch-->>Svc: rejects Svc-->>NEP: rejects (floating promise) Note over NEP: Unhandled rejection → error telemetry ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `extensions/copilot/src/extension/inlineEdits/node/nextEditProvider.ts` | root cause / fix site | L1648-1653: `this._snippyService.handlePostInsertion(...)` called with no `await` and no `.catch`, so a rejection escapes as an unhandled error | | `extensions/copilot/src/platform/snippy/common/snippyServiceImpl.ts` | rethrow site | L40-44: `catch (e) { throw e; }` re-throws the fetch failure up to the floating caller | | `extensions/copilot/src/platform/snippy/common/snippyFetcher.ts` | crash site | L70-71: `if (fetchResponse.status !== 200) { throw new Error(\`Failed with status \$\{status} ...\`); }` | | `extensions/copilot/src/platform/snippy/common/snippyCompute.ts` | contributing mismatch | L8: `MinTokenLength = 65` — client pre-check floor is looser than the service's 110-token floor, so short sources pass the client gate but are rejected by the server | ### Repro Steps 1. Use the Copilot Chat extension with Next Edit Suggestions (code referencing / public-code matching enabled). 2. Accept a short next-edit suggestion whose surrounding source clears the client's local 65-lexeme pre-check but is below the snippy service's token minimum (~110 tokens). 3. `runSnippy` fires `handlePostInsertion`; the snippy `/match` request returns HTTP 400 (`source too short`). 4. Because the promise is unawaited and uncaught, the rejection surfaces as an unhandled error and is reported to telemetry. Deterministic given a source between the two thresholds; otherwise triggered whenever the service rejects the request for any reason. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** (`nextEditProvider.ts`): `runSnippy` now `await`s `handlePostInsertion(...)` inside a `try/catch` and routes any failure to `this._logService.error(e, ...)`. This attaches a rejection handler at the fire-and-forget boundary that owns the background operation, so the failure is recorded as a *handled* error through the existing log/telemetry pipeline instead of escaping as an unhandled rejection. This follows the principle of fixing the error at the boundary that owns the best-effort background work — snippy code-referencing is explicitly a best-effort check, so its failures should not appear as unhandled application errors. The `logService.error` call preserves telemetry visibility of genuine failures; nothing is silently swallowed. **Alternatives considered:** - Aligning the client `MinTokenLength` (65) with the server's 110-token floor — rejected: the exact server threshold is not a stable contract the client can safely hardcode, other non-200 responses would still leak, and it would not fix the underlying missing-rejection-handler defect. - Swallowing the error inside `snippyServiceImpl.handlePostInsertion` (removing the rethrow) — rejected: that hides all fetch failures from callers/telemetry rather than handling them at the fire-and-forget site, and would violate the "never silence errors" principle by dropping them entirely. ### Recommended Owner `@ulugbekna` — dominant recent author of `nextEditProvider.ts` (author of the most recent NES/inline-edits commits touching this file, merged into `microsoft/vscode`), making them the natural owner for this fire-and-forget call site in the inline-edits area. > Generated by [errors-fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/32384235362) · opus48 · 461.5 AIC · ⌖ 11.7 AIC · ⊞ 18.6K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-id%3A+errors-fix%22&type=pullrequests)
