title: sessions: keep ignored blocked sessions ignored
body:
Ignoring a blocked session in the title bar indicator (e.g. **Ignore CI Failure**) only held until the user opened another session or the new-session view — the very same block then surfaced again, even though nothing about the session had changed.

## Root causes

Two independent bugs, both producing the same symptom.

**1. The acknowledgement state lived in a widget the command center throws away.**

`SessionsTitleBarWidget` is a command center action view item, and it created its own `BlockedSessionsIndicatorModel` — the only place acknowledged/ignored occurrences are stored. The sessions title bar calls `centerToolbar.refresh()` whenever `IsNewChatSessionContext` changes, which clears the action bar, disposes every view item and builds new ones. Opening a different session or the new-session view flips that context key → new widget → new model → every ignore forgotten.

**2. The raw blocked set briefly "unblocked" the session, which deleted the acknowledgement.**

`BlockedSessions` held its ref-counted GitHub pull request and CI model references on `reader.store`, which the observable framework disposes *before* each recompute. Since `getSessions()` returns a fresh array, every `onDidChangeSessions` recomputed the derived, dropped the last reference, disposed the shared models and re-created empty ones — so the session left the blocked set until the data was refetched. The cleanup autorun read that gap as "no longer blocked" and released the acknowledgement; when the failure reappeared, so did the pill.

## Fixes

- **Ownership** — `SessionsTitleBarContribution` now owns the `BlockedSessionsIndicatorModel` and `SessionActionFeedback` and passes them into each widget, so acknowledgements (and the transient "Approved N sessions" confirmation) survive command center rebuilds. The widget keeps no durable state.
- **Reference lifetime** — `BlockedSessions` and `BlockedSessionsCIFixModel` use `reader.delayedStore` (disposed *after* the recompute), so a recompute never drops the last reference to the shared, ref-counted GitHub models. This also removes a lot of needless model teardown and refetching.
- **Durable CI acknowledgements** — acknowledgements now record their reason. A `FailingCI` acknowledgement is keyed by the failing commit, so it is kept while the session is transiently absent from the blocked set and only expires when a *new* commit fails. `NeedsInput` acknowledgements keep the previous clear-on-absence behaviour, since their occurrence id has no per-episode identity.

## Logging

Per the ask, the feature is now diagnosable from a trace log alone:

- `[BlockedSessions] computed blocked sessions (n of m): [...]` on every recompute (level-guarded), so transient drop-outs are visible.
- `[BlockedSessionsIndicator]` traces model creation/disposal (including how many acknowledgements a dispose discards), every acknowledgement added, **kept or released with the reason**, blink queuing, and the set actually surfaced.
- `[SessionsTitleBar] creating the title bar widget` exposes command center churn.

A repro now reads as a straight line: raw set → acknowledgement decision → surfaced set.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`, `npm run valid-layers-check`, eslint and hygiene on the changed files — all clean.
- `BlockedSessions` (13) and `BlockedSessionsIndicatorModel` (22) suites pass, including two new regression tests.
- The new *"keeps the pull request and CI models referenced across recomputes"* test was confirmed to **fail** against the old `reader.store` behaviour (`blocked: []`, `released: ['owner/repo/30', 'owner/repo/30/sha30']`), so it genuinely guards the regression.

No specification update is included: `LAYOUT.md` has since been rewritten around an explicit change gate ("do not update for layout bug fixes") and no longer carries the blocked-sessions prose, so the behaviour is documented by the regression tests and code comments instead.

title: Fix lost race leaving a signed-out user on an Available marketplace
body:
## Problem

When a private/enterprise marketplace is configured (`extensions.gallery.serviceUrl`), an account change that happens **while the manifest is being fetched** can leave a signed-out (or otherwise ineligible) user looking at an `Available` marketplace.

`WorkbenchExtensionGalleryManifestService.handleMarketplaceAccountAccess` awaits the manifest fetch and then calls `update(manifest)` with no supersession. Sequence:

1. Account is eligible → a fetch starts and parks.
2. The account changes mid-fetch (e.g. sign-out) → `onDidChangeAccount` fires → `handleMarketplaceAccountAccess` runs again, sees no account, and sets `RequiresSignIn`.
3. The original, now-stale fetch resolves and calls `update(manifest)` → status flips back to `Available`.

End state: **signed-out user, `Available` marketplace.**

> Note: an earlier revision of this PR also addressed a "dropped event" defect (the account-change listener being registered *after* the initial `await`). That has since landed on `main` independently (the listener is now registered before the await), so this PR is rebased down to the remaining, still-present race.

## Fix

Add a cancellation generation so a superseded run cannot publish:

- `beginResolution()`, backed by a `MutableDisposable<CancellationTokenSource>`, cancels the previous run and returns a fresh token. It is called at the top of `handleMarketplaceAccountAccess`.
- The token is threaded into `getExtensionGalleryManifestFromServiceUrl` (replacing `CancellationToken.None`) and checked after each `await` before any `update(...)`, so a run that has been superseded by a newer account change returns without publishing.

The change is confined to `handleMarketplaceAccountAccess` and the fetch signature; no new status or behavior is introduced. Channels stay correct on their own because the constructor already re-publishes on every `onDidChangeExtensionGalleryManifest`.

## Tests

Adds one regression test to `extensionGalleryManifestService.test.ts` (GitHub default-account path): it parks the manifest fetch, fires a sign-out (`onDidChangeDefaultAccount` with no account) while it is parked, releases the fetch, and asserts the final status is `RequiresSignIn`.

Verified before/after against current `main` by reverting only the source fix (test left in place):

- **Before the fix:** the regression test fails with `actual 'available'` vs `expected 'requiresSignIn'`; the other 40 cases pass.
- **After the fix:** all 41 cases pass.

title: agentHost: stop a failed git probe from stalling Agent Merge
body:
Fixes a class of bug where a session with Agent Merge enabled sits idle forever without ever binding to its pull request, so review comments and CI failures never reach it.

Found while investigating a real session (`copilotcli:/7535d422-…`, PR #331760). Agent Merge was enabled and running — it had injected its autonomous configuration and the host was keeping the session resident for it:

```
[AgentService] Skipping idle eviction for a session held by Agent Merge: copilotcli:/7535d422-…
```

…but every evaluation died on the first check, exactly `backstopInterval` apart:

```
10:57:06 [AgentMergeController] Evaluation started: session=copilotcli:/7535d422-…
10:57:06 [AgentMergeController] Waiting for a current branch: session=copilotcli:/7535d422-…
11:07:06 [AgentMergeController] Evaluation started: session=copilotcli:/7535d422-…
11:07:06 [AgentMergeController] Waiting for a current branch: session=copilotcli:/7535d422-…
```

Its `agentMerge.controller` state had no `target`, confirming it never got far enough to bind the PR — so it never subscribed to PR events, and a review comment and a failing check both went unnoticed.

## Root cause

The session's persisted git state had lost its branch, while the worktree itself was perfectly healthy:

```jsonc
// session_metadata['agentHost.git']
{ "baseBranchName": "main" }   // no branchName, no hasGitHubRemote, no uncommittedChanges
```

`_computeSessionGitState` runs its probes independently and fills fields best-effort. `parseGitStatusV2` always yields `uncommittedChanges: 0` for any non-empty output, so its absence means `git status` itself returned `undefined`. The repository root is cached, so the function still returned an object — just a branch-less one. `_setSessionGitState` replaces persisted git state wholesale, so that object overwrote the good branch.

The failure left no trace: `_runGit` only logged when stderr was non-empty, and a timeout kill produces none.

## Why it never recovered

Three separate paths that should have repaired it did not:

1. `AgentMergeController._evaluate` calls `attachSessionGitHubPullRequest` (which begins with `refreshSessionGitState`), but only *after* the `if (!branchName) return` bail — so its own repair path was unreachable.
2. The lazy refresh on subscribe only fired when git state was entirely `undefined`; a *partial* state counted as "already computed" and masked it.
3. The file-monitor refresh needs watch interest plus an actual file change. A session held resident by Agent Merge alone — no client watching, no edits landing — gets neither.

## Changes

- **`agentHostGitService`** — return `undefined` when the status probe fails, so callers keep the state they already had instead of persisting a misleading one.
- **`agentMergeController`** — refresh git state before giving up on the branch. This also recovers sessions already stuck in this state, which matters because the bad state is persisted.
- **`agentService`** — treat a branch-less state as missing in the subscribe-time refresh.
- **`agentHostGitService`** — log git failures that produce no stderr (`warn` for timeouts/signals, `trace` for the `--quiet` probes' expected non-zero exits), so this can't fail invisibly again.

## Validation

`agentMergeController.test.ts` gains a regression test that reproduces the stall. Reverting just the controller change makes it fail the same way the real session did:

```
1) AgentMergeController
     recovers a session whose persisted git state lost its branch:
   Error: Timeout of 5000ms exceeded.
```

The git-probe change is covered by a new integration test, and was verified end to end against the compiled service: with the fix the degraded probe returns `undefined` and logs `Not reporting session git state because git status failed`; without it, it returns `{}` — the same shape as the corruption observed on disk.

Full `agentHost` unit suite: 5840 passing. The 11 failures are pre-existing and unrelated (`sessionPermissions`, `agentHostDebugLogs`, `agentHostRequestService`, `copilotAgent`, `localAgentHostMetadata`).

## What changed

title: Introduce compact codicons in chat components
body:
This pull request standardizes and updates the usage of compact codicon icons and their associated font sizes throughout the chat and AI customization features. The changes ensure a more consistent and visually compact UI by switching to compact icon variants and using a CSS variable for icon sizing. Additionally, some logic is updated to support these changes in both CSS and TypeScript/JavaScript code.

title: Fix PowerShell quoting for runInTerminal environment values
body:
### Summary

This PR fixes PowerShell environment value quoting when constructing commands for Debug Adapter Protocol `runInTerminal` requests.

Environment values were previously interpolated directly inside PowerShell single-quoted strings:

```ts
command += `\${env:${key}}='${value}'; `;
```

This works for ordinary values, but values containing embedded single quotes are not escaped correctly.

For example, an environment value such as:

```text
hello'world
```

was represented as:

```powershell
${env:QUOTE}='hello'world';
```

instead of the correctly escaped PowerShell representation:

```powershell
${env:QUOTE}='hello''world';
```

### Root cause

PowerShell single-quoted strings represent a literal single quote by doubling it (`''`).

The existing environment assignment wrapped values in single quotes without escaping embedded single quotes, so values containing `'` were not represented correctly.

The existing PowerShell `quote()` helper used for command arguments cannot be reused directly for environment values because it also special-cases values ending in a backslash. That behavior is appropriate for argument construction, but PowerShell single-quoted strings treat backslashes literally, so applying it to environment values would change values such as:

```text
C:\work\
```

into a value with an additional trailing backslash.

### Change

Environment values now escape embedded single quotes directly while preserving literal backslashes:

```diff
- command += `\${env:${key}}='${value}'; `;
+ command += `\${env:${key}}='${value.replace(/'/g, '\'\'')}'; `;
```

This applies the escaping required for PowerShell single-quoted strings without applying argument-specific trailing-backslash handling to environment values.

Existing handling of `null` environment values remains unchanged.

### Regression coverage

Added a focused `prepareCommand` regression test covering PowerShell environment values with:

* ordinary text;
* spaces;
* an empty string;
* a single embedded quote;
* multiple embedded quotes;
* a trailing backslash;
* a combination of backslashes and embedded single quotes.

For example:

```text
hello'world
```

is represented as:

```powershell
${env:QUOTE}='hello''world';
```

A value ending in a backslash:

```text
C:\work\
```

is preserved as:

```powershell
${env:TRAILING}='C:\work\';
```

And a value containing both an embedded quote and backslashes is represented without altering the backslashes:

```text
C:\it's\path\
```

becomes:

```powershell
${env:BACKSLASH_QUOTE}='C:\it''s\path\';
```

### Validation

The focused regression test passes:

```text
powershell - quotes environment values
1 passing
errorlevel: 0
```

The existing `prepareCommand` test suite also passes:

```text
Debug - prepareCommand
7 passing
errorlevel: 0
```

Client transpilation completes successfully:

```text
npm run transpile-client
✓ completed successfully
```

`git diff --check` also completes with exit code `0`.

The resulting PowerShell single-quoted representation was additionally verified directly in PowerShell.

### Scope

The change is intentionally limited to PowerShell environment value construction in `prepareCommand()`.

No behavior for other shells is changed, and existing handling of `null` environment values remains unchanged.

title: cli: reuse a fully-staged server download after an interrupted update
body:
## Summary

Fixes #331690.

`DownloadCache::create()` (used by the Rust CLI's server/CLI installer at `cli/src/tunnels/code_server.rs`, `cli/src/commands/serve_web.rs`, and `cli/src/tunnels/agent_host.rs`) unconditionally deleted its `.staging` directory before every download. If the process was killed after a download+extract fully finished populating `.staging` but before the atomic rename into the final commit-keyed directory (e.g. VS Code closed right as a server update finished downloading), the next launch discarded that already-complete download and re-fetched it from `update.code.visualstudio.com`, wasting bandwidth on a patch that was already available locally — exactly the scenario described in the issue.

## Root cause

In `DownloadCache::create()`:
1. Download happens into a sibling `<name>.staging` directory.
2. On success, `<name>.staging` is renamed into the final `<name>` directory.
3. On the *next* call, if `<name>` doesn't exist yet, any leftover `<name>.staging` was unconditionally wiped before starting a fresh download — with no way to tell "this is a partial download from a connection failure" apart from "this is a complete download that just never got renamed because the process was killed a moment too early".

## Fix

Write a small completion marker file (`.complete`) into the staging directory immediately after the `do_create` closure (the download+extract+verify logic) succeeds, before attempting the rename. On the next `create()` call:
- If the marker is present, the staged content is known-complete from a prior run — skip `do_create` entirely and go straight to the rename, avoiding any network request.
- If the marker is absent, the staging directory (if any) is a partial/corrupt leftover as before, and is wiped before a fresh download.

The marker is stripped from the final directory after a successful rename, so callers that enumerate the returned directory (e.g. the CLI-binary installer, which picks the first entry via `read_dir`) never see it.

This is fully contained in `DownloadCache` — none of its 4 call sites needed to change.

## Test plan

- [x] Added `cli/src/download_cache.rs` unit tests:
  - `test_existing_valid_target_is_reused_without_download` — an already-installed commit is returned without invoking `do_create`.
  - `test_missing_patch_triggers_download` — nothing cached → `do_create` runs and its output lands at the final path.
  - `test_incomplete_staging_download_triggers_fresh_download` — a staging dir without the completion marker (simulating a connection drop mid-download) is discarded and `do_create` runs again, with stale partial content not surviving into the result.
  - `test_interrupted_update_restart_reuses_completed_staging_without_redownload` — the core regression test: a staging dir with the completion marker (simulating a kill right before the final rename) is reused with `do_create` never invoked, and the marker itself doesn't leak into the final directory.

title: Ask the agent SDK about setup instead of guessing from the filesystem
body:
## The problem

A developer who pays for Claude directly hits a **GitHub Copilot sign-in wall**. Session-type availability was inferred by sniffing the filesystem for agent config files, and that guess is wrong in both directions: it gates users who have a perfectly good account, and it advertises agents to users who have none.

Separately, the agent SDK was downloaded on startup as a side effect of chat discovery — no one ever asked.

## The change

Stop guessing. Ask the agent's own SDK, and make the download an explicit choice.

**Wire contract.** Each agent publishes an SDK setup status — `notDownloaded` / `downloading` / `ready` — on a per-agent root-config key, alongside the capabilities it offers for getting an account (`setupDocsUrl`, `signInProviderName`). Account state is deliberately *not* on the wire: the workbench derives "no account" from `ready` + zero models, which already flows over AHP. Two wire sources for one truth would be free to disagree.

**No user-facing strings from the host.** Agents declare capabilities; the banner owns every sentence and localizes it via `vs/nls`. What crosses the wire is proper nouns the workbench cannot invent (`ChatGPT`, the agent's own display name).

**Explicit download.** A banner offers it; the workbench requests it by nonce. Consent is recorded **per agent** in application storage — pressing Download for Codex is not permission to fetch Claude's SDK. A later version bump re-downloads silently for a consented agent rather than nagging, since the cache is keyed by version and Insiders invalidates it daily.

**Background fetches stay invisible.** Only a setup-driven fetch registers download progress interest, so a fetch the user never asked for never surfaces a progress UI, and the host keeps reporting `notDownloaded` for it. Standing consent counts as setup-driven: a version bump re-downloads without a second question, but the user still sees why their agent is briefly unavailable.

`AgentSdkSetupChannel` holds the nonce handling, in-flight latch and publish ordering once; Claude and Codex differ only in their capability literals.

## Removed

The filesystem-sniffing paths this replaces: `codexLocalAuth`, and the "we've discovered your existing Claude configuration" notification — which asked users to sign in again right after they had declined the sign-in modal.

## Testing

- Unit sweep across the agent-host tree: 1699 passing, 0 failing.
- Claude and Codex replay e2e suites: unchanged pass counts (94 and 48).
- Walked live in a launched Code OSS against a local throttled CDN standing in for what the build stamps into `product.json`: download offered → clicked → progress → models enumerate → banner resolves, for both agents; plus the per-agent consent case (consented agent re-downloads silently on a version bump while the other still asks).

## Known gaps

A failed download is not yet surfaced to the user as an error — it republishes `notDownloaded`, so the banner re-offers the button. Deferred deliberately.

The banner is scoped to the window's **ambient** agent host — which *is* the remote server in a remote window, so those are covered. The Sessions app's *additional* connections (`remote-<authority>-<agent>`) show no banner. That is pre-existing structure shared with the Copilot sign-in notification, which is scoped identically; sessions against those hosts still fetch the SDK on demand via the ordinary load path. Moving both banners to per-connection setup state is the follow-up.

## What changed
- keep local rotated logs and local user-data sidecars as URI/size descriptors
- let the main process stream those files directly into the ZIP instead of transferring renderer strings

- avoid falling back to full output-model contents when source-backed collection fails

## Why
A fully rotated renderer/shared log setup can retain and serialize tens of MiB in the renderer before the native ZIP size check runs. Passing local resources avoids the renderer and IPC memory amplification while preserving inline support for genuinely non-local resources.

title: Use synchronous hooks for ESM ASAR resolution
body:
## Background

VS Code installs a custom ESM resolution hook in Electron processes to:

1. Map ESM `fs` imports to Electron's ASAR-unaware `original-fs`.
2. Resolve application bare package imports from `node_modules.asar`.
3. Prefer dependencies bundled closer to an importer.
4. Prevent resolution from escaping the application into an outer checkout's `node_modules`.

The hook currently uses Node's asynchronous `module.register`. Node runs those hooks on a dedicated loader worker, while static module linking synchronously waits for the worker.

This became visible while investigating Windows startup performance after Agent Host began prewarming during `WorkbenchPhase.BlockRestore`. An Agent Host utility-process profile attributed:

- 149 ms to `node:internal/modules/esm/hooks#makeSyncRequest`
- 92 ms to ESM source compilation
- 64 ms to process spawn

Most `makeSyncRequest` time was the main Agent Host thread waiting synchronously for the loader worker during static module linking.

Node 24 provides `module.registerHooks`, which runs synchronous hooks in-process. VS Code already uses this API in the extension host.

## Change

Port the existing ASAR resolver to `module.registerHooks`.

Resolution behavior remains the same:

- ESM `fs` maps to `node:original-fs`.
- Bare packages first use default resolution so an importer's closer bundled dependency wins.
- A default resolution outside the application tree is rejected.
- Missing packages are looked up in `node_modules.asar`.
- Package self-reference resolution still applies real `exports`, `main`, and ESM import conditions.
- Packages without exports retain the direct, escape-proof archive fallback.
- Electron built-ins remain excluded.
- Resolution tracing through `VSCODE_ASAR_TRACE` remains available.

Synchronous hooks also apply to CommonJS resolution, unlike asynchronous hooks. The resolver therefore explicitly bypasses contexts containing the `require` condition, preserving existing `require()` and `createRequire()` behavior.

## Startup scenario improvement

The final A/B uses two fully bundled current-source Windows desktop applications:

- Same source revision
- Same official Electron runtime
- Same product/resources/extensions
- Same minification and NLS processing
- Complete `out/` directories differ only by this change

Each app received three warmups followed by 30 measured starts. Every individual start was interleaved, alternating A/B and B/A order. The standard performance scenario opens a deterministic local folder and one text file with extensions, updates, experiments, workspace trust, GPU, telemetry, and crash reporting disabled.

| Metric | Baseline | Synchronous hook | Paired change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Total startup | 1435.5 ms | 1420.5 ms | **-18.5 ms** |
| Bootstrap 95% interval | | | **-33.5 ms to -7.0 ms** |
| Main bundle load | 152.0 ms | 118.0 ms | **-33.5 ms** |
| Workspace service init | 54.0 ms | 43.5 ms | **-11.0 ms** |
| Storage init | 22.0 ms | 18.0 ms | **-4.0 ms** |

The phase measurements overlap and should not be summed. The conservative end-to-end startup win is 18.5 ms on this Windows host.

## Improvements to other scenarios

The same bootstrap is shared by Electron main/CLI and `bootstrap-fork` processes such as Agent Host, extension host, shared/process services, file watchers, and terminal hosts.

Measured improvements in the packaged A/B:

| Scenario | Baseline | Synchronous hook | Paired change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Agent Host start to protocol connect | 962.5 ms | 759.0 ms | **-203.0 ms** |
| Shared-process connection | 518.0 ms | 420.5 ms | **-98.0 ms** |
| Extension registration | 761.5 ms | 734.5 ms | **-20.0 ms** |

Agent Host launch timing relative to workbench startup is unchanged (+4 ms, interval includes zero), while protocol connection becomes substantially faster. This preserves the early prewarm behavior required by #324330 rather than moving work after startup.

The packaged CLI also starts successfully through the synchronous hook.

## Compatibility / lack of regressions

Validation covered the behavioral differences between asynchronous and synchronous Node hooks:

- Direct packaged assertion:
  - ESM `import('fs')` resolves to `original-fs`.
  - CommonJS `require('fs')` remains the normal Electron/Node module.
- Packaged GUI standard startup succeeds.
- Packaged CLI `--version` succeeds.
- Packaged Agent Host resolves ASAR dependencies, connects, and lists sessions.
- No module resolution errors in correctly bundled baseline/fix runs.
- Agent Host launch is not deferred.
- Production desktop bundling succeeds.
- Client typecheck succeeds.

Tests:

```text
AgentHostPrewarmContribution and LocalAgentHostService: 19 passing
Agent Host diff worker: 6 passing
```

The diff-worker coverage is relevant because synchronous hooks are process-local and are not inherited by worker threads; the existing worker imports only built-ins/internal files and continues to pass.

Two independent implementation/diff reviews found no significant correctness or compatibility issue.

## Commands

```text
npm run typecheck-client
node build\next\index.ts bundle --minify --nls --target desktop --out perf-test\cache\bundle-sync-hook-pr
scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\services\agentHost\test\electron-browser\agentHostService.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\electron-browser\localAgentHostService.test.ts --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\diffWorkerMain.test.ts
```

title: chat: fix Find reporting matches it cannot reveal, and navigate newest first
body:
Follow-up to #330340 / #330585, fixing bugs found while using Find on a real transcript.

Searching `chang` on a conversation with 4 visible matches reported **7**, and pressing Next walked past three positions that could never be reached. Wrapping past the last match updated the counter but did not move the transcript. This PR fixes those, and changes navigation to run backwards in time.

## Find could only ever scroll down

Revealing a match used `Element.scrollIntoView`. The chat list picks up native scrolling by reading the container's `scrollTop` and resetting it to `0` (`scrollToActiveElement` in `listView.ts`), so the browser can only hand it a **positive** delta — `listView.ts` says as much: *"The scroll event on the list only fires when scrolling down."*

So any upward reveal silently did nothing, including the wrap from the last match back to the first. Reveal now writes the list's own scroll offset, which works in both directions. Code-block matches derive their position from the editor's layout rather than a DOM node, since Monaco only mounts visible lines.

## Matches now run newest first

Most of a conversation is in the past, so Find starts from the turn you are looking at and works backwards: `1 of 12` is the most recent match, Next moves further back, and the cap keeps the newest matches rather than the oldest.

`_seedActiveIndex` picks the newest match at or above the viewport, using the bottom-most item intersecting it.

> ⚠️ `SimpleFindWidget` hardcodes a down-chevron for Next, which now means *older*. Left alone for consistency with other find widgets — worth a look during review.

## The count was inflated by text that never renders

Three separate causes, each fixed where text is indexed rather than corrected afterwards:

- **Markdown link targets.** `renderAsPlaintext` emitted a list item's raw source instead of parsing its tokens, so `renderer.link` was never reached and `- Added [src/](/Users/…/change-port-to-1242/src)` kept its target — of which only `src/` renders. This was the whole 7-vs-4 gap: the three unreachable matches were all inside link URLs. Fixed in `markdownRenderer.ts` behind an opt-in `omitMarkdownSyntax`, so the ~90 other callers are untouched.
- **Filtered responses.** The renderer drops the references slot, body and citations when `responseIsFiltered`, keeping only the error message. The model indexed all of it, and mis-predicted every part index for the row.
- **Parts merged into one block.** Plaintext is trimmed per part then concatenated, so `See ` + `foo.ts` + ` for details` was indexed as `Seefoo.tsfor details` — inventing matches *and* hiding the sentence actually on screen.

Also removes `dropActiveMatch`, an earlier workaround that corrected the total after the fact and made it change as the user navigated. With the count right at the source it is no longer needed.

## The count settled visibly while typing

Every keystroke published its own count, so typing `chang` showed five different numbers. The search is now debounced (150 ms) and the count is held until the query has been searched and its match located, so the label moves once. Pressing Enter during the debounce flushes the pending search and lands on its first match.

## Notes for review

- `MAX_SEGMENT_SCAN = 100_000` and `SEARCH_DEBOUNCE_DELAY = 150` are judgement calls, not derived values.
- **Not** included, despite being flagged during review: highlights still do not repaint on scroll (`onDidRerenderRow` only fires for the row being edited), and `_repaintVisibleHighlights` is still quadratic in matches per row.
- The list-item markdown leak still affects other `renderAsPlaintext` callers — most visibly, screen readers announce full URLs for links in bulleted lists. They need the same option.

## Validation

Unit tests cover reveal geometry in both directions, newest-first ordering, viewport seeding, the per-segment cap keeping the newest occurrences, the settle logic, and each indexing fix. Manual checks worth doing: search on a long transcript and wrap past the last match; toggle Match Case then immediately press Enter; type quickly and watch the counter.

title: agentHost: wait for provider catalog migration before restoring a session
body:
Fixes #331648

## What

On Agents Window startup after an update, a restored session could show a persistent **"Couldn't open session / Session not found on backend"** error even though the session existed and loaded fine after navigating to another session and back.

## Why

`AgentService.listSessions()` waits for each provider's registration-time catalog migration via `_awaitInitialProviderMigration()`, but `restoreSession()` did **not**. A restored editor subscribes during startup and triggers `restoreSession()` while the provider's initial catalog migration is still in flight. During that window the provider's `getChatMetadata()` returns `undefined`, and `_restoreSessionState()` threw a false `AHP_SESSION_NOT_FOUND`. The host failure is transient (a later restore succeeds), but the client bakes it into synthetic chat history that only clears when the session is re-subscribed (navigate away/back).

## How

Give `restoreSession()` the same gate `listSessions()` already has:

- Extract `_awaitInitialProviderMigrationForProvider(provider)`, reusing the existing compare-and-replace single-flight retry, and refactor the aggregate `_awaitInitialProviderMigration()` to delegate to it (all providers retry concurrently, fail-fast).
- In `_doRestoreSession`, after the early tombstone check, await the session provider's initial migration, then **re-check the tombstone** before the registry/metadata work so a session deleted during the (potentially long) wait is not resurrected. The final atomic tombstone-aware registration is unchanged.
- Classify the outcome truthfully: `_restoreSessionState` throws `AHP_SESSION_NOT_FOUND` only when the catalog was ready (a genuine miss), otherwise `JSON_RPC_INTERNAL_ERROR` — so a still-unavailable catalog is never misreported as a missing session (which would re-create the sticky symptom).

No UI retry timer, no new provider API, and tombstone/deletion guarantees are preserved.

## Tests

New nested suite `initial provider migration race (#331648)` in `agentService.test.ts` covering:
- waits for migration instead of a false `SESSION_NOT_FOUND` (red before / green after)
- re-checks the tombstone after the wait and does not resurrect a deleted session
- a genuinely missing session is still reported not-found once migration completes
- an unavailable catalog is reported as an internal error, never a false not-found
- a stalled provider migration does not block restoring a ready provider

The existing "coalesces concurrent restores" test gets `onDidDiscoverChats = Event.None` to isolate it from an incidental discovery-triggered reconciliation whose timing shifted under the new wait (root-caused via instrumentation; not a real regression).

## Validation

- Full `agentService.test.js`: **337 passing, 0 failing**
- `npm run typecheck-client`: clean
- eslint on both changed files: clean

## Reviewer notes

Considered but intentionally not done here:
- A typed provider `found | missing | unavailable` result would let providers distinguish "temporarily unavailable" from "missing" without inferring readiness from migration completion.
- `restoreSession` has no `CancellationToken`; a disconnect during a long first-start migration keeps the (pre-existing) wait alive. Adding restore cancellation is a separate change.

title: agentHost: cover GraphQL mutation roots and null merge permission
body:
Follow-up to #331712, addressing two review comments that arrived after auto-merge had already landed that PR.

### The mutation fix had no regression coverage

The existing mutation tests only match operation names and variables, so reintroducing the invalid root-level `rateLimit` selection would still have passed. That is precisely why the original bug survived.

`ProgrammableGitHubServer` now rejects any mutation that selects a `Query`-root-only field at the mutation root. Putting the check in the fake server rather than in per-test assertions means **every** current and future mutation test enforces it automatically, with no opt-in required.

Verified by temporarily reintroducing the bug — it now fails with a direct diagnostic instead of silently passing:

```
GraphQL mutation selected rateLimit on the Mutation root, which GitHub only exposes on Query
```

The root-field parser handles aliases (`pullRequest: __type(...)`), arguments containing braces (`orderBy: { field: UPDATED_AT }`), and nested selections, so a nested `rateLimit` is correctly ignored.

### The permission test only covered `READ`

`viewerPermission` is `null` under GitHub App authentication, which deliberately disables Agent Merge. That fail-closed path could previously have regressed independently of the ordinary read-only case.

The test now snapshots the whole `RepositoryPermission` range including `null`, in a single assertion:

```ts
{ ADMIN: true, MAINTAIN: true, WRITE: true, TRIAGE: false, READ: false, null: false }
```

### Verification

- All 92 `platform/github` tests pass against current `main`
- `typecheck-client` and `eslint` clean
- Test-only change; no production code touched

title: policy: disable 3P harnesses under managed settings
body:
Enterprises that configure GitHub Copilot **managed settings** were still able to reach the third-party (Claude / Codex) harnesses, which are not governed by those settings.

Managed settings are composed and enforced by the **Copilot runtime**, so they never reach the Claude or Codex harnesses. That left a governed user with an ungoverned path around every control the enterprise configured — MCP allow/deny lists, plugin lockdown, permission and sandbox controls, OTel, and the rest.

This change disables both third-party harnesses whenever managed settings are in effect.

## What changed

**`IPolicyData.managedSettingsActive`** (`src/vs/base/common/defaultAccount.ts`) — `true` when *any* delivery channel (native MDM, server endpoint, or file on disk) supplies *any* managed setting. Unlike `managedSettings`, it is **not** projected onto the keys VS Code declares, so a purely runtime-owned key (e.g. `permissions.deny`) still counts as governance.

**`thirdPartyAgentEnabledValue`** (`src/vs/platform/policy/common/copilotManagedSettings.ts`) — shared `value` callback returning `false` when preview features are disabled **or** when `managedSettingsActive` is set, and `undefined` otherwise so an ungoverned user's own setting falls through.

**`Claude3PIntegration` / `Codex3PIntegration`** (`src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/agentHostStarter.config.contribution.ts`) — both policies now share that callback, replacing their duplicated `chat_preview_features_enabled` checks.

**Source attribution** (`src/vs/workbench/services/policies/common/accountPolicyService.ts`) — populates the new flag from `pickManagedSettings(...).activeSources`, and adds a matching presence probe so **Developer: Policy Diagnostics** attributes the value to the governing channel (`nativeMdm` / `server` / `file` / mixed) rather than to `account`.

## Notes for reviewers

- **The rule keys off *presence*, not a value.** The two policies therefore deliberately declare **no** `managedSettings` keys — nothing new joins the native MDM watcher schema, and `policyData.jsonc` is unchanged (`value` callbacks aren't serialized). I re-ran `npm run export-policy-data` to confirm.
- **Precedent.** This mirrors the existing runtime-owned `sandbox.enabled` floor retiring the local harness via `IAgentHostEnablementService.managedSandboxEnforced` — VS Code reads a runtime-owned signal to decide which harness to offer, rather than mirroring it as a VS Code policy.
- **Attribution probe re-evaluates the `value` callback.** `PolicyDefinition.value` is already required to be pure and deterministic, so this is safe, but it's worth a look.
- ⚠️ **This is a hard lock** — a governed user cannot re-enable Claude/Codex even if the enterprise never intended to restrict them. If admins should be able to opt back in, that would need its own managed-settings key. Flagging explicitly as a product decision.

## Validation

- Full `tsc --noEmit` over `src/` — clean; `gulp compile-client` — 0 errors.
- `hygiene` — clean (11,310 files); ESLint clean on changed files.
- `AccountPolicyService` suite: **28 passing**, including two new tests — a runtime-only file-channel key disables the harness and is attributed to `fileManagedSettings`, and an ungoverned account is left untouched. Broader policy/managed-settings suites: **179 passing**.
- Skill documentation updated (`.github/skills/policy-and-managed-settings/github-managed-settings.md`) with the new helper and its invariants.

title: agentHost: fix invalid GitHub GraphQL fields breaking Agent Merge
body:
Two GraphQL documents selected fields that don't exist in GitHub's schema, so both requests failed at validation time before ever executing.

### Bug 1 — `PullRequest.viewerCanMerge` (the reported error)

```
Field 'viewerCanMerge' doesn't exist on type 'PullRequest'
```

This field has never existed. The nearest real field, `viewerCanMergeAsAdmin`, means "can bypass branch protections and merge immediately" — wrong semantics for a general permission check.

Merge permission is now derived from `Repository.viewerPermission`, mapping `ADMIN`/`MAINTAIN`/`WRITE` to true. It fails closed when the field is `null` — which GitHub returns for GitHub App authentication — matching the behaviour of the existing REST fallback.

### Bug 2 — `rateLimit` on mutations (found while auditing)

`rateLimit` exists only on the `Query` root, but all four pull request mutations selected it at the `Mutation` root:

```
Field 'rateLimit' doesn't exist on type 'Mutation'
```

So *every* Agent Merge write — reply to review thread, resolve thread, enqueue PR, enable auto-merge — was failing the same way, not just mergeability refresh.

Rate limits are still tracked from the `x-ratelimit-*` response headers in `GitHubTransport`, so nothing is lost. Worth noting `agentHostOctoKitService.ts` already had the correct form — the two copies had drifted.

### Verification

Rather than checking fields by hand, I pulled GitHub's live schema via `gh api graphql` introspection and validated **every** GraphQL document in the repository against it — handling conditional interpolations (`includeMergeQueue`, `includeRequiredness`), dynamic issue-linkage batches, and array-joined documents.

All 31 documents now validate. The other 29 — checks, review threads, search, the capabilities probe, the sessions fetchers, and the Copilot extension's `githubAPI.ts` — were already correct.

- `npm run typecheck-client` passes
- `eslint` clean on changed files
- GitHub node tests: 43 passing, including a new test asserting a `READ`-permission viewer yields `viewerCanMerge: false`
- Wider `platform/{github,agentHost}` run shows 13 failures both with and without this change — all pre-existing and unrelated

### For reviewers

The permission mapping is the one judgement call worth a look. `viewerPermission` is a repository-level permission, whereas the old (non-existent) field implied a PR-level check. Push access is what actually gates merging, so this should be equivalent in practice — but it will now return `false` under GitHub App auth where the intent may have been `true`. That direction is deliberately conservative and consistent with the REST fallback.

Also worth flagging: the mutation bug had passing unit tests, because the mock server never validated queries against a schema. A CI step running this kind of schema validation would catch the whole class of bug — happy to add one as a follow-up if that's wanted.

title: multiDiffEditor: fix: preserve live document state across refreshes
body:
## Problem

In the Agents window's Branch Changes editor, a file could expand after the user had collapsed it. Scrolling only revealed the reset: the state changed earlier when marking a file as Viewed triggered a live changeset refresh.

The shared multi-diff widget retained the originally restored per-document state indefinitely. Whenever the document list changed, it rebuilt `VirtualizedViewItem` wrappers and reapplied that original snapshot—even when the underlying `DocumentDiffItemViewModel` was still the same live object. A stale `collapsed: false` value could therefore overwrite a newer user-selected `collapsed: true` value.

## Fix

This change treats persisted document state as one-time bootstrap state rather than continuously enforced state:

- Restore each `DocumentDiffItemViewModel` at most once.
- Maintain a write-through cache of the latest collapse and modified-editor selection state.
- Bootstrap genuinely recreated view models from that latest state.
- Preserve the last known selection when an editor is temporarily unavailable during virtualization or disposal.
- Guard cache writes by the current multi-diff model so disposed wrappers cannot contaminate a replacement model.
- Clear restoration state when installing a model without view state.
- Initialize a pooled editor with the restored selection—or `(1,1)` when none exists—before publishing it to observers.

This preserves current user interaction across additive resource refreshes while still supporting delayed documents and remove/re-add scenarios.

## Deliberate behavior

Repeated `setViewState` calls for the same model no longer overwrite newer live state, including state for temporarily absent documents. The first state replaces the cache; later calls only seed previously unseen document keys.

A replacement model starts clean unless it is explicitly given view state, even when it contains the same original/modified URI pairs as the previous model.

## Tests

Added real-widget browser regressions covering:

- An additive document-list refresh retaining current collapse and selection state.
- A delayed document receiving persisted state once, then retaining user changes.
- Forced virtualization and pooled-editor reuse without cross-document selection transfer.
- A document without saved selection receiving the editor default instead of recycled state.
- Remove/repeated-restore/re-add view-model recreation restoring the latest live state.
- Replacement-model isolation and late explicit restoration.

## Validation

title: agentHost: log shadowed Claude customizations in multi-root workspaces
body:
Fixes #331508

## Problem

In a multi-root workspace, when two folders each contribute a standalone **skill** (or custom **agent**) with the **same name**, first-name-wins discovery keeps the primary folder's copy and drops the other. Because the Claude SDK/CLI exposes standalone skills/agents by name only (no source-scoped identity like `plugin:skill`), the shadowed copy is **unreachable by any name** — and it was previously dropped **with no diagnostic**.

This matches the issue's minimum expected behavior: *"or at minimum some indication that a discovered customization was shadowed."*

## Change (log-only; discovery output unchanged)

- `selectFirstClaudeCustomizationByKey` gains an optional `onShadowed(shadowed, winner)` callback, invoked for each later item dropped by the first-name-wins merge. Return value and precedence are unchanged; the `.has()` claim check is preserved so the helper stays safe for any future caller.
- The multi-root discovery path passes a callback that logs a `warn` for each shadowed agent/skill:
  ```
  [claudeMultiRootCustomizationDiscovery] skill 'deploy' at '<uri-B>' is shadowed by '<uri-A>' from another workspace folder and is unreachable by name
  ```
- Same-named **user-scope** (`~/.claude`) copies are excluded by object identity, so ordinary project-over-user precedence stays quiet. Using identity (not path containment) keeps this correct even when a workspace folder lives under the home directory.

Only the multi-root branch is affected; single-root project/user precedence is unchanged and matches the Claude CLI. This is a diagnostic — the shadowed copy remains unreachable by name at the SDK level (verified against the Claude CLI), so this surfaces the collision rather than silently discarding it. A scoped-name / disambiguation solution would require SDK support and is out of scope here.

## Docs

- `src/vs/sessions/AI_CUSTOMIZATIONS.md` — documented the new diagnostic and the user-scope exclusion.

## Test

- Added a regression test in `claudeMultiRootCustomizationDiscovery.test.ts`: a workspace-vs-workspace **skill** and **agent** collision each warn exactly once, and a same-named **user-scope** copy produces no warning.

## Validation

title: Apply multi-diff options before attaching models
body:
tl;dr: I was debugging a window hang when I open a certain session. The session had a changed file which was minified with very long lines. Based on logs and traces, it appears that the multi-diff editor was rendering with a slower accessibility-friendly wrapping mode, but I did not have accessibility mode enabled. Looks like the option is not properly passed into the multi-diff editor. 

> fell back to Electron's native signal

I don't understand this part, why Electron is reporting that accessibility mode should be enabled 🤷 

## Problem

`MultiDiffEditorInput` resolves the correct resource-scoped `editor` and `diffEditor` configuration for each file, but `DiffEditorItemTemplate` attached the file models before applying those options. Attaching a model immediately constructs its editor view model and computes line wrapping, so the first construction ran with the diff editor's initial/default options instead of the user's configured options.

This becomes especially expensive when Electron reports native accessibility support as enabled while the user has explicitly configured `editor.accessibilitySupport: "off"`. Before the configured value was applied, the editor saw accessibility support as unknown, fell back to Electron's native signal, and selected the advanced DOM-based wrapping strategy. Opening an Agents changeset containing multi-megabyte generated JavaScript and CSS with very long minified lines then spent about 52 seconds in `_constructLines`, primarily in repeated `Range.getClientRects()` calls, blocking the renderer.

Although this was reproduced by switching to a remote Agent Host session, SSH transport was not the bottleneck: the remote file reads completed quickly, and the renderer stalled afterward while attaching the models. The underlying issue is shared multi-diff initialization order.

## Fix

Apply each document's editor options before calling `setDiffModel`. This ensures accessibility, wrapping, and other resource-specific settings participate in the initial view-model construction instead of taking effect only after the expensive work has already happened.

This does not disable accessibility or wrapping. It makes the initial multi-diff model attachment honor the same effective configuration that subsequent updates already use.

## Testing

Added a browser regression test that verifies:

- document options are applied before model attachment;
- `editor.accessibilitySupport: "off"` is present at attachment time; and
- the embedded editor computes accessibility support as disabled.

Also ran the related diff and multi-diff unit tests and targeted ESLint checks.

(Written by Copilot)

title: byok: omit store for custom Responses endpoints
body:
## Summary

- Omits `store` from Custom Endpoint Responses requests when `zeroDataRetentionEnabled` is not configured, allowing each implementation to apply its own default.
- Keeps explicitly enabled zero data retention requests stateless by sending `store: false` and not reusing `previous_response_id`.
- Preserves ordinary OpenAI BYOK behavior and Custom Endpoint request shaping after context-size cloning.

Fixes #331636

<details>
<summary>Technical context for AI-assisted review</summary>

### Intent and previous behavior

Custom Endpoint Responses models share the OpenAI-compatible endpoint implementation. That implementation coerced the optional zero data retention flag to a boolean and assigned `store` from the result, so an omitted flag became `store: true`. Custom Responses implementations can rely on the property being absent and applying their own retention default, particularly when continuing a tool-calling turn.

### Implementation

The Custom Endpoint endpoint now removes `store` only for Responses requests whose zero data retention setting is undefined. Explicitly enabled zero data retention continues through the shared path, which sends `store: false` and disables stateful marker reuse. The Custom Endpoint clone path preserves the concrete endpoint type so context-size overrides do not discard this request shaping.

### Behavior and constraints

- Chat Completions and Messages requests are unchanged.
- Explicit `zeroDataRetentionEnabled: false` retains the existing `store: true` behavior.
- Ordinary OpenAI BYOK endpoints retain their existing Responses behavior.
- Stateful `previous_response_id` reuse remains enabled only when retention permits it.

### Review context

The main compatibility boundary is the tri-state configuration: omitted, explicitly enabled, and explicitly disabled must remain distinct for Custom Endpoint models while other providers keep their current behavior.

</details>

title: Run UI validation scenarios without configuring an MCP server
body:
Stacked on #331674: this PR targets that branch, so the diff below is only the runner. It will retarget to `main` automatically once #331674 merges.

## Why

The `ui-scenario-validation` skill could only be used by first registering `test/mcp` as an MCP server and then driving `vscode_automation_evidence_start` / `_step` / `_finish` by hand. That is a lot of setup for a one-off reproduction, and it puts the capability out of reach of a plain request like *"reproduce this issue against Insiders and record it"*.

## What

`runScenario` takes a scenario file and runs it end to end:

```bash
node test/mcp/out/runScenario.js <scenario.js> --build "<app-root>"
```

A scenario is plain JavaScript — kept outside the repository, next to the run it produces:

```js
module.exports = {
	id: 'vscode-250159-settings-search',
	title: 'Settings search matches across title and description',
	source: 'https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/250159',
	workspacePath,
	steps: [
		{
			id: 'SS-01',
			title: 'Open the Settings editor',
			async run(context) {
				await context.workbench.quickaccess.runCommand('workbench.action.openSettings2');
				await context.page.waitForSelector('.settings-editor', { state: 'visible', timeout: 20000 });
				return 'The Settings editor is visible.';
			}
		}
	]
};
```

Each step receives the `Application`, the `Workbench` helpers and the Playwright `Page`. It returns a string describing how it was validated, throws to fail, or calls `skip(reason)` when a precondition is unavailable.

The runner launches VS Code with video and tracing, captures a screenshot at every step boundary, stops at the first failed or skipped step, writes `report.html`, and renders the chapter titles onto the recording. Clean capture is on by default, so the recording shows unmodified UI and titles are added afterwards.

**A skipped step reports the run as `aborted`, not `passed`** — the scenario did not validate, and reporting a pass would overstate the result. Exit codes: `0` passed, `1` failed or aborted, `2` usage.

The skill is rewritten around this flow. The MCP server stays available for interactive exploration, where inspecting the UI before choosing an assertion is worth the setup.

## Verification

The example in `SKILL.md` was extracted from the file programmatically and run verbatim against installed Insiders, so the documented API is executed rather than assumed:

```
Evidence run: .../vscode-250159-settings-search-2026-08-19T18-14-49-151Z
  PASS SS-01 Open the Settings editor
  FAIL SS-02 Search across title and description: Max Requests is absent. Found: Confirm Edit Request Removal, ...
Report: .../report.html
Rendered 2 step chapters into videos/annotated.mp4
Outcome: failed
```

That failure is the point: it reproduces [#250159](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/250159). Also verified:

- `skip()` stops the run, leaves later steps unexecuted, and reports `aborted`
- malformed scenarios (missing `id`, duplicate step ids, missing `run`) fail before VS Code launches
- the dev-build path still launches and finishes
- the annotated video contains the step cards and the real, unmodified workbench

## Note on the example

The first draft of the documented example asserted that a setting was **absent** without scrolling the settings tree. That tree is virtualized, so it renders only the rows near the viewport — the assertion would have been satisfied by a setting merely being below the fold. The example now scrolls the whole list, and the skill calls this trap out explicitly.

title: markdown: fix: correlate forwarded undo/redo restores
body:
Companion to microsoft/vscode-packages#279 (`markdown-editor: fix: correlate forwarded history restores`).

## Problem

The Markdown custom editor does not own its undo stack — the backing `TextDocument` does — so undo/redo chords in the webview are forwarded to the extension host, which runs the built-in `undo`/`redo` command. That forwarding was fire-and-forget:

- The webview never learned whether the command actually restored anything, so it could not attribute a restore to the chord or reveal the restored caret.
- Restored content arrived only via the generic `update` message, which carried no version, so a slow or reordered message could apply superseded text.
- A failed command silently did nothing.

`@vscode/markdown-editor` is gaining an asynchronous history strategy whose `undo`/`redo` return `PromiseLike<{kind:'unchanged'} | {kind:'restored', state}>`, with the controller revalidating the returned state before its reveal. This PR is the host half of that contract.

## The handshake

```
webview   --> { type: 'history', command, requestId }
extension --> { type: 'historyResult', requestId, status: 'restored' | 'unchanged' | 'failed', ... }
```

`restored` also carries `content` and `documentVersion`. Ordinary `update` messages now carry `documentVersion` too.

## Webview (`markdown-editor-src/editor.ts`)

- Each chord gets a monotonically increasing `requestId`; the pending `resolve`/`reject` pair is tracked and settled by the matching result. On dispose, in-flight requests resolve as `unchanged` so controller continuations cannot run against a torn-down editor.
- `#lastDocumentVersion` tracks the host revision whose content was last applied; `update` messages and history results with an older version are ignored. Messages without a version are still accepted, so an older host keeps working.
- A `restored` result applies the authoritative content via `replaceSourceText` (which maps the selection through the change and clears stale pending-paragraph state), captures the exact resulting `sourceText`/`selection`, and resolves `{kind:'restored', state}`. A no-op resolves `{kind:'unchanged'}`; a `failed` result rejects.
- `onError` logs the rejection and deliberately posts nothing, so a broken request cannot start another protocol round trip.

## Extension (`src/preview/markdownEditorProvider.ts`)

1. Drain `editQueue` so the chord cannot race a pending edit.
2. If the panel is not active, reply `unchanged` — the command would land on a different document.
3. Snapshot `document.version` immediately before the built-in command, await it, then capture version and content immediately after.
4. Reply via the pure helper `historyResultPayload`: `restored` (with content and the new version) only when the command changed `document.version`, otherwise `unchanged`. A rejection is traced and replied to as `failed` with a safe, non-leaking message.

All ordinary `update` posts now include `documentVersion`.

## Intentional cross-version source compatibility

The history strategy is assigned to a local variable rather than written inline in the `EditorController` options. As an inline literal, the extra `asynchronous`/`onError` members would trip excess-property checking against the **currently published** synchronous `IHistoryStrategy`. As a variable, the object stays assignable to the current interface (which ignores the extras and tolerates the promise as a `void` return) while the **forthcoming** package recognizes it as an `IAsynchronousHistoryStrategy`. No future-only types are imported; the result shape is mirrored with local declarations, so CI against the published package is unaffected.

## Validation

- Type-checked `markdown-editor-src` against **both** the published and the forthcoming package type definitions; both pass. A probe confirmed the future-only type is genuinely absent from the published package, i.e. the compatibility concern is real rather than theoretical.
- New focused unit test for `historyResultPayload` covering no-op vs. restored attribution.
- `npm run build-markdown-editor`, `tsc --noEmit` for the extension, and ESLint over both changed source trees.

No dependency, lockfile, or generated `package.json` contribution changes are included; the local package link used for verification was removed.

## Risks

- Until the new package ships, the returned promise is ignored by the published controller, so behavior there is unchanged; the correlated reveal activates with the package upgrade.
- The stale-version guard assumes monotonic `TextDocument.version`, which holds.
- Panel-inactive chords now reply `unchanged` rather than being silently dropped — this is the intended causal attribution, not a regression.

title: Make UI scenario validation work against an installed build, without an MCP server
body:
The `ui-scenario-validation` skill documents running a scenario against an installed build, and driving it through the `test/mcp` MCP server. Neither worked as documented: the installed-build path could not launch at all, and the MCP requirement put the skill out of reach of a plain request.

## `VSCODE_DEV=1` was applied to `--build` runs

Launching against installed Insiders always failed with:

```
Failed to launch Electron within 60000ms.
Original error: electronApplication.waitForEvent: Timeout 60000ms exceeded while waiting for event "window"
```

The Electron environment is resolved once at module load, and correctly: `VSCODE_DEV`, `VSCODE_CLI` and `VSCODE_REPOSITORY` are only set when there is no `--build`. `getApplication` then re-applied the same block unconditionally, so every launch was marked as running from source. A packaged build that believes it is running from a checkout never opens a window, so Playwright waits for a `window` event that never arrives.

Bisected against installed Insiders, holding everything else constant:

| Environment | First window |
|---|---|
| clean | opens |
| `VSCODE_DEV=1` | **never opens** |
| `VSCODE_CLI=1` | opens |
| `VSCODE_REPOSITORY=<repo>` | opens |

`VSCODE_DEV` alone accounts for it. The duplicated block also re-derived and re-validated the dev Electron path, which is already validated at module load for whichever target is selected, so it is removed rather than made conditional.

## The installed extensions directory was used

No extensions directory was ever passed, so a `--build` run loaded whatever the user has installed. That contradicts the isolated-profile guarantee the skill relies on: third-party extensions change the product under test and their logs are copied into the evidence bundle.

A settings-search scenario recorded before this change shipped logs for GitLens, ESLint, Prettier, the .NET runtime extension and two internal extensions, and their contributed settings appeared in the result list being asserted on. After it, the only extension left is the one bundled with Insiders — part of the product under test.

The launcher now uses an isolated directory under the existing test data path, matching what `test/smoke/src/main.ts` already does.

Per-run `extraArgs` are appended *after* the generated arguments, and `argv.ts` resolves a repeated string option with `val.pop() // take the last`, so a caller could have handed back the real directory. A shared `assertNoProfileOverrides` helper now rejects `--user-data-dir` and `--extensions-dir` (both `--opt value` and `--opt=value`) on the launch path *and* the restart tool, which previously had no guard at all.

## A stable build was downloaded on every run and never used

`setup` downloaded the previous stable release on every `--build` launch. The test data directory it downloads into is wiped at startup, so this was not a one-time cost: **335 MB and about 36 seconds on every run**, before VS Code even started.

The downloaded path was only ever assigned to `opts['stable-build']`, which nothing in this server reads — migration tests belong to the smoke test runner, which has its own copy of this logic. Removed, along with the now-unused `--stable-build` option.

## Running a scenario no longer needs an MCP server

The skill could only be used by first registering `test/mcp` as an MCP server and then driving `vscode_automation_evidence_start` / `_step` / `_finish` by hand. `runScenario` takes a scenario file and runs it end to end instead:

```bash
node test/mcp/out/runScenario.js <scenario.js> --build "<app-root>"
```

A scenario is plain JavaScript, kept outside the repository next to the run it produces:

```js
module.exports = {
	id: 'vscode-250159-settings-search',
	title: 'Settings search matches across title and description',
	source: 'https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/250159',
	workspacePath,
	steps: [
		{
			id: 'SS-01',
			title: 'Open the Settings editor',
			async run(context) {
				await context.workbench.quickaccess.runCommand('workbench.action.openSettings2');
				await context.page.waitForSelector('.settings-editor', { state: 'visible', timeout: 20000 });
				return 'The Settings editor is visible.';
			}
		}
	]
};
```

Each step receives the `Application`, the `Workbench` helpers and the Playwright `Page`. It returns a string describing how it was validated, throws to fail, or calls `skip(reason)` when a precondition is unavailable.

The runner launches VS Code with video and tracing, captures a screenshot at every step boundary, stops at the first failed or skipped step, writes `report.html`, and renders the chapter titles onto the recording. Clean capture is on by default, so the recording shows unmodified UI and the titles are added afterwards.

**A skipped step reports the run as `aborted`, not `passed`** — the scenario did not validate, and reporting a pass would overstate the result. Exit codes: `0` passed, `1` failed or aborted, `2` usage.

The skill is renamed to `validate-ui-scenario` and rewritten around this flow. Workspace skills are surfaced as slash commands named after the skill, so the name is what a user types: `/validate-ui-scenario reproduce <issue url> against my installed Insiders`. The MCP server remains available for interactive exploration, where inspecting the UI before choosing an assertion is worth the setup.

## The recording is captioned, not chaptered

Step titles were shown on full-screen cards spliced between segments. That stretched the timeline, and it told the viewer nothing about what the step actually *checked* — the validation detail was meant to appear on those cards but never did, because it was read from the opening capture, which only records that a step started. The field was always empty.

The band is drawn above the frame instead: `pad` grows the canvas and `drawtext` writes into the added strip, timed with `enable='between(t,...)'`. The recording keeps its original length, and **no recorded pixel is covered** — the status bar and the bottom of the workbench stay readable. Each caption carries the step number and id, its status, the title, and the validation detail from the closing capture, coloured green, red or amber; the run outcome sits in the corner for the whole video.

This also collapses the render to a single ffmpeg pass; the previous version trimmed a segment per step, generated a card per step, and concatenated them.

Verified on a real run — the captions track the UI state, not just the arithmetic: during `SS-01` the settings search box is empty, and it contains `chat confirm` during `SS-02`. Also checked with synthetic manifests: a detail containing `100%` renders (drawtext expansion stays off), over-long titles and details wrap and then truncate rather than overflowing, a skipped step shows amber with no detail line, and a missing ffmpeg still exits 0 with a warning.

## Scenario files need a `.cjs` extension

This package is an ES module package, so a CommonJS scenario saved as `.js` inside the repository is treated as ESM and fails to load — which is exactly what the skill told people to do. My own verification missed it because I had been running scenarios from outside the repository. The skill now says `.cjs`, and an ES module scenario with a default export works as well.
## Verification

Everything below was exercised on Windows against installed Insiders 1.135.0-insider and against a dev build from source.

The example in `SKILL.md` was extracted from the file programmatically and run verbatim, so the documented API is executed rather than assumed:

```
Evidence run: .../vscode-250159-settings-search-2026-08-19T18-14-49-151Z
  PASS SS-01 Open the Settings editor
  FAIL SS-02 Search across title and description: Max Requests is absent. Found: Confirm Edit Request Removal, ...
Report: .../report.html
Rendered 2 step chapters into videos/annotated.mp4
Outcome: failed
```

That failure is the point: it reproduces [#250159](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/250159) — searching `chat confirm` in the Settings editor does not match `Max Requests`, while `max requests` does. Also verified:

- installed Insiders via `--build`: fails to launch before this change, records a full run after
- the dev build path is unchanged, and still launches and finishes
- `skip()` stops the run, leaves later steps unexecuted, and reports `aborted`
- malformed scenarios (missing `id`, duplicate step ids, missing `run`) fail before VS Code launches
- the annotated video contains the step cards and the real, unmodified workbench
- a full `--build` evidence run drops from about 90s to 19s, with the first window arriving 173ms after launch

## Note on the example

The first draft of the documented example asserted that a setting was **absent** without scrolling the settings tree. That tree is virtualized, so it renders only the rows near the viewport — the assertion would have been satisfied by a setting merely being below the fold. The example now scrolls the whole list, and the skill calls this trap out explicitly.

title: Coalesce pane composite bar layout updates
body:
## Background

This change comes from a local investigation of Windows desktop startup performance from July 1 through August 18:

- Inventoried 154 published Insiders builds.
- Ran a 25-build randomized coarse sweep with repeated anchor sentinels.
- Confirmed the primary August boundary with interleaved A/B/A measurements.
- Localized one regression to the Electron 42.8.0 -> 42.8.1 transition.
- Reproduced the renderer regression with the identical VS Code app on official Electron runtimes.

A minimal renderer benchmark isolates the underlying runtime change:

| Electron | Forced layout | Cold JS | Warm JS |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 42.8.0 | 110.0 ms | 1.2 ms | 6.5 ms |
| 42.8.1 | 145.2 ms | 1.2 ms | 6.5 ms |
| 42.9.3 | 143.5 ms | 1.1 ms | 6.5 ms |

The Blink layout regression persists in Electron 42.9.3, so this PR mitigates one forced-layout hotspot in the workbench.

Startup CPU profiles map the hottest width read to:

```text
ActionBar.getWidth
<- ToolBar.getItemsWidth
<- AbstractPaneCompositePart.getToolbarWidth
<- AbstractPaneCompositePart.layoutCompositeBar
<- AbstractPaneCompositePart.onTitleAreaUpdate
```

Each title-action update synchronously relaid out the composite bar and read every toolbar item's `clientWidth`.

## Change

Coalesce title-action-driven composite-bar layouts to one animation frame. A real synchronous part layout cancels any pending frame and computes the same final layout immediately.

This preserves the final UI state while avoiding redundant intermediate width measurements during startup.

## Performance

Fixed/unfixed traces on the same source revision and Electron runtime:

| Metric | Before | After | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `ActionBar.getWidth` CPU self-time | 56.9 ms | 5.9 ms | **-51.0 ms** |
| Forced style/layout | 230.1 ms | 215.9 ms | **-14.2 ms** |
| Style update | 136.6 ms | 122.8 ms | **-13.7 ms** |

Non-instrumented A/fix/A source-build measurements:

- Workbench startup marker: **5-9 ms faster**
- Total dev startup: 53-60 ms faster, though most of that larger number is development module-loading variance and is not attributed to this change.
- Baseline control drift: 7 ms.

The conservative expected product win is **5-14 ms** on this Windows host under Electron 42.8.1.

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- `scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\test\browser\parts\compositePart.test.ts --run src\vs\base\test\browser\ui\toolbar\toolbar.test.ts`
  - 9 passing
- Lifecycle and diff reviews found no significant issues.

title: agentHost: keep Agent Merge monitoring sessions without a client
body:
## Problem

Agent Merge only ran while a client had the session open and subscribed. Enabling it and then closing or navigating away from the session silently stopped the autonomous repair/merge work until the session was reopened, and a session enabled but never opened in the client never started monitoring at all.

## What changed

The Agent Host now keeps an Agent-Merge-enabled session resident on its own, independent of any client.

**Session hold (`AgentMergeController`)**
- The controller owns a hold on the sessions it monitors, maintained eagerly at its own state transitions and exposed as `holdsSession()`.
- `AgentService` skips idle eviction and empty-session GC for a held session, and re-arms the release when `onDidReleaseHold` reports the hold ended — so disable, archive, and terminal states (merged/closed PR, branch retargeted, attempt budget exhausted) return the session to normal eviction rather than pinning it for the life of the host.
- Tracking the hold at transitions rather than lazily on query keeps the answer correct for a session the host has never had reason to evict.

**Enablement index (orchestrator database)**
- Enablement is mirrored into an index of session URIs in the orchestrator database's existing `metadata` table, so startup finds the few monitored sessions with one query plus a single-row registry lookup each, instead of opening every per-session database. This matters at scale: 1000 sessions with 2 enabled previously meant 1000 database opens.
- Enable, disable, archive, and delete all maintain the index. Delete clears it in the same transaction that removes the session; archive clears it from the action. Stale entries (left by a crash) self-heal — an entry whose session is unregistered or archived is dropped on the next pass instead of restored.

**Startup / discovery**
- Provider registration, and turning the global feature on, restore the indexed sessions so their controllers resume. Monitoring therefore survives a host restart and works for a session never opened in this client.

Both local and remote Agent Hosts run this controller in their own process, so the behavior is provider-neutral and applies to both.

## Security

The index is a derived pointer only. It stores a URI and grants nothing: enablement and all host-owned target state (bound branch/PR, comment watermark, attempt budgets) are still read from session config, and `agentMerge.controller` remains blocked from client writes at the dispatch boundary.

## Tests

New `Agent Merge durable session monitoring` suite covering:
- stays resident after the last unsubscribe, and is released once disabled;
- enablement recorded in the host index rather than per-session databases;
- resumes on a fresh host with no client opening it, and is released once disabled;
- archived session dropped from the index instead of restored;
- index cleanup on archive and on delete;
- archived session released like any other idle session.

Each new assertion was verified to fail against the pre-fix behavior.

## Validation

- `tsc --noEmit` on `src/tsconfig.json`: clean
- `npm run valid-layers-check`: clean
- ESLint on changed files: clean
- `AgentService (node dispatcher)` 325 passing, `AgentSessionRegistry` 23 passing, `AgentMerge` 6 passing

Note: `npm run hygiene` fails in this worktree on a pre-existing `check-package-json` path bug (`C:\C:\...`), reproduced identically on a clean tree, unrelated to this change.

## Reviewer notes

- No schema migration: the index lives in the existing `metadata` table. Sessions enabled *before* this change are not indexed and resume the first time they are opened, which re-indexes them. An eager one-time backfill was deliberately left out since it reintroduces the full scan this change removes.
- `unregisterSession` became a transaction (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE`) so the session row and its index entry are removed atomically, matching `tombstoneAndUnregisterSession`.

remove Agent Host parsing and propagation of the runtime-managed sandbox enablement value
