title: [WIP] Fix issue with opening plugin-provided files as read-only
body:
Thanks for asking me to work on this. I will get started on it and keep this PR's description up to date as I form a plan and make progress.

> ----
> 
> *This section details on the original issue you should resolve*
> 
> <issue_title>Customizations editor: "Open" does not open extension/plugin-provided files read-only (extractSource reads a property that is never set)</issue_title>
> <issue_description>Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: N/A (requires an extension- or plugin-contributed customization)
> 
> - VS Code Version: 1.133.0 (`main`, found via source analysis)
> - OS Version: N/A (platform-independent)
> 
> ### Steps to Reproduce
> 
> 1. Install an extension or plugin that contributes a chat customization (an instruction, skill, prompt, …).
> 2. Open the **Customizations** editor and select that item.
> 3. Invoke **Open** from its context menu.
> 
> **Expected:** the file opens read-only, with the message *"This file is provided by a plugin or extension and cannot be edited."*
> 
> **Actual:** the file opens fully editable. Users can edit files that live inside an extension's install directory, where their changes will be silently discarded on the next extension update.
> 
> ### Root cause
> 
> `extractSource()` in `aiCustomizationManagement.contribution.ts` reads the wrong property:
> 
> ```ts
> function extractSource(context: AICustomizationContext): AICustomizationSource | undefined {
> 	if (URI.isUri(context) || typeof context === 'string') {
> 		return undefined;
> 	}
> 	return context.storage;   // <-- the menu context has `source`, not `storage`
> }
> ```
> 
> The context object built by `aiCustomizationListWidget.ts` (both the inline action bar and the right-click menu) is:
> 
> ```ts
> const context: Record<string, unknown> = {
> 	uri: element.uri.toString(),
> 	name: element.name,
> 	promptType: element.promptType,
> 	source: element.source,          // <-- `source`
> 	pluginUri: element.pluginUri?.toString(),
> 	itemId: element.id,
> };
> ```
> 
> There is no `storage` property, so `extractSource()` always returns `undefined`. It type-checks only because `AICustomizationContext` has an `[key: string]: unknown` index signature and declares `storage?: PromptsStorage` — a field nothing ever populates.
> 
> ### Impact
> 
> `extractSource()` has two call sites:
> 
> - **Open** (`aiCustomizationManagement.openFile`) — the read-only guard `source === extension || source === plugin` never fires. This is the user-visible bug above. The **Open** menu item has no `when` clause, so it is offered for every item including extension- and plugin-provided ones.
> - **Delete** (`aiCustomizationManagement.delete`) — the in-action `source` guards (the plugin *"uninstall the entire plugin?"* prompt, and the *"Cannot Delete Extension File"* dialog) are dead code. **No data-loss risk**, because the Delete menu item itself is correctly gated by `WHEN_ITEM_IS_DELETABLE`, which uses the `AI_CUSTOMIZATION_ITEM_STORAGE_KEY` context key — and *that* key is correctly populated from `element.source`. The guards are unreachable defence-in-depth rather than the active protection.
> - Delete telemetry (`chatCustomizationEditor.deleteItem`) records `storage: source ?? ''`, so that dimension is always the empty string.
> 
> ### Suggested fix
> 
> Read `context.source` instead of `context.storage`, and drop the unused `storage?: PromptsStorage` field from `AICustomizationContext` so the type reflects what the widget actually sends. Note the declared return type is `AICustomizationSource` while the (unused) field is typed `PromptsStorage` — worth reconciling at the same time.
> 
> Found while investigating microsoft/vscode#329751.</issue_description>
> - Closes microsoft/vscode#329752
>

>

> </comments>
- Fixes #329752

title: Chat input pills: reusable widget, artifacts, customizations and visibility
body:
Reworks the pill row above the Agents-window chat input, and consolidates how pills are rendered.

## What changed

**Reusable widget.** The pill row is left-aligned and horizontally scrollable, driven by a reusable observable `ChatPillsWidget` in `vs/workbench/browser`. Sessions owns every adapter from session state and menus, so the workbench layer never imports sessions.

**Metadata placement setting.** `chat.agentSessions.showSessionMetadataInInput` (default off) moves the session header metadata pills down into the input row, hides the header's second row, moves Chats into the title toolbar after New Chat, and shows read-only workspace metadata next to the session title.

**Artifacts.** New agent-host tools `add_artifact` / `remove_artifact` / `list_artifacts`, gated by `chat.artifactTools.enabled`, persisted across host restarts and streamed to the client over the session `_meta` bag. GitHub pull request and issue artifacts are promoted into the session's GitHub links instead of appearing twice; only session-created pull requests are eligible to become the main pull request.

**Customizations.** The customizations a chat used or read are derived from its output stream and surfaced in a pill; clicking an entry reveals it in the customizations editor. Detection reuses the existing chat-state subscription, caches completed turns by id, and only re-parses the in-progress turn while streaming.

**Visibility menu.** Right-clicking the row offers `Hide <pill>` for the clicked pill, then the kinds with data, then those without. Customizations and Subagents start hidden; Changes can never be hidden.

**One set of pill implementations.** Everything now renders through one base plus four implementations: icon + label, dropdown (extends icon + label), resource label, and the animated changes pill. This removes the duplicated `SessionActivityPill`, the hosted-pill wrapper and their CSS.

## Notable fixes found along the way

- `VisibleSession` forwards `ISession` properties by hand and silently dropped `artifacts`; added a generic regression test that diffs wrapper against wrapped.
- The toolbar swallowed `contextmenu` per item, so right-clicking a pill never reached the row's visibility menu — only the empty strip beside it worked.
- `focus()` did not restore the tab stop that `blur()` removed, so arrowing between pills left the row with no tabbable item and Shift+Tab could not return to it. The same bug existed in `automationsView.ts`.
- Promotion now requires a link the pull request / issue pills can actually render, so an enterprise host does not vanish from both the artifacts pill and the GitHub pills.

## Validation

`tsc --noEmit`, ESLint, stylelint and `valid-layers-check` all clean. Unit tests cover the artifact model and tools, the customization parser (ordering, de-duplication, incremental re-parse), the visibility menu and defaults, pill focus and context-menu behaviour, and the GitHub promotion rules; the local agent-host provider suite passes in full. UI verified in the component explorer.

title: chat: preserve unresolved custom mode ids
body:
This fixes a restore race for custom chat modes that are referenced by persisted input state before custom modes have finished loading.

When `setChatMode` cannot immediately resolve a persisted custom mode, it still needs to show a usable Agent/Ask fallback. Previously, later `_syncInputStateToModel()` calls persisted that fallback ID back into the model, replacing the original custom mode ID with `agent`. When `modes.onDidChange` fired, the existing `_restorePersistedCustomModeIfAvailable()` recovery path then saw a builtin mode and skipped recovery.

The fix keeps the unresolved requested mode ID separate from the displayed fallback:

- Adds `resolveChatModeOrFallback(modes, id)` to return both the displayable `mode` and an optional `unresolvedId`.
- Tracks `_unresolvedModeId` in `ChatInputPart` while the fallback is active.
- Persists `_unresolvedModeId ?? mode.id`, preserving the user's intended custom mode across syncs.
- Clears the unresolved ID on session switch.
- Avoids repeatedly resolving an ID that is already known to be unresolved in `_syncFromModel`.
- Guards `validateCurrentChatMode()` so `chat.agent.enabled: false` does not overwrite the pending custom mode ID with `ask` while the fallback is only standing in for an unresolved custom mode.

This shape preserves intent instead of adding another retry loop: the model continues to hold the user's requested mode ID, while the UI can temporarily render a safe fallback until the normal `modes.onDidChange` recovery path has the information it needs. Unresolved `mode.id` is already an expected condition for agent-host/custom modes that register later and for missing customizations, and consumers validate before use.

Testing:
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npx eslint src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/input/chatInputPart.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/chatModes.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/chatModeService.test.ts`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- `npm run test-node -- --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/chatModeService.test.ts`
- Chat common test sweep: 83 passing
- Full compile: 0 errors
- Manual GUI check: custom agents surface correctly and the selected custom agent survives restart

Added coverage for:
- Resolving a known custom mode
- Falling back to Agent while returning the unresolved custom mode ID
- Recovering after the custom mode becomes available
- Falling back to Ask when Agent is unavailable

Note: an attempted without-fix baseline using an empty session did not reproduce because empty sessions already have a separate recovery path. This PR targets restored sessions with persisted input state/history.

title: fix: guard stale cursor line in toInlineSuggestion (fixes #331652)
body:
### Summary
`toInlineSuggestion` throws `Error: Illegal value for line` when computing whether an async next-edit-suggestion (NES) can be rendered as ghost text. The crash is `doc.lineAt(cursorPos.line)` in `tryRebaseAsCursorEdit` (`isInlineSuggestion.ts:49`): `cursorPos` is the request cursor VS Code core captured when it invoked the inline-completion provider, but NES results are processed asynchronously. If the document is edited (shrinks) before the result is processed, `cursorPos.line` exceeds the current `document.lineCount`, so `lineAt` rejects it. First seen in `GitHub.copilot-chat` 0.61.0 (new anomaly, not present in 0.59.0).

Fixes microsoft/vscode#331652
Recommended reviewer: `@ulugbekna`

### Culprit Commit
`a53a3fd5160` — "Fix inline suggestion false negatives via canonical cursor-edit rebasing (#325278)" by `@ulugbekna`. This commit added `tryRebaseAsCursorEdit`, which unconditionally calls `doc.lineAt(cursorPos.line)`. The prior implementation only touched the cursor line when the edit range already sat on it, so a stale cursor line never reached `lineAt`. This matches the "new in 0.61.0" telemetry signal.

### Code Flow
```mermaid
flowchart TD
  A[VS Code core captures request cursor position] --> B[provideInlineCompletionItems]
  B --> C[async NES computation]
  C --> D[document edited/shrinks in background]
  D --> E[_provideInlineCompletionItems processes result]
  E --> F[toInlineSuggestion cursorPos document range newText]
  F --> G[advanced path calls tryRebaseAsCursorEdit]
  G --> H[doc.lineAt cursorPos.line]
  H --> I[throws Illegal value for line: cursorPos.line >= document.lineCount]
```

### Affected Files
- `extensions/copilot/src/extension/inlineEdits/vscode-node/isInlineSuggestion.ts` — crash site (`tryRebaseAsCursorEdit`) and entry point (`toInlineSuggestion`).
- `extensions/copilot/src/extension/inlineEdits/vscode-node/inlineCompletionProvider.ts:451` — sole caller; passes the async request `position` into `toInlineSuggestion`.

### Repro Steps
1. Trigger a next-edit suggestion near the end of a document with inline-completions/advanced rebasing enabled.
2. Before the async NES result is served, delete text so the document has fewer lines than the original request cursor line.
3. When the result is processed, `toInlineSuggestion` calls `doc.lineAt(cursorPos.line)` with an out-of-range line and throws the illegal-line error.

### How the Fix Works
**Chosen approach** (`isInlineSuggestion.ts`): add a guard at the top of `toInlineSuggestion` that returns `undefined` when `cursorPos.line` is outside the valid range `[0, doc.lineCount)`. `cursorPos` crosses the VS Code core to extension boundary asynchronously (the producer of the position is core, not reachable from the extension), and by result-processing time the document may have mutated. A stale cursor means the edit was computed against a document state that no longer exists, so it genuinely cannot be rendered as ghost text — returning `undefined` is exactly the function's existing "not renderable" contract, not error suppression. The guard is placed at the single entry point that establishes the "valid cursor line in doc" precondition all helpers (`tryRebaseAsCursorEdit`, `tryAdjustNextLineInsertion`, `validateSameLineGhostText`) rely on, rather than at the individual `lineAt` crash site. No try/catch is introduced and no logging is removed. After this change, `tryRebaseAsCursorEdit` at `isInlineSuggestion.ts:49` cannot receive an out-of-range `cursorPos.line` because `toInlineSuggestion` rejects it before dispatching to any helper.

**Alternatives considered**: guarding directly inside `tryRebaseAsCursorEdit` around the `lineAt` call — rejected because the same stale-cursor precondition is shared by the other helpers, so the guard belongs at the common entry point; wrapping the call in try/catch — rejected because it would hide the staleness instead of expressing the not-renderable contract.

### Recommended Owner
`@ulugbekna` — author of the culprit commit `a53a3fd5160` (#325278) that introduced the unconditional `doc.lineAt(cursorPos.line)` call in the inline-suggestion rebasing path.

title: Fix keyword color too similar to function color in 2026 themes
body:
## Problem

Fixes #331622.

In the **2026 Dark Theme**, keywords (`if`, `import`, `try`, `except`, `for`, `while`, etc.) are visually hard to distinguish from function names, as reported with a screenshot in the issue.

## Root cause

`2026-dark.json` defines its own `tokenColors` rule for the generic `"keyword"` scope (`#ff7b72`, coral-red). However, `dark_plus.json` (an ancestor via the theme `include` chain: `2026-dark.json` → `dark_modern.json` → `dark_plus.json`) already defines a **more specific** rule for `"keyword.control"` (`#C586C0`, magenta).

VS Code's TextMate scope matching always prefers the most specific matching selector, regardless of which theme in the include chain defined it. Since most real keywords use scopes like `keyword.control.flow.python` or `keyword.control.import.python`, they match `keyword.control` (2 segments) rather than the theme's own `keyword` (1 segment) rule — so the inherited `#C586C0` wins over the theme's intended `#ff7b72`.

`#C586C0` (magenta) sits visually very close to the theme's `entity.name.function` color (`#D2A8FF`, lavender) — both are pastel purple/magenta tones on the same near-black background, which is exactly the collision reported in the issue.

I confirmed this by downloading the screenshot attached to the issue and sampling its pixels directly: `import`/`from`/`as` render as `#C586C0`, while the called/imported function name renders as `#D2A8FF`.

The same issue exists in `2026-light.json` (`keyword` = `#cf222e`, shadowed by `light_plus.json`'s `keyword.control` = `#AF00DB`, close to that theme's `entity.name.function` = `#8250df`), so I fixed both for consistency.

## Fix

Minimal, one rule changed per theme: add `"keyword.control"` alongside `"keyword"` in each theme's own `tokenColors`, so the theme's intended color wins for control-flow keywords too — the same pattern the theme already uses elsewhere (e.g. its `storage.modifier.*` overrides).

```diff
 {
-    "scope": "keyword",
+    "scope": [
+        "keyword",
+        "keyword.control"
+    ],
     "settings": {
         "foreground": "#ff7b72"
     }
 },
```

(analogous change in `2026-light.json` with `#cf222e`)

## Validation

There are no existing automated tests asserting specific theme color values in this repo, so none were added — theme color changes are conventionally validated visually. To verify without a full Electron build, I wrote a small script that replicates the actual theme `include`-merge and TextMate scope-specificity resolution logic from `colorThemeData.ts`, and confirmed:

| Scope | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `keyword.control.flow.python` | `#C586C0` | `#ff7b72` |
| `keyword.control.import.python` | `#C586C0` | `#ff7b72` |
| `entity.name.function` | `#D2A8FF` (unchanged) | `#D2A8FF` (unchanged) |

I also rendered a before/after swatch confirming the visual improvement, and re-verified the equivalent scopes/colors for the light theme fix.

## Test plan

- [x] Confirmed root cause via pixel-sampling the issue's screenshot
- [x] Confirmed fix via scope-resolution simulation matching production merge logic
- [x] `git diff` reviewed — only the two theme JSON files touched, one rule each

title: Cap External Agent Sessions to 30 Days (replace `all`, enforce ingest/prune retention)
body:
## Description

This changes external-session visibility from unbounded to a strict 30-day retention model to reduce slow session surfacing/filtering and keep catalog size bounded. The `all` mode is removed from user-facing options and behavior, while legacy persisted `all` values are migrated/treated as `last30Days`.

- **Mode and settings surface**
	- Replaced `ChatExternalSessionsMode.All` with `ChatExternalSessionsMode.Last30Days`.
	- Updated external session picker/menu labels and ordering to use **Last 30 Days** as the terminal option.
	- Updated Agent Host schema and chat configuration enums/descriptions accordingly.

- **Backward compatibility for persisted config**
	- Added settings migration: `chat.agentSessions.showExternal = "all"` → `"last30Days"`.
	- Added runtime fallback in Agent Host root-config read path so legacy stored `"all"` is interpreted as `Last30Days`.

- **Single shared retention constant**
	- Introduced `EXTERNAL_SESSION_MAX_AGE_MS = 30 * DAY_MS` and reused it across:
		- visibility filtering (`Last30Days` mode),
		- external discovery/migration ingestion cutoffs.

- **Ingestion hard cap**
	- External/provider-discovered sessions older than 30 days are skipped at registration time (adoptable-legacy exclusions preserved).

- **Deferred stale-row pruning**
	- Added delayed post-startup prune routine for stale external registry rows (never local, never adoptable-legacy).
	- Prune result count is logged at info level.
	- Reconciliation/list invalidation is triggered only when rows are actually removed.

- **Targeted coverage updates**
	- Updated mode-dependent tests from `All` → `Last30Days`.
	- Added coverage for:
		- `Last30Days` boundary semantics,
		- ingestion skip for >30-day external sessions,
		- prune behavior keeping adoptable-legacy rows intact.

```ts
const EXTERNAL_SESSION_MAX_AGE_MS = 30 * DAY_MS;

case AgentHostExternalSessionsMode.Last30Days:
	return session.modifiedTime >= now - EXTERNAL_SESSION_MAX_AGE_MS;
```

title: Fix extension command titles losing localization after install/update

## Description

Fixes #330908 — Extension command titles lose localization after installing/updating an extension until full restart.

### Root Cause

When an extension is installed or updated while VS Code is running, the **incremental scan** path (`scanExistingExtension` → `createExtensionScannerInput`) is invoked **without a `language` argument** (see `scanLocalExtension` in `extensionManagementService.ts`, which calls `scanExistingExtension(location, type, { includeInvalid: true })`).

In `createExtensionScannerInput`, the `language` was only used for `translations` via `language ?? platform.language`, but the value stored in `ExtensionScannerInput.language` was the **raw `undefined`**. As a result, `findMessageBundles` hit this early return:

```ts
if (nlsConfiguration.devMode || nlsConfiguration.pseudo || !nlsConfiguration.language) {
    return c({ localized: joinPath(extensionLocation, 'package.nls.json'), original: null });
}
```

…so `package.nls.<locale>.json` was never loaded for the updated extension, and the manifest `%key%` references were not translated. Command titles reverted to English until a full restart (which triggers a full scan with the correct language).

The remote path (`remoteExtensionsScanner.ts`) already passes `{ language }` correctly — only the local incremental path was affected.

### Fix

Fall back to `platform.language` when no explicit language is passed, so the language stored in `ExtensionScannerInput` matches what was already used for `translations`:

```ts
language = language ?? platform.language;
const translations = await this.getTranslations(language);
```

### Validation

- Added test: `scan existing extension without language uses platform language for nls` — verifies that scanning without a language still localizes the manifest using the platform language.
- 30 tests passing in `extensionsScannerService.test.ts` (the single pre-existing failure `scan system extensions include additional builtin extensions` is an environment-only issue with bare mocha — `Cannot determine URI for module id!` — unrelated to this change; it fails identically on `main`).

title: sessions: fix: guard chat grid neighbor lookup before layout
body:
Fixes #331616

## What changed

This change tracks whether the current Agents window session grid has completed its first layout. Reconciliation uses logical group order until geometric neighbor queries are safe.

It also adds a regression test for opening and focusing a session whose active chat is a child chat with a `parentChat`.

## User-visible failure

Opening an affected session could leave the chat area partially initialized:

- The main chat tab was visible.
- No tab was active.
- The active child chat tab was missing.
- The **Start a parallel conversation** composer was rendered and focused.

Clicking the visible main tab repaired the view and caused the remaining chat tab to appear.

## Root cause

`ChatGroupsView.setSession` previously created and attached a new `SerializableGrid`, installed an `autorun` that synchronously invoked `_reconcile`, and only then called `_applyLayout`.

When the outer `ChatGroupsView` had already been laid out and the session's active chat had a `parentChat`, reconciliation attempted to place the child beside its parent. `_findAdjacentGroup` called `SerializableGrid.getNeighborViews`, but the new grid had not received its first `layout()` call and threw:

```text
Can't call getNeighborViews before first layout
```

The main chat had already been assigned before the exception. Since those observable writes were not rolled back, the UI retained the main tab while failing to assign or activate the child chat, producing the partial state above.

## Why this fix

The current grid resets a `_gridDidLayout` flag when the session changes and sets it after `layout()` completes. `_findAdjacentGroup` only calls `getNeighborViews` once that flag is true; before then it uses its existing logical group-order fallback.

This retains the original reconcile-before-layout ordering, so the resolved chat view is laid out once and the transient parallel-conversation composer is not laid out before being replaced.

The change does not add exception handling or a focus-specific workaround.

## Validation

- Added a regression covering an already-laid-out view with an active child chat, including the replacement chat view's layout and document-scoped focus.
- The regression records layout calls: one for the resolved chat and zero for the transient composer.
- All 13 `ChatGroupsView` unit tests pass.
- Targeted ESLint passes.
- Client TypeScript type-check passes.
- `git diff --check` passes.
- Manual end-to-end verification on macOS against the fixed source build:
  - Created a session with a main chat and active parallel child chat, switched away, and reopened it.
  - Both tabs were present, the child was active and rendered, focus was inside its chat input, and the parallel-conversation composer was absent.
  - The renderer log contained no `Can't call getNeighborViews before first layout` error.

title: agentHost: migrate legacy Copilot CLI sessions on open, not just in the list
body:
Fixes #331266

## The problem

A legacy Copilot CLI session has two addresses: `copilotcli:/<id>` (extension host) and `agent-host-copilotcli:/<id>` (agent host). Only opening the second one migrates it. Opening the first works — you get your session — but it silently never migrates,
so you are in the same position next time.

The first attempt at this filtered the **session list**: wait for agent host discovery, then show only the agent-host row. That covers clicking a row, and nothing else.

Sessions are addressed by **URI** everywhere else, because a URI is what's durable:

| Path | Trigger |
| --- | --- |
| `ChatEditorInput.resolve` | Reopening a window with a chat editor open |
| `_restoreVisibleSessions` | Agents window restoring its grid |
| `openSessionByResource` | Session links, hover, picker, Open as Editor |
| `openSession` | Commands and direct navigation |

None of these consult the list. Window restore is the common case and needs no unusual action, which is why it was easy to miss.

## The approach

Redirect the legacy address rather than trying to hide every reference to it.

When anything opens `copilotcli:/<id>`, we derive the agent-host twin and subscribe to it. **That subscribe is the migration**: `subscribe` → `restoreSession` → `ensureChatAdopted`, the existing adoption path — provenance check, working-directory recovery, metadata persistence. No adoption logic is duplicated or reimplemented.

- Subscription carries state → adopted; open the agent-host resource.
- Subscription errors → not ours to adopt; open the legacy resource, as today.

Because classification is per-session, it does not depend on the catalogue scan finishing — which is what made list-based gating fragile at scale.

## Impact on other sessions

`migratedCopilotCliResource()` returns `undefined` **synchronously** for anything that is not a `copilotcli:` URI, so native, Claude, and Codex sessions never reach a probe. Already-adopted sessions short-circuit with no round-trip. Probes are bounded (10s) and every failure path degrades to current behaviour.

Failures are deliberately **not** cached: the host reports every restore failure as `SessionNotFound`, so a genuine refusal cannot be told apart from a transient one (host restarting). Caching would silently pin a session to the legacy path for the rest of the window's life.

## List behaviour

The list keeps one rule: if a `copilotcli:` row and its `agent-host-copilotcli:` twin are both present, hide the legacy one. It is a pure function of the current list — no timing, no config, no readiness tracking. A legacy row with no twin stays visible, because opening it now redirects.

Both windows previously carried duplicate copies of this logic; it is now a single shared helper, including the rule that a remote agent-host session
(`remote-<authority>-copilotcli:`) must never be deduped against a local twin even when the raw ids collide.

## Also in this PR

Fixes found while working on the above:

- **Setting off→on no longer loses sessions** — disabling migration retracts adoptable   rows, but discovery skips chats already in the registry and so could never  re-announce them. Re-enabling now restores exactly the retracted keys, and only   forgets a key once it is confirmed surfaced.
- **Working-directory recovery from the extension host's marker**, so worktree sessions   the SDK reports without a `cwd` stay reachable once the extension is retired. The  project resolves from the recovered directory, not the repository root.
- **Discovery is batched**, and a failed marker read is no longer memoized (previously a  session created while the host was running stayed non-adoptable until restart).
- **Discovery retry backs off 250ms/1s/5s** instead of a flat 5s — the race it recovers   from cleared in well under a second in every sampled startup log.

## Testing

- Probe: redirect on adoption, retry after refusal, non-legacy resources never probed,  no connection declines.
- Resource resolution: redirect, no-claim fallback, provider throw falls back rather  than blocking the open.
- Dedupe: twin hides legacy, no twin keeps legacy, remote never deduped, unrelated  providers untouched.
- Host: off→on→off toggle cycle, marker recovery including worktree precedence, and a  marker written after an initial read miss.

title: Fix YAML indentationRules: no indent after property, & typo breaks anchors, missing block-scalar support
body:
Fixes #330394

`extensions/yaml/language-configuration.json` had three separate bugs in its indentation rules, all reported in #330394:

### 1. Typing `foo:` + Enter doesn't indent

`increaseIndentPattern` does match `foo:`, so the regex itself wasn't the problem. The actual cause is in `extensions/yaml/package.json`: a `configurationDefaults` block sets `"editor.autoIndent": "advanced"` for `[yaml]` and `[dockercompose]`, overriding the editor's global default of `"full"`.

`indentationRules` (`increaseIndentPattern`/`decreaseIndentPattern`) are only evaluated when the effective `autoIndent` strategy is `Full` — see the early-return guards in `src/vs/editor/common/languages/autoIndent.ts` (`getInheritIndentForLine`, `getIndentForEnter`, etc.). At `"advanced"`, only `onEnterRules` and the default bracket-pair indent logic run (`src/vs/editor/common/languages/supports/onEnter.ts`), and YAML's language configuration defines no `onEnterRules`. So the increase/decrease-pattern engine was never reached, regardless of whether the pattern matched.

This also explains why the reporter's own extension — registering the identical `language-configuration.json` under a custom language id — worked correctly: it had no matching `configurationDefaults` override, so it inherited the real `"full"` default.

**Fix:** remove the `"editor.autoIndent": "advanced"` override from both `[yaml]` and `[dockercompose]` in `package.json`, letting them fall back to the global `"full"` default. Nothing in the repo's history indicated `"advanced"` was chosen intentionally for these languages.

### 2. Anchors (`foo: &anchor`) don't indent

The pattern used the literal string `&\w+` instead of `&\w+`. This traces back to the commit that introduced `indentationRules` for YAML in 2018 (`1aa00f53bc4`), which appears to have adapted the pattern from a source using HTML/XML entity escaping and never corrected it.

**Fix:** `&` → `&`.

### 3. Block scalars (`foo: |`, `foo: >`) don't indent

`increaseIndentPattern` had no case at all for block scalar indicators. Per the YAML spec, `|` (literal) and `>` (folded) start a block scalar whose content must be indented on following lines, optionally followed by chomping (`-`, `+`) and/or explicit indentation-indicator digits (e.g. `|-`, `>2`, `|+1`).

**Fix:** added `\|[0-9+-]*` and `>[0-9+-]*` as additional alternatives in the pattern's trailing group.

### Testing

Added regression tests in `src/vs/workbench/contrib/codeEditor/test/node/autoindent.test.ts` that load the real `extensions/yaml/language-configuration.json` and verify, via `getReindentEditOperations`, that indentation now increases after a property (`foo:`), an anchor (`foo: &anchor`), and a block scalar (`foo: |`), while a plain scalar (`foo: bar`) correctly does not — guarding against regression.

Full source build compiles cleanly (`npm run compile`, 0 errors) and the existing node unit test suite passes unaffected (14,789 passing; the only 2 failures are pre-existing, unrelated flaky tests in `AgentService` and `McpStdioStateHandler`).

title: Select-to-line-start jumps to end of previous line when before an indented token
body:
Fixes #331582

## Problem

When the cursor sits right before an indented token on a line — i.e. right after the leading whitespace/tabs and before the first real character — pressing `Cmd+Shift+Left` (macOS) / `Ctrl+Shift+Home`'s sibling `Shift+Home` (`cursorHomeSelect`) selects backwards across that line's own indentation to column 1, instead of doing anything useful with the previous line:

```ts
const memberships = await this.entityManager.find(
    |CompanyMembershipEntity,
```

Press `Cmd+Shift+Left` once → selection spans only the leading spaces on the *same* line:

```ts
|    CompanyMembershipEntity,
```

Pulling `CompanyMembershipEntity` up onto the `find(` line then requires pressing Backspace once per indentation character/tab-stop, rather than once.

## Root cause

`cursorHomeSelect` and plain `cursorHome` both call the same "smart home" toggle in `MoveOperations.moveToBeginningOfLine` (`src/vs/editor/common/cursor/cursorMoveOperations.ts`):

- if the cursor isn't yet at the line's first non-whitespace column, move there;
- if it's already there, move to true column 1 of the *same* line.

That second stage never looks outside the current line, so when the cursor is already positioned right before the content (immediately after the indentation), the only thing left to select on that line is the indentation itself — which isn't useful on its own, since a single Backspace from column 1 already joins the line with the previous one and keeps the indentation as-is.

## Fix

In `MoveOperations.moveToBeginningOfLine`, when selecting (`inSelectionMode`) and the cursor is already at the first non-whitespace column of a line that (a) actually has leading whitespace and (b) isn't the first line of the buffer, extend the selection to the end of the previous line instead of column 1 of the current line:

```ts
if (inSelectionMode && firstNonBlankColumn > minColumn && lineNumber > 1) {
    const previousLineNumber = lineNumber - 1;
    return cursor.move(inSelectionMode, previousLineNumber, model.getLineMaxColumn(previousLineNumber), 0);
}
```

A single Backspace afterwards then removes the newline and the entire indentation in one step, pulling the token onto the previous line.

Unaffected on purpose:
- Plain (non-select) `Home`/`Cmd+Left` — unchanged, still stays on the current line.
- Lines with no leading whitespace — nothing to skip, so the toggle behaves as before.
- The first line of the buffer — no previous line to jump to.
- Any selection call where the cursor isn't yet at the first non-whitespace column — unchanged, still moves there first as before.

This only touches the shared model-level move function, so it applies consistently whether reached through the plain (non-wrapped) path or the soft-wrap–aware view-line path that already delegates to it.

## Testing

Added to `src/vs/editor/test/browser/controller/cursor.test.ts`, next to the existing "move to beginning of line" tests:
- The exact repro from the issue (spaces indentation), including that a second press falls back to the normal same-line toggle once there's nothing left to skip.
- Tabs indentation.
- Previous line ending in punctuation (`{`), confirming the cursor lands immediately after it.
- Plain (non-select) Home is unaffected.
- A line with no leading whitespace is unaffected.

Validation performed:
- `scripts/test.bat --run vs/editor/test/browser/controller/cursor.test.js` — 259 passing (254 pre-existing + 5 new), 0 failing.
- `scripts/test.bat --run vs/editor/test/browser/controller/cursorMoveCommand.test.js` — 56 passing, 0 failing.
- `scripts/test.bat --run vs/editor/contrib/wordOperations/test/browser/wordOperations.test.js` — 57 passing, 0 failing.
- `npm run typecheck-client` — 0 errors.

title: agentHost: Collect and package debug logs on the host
body:
## Summary

Reworks **Developer: Export Agent Host Debug Logs** so the Agent Host owns discovery and packaging of host-side diagnostics instead of the client guessing host filesystem paths.

- Adds a typed private AHP extension request, `vscode/collectAgentHostDebugLogs`, returning an opaque artifact URI.
- Uses the Copilot SDK's `session.rpc.debug.collectLogs` API for SDK-owned events, process logs, and shell logs.
- Keeps client-owned logs on the client: window/shared-process output, AHP JSONL transport logs, remote-forwarded channels, and usage/customization sidecars.
- Produces one final ZIP; native exports flatten the Agent Host archive into it.
- Supports export with or without an active session. With a session, SDK events/shell logs are included. Without one, collection remains host-wide and excludes unrelated session events/shell logs.

## Remote transfer

The artifact contract is a URI, not inline bytes.

- Local Agent Host artifacts are ordinary local `file:` URIs and never transfer archive bytes over IPC.
- Remote Agent Host artifacts are downloaded through the private `vscode/readAgentHostDebugLogsChunk` request in bounded 1 MiB chunks.
- The old whole-file Base64 read path is not used as a fallback.
- The chunk reader only serves artifacts produced and retained by the collector; it is not a general-purpose remote file read.

## Safety and lifecycle

- Bounds archive bytes, staged bytes, individual files, and archive entry count.
- Keeps the tail of oversized logs so recent failures remain diagnosable.
- Validates ZIP entry count/expanded size before flattening and rejects duplicate final paths.
- Expires abandoned host artifacts and cleans staging/artifacts on completion and shutdown.
- Validates the returned artifact URI scheme, kind, and declared sizes.
- Verifies actual streamed byte count against the declared artifact size.
- SDK/provider collection failures surface to the user instead of silently switching to a second path-guessing implementation.

## Compatibility

This intentionally uses the existing private AHP extension-method seam rather than changing the generated public protocol while the shape settles. A remote host that predates the request returns `MethodNotFound` as an explicit collection failure.

## Validation

- Client typecheck and full product/Copilot compile pass.
- Agent Host, chat browser, Agents provider, ZIP, protocol routing, and streaming tests pass.
- Layer validation and hygiene pass.
- Manually verified in Code OSS:
  - Active Copilot session ZIP includes `agenthost.log`, SDK `events.jsonl`/process logs, and client-owned logs.
  - No-active/New Session ZIP includes host/window/shared/AHP/process logs without unrelated `events.jsonl`.
  - Active Codex session produces the common host artifact without Copilot-specific entries.
  - Repeated exports leave no temporary artifacts.

title: Reject null in vObjAny()
body:
### Problem

`TypeofValidator` compares `typeof content` against the expected type name:

```ts
if (typeof content !== this.type) {
    return { content: undefined, error: { message: `Expected ${this.type}, but got ${typeof content}` } };
}
```

`typeof null === 'object'`, and `vObjAny()` is `new TypeofValidator('object')`. So null passes validation:

```
vObjAny().validate(null)   ->  { content: null, error: undefined }
```

Two things that makes wrong:

- The declared type is `ValidatorBase<object>`, and TypeScript's `object` excludes `null`. A caller trusting the result gets a `null` the types say cannot be there.
- Its own `getJSONSchema()` returns `{ type: 'object' }`, and in JSON Schema `object` excludes null too (`null` is a separate type). The validator contradicts the schema it advertises.

`ObjValidator`, in the same file, already guards exactly this:

```ts
if (typeof content !== 'object' || content === null) {
    return { content: undefined, error: { message: 'Expected object' } };
}
```

And the one in-tree caller works around it, re-checking after a *successful* validation — `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/claude/claudeSubagentResolver.ts`:

```ts
const r = vObjAny().validate(input);
if (r.error || r.content === null || Array.isArray(r.content)) {
    return undefined;
}
```

That `r.content === null` branch only exists because `vObjAny()` lets null through.

### Change

Reject null for the `'object'` case, and report it as `null` rather than `object` so the message is accurate for every typeof validator. `vString().validate(null)` previously said *"Expected string, but got object"*.

Before / after, running the real module:

| input | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `vObjAny().validate(null)` | `OK content=null` | `Expected object, but got null` |
| `vObjAny().validate({a:1})` | `OK` | `OK` (unchanged) |
| `vObjAny().validate([1,2])` | `OK` | `OK` (unchanged) |
| `vObjAny().validate('str')` | `Expected object, but got string` | unchanged |
| `vString().validate(null)` | `Expected string, but got object` | `Expected string, but got null` |

Arrays still pass, as before — only null changes.

I left the `r.content === null` check in `claudeSubagentResolver.ts` alone. It is now redundant but still correct, and it guards untrusted SDK JSON; removing it felt like the wrong thing to bundle into this fix.

### Tests

Added `src/vs/base/test/common/validation.test.ts` — the module had no tests. It covers null rejection, that objects and arrays still pass, non-object rejection, and the corrected `null` message on the other typeof validators.

### Verification

I could not run the repo's test harness — I worked from a sparse checkout (`src/vs/base`, `src/vs/platform`, `src/vs/editor/common`) because a full clone kept timing out here, so there is no `node_modules` to build against. What I did run:

- Executed the real `validation.ts` module directly to produce the before/after table above, with the fix stashed and unstashed.
- `tsc --strict --noEmit` on `validation.ts`: **no errors**.
- The 8 errors `tsc` reports for `validation.test.ts` are all `Cannot find name 'suite'/'test'` and `Cannot find module 'assert'`. I checked this is environmental: running the identical command against the existing `src/vs/base/test/common/numbers.test.ts` produces 9 errors of the same class.

So the test file has not been executed by the real runner. Worth a CI run before merging, and I am happy to adjust if it disagrees with local conventions.

### Note

`TypeOfMap` also has a `null: null` entry, but no validator is ever constructed with it, and it could not work as written for the same `typeof` reason. Left alone as out of scope — flagging it in case it is meant to be used.

title: Render an embedded attachment that has no content type
body:
Fixes #331568.

A pasted image renders as a broken thumbnail because its attachment was persisted without a `contentType`, and the restore path reads that field unguarded:

```ts
if (!attachment.contentType.startsWith('image/')) {
```

Evaluated in the running workbench against the exact record from a real session database:

```
{"type":"embeddedResource","label":"Pasted Image","displayKind":"image","data":"iVBORw0KGgo…"}

(s) => s.contentType.startsWith("image/")
→ TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'startsWith')
```

### Fix

The guard lives in `state/sessionState.ts`, the hand-written layer where VS Code-specific helpers over the generated protocol types already live:

```ts
export function embeddedAttachmentContentType(attachment: { contentType?: string; displayKind?: string }): string | undefined {
	return attachment.contentType ?? (attachment.displayKind === 'image' ? 'image/png' : undefined);
}
```

`displayKind` already records that the attachment is an image, so the type is inferred from what the record states rather than assumed. An attachment with neither falls through to the generic branch instead of being treated as an image.

Three call sites now resolve the content type through it: `stateToProgressAdapter.ts`, `codexPromptResolver.ts`, and `copilotAgentSession.ts`.

### Why this does not change the protocol type

An earlier revision of this PR made `contentType` optional in `state/protocol/channels-chat/state.ts`. That was wrong twice over, and both commits are kept so the reasoning is visible.

That file is generated output. It carries `DO NOT EDIT -- auto-generated by scripts/sync-agent-host-protocol.ts` and is synced from `microsoft/agent-host-protocol`, so the next sync would have silently reverted the change.

It was also the wrong request to make of the protocol. Upstream declares `contentType` as required, and every current producer in this repo sets it (`agentHostSessionHandler.ts` in all four places, and `copilot/mapSessionEvents.ts`). A record without one is therefore not a protocol gap; it is a record written by an older build that is still on disk. The helper's parameter is structural rather than `MessageEmbeddedResourceAttachment` precisely because the record it defends against is one the declared type says cannot exist, and the tests construct it the same way and say so.

### Verification

- Three tests over the real persisted shape: an image with no content type restores as an image, a declared content type still wins, and a non-image with no content type restores as generic. The first and third fail if the guard is removed; the second passes either way by design, since it guards against the inference overriding a declared type.
- Confirmed in the running workbench: the shipped expression throws on that record, the fixed one returns `true` and hands on `image/png`, and a non-image with no content type returns `false`.
- `tsc --noEmit` reports no errors in any of the touched files.

### Notes

Every current producer defaults the field, so newly pasted images were never affected. This repairs attachments already written, which otherwise stay broken for the life of the session, and which no producer-side change can reach.

I have not identified which producer wrote a record without the field. The one I have predates the build I could inspect, and I would rather say so than name a suspect I cannot demonstrate.

title: chat: add a render-only Permissions area to the Customizations editor
body:
Adds a **Permissions** group to the Chat Customizations editor sidebar — Terminal, Files and Network — behind the off-by-default `chat.customizations.permissions.enabled` setting.

Today the only way to see what governs an agent is `Developer: Policy Diagnostics`, which dumps raw JSON for the managed slice. This gives users a real answer to *"why did it ask me?"* and *"what did my org lock down?"*.

> [!NOTE]
> Draft. The UI can only populate one of five permission layers until the runtime exposes a read API for its resolved rule set — tracked in `github/copilot-sdk-internal#244`. See *Known limitation* below.

## The design constraint

**The Copilot runtime is the source of truth for permissions.** It owns the rule DSL, the matcher, and the precedence between managed policy, configured rules, location grants and session grants. This PR is deliberately **render-only** and re-derives none of it:

- `chatPermissionRuleSyntax.ts` only splits `Kind(argument)` for display, and says so in its own header.
- Domains exist **only** for the four rule families `parse_managed_rule` accepts — `Shell`/`Bash`/`PowerShell`, `Read`, `Edit`/`Write`, `Domain`. MCP servers and built-in tools are governed by different contracts and get no domain until the runtime can report rules for them.
- Managed rules render read-only.

This follows the `policy-and-managed-settings` skill: *"Do not duplicate a runtime parser, matcher, or security decision in VS Code."*

## Known limitation (why it's a draft)

The runtime exposes no read API for its resolved rule set — only the managed slice, via the slow `getManagedSettings()` diagnostics probe. So the snapshot reports **only** `ChatPermissionScope.Managed` and the UI explicitly names the layers it could not read.

That honesty is deliberate and load-bearing. `ChatPermissionSnapshot` distinguishes `loading` / `unavailable` / `error` / `available`, every `available` snapshot carries `resolvedScopes`, and a provider that fails is surfaced rather than dropped. **Rendering an empty list would assert "nothing governs this agent" — the opposite of the truth under `failClosed`.**

When the runtime ships the projection, `browser/permissions/chatPermissionSnapshotService.ts` is the only file that changes.

## Design language

The sections deliberately reuse the customization sections' chrome rather than approximating it — they join the same selector lists for the content panel, the title header (title / description / inline learn-more), the search row and the collapsible group headers, so consistency holds by construction.

What stays different is what a row *means*: a permission rule is a read-only statement of what the runtime enforces, not something authored here. So there is no create button (the primary-action slot holds **Refresh**), uneditable rows carry a lock, each row ends in an allow/ask/deny pill, and a rule overridden by a higher layer is struck through with a `→ 🔒 Managed Ask` badge naming the winner.

## Screenshots

Covered by four component fixtures (`chatPermissionsSection.fixture.ts`), each in Dark and Light: managed-only, all scopes with a shadowed rule, partial provider failure, and unavailable.

## Reviewer notes

Bugs found and fixed during review passes, worth a look since they're the risky parts of the diff:

**Sidebar refactor** (the `WorkbenchList` went from `ISectionItem` to a union including non-selectable group headers, so indices now refer to `sidebarItems`, not `sections`):
1. `layoutSidebar` still sized from `sections.length * 26`, ignoring the 28px headers, clipping the last rows.
2. Blank pane on harness switch — this change *introduced* the path, since the previous contributed section was Codex-only while permissions use `supportsHarness: () => true`.

**Snapshot correctness:**
3. Disabling the agent host mid-probe left the in-flight generation valid, so a late result could overwrite the disabled state.
4. Provider failures arrive in-band as `{ error }`, not thrown. Skipping them made a timeout look like "not supported", and a mixed result could present one provider's rules as the whole policy. Now: all-failed → `error`; partial → `available` + a warning banner listing who failed.
5. Selecting a permission section focused the hidden prompts search box; contributed sections now route through their own `focus()` via one shared helper.

Also note `allow-auto-only` is read from the raw managed slice: it's in the runtime's `managed-settings-schema.json` and enforced in `managed.rs`, but the bundled SDK typings still declare only `"disable"`. The resolved `bypassPermissionsDisabled` / `failClosed` verdict is treated as a floor the raw settings may refine but never soften.

## Validation

- `tsc -p src/tsconfig.json` clean; `valid-layers-check` passes
- `npm run eslint` clean
- 48 tests pass (`chatPermission` + `aiCustomization`)
- 8 component fixtures render without errors
- Hygiene/pre-commit hook passes (it caught invalid CSS font-size tokens and indentation along the way)

title: agentHost: report completed model calls per turn
body:
https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/8738

## Overview

### What

Adds `modelCallCount` to the existing per-turn `agentHost.turnCompleted` telemetry event. The measurement reports completed upstream model-response rounds attributed directly to the turn, including responses that request tools and the final tool-free response.

Before this change, equivalent turn-depth analysis was available only for a subset of Copilot turns through `toolCallDetails.numRequests`. After this change, the turn event carries the rollup across Copilot, Claude, and Codex, including turns without tool details.

Provider-native completion boundaries remain intact:

- Copilot uses the response's `apiCallId`, with stable request/message fallbacks, and collapses split assistant messages from one API call.
- Claude uses completed canonical assistant messages and excludes aborted streams.
- Codex uses cumulative per-response token-usage snapshots, retaining a session baseline so replayed and rate-limit-only updates do not increment the count.

The host routes model-call signals through the existing active-turn and subagent mapping, then deduplicates provider call identities in `AgentHostTurnTracker` before emitting the final count.

### Why

Turn-level model-call depth helps identify expensive or looping turns and correlate them with latency, failures, interaction modes, model selection, and subagent use. Keeping the rollup on `agentHost.turnCompleted` avoids a Copilot-only tool-event join and gives the same analysis across Agent Host providers.

## Property-by-property parity

No properties are added or changed.

## Measurement-by-measurement parity

| Measurement | Source | Parity |
|---|---|---|
| `modelCallCount` | Deduplicated completed response boundaries from Copilot `assistant.message`, Claude canonical assistant messages, and Codex per-response usage updates | ✅ Same completed model-response-round signal across providers |

Failed provider attempts that never complete a response are deliberately excluded. Existing per-call response telemetry remains the source for attempt-level reliability analysis.

## Row-count and dashboard implications

- Event cadence remains one `agentHost.turnCompleted` row per tracked turn.
- New rows carry a numeric count, including `0` when no completed response was observed.
- Historical rows have no `modelCallCount`; queries must not treat missing historical values as zero.
- Main-agent and subagent calls are attributed to their own turn rows.
- Copilot rollout can be checked by joining to `toolCallDetails` on turn ID and comparing against `numRequests`.

## Semantic-shift ledger

| Field | Shift | Impact |
|---|---|---|
| `modelCallCount` versus provider attempts | Counts completed model responses, not failed retries or transport attempts | Supports turn-depth and loop analysis; attempt-level failure rates continue to use response telemetry |

title: Notify creators when delegated sessions need attention
body:
Depends on #331518.
Fixes #331521.

## Summary

Add opt-in lifecycle notifications from delegated child sessions to their creator after the foundational orchestration relationships in #331518.

- Extend `create_session` with `notifyOnIdle: "once" | "always"`.
- Arm notification delivery when a child starts work.
- Notify its creator when the child needs input, becomes idle, or errors.
- Suppress duplicate terminal notifications and rearm `always` notifications on the next work cycle.
- Observe exact session-status transitions so queued work cannot hide a completed cycle.
- Restore a cold creator before delivery.
- Queue a system notification instead of replacing an active creator turn.
- Persist notification state and consume it only after dispatch so failed creator resolution can retry.

## User benefits

- Notice blocked delegated work without repeatedly checking each child session.
- Run parallel investigations or implementation tasks and receive updates in the creator conversation.
- Preserve notification policy and delivery state when sessions are evicted and restored.
- Avoid child completions interrupting or replacing active creator work.

## Why this is separate

Notification delivery introduces lifecycle observation, deduplication, restoration, and concurrency behavior beyond the durable lineage and discovery model in #331518. Keeping it stacked makes those concerns independently reviewable and revertible.

## Known limitations and follow-ups

- Notifications queued while the creator is busy are process-local. A host restart before the pending message drains can lose that queued delivery; a durable outbox is intentionally out of scope.
- The creator can inspect a child that needs input but cannot complete its pending input request from the creator conversation. #331541 tracks a typed response flow.

## Validation

- Agent Host unit suites: 460 passing, 17 pending.
- Copilot Agent Host provider E2E: 157 passing, 15 pending, including real `create_session` orchestration metadata publication.
- Copilot prompt snapshots: 21 passing across 19 model baselines.

title: Read project customizations on the host's own filesystem
body:
Fixes #331526.

In a remote window the agent host reads project-scope customizations off a URI it cannot resolve, so it finds none. The symptom users hit is that a new chat offers no workspace slash commands until a turn has run.

The window hands the session its working directory in the client's namespace. A diagnostic build of the host logged, for a fresh chat in a dev container:

```
workingDirectory = vscode-remote://dev-container+<hex>/workspace/printstream
userHome         = file:///home/node
```

The host runs inside that container and its file service only answers for `file:`, and `getSessionCustomizations` passes the working directory straight to four disk scans (agents/skills/commands, rules, MCP servers, hooks). Each returns empty rather than raising, so the customizations are absent with nothing in the log.

### Fix

A conversion beside the other agent-host URI helpers, applied only to reads the host performs itself:

```ts
export function toHostLocalUri(resource: URI): URI {
	if (resource.scheme !== Schemas.vscodeRemote) {
		return resource;
	}
	return URI.file(resource.fsPath);
}
```

The path is the part both namespaces agree on, which materialize already relies on by handing the SDK `workingDirectory.fsPath` as its cwd. This applies the same reading to the host's own disk access.

Deliberately narrow:

- **Only `vscode-remote:`.** Stripping the authority off any other scheme would name a local file that is not there rather than the resource meant. A local window compares `file:` to `file:` and is untouched.
- **Only host-side reads.** `workingDirectory` and `workingDirectories` are unchanged for everything else; anything sent back to the client, or compared against client-supplied URIs, keeps the namespace the client uses.

### Verification

- Unit tests for the conversion: the remote rewrite, a `file:` no-op, a non-remote scheme left alone, and that the client authority never leaks into a host read.
- Verified live in a dev-container window. Before: 17 suggestions in a fresh chat, none of them the project's six commands. After: 23, with all six present and no turn run.
- An equivalent command placed in `~/.claude/commands/` was offered before the first turn both before and after the fix, which isolates the failure to project scope rather than to the suggestion pipeline.
- The `file:` URI shape this produces is one the client already resolves: a user-scope command, which has always been surfaced as a host-local `file:` URI, resolves and runs end to end. So project entries now arrive in a shape with a working precedent rather than a new one.

### What is not covered

The conversion is unit-tested and the wiring is verified live, but there is no unit test asserting that `getSessionCustomizations` passes the converted form, because that needs a fully constructed session and the existing tests stub the method rather than exercise it. I would rather say so than imply coverage that is not there.

The Codex customization scan takes working directories the same way and joins onto them, so it looks like the same shape. I have not reproduced it there and have left it out of this change.

title: Improve workspace resolution in agent session tools
body:
Fixes #330948

## Expected user benefits

- Ask an agent to start work in a known project by display name instead of supplying an exact filesystem path.
- Start delegated work from the configured project root rather than accidentally reusing a transient worktree.
- Discover remote project URIs and every folder in a multi-root session through the existing `list_sessions` tool.
- Pass a returned project or working-directory URI directly to `create_session`.
- Receive explicit candidate URIs when a project name is ambiguous instead of silently choosing the wrong workspace.
- Preserve the existing compact fields for model and client compatibility.

## Changes

- Keep workspace discovery within the existing `list_sessions` and `create_session` tools rather than adding another model-visible tool.
- Add `projectUri` to serialized sessions while preserving the human-readable `project` field.
- Add `workingDirectories` for multi-root sessions while preserving the primary `workingDirectory` field.
- Let the `list_sessions.workspace` filter match a project display name, project URI, or any working directory.
- Let `create_session.workspace` resolve a unique project display name to its configured project root.
- Reject ambiguous project names with the candidate project URIs.
- Compare parsed workspace URIs with URI comparison semantics instead of string-key deduplication.
- Cover remote URIs, multi-root metadata, configured-root preference, ambiguous names, and remote cross-provider creation.

## Design rationale

Workspace metadata already comes from known session metadata, so a separate `list_workspaces` tool would be another projection of the same authority and would add its description and schema to every model prompt. Extending the existing tools closes the actual information gap with no extra always-advertised tool:

1. `list_sessions({ includeArchived: true, workspace: "Visual Studio Code" })` can locate matching known sessions and returns the configured `projectUri` plus working directories.
2. `create_session({ workspace: "Visual Studio Code", ... })` resolves the name directly when unique.
3. The agent can pass an explicit returned URI when several projects share a name.

Provider selection remains model-driven, as it is today. A test verifies that a remote project URI discovered from one session can be used to create a session with a model from another provider.

## Scope

Only projects already visible through known Agent Host sessions are resolved by name. A global recent-workspace catalog, fuzzy ranking, and new-folder permission flows remain out of scope.

## Follow-up

- #331553 tracks starting an agent session without a folder and binding the existing conversation to a workspace later, after the request or context identifies the appropriate project.

title: Add cross-session delegation and notifications
body:
Part of microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#8366.
Part of #331521.

## Scope

A session remains the user-visible unit of work: one workspace/worktree, lifecycle, and aggregate diff. `create_chat` is the preferred primitive for parallel subtasks that should stay within that unit.

This PR adds coordination for the complementary cross-session case, where delegated work needs an independent workspace, worktree or branch, provider, or lifecycle.

## Expected user benefits

- Delegate independently scoped work across repositories, workspaces, or branches.
- Discover delegated sessions through durable creator/parent relationships and labels.
- Inspect child context, steer work, and receive completion or input-needed notifications without polling.
- Keep fire-and-forget work isolated by disabling direct child-to-creator coordination.

## Changes

- Guide models to prefer `create_chat` for shared-workspace subtasks and reserve `create_session` for independently scoped work.
- Persist creator identity separately from hierarchy placement, with an optional label and coordination policy.
- Extend `create_session` with `coordinateWithCreator`, `notifyOnIdle`, and `label`.
- Extend `list_sessions` with parent and label filters and expose permitted orchestration metadata.
- Enforce disabled creator coordination across relationship discovery and prompt-producing tools.
- Restore persisted orchestration metadata and notification state.
- Deliver opt-in input-needed, idle, and error notifications through a dedicated coordination service, queueing behind active creator work.

## Alignment with GitHub Copilot app

The relationship and notification primitives align with the GitHub Copilot app, while VS Code additionally distinguishes chats within a session. The App-style session workflow remains available for genuinely independent work; same-session orchestration should use chats so users retain one aggregate diff.

## Follow-ups

- #331554 tracks delegated-work UX; the parent session and its aggregate result should remain primary.
- #331541 tracks answering a child's pending input request directly from the creator.

title: Add standalone Copilot source build pipeline
body:
## Summary

- add a standalone pipeline that builds the Copilot SDK and all runtime targets from source
- publish the source-built npm packages to the internal VS Code feed
- queue the existing product build with `VSCODE_SDK_CANARY_VERSION` and `VSCODE_CLI_CANARY_VERSION` overrides
- leave the existing product pipeline unchanged
- run artifact-based sanity tests when the queued product build is unpublished
- incorporate the review feedback from #330768

## Validation

- `node --experimental-strip-types --test build/lib/test/copilotSourcePipeline.test.ts build/lib/test/copilot.test.ts` (24 tests passed)
- pre-commit hygiene
- [Current Copilot source validation 466127](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=466127) is running against validation commit `138e7825393` based on PR head `759646de601`; product publish and release are disabled
- Prior [Copilot source pipeline 465834](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=465834) succeeded for all eight runtime targets and published `0.0.0-vscode.1.134.0.465834`
- Prior [product build 465837](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=465837) succeeded across all stages with the SDK/runtime overrides

## Failure investigation

[Initial run 464620](https://dev.azure.com/monacotools/Monaco/_build/results?buildId=464620) exposed direct Corepack, Cargo, and PyPI access blocked by 1ES network isolation. The pipeline now provisions the runtime-pinned pnpm through authenticated npm, uses the internal Cargo and Python feeds, installs target-capable rustup alongside RustInstaller, and downloads each runtime artifact by explicit name.

Supersedes #330768.

## Upstream build overlap and future simplification

No upstream implementation is copied verbatim. Of the approximately 1,755 production lines added here:

- roughly 300 lines reimplement release/package behavior such as version stamping, package metadata assembly, source-map policy, and publication checks
- roughly 350–450 lines mirror upstream build orchestration and entrypoint contracts while delegating the actual builds
- roughly 1,000–1,100 lines are VS Code/Azure-specific authentication, internal-feed, artifact, validation, and product-build integration

For the SDK, this pipeline delegates compilation to the SDK repository’s build command but currently mirrors its install, version, package, and publish sequence. For the private runtime repository, this pipeline delegates native compilation, JavaScript bundling, and package staging to repository-owned entrypoints; it does not reproduce those implementations. VS Code owns secure checkout, target fan-out, toolchain/feed setup, artifact validation, internal package publication, and the product-build handoff.

A useful follow-up would be stable upstream entrypoints that emit publish-ready artifacts:

- an SDK entrypoint accepting the desired package version and runtime dependency version and returning an npm tarball
- a runtime entrypoint accepting target and version inputs and returning a final platform package, ideally alongside a supported-target manifest

With those contracts, we could substantially simplify or remove `buildCopilotOverride.ts`, much of `copilotRuntimeSource.ts`, `install-runtime-build-toolchain.ts`, the runtime package assembly in `copilotSourcePublish.ts`, and most of `source-publish-runtime-job.yml`. Package-only entrypoints would remove an estimated 300–450 lines; entrypoints that also own toolchain/bootstrap behavior could remove approximately 600–800 lines.

The runtime references above intentionally describe contracts and responsibilities only; they do not quote or link to private source.

## Authoritative build overrides

The mechanism supports a generic `package.json` `buildOverrides` map from package name to immutable source commit. The Copilot source pipeline reads those values directly; it no longer accepts SDK/runtime source-ref parameters. This PR intentionally leaves the map absent after validation, so normal product builds remain unchanged; a branch adds the map only when it intentionally needs source-built dependencies. Internal package versions are deterministic from the VS Code version and full VS Code commit, and the child product build is pinned to that exact branch and commit.

Every published source package carries provenance metadata for the VS Code commit, source commit, dependency version, and diagnostic source-build ID. Product builds automatically detect committed Copilot overrides, reconstruct the expected internal version, validate provenance, and apply it. If matching packages were not published, the build fails with a link to the Copilot source pipeline. This failure is intentional while an override is committed: it must never be silently ignored. The validated overrides were removed from this PR after the successful source/product build runs. Manual SDK canary parameters remain supported only when no Copilot `buildOverrides` are present.

## Summary

Fix false-positive **Input needed** status in the Agents window when a visible Agent Host session keeps working after a confirmation has been resolved.

## Root cause

The Agent Host protocol already cleared the input request and changed the aggregate session state back to `InProgress`. However, the Agents-window provider used its live `SessionState` subscription only to synchronize configuration, metadata, changesets, and the per-chat catalog.

The top-level `ISession` status and activity were updated only by root summary notifications or a later `listSessions()` refresh. This allowed the session row to retain an older `NeedsInput` value while a subagent or peer chat continued running.

## Fix

- Reconcile the top-level session status and activity from each subscribed `SessionState` snapshot.
- Keep read and archive flags synchronized through the same path.
- Share protocol-status translation between live snapshots and root summary notifications.
- Emit the existing provider change event only when the adapted values change.
- Document the live-snapshot ownership contract for visible Agent Host sessions.

This does not suppress legitimate confirmations, change protocol status precedence, special-case subagents, or add polling.

## Test plan

- Added a regression where:
  - the list snapshot starts at `InputNeeded`;
  - confirmation has been resolved;
  - the subscribed session state is `InProgress`;
  - a tool-origin subagent chat remains active.
- Verified that the top-level session immediately exposes `InProgress`, current activity text, and the correct read state without waiting for turn completion or a session-list refresh.

## Description

The single `mouseMarker` in `ToggleScreencastModeAction` was always parented to `layoutService.activeContainer`. Mouse listeners fire for events from any window and position the marker using the event's `clientX`/`clientY`, which are relative to the originating window.

The omni chat input window deliberately keeps the **main** window active while it is shown (unless it holds focus). So hovering it left `activeContainer` pointing at the main window while the coordinates came from the omni window — placing the marker in the wrong container with mismatched coordinates. Other aux windows don't reroute the active window, so they were unaffected.

- **`src/vs/workbench/browser/actions/developerActions.ts`** — on each mouse event, re-parent the marker to the container of the window where the event originated before positioning:

```ts
const targetContainer = layoutService.getContainer(getWindow(e));
if (mouseMarker.parentElement !== targetContainer) {
    targetContainer.appendChild(mouseMarker);
}
```

This is a general correctness fix rather than an omni-specific special case.

title: agentHost: retry legacy migration when a provider cannot enumerate yet
body:
Fixes #331452

## Problem

`listChatsToMigrate()` returns `undefined` to mean *"this provider cannot enumerate its catalog yet"* (e.g. its client is still starting), not *"there is nothing to migrate"*. `_migrateLegacyProviderChats` treated the two as the same and returned. `_ensureLegacyChatsMigrated` is invoked only from `registerProvider`, and nothing re-arms it, so a single early return disabled the backfill for the entire process.

Since #329633 / #330665 made the session registry the source of truth for enumeration, this backfill is what populates a newly created registry. Losing that race meant `listSessions()` published a near-empty registry as authoritative, and `BaseAgentHostSessionsProvider._refreshSessions` evicted every cached session missing from it — sessions whose data was intact on disk.

## From the reporting user's logs

```
11:06:23.145  [Copilot] Listing chats to migrate...
11:06:25.467  [Copilot] Client unavailable while listing chats to migrate:
              Copilot startup config changed while the client was starting
11:06:25.467  [Copilot] Listing chats to migrate...
11:06:26.305  [Copilot] CopilotClient started successfully
11:06:26.434  [Copilot] Found 23 legacy sessions
11:06:30.967  [Copilot] Chat discovery: ... 1 already known to Agent Host ...
```

The migration gave up at `25.467`. One second later the same call returned all 23 sessions — but that caller was the read-only fallback in `_getSessionMetadataFromCatalog`, which does `allSessions?.find(...)` and discards the rest. Hence `1 already known to Agent Host`: of 93 sessions on disk, only the restored one reached the registry.

Corroborated by the user's database, which had `sessionRegistryBackfilled:claude` and `sessionRegistryBackfilled:codex` but not `sessionRegistryBackfilled:copilotcli`.

## Changes

- `_enumerateLegacyProviderChatsWithRetry` retries with bounded backoff instead of giving up on the first "not ready".
- `_incompleteProviderCatalogs` tracks providers whose backfill has not completed a real enumeration. It is set *before* enumerating, so a throw counts too.
- `_ensureProviderCatalogsComplete` replaces the bare `_awaitInitialProviderMigration()` call in `_computeSessions`: it awaits the initial pass, re-attempts incomplete providers **in-process**, and otherwise throws. Failing is the safe signal — `_refreshSessions` already treats a rejection as transient, keeping its cache and retrying with backoff, so no protocol change is needed.
- The migration's `register` call now uses `_retryRegistryMutation`, for parity with `_registerDiscoveredChats`.
- Per-pass logging of enumerated/registered counts.

The retry is a latency optimisation; the completeness gate is the correctness fix. A timing budget alone would still lose on a slow enough machine.

## Tests

Three regression tests: deferred-then-successful enumeration, a never-ready provider failing the listing rather than publishing an empty registry, and in-process recovery without a restart. Each fails without the production change.

`a discovery signal does not bypass completed legacy migration semantics` asserted `migrationCalls: 1, registered: []` for a provider that returned `undefined`, which encoded this bug as intended behaviour. Rewritten to keep its real purpose — a *completed* migration is not re-run — while allowing an *unperformed* one to be retried.

Typecheck clean; full node unit suite passing. Note that the tests use a mock agent, so they cover the logic rather than real provider-client startup timing.

## Notes

Affected users self-heal: the failed run never wrote `sessionRegistryBackfilled:<provider>`, so the corrected migration re-runs. This can also surface older on-disk sessions that were never registered — correct migration behaviour, but it may look like sessions appearing from nowhere.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Per-provider completeness + a catalog generation in the protocol, so clients can evict precisely instead of relying on all-or-nothing failure.
- `_computeSessions` drops registry rows when `getChatMetadata` fails or returns `undefined` — a separate pre-existing eviction vector.
- A stale in-flight list response can still race late registrations; `_registryEpoch` invalidates memoization but is not re-checked before returning.

title: Reconcile external sessions in a single catalog pass
body:
## Problem

Changing `chat.agentSessions.showExternal` took **30-50 seconds** to take effect on a profile with ~600 sessions.

`_reconcileExternalSessions` walked the whole session catalog **once per mode** on a mode change, and each walk opens every registered session's database (`Limiter(4)`). The session list kept showing the old setting for that entire window.

From a real log:

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 13:49:01 | `showExternalSessions: last7Days` mirrored to the host |
| 13:49:35 | catalog pass #1 finishes (`hid 288 of 599 … 'none'`) |
| 13:49:51 | catalog pass #2 finishes → sessions finally appear (**~50s**) |
| 13:50:53 | `showExternalSessions: none` mirrored to the host |
| 13:51:30 | user opens an unrelated session |
| 13:51:32 | reconciliation finishes → **all external sessions disappear (~39s late)** |

The delayed retraction landing two seconds after an unrelated click made it look like opening a session had destroyed the list.

## Change

Derive both the outgoing and incoming visible sets from a **single** `listSessions(All)` pass. `All` is a superset of every mode and `_shouldIncludeSession` is a pure predicate over the rows, so this is equivalent. Non-mode-change reconciliations keep the plain current-mode path so they still share the in-flight list cache.

## Logging

None of the above was diagnosable from logs — nothing recorded why the mode changed, which window changed it, or how long reconciliation took. Added:

- **`RemoteAgentHostProtocolClient`** — each window logs what it mirrors into the shared host root config and from which configuration target. These keys are host-level and last-writer-wins across windows, so this identifies which window wrote a value.
- **`AgentService`** — external-sessions mode transitions (`'last7Days' -> 'none'`).
- **`AgentService`** — reconciliation duration plus published/retracted/visible counts.
- **`AgentService`** — catalog pass timing, promoted to `info` above 1s.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- A single pass over hundreds of session databases is still seconds; caching per-session metadata would remove the disk work from a mode change entirely.
- In `Recent` mode every external session `modifiedAt` change queues a full catalog pass.
- One "open session" fires three parallel `subscribe` calls that each independently attempt worktree recreation, logging the same failure 3-4 times per click.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` clean against latest `main`.
- Node unit suite: 14713 passing, 7 failing — all 7 pre-existing in `sessionPermissions.test.js` (shell-redirect path resolution), identical to the baseline run before these changes.
- Existing `AgentService` external-sessions mode-transition tests cover this path and pass.
