title: markdown: fix: open absolute file links in Markdown editor
body:
## Summary

Fix absolute filesystem links in the experimental Markdown editor without changing standard Markdown link semantics.

- Preserve the Markdown language service's normal resolution whenever its target exists or cannot be inspected reliably.
- Fall back to an authored absolute path only when the normal target is definitely missing and the absolute candidate is definitely an existing file.
- Enable the fallback only from the experimental Markdown custom editor's user-click path; standard preview and passive rich-link resolution remain unchanged.
- Model JSON-RPC's `null` no-result response and normalize it to `undefined` at the client boundary.

## Problem

Markdown links are URI references, so a slash-prefixed link such as `/tmp/example.md` is normally interpreted as root-relative to the workspace. The Markdown language service may return that workspace-relative target even when it does not exist in order to support create-file workflows.

In the experimental Markdown editor, this means clicking a link to an existing absolute filesystem file can instead open a nonexistent workspace-relative file and show the create-file flow.

Globally redefining slash-prefixed Markdown links as filesystem paths would break portable repository links such as `/docs/setup.md`, so this change keeps normal Markdown resolution authoritative and adds a conservative fallback.

## Resolution behavior

For the explicitly fallback-enabled open call:

1. Resolve the link normally through the Markdown language service.
2. Return immediately if there is no concrete normal target, for external links, or for links that cannot safely identify an absolute filesystem path.
3. Preserve an existing normal target.
4. Preserve the normal result if its filesystem provider is unavailable or stat returns an indeterminate error.
5. Only when the normal target is definitely missing, stat the absolute candidate.
6. Use the candidate only when it definitely exists and is not a directory.

Filesystem probes distinguish `found`, `notFound`, and `unavailable`. Since this is speculative behavior, permissions failures and missing providers preserve the established result instead of breaking the click.

## Scope and safety

- A single `MdLinkOpener` is shared, but only the Markdown editor's `openLink` message handler explicitly enables the fallback.
- Passive rich-link presentation resolution never enables the fallback and performs no additional filesystem probes.
- Absolute paths are considered only for `file` and `vscode-remote` source documents.
- Remote paths retain the source scheme and authority, so they resolve on the remote filesystem.
- Untitled and virtual-workspace documents do not target the local machine.
- Explicit URI schemes—including all `file:` URIs—remain outside this fallback.
- Protocol-relative, UNC, authority-bearing, mixed-separator, and percent-encoded UNC variants are rejected before filesystem access. A post-`Uri.file()` authority check provides defense in depth.
- Drive-letter paths are considered only on Windows extension hosts, preventing relative probes on macOS, Linux, and web.
- Directories are not reinterpreted through the file-opening fallback.
- Numeric line-fragment handling remains authoritative.

The fallback checks the exact authored path. It does not infer a `.md` extension or recompute heading-name anchors. It also requires the language service to provide a normal target, so a standalone document without workspace-resolution context may remain unchanged when the language service returns no target.

## Validation

- Markdown extension TypeScript compilation: passed with 0 errors.
- Targeted ESLint across all eight modified files: passed.
- Focused desktop extension-host suite: 14 passing.
- Focused browser extension-host suite: 14 passing.
- Repository hygiene pre-commit hook: passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.

## Related discussion

Related to #307837, which discussed a similar fallback for the built-in Markdown flow. This change intentionally has a narrower scope: only the experimental Markdown custom editor opts in, while standard preview behavior remains unchanged.

The outer hover clipped the overflow, which made metadata and action rows unreachable. `HoverWidget.layout()` clears the content node's previous `maxHeight` before recalculating the hover dimensions. The layout previously restored a height constraint only on the outer hover container, so the `DomScrollableElement` content kept its full height and did not expose an internal scroll range. This change: - clears the outer hover's previous height constraint before measuring its natural layout; - reserves space for borders and fixed status, action, and hint rows; - constrains the scrollable content to the remaining available hover height; - preserves the existing vertical scrollbar padding behavior once content overflows; and - keeps short hover content non-scrollable. The fix is implemented in the shared hover widget so all workbench hover consumers receive consistent overflow behavior. ## Verification - HoverService unit suite on current `main` with this change: `37 passing` - Pre-commit hygiene: passed for both changed files - Manually verified with a 40-line commit body in Source Control Graph: - content viewport: 400 px - content scroll height: 931 px - mouse-wheel input increased `scrollTop` from 0 to 50 - metadata and the final commit-message lines are reachable through the hover scrollbar ## Screenshot **Before** **After**

title: agentHost: Exclude subagent chats from billed credit telemetry
body:
Addresses the review comment on #330931.

## Problem
`CopilotAgentSession` folds each subagent charge into the parent turn's `totalNanoAiu` and *also* emits the same cumulative component on the child chat. Because `agentHost.turnCompleted` recorded both channels, summing `billedNanoAiu` across events double-counted nested usage.

## Fix
Skip subagent chat channels when recording billed credits, mirroring the guard `_trackTurnUsage` already applies for the same reason. Credits stay attributed to the parent turn, which already includes the subagent cost, so the measurement remains additive.

## Validation
- `npm run transpile-client`
- `.\scripts\test.bat --run src\vs\platform\agentHost\test\node\agentHostTurnTelemetry.test.ts` (25 passing)
- Confirmed the new parent-plus-subagent test fails without the guard: the subagent turn reported 1e9 that the parent's 3e9 already contained, so the sum was 4e9 instead of 3e9.

Note: this same fix ships together with the feature in the `release/1.134` backport (#331436).

title: Fix Agent Merge stalling on indeterminate pull request state
body:
## Problem

Agent Merge silently stalled: it bound to the pull request, then reported `Gate is indeterminate` roughly 40 times over 32 minutes and never looked at the CI failures or PR comments it was configured to handle.

```
23:13:11 Started session runtime: overrides=addressReviews,fixCI,mergePullRequest,resolveConflicts
23:13:20 Bound session to its pull request
23:13:35 Pull request state ready
23:13:35 Gate is indeterminate: reason=Pull request state is incomplete or stale   <- x40
23:45:07 Disabling Agent Merge: the checked-out branch changed while PR state was refreshing
```

Two independent bugs in the GitHub platform layer, both reproduced against `api.github.com`.

## Bug 1: the capability probe exceeded GitHub's introspection limit

`capabilitiesQuery` selected `__Type.fields` three times; GitHub allows two. The live response:

```
HTTP/2.0 200 OK
{"errors":[{"type":"INTROSPECTION_LIMIT_EXCEEDED",
  "message":"Introspection fields may only be used 2 times, but some fields were used more than that: __Type.fields (3)"}]}
```

HTTP 200 with errors means `_probe` returned `unavailableCapabilities`, which is why every log line reported `graphql=false` for **api.github.com**. Since `INTROSPECTION_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` is not a schema-validation error the result was never cached, so the probe repeated forever.

That cascades through `plan()`: `reviewThreads` -> `unavailable`, `checks` -> `restChecksFallback`, `mergeability` -> `restMergeabilityFallback`, all hardcoded `complete: false`. `evaluateAgentMerge` requires all three complete, so the gate could only ever return `'Pull request state is incomplete or stale'`.

`RequirableByPullRequest` now gets an existence check rather than a field enumeration. This is exact, not a heuristic: `isRequired` is that interface's only field, confirmed against the live schema.

## Bug 2: every conditional REST GET threw on 304

```
REST GET api.github.com/repos/microsoft/vscode/pulls/331332/reviews failed (malformedResponse:304)
REST GET .../commits/d2c2865.../status failed (malformedResponse:304)
REST GET .../commits/d2c2865.../check-runs failed (malformedResponse:304)
```

GitHub may answer a conditional request with a reissued validator. Verified live:

```
200-path etag=[W/"4ee1eec6a2ddc9...2694"]
304-path etag=[  "4ee1eec6a2ddc9...2694"]
```

The literal comparison treated this as a protocol violation. It was also self-perpetuating: the stored validator was never updated, so each later revalidation resent the stale `If-None-Match` and failed identically until the cache was evicted, which stopped `checks` and `submittedReviews` from refreshing at all.

A 304 backed by a cached entry is now accepted, and the reissued ETag and Link are adopted so the next revalidation sends the validator GitHub last handed out.

## Logging

`graphql=false` is indistinguishable from a legitimately old GitHub Enterprise host, which is what hid this for so long. Probe errors that disable GraphQL are now logged (`warn` for unexpected errors, `debug` for genuine schema mismatches) with the GraphQL error type included, so `INTROSPECTION_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` would point straight at the cause.

## Testing

- `stays within the GitHub introspection budget` - asserts the query never regresses past two `fields` selections
- `warns when an unexpected probe error disables GraphQL capabilities`
- `adopts a reissued validator when revalidating with a 304` - seeds `"old"`, returns a 304 carrying `W/"new"`, and asserts the *next* revalidation sends `If-None-Match: W/"new"`, proving the stored validator was refreshed rather than left stale
- `rejects a 304 that answers no cached representation` - keeps the genuine protocol violation covered

90 tests pass in `vs/platform/github/test/node`, 15 in the agent merge suites, and `typecheck-client` is clean.

title: Recover chats with inaccessible vision history
body:
Fixes #331428

Restored chats can replay an uploaded historical image after its attachment URL
is no longer accessible. CAPI returns `vision_attachment_not_accessible`, but
Agent mode currently retries the unchanged request and later turns replay the
same stale image.

This change:

- Classifies `vision_attachment_not_accessible` consistently for HTTP and
  WebSocket responses.
- Prevents generic Agent mode retries for only this error code.
- Retries once without the historical image set implicated by the failed
  request.
- Closes stale WebSocket state and resubmits the complete cleaned request.
- Persists SHA-256 hashes of unavailable image sources in existing turn
  metadata, never raw URLs or image bytes.
- Omits only matching historical sources after restoration.
- Preserves images attached after recovery.
- Preserves existing behavior for unrelated bad requests, server failures,
  and network failures.

The backend error does not identify which image failed. When several historical
images were present in the failed request, the recovery conservatively
quarantines that historical image set.

This PR does not make uploaded attachment URLs durable. A complete storage fix
would retain durable attachment identity or image bytes and regenerate URLs
when restoring history. That requires separate decisions about retention,
privacy, session size, migration, and VS Code/Copilot ownership.

Validation:

- Reproduces a restored-history request containing an inaccessible image.
- Proves the clean retry succeeds without replaying that image.
- Proves a later turn remains usable.
- Proves recovery metadata survives conversation restoration.
- Proves images added after recovery remain available.
- Covers HTTP and WebSocket recovery.
- Confirms unrelated `BadRequest` retry behavior remains unchanged.
- Confirms server and network retries remain unchanged.
- 119 focused tests pass.
- Extension TypeScript check passes.
- Scoped ESLint passes.
- `git diff --check` passes.

title: Preserve session type when splitting a Chat Editor
body:
Fixes #331422

### Problem

Splitting a Chat Editor (`View: Split Editor`) that hosts a running agent-host session produced a new pane with an **invalid chat input state** — the Agent Mode (`Interactive`/`Plan`) picker was missing and permission controls were wrong.

### Root cause

`View: Split Editor` duplicates the editor via `ChatEditorInput.copy()`, which returned a **generic `vscode-chat-editor:` placeholder** with no session type. `ChatEditor.setInput()` reads the session type **before** resolving the input; the placeholder classifies as `local`, so the widget is `unlockFromCodingAgent()`ed. The input then resolves into a **new agent-host session**, but the lock decision is never revisited, so the `chatIsAgentHostSession` context key stays `false` and the Agent Mode picker (gated on it) is filtered out.

The working `Ctrl+N` / New Chat path (`clearChatEditor`) avoids this by replacing the editor with a **typed** URI up front, so `setInput()` sees the real type before resolving.

### Fix

Make `ChatEditorInput.copy()` mint a new **untitled URI of the source pane's own session type** (local or agent-host), so a split reproduces the source harness (Claude → Claude, Copilot → Copilot, Codex → Codex) and `setInput()` locks the widget correctly before rendering. When the source type is unknown or cannot start a new session, it falls back to the previous generic URI.

Also extracts a shared `getNewChatSessionResource(sessionType)` helper into `chatUri.ts` and reuses it from `clearChatEditor` and the default session-resource helpers in `constants.ts`, removing three copies of the same URI-construction logic.

### Scope

- New split panes start an **empty** chat of the same type (they do not fork the source conversation's live model/mode/permission overrides).
- This does not change the pre-resolve behavior of `ChatEditor.setInput()` for other entry points (Move Chat to window, Import); those remain as-is.

### Testing

- `npm run typecheck-client` — passes.
- Unit tests: `ChatEditorInput` suite — 7 passing, including 3 new regression tests (agent-host source → distinct same-type untitled URI; local source → new local session; guard-false → generic fallback).
- Manual: split Copilot / Claude / Codex editors → same type + Agent Mode picker + correct permissions; split a local chat → stays local.

title: Fix section checkbox state when all items are unchecked
body:
## Summary

The Agent Customizations migration UI (introduced in #330539 / #330772, tested in #330793) groups migration candidates (e.g. Workspace/User prompt files, or Agents/Instructions) under a section with a "select all" group checkbox. Unchecking every individual item in a group was expected to also uncheck the group checkbox, but it stayed checked.

## Root cause

`renderCustomizationMigrationPage` computes each group checkbox's initial `checked` state once, from `customizations.every(...)`, when the group is rendered. Clicking the group checkbox itself triggers a full page re-render (which recomputes this correctly), but toggling an individual item's checkbox only updated the item's own state — nothing recalculated or updated the containing group's checkbox afterward, so it kept showing whatever state it had at the last full render.

## Fix

`renderSelectionCheckbox`/`renderItem` now accept an optional `onSelectionChange` callback. `renderGroup` passes a callback that recomputes `customizations.every(...)` for that group and updates `groupCheckbox.checked` accordingly, so the group checkbox stays in sync as individual items are (un)checked — without a full page re-render.

## Tests added

Added a regression test in `aiCustomizationManagementEditor.test.ts`: `unchecking every item in a migration group unchecks the group checkbox`. It renders a group with two items, unchecks them one at a time, and asserts the group checkbox's `aria-checked` goes to `false` after the first uncheck and stays `false` after the last — then re-checking both items brings it back to `true`. Verified this test fails (group checkbox stays `true`) against the unpatched code and passes with the fix.

## Validation performed

- `npm run typecheck-client` — no errors
- `scripts\test.bat --run vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/browser/aiCustomization/aiCustomizationManagementEditor.test.js` — 12/12 passing
- `scripts\test.bat --runGlob "**/aiCustomization*.test.js"` — full related suite, 61/61 passing

title: agentHost: reselect new-chat folder when its workspace folder is removed
body:
Fixes #331200

## Problem

In a multi-root Editor Window, a new (untitled) agent-host chat pins a **primary working directory** (e.g. folder `B` in a workspace `[A, B, C]`). When the user removes folder `B` from the workspace, the new Chat Editor kept showing `B` as selected — and the Folder picker could even become disabled. The not-yet-started session should instead reselect the folder a freshly created chat would pick (a still-valid sticky default, otherwise the first remaining folder `A`).

## Root cause

For an untitled chat the selected primary lives in **two** places, neither of which was invalidated on a workspace-folder change:

1. the per-session explicit selection in `AgentHostNewSessionFolderService`, and
2. the provisional backend session's immutable primary in `AgentHostUntitledProvisionalSessionService` (surfaced to the chip via `getWorkingDirectory`).

Because the picker chip, config chips, and first-Send / `tryRebind` all read from these, a UI-only fix would have left the provisional session — and the first prompt — still rooted in the removed folder.

A started session is different: its working directory is the agent's fixed process root, so it must keep the removed primary (owned by `AgentHostSessionWorkingDirectorySynchronizer`, unchanged here).

## Changes

All under `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/`:

- **`agentHostNewSessionFolderService.ts`** — on `onDidChangeWorkspaceFolders`, clear an explicit per-session selection whose folder is in `event.removed` and no longer present (using `extUriBiasedIgnorePathCase`). The window-level sticky default is intentionally left intact so it resurfaces if the folder is re-added. Added `resolveNewSessionPrimary()` implementing new-session precedence (valid explicit → valid sticky default → first workspace folder → `undefined`), validated against the current folders so it is order-independent between the two listeners.
- **`agentHostUntitledProvisionalSessionService.ts`** — when an **untitled** draft's primary is removed, reselect via `resolveNewSessionPrimary()` and recreate the provisional at the new primary (widened `_changeWorkingDirectory` to accept `undefined` for an emptied workspace). Gated with `isUntitledChatSession` so started/rebound entries (kept in `_entries` under their real resource) keep their immutable primary and only reconcile secondaries.
- **`agentHostFolderPickerActionItem.ts`** — removed the render-time `clear()` side effect (the service now owns staleness; standalone external folders are preserved) and set the ARIA label after the visible text is written (the base derives the label from `element.textContent`, so it previously lagged one selection behind).

## Reviewer notes

- Reselection is a fall-through (default/first), not a written explicit choice, so it mirrors a brand-new chat and doesn't corrupt the sticky "last picked" default.
- Standalone folders outside the workspace are preserved: detection is gated on `event.removed`, so a folder that was never a workspace member is never treated as stale.
- The ungated `onDidChangeFolder → _changeWorkingDirectory` path stays safe for started sessions because on removal the folder service *clears* (never reselects) the selection, so it no-ops; a comment documents this coupling.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck-client` — clean
- Hygiene (`npm run precommit`) — clean
- Unit suites (Electron runner):
  - `agentHostNewSessionFolderService.test.ts` — 12/12 (added: removed-selection clears; sticky default survives + resurfaces on re-add; external selection preserved; `resolveNewSessionPrimary` precedence)
  - `agentHostUntitledProvisionalSessionService.test.ts` — 46/46 (rewrote the test that asserted a removed primary is retained → now asserts reselection; added: single-working-directory provider reselect, zero-folders recreate, secondary-only preservation, reorder no-op, multiple drafts, started-session preservation, and a removal-racing-first-Send `tryRebind` case)
  - `agentHostChatContribution` / `agentHostGenericConfigChips` / `agentHostFolderPickerDecision` / `agentHostFolderPickerTip` — all green

title: fix: use fresh service accessor when lazily initializing chat attachment context (fixes #329610)
body:
## Summary

Opening the context menu on a chat symbol attachment (or a chat inline symbol anchor) throws `Illegal state: service accessor is only valid during the invocation of its target method`.

`hookUpSymbolAttachmentDragAndContextMenu` captures the `ServicesAccessor` passed to it via `invokeFunction`, but uses it *lazily* from inside the `ensureContextKeyService` closure, which runs on context-menu open — by then the accessor has already expired, so `accessor.get(IFileService)` inside `setResourceContext` throws.

Fixes #329610
Fixes #331400

## Root cause

Introduced by #300009, which moved the scoped context-key-service creation (and the `setResourceContext(accessor, ...)` call) out of the synchronous `invokeFunction` body and into the lazy `ensureContextKeyService` closure. The captured `accessor` is only valid during the original `invokeFunction` invocation, so the deferred `accessor.get(...)` call now throws.

## Fix

In `ensureContextKeyService`, obtain a fresh accessor by wrapping the deferred `setResourceContext` call in `instantiationService.invokeFunction(...)` instead of reusing the stale captured `accessor`. `instantiationService` is already captured at the top of the function and remains valid for the widget's lifetime — this mirrors the pattern already used a few lines above in the `dragstart` handler (`instantiationService.invokeFunction(accessor => fillEditorsDragData(...))`).

## Note for reviewers

#331414 is an open alternative fix for the same root cause (#329610) that resolves services eagerly and changes `setResourceContext`'s signature. This PR is a smaller, more surgical diff (1 line) that reuses an existing pattern in the file rather than reshaping the helper's signature — posting it so maintainers can pick whichever approach they prefer; happy to close this in favor of #331414 if that's preferred.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck-client` passes
- [x] `node build/eslint.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/attachments/chatAttachmentWidgets.ts` passes with no warnings
- [x] Manual repro: attach a symbol to chat input / get a response with an inline symbol anchor, right-click it, confirm no console error and the context menu populates resource-based actions correctly

title: agentHost: expand the legacy enterprise settings bridge
body:
## Summary

Expands the gated legacy-settings bridge (`chat.agentHost.copilot.mapLegacySettingsToManagedSettings`) beyond its initial two mappings, and clears the structural debt that made expanding it unsafe.

Refs #331143, #330349, #330472, github/copilot-sdk-internal#209

## What this does

| VS Code setting | Trigger | SDK contribution |
|---|---|---|
| `chat.tools.global.autoApprove` | policy `false` | `disableBypassPermissionsMode: 'disable'` *(existing)* |
| `chat.tools.terminal.enableAutoApprove` | `false` | `ask: ['Shell']` *(existing)* |
| `chat.agent.deniedNetworkDomains` | filter on, list populated | `deny: ['Domain(d)', …]` **(new)** |
| `chat.agent.networkFilter` | on, neither list configured | `deny: ['Domain']` **(new)** |
| `chat.tools.terminal.autoApprove` | entries valued `false` | `ask: ['Shell(cmd)', …]` **(new)** |

## Why several candidate mappings were deliberately *not* added

I ran a three-model review council over the plan and cross-checked its claims against the agent runtime. Four proposed mappings turned out to be wrong, and one proposed "fix" was actively dangerous:

- **Allow-list padding was going to be the headline fix — it is a security bug.** The plan was to pad `allow` with wildcards so a restriction stayed inside its own rule family. But a covered request resolves to `managed_allow`, which the runtime returns as **approved without prompting**, and the runtime only intersects allow lists when more than one managed source supplies one. A lone list from VS Code is never intersected, so padding would have granted blanket auto-approval and could have *relaxed* an MDM policy. This bridge now never emits `allow`, and says why.
- **`chat.agent.allowedNetworkDomains`** — VS Code blocks whatever a populated allow list omits; a managed `allow` does not block what it omits, so bridging it would silently downgrade a block into a prompt.
- **`chat.tools.eligibleForAutoApproval`** — keyed on tool reference names, but the SDK only has families, so a per-tool `false` would become a family-wide restriction, and most tool names have no family at all.
- **`chat.agent.enabled`** — reviewers disagreed on the correct rule set (one flagged the proposed `Domain` deny as over-restrictive, another flagged the omission of `Read` as a file-exfiltration gap), which is itself evidence the mapping is not well-founded. VS Code already blocks these sessions host-side.
- **`chat.defaultConfiguration.approvals`** — a startup preference rather than an enterprise restriction, and `allow-auto-only` is rejected by both the SDK type and the runtime parser.
- **`chat.tools.edits.autoApprove`** — already enforced host-side with ordered last-match-wins semantics that managed rules cannot represent.

Anything requiring the SDK's per-session contract to accept more than `permissions` (MCP allow/deny lists, plugins, marketplaces, hooks, model, telemetry, sandbox, remote control) stays out of scope; those already reach the runtime through Copilot-side MDM.

## Notable corrections to the shipped behavior

- `chat.tools.terminal.autoApprove: false` means *require explicit approval*, so it maps to `ask`, not `deny` — `deny` is terminal in the runtime and would remove the user's approval path.
- `Domain(*)` is not an all-domains wildcard; rule arguments are normalized as URL patterns. The kind-only `Domain` rule is the correct form.
- Rules are now deduplicated. Two settings can legitimately restrict the same operation, and duplicates were previously parsed and evaluated twice.

## Known behavior, documented rather than changed

Contributing any rule makes the runtime's managed policy active, which causes unmatched shell/read/write/URL/factory requests to require approval. That is broader than any single mapping intends, but it errs toward prompting, and the only mechanism to narrow it is the `allow` list described above. Documented in code as a deliberate tradeoff.

## Commits

Each mapping and each debt fix is a separate commit.

## Validation

- `npm run compile` — 0 errors
- `npm run test-node` — 14717 passing, 0 failing
- `npx eslint` on all changed files — clean
- `git diff --check` — clean
- 13 new unit tests covering rule validation, the new mappings, skip behavior for untranslatable input, and dedupe

## Not yet done

- Manual pass against the #331143 TPI checklist
- Gate still defaults to `false`; graduation plan not settled

title: fix: resolve services eagerly for chat symbol attachment context menu (fixes #329610)
body:
### Summary Opening the context menu on a **symbol attachment** in the chat input throws `Illegal state: service accessor is only valid during the invocation of its target method`. The context-key service for symbol attachments is initialized lazily on the first context-menu open, and that lazy closure calls `setResourceContext(accessor, ...)`, which does `accessor.get(IFileService)` on a `ServicesAccessor` whose `invokeFunction` scope has long since returned — so the accessor is no longer valid and throws. Fixes microsoft/vscode#329610 Recommended reviewer: `@roblourens` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | `1eb2581989c2` | | Author | `@roblourens` | | PR | (not resolved) | | Message | Lazy initialization of symbol attachment context key service | | Why | It moved `setResourceContext(accessor, ...)` (line 2027) into the `ensureContextKeyService` closure that runs on the CONTEXT_MENU DOM event, outside the `instantiationService.invokeFunction(...)` scope where `accessor` was created. `accessor.get()` is only valid during that invocation, so the deferred call throws "Illegal state". | ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant User as User participant Invoke as invokeFunction(accessor) participant Hook as hookUpSymbolAttachmentDragAndContextMenu participant Closure as ensureContextKeyService (lazy) participant Ctx as setResourceContext participant Accessor as ServicesAccessor Invoke->>Hook: accessor valid here Note over Hook: captures accessor in closure,
returns (scope ends) User->>Closure: contextmenu event (later) Closure->>Ctx: setResourceContext(accessor, ...) Ctx->>Accessor: accessor.get(IFileService) Note over Accessor: 💥 Illegal state:
accessor no longer valid ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/attachments/chatAttachmentWidgets.ts` | crash site | L2022 (from stack): `setResourceContext(accessor, ...)` inside lazy `ensureContextKeyService` | | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/attachments/chatAttachmentWidgets.ts` | root cause | L2077-L2080: `setResourceContext` calls `accessor.get(IFileService/ILanguageService/IModelService)` on a captured accessor invoked after its `invokeFunction` scope ended | ### Repro Steps 1. Open the chat/agent input. 2. Attach a **symbol** (e.g. via "Add Context" → a symbol, or drag a symbol into the input). 3. Right-click the symbol attachment widget to open its context menu. 4. On first open, `ensureContextKeyService()` runs and calls `setResourceContext(accessor, ...)`, which invokes `accessor.get(IFileService)` outside the original `invokeFunction` scope → `Illegal state: service accessor is only valid during the invocation of its target method` is thrown to the unhandled-error pipeline. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — In `hookUpSymbolAttachmentDragAndContextMenu`, resolve `IFileService`, `ILanguageService`, and `IModelService` **eagerly** at the top of the function, while the `ServicesAccessor` is still valid (inside its `invokeFunction` scope). `setResourceContext` is changed to accept these already-resolved services instead of the accessor, so the lazy `ensureContextKeyService` closure no longer touches the stale accessor. This fixes the bug at its source — the invalid deferred `accessor.get()` — rather than masking it at the crash site with a try/catch (which would suppress a real "used an accessor out of scope" defect and keep it out of telemetry). The sibling `hookUpResourceAttachmentDragAndContextMenu` is updated the same way for consistency; it already resolved the context eagerly, so it only switches to passing services explicitly. **Alternatives considered** - Wrap the lazy `setResourceContext` call in a try/catch: rejected — it hides the invalid-accessor bug from telemetry instead of fixing the data producer, and the resource context would silently never be set. - Capture only the resolved `StaticResourceContextKey` inputs but keep resolving inside the closure: rejected — the closure runs outside the accessor scope by design, so any `accessor.get()` there is inherently invalid. ### Recommended Owner `@roblourens` — author of the culprit commit that introduced the lazy context-key initialization, and owner of the chat attachment widget code. > Generated by [errors-fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/32086779992) · opus48 · 348 AIC · ⌖ 11.9 AIC · ⊞ 18.6K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-id%3A+errors-fix%22&type=pullrequests)

title: agentHost: fix /fleet turn ownership after Plan → Interactive
body:
Fixes microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#8837

## Problem

Running `/fleet` immediately after switching the agent from **Plan** to **Interactive** left the chat stuck — the agent replied that plan approval was "declined twice" and the clarification UI returned "No active turn." The logs confirmed two compounding turn‑lifecycle defects in `CopilotAgentSession`, not a renderer hang:

- **RC1 — stale mode.** The effective SDK agent mode was pushed only *after* runtime slash‑command invocation (`applyMode` at the end of `_send`), and for a non‑`agent-prompt` result the early `return` skipped it entirely. So `/fleet` ran under the SDK's stale **Plan** mode and called `exit_plan_mode`.
- **RC2 — turn completed too early.** `/fleet` starts an asynchronous SDK agent loop, but the runtime `commands.invoke` returns a synchronous `completed` result. VS Code treated that as terminal, emitted `chat/turnComplete`, and cleared `_currentTurn` ~100 ms in — orphaning fleet's plan review, `ask_user`, tool calls, and final output (all emitted with an empty turn id).

## Fix (VS Code‑only, temporary)

This is a localized compatibility shim, removable once the SDK returns an `agent-prompt` result for `/fleet` from `commands.invoke`.

- **RC1:** apply the effective mode *before* invoking any non‑skill runtime command, keeping the later application so an `agent-prompt` result can still override it.
- **RC2:** route canonical built‑in `/fleet` (`kind === 'builtin' && name === 'fleet'`) through the dedicated `session.rpc.fleet.start` RPC and keep the AHP turn alive until the SDK's terminal `session.idle`.
  - Rejects attachments up front (the RPC has no attachment field).
  - Runs a shared best‑effort preflight helper `_prepareSdkTurn` (mode → permission → sandbox → MCP), used by both the normal send path and fleet — no strict/best‑effort asymmetry with a normal autopilot send.
  - Marks the turn running on `{ started: true }`, throws on `{ started: false }`/rejection while the turn is current, and treats a racing `session.idle` as authoritative (no second terminal action).
  - Guards aborts both **during preflight** (never starts the loop) and **racing the RPC** (discards the turn without a duplicate terminal action), capturing the abort token up front because an aborted idle resets the live token.

The routing intentionally bypasses `commands.invoke` invocation telemetry and `allowDuringAgentExecution` gating for `/fleet` only; this is documented at the call site as part of the temporary workaround.

## Out of scope

The independently‑confirmed empty‑turn‑id full‑message leak is tracked separately; keeping the turn alive (RC2) already prevents the primary fleet path from reaching it. This PR does not modify that handler or its tests.

## Tests

Added a `/fleet lifecycle` suite (14 cases) plus 2 RC1 mode‑ordering tests to `copilotAgentSession.test.ts`, and extended the SDK mock with `rpc.fleet.start` and an ordered RPC trace. Coverage: happy path + exactly‑once completion, strict preflight ordering, client‑`fleet` still using `commands.invoke`, alias/case + empty prompt, attachment rejection before side effects, `started:false`, RPC rejection, idle‑before‑settlement (success and late reject), aborted‑idle after start, abort racing settlement, abort during preflight, event‑id binding to the original turn (before/after RPC), and plan‑review/`ask_user` during an active fleet turn.

title: fix: wrap Luna dictation alias picker endpoint in test mock (build fix for vscode-engineering#3637)
body:
## Build failure

The unit test `LanguageModelAccess model info › publishes a core-only Luna alias for dictation cleanup without publishing hidden models directly` failed on `main`. It asserts `lunaPublishedDirectly: false` but observed `true`, so the hidden `gpt-5.6-luna` model was being published as a top-level, user-selectable language model.

## Root cause

The failure is a test-setup regression, not a production defect. In production, `AutomodeService.resolveAutoModePickerEndpoint` (`extensions/copilot/src/platform/endpoint/node/automodeService.ts`) always wraps the chosen base endpoint in an `AutoChatEndpoint`, which is published under the pseudo model id `auto`. A hidden model such as `gpt-5.6-luna` is therefore never surfaced directly in the model picker.

The test's `IAutomodeService` mock instead returned the raw `lunaEndpoint` from `resolveAutoModePickerEndpoint`. `LanguageModelAccess._provideLanguageModelChatInfo` then pushed that hidden endpoint into the published set under its own model id `gpt-5.6-luna`, making `lunaPublishedDirectly` true. The assertion was correct; the mock was infidelitous to production behavior.

## How the fix works

The mock now mirrors production by returning a real `AutoChatEndpoint` that wraps `lunaEndpoint`. The wrapper is instantiated from the test's instantiation service (all required services — `IDomainService`, `ICAPIClientService`, etc. — are provided by `createExtensionTestingServices`) after the testing accessor is created, and assigned to the closure variable the mock returns. A base-count cache entry for the `auto` pseudo model is pre-seeded (matching the existing pattern for the other endpoints) to keep the test deterministic and fast. With the wrapper in place, the picker endpoint publishes as `auto`, `gpt-5.6-luna` is no longer published directly, and the assertion passes.

## Rollback evaluation

Recommendation: **Do not roll back**.

Public culprit commit/PR: `83dfbdd3a9d94908ae3c92c3ec0ca34f2afe8dcf` (PR #331338). The originating change is a legitimate feature (a core-only Luna dictation-cleanup alias); only its accompanying test mock diverged from production behavior. title: Tell the caller a consumed queued message was sent
body:
A message the provider consumes from the queue is reported to its caller as cancelled, and a message the provider drops is never reported at all.

### The queue has three exits and only one of them is right

`ChatService.sendRequest(..., { queue })` returns a promise that resolves when the queued message is eventually processed. Three things can retire that message, and each settles it differently:

1. **The normal dequeue** (`processNextPendingRequest`) settles it with the real send result. Correct.
2. **`removePendingRequest`** settles it as `{ kind: 'rejected', reasonCode: 'cancelled' }`. Correct for a message the user withdrew, and it is also what the agent host's server-initiated turn path calls to clear the message the provider just *consumed*, so a delivered message reports cancellation.
3. **`syncPendingRequestsFromRemote`** intends to settle anything the provider's queue no longer lists, but never does: `getPendingRequests()` returns the model's live array and `replacePendingRequests` empties it in place, so the loop that settles dropped messages iterates an array that has already been cleared. Those callers wait forever.

The root cause behind the first two is that the client has no notion of *consumed*: every route that observes a message leaving the provider's queue treats it as withdrawn.

### What callers do with it

`acceptAndAwaitSentRequest` returns `undefined`, documented as "`undefined` if it never was [sent]", and `chatSessionRoutingController._resolveQueuedCompletion` reports `{ status: 'rejected', reasonCode: 'cancelled' }`. Both describe a message that was in fact delivered and is being answered.

### The fix

- The chat service settles a consumed message where it creates the request for it, in the `onDidStartServerRequest` handler, which already receives the id the message was queued under. The completion promise is built from the response model with a listener owned by the session's store, so a session closed mid-turn does not leak it.
- `syncPendingRequestsFromRemote` takes the id of the message that became the active turn and leaves it alone. This matters independently of ordering: both the reconciliation and the server-turn detection follow the same provider state change, and their listeners run in registration order, so a fix that relied on winning that race would be fragile.
- The agent host's removal loop skips the id that is about to become the turn, so the cancel path cannot settle it first.
- `existing` is copied before `replacePendingRequests`, which makes the dropped-message settlement actually run.

Fixing the aliasing on its own would newly reject every consumed message, since the loop starts working; the consumed guard is what keeps that correct. The three tests are each tied to one of these: reverting the aliasing fix fails only the dropped-message test, reverting the consumed guard fails only the consumed-reconciliation test, and removing the settlement fails only the sent test.

Found while checking whether #330785 reusing a pending message id as the request id was safe. It is safe, and that is recorded on that PR; this is what the check turned up alongside it. It reproduces on `main` without either of my open branches, but promoting a steer into its own turn makes route 2 the ordinary path for every mid-turn message rather than an occasional one.

title: Report vision support for natively served Claude models
body:
Fixes #331347.

A pasted image in a Claude session on the native (BYO-Anthropic) transport is attached, sent, and understood by the model, but the UI marks it unsupported: the attachment renders with a warning icon and the hover reads "*{model}* does not support images." Users conclude the attachment was dropped and stop pasting images.

`fromSdkModelInfo` hardcoded the capability:

```ts
supportsVision: false,
```

while the CAPI projection directly above it reads the real one (`supportsVision: !!supports?.vision`), so the two transports disagreed about the same underlying models.

`ModelInfo` in `@anthropic-ai/claude-agent-sdk` has no vision field at all. It carries `supportsEffort`, `supportedEffortLevels`, `supportsAdaptiveThinking`, `supportsFastMode` and `supportsAutoMode`, and nothing about image input. So `false` was standing in for "the SDK does not say", but it does not read that way downstream: `agentHostLanguageModelProvider` collapses the value to a boolean (`vision: m.supportsVision ?? false`) and `chatAttachmentWidgets` treats it as authoritative, so "unknown" became a positive claim that the model cannot accept images.

Leaving the field unset changes nothing for the same reason, which makes `true` the accurate answer for this transport: every row it offers is a Claude model, and image input is available across them. The comment says so at the seam, so whoever adds a real capability to `ModelInfo` can replace it with the actual signal.

The existing projection test asserted the old value and now asserts the new one, with a note about why.

title: agents window: fix sessions list progress
body:
## Summary

Fixes Sessions list progress indicators becoming stale in either direction:

- a session is running, but the list does not show a spinner;
- a session has completed, but the list continues showing a spinner.

## Root cause

The Agent Host correctly aggregated chat activity into the session status, but did not publish the resulting session-summary updates for sessions initially returned by `root/listSessions`.

A recent publication filter only emitted `root/sessionSummaryChanged` for sessions recorded as published. That record was updated for `root/sessionAdded`, but not for `root/listSessions`. As a result, restored/listed sessions were visible to the client while the host still treated their summaries as unpublished.

The subscribed chat continued receiving live `session/chatUpdated` actions, so the chat content showed the correct state. The Sessions list depended on the suppressed root summary update and retained its previous state, producing the mismatch.

## Fix

- Record summaries returned by `root/listSessions` as published without emitting redundant `root/sessionAdded` notifications.
- Preserve the listed summary as the notification-diff baseline so subsequent status and activity changes are emitted normally.
- Keep filtered sessions unpublished, preserving the existing external-session visibility behavior.
- Remove the client-side status recomputation workaround; the UI now consumes the status published by the Agent Host.
- Add a protocol-level regression test covering a restored session returned by `listSessions` and its subsequent transition to in progress.

title: agentHost: sync BYOK experiment enablement
body:
## Summary

- Synchronizes the experiment-resolved BYOK setting through agent-host root configuration.
- Makes BYOK models available to model selection and new sessions only when the shared enablement gate allows them.
- Preserves explicit environment overrides and allows setting changes to take effect without restarting the agent host.

<details>
<summary>Technical context for AI-assisted review</summary>

### Intent and previous behavior

BYOK experiment defaults resolve in the renderer, but the main-process configuration used for launch-time environment variables does not include that experiment layer. The renderer could therefore enable BYOK while the agent host remained disabled.

### Implementation

The BYOK setting now maps to a local-only agent-host root-config key. The typed Agent Host configuration descriptor requires every experiment-backed setting to declare an agent-host mapping.

The renderer keeps the BYOK reverse-RPC channel available for later enablement and registers a no-op channel when the language-model handler is unavailable. A shared gate applies explicit environment overrides before synchronized root config and is used for both model publication and per-session provider/model synthesis.

### Behavior and constraints

- BYOK remains local-only because remote agent hosts cannot access the local extension-host language model API.
- Explicit environment overrides take precedence over synchronized configuration.
- Disabled BYOK models are neither shown in the picker nor added to new session configuration.

</details>

title: Match a remote host's working directories against the window's folder
body:
Fixes #330979.

In a remote window every agent session is filtered out of the list.

The store receives each session's working directories wrapped for the agent-host filesystem, and compares them to the window's workspace folder:

```
directory: vscode-agent-host://b64-<encoded host address>/workspace/printstream?_ah=<meta>
folder:    vscode-remote://dev-container%2B<hex>/workspace/printstream
```

`isEqualOrParent` compares schemes before anything else:

```ts
isEqualOrParent(base: URI, parentCandidate: URI, ignoreFragment: boolean = false): boolean {
    if (base.scheme === parentCandidate.scheme) {
```

so the containment check short-circuits to `false` however identical the paths are, and the list comes back empty rather than partial.

### Fix

The wrapper carries the original URI in its `_ah` query, so `fromAgentHostUri` recovers the directory exactly as the host named it. For a host running in a dev container that is the very `vscode-remote:` URI the window uses for that folder: measured in a live window, the unwrapped authority equals the folder's authority byte for byte. Containment then does the rest, so a sibling or a prefix-only lookalike (`/workspace/printstream-2`) still does not match.

This matters beyond making the comparison work. A bare path carries no host identity, so deciding it belongs to the folder's machine can only ever be an assumption. The unwrapped URI carries that identity, so a directory on a *different* remote is rejected on the evidence rather than adopted.

The scheme rewrite stays, narrowed to what it is: the fallback for a host that reports a bare `file:` path with no wrapper to unwrap. It applies only to a `file:` directory against a folder that has an authority, so a local window compares `file:` to `file:` and is untouched, and it is the only part that still assumes this store's single host connection is the folder's machine.

### Verification

- The matching predicate is exported so the tests exercise it rather than a replica. Coverage: the wrapped dev-container pair from the issue, a wrapped directory on a different remote, the bare `file:` fallback, nested and sibling directories, the prefix-only lookalike, the already-remote form, a mismatched authority, and a local window in which nothing is rewritten. The wrapped case fails if the unwrap is removed.
- Verified live in a dev-container window: sessions list, including ones created minutes earlier. Before the fix the same window listed none.

An earlier revision of this PR did the scheme rewrite alone. It does not fix this case, because the reported directory is not `file:` at all, so the rewrite never fires. I am noting that rather than quietly replacing it, since the description above previously claimed otherwise on the strength of host-side logs, which report a directory before the client wraps it.

title: Count the session's changes, not the branch's divergence
body:
Fixes #330941.

The session-list chip is computed from the `changeKind: 'branch'` changeset in two places. A branch measures itself against its upstream, so it includes every commit made before the session existed and by everyone else. A session that has never run a turn, and owns no file edits at all, still gets a count.

**The write path** produced the chip during the branch refresh, on this premise:

> SINGLE-folder: derive it from the primary branch `diffs`, exactly as before — that branch changeset IS the whole session footprint.

That premise is the defect. Ownership moves to the `changeKind: 'session'` changeset, which is the session's own footprint.

**The read path** did the same for unopened sessions, and persisted what it derived, making the wrong number durable:

```ts
const liveSession = this._stateManager.getChangesetState(buildBranchChangesetUri(sessionUri));
const liveChanges = computeChangesSummaryFromLiveState(liveSession);
if (liveChanges) {
    this.persistChangesSummary(sessionUri, liveChanges);
    return liveChanges;
}
```

Worth noting the helper it called documents the opposite of what the call site did — "Only the `changeKind: 'session'` entry feeds the summary" — so the contract and the caller already disagreed. That fallback is gone; with no session-scoped evidence the honest rendering is no chip, and the next completed turn writes the real one.

Fixing either half alone does nothing, which is worth knowing before splitting this up: with only the read path fixed, the write path has already persisted the branch number and the read path then serves it faithfully from `META_CHANGES_SUMMARY`. My first attempt at this asserted exactly that and failed on `{"additions":16070,"deletions":634,"files":1}`.

`summariseDiffs` distinguishes "computed, and empty" (a real zero) from "could not compute" (`undefined`), and only the former is written, so the move cannot substitute a misleading `0 files` for a missing chip.

### The trade this makes, explicitly

Session diffs come from checkpoints:

```ts
if (kind === 'session') {
    const latestTurnId = this._latestTurnIdAcrossChats(session);
    if (!latestTurnId) { return undefined; }
```

So a session with no checkpoints — checkpointing disabled, or one that never completed a turn — now shows no chip rather than a wrong one. I believe that is correct, and it is the same principle as the read-path change, but it is a visible behaviour change and I would rather name it than have it found in review.

### Coverage

The characterization test `single-folder summary stays branch-derived (byte-for-byte unchanged)` asserted the old behaviour and is replaced by one asserting the branch refresh no longer writes or persists the chip, while the branch changeset data itself is unaffected.

I did not manage to unit-test the positive half — a session refresh writing the chip — in this suite: it needs a turn on the default chat plus baseline and turn checkpoints, and the turn would not land in `sessionState.turns` through the harness I had. Flagging that gap rather than claiming coverage I do not have.

Multi-folder sessions aggregate every repository's *branch* diff through `_updateMultiFolderChangesSummary`, so they carry the same defect by the same reasoning. Left alone here because the fix is the same decision applied to a more complex path, and this change is easier to review on its own.

### Rebased onto current main

Upstream has since added multi-folder summary ownership, which touches the same block. That work is preserved unchanged:

- The all-folder aggregate for a multi-root session stays on the branch path, exactly as upstream wrote it. This PR still does not change multi-root behaviour.
- The legacy `'diffs'` key and the single-folder summary move to the session path, guarded by `!isMultiRootSession(...)` so the two paths cannot both write the summary.

The characterization test `single-folder summary stays branch-derived` is replaced in place, rather than deleted, by `a branch refresh no longer writes the chip from the branch divergence`. Its premise is the assumption this PR disputes: it reads "the single primary branch diff IS the whole session footprint", which holds only when the session owns its branch. The replacement keeps the same harness and asserts the branch changeset data is still published, so only the chip ownership is withdrawn.

Full unit suite after the rebase: 14705 passing. The 11 failures are pre-existing on main, in the title controller and turn telemetry, which this PR does not touch.

title: Fix omni chat picker anchoring at non-zero zoom levels
body:
## Description

The omni chat action-widget / picker windows (model picker, context pickers, confirmation menus) are hosted in a separate frameless auxiliary window positioned relative to the omni input surface. The positioning math mixed two coordinate systems, so at zoom levels other than 0 (e.g. Ctrl +/- to zoom level 2) the pickers appeared detached from the omni input.

Root cause: `getBoundingClientRect()` reports **CSS px** within the zoomed content, while native window bounds (`getWindowPosition` → Electron `win.getBounds()`) are **device-independent screen px**. 1 content CSS px = `zoomFactor` screen px, so the offsets only lined up at zoom factor 1.

Changes (`chatInputWindowService.ts`, `_openActionWidgetWindow`):

- **Screen positioning** — scale in-content offsets (`sourceTop`, `sourceRight`, `right`-placement `preferredY`) by `getZoomFactor(sourceWindow)` before adding them to native screen bounds.
- **Internal anchor** — anchor the picker against the widget window's content `clientHeight` (CSS px) instead of the device-independent bounds `height`, since the widget window inherits the source window's zoom.

## Description

The omni chat input runs inside a small, frameless auxiliary window with `overflow: hidden`. Custom toolbar hovers can't fit above/below their button, so they get clamped **on top of** the target. Because the tooltip overlays its own button, the mouse `MOUSE_LEAVE`/`MOUSE_OVER` pair toggles the hover on and off in a loop — the flicker seen on the send button.

Changes:

- **`ChatInputPart` toolbars use native tooltips in the omni window** — when `ChatContextKeys.inChatInputWindow` is set, the shared `hoverDelegate` is `nativeHoverDelegate` instead of `createInstantHoverDelegate()`. This covers all five input toolbars (input actions, execute/send, side, secondary, status).

```ts
const isOmniInput = this.contextKeyService.getContextKeyValue<boolean>(ChatContextKeys.inChatInputWindow.key) === true;
const hoverDelegate = isOmniInput ? nativeHoverDelegate : this._register(createInstantHoverDelegate());
```

title: agentHost: Speed up rename chat tool
body:
## Summary

- return from `rename_chat` immediately, before session lookup or persistence completes
- retain the targeted session-registry lookup instead of full `listSessions()` enumeration
- run the rename independently in the background and log deferred failures
- share live-session metadata overlay logic between targeted lookup and `listSessions()`

## Performance

Previously, every rename blocked the agent while hydrating and overlaying metadata for every registered session, including provider metadata and per-session database reads, and then persisted the rename before returning.

The tool now returns immediately. Background work performs one indexed session-registry query, uses live in-memory metadata when available, and at most reads provider metadata for the single target session. This removes all asynchronous lookup and persistence work from the agent-facing tool latency while also changing target resolution from work proportional to the total session count to a constant-size lookup.

Since completion happens after the tool returns, deferred failures are logged and the tool/display result describes a requested rename rather than completed persistence.

## Follow-up

The callback-based `ISessionServerToolAccessor` wiring should be cleaned up separately with a dedicated injectable service or tool-handler classes. That architectural refactor will follow in a separate change so this performance fix stays focused.

title: Filter archived (read-only) sessions out of omni chat pending items
body:
Omni chat surfaced archived sessions as pending items, showing an "Archived sessions are read-only." banner and allowing follow-ups to be routed to an archived session.

## Description

The omni pending-chat list in `chatInputWindowService.ts` was built from every `ChatModel` reporting `requestNeedsInput`, without excluding archived ones. When such an item is shown, the omni input calls `widget.setModel(model)` and adopts that read-only session model. Because the omni `ChatWidget` builds its `ChatReadOnlyBanner` with an `undefined` message, it falls back to the banner's default text — `"Archived sessions are read-only."` — and the archived session becomes a routing target.

Other omni paths (routing candidates, `_refreshSessions`, `_loadPendingSessionModels`) already excluded archived sessions; this list was the gap — e.g. a session archived *after* its model was loaded still lingers in `chatService.chatModels`.

- **Exclude read-only models from pending items**: add `.filter(model => !model.isReadOnly.read(reader))` when composing `pendingChats`, so archived sessions are never surfaced, adopted by the omni input, or routed to.

```ts
const pendingChats: IChatInputWindowPendingChat[] = [...this.chatService.chatModels.read(reader)]
    // Archived sessions are read-only, so their pending prompts must not
    // surface in omni: routing must never target them and the omni input
    // must never adopt a read-only model (which shows the read-only banner).
    .filter(model => !model.isReadOnly.read(reader))
    .filter(model => !!model.requestNeedsInput.read(reader) && !this._hasOnlyResolvedPendingTools(model, reader))
```

The banner is driven by `model.isReadOnly` (`chatWidget.ts` `setReadOnly` autorun), so filtering at the source removes both the erroneous banner and the ability to send to archived sessions.

## Notes

No unit test added: the predicate lives inside a service `autorun` closure that isn't instantiated in tests, and the existing `chatInputWindow.test.ts` suite only covers pure helpers.

title: Complete the response for the turn that ended
body:
A turn ending completes the response belonging to whichever turn is current, not the one that ended. When two turns overlap, the outgoing turn closes the incoming turn's response and every progress batch after that is dropped into it — the turn renders empty.

`isCompleteObs` lives on `AgentHostChatSession`, so both completion paths address the session rather than a turn:

```ts
// _handleTurn
this._activeSessions.get(request.sessionResource)?.isCompleteObs.set(true, undefined);
// _trackServerTurnProgress
onTurnEnded: () => chatSession.isCompleteObs.set(true, undefined),
```

`startServerRequest` resets the flag when it creates the next turn's request/response pair, so the outcome depends on which lands first.

**Measured.** I instrumented `startServerRequest`, `appendProgress` and both turn-end paths with logpoints and drove real turns against a dev container, with a host that starts a new turn when one preempts another.

Benign ordering — the preempted turn ends first, the reset lands last, the turn renders:

```
      0ms  clientTurnEnded
    523ms  startServerRequest
   7327ms  appendProgress …(19)
  19602ms  serverTurnEnded
```

Adverse ordering, from the same setup with a tool-heavy turn (twelve read-only Bash calls) instead of plain text:

```
      0ms  startServerRequest
      5ms  clientTurnEnded      <-- closes the response created 5ms earlier
   2882ms  appendProgress …(16 calls, all dropped)
  26199ms  serverTurnEnded
```

That turn's rendered row is the word `Claude` and nothing else. Sixteen progress batches were produced and discarded. Text-only turns leave ~500ms between the two events and never showed the inversion, in-process or over a socket; a turn ending tool calls closes that gap to milliseconds.

The user-visible failure is total and silent: text, tool calls and any question the model asks all vanish. The changeset chip still renders, because changesets are a separate channel subscription, and no stop button appears because the client believes the turn is over.

**The fix** records which turn owns the response when one claims it, and ignores an end signal from any other turn. A response nothing has claimed is still completed by whichever turn ends, so ordinary sequential turns are unaffected.

Overlap is reachable today through the server-initiated turn path, and any change that lets one turn preempt another makes it routine — #330785 is where I hit it.

The rule is extracted as `completionAppliesToResponse` so it can be tested without standing up a chat session, following `unwrapSessionLoadErrorMessage` in the same file.

title: Resolve a client tool to the client that is still there
body:
Fixes #331289.

A client tool call is stamped with an owning `clientId` resolved through `SessionClientToolsModel.ownerOf`. With no caller-supplied preference that resolved to the *first-inserted* contributor, and a window reload connects with a new `clientId` while the departed client's entry can still be present. Every subsequent call was then stamped with a client that had gone away, and failed on arrival:

```
17:14:38.827  chat/toolCallStart      clientId=<old>
17:14:38.830  chat/toolCallComplete   Client <old> disconnected before completing openBrowserPage
17:14:40.646  chat/toolCallComplete   …another active client now provides openBrowserPage. You may try calling the tool again.
```

Three milliseconds from start to failure, and the retry advice cannot be taken: the retry resolves to the same departed client. In the session this came from it was still happening 2 hours 8 minutes after that client disconnected, so it is not the disconnect-grace window elapsing — the tool is dead for the life of the session, and the model eventually concludes the tool itself is broken.

The host is simultaneously right and wrong about this: the "another active client provides it" sentence is guarded by `_hasReplacementActiveClientTool`, which reads `state.activeClients` and correctly sees the live client, while `ownerOf` reads the tool model and answers with the dead one. Two registries, permanently disagreeing.

This makes the resolution self-correcting rather than chasing the disagreement. The model now tracks the most recent contributor and prefers it when the caller expresses no preference. A reconnecting window re-pushes its tool list, so the newest contributor is the one most recently known to be alive; an explicit `preferredClientId` still wins, and removing the latest contributor falls back to whoever remains.

`canRefineContributor` makes this worth fixing at the point of resolution: a client contributor may only be refined by the same client, so once a call is stamped with a departed id nothing downstream can re-point it.

Scope is deliberately narrow — only the Claude path goes through `SessionClientToolsModel`. `codexMapAppServerEvents.ts:748` resolves through `ActiveClientToolSet` directly and has the same shape, but I have not reproduced it there and have left it alone.

Two existing tests asserted the first-inserted default and are updated to the new behaviour, since that default is what produced the bug. Added coverage for the reconnect case itself and for the fallback when the latest contributor is removed.

title: Forward fontSize, fontFamily and opacity on decoration attachments
body:
# Forward `fontSize`, `fontFamily` and `opacity` on decoration attachments

The editor's renderer already applies `fontSize`, `fontFamily` and `opacity` to a decoration's
`before`/`after` attachment, and the internal render-options interface already declares all
three — but `ThemableDecorationAttachmentRenderOptions.from()` builds an explicit allowlist that
predates that support, so an extension's values are dropped on the way out of the extension host
and never reach the renderer.

This adds the three properties to the converter and to the public API. No renderer change is
needed; the plumbing on the other side of the boundary is already there.

## Evidence, at `main` (518720d5)

The renderer collects them for attachments:

- `src/vs/editor/browser/services/abstractCodeEditorService.ts:801`
  ```ts
  this.collectCSSText(opts, ['verticalAlign', 'fontStyle', 'fontWeight', 'fontSize', 'fontFamily',
      'textDecoration', 'color', 'opacity', 'backgroundColor', 'margin', 'padding'], cssTextArr);
  ```
- `src/vs/editor/browser/services/abstractCodeEditorService.ts:587,604-605` — `_CSS_MAP` has
  `opacity: 'opacity:{0};'`, `fontSize: 'font-size:{0};'`, `fontFamily: 'font-family:{0};'`.
- `src/vs/editor/common/editorCommon.ts` — `IContentDecorationRenderOptions` declares
  `fontSize?: string`, `fontFamily?: string`, `opacity?: string`.

The converter drops them:

- `src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostTypeConverters.ts:508-527` —
  `ThemableDecorationAttachmentRenderOptions.from()` returns a literal with twelve keys; these
  three are not among them.
- `src/vscode-dts/vscode.d.ts:1119` — the public interface omits them for the same reason.

## Before / after, from an extension's point of view

```ts
const type = vscode.window.createTextEditorDecorationType({
    before: {
        contentText: '[2, 8, 128]',
        width: '14ch',
        color: new vscode.ThemeColor('editorInfo.foreground'),
        fontSize: '10px'          // ← not in the API before this change
    }
});

editor.setDecorations(type, [new vscode.Range(0, 0, 0, 0)]);
```

**Before:** the attachment renders at the editor's font size. `fontSize` is not accepted by the
public type at all, and a cast past it is silently dropped by the converter.

**After:** the attachment renders at 10px, because the value now reaches the renderer that
already knew what to do with it.

There is a workaround today, and it is the reason this is worth fixing: `fontStyle` *is*
forwarded and is interpolated into the generated CSS unchanged, so `fontStyle: 'normal;font-size:10px'`
injects the declaration. That works, and it is the kind of thing that stops working without
warning. A one-line allowlist addition is a better answer than a hole.

## Motivation

Gutter-style annotations — a fixed-width column of shapes, sizes or timings rendered left of the
code via `before` attachments — read better at a smaller size than the code they annotate, the
way line numbers do. Inlay hints are not an alternative here: they take no width, so they cannot
hold a column, and they take their colour from six global theme keys rather than per-hint.

The shipped precedent for this kind of readout is decorations: `extensions/git/src/blame.ts`
uses an `after` attachment with a `ThemeColor` and per-range `renderOptions`.

## Tests

`src/vs/workbench/api/test/browser/extHostTypeConverter.test.ts` gains one case asserting the
converted object, following the snapshot-style `assert.deepStrictEqual` the surrounding suite
uses.

```
./scripts/test.sh --grep ExtHostTypeConverter
```

## Notes

- No behaviour changes for existing extensions: three optional properties are added, and an
  extension that sets none of them converts to exactly what it converted to before.
- `opacity` and `fontFamily` are included because the renderer collects them in the same call as
  `fontSize`; adding only one of the three would leave the same asymmetry for its two immediate
  neighbours.

title: Share one model-selection policy between Workbench chat and the Agents Window
body:
Workbench chat and the Agents Window both had to answer "which model does this chat open on?", and they answered it differently. The Agents Window had its own engine for it, `transitionModelSelection`, which lived in shared code but had exactly one caller — so it bought nothing, and the two windows were free to disagree.

They did. If a chat had a model restored onto it, the Agents Window treated that as the user's choice and left it alone, while Workbench treated it as leftover from the previous chat and let `chat.defaultModel` overwrite it.

## What changed

**One implementation, and the second is deleted.** The Agents Window now uses Workbench's `ChatInputModelSelectionController` through the existing runtime seam. `SessionModelSelection` is the adapter that connects them. `transitionModelSelection` and its supporting types are gone.

**Chats say where their model came from.** `IChat.modelSource` records whether a model is the chat's own (`Chosen`) or was put there for it (`CarriedOver`), and `setModel` makes the caller say which. Only a chat's own model outranks `chat.defaultModel`, and the model id alone cannot tell you which case you have.

It is required rather than optional, because an absent value has to mean something: it is read as the chat's own, since the alternative is overwriting a model the user picked. A provider that cannot account for a model says `undefined` deliberately.

**Model state is per chat.** Everything about a chat's model is keyed by chat resource, so one chat's choice can't leak into another.

## Behaviour changes

Five, all deliberate — worth knowing if you bisect here:

- A model a new peer chat only inherited no longer blocks `chat.defaultModel` from seeding it.
- "Is this conversation empty?" is read from the chat, not the session, so a new peer chat in a finished session can still be seeded.
- A resumed agent-host session restores its model from the saved draft. Needed because a chat that has already run is never given a model, so without this a reopened session would show one but not actually have one.
- `forkChat` inherits the source chat's model and agent, matching `createSideChat`, instead of taking the session default.
- A chat waiting for a model its pool hasn't published keeps waiting, even after you visit another chat and come back. Previously the temporary stand-in could be mistaken for the chat's real answer, and the awaited model was lost.

## Testing

Both windows run the same conformance matrix (`modelSelectionConformance.ts`). Each case checks both what the picker shows and what the chat actually runs on. Every field is read through `conformanceInputs`, whose fields are all required, so if one side stops reading a field it fails to compile instead of quietly testing something else. That guard caught a real gap: the Workbench side had been ignoring `catalogResolved`.

The matrix covers precedence once the model catalog has settled. It is not a parity proof: while models are still loading the two windows differ. The Agents Window waits — blank picker, send blocked — rather than pick a model it might have to change. Workbench chat shows a stand-in and lets you send, then swaps in the real model when it publishes.

That difference is worth being honest about, because it is not free. Both windows write the selected model to the same place (the chat draft, which is what a resumed session reads back), so a stand-in is visible to the backend either way. If you send in the window before the real model arrives, Workbench sends on the stand-in; the Agents Window won't let you. The rule that actually matters is shared — a stand-in never replaces the model a chat is waiting for — but the send gating is not, and aligning it is a follow-up: making Workbench wait would block the composer on every cold start, which needs its own change and its own justification.

### Verification

- Full `vs/sessions` suite — 2380 passing
- Full `vs/workbench/contrib/chat` suite — 5957 passing
- Component fixtures — 1072 rendered, 0 errors
- `valid-layers-check`, `tsc --noEmit -p src`, eslint — clean

Layering is unchanged: `vs/sessions` imports from `vs/workbench`, never the reverse.

title: chat: describe BYOK Responses failures that omit error details
body:
## Summary

- BYOK chat requests that fail mid-stream now explain what happened instead of showing `{"code":0,"message":"","metadata":{}}`.
- Failures carry the provider's response id, so a user report can be correlated with the provider's own logs.
- A stream error that arrives without a message no longer replaces the reason the request already computed.
- Restores diagnosability for these failures; it does not change when or why a provider fails.

Related to #330408

<details>
<summary>Technical context for AI-assisted review</summary>

### Intent and previous behavior

The OpenAI Responses contract requires `code` and `message` whenever a terminal event carries a non-null `error`. Providers violate this in practice and terminate a stream with an error object that is present but field-less.

`mapResponsesApiError` only guarded against a null or absent error. A present-but-empty object fell through: `message` collapsed to `''`, and `metadata.code` became `undefined`, which `JSON.stringify` drops. The result was an error struct with no information in it.

BYOK amplifies this. `hydrateBYOKErrorMessages` promotes the serialized stream error to the entire user-facing reason, so the hollow struct became the whole message. An upstream outage, a malformed request, and a transport fault were indistinguishable, which is why earlier reports of this string were triaged as generic request failures.

### Implementation

`mapResponsesApiError` now separates a usable error from a non-conforming one. When no message is present it synthesizes a description naming the terminal event, the response status, and the response id; the wording adapts depending on whether a provider code survived. Metadata keys are spread conditionally so serialization can no longer reduce them to `{}`.

Callers supply that identity through a small context helper, applied at all three call sites that share this mapping (`error`, `response.incomplete`, `response.failed`), so the invariant is restored once rather than patched per branch.

`hydrateBYOKErrorMessages` gained a matching guard: it keeps the fetcher's original reason when a stream error carries no message, which prevents any future producer of an empty error from blanking the message again.

### Behavior and constraints

- Well-formed errors are unchanged; their provider message and code still pass through.
- Successful responses are unaffected. OpenAI sends `error: null` on success, which continues to map to `undefined`.
- Synthesized text contains only the event type, status, response id, and provider code. No prompt content or credentials.
- `metadata` gains a `responseId` key when the response envelope supplies one, including for well-formed errors.
- Chat Completions is untouched; it forwards the provider error verbatim and never produced this shape.

### Review context

The mapping dates to 1.121.0 and is byte-identical through 1.133.0, so the broken serialization is not a recent regression. What changed is exposure: the Agent Host BYOK proxy moved from Chat Completions to Responses in 1.132.0, which first routed Agents Window traffic through this path eight days before the first report. The editor-window BYOK path has advertised the Responses endpoint for much longer, which matches an earlier report of the identical string on 1.130.0.

The reference to #330408 is deliberately non-closing. Repeated live requests against the affected model, including agent-sized payloads and a counterfactual that toggled the request fields VS Code sends only to that model family, all completed normally. The request shape is therefore not a deterministic trigger, and the underlying failure is unexplained. A transport-layer hypothesis remains open: an earlier report of this same string was resolved by switching the fetcher, and the reports here span both local and remote hosts, where the available fetcher differs. Once this ships, the surfaced message should identify which of those paths is responsible.

</details>

title: fix localization format string parsing
body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/331074

## Root cause

The About dialog was showing the commit SHA in the `OS:` field because the NLS formatter only parsed the first character of a placeholder index. In `src/vs/nls.ts`, the code used `rest[0]` when replacing `{10}` / `{11}` entries, so `{10}` was treated as argument index `1` instead of `10`.

This was latent for years, but it became visible when the Copilot package versions were added to the About dialog in #329027. That change introduced double-digit placeholders (`{8}` to `{10}`), causing the value for the `OS:` line to resolve to the commit SHA instead of the OS string.

This is a broader NLS bug as well: any localized string with placeholders above 9 would be mis-substituted.

## Fix

Parse the full captured digit group (`parseInt(rest, 10)`) when resolving placeholder indexes, rather than only the first character. This fix is applied in both the main NLS formatter and the vendored Copilot copy.

Also adds a regression test covering multi-digit placeholders.
