title: Render a window shadow on the floating chat input window
body:
## Description

The Omni chat input hosts its content in a frameless, transparent auxiliary window sized tightly to the input. With no chrome and no shadow, it doesn't read as a separate window and gets mistaken for an inline input box.

Since the window bounds hug the surface, a `box-shadow` alone would be clipped at the window edge. The fix reserves a transparent gutter around the surface and grows the window bounds by that gutter, so the shadow renders into the transparent band while the input keeps its exact content size.

- **`media/chatInputWindow.css`** — introduce `--omni-window-shadow-size: 16px`, drive the surface `margin` / `height` calc from it (replacing the 1px stroke), and add `box-shadow: 0 3px 10px 0 var(--vscode-widget-shadow, …)` (matching the shadow token used by suggest/action widgets).
- **`chatInputWindowService.ts`** — add `CHAT_INPUT_WINDOW_SHADOW_SIZE = 16` (kept in sync with the CSS var); `fitWindowToInput` and `_defaultBounds` now pad width/height by `2 * shadow` so the surface size is preserved and the shadow isn't clipped.

Pending-approval panel sizing and action-widget anchoring measure relative `getBoundingClientRect()`s, so the inset gutter is transparent to them.

title: agentHost: make startup session discovery registry-first
body:
agentHost: make startup session discovery registry-first (#331155)

A 2026-08-17 Insiders reproduction with 941 SDK sessions and 1,437
per-session databases (~946 MB) showed the ~60s delay is not migration —
`sessionRegistryBackfilled:copilotcli` was already true and migration was
skipped. The time went to per-session SQLite work during discovery and
listing: classification took 66.9s (113 external, 342 adoptable
extension-host, 486 already known), registration of the 113 emitted
candidates another 21.9s, and the first two AHP `listSessions` calls
109.8s and 91.0s, with a third 73.2s window after discovery.

Each measured phase is addressed:

- Classification (66.9s): discovery is now registry-first. `IAgent` gains
  an optional `setKnownSessionsFilter` seam that `AgentService` installs
  at provider registration; it answers, in one registry query for the
  whole candidate set, which sessions the host already owns.
  `CopilotAgent` drops those candidates instead of opening a session
  database each, so the 486 already-known sessions cost no DB opens.
  Tombstoned sessions are absent from the registry and therefore never
  reported as known, so an explicitly deleted session still reaches
  `register`, whose atomic tombstone check declines it. Provenance of a
  registered row stays owned by the explicit create/restore paths.

- Classification (the 342 adoptable rows): while migrate-legacy is off,
  adoptable extension-host candidates are never emitted, so their
  Git-touching project resolution is now skipped entirely instead of
  being computed and then filtered away. `_emitCopilotChats` keeps its
  filter as a re-check, since the setting can flip mid-pass.

- Registration (21.9s): `_registerDiscoveredChats` rejects an
  already-registered candidate with unchanged provenance before
  `_isChatBacking()` or any other per-session I/O.

- Listing (109.8s / 91.0s / 73.2s): `listSessions()` coalesces concurrent
  computations per external-sessions mode, so the burst a multi-window
  restore produces shares one registry traversal. The shared entry
  records the registry epoch it started at and every registry mutation
  invalidates it, so a caller arriving after a mutation starts a fresh
  pass rather than joining a possibly pre-mutation one. Each caller gets
  its own array; rejections are shared only with callers already waiting.

- `_readStoredSessionMetadata` / `_readSessionMetadata` now issue one
  bulk `getMetadataObject()` query instead of nine and six single-key
  reads, shrinking the cost of the fallback path that runs when no host
  filter is installed.

Deferred deliberately: seeding a newly discovered external session as
read still creates its database purely to hold one flag. Dropping the
write without a durable default would flip every discovered external
session to unread, because the list overlay only applies `IsRead` when
the key is present. The correct default belongs on the registry row and
is left to the registry list-projection change; the reasoning is
recorded on `_initializeExternalSessionReadState`. Removal of
`_awaitInitialProviderMigration()` is likewise not attempted: the
reproduction proves migration was already skipped.

Tests assert call/open counts rather than wall-clock thresholds:
registry-known candidates cause zero session DB opens; disabled
adoptable candidates resolve no projects; re-registering a known
discovered chat performs no per-session I/O; the known-sessions filter
reports registered sessions only and leaves tombstones to registration;
concurrent list calls share one computation but not their arrays; a
mutation during an in-flight list is not served from it; and stored
metadata is read with a single bulk query.

title: agentHost: address agent merge review feedback
body:
Follow-up to #331010, addressing the review comments left on that PR after it was merged.

### Setting rename

The Agent Merge settings no longer carry `agentHost` in their ID:

`chat.agentHost.agentMerge.*` -> `chat.agentMerge.*`

### Security

- The host now owns `agentMerge.controller` session config. `SessionConfigChanged` actions coming from a client that target host-written keys are rejected, so a client cannot forge a controller state (target, enabledAt, watermark, budgets) that later makes the gate return `confirmed: true` and triggers a native merge. Covered by two regression tests.
- `_canRepairFork` fails closed when head repository provenance is missing.
- Refs pointing at a different GitHub host are ignored.

### Correctness

- Injected autonomy configuration is reconciled on every cycle instead of once, and keys revoked by policy are rolled back. Configuration is never widened while a turn is active.
- The merge target is revalidated before starting a turn and again before merging; the merge step re-reads live state, config, target and top-level comments.
- `AgentMergeRepairAction` is split out of `AgentMergeAction` so repair paths cannot express a merge.
- Stopping the runtime cancels the controller's in-flight turn.

### Prompt bounding

Review threads now carry all of their feedback comments rather than only the first, and the prompt is bounded by explicit per-section caps plus a 20k character aggregate budget.

### Commands

Enable/disable commands have separate preconditions driven by a dedicated context key, and the configure quick pick exposes reset as a title button rather than a list entry.

title: Fix notification close button running default action instead of dismissing
body:
When a notification has action buttons and you click the X to close it, the intent is usually to dismiss without picking an action. Instead, the close button was silently running the last primary action — same as pressing it explicitly. For destructive choices like "Delete" or "Don't Save" that's a pretty bad surprise.

Traced it to `renderSecondaryActions` in `notificationsViewer.ts`. The close handler was wired to `ClearNotificationAction` which just calls `notification.close()`, but the dismiss-on-X path got mixed up with the action-runner path somewhere in a recent refactor. The fix makes the X button call `notification.close()` directly without going through the primary action runner. Notifications with no actions are unchanged.

Verified by opening a notification with multiple choices and pressing X — it dismisses cleanly without triggering any action.

Fixes #330794

title: Fix Remote Explorer showing "Server Returned 404" instead of container list
body:
After a recent update, opening the Remote Explorer sidebar with dev containers throws a "Server Returned 404" error notification and shows nothing. The extension is hitting `/v1/containers` which was removed — the service now expects `/v2/containers`.

Two changes in `containerList.ts`: updated `CONTAINER_LIST_API_PATH` to the v2 path, and added a 404 guard in `fetchDevContainers` that returns an empty array instead of propagating the error. The guard is intentionally narrow — only 404 gets swallowed, everything else still surfaces so real connectivity issues don't disappear silently. With older service versions the sidebar just shows empty rather than an error banner.

Tested against the updated endpoint (containers populate) and against a service that returns 404 (sidebar shows empty, no notification). 500s still fire the error notification.

title: Fix gopls semantic token colors in Dark Modern theme
body:
The Dark Modern theme inherits from Dark+ which inherits from the base Dark VS theme. The semantic token type `keyword` — which gopls sends for Go keywords — resolves to the `keyword.control` TextMate scope. Dark+ assigns that scope the color `#C586C0` (purple), and Dark Modern had no override for it, so Go keywords ended up purple even though every other token color in Dark Modern was updated to match the theme's revised palette.

The same applies to `function` and `method` — without explicit mappings they fall through to inherited values that weren't necessarily chosen with Dark Modern in mind.

Added a `semanticTokenColors` block to `dark_modern.json` that pins `keyword` to the blue `#569cd6` used by all other keyword-scoped tokens in the theme, and `function`/`method` to the yellow `#DCDCAA` consistent with how functions are colored everywhere else.

Tested by opening a Go file with gopls active under Dark Modern before and after the change. Keywords and function names now match the colors used by TypeScript/Python/C# in the same theme rather than inheriting the old purple tone from Dark+.

Fixes #330173

title: Resolve a slash command whose content cannot be read
body:
Fixes #331138.

### Problem

In a remote window, a chat message containing a slash command never submits. The command autocompletes and renders normally, Enter does nothing, and no error reaches the UI. Reproduced with `/commit` and `/deep-research` in a dev container; the same commands work in a local window.

### Cause

`resolvePromptSlashCommand` parses the command's URI unconditionally:

```ts
const parsedPromptFile = await this.promptsService.parseNew(command.uri, token);
```

Not every command's `uri` is readable. Built-in skills are published as discovery-only entries on the `agent-builtin` scheme, carrying a name and description with nothing behind them — as `buildBuiltinSkillsContainer` states: *"the entries have no openable content"*. `parseNew` therefore rejects with `Unable to resolve nonexistent file`, and because `parsedPromptFile` is a required field the rejection escapes the resolver.

The caller is the input-decoration update, so the rejection lands on the path that produces `parsedInput`:

```
FileService.doReadFileStream
  ← parseNew
  ← resolvePromptSlashCommand
  ← updateAsyncInputEditorDecorations   (chatInputEditorContrib.ts:341)
  ← triggerInputEditorDecorationsUpdate
  ← get parsedInput ← updateChatInputContext
```

That is why the message cannot be sent and why nothing is reported: the failure is in the decoration/parse path, not in send.

The trigger is *accepting* the completion, not pressing Enter — typing the same characters without accepting the suggestion sends fine.

Local windows are unaffected only because the commands that resolve there happen to be file-backed.

### Fix

Treat parsing as best-effort and make `parsedPromptFile` optional. A command that cannot be read still resolves; only its body is unavailable. This also covers a file-backed command deleted between discovery and use, which fails identically today.

`promptFilePickers.ts` already treats a failed parse this way (`parseNew(...).catch(() => undefined)`), so this brings the two resolvers in line with existing behaviour rather than inventing a new convention.

The two consumers that dereferenced the field now skip only the part that needs a body: `chatWidget` still records prompt-run telemetry and applies header metadata when present, and `chatSessions.contribution` returns no variable entry when there is no prompt file.

### Verification

New test: a command whose content cannot be read still resolves, with `parsedPromptFile` undefined. It fails without the fix —

```
1 failing
  resolvePromptSlashCommand - unreadable command content
    Error: Unable to resolve nonexistent file
```

— and passes with it. 14613 node unit tests pass; `tsc --noEmit -p src/tsconfig.json` is clean apart from two `assignmentService.ts` errors that are present on `main` unchanged.

Also verified against a live dev-container window with the equivalent change applied to the installed build. Accepting a built-in skill completion and pressing Enter now submits. The underlying read still fails, exactly as it should for a resource with no content —

```
[warning] [RemoteAgentHostProtocol] Request 38 failed:
  {"code":-32008,"message":"Resource not found: agent-builtin:/skill/update-config"}
```

— but it is now absorbed rather than taking the submission down with it.

title: fix(process-explorer): report memory footprint on macOS
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Fixes #194322

## Root cause

On macOS the process explorer's memory column is derived from the `%mem` column of `ps`, which is based on the resident set size (RSS). RSS ignores compressed memory, so the values diverge significantly from what Activity Monitor shows — the issue reporter saw 4 GB for one helper process in Activity Monitor while the process explorer accounted for less than 1 GB in total.

The MEM column of macOS `top` reports the physical footprint of a process, which is the same value Activity Monitor displays (verified against `footprint -p <pid>`, which prints `phys_footprint` directly):

| process | ps RSS-based (before) | top MEM / footprint (after) |
|-|-|-|
| Google Chrome | 232 MB | 333 MB |
| Electron renderer | 457 MB | 667 MB |
| node with 256 MB Buffer | 295 MB | 268 MB |

Unlike `vmmap` (discussed in the issue), `top` is preinstalled on every macOS system, and the Linux code path is untouched.

## What changed

- After the process tree is built from `ps` output as before, darwin now runs a single `top -l 1 -stats pid,mem -pid <pid>...` invocation limited to the pids of the tree (~1s, comparable to the existing 1s CPU sampling on Linux) and overrides the memory values with the reported footprints in bytes. This also handles `top`'s `K`/`M`/`G`/`T` suffixes and the `+` compressed-memory marker.
- If `top` fails or omits a pid, the ps-derived value is kept as a fallback, so behavior degrades to the status quo instead of breaking.

## How to test

- Added unit tests for the `top` output parser in `src/vs/base/test/node/ps.test.ts` (`npm run test-node`).
- Manual: open the Process Explorer (Help > Open Process Explorer) on macOS and compare the Memory column with Activity Monitor for the same pids — the values now match Activity Monitor instead of being consistently lower.

title: Add ESLint rule for command title capitalizatio
body:
Implements #243333 by adding a new ESLint rule that validates command titles follow Microsoft title-style capitalization guidelines.

## Changes
- Added `code-command-title-capitalization.ts` ESLint rule
- Added comprehensive test file with valid/invalid cases
- Updated `eslint.config.js` to register the new rule

## Rule Behavior
The rule validates that command titles follow Microsoft title-style capitalization:
- Articles (a, an, the) are lowercase unless first/last word
- Prepositions of 4 or fewer letters are lowercase unless first/last word  
- Conjunctions (and, but, or, nor, yet, so) are lowercase unless first/last word
- All other words are capitalized (first letter uppercase, rest lowercase)
- Hyphenated words are handled correctly
- Case normalization handles ALL CAPS and mixed case inputs

## Reference
Microsoft Style Guide: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/style-guide/capitalization#title-style-capitalization

title: agentHost: discover external Copilot sessions
body:
## Problem

Copilot sessions created outside the Agent Host never appeared in the Agents window, even with `chat.agentHost.showExternalSessions` set to `all`.

`CopilotAgent` had a single discovery path, `_discoverExtHostChats()`, which:

1. only matched **legacy VS Code extension-host** CLI sessions, via a `~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/vscode.metadata.json` sidecar with `origin === 'vscode'`;
2. hard-coded `external: false` on everything it emitted;
3. was gated entirely behind `chat.agentHost.migrateLegacyCopilotCli.enabled`.

A session created by the standalone `copilot` CLI or the GitHub Copilot app — which all share `~/.copilot` — has no such marker, so it was dropped at step 1 and never reached `AgentService._registerDiscoveredChats`. The registry therefore never held a Copilot row with `external = true`, and the setting had nothing to filter.

Claude (`_emitClaudeCodeChats`) and Codex (`_emitCodexChats`) both emit every unknown native chat as `external: true`. Copilot was the outlier, and `AGENTS.md` §3a documented the gap as intentional.

## Change

`_discoverCopilotChats()` / `_emitCopilotChats()` enumerate the whole SDK catalog and classify each chat Agent Host does not already own:

- **legacy extension-host chat** → `external: false` + `ehcliAdoptable` meta, still gated on migrate-legacy (unchanged behavior);
- **anything else** → `external: true`, ungated.

"Already owns" is the presence of a per-session database under `{userDataPath}/agentSessionData` (never the shared Copilot home), which also keeps peer-chat backings out of the payload. Subagent sessions and marked chat backings are filtered centrally by `AgentService` as before.

Discovery now starts on first-listener attach behind a `retry` wrapper, mirroring Claude and Codex, so a cold CLI client doesn't lose the pass. The retry honors the file's existing `_shutdownPromise` / `_store.isDisposed` guard so teardown stops it rather than sleeping on a dead client.

Chats whose SDK context carries no working directory are still dropped. `_doResumeSession` requires one unconditionally and a discovered chat has no other source for it — `_initializeExternalSessionReadState` writes only `agentHost.isRead` — so surfacing one would list fine and then throw on open, with a plain `Error` rather than the `SessionWorkingDirectoryMissingError` the UI handles gracefully.

## Logging

A session that was discovered but filtered out by the setting was previously indistinguishable from one that was never discovered. The pipeline is now traceable end to end at `info`:

```
[Copilot] Listed N SDK session(s) for <reason>
[Copilot] Chat discovery: N SDK session(s) -> X external, Y adoptable legacy extension-host, Z already known to Agent Host, W without a working directory
[Copilot] Chat discovery: emitting X of Y discovered chat(s) (adopt legacy extension-host chats: <bool>)
[AgentService] discovery for provider <id>: N candidate(s) (X external), Y registered, Z suppressed as subagent/chat backing
[AgentService] listSessions hid N of M session(s) (showExternalSessions: '<mode>')
```

The last line is deduped on `hidden/total/mode` so a steady state logs once instead of on every refresh. All lines carry only counts, a mode name and session URIs — no file paths, summaries or user content.

## Notes

- `_registerDiscoveredChats` now computes its return value from a counter instead of `results.some(...)`. Semantically identical (booleans only); the value has no consumer today.
- The "empty session DB counts as known" semantics of `_readStoredSessionMetadata` are deliberately left alone — an empty DB is how Agent Host records a chat it already touched, and the pre-existing test `does not discover an extension-host chat with an empty Agent Host database` asserts exactly that. The trade-off is now written down in `AGENTS.md` rather than silently relied upon.

## Testing

Four new tests in a `external chat discovery` suite cover the standalone-CLI, GitHub-Copilot-app (`origin: 'other'`), adoptable-legacy, and already-owned / no-working-directory cases. `writeExtensionHostMarker` was hoisted out of the nested migration suite so both suites share it.

- `copilotAgent.test.ts` — 267 passing (3 consecutive runs)
- `agentService.test.ts` — 290 passing
- `tsc --project src/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — clean apart from two pre-existing `@github/copilot-sdk` type-skew errors in `copilotAgentSession.test.ts` / `copilotToolDisplay.test.ts`

`provisional session anchors customization discovery to the additional roots (gated)` is flaky against its 2000ms timeout **on this branch's merge base** (failed 2 of 3 baseline runs); it passed 3 of 3 with these changes applied.

## Blast radius

Measured against a real `~/.copilot` with 975 SDK sessions: 492 have no Agent Host DB, of which 453 carry an extension-host marker (still gated as adoptable-legacy), leaving ~39 true externals — only 20 within the default 7-day window.

Worth flagging: a few arrive in same-second triples that look like CLI-spawned sub-sessions and will surface as separate rows. The SDK's `SessionMetadata` exposes no parent/subagent field, so there is no signal to suppress them; Claude and Codex have the same exposure today.

title: Fix typing over RTL selection requiring two keypresses
body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/monaco-editor/issues/5448

### Description of Proposed Changes
This PR resolves an input bug in the legacy `<textarea>` input pipeline (the path used when `editContext` is disabled, such as natively in Safari). 

* **The Problem:** When selecting text from right to left (RTL selection) and typing a key, the selected text is not replaced on the first keypress. A second keypress is required.
* **The Root Cause:** `TextAreaState` expects standard, normalized selection bounds (`selectionStart <= selectionEnd`). However, the `getSelectionStart()` and `getSelectionEnd()` methods in `TextAreaWrapper` were flipping these values for backward/RTL selections. This caused `selectionStart > selectionEnd` to be written and read, which violated native browser behavior (browsers automatically clamp/collapse native selections where start > end) and resulted in a state diff mismatch inside `deduceInput` (computing `replacePrevCharCnt = 1` instead of `0`).
* **The Fix:** Removed the direction-based flipping logic in `TextAreaWrapper.getSelectionStart` and `getSelectionEnd` to always return standard LTR range bounds, aligning with the expected format in `TextAreaState` and maintaining selection synchronization.

---

### How to Test
1. Open the Monaco Editor playground (or test runner) with `editContext: false` configured (or open in Safari with default options).
2. Place the cursor at the end of a line (e.g. after the semicolon in `const U = 19.05;`).
3. Press `Shift+ArrowLeft` once to select the `;` character backwards.
4. Press the `a` key once.
5. **Expected Behavior:** The selection `;` is immediately replaced with `a` on the first keypress, resulting in `const U = 19.05a`.

title: Respect ancestor .gitignore files in Explorer
body:
Fixes #189951

## Description

When `explorer.excludeGitIgnore` is enabled for a workspace nested inside a Git repository, Explorer currently discovers `.gitignore` files only while traversing downward from the workspace root. As a result, rules from `.gitignore` files between the workspace and repository root are never loaded.

This change:

- discovers ancestor `.gitignore` candidates up to the nearest `.git` repository boundary;
- stops ancestor discovery when the workspace is itself a repository;
- creates stable parent-chain placeholders so child negation rules continue to override ancestor rules;
- watches existing and missing ancestor `.gitignore` files for add, update, delete, and restore events;
- serializes workspace `.gitignore` processing behind ancestor initialization; and
- disposes external watches when the setting is disabled or a workspace folder is removed.

## How To Test

1. Create a Git repository with a root `.gitignore` containing `*.log`.
2. Create and open a nested folder as the VS Code workspace.
3. Enable `explorer.excludeGitIgnore`.
4. Add a `.log` file inside the workspace.
5. Confirm Explorer hides the file.
6. Add a workspace `.gitignore` containing `!keep.log` and confirm `keep.log` remains visible.
7. Update, remove, and restore an ancestor `.gitignore` and confirm Explorer refreshes without reloading the window.

## Validation

- Test-only black-box regression: fails on the unchanged baseline (`false === true`).
- Explorer browser tests: 8 passed.
- Client compilation: passed with zero errors.
- Focused ESLint: passed with zero warnings.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- Manual A/B verification at the same base commit:
  - reproduced the missing ancestor rules on baseline;
  - confirmed root and intermediate ancestor rules on the fixed build;
  - confirmed child negation remains effective; and
  - confirmed live update, deletion, and restoration refresh Explorer correctly.

Only the Explorer filter implementation and its regression tests are changed.

title: multiDiffEditor: Apply the editor scrolling settings
body:
I noticed that setting `editor.mouseWheelScrollSensitivity` didn't work in the diff viewer for Git commits. This PR fixes it. :) Two older issues and a PR addressed similar problems, but were still open - I've incorporated their changes and feedback into this one as well.

The multi-file diff editor gives every per-file diff editor `handleMouseWheel: false` and sizes it to its content height, so the one scrollable that hosts all files handles the wheel. That scrollable was set up with fixed values, so four `editor.*` settings had no effect there:

- `editor.mouseWheelScrollSensitivity` and `editor.fastScrollSensitivity` fell back to the defaults in `resolveOptions`, 1 and 5.
- `editor.scrollPredominantAxis` fell back to its default, true.
- `editor.smoothScrolling` was ignored. Smooth scrolling was always on,
  while a normal editor has it off by default.

The same wheel tick that scrolls a normal editor tab by the configured amount moved the diff of a commit by the default amount instead.

Read all four settings from the configuration and keep the scrollable in sync with them. The values go through the editor option validation, so odd values behave as they do in a normal editor, and the smooth scroll duration reuses `SMOOTH_SCROLLING_TIME`.

This covers every user of the widget: the diff of a commit from the Source Control Graph, the Changes editor, and the notebook multi diff editor.

Fixes #261443
Fixes #200855

Supersedes #262669. That change covers the sensitivity settings and the predominant axis but not smooth scrolling, does not validate the values, has an unused import that fails the build, and has no tests.

title: Harden agent session release lifecycle
body:
## Summary

This is a lifecycle-hardening follow-up to [#330132](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/330132), which fixed [#331027](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/331027): Agent Host could release a Copilot SDK session while that session still owned a running detached shell.

The original fix correctly separated two kinds of idleness:

- AHP turn idleness: the agent loop has finished and the UI may show the session as idle.
- Provider-session releasability: detached SDK work may still be running, so the provider session must remain alive.

After that fix, review uncovered races around clients subscribing, disconnecting, and reconnecting while provider release or session restoration was asynchronous. This PR closes those gaps.

Since this PR was opened, `main` introduced `AgentHostSubscriptionService` and `AgentSessionResidency`. Those components now provide most of the original release hardening: release deduplication, provider preflight, retry after a detached-task veto or release failure, subscriber revalidation, and release-before-evict ordering. The old duplicate implementation was removed from this branch. The remaining changes cover lifecycle gaps that the refactor does not represent.

## How We Got Here

The initial detached-shell failure looked like this:

1. A chat started a shell with `mode: async` and `detach: true`.
2. The shell tool call returned immediately with a background shell ID.
3. The SDK emitted `session.idle` because the main agent loop was finished.
4. The final AHP client unsubscribed from the idle session.
5. Agent Host released the provider session after its grace period.
6. Releasing the SDK session destroyed the still-running detached shell, so its completion event and output never arrived.

[#330132](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/330132) fixed that by asking the provider whether its chats can be released and retrying later when detached work is still active.

That introduced or exposed longer asynchronous windows in the subscription lifecycle: a new subscriber may wait for a provider release to finish, or may need to restore an evicted session before its baseline snapshot is available. A client can disconnect or reconnect during either wait. This follow-up ensures those interleavings cannot leave stale ownership or corrupt client state.

## Specific Failures This Avoids

### Dead Client Permanently Pins a Session

A subscribe request can wait for an in-flight provider release or a cold session restore. If the transport disconnects during that wait, cleanup may run before `AgentService` has registered the subscriber. Without cancellation ownership:

1. disconnect cleanup removes nothing because the subscriber is not registered yet;
2. the asynchronous subscribe later resumes;
3. it registers the now-dead client ID;
4. no later path removes that subscriber;
5. `hasSessionSubscribers` remains true forever, preventing residency release and session GC.

The pending subscription record plus the `isActive` ownership predicate prevent the stale request from registering after disconnect.

### Older Subscribe Cleans Up a Newer Subscribe

Two subscribe attempts for the same client and resource can overlap around disconnect/reconnect. The older request can fail after the newer request has already become current. Cleanup must be identity-aware; otherwise the older completion can remove the newer request's subscriber registration.

### Actions Arrive Before the Baseline Snapshot

The protocol handler must remember a pending subscription so disconnect can cancel it. However, an entry in the normal subscription map is also used to decide which clients receive actions. Treating a pending entry as active can send actions before the subscribe response contains its baseline snapshot. The client then has no correct state against which to apply those actions.

State subscriptions now distinguish pending from active delivery. Pending subscriptions participate in cancellation and refcount ownership but are excluded from action routing until their baseline has resolved.

### Reconnect Delivers the Same Action Twice

Reconnect restores several channels concurrently. One channel may restore quickly while another requires a slow provider/session restore. If the fast channel becomes active immediately, an action emitted during the remaining wait can be:

1. broadcast live to the reconnecting transport; and
2. included again in the reconnect replay because its sequence is newer than the client's pre-reconnect sequence.

Many state actions are not idempotent, so applying the envelope twice can duplicate deltas or other append-style state. Successful reconnect subscriptions are activated as a batch immediately before replay is assembled.

### Snapshot Reconnect Silently Misses an Action

When the replay buffer no longer covers the client's gap, reconnect returns fresh snapshots instead of replaying actions. While subscriptions are held pending as a batch, state can still change after a fast channel's first snapshot was captured but before a slower channel finishes restoring. The final snapshot response is refreshed from authoritative state so that change is not silently omitted.

### Overlapping Transports Drop the Shared Refcount

The protocol intentionally permits an old and new transport for the same logical client to overlap during reconnect. If the old transport closes while the new transport's subscription is still pending, the pending entry must count as ownership for refcount cleanup even though it must not receive actions yet. Otherwise the old transport can remove the client ID that the reconnecting transport is in the process of retaining.

### Shutdown Continues Release Work

`AgentSessionResidency` can be inside an asynchronous provider preflight when the host shuts down. Once disposed, it must not:

- continue into provider release or cache eviction; or
- add a retry timer to its already-disposed `DisposableResourceMap`.

The residency disposal checks stop both continuations. `AgentService.unsubscribe` also avoids scheduling GC after the service has been disposed.

## Current Architecture

- `AgentHostSubscriptionService` remains the authoritative active subscriber registry.
- `AgentSessionResidency` owns release preflight, retry, deduplication, subscriber revalidation, and release-before-evict behavior.
- `ProtocolServerHandler` owns pending protocol-request identity because connection close and explicit unsubscribe occur at that layer.
- `AgentService.subscribe` accepts an ownership predicate so it can avoid registering a request that the protocol layer has already cancelled.
- Pending protocol subscriptions become active only when their baseline is ready; reconnect activation is coordinated with replay/snapshot construction.

No parallel pending-subscription registry was added to `AgentService`.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- targeted ESLint for all changed Agent Host files
- targeted `AgentService`, `AgentSessionResidency`, and `ProtocolServerHandler` suites: 511 passing, 16 pending
- pre-commit hygiene checks
- multiple Opus 5 reviews focused on correctness, necessity, and simplification

title: agentHost: Make the turn observer the only producer of turn progress
body:
Follow-up to #331045 (now merged). **Draft on purpose** — targeted for after the next release branch so it gets bake time in Insiders.

### Why

#331045 fixes a real bug but treats a symptom. The underlying problem is that reconnect runs **two** independent converters over the same response parts:

| | what it is | when it runs |
|---|---|---|
| `activeTurnToProgress` | one-shot imperative snapshot | reconnect only |
| `_observeTurn` | always-on reactive observable graph | live, reconnect, server-initiated |

Their overlap is managed by three hand-maintained continuity parameters — `adoptInvocations`, `seedEmittedLengths`, `initialResponsePartCount` — which are positional bookkeeping that must stay in sync between two converters that evolve independently. Every new response-part kind or tool status needs a matching dedup rule on the other side, and nothing enforces it.

It had already decayed in four places:

1. **A settled tool call cannot be adopted.** The snapshot renders it as `toolInvocationSerialized`, which `adoptInvocations` cannot represent, so the live graph emitted a duplicate — and that duplicate split a still-streaming response in two at the reconnect boundary.
2. **The same split for completed *subagent* tools**, which had to be exempted from the first guard so their child session would still be observed. Fixing it needed a second, separate mechanism to decouple observation from emission.
3. **`onFileEdits` was never wired on the reconnect path.** A tool completing with file edits after reconnect gets `presentation = Hidden` from `finalizeToolInvocation`, and the edit pills meant to replace it are never emitted — the card vanishes.
4. **`PendingResultConfirmation` is missing** from the `activeTurnToProgress` branch chain, so such a tool renders nothing at all on reconnect.

Items 1 and 2 are what #331045 patches, with two separate guards. Same root cause, four symptoms, and the next part kind added makes a fifth.

### What this does

Deletes the snapshot path.

`_observeTurn` is derived from state, and `autorunPerKeyedItem` runs **synchronously** on install, iterating every existing response part — so its first pass already replays the entire accumulated turn. The snapshot was recomputing what the graph produces anyway.

Reconnect is now just "install the observer", which happens before `provideChatSessionContent` returns, so `progressObs` is populated by the time the session is handed out. All three continuity parameters disappear, along with both guards from #331045, the adoption branches in the three tool-setup functions, and the cleanup that settled the orphaned snapshot invocation. `onFileEdits` is wired on the reconnect path, which the single-producer path requires (otherwise it would hit symptom 3).

`activeTurnToProgress` is no longer referenced by the handler; it stays exported for the cloud-sandbox read-only path.

**Reconnect is no longer a special case** — it is the same code path a live turn takes, so a reconnected response is indistinguishable from one watched the whole time. The invariant is structural instead of hand-maintained; there is no boundary left to get wrong. The settled-subagent case from symptom 2 needs no special handling here at all: it just falls out.

### Restore Checkpoint fix (from review)

Wiring `onFileEdits` on the reconnect path exposed an ordering problem that code review caught. The callback fires during the observer's synchronous replay, inside `provideChatSessionContent` — **before the ChatModel is created** — so `_ensureSnapshotController` found no model and `controller?.addToolCallEdits(...)` silently no-oped. Since the active turn is not in `_pendingHistoryTurns` either, edits from tools that completed before the reconnect never reached a checkpoint, leaving Restore Checkpoint without a boundary for that turn.

Those edits are now queued and flushed when the matching model appears. The pills rendered either way, so only the checkpoint data was affected.

### Risk / what to watch in Insiders

- **Rendering change:** settled tools in an active turn now render as finalized live invocations rather than serialized parts. More consistent with live turns, but it is a real change and the unit tests here are mock-driven — worth exercising a real reconnect against a long session with completed tools, file edits, terminals, and subagents.
- **Perf:** replaying a long turn now constructs live `ChatToolInvocation` objects for every completed tool instead of plain serialized objects. Same order of magnitude, but a turn with hundreds of tool calls does more work on reconnect.

### Testing

- Full `AgentHost` suite: 2210 passing. `npm run typecheck-client` clean. CI green.
- `records edits from a tool that completed before reconnect once the model appears` drives a real `AgentHostSnapshotController` and asserts `hasEditsInRequest`; verified failing before the checkpoint fix.
- Both reconnect regression tests from #331045 carry over, now asserting this branch's behavior — a finalized `toolInvocation`, which is exactly what a live turn produces for a mid-turn completion.
- Exactly one pre-existing test needed updating: `reconnecting to an active turn with owned client tool completes the initial snapshot invocation`, whose entire subject was the orphaned-snapshot workaround. With one producer there is no orphan, so it now asserts what actually matters — exactly one invocation, no duplicate.

title: agentHost: Don't split the final response at the reconnect boundary
body:
Reconnecting to an agent host session while a turn is still streaming could split the final assistant response in two — in the observed case mid-word, with the prefix folded into the collapsed tool/thinking section and the remainder rendered as a separate markdown block outside it, making it look like a tool call had interrupted the answer.

### Root cause

Reconnect runs **two** independent converters over the same response parts:

| | what it is | when it runs |
|---|---|---|
| `activeTurnToProgress` | one-shot imperative snapshot | reconnect only |
| `_observeTurn` | always-on reactive observable graph | live, reconnect, server-initiated |

They de-duplicate through `adoptInvocations`, which is keyed on live `ChatToolInvocation` instances. A tool call that had **already settled** before reconnect is rendered by the snapshot as a `toolInvocationSerialized` part, which cannot be adopted — so the live graph emitted a second, live invocation for it.

That duplicate lands *between* the restored markdown prefix and the markdown still streaming into the same response part. `ChatResponseModel` only merges a markdown update into an immediately preceding markdown part, so the two fragments stayed separate:

```
markdown prefix
tool invocation   <-- spurious
markdown continuation
```

On completion, disclosure grouped the prefix into the preceding activity section and left the continuation outside it, exposing the reconnect boundary as if it were a semantic boundary in the model's answer.

The underlying data was never wrong: the model produced one continuous response, the agent host persisted one continuous markdown part, and AHP delivered the snapshot and continuation correctly. The split was introduced entirely in the workbench.

### Fix

Record what the snapshot emitted **per tool call** rather than only the adoptable subset, so per-tool setup can skip a settled tool call that the snapshot already rendered in full. Subagent tools are excluded from the skip because their setup is what streams the child session's inner tool calls into the parent response.

This is deliberately the minimal, low-risk fix. The deeper problem is that two converters exist at all and must be kept in sync by hand; a follow-up PR removes the snapshot path entirely so reconnect and live turns share one code path. That one is riskier and wants more bake time in Insiders.

title: fix: update find searchScope when the selection changes
body:
## Description

The `searchScope` change detection in `FindReplaceState.change()` has inverted comparison logic since the multi-selection refactor in b9efdab4831 (2020): a new scope was considered *unchanged* whenever any existing scope range differed from one of the new ranges. As a result, moving or resizing the selection while Find in Selection is active kept the stale scope, and the match count never updated.

This is the root cause of the symptoms in #237774:

1. Select two lines (3 matches of the search term) → widget reports 1 result
2. Toggling Find in Selection off → highlights disappear unexpectedly
3. Changing the selection after a search → count stays at the old value

Replace the inverted per-range comparison with a proper set-equality check (`searchScopesEqual`): same length, and every new range must be equal to some existing range. The scope is now updated whenever the selection actually changes, and no redundant change event fires when the scope is identical.

title: agentHost: fix resuming sessions with deleted worktrees
body:
## Summary

Fixes #331030.

Archived worktree sessions are read-only, and archiving deliberately removes their worktree after preserving the branch and source-repository metadata. When an archived session is reopened, the Copilot SDK still requires an existing working directory in order to load its transcript. The intended behavior is therefore to resume the SDK against the source repository for history only, rather than recreate the archived worktree.

## What went wrong

Copilot sessions can have two different identities:

- The **Agent Host configuration/session ID**, which owns working-directory metadata and customizations.
- The **Copilot SDK session ID**, which identifies the persisted SDK conversation.

When those IDs are equal, restoration uses `_resumeSession` / `_doResumeSession`. That path already calls `resolveWorkingDirectoryForResume` before constructing the SDK launch plan.

When the IDs differ, restoration uses `_resolveOrResumeChatSession` for the exact persisted chat backing. Modern default chats can use this path—not only additional or peer chats. This path previously passed the deleted worktree directly to `client.resumeSession`, bypassing the existing resolver and producing:

> Request session.resume failed with message: Directory does not exist or cannot be accessed: /path/to/removed/worktree

## Fix

Route the divergent-backing path through `IAgentConfigurationService.resolveWorkingDirectoryForResume` too.

The resolver does not change the process cwd. It returns the safe directory that should be supplied to the resumed SDK session:

- If the persisted directory still exists, return it unchanged.
- If it is missing and the session is archived, return the persisted source-repository root so the read-only transcript can load.
- If it is missing and the session is live, recreate the preserved worktree and return that path; never silently run an interactive session in the source repository.
- If no safe directory can be recovered, surface `SessionWorkingDirectoryMissingError`.

The resolved directory is then used consistently for the SDK launch plan, shell manager, and customization discovery.

For multi-root sessions, the change replaces only index 0 (the deleted primary worktree) with the resolved directory, preserves secondary roots, and persists the corrected ordered root set. This prevents the next restore from reading a stale primary path from `copilot.workingDirectories`.

## Tests

- Added regression coverage for a default chat whose Agent Host ID differs from its Copilot SDK backing ID.
- Verifies that the resolved repository is used as the launch/customization directory.
- Verifies that secondary roots are preserved.
- Verifies that the corrected root set is persisted.
- `npm run typecheck-client`

title: Keep the expected managed settings 404 out of the DevTools console
body:
### Problem

Developer Tools logs this repeatedly, and it looks like a failure:

```
api.github.com/copilot_internal/managed_settings:1  Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 ()
```

The `404` is not a problem — it is how the endpoint says "this account has no managed settings", and `DefaultAccountProvider` already handles it as a normal outcome. The problem is purely that it gets printed.

### Why it can't be fixed in the renderer

Chromium emits that line from the document's network stack for any response with an error status. Measured via the DevTools `Log` domain (`Log.entryAdded`, which is exactly what the console renders):

| request from the renderer | printed? |
|---|---|
| `fetch` | yes |
| `XMLHttpRequest` | yes |
| `fetch` + `keepalive` / `cache: 'no-store'` | yes |
| same, inside an iframe | yes |

There is no request option that suppresses it, and it is not a `console.*` call that could be filtered.

### Fix

Rewrite the status in the main process before the response reaches the window, using the same `session.defaultSession.webRequest.onHeadersReceived` mechanism that already sits a few lines above in `app.ts` (used to add `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` for the PRSS CDN). The real status travels in a response header that the workbench restores immediately, so **every downstream code path still sees the `404` it sees today** — including the retry-next-session logic and the `noSettings` handling.

Scope is deliberately tight: only a `404`, only from `https://api.*/copilot_internal/managed_settings` (covering GHES, whose host is also `api.`-prefixed). Any other status, endpoint or genuine failure is reported exactly as before.

One subtlety worth flagging for review: the request is cross-origin, so the marker header is invisible to the window unless it is added to `Access-Control-Expose-Headers`. That list is *extended*, not replaced — replacing it would hide the `x-ratelimit-remaining` / `retry-after` headers that the rate-limit logic reads off this same response.

### Verification

Ran the shipped predicate and handler verbatim in Electron (the `.build/electron` binary this repo uses), against a real `https://api.github.com/copilot_internal/managed_settings?client_id=…` URL served by a local HTTPS endpoint that mimics GitHub's response (CORS, its own `access-control-expose-headers`, `x-ratelimit-remaining`), with the DevTools `Log` domain attached:

```
managed_settings (real URL + query)
   renderer: {"status":200,"original":"404","rateLimit":"4999","body":"{\"message\":\"Not Found\"}"}
   console : silent
other copilot endpoint (untouched)
   renderer: {"status":404,"original":null,"rateLimit":"4999","body":"{\"message\":\"Not Found\"}"}
   console : PRINTS -> Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found)
```

So: the noise is gone, the true status is recovered, the rate-limit headers survive, and neighbouring endpoints are unaffected.

Also: `scripts/test.sh` on the three related suites (53 passing, including new unit tests for the URL predicate and the status restore), plus `tsc -p src/tsconfig.json`, `eslint`, and `valid-layers-check`.

### Notes

- Desktop only. The web workbench still prints it; that would need the service to stop answering `404`.
- While investigating I found a separate, unrelated inefficiency: `findMatchingProviderSession` lists one session once per scope set it matches, so a full-scope GitHub session is listed 3× and the identical request is sent 3× with the same token. That is a real bug but it is *not* the cause of the printing, so I have left it out of this PR — happy to send it separately.

title: agentHost: Add agent merge controller
body:
## Summary

Adds a provider-neutral Agent Merge controller to the Agent Host so Copilot, Codex, and Claude can maintain a pull request through the same lifecycle.

- watches the session pull request through the shared GitHub API service
- deterministically gates review feedback, required CI failures, conflicts, and merge readiness before starting a model turn
- gives repair turns narrowly scoped GitHub tools for CI diagnostics, review-thread replies, and workflow reruns
- performs final direct merges and merge-queue enrollment in native Agent Host code rather than delegating them to the model
- persists per-session enablement, pull request binding, action overrides, watermarks, attempt budgets, and injected permission-mode state across restores
- adds experimental `chat.agentHost.agentMerge.*` settings and Agents Window commands to enable, disable, or configure the active session
- adds structured `ILogService` diagnostics without logging prompts, comment bodies, CI logs, credentials, or local paths

## Behavior and safety

Agent Merge fails closed when GitHub state is incomplete, does not create turns while required checks are pending, and only treats feedback from repository owners, members, collaborators, or the Copilot pull request reviewer as actionable. The agent is never authorized to merge. A fresh native readiness check runs immediately before direct merge or queue enrollment.

Enabling Agent Merge switches the session to Autopilot mode and Assisted approvals unless managed policy forbids elevated approval modes. Disabling restores values only when they still match the injected values, preserving later manual changes. Branch or pull request identity changes disable the controller and require explicit re-enablement.

The initial VS Code surface is intentionally command-only; no dedicated status UI is included yet.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- focused Agent Merge, GitHub query, configuration sync, and controller unit tests: 23 passing
- `git diff --check`

The implementation and follow-up lifecycle fixes were reviewed with Claude Opus 5, including dedicated passes for correctness, concurrency, provider parity, structure, composability, and maintainability.

title: Settle Copilot WebSocket requests when `error` is not followed by `close`
body:
Fixes #331003

## Description

An active Copilot Responses API WebSocket request currently settles connection failures from the socket `close` listener. The `error` listener only stores `_pendingErrorMessage` for that later close.

Observed Electron failures can emit `error` without a subsequent `close`. In that case `handle.firstEvent` and `handle.done` remain pending indefinitely, which also prevents the existing HTTP retry path from running.

This change settles the active request immediately on `error`, marks the connection closed, and closes the socket. A focused regression simulates an error with no close event and verifies both promises reject.

cd extensions/copilot
node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/platform/networking/node/test/chatWebSocketManager.spec.ts

body:

title: Use refresh token for XAA when available
body:
For #316625

## Summary

In the XAA (Cross App Access / Enterprise Managed Auth) flow, VS Code bootstraps an IdP session with the `openid offline_access` scopes, obtaining both an ID token and a refresh token. Previously, only the ID Token was used as the `subject_token` in the RFC 8693 token exchange that mints an ID-JAG (leg 2). Because ID tokens are short-lived (typically 1 hour), any attempt to silently obtain an access token for an MCP server after the ID token expired would fail, even though a long-lived refresh token was already in storage and never used.

This PR changes the subject token preference:

- Prefer refresh token when one is available in the stored IdP session. Refresh tokens are long-lived and do not have the expiry problem.
- Fall back to ID token for IdPs that do not issue a refresh token (e.g. when `offline_access` is refused).

## Changes

- `oauth.ts`: Adds `TOKEN_TYPE_REFRESH_TOKEN` constant. Generalises `buildIdJagExchangeBody` to accept explicit `subjectToken` / `subjectTokenType` parameters instead of hardcoding ID token.
- `extHostAuthentication.ts`: Widens `_tokenStore` visibility from private to protected so the XAA mixin can look up raw tokens (including refresh token) by access_token.
- `extHostXaaAuthProvider.ts`: Adds `_hasSubjectToken()` helper. Updates `_mintResourceToken` to resolve the subject token — looking up the raw `IAuthorizationToken` from the store and preferring refresh token when present. Updates the early guards in `getSessions` and `createSession` to accept either token type.
- `oauth.test.ts`: Updates existing `buildIdJagExchangeBody` call sites to pass the explicit token type argument; adds a new test case for the refresh token subject type.

## Testing

1. Sign in to an IdP that issues refresh tokens with `offline_access` — confirm the token exchange request sends `subject_token_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:refresh_token`.
2. Wait for / simulate an expired ID token in the stored session — confirm silent re-mint succeeds without prompting the user.
3. Sign in to an IdP that does not issue a refresh token — confirm the flow falls back to ID token and behaves as before.

title: Migrate per-request credits when adopting legacy EH Copilot CLI sessions
body:
Fixes  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/329999

### Summary

 When a legacy extension-host Copilot CLI session is migrated in place to the agent host, its per-request credit info was lost.

**Why it was lost:** the extension host persists credits in a sidecar file next to the SDK event log — `~/.copilot/session-state/<id>/vscode.requests.metadata.json`, as `RequestDetails[]` with `creditsUsed`. The agent host instead keeps them in the per-session SQLite `turn_usage` table, which `AgentService._applyPersistedTurnUsage` overlays onto turns at restore. `mapSessionEvents` does not reconstruct usage from `events.jsonl`, so adoption — which reuses the event log verbatim and seeds only VS Code-layer metadata — left `turn_usage` empty.

**Fix:** after a successful adoption, `CopilotAgent._adoptLegacyTurnUsage` reads the sidecar and writes one `turn_usage` row per request. `RequestDetails.copilotRequestId` is the SDK `user.message` envelope id — the exact id `mapSessionEvents` restores turns under — so no id translation is needed. Credits convert to nano-AIU (`credits * 1e9`), the unit the renderer divides back out.

**Scope**

Deliberately limited to sessions actually being migrated. `_adoptLegacyTurnUsage` is called from exactly one place — the success path of `ensureChatAdopted`, past every eligibility gate — so it is unreachable for:

- native / already-adopted agent-host sessions (live usage stays authoritative, never rewritten)
- other Copilot SDK sessions sharing `~/.copilot` (standalone CLI, Local agent, the GitHub Copilot app's `origin: 'other'` markers)
- any session at all when `chat.agentSessions.migrateLegacyCopilotCli` is off (default)

No protocol, schema, or setting changes. The restore and live-usage paths are untouched.

title: agentHost: EH migration - show worktree sessions in a window opened on their repository folder
body:
Fixes #329966
Fixes #329970

### Summary

Legacy Copilot CLI sessions that used a worktree didn't migrate when opened from the editor window, even though the same session migrated fine in the Agents window.

**Why:** the session list decides which sessions belong to your window by checking whether the session's folder sits inside the folder you have open. A worktree session runs in a separate folder *next to* the repository, not inside it — so it failed that check and never appeared in the list. Without it, clicking the session opened the old extension-host version instead of the agent-host one, and migration never ran. The Agents window has no folder open, so it shows everything and worked fine.

**Fix:** also match a session by its repository. The agent host already knows which repo a worktree session belongs to; that information just wasn't reaching the list. Now a session shows up if either its folder *or* its repository matches the window.

This only ever adds sessions to the list, never removes them, so nothing that shows today can disappear. Sessions from other repositories still don't appear.

It also fixes the same problem for regular (non-migrated) worktree sessions, which were invisible in folder windows too.

### Tests

Added a test covering a worktree session in a window opened on its repository, which also checks that a worktree from a *different* repository stays hidden.

title: Add regression tests for thenable RPC proxies
body:
Follow-up to #330923, which stopped the observable debugger RPC proxies and Copilot's worker RPC proxy from answering `then`. This adds the regression coverage that was intentionally left out of that PR.

## Why

Those proxies synthesize a callable for **any** property name, so without the guard `proxy.then` is a function and the proxy is a **thenable**. `await`ing one — or returning it from an `async` function — hands the promise machinery's own `resolve`/`reject` callbacks to a remote `then` call that never invokes them, and the await never settles. That is the deadlock originally hit in #330571.

The guards are four unremarkable-looking lines. Without tests, a future reader can delete them as dead code and silently reintroduce a hang that only shows up as a spinner in the UI.

## Tests

| Test | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| `src/vs/base/test/common/observableInternal/logging/debugger/rpc.test.ts` | `SimpleTypedRpcConnection` `requests` + `notifications` proxies |
| `extensions/copilot/src/util/node/test/worker.spec.ts` | `createRpcProxy`, exposed publicly as `WorkerWithRpcProxy.proxy` |

Each asserts the proxy exposes no `then` and that awaiting it resolves to the proxy itself. The Copilot test additionally asserts no remote call was dispatched, since the failure mode is a spurious `then` call over the wire.

## Validation

Confirmed these are genuine regression tests, not tautologies — each was run with its corresponding guard temporarily reverted and **fails**, then passes once restored:

- Core, guards reverted: `AssertionError: + [AsyncFunction (anonymous)] - undefined`
- Copilot, guard reverted: fails on the `then` assertion
- Both green against current `main`

The core test needs `observableInternal` internals, so it carries an `eslint-disable-next-line local/code-no-deep-import-of-internal` matching the existing convention in `src/vs/base/test/common/observables/observable.test.ts`.

title: agentHost: stop legacy Copilot CLI sessions from migrating on list/scroll and enforce the migrate setting
body:
Fixes #330383

### Summary

**Context**
Two behaviors could still migrate extension-host Copilot CLI sessions the user never intended to migrate 

**1. Listing/scrolling migrated sessions.** The sessions list runs a read-state migration that dispatches session/isReadChanged for each row. In AgentService.dispatchAction, a session action on an un-loaded session triggers restoreSession → ensureChatAdopted, which writes the migration database. So merely refreshing or scrolling the list adopted sessions.

**2. Toggling the setting off didn't fully stop migration.** A session surfaced as adoptable while the setting was on stayed adoptable after it was turned off (migrateLegacyEnabled || surfacedAdoptable), so opening it still migrated — an ON→OFF inconsistency.

### **Changes (all in agentService.ts):**

**1. Passive read/archive actions no longer migrate.** Added _isPassiveMetadataAction and, in dispatchAction, drop a passive session/isReadChanged / isArchivedChanged action when it targets an un-loaded, surfaced-adoptable legacy session. The client applies read/archive optimistically and un-opened sessions hold no server-side pending state, so dropping the action is side-effect-free.

**2. Open-adoption strictly gated on the live setting.** In _doRestoreSession, adoption is now !external && migrateLegacyEnabled (removed the || surfacedAdoptable term). Migration happens only while the setting is on, and only on explicit open.

**3. Un-surface adoptable entries when the setting turns off.** Folded into the existing onDidRootConfigChange handler: on an ON→OFF transition, adoptable-legacy entries that were surfaced but never opened are retracted (reusing retractSurfacedSession; no data deleted). This removes the stale-entry dead-end that (2) would otherwise create — the extension-host provider entry takes back over, so the session stays visible and opens via the legacy path.

### **Behavior:**
**Setting OFF** (default): EH sessions remain visible; opening never migrates; listing/scrolling never migrates.
**Setting ON**: only an explicit open migrates; listing/scrolling/marking-read never does.
**ON → OFF** (same run): surfaced-but-unopened entries are retracted; opening no longer migrates; already-migrated sessions stay migrated.

### **Tests**
Updated the outdated "adopts even when the setting is off" test to the strict semantics (off → no adopt; on → adopts).
Added regressions for the passive-drop and the un-surface-on-disable behaviors.

title: sessions: collapse cloud sandboxes into one agent host filter entry
body:
## The problem

The agent host filter (the host picker on vscode.dev/agents) assumed **one provider = one host**. `AgentHostFilterService` turned every registered remote agent-host provider into exactly one picker entry, and `SessionsList.update()` scoped the list with `session.providerId === selectedProviderId`.

Cloud sandboxes broke that assumption. `CloudSandboxAgentHostContribution._ensureProvider` registers one provider **per sandbox environment** (`agenthost-cloudsandbox__<envId>`), and Mission Control creates one session per environment. So a user with 20 tasks got 20 picker entries, each showing exactly one session — burying the tunnel machines the picker exists to switch between.

The conceptual mismatch: a picker entry meant two things at once — *which machine am I connected to* (identity) and *which sessions do I see* (scope). For tunnels those are 1:1. A sandbox is a per-session ephemeral box, so the 1:1 assumption collapses.

Knock-on effects from the same root cause:
- Default selection could land on a sandbox — `_validate` fell back to `hosts[0]` sorted alphabetically, so a fresh vscode.dev profile could open scoped to a random task's ephemeral environment.
- `Manage Remote Agent Hosts…` listed every sandbox as a removable host.
- `WebWorkspacePicker` scoped new-session workspaces to a single entry, so "new session" targeted one sandbox.

Desktop was unaffected — `_applyHosts` only computes a selection when `isWeb`.

## The change

Decouple "connection" from "picker entry" via a new `IAgentHostGroup`. Each sandbox keeps its own provider and connection (one address, one credential set, one session-type authority), but providers sharing a group id fold into **one** filter entry.

- **`IAgentHostGroup`** (`sessions/common/agentHostSessionsProvider.ts`) — a provider may declare `hostGroup: { id, label, icon?, order?, connectable? }`. Tunnels/WSL/SSH omit it and keep the existing 1:1 mapping.
- **`IAgentHostFilterEntry`** gains `id`, `providerIds`, `icon`, and `connectable`. `AgentHostFilterService._rewatchProviders` buckets by `hostGroup?.id ?? provider.id` and rolls up member status (a group reads connected if any member is).
- **Selection is set-based** — `selectedProviderId` → `selectedHostId` + `selectedHost`. Consumers scope by the entry's whole `providerIds` set.
- **Cloud sandboxes declare the group** — `{ id: 'cloudsandbox', label: 'Cloud Sandboxes', icon: package, order: 1, connectable: false }`. `connectable: false` because a sandbox connects when one of its sessions is opened, so a connect/disconnect toggle would act on nothing the user pointed at.

Collateral fixes in the same change:
- `_validate` prefers the first **connectable** entry, so a fresh profile can't default into the sandbox group. (Worth noting: "Cloud Sandboxes" sorts before "Host A" alphabetically — only this rule keeps the default off it. There's a test for exactly this.)
- The connect/disconnect button is hidden and the "(disconnected)" menu suffix dropped for non-connectable entries — a group of 12 sandboxes reading "disconnected" looked broken.
- Grouped members are excluded from `Manage Remote Agent Hosts…` — you can't meaningfully "remove" a sandbox; discovery would just recreate it.
- `WebWorkspacePicker` shows recents across all group members but no "Select Folder…" for a group, since there's no single machine to browse.

## Migration

The persisted storage key is unchanged and now holds an entry id. A stale `agenthost-cloudsandbox__<envId>` value simply fails validation and falls through to the connectable-first fallback — no migration code needed.

## Reviewer notes

- **`_rewatchProviders` autorun**: `connectionStatus.read(reader)` is the unconditional first statement of every loop iteration, so no provider can drop out of the autorun's dependency set when grouping short-circuits.

`/btw` currently opens another full chat. This change keeps the source transcript and composer in place and presents the side answer in a transient card immediately above the existing composer.

## Reviewer TL;DR

**A normal durable side chat, with a transient presentation.** The provider still owns the conversation, history, model and response. Closing removes only the card; the same backing chat remains recoverable from the session's Side Chats menu. **Open Full Chat** opens that conversation through the normal Sessions navigation path.

The feature defaults off behind `chat.agentSessions.transientSideChat` (`config.chat.agentSessions.transientSideChat` in ExP). Disabled treatment or an unavailable source host uses the existing full-chat open-and-split flow.

**Invariant:** `/btw` must not hide, replace, move, rebind, or restyle the source composer.

Rebased onto `main` at `17c5935aa72`. The history remains four dependency-ordered commits:

| Commit | Purpose | Review focus |
|---|---|---|
| `570205ea0fb` — `chat: refactor: support embedded response widgets` | Generic response-widget options, hidden-input layout, focus-local routing | Existing full-chat behavior stays the default; embedded renderers cannot shadow full surfaces |
| `41d2771964c` — `sessions: refactor: make send lifecycle explicit` | Request IDs, awaited `preserveActiveChat`, close history, provider option boundary | Concurrent and failing sends cannot affect another navigation follow |
| `2faa43c0465` — `sessions: feat: add transient side-chat presentation` | Card, rollout gate, orchestration, all entry points, accessibility and regressions | Presentation ownership, cleanup, error handling, focus and measured layout |
| `301fb9e55a9` — `agentHost: polish: skip side-chat rename round-trip` | Independent latency optimization | Rename reminder suppressed only for `SideChat` origins |

The durable architecture contract is in `src/vs/sessions/SESSIONS.md`, **Transient side questions**.

## Ownership and flow

```text
/btw, response-selection question, or workbench Ask in Side Chat
  -> create a real provider-backed side chat
  -> ISideChatOrchestrationService.prepare(...)
     -> control / no live interactive host: open and split the full side chat
     -> treatment + live host: close with skipHistory, publish transient state
  -> prepared.send(...)
     -> transient: awaited send with preserveActiveChat
     -> full: ordinary foreground send
  -> provider streams into the side-chat model
```

`ITransientSideChatService` stores resource identities, not provider facades. It resolves current session/chat state reactively and revalidates a per-source presentation ID after awaiting close. Replaced questions, deletion, facade replacement, setting disable, final-host disposal and read-only transitions cannot leave a stale live card.

`ISessionsManagementService` owns provider routing and paired send-start/send-end request IDs. `ISessionsService` owns visible navigation. The `background` and `preserveActiveChat` flags never cross the provider boundary; the explicit provider field picker has a compile-time exhaustiveness guard.

Promotion and full-chat fallback verify that the requested destination became active. A late promotion result cannot delete a replacement card.

## Layout and shared widget integration

The variable-height card is an **in-flow child of `ChatInputPart`**, after the floating status-pill lane and before banners/the original composer. It does not use the fixed-height floating lane or inherit that lane's pointer-event behavior.

The nested `ChatWidget` renders response rows only, with no header/footer, follow-ups, pet or go-to-bottom control, and no visible nested composer. It is created lazily; model loads are identity/cancellation guarded; dismissal releases the widget, model reference, listeners and scheduled layout.

`isEmbedded` provides focus-local action routing while excluding the renderer from full-widget discovery. Event-driven consumers use `lastFocusedChatSurface`. Embedded widgets inherit the enclosing surface's Find support, so Cmd/Ctrl+F continues working from the answer. Both Sessions and workbench Agent Host pills explicitly publish persistent-content visibility, including when the input is read-only.

Layout is frame-coalesced and skips unchanged dimensions. Short answers stay compact; long answers are capped at **60% of the source view**, including the fractional header height, divider and outer borders. Scrolling remains inside the answer. Auto routing metadata is hidden only inside transient cards; the ordinary full chat still shows it.

## Failure handling and accessibility

`FailedAndPresented` means a live card owns the send failure. Dismissed or promoting cards decline that ownership, allowing normal caller notification instead of losing the error during promotion. Failure details are retained if promotion itself fails.

The card is a labelled region described by its question and visible status. Announcements are transition-based. Escape dismisses a pending or completed card, but yields to code-editor selections, suggestion UI and hover. From the source input it additionally yields to active requests, dictation, editing and confirmation interactions. Close returns source focus; successful promotion focuses the full-chat destination.

## Review and verification

Opus 5 maximum-reasoning reviews covered Sessions presentation, lifecycle/orchestration, shared workbench behavior and latest-main integration. Findings were fixed and re-reviewed. The OSS run then exposed routing metadata and border-budget regressions; those were fixed, regression-covered, re-reviewed, and the entire live flow was repeated.

Current validation:

- Complete development build via `npm run build-fast`; client type check and changed-file ESLint/Stylelint pass.
- **283 focused Electron tests pass** (2 existing pending), including send/promotion races, read-only pill visibility, real fractional-header/border measurement, metadata scoping, source input, Find and side-chat entry points.
- **44 Agent Host title tests pass**.
- **Ten authenticated, provider-backed Code OSS scenarios pass on the final rebased build**: source context/composer identity and styling; Find from the card; draft preservation; strict height cap; internal wheel scrolling; code-selection Escape; promotion; pending-card dismissal; selected-response questions; and live setting disable/full-chat fallback.

Screenshots, a Playwright trace, assertion results and a 59-second recording were retained with the session's OSS evidence report.
