title: AgentHost: fall back to Auto when a selected Copilot CLI model is unavailable
body:
> [!NOTE]
> This is a **potential fix** based on a telemetry investigation, not a confirmed
> root-cause fix. This PR description was written by GitHub Copilot, and the commit is
> co-authored by Copilot. Please review the reasoning critically before merging.

## Problem

During the AHP stable rollout (`ahp-both-windows`, 25% stage), **Copilot CLI on the Agent Host**
(`sessiontype = agent-host-copilotcli`) shows roughly **2× the request error rate** of Copilot CLI on
the Extension Host (`copilotcli`). Claude on Agent Host is at parity-or-better, so this is specific to
the Copilot CLI model path, not the Agent Host generally.

The regression is concentrated in **model selection**. Comparing the two harnesses by model class and
looking at the full **success rate** (not just error rate):

| Model class | AH success% | EH success% | note |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| auto | 86.3 | 87.1 | ~parity |
| named (claude-*, gpt-*, …) | 87.0 | 87.6 | ~parity |
| **path-like (BYOK/Ollama/custom)** | **51.0** | **87.5** | **the regression** |
| empty (no resolvable model) | 34.4 | 29.5 | bad on both |

The standout is **path-like model ids** (BYOK/Ollama/custom models such as
`ollama/qwen2.5-coder:latest`, `provider/model:7b`): they are **~38× more prevalent on the Agent Host
picker** than on the Extension Host and drop from ~88% to ~51% success. These are selectable on the AH
Copilot-CLI picker (the harness publishes its own model list, including bridged renderer BYOK models),
whereas the EH `copilotcli` picker never offered them. This is **causally isolated**: within the same
ExP cohort — and even for the *same* treatment-cohort users — path-like models succeed on EH but fail
on AH, and a separate harness-side event (`agenthost.turncompleted`, un-redacted model) reproduces the
same 51% / 88% split.

Two code facts make an unavailable/stale selection fail hard instead of degrading gracefully:

1. The AH send path forwards the remembered model id **raw** to the harness/SDK with no
   validate-and-fallback step (`baseAgentHostSessionsProvider` → `copilotSessionLauncher`).
2. The restore path was recently changed (#326938) to keep a remembered agent-host selection
   `pending` (wait for the async model list) instead of falling back to Auto — which is correct for
   restore, but means a genuinely-unavailable selection can still be *sent*.

The Copilot SDK then throws on an unroutable model id rather than falling back to Auto, so the whole
turn errors.

## What this PR does

Adds a small **send-time** validation in `BaseAgentHostSessionsProvider`. Before dispatching a
request, `_resolveSendModelId(...)` resolves the selected model against the session's available
models (`getModelsSnapshot`). If the selection is **conclusively `unavailable`** *and* the harness
supports Auto, it drops the selection so the request falls back to the harness default/Auto instead
of erroring on a model id the harness cannot route. It is applied in both send paths
(`_sendCommittedChatRequest` and `_sendNewSessionRequest`).

This intentionally mirrors the model picker's own removed-model fallback, applying it at send time
where an unavailable selection is authoritative (the restore-time `pending` grace from #326938 is
preserved — `pending` selections are left untouched). Sessions that require an explicit model and do
**not** support Auto (e.g. Copilot Free/Student Claude) keep their selection, so the existing "no
models available" UX is unchanged.

## ⚠️ Product caveat (BYOK → Auto)

For a *deliberately-chosen* BYOK/Ollama model, silently redirecting to Copilot's cloud `auto` defeats
the user's local/privacy intent and sends their prompt to the cloud. This guard only fires when the
selection is **conclusively unavailable** (the request would otherwise fail), so it trades a hard
failure for a cloud fallback — but reviewers should decide whether a **clear, actionable error** (or a
hardened BYOK bridge) is preferable to Auto for BYOK selections. Note BYOK-on-AH is currently
experimental (remote unsupported per #325738; local behind `chat.agentHost.byokModels.enabled`).

## Scope / expected impact

- Targets the **path-like/BYOK and stale-selection** slice — the clearest, causally-isolated
  regression (~715 devices). Together with the `empty` bucket this is ~57% of AH Copilot-CLI errors.
- `named`/`auto` models are **at success parity** AH vs EH (~87% each), so they are **not** the target
  and not meaningfully regressed. (This corrects an earlier framing that described a "broad degradation
  of all models" — the total-error increase there is mostly offset by fewer cancellations.)
- Only partially helps the `empty`-model bucket (no resolvable model / not-authed / model-list-not-
  ready) and does **not** address BYOK-bridge *inference* failures (where a model resolves but the
  renderer↔node↔loopback bridge fails mid-stream, ~1/3 of path-like failures).

## Testing

- ESLint clean; type-checks locally.
- ⚠️ No automated test added yet and this has not been validated against live sessions — it is a
  proposed mitigation. Suggested validation: confirm the AH `copilotcli` success rate for the
  path-like model bucket improves without regressing sessions that legitimately use Auto or a valid
  explicit model.

## Analysis reference & caveats

- Regression is a property of the harness (`sessiontype`), not the ExP cohort; present within every
  VS Code build (rules out a version confound); appeared only when the 25% ramp routed the general
  population onto the Agent Host path.
- **Data limitation:** there is no direct error-category telemetry for the regression period — the
  `errorType`/`modelSelectionKind` fields are on `agenthost.turncompleted` (not
  `interactivesessionproviderinvoked`) and only on 1.131-insider. The root cause is inferred from the
  model-class correlation + code + corroborating issues (#318401, #319583, #326938, #326941, #321810).

title: Stream built-in shell output over AHP terminal channel
body:
Related: https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/pull/352
Resolves: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/324825
Part of: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/323399

Adopts the terminal completion model from microsoft/agent-host-protocol#352 and supersedes the cumulative-Text approach from #326291.

- Re-vendor the pending AHP contract: remove `terminalComplete`, move `exitCode`/`preview`/`truncated` onto the terminal block as `result`, and add `isPty` to terminal tool results and terminal state.
- Stream public Copilot SDK `tool.execution_partial_result` events into output-only AHP terminal channels for runtime-executed shell tools, while leaving client-hosted PTY terminals on their existing path.
- Treat partial output as cumulative runtime snapshots: append only the unseen suffix while the snapshot grows, then clear and replay it when truncation rewrites the snapshot.
- Create the output channel before publishing its terminal block, including commands with no partial events; seed final preview data, persist the exit result, and keep background channels open until `shell_completed` supplies the real exit code.
- Attach non-PTY channels to chat through a read-only output source without creating an `ITerminalInstance`, adding a root terminal entry, opening a bottom-panel terminal, or exposing terminal Focus/Show actions.
- Render plain-text output in the existing detached xterm, normalize LF to CRLF only in the Agent Host output adapter, and serialize append/reset writes so streaming output is neither duplicated nor stale.
- Preserve live auto-expansion and running/completed command decorations for output-only tools while leaving the existing PTY decoration path unchanged.
- Reconstruct history with a stable non-PTY terminal URI and structured result, while retaining a structural fallback for old persisted `terminalComplete` blocks.
- Re-apply the local `CompletionItem.label` extension from #326807 after protocol generation. The generated snapshot still needs a final `.ahp-version` sync after microsoft/agent-host-protocol#352 lands.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- The `isPty` and `result: TerminalCommandResult` shapes come from the protocol change itself: [`ToolResultTerminalContent`/`TerminalCommandResult`](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/blob/4c2e10105f13b1de659d3f253f8ad05fc48036a8/types/channels-chat/state.ts#L1398-L1432) and [`TerminalState.isPty`](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/blob/4c2e10105f13b1de659d3f253f8ad05fc48036a8/types/channels-terminal/state.ts#L110-L116).
- The attach-once terminal-block policy extends the existing PTY completion deduplication in [`copilotAgentSession`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9aab2f51076649ada9d3d8412558fd1484dd5f04/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L3293-L3304).
- Updating terminal state before dispatching data, so late subscribers can reconstruct output from the snapshot, follows [`AgentHostTerminalManager._handlePtyData`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9aab2f51076649ada9d3d8412558fd1484dd5f04/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostTerminalManager.ts#L608-L638).
- The output-only channel URI follows the existing Agent Host shell namespace in [`copilotShellTools`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9aab2f51076649ada9d3d8412558fd1484dd5f04/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotShellTools.ts#L172-L179).
- Output-only auto-expansion reuses the command lifecycle semantics already used by the AHP terminal path in [`ChatTerminalToolProgressPart._attachAhpCommandSource`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9aab2f51076649ada9d3d8412558fd1484dd5f04/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentParts/toolInvocationParts/chatTerminalToolProgressPart.ts#L926-L987).

title: gate nonpty terminal actions
body:
Summary
Fixes the inline terminal preview offering "Focus/Show Terminal" and a "view stale terminal" action for non-pty (SDK built-in / streaming) shell runs, where there is no real interactive terminal to focus.

The bug
The chat terminal preview (ChatTerminalToolProgressPart) decides whether to show the Focus/Show-Terminal action purely from whether a terminal instance exists (_toolbarHasInstance = !!terminalInstance), and its "open the terminal" fallback calls terminalService.openResource(terminalCommandUri). Neither has any notion of whether that terminal is a real interactive pty or an output-only, non-pty channel.

That distinction started to matter with the shell-output-streaming work (https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/327067): to stream output, a non-pty SDK shell run now emits a Terminal content block (agenthost-terminal://shell/copilotNonPtyShells/{toolCallId}, isPty: false). The adapter sets terminalToolSessionId for any Terminal block with no isPty guard, so a non-pty run now gets a terminalToolSessionId → a revived ITerminalInstance → _toolbarHasInstance === true → the Focus/Show action and the stale openResource fallback render. But these terminals are output-only: there is nothing interactive to focus, and "opening" them just surfaces an empty/stale terminal.

The protocol already carries the needed signal — isPty on ToolResultTerminalContent / TerminalState — but it was only consumed on the host side (agentHostPty uses it to set convertEol). It never reached IChatTerminalToolInvocationData, and the widget never gated any UI on it.

Approach
Propagate the existing isPty signal end-to-end to the renderer, and gate the instance-dependent affordances on it — rather than inventing a new heuristic in the UI. Output-only non-pty terminals keep their preview (command, decoration, streamed output) but drop the actions that only make sense for a real interactive pty.

Changes and why
stateToProgressAdapter.ts (buildTerminalToolSpecificData) and agentHostSessionHandler.ts (_reviveTerminalIfNeeded) — read isPty off the Terminal content block and carry it onto the invocation data, in both producers, via a shared getTerminalContentIsPty helper.
Why: the terminal payload is built in two places — the main builder (create / streaming refresh / finalize / history replay) and the async terminal-revive path — so both must set the flag for it to stay consistent across every lifecycle stage. ?? existing preserves it across streaming refreshes.

chatService.ts (IChatTerminalToolInvocationData) — add the isPty field.
Why: the renderer had no channel to learn a terminal was non-pty; this is the missing carrier.

chatTerminalToolProgressPart.ts — add a single _isNonPtyTerminal (isPty === false) check and use it to hide the Focus/Show Terminal action and early-return focusTerminal() for non-pty terminals. The early-return covers every caller — the toolbar button, the "Focus Most Recent Terminal" command, and the collapsible "Show" link — including the stale openResource(terminalCommandUri) fallback.
Why: for output-only non-pty terminals there is no interactive session to focus; showing the action or opening a stale/empty terminal is misleading. The command decoration and streamed output are unaffected — only the interactive affordances are withheld.

stateToProgressAdapter.test.ts — assert isPty is threaded from the block (false / true / unset) and that it survives a streaming-output refresh (the revive → refresh race).

Notes / not in scope
Command decoration and output streaming for these runs are handled by https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/327067 (exit code now lives on the terminal block result; output streams via the non-pty channel). This PR only removes the incorrect interactive affordances.
The isPty semantics match the protocol flag added in https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/327067: false = output-only non-pty channel; true/absent = pty-backed (custom-terminal or local) — those keep Focus/Show.
Known gap / follow-up
The isPty data-threading is unit-tested, but the widget gating behavior itself — Focus/Show hidden and focusTerminal() a no-op for non-pty cards — has no direct test. ChatTerminalToolProgressPart is never constructed in the test suite, and doing so needs substantial service/DOM mock setup, so it was left as a follow-up rather than done here. The gating is currently covered by the adapter tests plus reasoning; a widget-level test should be added to lock it in.

title: sessions: fix Agents window hang with per-group editor limit of 1
body:
Fixes #327066

## What

Enforce `showTabs: 'multiple'` and `limit: { enabled: false }` on the single-pane editor part (`SinglePaneMainEditorPart`) via the existing `enforcePartOptions` API.

## Why

The single-pane docked tab bar keeps several managed editors open at once — the pinned Changes multi-diff tab, the Files placeholder, and any real file tabs (`[Changes][Files][file…]`). Two user settings break this layout:

- `workbench.editor.showTabs` set to `single`/`none` collapses the docked tab strip.
- `workbench.editor.limit` (especially `perEditorGroup: true, value: 1`) makes `EditorsObserver` auto-evict the least-recently-used tab. Since the managed tabs are pinned (not sticky), they get evicted, the managed-tab reconciliation reopens them, and the observer evicts again — an infinite open/close loop that hangs the renderer (the reported bug).

## Notes for reviewers

- Scoped to the single-pane editor part only; the user's `workbench.editor.showTabs` / `workbench.editor.limit` settings are untouched everywhere else.
- `limit: { enabled: false }` is sufficient because `EditorsObserver.ensureOpenedEditorsLimit` returns early when the limit is disabled, so the other limit fields are never read.
- The `showTabs` enforcement was already present; this PR adds the `limit` enforcement to close the hang.

title: chat: segmented voice/dictation toggle with hold-to-talk and listen-button styles
body:
## Segmented Voice / Dictation input toggle — two interaction styles

Option A:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c09956a3-133e-46a2-84b9-3c3429195b7e


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/964adb82-716f-4ee8-94be-e1ff813e5304

Option B:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dc28cb69-eb4d-4010-89bc-cdd4658153e6






Replaces the two independent mic buttons in the chat input with a **single segmented control** that unifies Dictation and live Voice Mode, and adds **two selectable Voice Mode interaction styles** to compare. Everything is gated behind experimental settings and defaults off.

### Why
Watching people use Voice Mode for the first time, a recurring problem was ending up in *both* dictation and voice at once, and confusion about which button connects vs. toggles listening vs. disconnects. This unifies the two into one discoverable control with clear animated state feedback, and mutual exclusion so you can only be in one mode at a time.

### Settings
- `chat.voiceInputMode.segmentedToggle` (boolean, default `false`) — show the single segmented control instead of the two separate mic buttons.
- `chat.voiceInputMode.interactionStyle` (`holdToTalk` | `listenButton`, default `holdToTalk`) — how Voice Mode drives listening.

### The two interaction styles
1. **`holdToTalk`** — the voice button is push-to-talk: **hold** it (or the `Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+Space` keybinding) to talk, release to send; a **quick tap** turns Voice Mode off.
2. **`listenButton`** — the voice button is a **power toggle** (connect / disconnect, and starts listening on connect); a **separate person-voice button** toggles listening on and off in manual mode.

### Highlights
- Dictation and Voice Mode live in one constant-size housing; icons slide/collapse between states.
- Voice Mode renders as an animated **Device EQ waveform** that transforms by state: idle undulating wave, **blue** mic-reactive listening, **purple** TTS-reactive speaking, and a short "silent" hover preview for disconnect — colors match the input-box glow.
- **Fix:** live Voice Mode previously cut off after ~one word. `pttDown`/`pttUp` now take a `force` flag so hold-to-talk records a clean turn and finishes on release, bypassing the short-tap toggle mode and the auto-send silence timer.
- Removes the Voice Mode settings gear from the voice widget/header.
- Dev-only **prototype walkthrough** commands (one per style) drive the pill bars, colors, hover previews and the real input-box glow so the styles can be compared without a live backend.

Legacy standalone voice/dictation buttons remain as the fallback when the setting is off.

### Testing
- Enable `chat.voiceInputMode.segmentedToggle`.
- Try each `chat.voiceInputMode.interactionStyle`.
- Dev preview without a backend: run **Developer: Voice Input Mode: Prototype Walkthrough — …** from the Command Palette; clear with **Voice Input Mode: Simulate — Clear**.

title: Stream built-in shell output over AHP terminal channel
body:
Related: https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/pull/352
Resolves: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/324825
Part of: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/323399

- Adopt the terminal completion model from microsoft/agent-host-protocol#352: move command `exitCode`/`preview`/`truncated` onto the terminal result and distinguish PTY-backed terminals from plain-text output channels with `isPty`.
- Stream public Copilot SDK `tool.execution_partial_result` events from runtime-executed shell tools into output-only AHP terminal channels, while keeping client-hosted PTY terminals on their existing path.
- Treat partial output as cumulative runtime snapshots: append only the unseen suffix while a snapshot grows, then clear and replay it when runtime truncation rewrites the snapshot.
- Create an output channel on the first partial result or when foreground shell completion supplies retained output or exit metadata. Leave background shell handoff and completions with neither output nor exit metadata out of the inline terminal path.
- Prefer structured SDK `shell_exit` metadata for the command result. When the external SDK bridge removes that block, use the runtime's trailing shell-completion marker as a scoped non-PTY fallback for the exit code and retained preview.
- Attach output-only channels to chat through a read-only output source without creating an `ITerminalInstance`, adding a root terminal entry, opening a panel terminal, or exposing terminal Focus/Show actions.
- Render the plain-text stream in the existing detached xterm, normalize line endings only in the Agent Host output adapter, and serialize snapshot writes so growing or rewritten output is not duplicated or stale.
- Preserve live auto-expansion and running/completed decorations for output-only tools. Existing Local harness and Agent Host PTY terminal behavior remain on the original path unless `isPty === false`.
- Scope output-channel URIs by Agent Host session and tool call, and reconstruct completed history from the terminal's structured result.
- Re-vendor the generated protocol snapshot after microsoft/agent-host-protocol#352 lands and use its final commit for `.ahp-version`.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- The `isPty` and `result: TerminalCommandResult` shapes come from the protocol change itself: [`ToolResultTerminalContent`/`TerminalCommandResult`](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/blob/4c2e10105f13b1de659d3f253f8ad05fc48036a8/types/channels-chat/state.ts#L1398-L1432) and [`TerminalState.isPty`](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/blob/4c2e10105f13b1de659d3f253f8ad05fc48036a8/types/channels-terminal/state.ts#L110-L116).
- Publishing a terminal block once extends the existing PTY completion deduplication in [`copilotAgentSession`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9aab2f51076649ada9d3d8412558fd1484dd5f04/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L3293-L3304).
- Updating terminal state before dispatching data, so late subscribers can reconstruct output from the snapshot, follows [`AgentHostTerminalManager._handlePtyData`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9aab2f51076649ada9d3d8412558fd1484dd5f04/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostTerminalManager.ts#L608-L638).
- The output-only channel URI follows the existing Agent Host shell namespace in [`copilotShellTools`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9aab2f51076649ada9d3d8412558fd1484dd5f04/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotShellTools.ts#L172-L179).
- Output-only auto-expansion reuses the command lifecycle semantics already used by the AHP terminal path in [`ChatTerminalToolProgressPart._attachAhpCommandSource`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/9aab2f51076649ada9d3d8412558fd1484dd5f04/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentParts/toolInvocationParts/chatTerminalToolProgressPart.ts#L926-L987).

title: Avoid :has() selectors that trigger workbench-wide style invalidation
body:
Fixes #327048

A `:has()` whose anchor exists in the live DOM makes every DOM mutation, including the inline `letter-spacing` writes the editor performs on each layout, pay a style recalc that scales with the whole visible workbench (measurements and per-rule profiling in the issue). The single biggest offender is the chat working set scrollbar rule; the root-anchored rules in floatingPanels.css and sessionsPolicyBlocked.css are the same hazard and the same class of problem that #324986 already fixed for the automations dialog.

Changes:

- `chat.css`: the working set scrollbar padding is keyed off an `overflowing` class toggled in `chatInputPart.ts`, which already computes the overflow condition (`allEntries.length > maxItemsShown`), instead of `:has(.visible.scrollbar.vertical)`. Behavior note: the padding now applies whenever the list overflows, not only while the auto-hide scrollbar is faded in. This also stops the labels from shifting under the scrollbar mid-scroll.
- `floatingPanels.css`: the two root-anchored `:has()` rules are replaced by `activitybar-compact` (mirrored onto the workbench root by `activitybarPart.ts`) and `noactivitybar` (toggled by `layout.ts` like the other part visibility classes). A `:not(.noactivitybar)` on the compact rule keeps the hidden+compact case resolving to the hidden inset, matching the specificity behavior of the old rules.
- `sessionsPolicyBlocked.css`: `.monaco-workbench:has(.sessions-policy-blocked-overlay)` becomes a class toggled for the overlay's lifetime.
- `build/stylelint.ts`: new check that errors on `:has()` anchored to a root compound (`body` / `html` / `:root` / `.monaco-workbench`), with a `stylelint-disable has-anchor-checker` escape. It flags all three historical instances (including the original #324985 one) and has no hits on current `src/**/*.css`.

Testing:

- Runtime equivalent of this change (deleting the offending rules from CSSOM plus one full restyle) takes the forced-recalc microbenchmark from 13-16ms to 0.04ms on my machine and makes sash dragging smooth again; details in the issue.
- Verified sash dragging, working set overflow padding (7+ files in the working set), compact/hidden activity bar insets under floating panels, in a local dev build.
- Lint check verified against the three historical bad selectors (all flagged) and a full run over `src/**/*.css` (no findings).

title: Fix Voice Mode panel dictation misrouting to background chat editor
body:
Fixes #327024

## Problem

In Voice Mode with the **panel** chat input, running a request could send it to a **background chat editor** that had been focused earlier instead of the panel, with narration/updates following that background session.

## Root cause

`_chat.voice.acceptInput` routed to `IChatWidgetService.lastFocusedWidget`, which is only updated on a chat widget's `onDidFocus` and is never cleared on blur (only on dispose). After a chat editor was opened/focused it stayed the `lastFocusedWidget`, and because dictating in the panel voice input does not DOM-focus the panel's chat input, the request was dispatched to that stale editor — even though `_chat.voice.getCurrentSession` (reading the panel view pane's own widget) reported the panel.

## Fix

Only trust `lastFocusedWidget` while it still holds input focus (an intentionally focused chat editor); otherwise fall back to the panel view pane's own widget (`this._widget`), keeping the send target consistent with `_chat.voice.getCurrentSession`.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` — clean
- eslint on changed file — clean

title: Fix: apply chat.defaultModel on every new local session
body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/326877

Follow-up to the chat.defaultModel work. Fixes remaining cases in local agent sessions where a new/empty conversation kept the previous session's model instead of resetting to the configured default. These already worked correctly in Agent Host (AHP) sessions.

### **Repro (local only)**
Case 1: Set chat.defaultModel → new session → change model → run a command → press + (new session) → new session showed the previous model instead of the default.

Case 2: Open an old session (non-default model) → back to list resets to default ✓ → change model → run a command → back to list → did not reset to default.

### **Root cause**
Model selection lives in ChatInputModelSelectionController. When any path (re)binds a new/empty session whose incoming input state carries a model spilled over from the previous session, the sync path applies it as a SessionRestore:

> _syncFromModel → syncFromConversationState → _applySessionRestore → _selectionReason = SessionRestore.

applyConfiguredDefault() (run at the end of handleViewModelChange) then bailed because its guard used isAuthoritativeModelSelectionReason(_selectionReason), which counts SessionRestore as authoritative — so the configured default never re-applied.


### Fix
In chatInputModelSelectionController.ts, applyConfiguredDefault() now blocks only on a genuine in-conversation choice — UserSelection or ProgrammaticSelection — instead of any authoritative reason:

```
if (!this._runtime.isEmpty()
    || this._selectionReason === ModelSelectionReason.UserSelection
    || this._selectionReason === ModelSelectionReason.ProgrammaticSelection
    || (this._intent && this._intent.kind !== 'remembered')) {
    return false;
}

```
### Rationale:

A genuinely reopened conversation is non-empty, so it's already protected by !isEmpty() (its saved model is kept).
On an empty session, SessionRestore can only be spillover, so it must yield to the configured default — covering the + new-session, back-to-list, clear/new-chat, late-policy, and model-list-load paths (all route through applyConfiguredDefault).
Genuine in-empty-session user picks and mode-forced selections still stick.

title: fix: persist chat editing timeline telemetryInfo so sessionResource survives reload (fixes #326994)
body:
### Summary An uncaught `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toString')` fires in the chat-editing telemetry path (2500 hits / 965 users on v1.129.1). The crash happens in `ChatModelStore.get` when it calls `uri.toString()` on an `undefined` URI. The `undefined` originates from a `IModifiedEntryTelemetryInfo.sessionResource` field (declared non-nullable `URI`) that becomes `undefined` after a chat editing session is persisted and restored. The producer is `ChatEditingSession._getTelemetryInfoForModel`, which returns an object whose fields are implemented as **prototype getters**. When the checkpoint timeline is persisted with `JSON.stringify`, prototype getters are not own enumerable properties and are silently dropped, so each persisted `telemetryInfo` becomes `{}`. After reload, entries reconstructed from the timeline carry `sessionResource: undefined`, which later crashes the telemetry pipeline. Fixes microsoft/vscode#326994 Recommended reviewer: `@connor4312` ### Culprit Commit Not pinpointed to a single SHA (git history unavailable in this environment). The regression window (first seen 2026-07-15, v1.129.0-insider) corresponds to the introduction of the getter-based `_getTelemetryInfoForModel` object (comment: "Make these getters because the response result is not available when the file first starts to be edited") combined with the checkpoint-timeline persistence path that serializes `telemetryInfo` verbatim. The timeline persistence/replay code is owned by `@connor4312` (checkpoint timeline, epoch replay, edit restore). ### Code Flow ```mermaid flowchart TD A["_getTelemetryInfoForModel
returns object with prototype getters
chatEditingSession.ts:1035"] --> B["FileOperation / IFileBaseline
hold live telemetryInfo"] B --> C["timeline.getStateForPersistence()
chatEditingCheckpointTimelineImpl.ts:444"] C --> D["storeState: JSON.stringify(data)
getters dropped -> telemetryInfo = {}
chatEditingSessionStorage.ts:191,197"] D --> E["restoreState: revive(data.timeline)
telemetryInfo still {} -> sessionResource undefined
chatEditingSessionStorage.ts:114"] E --> F["_reconstructFileState -> setContents
entry gets _telemetryInfo with undefined sessionResource
chatEditingCheckpointTimelineImpl.ts:475"] F --> G["_notifySessionAction reads
_telemetryInfo.sessionResource (undefined)
chatEditingModifiedFileEntry.ts:272,316"] G --> H["notifyUserAction:
_sessionModels.get(action.sessionResource)
chatServiceImpl.ts:377"] H --> I["ChatModelStore.get(undefined)
toKey: uri.toString() -> TypeError
chatModelStore.ts:99,246"] ``` ### Affected Files - `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chatEditing/chatEditingSession.ts` — `_getTelemetryInfoForModel` (the producer). **Modified.** - `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chatEditing/chatEditingCheckpointTimelineImpl.ts` — persists/replays `telemetryInfo` (context, unchanged). - `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chatEditing/chatEditingSessionStorage.ts` — `JSON.stringify`/`revive` of the timeline (context, unchanged). - `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/model/chatModelStore.ts` — crash site `get`/`toKey` (context, unchanged; intentionally not patched). ### Repro Steps 1. Start a chat editing session and let the agent modify a file (creates timeline operations/baselines whose `telemetryInfo` is the getter-based object). 2. Persist the session (`storeState`) and reload the window so the session is restored from disk (`restoreState` → `revive(data.timeline)`). 3. Manually edit the AI-edited file. After ~1s the `RunOnceScheduler` in `chatEditingModifiedFileEntry` fires `_notifySessionAction('userModified')`. 4. `_telemetryInfo.sessionResource` is `undefined` (lost during serialization) → `ChatModelStore.get(undefined)` → `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'toString')`. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** (`chatEditingSession.ts`): add a `toJSON()` method to the anonymous `IModifiedEntryTelemetryInfo` class returned by `_getTelemetryInfoForModel`. `toJSON()` snapshots each getter value into a plain object with own enumerable properties (`agentId`, `modelId`, `modeId`, `command`, `sessionResource`, `requestId`, `applyCodeBlockSuggestionId`, `feature`; `result` is set to `undefined`, matching the snapshot-entry serialization which also drops `result`). `JSON.stringify` honors `toJSON`, so the fields — including `sessionResource` as a serialized URI — now survive persistence and are correctly revived by `revive(data.timeline)`. This is a fix at the data producer, not at the crash site: the object that enters the persistence pipeline is made serializable, rather than adding a null-guard where the `undefined` finally surfaces. Live consumers are unaffected because they read the fields via normal property access, which still hits the getters; only `JSON.stringify` uses `toJSON`. It also restores the other telemetry fields (`requestId`, `agentId`, etc.) that were silently lost from persisted timelines by the same getter-serialization gap. After this change, `_getTelemetryInfoForModel` (chatEditingSession.ts:1035) cannot produce a `telemetryInfo` whose persisted form lacks `sessionResource`, because `toJSON` emits `sessionResource` as an own enumerable property that `JSON.stringify` serializes and `revive` restores. **Alternatives considered:** - Explicitly serialize/deserialize `telemetryInfo` inside the timeline persistence (a dedicated DTO like the snapshot-entry path): rejected as more invasive (new DTO + revive plumbing in the timeline) while addressing the same root cause less directly. - Converting the getters to eager own properties: rejected because the getters exist intentionally so late-available fields (e.g. `result`) reflect the current response state during live use. - Guarding `sessionResource`/`toKey` at the crash site or in `notifyUserAction`: rejected because it hides the bug at the consumer instead of fixing the data producer, and the telemetry pipeline depends on real values. ### Recommended Owner `@connor4312` — owns the chat-editing checkpoint timeline persistence and edit-restore code path (authored the timeline epoch/replay/restore logic in `chatEditingCheckpointTimelineImpl.ts`), which is where the getter-based `telemetryInfo` is serialized and lost. > Generated by [errors-fix](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-engineering/actions/runs/29934562836) · 3.8K AIC · ⌖ 34.9 AIC · ⊞ 71K · [◷](https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amicrosoft%2Fvscode+%22gh-aw-workflow-id%3A+errors-fix%22&type=pullrequests)

title: Agents: honor a late Worktree toggle for Codex sessions (#326963)
body:
## What & why

Builds on the now-merged #326973, which added the reactive worktree-isolation handler that reconciles the pending working-directory marker (`notePending` / `clearPending`) when a still-Creating session's isolation config changes. That fix covers Claude; this PR closes the remaining **Codex-only** gap.

**The gap:** A Codex session that starts in **Folder** isolation eagerly prewarms a folder-bound thread during `createSession`. If the user then checks **Worktree** before the first send, the host correctly creates the worktree and marks the working directory pending, but the already-materialized prewarm thread is never evicted. Because `_sendMessage` only adopts the host-provided directory when `threadId === undefined` (and `_materializeIfNeeded` no-ops once a thread exists), the first turn silently ran in the **folder**, ignoring the worktree.

**The fix:** Implement `CodexAgent.onSessionConfigChanged`. The host invokes it *after* updating the pending marker, so it consults the same single-source-of-truth predicate the prewarm scheduler uses (`isWorkingDirectoryPending`). When the working directory has flipped to pending and there is an unclaimed, materialized prewarm thread, it evicts that stale thread: clears the prewarm timer, drops the thread mapping, and best-effort unsubscribes **only** if a connection already exists (we must never spawn Codex just to tear down a prewarm). The next send then re-materializes in the worktree.

## Diff shape

Purely additive — `2 files changed, 108 insertions(+)`, 0 deletions:

- `src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/codex/codexAgent.ts` (+32): `onSessionConfigChanged` + private `_evictStalePrewarm` + exactly one new comment explaining the prewarm-eviction guard.

title: Extend built-in on-device dictation to editor and terminal
body:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1d033fb7-fc5d-4565-acf3-4c4539f641f9

Extends VS Code's built-in on-device dictation engine (`ILocalTranscriptionService`, surfaced through `IChatSpeechToTextService`) to two more speech surfaces that previously required the `ms-vscode.vscode-speech` extension: **editor dictation** and **terminal voice dictation**.

Fixes #326969. This PR intentionally **excludes** item 3 (read-aloud / text-to-speech), which will be covered by voice mode.

## What changed

Both surfaces now prefer the built-in on-device engine when it is configured (private, in-box, no audio leaves the machine), and fall back to the extension's `ISpeechService` provider where built-in transcription is unsupported (web/remote or `chat.speechToText.enabled: false`). This mirrors the chat input's existing precedence and gates on the same `chatSpeechToTextConfigured` predicate.

- **Editor dictation** (`editorDictation.ts`): when built-in is configured, editor dictation reuses the shared chat dictation renderer (`dictationSession.ts`) — live transcript, interim shimmer, caret parking, and the "Listening…" placeholder — since the editor surface is itself an `ICodeEditor`. The floating stop widget is still shown for a mouse affordance. The Start action precondition is now `HasSpeechProvider OR built-in configured`, so it works without the extension. The extension path is unchanged.
- **Terminal voice** (`terminalVoice.ts`): the built-in engine streams a single growing cumulative transcript (rather than discrete per-utterance `Recognizing`/`Recognized` events), so it is rendered live into the existing ghost-text/decoration UI and sent to the terminal once the silence timeout elapses or the user stops. The extension path is unchanged.
- **Terminal action** (`terminalVoiceActions.ts`): "Start Dictation in Terminal" now starts immediately when the built-in engine is configured, only prompting to install/enable the speech extension when neither engine is available.

## Single speech stack / icon behavior

These surfaces each expose a single built-in command; the extension only ever contributed the `ISpeechService` provider (not separate editor/terminal icons). Routing the existing commands through the built-in engine means there is no second mic/keybinding, consistent with how the chat input already shows a single mic when built-in dictation wins.

## Telemetry

The `chatSpeechToText.session` event gains a `surface` dimension (`chat` | `editor` | `terminal`) so built-in dictation usage and reliability can be attributed per surface. It is threaded through `IChatSpeechToTextService.start(window, surface)` and `startDictation(..., surface)`, defaulting to `chat`; editor and terminal pass their respective surface. Previously all three surfaces fired the same event with no way to tell them apart.

## Not included

- Read-aloud / text-to-speech (issue item 3).
- Keyword activation ("Hey Code") stays extension-only for now.

title: Agents: fix worktree isolation regression for late Worktree toggle (#326963)
body:
Fixes #326963.

## Problem

Repro (Copilot CLI, git-backed folder): create a session, **uncheck** New Worktree, send; quit; create a session in the same folder, **check** New Worktree, send — the session is created **without** a worktree. Works in 1.129.0, broken in 1.130.0.

Root cause is the worktree-isolation unification (#324246). `AgentService.createSession` froze the worktree decision at create time from the draft's *initial* isolation:

```ts
const deferWorktreeCreation = sessionConfig?.values?.[SessionConfigKey.Isolation] === 'worktree' && ...;
```

A new-session draft is seeded with the user's *remembered* isolation (`folder` after step 2), so `deferWorktreeCreation` is `false` and the session's working directory is fixed to the folder. Checking Worktree before the first send updates the live config, but the host never re-derives the pending decision, so first-send resolution returns the folder. (The reverse, `worktree -> folder`, happened to work because such a session *was* marked pending.)

## Fix

Defer working-directory resolution for **every git-capable provisional session**, not only worktree-initial ones, and resolve the final folder/worktree choice from the **live** session config on first send:

```ts
const worktreeCapable =
    sessionConfig?.schema.properties[SessionConfigKey.Isolation]?.enum?.includes('worktree') === true
    || sessionConfig?.values?.[SessionConfigKey.Isolation] === 'worktree';
const deferWorkingDirectoryResolution = worktreeCapable && !config?.fork && !config?.importConversation;
```

The session stays pending until first send, where `resolveWorkingDirectory` reads the live config and creates the worktree (or returns the folder). Because the pending gate also drives `CodexAgent._schedulePrewarm`, this additionally prevents Codex from prewarming a **folder-scoped** thread before the choice is finalized — so the fix covers Copilot, Claude, and Codex uniformly.

Safety: `_pending` is only ever set in `_createProviderSession` (create time), never on restore, so a restored worktree session still resolves its existing worktree with no duplicate. The `worktree -> folder` path is unchanged. Only cost: git *folder* Codex sessions defer their eager prewarm to first send (minor first-turn latency).

## Relationship to #326973

An alternative minimal fix (#326973) reconciles the pending marker reactively on the client `SessionConfigChanged` while the session is `Creating`. That correctly fixes the reported Copilot case, but leaves a Codex eager-prewarm race (the folder thread is already bound, so the created worktree is ignored) — see my comment there. This PR closes that at the create-time gate instead, so no folder thread is ever bound. The two are alternatives; pick whichever the team prefers.

## Test

`agentService.test.ts`: `folder`-at-create -> `SessionConfigChanged(worktree)` -> first send now creates the worktree end-to-end (`addWorktreeCalls` populated, `pendingAfterSend: false`, config reflects `worktree`), plus the failed-create path leaves no stale pending marker.

## Validation

- `valid-layers-check`: no violations from this change.
- The four changed production files are type-clean and change no cross-file signatures. A fully green `typecheck-client` is currently blocked by a stale shared `@github/copilot-sdk` in `node_modules` (unrelated SDK/native-module errors in untouched files); a real `npm ci` is needed for the full suite.

Draft while the team decides between this and #326973.

title: dictation: publish native runtime to CDN instead of npm/NuGet at runtime
body:
## Why

Follow-up to #326839. That PR provisions the Foundry Local native dictation runtime by downloading the N-API addon from **npm** and the core libraries from **NuGet** at runtime. Per review feedback, we shouldn't download from npm at runtime — instead we should **publish the deps to VS Code's CDN and consume them like the Claude/Codex agent SDKs** (see [`build/agent-sdk/README.md`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/build/agent-sdk/README.md)).

## What

Mirror the `build/agent-sdk/` pipeline for a new per-target **dictation runtime** artifact, and rewire the runtime to download a single content-addressed tarball from `main.vscode-cdn.net`.

### Build side — `build/dictation-runtime/`
- **`common.ts`** — reads the `foundry-local-sdk` version pin from the repo-root `package.json`; target map; CDN url + urlTemplate builders (`dictation-runtime/foundry-local/<version>/<target>.tgz`); sha256; results reader.
- **`package.ts`** — assembles `prebuilds/<target>/foundry_local_napi.node` (from the pinned npm prebuild) + `foundry-local-core/<target>/<libs>` (via the SDK's own NuGet installer, host-locked to the build agent's RID) and tars it with node-tar (portable, deterministic).
- **`upload.ts`** — idempotent HEAD-then-decide blob upload to `$web` (same auth as agent-sdk).
- **`produce.ts`** — per (platform, arch): build + upload (upload gated on `VSCODE_PUBLISH=true`), write a results json, emit `DICTATION_RUNTIME_RESULTS_FILE` setvariable.
- **`dictation-runtime-produce.yml`** — wired into the darwin / linux (non-armhf) / win32 compile steps right after the existing `agent-sdk-produce.yml` include.

### Runtime side
- **`product.ts`** — `IDictationRuntimeProductConfig { version, urlTemplate }` + `dictationRuntime?` field.
- **`gulpfile.vscode.ts`** — stamps `product.dictationRuntime` from the results file (desktop only).
- **`foundryLocalRuntime.ts`** — replaces the npm + NuGet legs with a single CDN tarball download + extract keyed on `{ version, urlTemplate }`; deletes the npm/NuGet/native-require helpers. **Dev builds (no product config) fall back to the SDK's own `node_modules` payload** — no download, no env var.
- **node / electron-browser `localTranscriptionService` + common `start()`** — thread the runtime download config from `product.json` through to provisioning.

The runtime cache/tarball layout mirrors the SDK's own package layout, so the patched loader (`VSCODE_FOUNDRY_LOCAL_NATIVE_DIR`) resolution stays a trivial path join:

```
<cacheRoot>/<version>/prebuilds/<target>/foundry_local_napi.node
<cacheRoot>/<version>/foundry-local-core/<target>/<core libraries>
```

title: Reliably restore the last-used chat model when it loads late
body:
## What this fixes

When you reopen VS Code (or open a new chat editor) for an agent-host session, the model picker should come back to the **last model you used** (e.g. `GPT-5.6`). Sometimes it came back as **`Auto`** instead.

**Why:** agent-host models load *asynchronously* after the agent host connects. The workbench only waited for your remembered model when the pool was still completely **empty** at startup. If the pool was already **partly** loaded (some models present, but not yours yet), your model looked "gone", so the input fell back to `Auto` **and stopped watching** — so when your model showed up a moment later, nothing switched to it.

## The change

`initialize` now arms **one** wait whenever a remembered model hasn't been restored yet — whether the pool is empty *or* partly loaded — and swaps your model in as soon as it appears. The wait ends cleanly (it can't linger) once the model's vendor says it's genuinely gone. The three restore waits are also consolidated behind a single `_watchModelChanges` helper.

This keeps the existing agent-host behavior (the "grace" from #326938) intact; it just removes the fragile assumption that the pool is either fully empty or fully loaded.

## How to test

1. Open a folder and start an agent-host (Copilot CLI) session; pick a model like **GPT-5.6** and send a message.
2. Wait for it to finish, then quit VS Code.
3. Reopen VS Code in the **same folder**.
4. ✅ The chat model picker restores to **GPT-5.6** (not `Auto`), even if the model list loads in stages.

## Tests

Added controller tests that fail if the fix is reverted:
- restores the remembered model when it appears after a partly-loaded pool,
- stops waiting (no lingering subscription) when the model is genuinely gone,
- doesn't arm a wait when there's nothing to restore,
- an explicit user pick cancels the wait.

Validated: `typecheck-client`, `valid-layers-check`, eslint, and the `ChatModelSelectionModel` / `ModelSelection` / `ChatInputModelUtils` suites all pass.

Follow-up (separate): a proper per-vendor "readiness" signal to also cover BYOK / signed-out and let us drop the agent-host special-case — tracked in #326943.

title: Simplify model selection restoration
body:
## Summary

Simplifies model selection and restoration across the Workbench and Sessions surfaces while preserving the async agent-host restoration fix from #326938.

- replaces Workbench waiter subscriptions and provisional-model bookkeeping with one first-class selection intent (`remembered`, `programmatic`, `session`, or `history`) and one catalog reconciliation path
- removes the unused configured-model pending branch and its `waitForConfiguredModel` / pending-source plumbing
- treats remembered profile selections as eventual intent: shows an unpersisted fallback, improves it when a location default appears, repairs it if it disappears, and restores the remembered model when available
- makes user, session, and programmatic selections authoritative so they cancel stale pending intent
- retains cold programmatic model requests for request editing, handoffs, and prompt metadata, and blocks sending until a required model resolves or is cancelled
- narrows cold model backfilling to transferred drafts; persisted drafts already carry the history-derived model

## Why

Model catalogs are populated incrementally. A remembered or required model can arrive after a fallback, while a newer user, session, or programmatic selection can happen before that model appears. The previous paths expressed these cases through overlapping flags, subscriptions, and duplicated restore blocks, making stale callbacks and incorrect fallback sends possible.

The selection policy is now explicit:

1. `chat.defaultModel` wins for a fresh conversation when it becomes available.
2. Remembered models remain pending without persisting or freezing the currently displayed fallback.
3. Explicit user choices, conversation/session restores, and programmatic requirements cancel older intent.
4. Every late application is checked against the current conversation before it can mutate selection.
5. An unresolved intent does not suppress ordinary catalog repair when the displayed fallback is removed.
6. A required cold programmatic model prevents send until it resolves or is cancelled.

Provider-owned catalog completeness remains a separate follow-up. This PR does not broaden vendor-specific readiness heuristics or make all model resolution asynchronous.

## Testing

- added controller coverage for intent precedence, cancellation, cold restoration, stale conversations, fallback improvement, fallback removal repair, and programmatic resolution
- added remote-session coverage for restoring a persisted history model while the live catalog is cold
- updated shared reducer and Sessions adapter coverage after removing dead configured-wait state

Validation:

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- 383 affected model-selection, persistence, diagnostics, Sessions, chat-service, picker, configuration, presentation, phone-target, and automation tests
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- targeted `npm run eslint`
- staged and targeted hygiene checks

title: Fix chat list row height swallowed during render (stale/clipped until resize)
body:
Fixes #326952

### Problem

A streaming chat response could render its content but stay **visually stale/clipped until a window resize** — the row looked stuck even though the data had arrived. Resizing (which forces a relayout) revealed the full content.

### Root cause

`ChatListItemRenderer.fireItemHeightChange` advanced `currentRenderedHeight` **before** the `_elementBeingRendered` suppression check. When a measurement arrived synchronously *during* a row's render pass (e.g. a content part's `onDidChangeHeight` firing as it is constructed), the height was recorded but the tree was never notified. A later, genuine remeasurement of that same height (e.g. from the row's `ResizeObserver`) then hit the `normalizedHeight === currentRenderedHeight` early-return and was silently deduped — so the tree kept a stale row height and the extra content was stranded below it.

### Fix

- Extract the decision into a pure, exported `reconcileChatItemHeight(...)`. On a measurement suppressed during render it now **keeps `currentRenderedHeight` untouched** and returns a new `deferReMeasure` decision; `fireItemHeightChange` schedules a next-frame re-measure that reliably delivers the grown height to the tree. This does **not** rely on the `ResizeObserver` re-delivering.
- Decouple the scroll-down button from the `chat-list-at-bottom` padding state (`computeScrollDownState`): the button now appears whenever the view is not at the bottom, so users can jump to the latest content (previously it was hidden for the whole auto-scroll/agent turn).

### Tests

- `reconcileChatItemHeight` — deterministic pure-function regression test (fails on the pre-fix commit-on-suppress behavior, passes on the fix).
- `fireItemHeightChange defers a mid-render measurement …` — real-render **integration** test that asserts the tree is notified after the render pass (verified stable across repeated runs).
- `computeScrollDownState` — locks in the button/padding decoupling.

All `ChatListRenderer` + `ChatListWidget` suites pass; `typecheck-client` and `eslint` clean.

### Draft — remaining before ready

- [ ] **Perf gate** (`npm run perf:chat`, streaming scenarios) to confirm the deferred re-measure adds no `forcedReflowCount` / `layoutDurationMs` regression. Risk is low (a single `getBoundingClientRect` at rAF, when layout is already settled), but not yet run.
- [ ] Live UI verification of the scroll-down button behavior.

title: Kimi: reduce tool calls / requests per turn (prompt-only, Kimi-gated)
body:
## Why

`kimi-k2.7-code` has the highest requests-per-user-request and tool-calls-per-turn of all models (prod ~10 req / ~11 tool-calls per turn; median 2 but P90 34; ~11.5% of "heavy" turns drive ~63% of tool volume). Cost/turn and cache rate are already good — the problem is request **count** (and code survival). Requests are roughly equal to tool calls, so Kimi barely batches and every tool call is its own round-trip.

## Evidence (msbench run 29887843010, kimi-k2.7-code, vscbench, 144 inst, 46.5% resolved)

Steps: median 7, mean 16.7, p90 52, max 154 (failed median 9 vs resolved 6 — long heavy tail). Analysis of 11 extracted trajectories:

- **No parallelism**: tool-calls/request ~= 1.0 (one resolved outlier hit 1.98, proving Kimi *can* batch).
- **Redundant reads**: 98/265 read_file calls (37%) are exact duplicates; ~half re-read within <=3 calls; compaction was ~absent, so this is genuine redundancy, not context eviction.
- **Under-batched edits**: replace_string 71 vs multi_replace 17 (~4:1); 35 consecutive same-file single edits a single multi_replace would cover (worst case: 30 single edits, 0 multi).
- **Terminal thrashing** on the hardest/failed cases: `run_in_terminal` is the #1 tool (327 total); one failed instance did 101 terminal + 18 web-fetch calls in a debug spiral.
- `manage_todo_list` is broad but NOT a spam source (1–5 calls/inst) — ruled out.

Even the *resolved* heavy instance showed the same inefficiencies, so cutting them should reduce requests without costing success.

## Change (Kimi-only, prompt-only, in `kimiPrompts.tsx`)

- **A. Parallel reads/searches** — Kimi's read guidance was softer than the identical Anthropic/OpenAI wording; strengthened it to plan needed files/ranges up front and issue them as parallel reads in one message.
- **B. Anti-redundant-read** (top lever) — new guidance in `contextHandling` plus a concise per-turn reminder (`KimiReminderInstructions`): don't re-read a file/range already read; it stays available.
- **C. Edit batching** — made the multi_replace preference imperative: >1 edit => one `multi_replace_string_in_file` call.
- **D. Loop/terminal budget** — new `avoidingLoops` bullet: stop repeating edit-run-inspect cycles; form a root-cause hypothesis after a couple of failures.

## Deliberately NOT changed

- temperature/top_p (forced 1.0/0.95) — left untouched.
- No `parallel_tool_calls` request param (the API already permits parallel; it's a model-behavior gap).
- No structural compaction/context-window change (compaction was rare in the eval).
- No tool-surface removal (edit tools are already minimal for Kimi).

## Validation

- `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` on the copilot extension: clean.
- `eslint kimiPrompts.tsx --max-warnings=0`: clean.
- Behavioral effect to be measured by benchmark eval on this PR.

## Follow-ups if the signal is weak

- Promote A/C into the per-turn reminder too; consider a Kimi-specific `read_file` nudge.

---

This pull request introduces a new set of generic `surface.*` theme tokens for container surfaces (such as floating panels), updates the modern workbench layout to use these tokens instead of the agent-specific ones, and refactors related CSS for better maintainability and consistency. Additionally, it standardizes font and spacing variable usage by replacing agent-specific variables with the default ones, and cleans up some CSS selectors for improved specificity and maintainability.

**Theme tokens and styling updates:**

* Added new `surface.background`, `surface.foreground`, and `surface.border` theme tokens in `src/vs/workbench/common/theme.ts`, with appropriate defaults and documentation for use with generic container "cards".
* Updated dark and light theme JSON files to define values for the new `surface.*` tokens, mirroring the previous `agentsPanel.*` values for consistency [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ed93cc8becd22ae30b99dc456a0aaa6b779e7b4b542d4bee95cf759ee517b3c9R287-R289) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-87dd8146fec1e0d71789bc1cb459b84af52652eab3e70b77227bbcdeaca73301R295-R297).
* Registered the new `surface.*` tokens in the stylelint variables list for editor integration and linting.

**CSS refactoring and variable standardization:**

* Updated all relevant CSS in `floatingPanels.css`, `editorBorder.css`, and related files to use the new `surface.*` tokens instead of `agentsPanel.*`, ensuring that floating panels and cards share a consistent look and are easily themeable [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-96cb2d8573ce4ce529610b032f2044a61b322357bff73870ab0196ceec6f17b3L16-R17) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-96cb2d8573ce4ce529610b032f2044a61b322357bff73870ab0196ceec6f17b3L25-R38) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-73774406b10b7aea37c99d6e66f2a4e427301ff26607dc69e475c731a1618b05L45-R67).
* Replaced agent-specific font and size variables (e.g., `--vscode-agents-fontWeight-semiBold`, `--vscode-agents-fontSize-label2`) with the default `--vscode-fontWeight-semiBold` and `--vscode-fontSize-label2` throughout style override CSS files for better maintainability and to avoid duplication [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-c718522311de21a7658a924bbd223350855e39acf9ddd9e1c4eaffa8f76a34dbL313-R313) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-949ec94438c04f89d57f6ad30dfdd93a1ea7e72c5d2d51b032ed5e6c16d0901fL148-R148) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-949ec94438c04f89d57f6ad30dfdd93a1ea7e72c5d2d51b032ed5e6c16d0901fL202-R202) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-c5122c2b03b035b623843dbb023ad264a4b1b7da4ad722e800292178087267e5L95-R95) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-915cccdddaa0b83d00bb30841bbd79387a84f1f638b32f49633b200309e03024L35-R35) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-915cccdddaa0b83d00bb30841bbd79387a84f1f638b32f49633b200309e03024L227-R224) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-915cccdddaa0b83d00bb30841bbd79387a84f1f638b32f49633b200309e03024L271-R275) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-915cccdddaa0b83d00bb30841bbd79387a84f1f638b32f49633b200309e03024L305-R302) [[9]](diffhunk://#diff-915cccdddaa0b83d00bb30841bbd79387a84f1f638b32f49633b200309e03024L347-R344).

**CSS selector improvements:**

* Simplified and unified CSS selectors in `keyboardFocusOnly.css` using the `:is()` pseudo-class for better specificity and maintainability [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ac3294ab4f135eb1db1a6f725ae25fbfdedc46311de22631c313542d04c8f47cL30-R30) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ac3294ab4f135eb1db1a6f725ae25fbfdedc46311de22631c313542d04c8f47cL43-R42).

**Minor layout and cleanup:**

* Moved the `.tab.sticky-compact` width rules to a more appropriate location in the CSS for clarity [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-915cccdddaa0b83d00bb30841bbd79387a84f1f638b32f49633b200309e03024R45-R48) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-915cccdddaa0b83d00bb30841bbd79387a84f1f638b32f49633b200309e03024L85-L91).

These changes improve the theming flexibility of the workbench, make the codebase easier to maintain, and ensure a more consistent visual appearance across different UI surfaces.

title: Restore last-used agent-host model instead of falling back to Auto
body:
## Summary

Agent-host chat sessions (e.g. **Copilot CLI**) publish their model list **asynchronously**, only after the agent host process connects. During that cold-start window, VS Code's model-restore logic treated a remembered/last-used model that wasn't in the (still-empty) pool as **conclusively unavailable** and reset the model picker to **Auto**, instead of waiting for the pool to load.

The result: after selecting a specific model (e.g. `GPT-5.6`) and reopening VS Code / a session / a different repo, the model picker showed **Auto** instead of the model you last used.

## Root cause

`isLanguageModelVendorAbsenceConclusive` only granted the built-in **Copilot** vendor a "an empty result during startup is transient" grace. Agent-host vendors (`agent-host-*` local, `remote-*` remote) load their models asynchronously too, but an empty resolution was treated as **final** → the remembered model resolved as `unavailable` → the restore gave up and fell back to Auto.

Because this defect is at the resolution layer, it leaked into **every** restore surface (a new editor, the sidebar chat view, and reopened existing sessions).

**Fix:** give agent-host vendors the same transient grace as Copilot, so an absent model on a still-empty pool resolves as `pending` (wait) rather than `unavailable` (give up):

```ts
return hasLiveModels || (hasResolved && vendor !== COPILOT_VENDOR_ID && !isAgentHostVendor(vendor));
```

This fixes all surfaces at once and naturally survives the transient empty resolutions emitted before the real models arrive (resolution stays `pending` until the pool loads). Two supporting hardening changes are included (see **Changes**).

## Issues fixed — with step-by-step repro

> These are agent-host sessions (Copilot CLI). The bug reproduces on a **cold start** — i.e. the first open before the agent-host model list has been fetched/cached. Reproducing reliably may require selecting a **non-Auto** model, sending a message, and fully **restarting** VS Code.

### Issue 1 — Reopening an existing session restores as Auto
1. Open folder **A** in VS Code.
2. Open a new chat editor for an agent-host session (Copilot CLI).
3. Select a specific model (e.g. **GPT-5.6**), send a message, and wait for completion.
4. **Fully exit** VS Code.
5. Start VS Code again in the **same** folder **A** — the previous session is restored automatically.
6. ❌ **Before:** the restored session's model shows **Auto**.
   ✅ **After:** the restored session shows the model you used (**GPT-5.6**).

### Issue 2 — Sidebar chat view opens on Auto after switching repos
1. Open folder **A**, select a model (e.g. **GPT-5.6**) in an agent-host session, send a message, wait for completion.
2. **Fully exit** VS Code.
3. Open VS Code in a **different** folder **B**.
4. Open a **new chat editor** — the model is correctly your last-used model.
5. Open the **Chat panel in the sidebar** (Copilot CLI).
6. ❌ **Before:** the sidebar chat shows **Auto** (even though the editor showed the right model).
   ✅ **After:** the sidebar chat shows your last-used model.

### Issue 3 — New chat editor in a different repo opens on Auto
1. Open folder **A**, select a model (e.g. **GPT-5.6 Terra**) in an agent-host session, send a message, wait for completion.
2. **Fully exit** VS Code.
3. Open VS Code in a **different** folder **B**.
4. Open a new chat editor for the agent-host session.
5. ❌ **Before (cold pool):** the model briefly/persistently shows **Auto**.
   ✅ **After:** the model shows your last-used model once the agent-host models load.

In all three cases the user's selection *was* saved correctly (in the per-session-type storage bucket); the bug was purely on the **restore/read** side — the picker gave up on the remembered model before the agent-host pool finished loading.

## Changes

- **`common/languageModels.ts`** — the root fix. Add `isAgentHostVendor(...)` (using platform-layer prefix helpers to avoid an import cycle) and exclude agent-host vendors from "conclusive absence", mirroring the existing Copilot behavior. This also lets `mergeModelsWithCache` keep cached agent-host models during the load window (same as Copilot).
- **`common/chatService/chatServiceImpl.ts`** — `loadRemoteSession` no longer drops the session's known model to `undefined` when the live lookup is cold; it carries the saved model (with metadata) into the restored input state, including through a transferred draft (new small helper `backfillRestoredModel`).
- **`browser/widget/input/chatInputModelSelectionController.ts`** — `syncFromConversationState` keeps waiting through transient empty agent-host resolutions and only falls back once the session-type pool has actually loaded without the model.

## Tests

New regression tests, **verified to fail if the root fix is reverted**:

- `modelSelection.test.ts` — `treats a resolved-but-empty agent-host vendor as still loading (pending)` (covers local + remote; and `unavailable` once the pool loads without the model).
- `chatModelSelectionModel.test.ts` — `initialize waits for a resolved-but-empty agent-host pool and restores the remembered model` (drives the restore through the real catalog resolver; asserts it waits through an intermediate empty event and applies the model on load) and `waits through a resolved-but-empty session pool and applies the restored model when it loads`.
- `chatService.test.ts` — `backfillRestoredModel` suite for the `loadRemoteSession` carry-over.

I temporarily reverted the root-fix clause and confirmed both new agent-host tests fail (`2 failing, 0 passing`), then restored it.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` ✅
- `npm run valid-layers-check` ✅ (new platform→chat import verified)
- ESLint on changed files ✅
- Suites: `ModelSelection` (55), `ChatModelSelectionModel` (19), `ChatInputModelUtils` (136, incl. cache — no regression), `backfillRestored`/`chatService` backfill (8) ✅

title: Make Add Selection to Next Find Match work with regex find mode
body:
Fixes #107090

## Problem

With regex mode enabled in the find widget, **Add Selection to Next Find Match** (`Ctrl+D`) does nothing. The reason: `MultiCursorSession` never receives the find widget's `isRegex` state — `findNextMatch` / `findPreviousMatch` / `findMatches` are always called with `isRegex = false`, so the regex pattern in the search box is searched literally and never matches.

## Fix

Thread the find widget's `isRegex` state through `MultiCursorSession`:

- When the find widget owns the search string (focus in the widget, widget revealed, search string non-empty), the session is created with `findState.isRegex` — mirroring how `Select All` already special-cases regex.
- When the selection owns the search text, behavior is unchanged (selected text is still matched literally).
- The session's `isRegex` is honored in `findNextMatch`, `findPreviousMatch`, and `findMatches`, so `Ctrl+D`, `Ctrl+K Ctrl+D`, and the previous-match variants all work with regex.

## Tests

Added a unit test (`issue #107090: AddSelectionToNextFindMatchAction works with regex find mode`) covering repeated `Ctrl+D` with a regex pattern. Ran the full multicursor suite: **18 passing**. `compile-src` finishes with 0 errors.

title: Hide 'Disable' dropdown action when extension is enabled only for workspace
body:
Fixes #244138

## Problem

When an extension is disabled globally but then enabled for the current workspace (`EnablementState.EnabledWorkspace`), the Disable button's dropdown shows both **"Disable"** and **"Disable (Workspace)"**. Disabling globally is meaningless in this state, because the extension is already disabled globally — the only sensible action is "Disable (Workspace)".

## Fix

`DisableGloballyAction.update()` previously enabled the action for both `EnabledGlobally` and `EnabledWorkspace`. It now only enables the action when the extension is enabled globally:

```ts
this.enabled = this.extension.state === ExtensionState.Installed
	&& this.extension.enablementState === EnablementState.EnabledGlobally
	&& this.extensionEnablementService.canChangeEnablement(this.extension.local);
```

As a result, when the extension is enabled only for the workspace, the dropdown contains just "Disable (Workspace)", matching the expected behavior described in the issue.

Verified with a full client compile (`npm run compile-client`, `compile-src` finished with 0 errors).

title: Fix OS_ID parsing in check-requirements-linux.sh for quoted values
body:
Fixes #232159

## Problem

`check-requirements-linux.sh` extracts the distribution ID from `/etc/os-release` with:

```sh
OS_ID="$(cat /etc/os-release | grep -Eo 'ID=([^"]+)' | sed -n '1s/ID=//p')"
```

This fails when the value is quoted (e.g. `ID="rocky"` on Rocky Linux 8.5, which is permitted by the os-release format), leaving `OS_ID` empty and causing the script to exit non-zero during devcontainer setup. It can also accidentally match the `ID=` substring inside other keys such as `VERSION_ID`.

## Fix

Replace the extraction with an anchored `sed` expression that strips optional single or double quotes:

```sh
OS_ID="$(sed -n 's/^ID=["'"'"']*\([^"'"'"']*\)["'"'"']*$/\1/p' /etc/os-release | head -n1)"
```

Verified locally with all three formats — `ID=rocky`, `ID="rocky"`, `ID='rocky'` — each correctly yields `rocky`, while `VERSION_ID` and `ID_LIKE` lines are no longer matched.

title: Preserve agent host terminal stream order for command output
body:
Follow-up to: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/325110

- Flush pending `terminal/data` before dispatching the next OSC 633 event so AHP actions preserve the PTY stream order.
- Keep command output between `terminal/commandExecuted` and `terminal/commandFinished`, as required by the AHP terminal contract and matching workbench/xterm shell integration.
- Prevent fast commands whose output and finish marker arrive in one PTY read from completing before live subscribers receive their output. Otherwise, output can become unclassified, command objects can report empty output, and executed/end marks can bracket an empty range.
- Keep ordinary output chunks batched into one `terminal/data` action without changing the protocol schema or version.
- Add coverage for server action ordering, client-state output attribution, and workbench AHP command output.

-----------------------------------------
Inspirations from:

- The ordering requirement comes directly from the [`TerminalCommandExecutedAction` and `TerminalCommandFinishedAction` AHP contract](https://github.com/microsoft/agent-host-protocol/blob/0960c7e1b74860bb055617839aa49ff976b5c39d/types/channels-terminal/actions.ts#L153-L182), which defines intervening `terminal/data` actions as the command's complete output.
- Workbench command detection models the lifecycle as command executed → terminal output → command finished in [`printStandardCommand`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/65f89ec8b234ea8e03a837302bfee2ecca8074c3/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/test/browser/capabilities/commandDetectionCapability.test.ts#L47-L58). Xterm routes OSC 633 `C` and `D` markers inline through [`ShellIntegrationAddon`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/65f89ec8b234ea8e03a837302bfee2ecca8074c3/src/vs/platform/terminal/common/xterm/shellIntegrationAddon.ts#L473-L510), and [`TerminalCommand.getOutput`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/65f89ec8b234ea8e03a837302bfee2ecca8074c3/src/vs/platform/terminal/common/capabilities/commandDetection/terminalCommand.ts#L123-L154) reads the output bounded by the executed and finished markers.
- When that order is not preserved, the [`terminalReducer`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/65f89ec8b234ea8e03a837302bfee2ecca8074c3/src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/state/protocol/channels-terminal/reducer.ts#L17-L87) places data received after completion into unclassified content, while [`AhpTerminalCommandSource`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/65f89ec8b234ea8e03a837302bfee2ecca8074c3/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminal/browser/ahpTerminalCommandSource.ts#L189-L257) only appends streamed data while the command is executing.

title: sessions: add a Quick Pick entry point for folder selection in new session
body:
## What changed

Adds a native `IQuickInputService` Quick Pick as an additional entry point for picking the target folder when starting a new session in the Agents Window, alongside the existing `WorkspacePicker` dropdown.

- New command `workbench.action.sessions.newSession.pickFolderQuickPick` ("New Session in Folder...") - discoverable via the Command Palette and bound to `Cmd+O` while the Agents Window is focused. The keybinding uses a higher weight than the desktop Open File/Folder actions so it wins on `Cmd+O` conflicts, without disabling those actions anywhere else.
- Lists recently used folders (own history + VS Code's own recents, deduplicated) followed by an always-present "Browse..." entry that opens the native folder dialog.
- Extracted `ISessionsRecentWorkspacesService`, the single source of truth for the sessions' own recently-used workspace folders, shared by the new Quick Pick and the existing `WorkspacePicker` dropdown (and its `WebWorkspacePicker`/`AutomationsWorkspacePicker` variants) so all folder-selection surfaces always agree on the same recent-folder list.
- Fixed `NewChatWidget` to keep the `WorkspacePicker` dropdown's displayed selection in sync when the active session's workspace changes externally (e.g. via the new Quick Pick command while the composer is already showing) - previously it kept showing the stale folder.

## Why

The Agents Window new-session view only had a custom `ActionWidget`-based dropdown for folder selection. This adds a lighter-weight, keyboard-first Quick Pick alternative without touching the existing dropdown's behavior.

## Notes for reviewers

- `sessionsProvidersService.ts` is untouched (no diff) - workspace resolution stays local to the picker and to the recent-workspaces service (which resolves entries internally before returning them), keeping `ISessionsProvidersService`'s surface unchanged.
- No default keybinding conflicts are introduced outside the Agents Window; `Cmd+O` elsewhere in VS Code is unaffected.

title: fix: hide implicit PR suggestion when already attached
body:
## Summary
- Fixes [#320371](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/320371): after attaching an implicit PR suggestion, a provider refresh could show the same PR suggestion again (and clicking it was a no-op).
- String/PR attachments store text in `value` and identity on `resourceUri`/`handle`. The old matcher only compared `handle` or URI from `value`, so a new handle after refresh made the suggestion look unattached.
- Extracted `isImplicitContextAlreadyAttached` and match string/PR suggestions by handle or `resourceUri` (not the editor `uri`, so file suggestions are not hidden).

title: Fix alt-click on the testing run gutter debugging the test (#326724)
body:
Fixes #326724

### Problem

Holding <kbd>Alt</kbd> while clicking the testing run glyph in the editor gutter used to run "Debug Test". It regressed to running "Add Conditional Breakpoint": the icon still swaps to the debug variant on Alt, but the click adds a conditional breakpoint instead of debugging the test.

### Cause

The alt-click "add conditional breakpoint" gesture added to the breakpoint editor contribution in #308687 competes with the testing gutter's established alt-click "debug test" gesture, since both live in the glyph margin.

`BreakpointEditorContribution` decides whether to handle a glyph-margin mousedown with a per-line heuristic: `marginFreeFromNonDebugDecorations(e.target.position.lineNumber)` plus icon-class matching. That check keys off the resolved line number and the decorations on it, not off what was actually clicked. When the click resolves to a different model line than the run glyph's decoration, the guard sees a "free" margin and the breakpoint contribution proceeds, shadowing the testing action.

### Fix

Defer to the testing gutter whenever the clicked element is the run glyph itself, identified by its stable `testing-run-glyph` marker class. This keys off what was clicked rather than a line-number heuristic, so the testing gutter's run and alt-click debug gestures are never intercepted.

### Verification

- Normal click on the testing gutter runs the test.
- Alt-click on the testing gutter debugs the test.
- Alt-click on an ordinary debug glyph margin still adds a conditional breakpoint.
- Alt-click on an existing breakpoint, including on a test line, still edits it.

@connor4312 for review, since this is assigned to you.

title: AH: fix subagent resource handling
body:
## Summary

Fixes inconsistent live rendering and grouping of Agent Host subagents.

Agent Host delegated tasks begin as streaming tool calls. Their initial `toolCallStart` action already includes:

- `toolKind: 'subagent'`
- The subagent description and agent name
- The `subagentChatUri` resource

The streaming adapter previously discarded this metadata until `toolCallReady`. As a result, the parent task could initially render as a generic tool. Child tools arriving from the subagent resource could then render separately or in the wrong position.

Reloading appeared to fix the issue because restored history was reconstructed from finalized tool metadata.

This change:

- Preserves subagent metadata when the streaming invocation is first created.
- Uses the `subagentChatUri` to subscribe to the child chat resource.
- Applies consistent handling to server and client-provided delegated tasks.
- Groups child tool calls under the correct parent subagent.
- Keeps live rendering consistent with restored session rendering.

## Testing

- Added coverage verifying streaming invocations retain subagent metadata before `toolCallReady`.
- Added coverage for client-provided delegated tasks and child-resource observation.
- Added coverage verifying child tools are grouped under the parent subagent.
