title: Fix: apply chat.defaultModel default on every new local chat session
body:
Fixes #326877


### Problem
`chat.defaultModel` was inconsistent between the Local chat harness and the Agents (AHP) harness. In Local sessions, after picking a different model and sending a request, creating a new chat would carry over the previous session's model instead of resetting to the configured default — only a window reload restored it. AHP behaved correctly.

### Root cause
Both harnesses share the pure precedence logic in modelSelection.ts, but drive it differently:

**AHP** (sessionModelSelectionModel.ts → transitionModelSelection) re-pushes the configured default on every new chat key, so a new conversation always resets to the default unless the user explicitly picked a model within that same chat.

**Local** (chatInputPart.ts) only applied the configured-default override on the empty-input draft path — i.e. when the freshly bound input model had no state. When a new chat's input model already carried a spilled-over selection, none of the override paths fired, and _applyConfiguredDefaultForEmptySession() wasn't triggered on a plain session switch. Reload worked only because construction re-runs initSelectedModel().

### Fix
Call the existing, already-guarded _applyConfiguredDefaultForEmptySession() from handleViewModelChange, after the incoming view model has been assigned. This is required because the helper resolves and validates the model through getCurrentSessionType(), which only reflects the incoming session once ChatWidget assigns the new view model (setInputModel runs before that). Running it there also lets reconcileSessionTypeForViewModelChange (which re-runs initSelectedModel on a genuine type change) settle first, and placing it after the transaction restores normal persistence. 

New intended behavior (both local and AHP):

- New session → configured default (chat.defaultModel) always wins, even over a spillover selection.
- Reopened conversation (non-empty) → no-op; the saved per-conversation model is restored.
- Setting unset → no-op; existing sticky "last-used model" behavior is preserved.

body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:

Agents Window automations can be claimed during startup before the requested session type or model catalog is ready. That transient state currently records a failed run and advances the schedule, causing an otherwise valid automation to be missed.

## Changes

- preflight the exact provider and session type before recording a run, leaving unavailable scheduled work due
- retry deferred work when session-type availability changes
- wait for an explicitly requested model using model, provider, session-type, cancellation, and disposal signals
- publish the first authoritative model-catalog result even when it is empty, so consumers can distinguish pending from unavailable
- clean up provisional sessions when readiness fails or is cancelled

Readiness is intentionally event-driven and has no arbitrary startup delay or timeout.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- hygiene checks
- targeted AutomationRunner, AutomationScheduler, SessionsManagementService, and language model unit tests

title: Fix voice mode multi-window auto-listen and cross-session glow
body:
Fixes microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#8507
Fixes microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#8514

## two windows both listen/reply in hands-free
Each window builds its own `IVoiceSessionController` (per-window `Delayed` singleton) with its own WebSocket, so when voice mode is active in more than one window (e.g. an editor window and the agents window), every window re-armed hands-free auto-listen and answered simultaneously.

**Fix:** gate the hands-free re-arm paths on this window having OS focus. Added `_isWindowFocused()` (`this._window.document.hasFocus()`) and applied it to `_enterAutoListen('auto')` and `_startBargeInListen()`. Connect-time arming (`source === 'connect'`) is a user gesture in the focused window and is left ungated. Only the focused window keeps listening; single-window behavior is unchanged.

## listening glow appears on the wrong session's input
The glow target was locked at connect time to `chatWidgetService.lastFocusedWidget` (a cross-window focused-widget singleton), so it stuck on the originally-focused pane and didn't follow session switches — glowing a background/non-active session while the correct pane showed the "Listening..." placeholder.

**Fix:** target each pane's own input container and gate the glow on the same per-session ownership the transcript overlay already computes (`voiceUiOwner = targetSession ?? ownerSession`). The glow now renders only on the input of the session voice is actually bound to, always matching the transcript overlay. Removed the now-unused locked-glow-widget autorun and `getActiveInputContainer`.

## Validation
- `npm run typecheck-client` ✅
- `npm run valid-layers-check` ✅

title: Show a plain spinner while dictation is starting
body:
### Problem

When the on-device dictation model is already downloaded (the common case), clicking the dictation mic gave **no feedback** during microphone acquisition + session open. `isPreparingModel` stayed `false`, so the toolbar button sat as a static mic until it abruptly jumped to "Listening…". Only the first-time download path showed any affordance (the determinate download ring).

### Fix

Mirror Voice Mode's `agentsVoice.connecting` pattern:

- New context key **`chatSpeechToTextStarting`**, set the moment dictation is triggered and cleared once we are actually listening (or once the determinate download ring takes over).
- New **`ChatSpeechToTextConnectingAction`** renders a plain auto-spinning `Codicon.loading` during that window.
- The toggle mic is hidden while starting/preparing; the download ring still wins when a real download is in progress, so the two spinner affordances never show together.

Wired in `chatSpeechToTextService.ts` (`start()`, `_setPreparingModel`, `_teardown`) so the state is race-free across the mic → session-open → listening transitions and every failure/cancel path.

### Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` ✅

title: Fix Voice Mode keybinding in Agents window
body:
Fixes microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#8428
Fixes microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#8517

## Problem

The Voice Mode shortcut (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Space) did not work reliably in the Agents window:

- **New-session view (#8428):** the shortcut did nothing — logs showed `From 3 keybinding entries, no when clauses matched the context.`
- **Linux (#8517):** the Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Space variant produced alt-modifier side effects (e.g. the terminal `+` button flipping to the split icon while Alt is held).

## Root cause

The workbench `agentsVoice.startVoiceInChat` keybinding is scoped to the `inChatInput` context key. Active sessions use the full `ChatWidget`, which sets `inChatInput`, but the **new-session composer** (`NewChatInputWidget`) is not an `IChatWidget` and never sets it — so the chord matched no when-clause there.

The earlier Linux Alt override (PR #325685) misdiagnosed #8428 as a chord conflict with parameter hints. Parameter hints only bind when a signature-help provider is present, which the chat input never has, so no conflict actually exists — and the Alt chord introduced #8517.

## Changes

- **`newChatInput.ts`**: re-bind Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+Space to `agentsVoice.startVoiceInChat` in the sessions layer, scoped to `sessionsChatInputHasDictationFocus && config.agents.voice.enabled`. The command id is preserved so push-to-talk hold mode keeps working.
- **`agentsVoice.contribution.ts`**: drop the Linux Ctrl+Alt+Shift+Space overrides on `startVoiceInChat` and `pushToTalk` so all platforms use Ctrl+Shift+Space.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` ✅
- `npm run valid-layers-check` ✅
- pre-commit hygiene hook ✅

title: Adopt AHP 0.7.0 workingDirectories + primaryWorkingDirectory in agent host
body:
## Summary

Syncs the generated agent host protocol copy to spec version **0.6.0** (`agent-host-protocol` @ `11f1a65e`), which renames the singular `workingDirectory` on session/chat state to a `workingDirectories` array in preparation for multiroot session support.

This is milestone 1 of multiroot support: a **pure, behaviour-preserving property adoption**. Sessions continue to use a single working directory — no user-visible change.

## What changed

- **Generated protocol (14 files):** re-synced to spec 0.6.0 via `scripts/sync-agent-host-protocol.ts`. The singular `workingDirectory` is replaced by `workingDirectories?: URI[]` on the session/chat state and summary types. (`.ahp-version` → `11f1a65e`.)
- **Consumers (39 files):** mechanical migration of the renamed property:
  - reads that consume a single directory → `x.workingDirectories?.[0]`
  - field-copy / passthrough sites → whole-array passthrough (`x.workingDirectories`)
  - object-literal writes from a single URI → `dir ? [dir] : undefined` (or `[dir]` in tests)

## Explicitly *not* in this PR

No multiroot client support is added here — no capability advertising (`multipleWorkingDirectories`), no `workingDirectorySet`/`workingDirectoryRemoved` state actions, no multi-folder workspaces, and no UI. Those land in a follow-up milestone.

## Validation

- `tsc --project ./src/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — clean
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — clean
- Pre-commit hygiene hook — passed

> Note: the singular `workingDirectory` on the pre-session config commands (`ResolveSessionConfigParams`, `SessionConfigCompletionsParams`) is intentionally retained — those resolve config before a session exists and are single-context by design.

## Follow-up

Once the spec PR (microsoft/agent-host-protocol#337) merges, repoint `.ahp-version`/sync source from the spec-branch commit to the merged commit.

title: Capture mic via AudioWorkletNode instead of deprecated ScriptProcessorNode (dictation + Voice Mode)
body:
### Problem

Audio capture for chat dictation and Voice Mode used `ctx.createScriptProcessor(...)`, which is deprecated:

> [Deprecation] The ScriptProcessorNode is deprecated. Use AudioWorkletNode instead.

Its `onaudioprocess` callback runs on the **main thread**, where it gets throttled or stops firing entirely (the Voice Mode path already kept a fallback drain timer for exactly this reason). When it stops, no PCM is streamed and dictation silently produces nothing.

### Change

Replace `ScriptProcessorNode` with an `AudioWorkletNode`, which runs on the dedicated audio rendering thread:

- New shared helper `chat/browser/pcmCaptureWorklet.ts` (`createPcmCaptureNode`) loads a PCM-capture worklet from a `blob:` URL (allowed by the renderer's `script-src` CSP) and invokes a callback with each fixed-size mono chunk on the main thread.
- **Chat dictation** (`chatSpeechToTextService.ts`): captures 4096-sample chunks, encodes to PCM16 and streams them. `_startCapture` is now async with a `this._audioContext !== ctx` teardown guard.
- **Voice Mode mic capture** (`voiceClient/micCaptureService.ts`): captures 2048-sample chunks to match the previous ScriptProcessorNode buffer size, so the per-chunk drain/diagnostic bookkeeping is unchanged. Includes a `this._micCtx !== ctx` guard if capture is stopped while the module loads.

### Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` passes cleanly.
- Pre-commit hygiene hooks ran (no `--no-verify`).

title: Show focus differentiator for ask-questions checkbox navigation
body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/321134


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4e797014-ea84-45d8-a58f-5358581cfd8d


## Problem

In the ask-questions carousel, multi-select (checkbox) rows are navigated with the up/down arrow keys by moving DOM focus. However the stylesheet applies `.chat-question-list-item:focus { outline: none; }`, and — unlike single-select, which moves its `.selected` background as you navigate — checkbox rows had no visual state tied to focus. As a result, the currently focused checkbox item had no differentiator during keyboard navigation.

## Fix

Added a focus indicator scoped to multi-select rows in `chatQuestionCarousel.css`:

```css
.chat-question-list-item.multi-select:focus {
	outline: 1px solid var(--vscode-focusBorder);
	outline-offset: -1px;
}
```

- Nested inside `.chat-question-list`, so it out-specifies the `outline: none` rule.
- Uses `--vscode-focusBorder` (matching the freeform textarea's focus treatment; works in high-contrast themes).
- Gated on `.multi-select`, so single-select rows are unaffected.

title: Dictation: download Foundry Local native runtime on demand
body:
Re-applies #326678 (on-device dictation via Foundry Local streaming ASR) **without shipping its native payload**, so we keep VS Code's minimum supported Linux glibc floor (Ubuntu 20 / Debian 10 / RHEL 8).

## Problem
#326678 bundled `foundry-local-sdk`'s prebuilt N-API addon (`foundry_local_napi.node`) and native core libraries. The addon requires `GLIBC_2.34` (verified on both `linux-x64` and `linux-arm64` via `.gnu.version_r`). The Linux dependency generator scans every shipped `.node` and would declare `libc6 (>= 2.34)`, raising the floor for the **entire product** and dropping Ubuntu 20 / Debian 10-11 / RHEL 8. It was reverted in #326769.

The ONNX Runtime / Foundry Core `.so` libraries themselves satisfy the current floor — only the addon is the problem.

## Approach — download the native runtime on demand
Rather than raise the whole-product glibc floor for an experimental feature, the native runtime is downloaded on demand at runtime, only on supported platforms, into a per-user writable cache. The GLIBC_2.34 addon is never in the scanned/declared package, so the floor is intact.

- **Packaging (`build/`)** — exclude every `foundry-local-sdk/prebuilds/**` and `foundry-local-core/**` from the package; drop the build-time core fetch (`ensureFoundryLocalCorePackage` / `build/lib/foundryLocal.ts`), the Linux dep-generator soname additions, and the darwin universal/macho skip entries.
- **SDK loader patch (`build/npm/postinstall.ts`)** — patch the SDK's `dist/detail/coreInterop.js` to honor `VSCODE_FOUNDRY_LOCAL_NATIVE_DIR` for both addon and core-library resolution, falling back to the original package-relative logic so dev-from-source still works. Idempotent; warns (does not fail) if the SDK's loader shape changes.
- **Runtime downloader (`src/vs/platform/localTranscription/node/foundryLocalRuntime.ts`)** — before loading the SDK, ensure the addon (extracted from the pinned `foundry-local-sdk` npm tarball) and the core libraries (via the SDK's own NuGet installer `runInstall`, targeted at the cache with its `binDir` option) are present, then point the loader at the cache via the env var. Version-stamped by SDK version, idempotent (`.complete` marker), and de-duped across concurrent sessions.

Cache layout mirrors the SDK package layout so the loader patch is a trivial path join:

```
<cacheHome>/chatDictationRuntime/<sdkVersion>/prebuilds/<rid>/foundry_local_napi.node
<cacheHome>/chatDictationRuntime/<sdkVersion>/foundry-local-core/<rid>/<core libs>
```

The **model** itself continues to download on demand at first use (unchanged).

## Proxy support
All three provisioning download legs honor a configured proxy:
- The npm-registry addon tarball (our own fetch) and the NuGet core libraries (via the SDK's bundled installer) read the standard proxy environment variables (`HTTPS_PROXY` / `HTTP_PROXY` / `ALL_PROXY`, with `NO_PROXY`) — our fetch attaches an `HttpsProxyAgent`, and the SDK's bare `https.get` calls are routed by temporarily pointing `https.globalAgent` at it (restored afterwards, no SDK patching). This matches how the GitHub desktop app's Rust `foundry-local-sdk` (reqwest/ureq) reaches the same endpoints.
- VS Code's `http.proxy` / `http.noProxy` **settings** are bridged into the dictation utility process and applied as those same environment variables before any download, so a proxy configured only in VS Code (not in the OS environment) is honored — including by the native Foundry Local **model** download, which reads OS-level/env proxy the same way.
- `http.proxyAuthorization` (a `Basic <base64>` value) is folded into the proxy URL's credentials, so both our fetches and the native model download authenticate to the proxy. `http.proxyStrictSSL: false` disables TLS certificate verification for the Node download legs (scoped to the dedicated dictation utility process).

TLS-intercepting proxies otherwise rely on the CA certificate being present in the OS trust store (matching `@vscode/proxy-agent` and the desktop app). Non-`Basic` proxy auth schemes (e.g. Negotiate/NTLM), and disabling TLS verification for the native model leg, are left to OS-level configuration.

## Also in this PR
Un-reverting #326678 also restores these related changes it originally made:
- Removes the `@huggingface/transformers` dependency and deletes the `build/npm/stubs/sharp/` stub it required.
- Deletes the prior on-device transcriber path (`nemotronTranscriber.ts`, ~797 lines), superseded by Foundry Local streaming ASR.
- Bumps `tar` `^7.5.16` → `^7.5.20`, kept in sync with the root `package.json` / lockfile for the hygiene check.

## Supported platforms
-  `darwin-arm64`, `linux-x64`, `linux-arm64`, `win32-x64`, `win32-arm64` (mirrors the SDK RID map and the existing dictation gate).

Un-reverts #326678. Refs #326769.

title: Dictation: make redundant-extension prompt sticky and mark shown only after response
body:
https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5b7f7377-fec2-456e-87a5-fb60e52e09a5

### Problem

The prompt to disable the redundant `ms-vscode.vscode-speech` extension (added in #326665) could silently never appear:

- It uses a **non-sticky** `Severity.Info` notification, which auto-hides after a few seconds (only error-with-action and progress notifications are sticky).
- It calls `markShown()` — burning the once-per-machine `StorageScope.APPLICATION` flag — **before** the prompt is shown, regardless of outcome.

On Insiders, `chat.speechToText.enabled` defaults to `true`, so the notifier fires on the first eligible launch. If the transient toast appeared while the user wasn't looking, it auto-dismissed and the flag was permanently set — so it never showed again.

### Changes

- Add `sticky: true` so the notification stays until the user responds.
- Move `markShown()` into each choice's `run`/`onCancel` so the flag is only burned once the user has actually acted on the prompt.
- Bump the storage key to `.v2` so machines that already burned the old flag get one more chance to see the (now sticky) prompt.

title: fix: don't cache rejected oniguruma WASM load promise (fixes #326825)
body:
### Summary

`TypeError: Failed to fetch` is thrown from `TextMateTokenizationFeature._loadVSCodeOnigurumaWASM` when the renderer fetches the local `onig.wasm` asset (e.g. while editors are being restored during window startup/teardown). The fetch itself is a transient/environmental failure, but the memoization in `_getVSCodeOniguruma` **caches the rejected promise permanently**: `this._vscodeOniguruma` is assigned the rejecting async IIFE and never reset on failure. As a result, a single transient blip poisons TextMate tokenization for the *entire session* — every subsequent language whose tokenizer is created re-awaits the same rejected promise, and each one re-reports the error through `onUnexpectedError`. This amplification explains the hits-per-user ratio (218 hits / 125 users in 1.129.1) and why the bucket appears in essentially every shipped version.

The fix stops the amplification: on failure we clear the cache so a later request can retry, while still re-throwing so the genuine failure is reported once (never silenced).

Fixes microsoft/vscode#326825
Recommended reviewer: `@alexdima`

### Culprit Commit

Not identified via `git blame` — the workspace is a shallow (fetch-depth=1) clone, so line history is unavailable. The memoization pattern is long-standing; the bucket history shows hits across every tracked version (1.110 → 1.129), so this is not a single-commit regression but a long-lived latent amplifier. The recent `feat: restore asar for node_modules (#324897)` change altered the built `onig.wasm` resource path (`node_modules.asar.unpacked/...`) and is a plausible contributor to the recent uptick in transient fetch failures, but it is not the root cause of the telemetry amplification.

### Code Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[LanguageService.requestRichLanguageFeatures] --> B[TokenizationRegistry.getOrCreate]
    B --> C[factory.resolve -> _create]
    C --> D[TextMateTokenizationFeature.createSupport]
    D --> E[_createTokenizationSupport try/catch]
    E --> F[_getOrCreateGrammarFactory]
    F --> G[_getVSCodeOniguruma - memoized]
    G --> H[_loadVSCodeOnigurumaWASM: fetch onig.wasm]
    H -- Failed to fetch --> I[rejected promise cached in _vscodeOniguruma]
    I -- reused by every later language --> G
    E -- catch --> J[onUnexpectedError -> telemetry, once per language]
```

### Affected Files

- `src/vs/workbench/services/textMate/browser/textMateTokenizationFeatureImpl.ts` — `_getVSCodeOniguruma()` memoization now clears the cached promise on failure.

### Repro Steps

1. Open a workspace so editors are restored on startup (multiple files of different languages).
2. Cause the `onig.wasm` fetch to fail transiently (network hiccup, resource unavailable during window teardown/reload, or a slow/aborted request while the window is closing).
3. Observe that once the first fetch fails, TextMate tokenization stays broken for the whole session and `Failed to fetch` is reported repeatedly (once per language whose tokenizer is requested), rather than a single transient report followed by recovery.

### How the Fix Works

**Chosen approach** (`textMateTokenizationFeatureImpl.ts`, `_getVSCodeOniguruma`): wrap the memoized async loader in a `try/catch` that, on failure, resets `this._vscodeOniguruma = null` before re-throwing. This fixes the defect at the data producer — the memoization cache is where the permanently-broken state is created — rather than at the crash site (`_loadVSCodeOnigurumaWASM`). The `catch` does **not** silence anything: it re-throws so `_createTokenizationSupport`'s existing `catch` still routes the genuine failure to `onUnexpectedError` exactly once, preserving the telemetry pipeline. After this change a transient `Failed to fetch` no longer poisons the whole session; the next tokenizer request re-attempts the load and can succeed.

**Alternatives considered:**
- Swallowing the error in `_createTokenizationSupport`'s catch (e.g. treating `Failed to fetch` like the benign missing-grammar case): rejected because it hides a real failure from telemetry instead of fixing the state-caching defect that causes the repeated reports.
- Adding a guard/try-catch at the crash site in `_loadVSCodeOnigurumaWASM`: rejected because it masks the symptom at the bottom of the stack and does not address the cache poisoning that produces the amplification.

### Recommended Owner

`@alexdima` — owns the editor tokenization / TextMate service area (`src/vs/workbench/services/textMate`, `src/vs/editor/common/tokenizationRegistry.ts`).

title: fix: handle malformed file icon theme parse errors (fixes #326826)
body:
### Summary
An unhandled error `Problems parsing file icons file: ... Closing brace expected` is thrown into telemetry when the user's currently-active file icon theme file contains malformed JSON and is reloaded. `FileIconThemeLoader.loadIconThemeDocument` rejects when `Json.parse` reports errors (`fileIconThemeData.ts:224`). This rejection propagates out of `reloadCurrentFileIconTheme` (`workbenchThemeService.ts:696`) with no error handling, becoming an unhandled promise rejection.

The sibling `reloadCurrentColorTheme` (line 524) already wraps its reload in a `try/catch` that logs the failure via `logService.info` instead of throwing — malformed user theme files are an expected, benign condition. The file-icon reload path simply never received that same handling, so identical bad input surfaces as a crash for icon themes but not for color themes.

Fixes microsoft/vscode#326826
Recommended reviewer: `@aeschli`

### Culprit Commit
Could not run `git blame`/`git log` in this environment (git history access denied). The inconsistency is long-standing: `reloadCurrentColorTheme` has the guarded pattern while `reloadCurrentFileIconTheme` does not.

### Code Flow
```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[ThemeFileWatcher / onDidChange / languageService.onDidChange] --> B[reloadCurrentFileIconTheme]
    B --> C[currentFileIconTheme.reload]
    C --> D[FileIconThemeLoader.load]
    D --> E[loadIconThemeDocument]
    E --> F{Json.parse errors?}
    F -->|yes| G[Promise.reject new Error 'Problems parsing file icons file']
    G --> H[Unhandled rejection -> telemetry]
```

### Affected Files
- `src/vs/workbench/services/themes/browser/workbenchThemeService.ts` — `reloadCurrentFileIconTheme`

### Repro Steps
1. Install/select a file icon theme.
2. Corrupt the theme's icon JSON file so it has a syntax error (e.g. a missing closing brace).
3. Trigger a reload (edit/save the theme file, or fire `languageService.onDidChange`).
4. The parse rejection escapes `reloadCurrentFileIconTheme` as an unhandled error.

### How the Fix Works
**Chosen approach** (`workbenchThemeService.ts`, `reloadCurrentFileIconTheme`): wrap the `reload` + `applyAndSetFileIconTheme` calls in a `try/catch` that logs via `logService.info`, mirroring the existing `reloadCurrentColorTheme` handler. This is not error-silencing at a crash site: the value producer is the *user's malformed theme file*, and the codebase's intended, already-shipping behavior for exactly this benign condition is to log-and-continue (as color themes do). The change restores consistency across the theme-reload paths and prevents a user-config error from being reported as a VS Code crash. The `logService.info` call preserves diagnostic visibility.

**Alternatives considered**: catching inside `loadIconThemeDocument` and returning an empty document — rejected because it would hide genuinely malformed themes from *all* callers (including explicit theme-set flows that should surface the error to the user), whereas the fix targets only the background auto-reload path, matching the color-theme precedent.

### Recommended Owner
`@aeschli` — historical owner of the workbench themes service (`src/vs/workbench/services/themes`).

title: fix: decouple embeddings registration guard from main-thread model snapshot (fixes #326819)
body:
### Summary `ExtHostEmbeddings.registerEmbeddingsProvider` throws `An embeddings provider for this model is already registered` even when the extension host holds no live registration for that model. The dedup guard (`_allKnownModels`) is shared with the asynchronous main-thread model snapshot delivered via `$acceptEmbeddingModels`. An in-flight/stale snapshot can re-populate a model id that the extension host has already locally unregistered, so the very next `registerEmbeddingsProvider` for that model — commonly the Copilot Chat embeddings provider re-registering on an authentication change — trips the guard. Impact: the Copilot Chat embeddings provider fails to register, so semantic/embeddings features silently break for the affected session and an unhandled error is reported. Fixes microsoft/vscode#326819 Recommended reviewer: `@jrieken` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | [`6eaf6487`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/6eaf6487a4d8301b981036bfa53976546eb6694f) | | Author | `@jrieken` | | PR | #219994 | | Message | make sure to reset known embeddings models | | Why | This commit made `$acceptEmbeddingModels` replace `_allKnownModels` with the main-thread snapshot while that same set was left doubling as the local registration dedup guard. Because registration never adds to the set and disposal deletes from it, a late-arriving snapshot re-adds a just-unregistered model and the guard on the next register throws. | > This is a latent core defect (July 2024), an ancestor of the shipped build `8a7abeba`. The recent-regression telemetry signal comes from the Copilot Chat extension (0.57.0) re-registering the embeddings provider on every `onDidAuthenticationChange`, which exercises the register-after-dispose path that exposes the pre-existing race. The fix belongs in core, where the unreliable guard state is produced. ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Ext as CopilotChat _registerEmbeddings participant EH as ExtHostEmbeddings participant Main as MainThreadEmbeddings Ext->>EH: register copilot.model (auth valid) EH->>Main: $registerEmbeddingProvider Main-->>EH: $acceptEmbeddingModels([copilot.model]) Note over EH: _allKnownModels = {copilot.model} Ext->>EH: dispose (auth change) Note over EH: _allKnownModels.delete(copilot.model) Main-->>EH: stale $acceptEmbeddingModels([copilot.model]) Note over EH: ⚠️ guard re-populated {copilot.model}
while no live registration exists Ext->>EH: register copilot.model (auth valid again) Note over EH: 💥 An embeddings provider for this model is already registered ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostEmbedding.ts` | Root cause + crash site | L32-34 threw off `_allKnownModels`, which L90 (`$acceptEmbeddingModels`) reassigns from the async main-thread snapshot: `this._allKnownModels = new Set(models)`. The guard and the snapshot were the same variable. | | `src/vs/workbench/api/browser/mainThreadEmbeddings.ts` | Producer of snapshot | L88-90: `onDidChange` fires `$acceptEmbeddingModels(Array.from(allProviders))` on every provider add/remove, sending racy snapshots to the extension host. | | `extensions/copilot/src/extension/conversation/vscode-node/languageModelAccess.ts` | Trigger | L546-575 `_registerEmbeddings`/`update` clears and re-registers the same `copilot.${model}` provider on every `onDidAuthenticationChange`, exercising the register-after-dispose path. | ### Repro Steps 1. Sign in so the Copilot Chat embeddings provider registers `copilot.text-embedding-3-small` (main thread broadcasts the model snapshot back). 2. Trigger an authentication change (token refresh / re-auth) so `_registerEmbeddings.update()` disposes the current registration and re-registers the same model. 3. When a previously-sent `$acceptEmbeddingModels` snapshot containing the model is delivered to the extension host after the local dispose but before the re-register, the guard still reports the model as present. 4. The re-register throws `An embeddings provider for this model is already registered`. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** (`src/vs/workbench/api/common/extHostEmbedding.ts`): Introduce a dedicated `_registeredModels` set that is the single source of truth for the local dedup guard — `registerEmbeddingsProvider` adds to it on register and the returned disposable deletes from it on dispose. title: fix: don't surface user sign-in cancellation as unhandled error (fixes #326818)
body:
### Summary

`unhandlederror-Cancelled` is fired when a user **cancels the Copilot sign-in flow** during chat setup. `ChatSetupController.signIn` catches the `CancellationError` thrown by `defaultAccountService.signIn`, but then unconditionally re-throws it wrapped in a `ChatSetupError` (line 182). That error propagates through `doSetup` → `progressService` and surfaces as an unhandled telemetry error. User cancellation is an expected outcome, not a failure, so it should not reach telemetry.

Fixes microsoft/vscode#326818
Recommended reviewer: `@roblourens`

### Culprit Commit

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Commit | [`efed051e`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/efed051eed971b8435eaaec518e3dbd2cc603384) |
| PR | microsoft/vscode#325725 |
| Author | `@roblourens` |
| Why | This PR ("Prompt for Agent Host authentication before send") added a new entry point that drives the chat-setup sign-in dialog for Agent Host requests. When a user cancels that newly-reachable sign-in prompt, the pre-existing unconditional re-throw in `signIn` now fires as an unhandled `Cancelled` error, matching the `recent-regression` signal and the shipped commit timeframe. The re-throw location itself predates this commit; the commit made the cancel path reachable at scale. |

Ancestry vs shipped commit `e586b8ac` is consistent (authored 2026-07-18, shipped build seen 2026-07-20). Confidence is moderate — the throwing line is older, but the new caller is the plausible trigger for the regression.

### Code Flow

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[User triggers chat setup / Agent Host auth] --> B[doSetup]
    B --> C[signIn]
    C --> D[requests.signIn -> defaultAccountService.signIn]
    D -->|user cancels auth| E[throws CancellationError 'Cancelled']
    E --> F[catch: logService.error + store signInError]
    F --> G[if signInError: throw new ChatSetupError]
    G --> H[propagates via progressService]
    H --> I[unhandlederror-Cancelled in telemetry]
```

### Affected Files

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/chatSetup/chatSetupController.ts` | Crash origin — `signIn` re-throws the caught cancellation as `ChatSetupError` |
| `src/vs/workbench/services/chat/common/chatEntitlementService.ts` | Producer — `ChatEntitlementRequests.signIn` awaits `defaultAccountService.signIn`, which throws `CancellationError` on user cancel |

### Repro Steps

1. Sign out of Copilot / start from a signed-out state.
2. Trigger chat setup sign-in (e.g. via the chat view or an Agent Host request that prompts authentication).
3. When the authentication provider dialog appears, cancel it.
4. Observe `unhandlederror-Cancelled` originating from `chatSetupController.ts` `signIn`.

### How the Fix Works

**Chosen approach** — `chatSetupController.ts`, `signIn` catch block (bypass/throw site at `chatSetupController.ts:182`): add a guard at the point where the caught error is classified so that a `CancellationError` returns a "cancelled" result (`defaultAccount: undefined`) instead of being stored and re-thrown. `doSetup` already interprets an undefined `defaultAccount` as a cancelled sign-in (it returns `undefined`), so no downstream change is needed. This distinguishes a deliberate user cancellation from a genuine sign-in failure — the same distinction the sibling `install` path already makes via `isCancellationError` — rather than treating every caught value as an error. `isCancellationError` was already imported and used in this file.

The guard is placed where cancellation is first classified (the earliest correct handling point), not as a blanket suppression: real errors still hit `logService.error` and still throw `ChatSetupError`, preserving the telemetry pipeline. It also avoids showing the misleading "Failed to sign in. Retry?" dialog after a deliberate cancel.

**Alternatives considered**
- Guarding at the `throw` on line 182 (`if (signInError && !isCancellationError(signInError)) throw`): still logs the cancellation as an error and shows the retry dialog; the earlier guard handles both correctly and closer to the source.
- Wrapping the propagation in `try/catch` upstream: hides the error instead of correctly classifying user cancellation, and risks swallowing genuine failures.

### Recommended Owner

`@roblourens` — author of the regression PR #325725 and owner of the chat/Agent Host authentication setup flow.

title: Config-action slash commands for Copilot agent-host chat inputs
body:
Fixes #325890

## What & why

In Copilot agent-host chat sessions, typing a permission/mode slash command (e.g. `/plan`) did **not** update the mode/permission pickers. This PR introduces **config-action slash commands** that toggle a session-config axis instead of sending a chat turn, and wires them into **both** the editor-window chat input and the Agents window.

Typing `/` now offers, for Copilot agent-host sessions only:

- **Permissions axis (`autoApprove`):** `/yolo`, `/yolo on|off`, `/allow-all`, `/autoApprove`
- **Mode axis (`mode`):** `/autopilot on|off`, `/autopilot <objective>`, `/plan <prompt>`, `/goal`

Selecting an item toggles the corresponding session config and the picker updates reactively; it does not send a chat turn.

## How it works

- **Producer (server):** the Copilot completion provider emits these items with an `action` bag (`{ applyConfig }`) on the completion attachment `_meta`. Runtime commands that collide (e.g. `plan`) are shadowed.
- **Consumer (client, shared across both windows):** a shared accept-handler runs the existing elevated-permission confirmation (`maybeConfirmElevatedPermissionLevel`) for elevated `autoApprove` values, then applies the change via a per-window seam — editor uses the AHP dispatch/provisional path; the Agents window uses `provider.setSessionConfigValue`.
- **Insert behavior:** toggle items insert nothing (`insertText: ''` + explicit `label`); `<prompt>` items keep `/cmd ` and show an argument hint.
- **Send path:** `CopilotAgentSession.send` intercepts these commands, re-applies the mode, and strips the leading token so it is not dispatched to the runtime.
- **Policy:** elevated auto-approve items are omitted when enterprise policy disables global auto-approval (client-side, mirroring the pickers), with clamps kept as defense-in-depth.
- **Cleanup:** the old hardcoded permission commands in `chatSlashCommands.ts` are unscoped from agent-host Copilot sessions so the completion pipeline solely owns them.

## Tests

- `agentMetaReaders` — round-trip of the new `action` `_meta`.
- `copilotConfigSlashCommands` — catalog items + send-path resolver.
- `CopilotSlashCommandCompletionProvider` — config items injected, runtime collision shadowing.
- `applyAgentHostCompletionAction` — elevated confirmation gating + policy-block predicate.

Validation: `typecheck-client`, `valid-layers-check`, ESLint, and the affected unit suites all pass.

## Known follow-ups (not in this PR)

A review flagged a few items to address separately: applying `autoApprove` on the manually-typed send path, avoiding empty turns for bare toggles, the `/goal` vs `toCopilotSdkMode('goal')` naming, tightening `_meta.action` trust, and remote-Copilot editor apply.

title: Fix Agent Host startup race in Remote-SSH windows
body:
## Summary

- wait for the Remote-SSH environment before starting the editor-side Agent Host handshake
- provide a transport factory so later transport loss can use AHP soft reconnect
- add regression coverage for the startup ordering race

## Root cause

The editor-side Agent Host client could begin connecting while Remote-SSH authority resolution was still replacing the management connection. The stale connection then closed the one-shot AHP client before the replacement server exposed `agentHostProxy`, leaving Agent Host agents unavailable until the window was reloaded.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- `npm run precommit`

title: Show all cloud sessions in the agents window regardless of active repo
body:
## Problem

In the agents window, the v2 Task backend's `fetchSessionList` scoped the cloud session list to the active workspace's repositories (via `getRepoId`). As a result, the agents window only showed sessions for the currently selected repo instead of all of the user's cloud sessions.

The `isAgentWorkspace` flag was passed to `fetchSessionList` but ignored (`_isAgentWorkspace`), so the agents window fell through to the repo-scoped code path whenever an active GitHub repo was present.

## Fix

Use the global user-scoped `agents/tasks` list when in the agents window, regardless of `repoIds`. This mirrors the existing v1 Jobs backend behavior in [`jobsApiBackend.ts`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/extensions/copilot/src/extension/chatSessions/vscode-node/jobsApiBackend.ts), which already gates on `isAgentWorkspace || !repoIds || repoIds.length === 0`.

```ts
if (isAgentWorkspace || !repoIds || repoIds.length === 0) {
    // global agents/tasks list — all the user's sessions
```

The global `agents/tasks` endpoint is already scoped to the authenticated user, so no `creator_id` filter is needed.

## Behavior

- **Agents window**: shows all of the user's cloud sessions across every repo, regardless of which folder/repo is active.
- **Outside the agents window**: unchanged — still repo-scoped via `creator_id`.

## Tests

Added a unit test asserting the agents window uses the global list (and never the repo-scoped endpoint) even when `repoIds` are present. All `fetchSessionList` tests pass.

title: [cherry-pick] NES: split open-tab vs related-file neighbor context
body:
Cherry-pick of #326626 from `main`.

## Summary

Two related improvements to the **xtab (NES / Next Edit Suggestions)** *neighboring-files context*. Both hinge on distinguishing neighbor snippets that come from **open tabs** vs. from **language-service "related" files** (the non-open-tab files a language service suggests, e.g. `related/typescript`, `related/cpp`).

1. **No line numbers for related-file snippets.** Snippets sourced from language-service related files now omit line numbers in the prompt, matching NES's *own* language-context path (`appendLanguageContextSnippets`, which already uses `IncludeLineNumbersOption.None`). Open-tab neighbor snippets are unchanged and keep their line numbers.
2. **Ability to turn off the related-files context.** A new `neighborFiles.includeRelatedFiles` option lets us disable the completions-style related-files context entirely, since NES already has its own language-context implementation (`ILanguageContextProviderService`). When off, the related-files LSP computation is **skipped entirely** (no wasted work), leaving only open-tab neighbors.

Both default to **behavior-preserving** settings, so this PR is a no-op until the new config is flipped.

## Motivation

NES's neighboring-files context (Jaccard-ranked snippets from Completions) overlaps with NES's own language context. This PR makes the two coexist cleanly: related-file snippets are formatted consistently with the language-context path (no line numbers), and the redundant related-files context can be switched off per experiment.

## What changed

**Point 1 — provenance tag + line-number formatting.** Each neighbor snippet carries its provenance, decided once at the source (where the neighbor type is known) rather than re-derived from URIs:
- `neighborFiles.ts` (completions-core): `isRelatedNeighboringFileType(type)` is a `switch` over the `Related*` enum members (robust to enum changes, no string-prefix matching). `getNeighborFilesAndTraits` stamps `isFromRelatedFile` on each related doc as it is materialized.
- `prompt.ts` / `selectRelevance.ts`: `SimilarFileInfo` and `ScoredSnippet` gain an optional `isFromRelatedFile`. `getSimilarSnippets` propagates it (and the source `uri`) onto every ranked snippet and guarantees it on its return type (`SnippetWithSourceInfo`).
- `similarFilesContext.ts`: `getSnippetsForPrompt` reads `s.isFromRelatedFile` directly — no post-ranking URI set / cross-referencing.
- `similarFilesContextService.ts`: `INeighborFileSnippet` gains `readonly isFromRelatedFile: boolean`.
- `recentFilesForPrompt.ts`: `appendNeighborFileSnippets` uses `IncludeLineNumbersOption.None` for related-file snippets, else the configured option.

**Point 2 — toggle**
- `xtabPromptOptions.ts`: adds `includeRelatedFiles` to `NeighborFilesOptions` (type + `VALIDATOR` + `DEFAULT_OPTIONS`, default `true`).
- `configurationService.ts`: new team-internal, experiment-based key `chat.advanced.inlineEdits.xtabProvider.neighborFiles.includeRelatedFiles`.
- `xtabProvider.ts`: wires the config into the `neighborFiles` options and threads the flag into `getSnippetsForPrompt` and the fire-and-forget telemetry `compute`.
- `neighborFiles.ts` (completions-core): `getNeighborFilesAndTraits` gains an `includeRelatedFiles: boolean = true` param; when `false` it returns early with open-tab neighbors only, before any related-files/LSP work.

## Behavior & compatibility

- **Defaults unchanged:** `includeRelatedFiles` defaults to `true`; related files continue to be included exactly as before. Line-numbering for open-tab snippets is unchanged.
- **Only new behavior** is (a) related-file snippets drop line numbers, and (b) the new exp key can turn related files off.
- Gated correctly for AI-disabled users — this is inside the existing xtab provider path and only runs when `neighborFiles.enabled` is on.

## How to review

Suggested reading order:

1. **`similarFilesContextService.ts`** — the new `isFromRelatedFile` field + the `includeRelatedFiles` param on the two service methods. This is the contract for everything else.
2. **`neighborFiles.ts`** (completions-core) — `isRelatedNeighboringFileType`, the `isFromRelatedFile` stamp on related docs, and the one-line early-return in `getNeighborFilesAndTraits` (`if (!includeRelatedFiles || featuresService.excludeRelatedFiles(...))`). Confirm skipping related files still returns open-tab neighbors + empty traits.
3. **`similarFiles.ts` / `selectRelevance.ts`** — the tag rides on `SimilarFileInfo` → each snippet; `getSimilarSnippets` guarantees `uri` + `isFromRelatedFile` on its return type.
4. **`similarFilesContext.ts`** — `getSnippetsForPrompt` classifies purely from `s.isFromRelatedFile` (no URI set), so multi-root relative-path collisions can't misclassify a snippet.
5. **`recentFilesForPrompt.ts`** — related snippets get `IncludeLineNumbersOption.None`; open-tab snippets keep the configured option.

## Tests

- `similarFiles.test.ts` (prompt): `getSimilarSnippets` preserves each source `uri` under a multi-root relativePath collision, and propagates `isFromRelatedFile` from source file → snippet.
- `neighborFiles.test.ts` (completions-core): `includeRelatedFiles=false` retains open-tab neighbors, keeps traits empty, and (via a call counter on the mocked provider) proves the related-files provider is never invoked — with a positive control for the enabled path.
- `recentFilesForPrompt.spec.ts` (xtab): related snippets omit line numbers; open-tab snippets keep them.

title: Support Go to Symbol (⇧⌘O) for chat sessions
body:
## Summary

Makes **Go to Symbol in Editor** (`⇧⌘O` / `Ctrl+Shift+O`) work for chat, treating each user request (prompt) as a navigable "symbol" so you can jump between exchanges in a conversation. Previously the palette just showed *"To go to a symbol, first open a text editor with symbol information."* for chats.

This works for both:
- **Chat editors** — via a new `ChatOutline` registered with `IOutlineService`, which also lights up the Outline pane and Breadcrumbs for free.
- **A focused chat widget** (including the **Agents window** and the sidebar chat view) — handled directly in the quick access provider.

## What a "symbol" is

Each **user request** becomes a top-level entry, labeled with the prompt text and a chat icon. Selecting one reveals and focuses that request in the chat.

## Changes

- **`chatOutline.ts` (new)** — `ChatOutline` / `ChatOutlineCreator` implementing `IOutline`/`IOutlineCreator`, matched to the `ChatEditor` pane. Registered in `chat.shared.contribution.ts`. No changes to the Go to Symbol picker were needed for the editor case — it consumes any registered outline.
- **`gotoSymbolQuickAccess.ts`**
  - Overrides `provide()` to prioritize a **focused chat** over an active file editor, so the chat wins when it has focus even with a file open side by side (otherwise the base routes to the file editor's symbols). Focus is detected via `isAncestorOfActiveElement` on the widget DOM node, checked before the quick input steals focus.
  - Unifies the chat and editor-pane outline paths through a shared `installNavigablePicks` helper.

## Notes / gotchas addressed

- **Label derivation:** request text is derived the way the chat list renders it (followup message, else the parsed request `parts`) rather than `messageText`, which agent-host/cloud sessions leave empty.
- **Icons:** codicons cannot be passed via `iconClasses` in this quick-pick path (see the existing `todo@jrieken` note in `notebookOutline.ts`); the icon is embedded inline in the label as `$(icon-id) …` with the request text escaped via `escapeIcons` so a literal `$(...)` in a prompt stays literal.

## Testing

- [ ] `npm run typecheck-client`
- [ ] `npm run valid-layers-check`
- [ ] Manual: `⇧⌘O` in a chat editor and in the Agents window chat lists requests and navigates to them; a file editor focused side by side still shows file symbols.

title: Chat dictation: always use Nemotron model, remove model setting
body:
The on-device chat dictation runtime is Microsoft Foundry Local's streaming ASR engine, and the only supported model is NVIDIA Nemotron (`nemotron-speech-streaming-en-0.6b` — the model the GitHub Copilot app ships). The `chat.speechToText.model` setting therefore only ever had a single valid value, and the legacy Whisper model IDs no longer resolve.

This PR removes model selection entirely and hardcodes Nemotron:

- **Remove the `chat.speechToText.model` setting.** Its migration is replaced with one that clears any explicitly-stored value so it doesn't linger as an unknown setting (this also drops the legacy `onnx-community/whisper-*` references).
- **`ChatSpeechToTextService`**: remove `MODEL_SETTING` and `_getModelId()`; start the local session without a model argument.
- **`ILocalTranscriptionService.start()`**: drop the unused optional `model` option from the interface, the electron-browser proxy, and the node implementation. The node service always uses the Nemotron default.

No user-facing behavior change: dictation already defaulted to Nemotron. This just removes the dead selection surface and the last Whisper references.

title: JSON - support ${workspaceFolder} in json.schemas fileMatch patterns
body:
Fixes #44135

Implements the approach from https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/44135#issuecomment-5022741898: `${workspaceFolder}` is expanded on the client, and the server API stays unchanged.

### Change

- `jsonClient.ts`: when collecting `json.schemas` settings, a leading `${workspaceFolder}` in a `fileMatch` pattern (also after a `!` exclusion prefix) expands to the workspace folder path. This happens in the two scopes with an unambiguous folder: workspace folder settings in a multi-root workspace, and workspace settings of a single-folder workspace. User settings and multi-root workspace-file settings are left untouched (no single folder to expand to). Non-array/non-string values pass through unchanged.
- `utils/strings.ts`: `escapeGlobCharacters`, used to insert the folder path into the pattern.
- `package.nls.json`: documents the new pattern form.

Since the expanded pattern carries the folder path, the server's implicit `**/` prefix no longer widens it below the folder — `${workspaceFolder}/*.json` matches only in the folder root, `${workspaceFolder}/sub/*.json` only in that subfolder, and existing patterns behave exactly as before.

### Validation

- A parity harness against the service's real `createRegex` + `vscode-uri` (66 cases): root-only and subfolder anchoring, recursive `**` patterns, exclusions, the multi-root `folderUri` gate, folder names with spaces/unicode/parens/`$`/glob metacharacters/`#`/`?`, uppercase drive letters, filesystem-root and drive-root folders, and malformed `fileMatch` values (bare string, non-string entries — no throw, pass through).
- End-to-end in a dev build, re-run on this revision: with a `${workspaceFolder}/*.json` schema and a plain `*.json` schema both requiring a property, the folder-root file reports two diagnostics and a file in a subfolder reports one — the anchored schema applies at the root only.

### Notes

- The folder path is spelled the way the server spells the document uris it matches against: a leading drive letter is lowercased and `#` and `?` are percent-encoded — `Uri.path` lowercases neither and decodes both. Glob metacharacters are encoded as `\xAB` escapes, which the glob parser copies through to the generated regular expression, so folder names like `my[proj]` or `w*s` match literally. A backslash escape can't be used for this — the parser has no escape syntax, so it copies the backslash through and still reads the next character as glob syntax.
- Being a path, the pattern is not tied to a scheme or authority, and the `**/` prefix still allows leading segments before it — the same as any absolute pattern written by hand today. In a multi-root workspace the existing `folderUri` gate still scopes each pattern to its folder.
- While validating the multi-root case I noticed folder-scoped `json.schemas` (in a folder's `.vscode/settings.json` inside a `.code-workspace`) don't reach the server even for plain patterns, also on stable 1.129 — that looks like a separate pre-existing issue, independent of this change. I can file it with the minimal fixture if useful.

title: Omni-chat with multi-session routing
body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/8461

Addresses #329698

## What

Adds a floating, frameless, always-on-top Omni Chat input that hosts the compact `ChatWidget`, including multiline editing, attachments, model/mode selection, dictation, Voice Mode, and input glow.

Toggle it with **Toggle Floating Chat Input Window** (`workbench.action.chat.toggleInputWindow`).

## Session routing

Omni submissions do not run in the input window's scratch session. `ChatSessionRoutingController` instead:

1. Collects active Copilot agent sessions, excluding Omni's scratch session and read-only or archived sessions.
2. Scores every candidate semantically, then enriches a bounded shortlist with clipped conversation history.
3. Uses the utility language model to select the most relevant session, with lexical scoring only as a deterministic tie-breaker.
4. Starts a new Copilot session when no existing session is a confident match or the user explicitly requests a new session.
5. In multi-root workspaces, determines the destination folder for a new session in this order:
   - **Attached resource:** the workspace folder containing the first attached file or resource that maps to the workspace.
   - **Explicit folder mention:** a case-insensitive, whole-name match against a workspace folder's display name or final path segment. Names shorter than three characters are ignored, and the longest matching name wins.
   - **Related session:** the first model-ranked result with confidence of at least 0.35 whose metadata maps to a workspace folder. The session's working directory is checked before its repository path; nested workspace matches prefer the deepest folder.
   - **Default:** the last folder selected for a new Agent Host session, when it is still part of the workspace.
   - **Final fallback:** the first workspace folder.

The resolved folder is shown in the proposed **New session in _folder_** destination. In a multi-root workspace, **Change Folder** lets the user override it before dispatch.

Before dispatch, Omni presents a correctable destination list:

- **Arrow keys** move between destinations.
- **Space** toggles destinations for fan-out.
- **Enter** sends to the selected destination(s).
- **Escape** cancels.
- Continuing to edit the prompt or attachments cancels the pending route.

Existing Agent Host routes preserve their session-owned model. New sessions use the model selected in Omni. Queued requests retain their session reference until delivery and distinguish sent, cancelled, removed, and failed outcomes.

Routing metadata and transcripts are scoped to Copilot providers; sessions owned by other providers are not sent to the Copilot router.

## Voice Mode

Voice Mode has explicit surface ownership:

- Omni owns capture, draft state, routed target, and active window as one transfer.
- A single route pins Voice Mode to the actual destination session.
- Fan-out clears the sticky target rather than selecting an arbitrary session.
- The hold-to-barge-in keybinding preserves an Omni-owned target when invoked in Omni, while invoking it from panel chat intentionally transfers ownership to panel chat.
- Closing, blurring after a completed turn, or disconnecting releases Omni ownership and stale routing state.

Pending questions and approvals from routed sessions are surfaced in Omni. Terminal approvals show the exact command plus approval message, disclaimer/risk explanation, custom choices, and reliable **Allow Once**/**Skip** controls. Resolved approvals retain semantic tombstones so rehydrated tool cards cannot become actionable again.

## Window behavior

- The leading grip moves the frameless window; Send and Close remain independent controls.
- The auxiliary window grows for multiline input, destination choices, pending questions, and approvals.
- Long approval content is bounded and scrollable.
- Model-picker expansion restores the previous fitted height without stealing focus after an asynchronous resize.
- The floating surface is hidden when AI features are disabled or Chat entitlement is hidden.

## Implementation

- `chat/common/sessionRouter.ts` defines the routing contract and parser.
- `chat/browser/sessionRouter/` owns candidate collection, history enrichment, ranking, folder selection, dispatch, queue lifecycle, and delivery feedback.
- `chat/browser/chatInputWindow/` owns the auxiliary surface, compact widget, routing host, pending-input UI, and sizing.
- `chat/browser/voiceClient/voiceSessionController.ts` owns atomic Voice Mode surface/target transfer, routed narration, and approval identity.
- Shared auxiliary-window bounds APIs keep browser-layer code independent of Electron-only native services.

## Validation

- Client compilation and layer checks
- Focused routing, Voice Mode, approval-identity, and routing-helper suites in Chromium, WebKit, and Firefox
- Manual testing of existing/new-session routing, multi-root folder choice, Voice Mode barge-in ownership, terminal approvals, custom approval options, long content, and multiple pending sessions

title: Fix Cmd/Ctrl+I dictation in the Agents window composer
body:
## Description

Pressing Cmd/Ctrl+I did nothing in the Agents window chat composer, while it worked in the main window chat input.

**Root cause:** the Agents composer (`NewChatInputWidget`) handled the dictation chord via a raw editor `onKeyDown` listener. That path loses the chord to `editor.action.triggerSuggest`, which binds Cmd/Ctrl+I as a secondary keybinding at `EditorContrib` weight. The main window works because it registers dictation through the keybinding service at `WorkbenchContrib + 1`, outranking Trigger Suggest.

**Changes** (`src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/browser/newChatInput.ts`):

- Register `sessions.action.chat.toggleDictation` (Cmd/Ctrl+I) through the keybinding service at `WorkbenchContrib + 1`, gated on a new `sessionsChatInputHasDictationFocus` context key and `chatSpeechToTextConfigured` — so it reliably wins the chord, and falls back to Trigger Suggest when dictation isn't available.
- Track the focused composer at module scope and route the command to it (the composer isn't an `IChatWidget`, so the shared Dictate action can't reach it); cleared on blur/dispose.
- Remove the fragile `onKeyDown` Cmd/Ctrl+I branch; expose a public `toggleDictation()`.

```ts
KeybindingsRegistry.registerCommandAndKeybindingRule({
	id: 'sessions.action.chat.toggleDictation',
	weight: KeybindingWeight.WorkbenchContrib + 1,
	when: ContextKeyExpr.and(
		SessionsChatInputHasDictationFocus,
		ContextKeyExpr.has(ChatContextKeys.speechToTextConfigured.key),
	),
	primary: KeyMod.CtrlCmd | KeyCode.KeyI,
	handler: () => activeDictationComposer?.toggleDictation(),
});
```

title: Voice: clear routing/pending state on disconnect and remove idle glow
body:
Fixes microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#8515

## Voice: clear routing/pending state on disconnect

`VoiceSessionController.disconnect()` (and `_handleFatalDisconnect`) reset most state but never cleared the user-picked routing target (`_targetSession`) or the always-on pending-confirmation snapshot (`_pendingToolConfirmations`).

Because `_targetSession` survived teardown, reconnecting from a different, newly focused session re-pinned voice to the *previously* targeted session:

- the previous session's input glow/mic indicator lit up again, and
- the next utterance was routed to it (sent as a plain follow-up request) instead of resolving its pending confirmation.

Both terminal-teardown paths now reset `_targetSession` and `_pendingToolConfirmations`, so a later `connect()` starts from focus-based detection.

### Repro (before)
1. Create a voice session ("Create a new file").
2. While it's working, disconnect voice → session shows "input needed".
3. Create a new session and reactivate voice.
4. The mic indicator reappears on the old session and voice is re-pinned there; saying "approve it" skips the question and is sent as a follow-up.

## Remove the connected-idle glow

Removes the white/themed "breathing" idle glow from voice mode in both the main window (`ChatViewPane`) and the Agents window (`agentsVoiceWidget` / `voiceInputDecorations`). Voice mode now only glows while **listening** or **speaking**.

- `voiceGlow.ts` drops the idle intensity/color/branch and exposes `isGlowingVoiceState()` so callers gate their animation loops consistently.
- Removes the now-dead `.voice-idle` CSS rules and the unused `isMotionReduced` glow plumbing.
- Updates `voiceGlow.test.ts` accordingly.

## Validation
- `npm run typecheck-client` passes.

title: Add telemetry for applied enterprise policies
body:
## Summary

Adds a consolidated `policy.applied` telemetry event for understanding enterprise policy adoption.

The event:

- Fires once after workbench restoration and again when effective policy state changes.
- Debounces change bursts by 500 ms and suppresses duplicate payloads.
- Reports the total number of applied policies.
- Reports whether selected chat, plugin, OpenTelemetry, telemetry-level, and feedback policies are applied.
- Reports low-cardinality value buckets for default-model auto selection, tool auto-approval being forced off, marketplace lockdown, OTel being forced on, and telemetry level.
- Never reports raw policy values, model identifiers, organization names, plugin IDs, marketplace URLs, or other user/admin-provided strings.

The contribution reads only authoritative effective values from `IPolicyService`. Delivery-source attribution is intentionally excluded because the current policy service API does not expose which child of `MultiplexPolicyService` supplied the winning value.

Supersedes #325385, preserving Harald's original commit and simplifying the implementation from five changed files to three.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/workbench/services/policies/test/browser/policyTelemetryContribution.test.ts`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- VS Code hygiene checks
- `@vscode/telemetry-extractor@1.14.0`

Focused tests cover the empty startup event, every reported policy and value bucket, privacy-safe handling of unexpected values, the total applied-policy count, debounced updates, and payload deduplication.

title: ah: fix client tool call confirmations
body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

Summary
- Client-provided tools could still show a confirmation prompt in Allow All or Assisted Permissions mode, even though Agent Host had already approved the invocation.

Root Cause
- Agent Host represented the approval using the protocol’s confirmed field, commonly as not-needed. The client tool bridge only recognized the separate autoApproveBySetting metadata flag, so it invoked the local tool without passing through the existing approval.

The local tool service consequently performed its own confirmation flow.

Changes
- Convert resolved protocol confirmation reasons into local pre-approval reasons.
- Continue supporting the existing autoApproveBySetting metadata path.
- Pass the resolved approval into local client-tool invocation.
- Apply late-arriving approval state if an invocation is already waiting for confirmation.
- Preserve whether approval came from: no confirmation being required, a setting, or, explicit user action.
- Client tools now proceed directly to execution when Agent Host has already approved them, avoiding both the prompt and transient “needs input” state.

title: Dictation: migrate on-device runtime to Foundry Local streaming ASR
body:
Vastly improves latency and accuracy of dictation

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d35dcb2f-e3b1-4a65-b728-e37f43efdd3e

## What & why

The GitHub Copilot app's on-device dictation feels snappier and more accurate than VS Code's. It runs through **Microsoft Foundry Local**'s native streaming ASR runtime (onnxruntime + onnxruntime-genai), which does decode, VAD and endpointing in native code, using NVIDIA's `nemotron-speech-streaming-en-0.6b` streaming RNN-T model.

This draft replaces VS Code's dictation pipeline (transformers.js Whisper + a hand-rolled Nemotron RNN-T decoder on `onnxruntime-node`) with the same **Foundry Local** engine for parity.

## Changes

- **Node service rewrite** (`platform/localTranscription/node/localTranscriptionService.ts`): drives `foundry-local-sdk` — async `FoundryLocalManager`, model download/load progress, a live streaming session. Buffers captured PCM until the session opens (so first-use download doesn't drop leading audio), then streams raw PCM16; accumulates a cumulative transcript from per-segment `is_final` results and emits interim/final transcripts.
- **Deleted** `nemotronTranscriber.ts` (native decode now lives in Foundry).
- **Setting**: `chat.speechToText.model` enum → Foundry model alias (`nemotron-speech-streaming-en-0.6b`, default).
- **Interface/proxy docs** updated to Foundry Local; platform gate kept (its `SUPPORTED_TARGETS` already match Foundry's prebuild targets exactly: darwin-arm64, linux-x64/arm64, win32-x64/arm64).
- **Packaging**: bundle `foundry-local-sdk` native addon + core libs (gulpfile ASAR-unpack + per-target prebuild filter, darwin macho/universal, linux dep scanner) in place of `onnxruntime-node`. Dropped `@huggingface/transformers`, `onnxruntime-node`, and the `sharp` stub.

title: Reset dictation transcript state on session teardown
body:
## Description

The on-device dictation transcript (`_finalizedText`/`_deltaText`) was cleared inconsistently across `ChatSpeechToTextService` session lifecycles: on `cancel()` and `_failSession()`, and on the *next* `start()` — but only *after* the async microphone-acquisition prompt. A normal `stopAndTranscribe()` ("Stop recording") left the prior transcript in service state, so a subsequent recording could resurface it.

Changes:

- **Centralize the reset in `_teardown()`** — every session-end path (stop, cancel, error, and `start()`'s error paths) already funnels through here, so the transcript is now cleared the instant a session ends rather than on the next start. This removes the window in which stale text could reappear.
- **Remove the now-redundant resets** in `start()`, `cancel()`, and `_failSession()`, making `_teardown()` the single source of truth for the invariant "no transcript survives the session that produced it."

The returned final transcript is captured in a local and telemetry (`transcriptLength`) is logged *before* `_teardown()`, so both remain correct.

Net diff: 6 insertions / 6 deletions in one file.

title: Prompt to disable redundant VS Code Speech extension when built-in dictation is available
body:
## Summary

Adds a one-time notification suggesting users disable the [`ms-vscode.vscode-speech`](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=ms-vscode.vscode-speech) extension once VS Code's built-in on-device chat dictation makes it redundant.

New workbench contribution `RedundantDictationExtensionNotifier` (registered at `WorkbenchPhase.Eventually`) shows the prompt **only when all** of the following hold:

1. **Platform supports built-in dictation** — `ILocalTranscriptionService.isSupported`, the same predicate that shows/hides the built-in mic button (false on macOS Intel, unsupported Linux archs, web, remote — no new platform logic).
2. **Built-in dictation is enabled** — `chat.speechToText.enabled === true`, so we never suggest disabling a working extension before its replacement is turned on.
3. **Extension installed & enabled** — via `IExtensionsWorkbenchService.queryLocal()` + positive `enablementState` check.
4. **Never shown before** — application-scoped `IStorageService` flag, set the moment the prompt appears, so it fires at most once ever regardless of the user's choice.

### Prompt

> VS Code now has built-in dictation, so the 'VS Code Speech' extension is no longer needed. Disable it?

- **Disable Extension** → `setEnablement(ext, EnablementState.DisabledGlobally)`
- **Keep** → dismiss

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck-client` — 0 errors.
- Manual: on a supported platform with the extension installed and `chat.speechToText.enabled` on, the prompt appears once; choosing *Disable Extension* disables it; the prompt does not reappear after restart.

title: fix: guard Quick Search "Open in Search View" against unmaterialized tree element (fixes #326646)
body:
### Summary `TreeError [SearchView] Tree element not found` is thrown when a user moves a Quick Search (Go to File / text search quick access) result into the full Search view via the "Open in Search View" / "More" / "See More Files" affordances. `TextSearchQuickAccess.moveToSearchViewlet` transfers its search model to the Search view and then calls `viewer.setSelection([currentElem])` on the view's `WorkbenchCompressibleAsyncDataTree`. Because that tree lazy-loads its nodes, `currentElem` (often a deep `Match` under a not-yet-expanded file, or a file match beyond the visible limit) may not be materialized in the tree yet, so `setSelection` throws. The impact is an unhandled error surfaced to telemetry and a failed "open in search view" gesture. Fixes microsoft/vscode#326646 Recommended reviewer: `@osortega` ### Culprit Commit | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Commit | [`88056f2`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/commit/88056f2c97d6bde7cf151bfff35b4c3e2c65b407) | | Author | `@andreamah` | | PR | #228886 | | Message | Use `WorkbenchCompressibleAsyncDataTree` for lazy loading AI results (#228886) | | Why | This commit converted the Search view tree from a fully-materialized sync tree to a lazy-loading async data tree. `moveToSearchViewlet` kept calling `setSelection`/`reveal` with an element reference that a sync tree always contained but the async tree only contains once its parent chain has been loaded, so the pre-existing call became able to throw `Tree element not found`. | > This is a long-standing mechanism (the async-tree conversion predates the shipped build by well over a year) surfaced as a recent telemetry spike, so it is effectively pre-existing; `88056f2` is named because it is the change that made the `setSelection` call unsafe. The fix is independent of exact culprit attribution. ### Code Flow ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant User as Quick Search pick participant QA as TextSearchQuickAccess.moveToSearchViewlet participant View as SearchView.replaceSearchModel participant Tree as CompressibleAsyncDataTree participant Model as CompressedObjectTreeModel User->>QA: accept "Open in Search View" / "More" QA->>View: replaceSearchModel(model) (queues async refresh) Note over View: setInput + queued updateChildren;
deep nodes not yet materialized QA->>Tree: setSelection([currentElem]) Tree->>Model: map element -> node (getNode/getCompressedNode) Note over Model: ⚠️ element not in nodes map Note over Model: 💥 TreeError [SearchView] Tree element not found ``` ### Affected Files | File | Role | Evidence | |------|------|----------| | `src/vs/base/browser/ui/tree/compressedObjectTreeModel.ts` | crash site | L347 `throw new TreeError(this.user, 'Tree element not found: ...')` (from stack) | | `src/vs/workbench/contrib/search/browser/quickTextSearch/textSearchQuickAccess.ts` | root cause | L219-L226: `viewer.setSelection([currentElem])` called on a lazy async tree with an element (`matches[limit]` L256 / deep `element` L291) that may not be materialized | | `src/vs/base/browser/ui/tree/asyncDataTree.ts` | precondition | L839-L850 `hasNode()` reports whether an element has been materialized in the async tree | ### Repro Steps 1. Open a folder with many text matches for a common term. 2. Open Quick Search (text search quick access) and type a term producing many results, enough to show the "More" / "See More Files" separators. 3. Trigger "Open in Search View" / "More" on a match whose file match is not expanded/loaded (or a file match beyond the shown limit). 4. Intermittently, the transferred Search view tree has not yet materialized that node, so `setSelection` throws `TreeError [SearchView] Tree element not found`. Timing-dependent: larger result sets and collapsed files increase the likelihood. ### How the Fix Works **Chosen approach** — `textSearchQuickAccess.ts` → `moveToSearchViewlet()`: guard the `setFocus`/`setSelection`/`reveal` block on `viewer?.hasNode(currentElem)`. When the element has not been materialized in the async tree, fall back to focusing the search widget — the exact behavior the existing `else` branch already provides for the "no element" case. This checks a documented precondition of the async-data-tree API before invoking it, at the site that produces the invalid call (fix at the caller that makes the unsupported call, not at the shared tree crash site). It reuses the same `hasNode` materialization check already used elsewhere in this view (`RefreshTreeController.refreshTree`, `searchView.ts` L2769), so it introduces no new contract and no `try/catch` that would hide errors from telemetry. **Lifecycle pattern**: async-init race (stale/unmaterialized cached reference) — the consumer holds a `RenderableMatch` that the freshly-input async tree has not yet loaded. **Producer site**: `src/vs/workbench/contrib/search/browser/searchView.ts:469` — `replaceSearchModel` calls `setInput` and only queues (does not synchronously complete) the tree refresh, so deep nodes are absent when control returns to the caller. **Why this fix**: after this change, `textSearchQuickAccess.ts:220` only calls `setSelection`/`reveal` when `hasNode` confirms the element exists, so `CompressedObjectTreeModel.getCompressedNode` can no longer receive an absent element from this path. **Alternatives considered**: awaiting a full recursive tree materialization/`expandTo` inside `replaceSearchModel` before returning — rejected because it would force-expand collapsed file matches (changing UX) and broaden the change well beyond the failing path for a gesture whose graceful degradation (focus the widget) already exists. ### Recommended Owner `@osortega` — current Search View owner per `microsoft/vscode-engineering` `triage/working-areas.md` (the culprit-commit author's change is effectively pre-existing;
